# Planyr — Backlog

Single source of truth for bugs and feature requests. Repo: `planyr` (product: **Planyr**).

> *"Single source of truth"* = the one file everyone trusts for what's done and what's left, so status never has to be tracked in anyone's head or in a chat thread.

---

## How this file works — Claude Code, read this first

- **On each run:** address every item under **🔲 Open**. Do **not** action anything under **🕓 Later / Roadmap** unless it's been moved up to Open. **⏳ Verify** items are already implemented and only awaiting a live check — they **park**, they never block a session (see the lifecycle below). Completed items live in `BACKLOG-DONE.md` — do not read it unless looking up a specific past item.
- **IDs are permanent.** The next B# = highest `B#` across **both** `BACKLOG.md` and `BACKLOG-DONE.md` + 1. Never renumber or reuse a number, even after items are done.
- **Items pasted from another chat are "blind" to this file** and may carry provisional `NEW-#` (or stale/colliding `B#`) labels — treat those as scratch references only and assign the real next `B#` when filing. When you file a chat item, add an **`Origin: filed <date> from chat`** line so its provisional `NEW-#` resolves to the real `B#` later.
- **Owner chat blocks are SHIP ORDERS (owner rule, 2026-07-15).** Filing a pasted item is step one, never the finish line: every chat-block item is **implement-in-this-session** work — file, ship, then park per the lifecycle. An item that genuinely can't ship this session (hard unshipped dependency / true blocker) is **flagged loudly in the session reply AND on the item**, never silently filed. A diagnosis/handoff doc arriving without a B# → **mint one on sight** (DEDUPE-FIRST still applies). Full text in `CLAUDE.md` → "Owner CHAT BLOCKS are SHIP ORDERS".
- **Before filing, DEDUPE-FIRST.** Search **Open, ⏳ Verify, AND Done** (`^### B` headings) before minting a `B#`. If an arriving report matches an existing item, do **NOT** create a new number — apply the **recurrence rule** below instead.
- **Bracket tags** like `[Site Planner]` mark the module. `(bug)` / `(feature)` / `(task)` marks the type. **`#tags`** (from the legend below) mark the theme — every Open / ⏳ Verify item carries one or more.
- **Always commit after editing this file or finishing a fix** — never leave the working tree dirty. A fix that isn't committed doesn't count as done.
- **Regenerate `BACKLOG_OPEN.md` in the SAME commit as any `BACKLOG.md` edit** (`node scripts/build-backlog-index.mjs`). It is the small, committed, chat-readable index of every Open/Verify item (B#, title, module, tags, Verify status) — **derived, never hand-edited**. CI runs `--check` and fails the build if it drifts from this file.
- **Never delete items.** Completed ones stay in `BACKLOG-DONE.md` as a record.
- **If an item is ambiguous,** don't guess. Mark it `[?]`, add your question inline, and leave it in Open.

### Item lifecycle — 🔲 Open → ⏳ Verify → ✅ Done (three states, B636)

Items no longer jump straight from Open to Done on a sandbox pass — live-only bugs (dependency arrows, export furniture sizing, …) kept boomeranging back. Every item carries a **`Verify:` field**:

- **`Verify: sandbox`** (the default) — a green build + the right unit/headless self-test is sufficient proof. On completion, move the whole block straight to `BACKLOG-DONE.md`.
- **`Verify: live`** — the fix can only be *confirmed* in the live app. **Mandatory `live` classes:** timing/race bugs · concurrency / multi-writer · GIS endpoint behavior · zoom- or data-density-dependent rendering · PDF / export parity · anything whose repro cites real project data. (This is the **LIVE-VERIFY** rule in `CLAUDE.md`.) After implementing, move the block to the **⏳ Verify** section with a dated note; it moves to Done **only after** a verification note is appended (date · method — Cowork or Michael on planyr.io · observed result). **Moving a `live` item straight to Done is a protocol violation.**

⏳ Verify items **park** — they never block a session; the session that implements one keeps going.

### Recurrence — a fix that didn't stick does NOT get a new number (B636)

When a new report matches an existing **Done or ⏳ Verify** item (search titles, tags, symbols): do **NOT** mint a new `B#`. **Move the original block back to 🔲 Open**, append a `Recurrence: <date> — <one-line report>` line, and add a visible count to the title, e.g. `(×3)`. Non-sticking fixes become visible on the one ID instead of scattering across new numbers.

### Theme tags (legend) — a tag may be used only if it appears here (B638)

## 🔲 Open

### B768160 — OCR scanned deed PDFs in the metes-and-bounds plotter `[Site Planner / land]` (feature) #site-planner #files  *(owner chat block 2026-08-25 — "i should be able to use a scanned legal description." A county-recorded deed is a scanned image almost by definition (the clerk scans the stamped instrument), so the plotter was refusing exactly the class of document it exists to read, working only on a pre-recording Word draft. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open/⏳Verify/Done for "OCR", "scanned", "tesseract", "deedOcr": no prior item. Net-new.)*
`[x]` Dropping a scanned PDF (no embedded text layer — `pdfText.js`'s "This PDF looks scanned" refusal) now runs client-side OCR (Tesseract.js, WASM, lazy-loaded — nothing leaves the browser except the fetch of the generic public English language model) automatically and pre-fills the SAME editable paste box with the read text, highlighting low-confidence tokens — it never plots from OCR output directly. Every other deed-text path (paste / .docx / .doc / a real-text-layer PDF) is byte-for-byte unchanged.
- Verify: live
- Blocker: real-data — the owner's actual scanned deed ("16 - Recorded Correction SWD.pdf", Chambers County) isn't attached to this session. Verified instead two ways: (a) against the owner's OWN measured facts from running stock Tesseract on that real deed directly (19/19 bearings recovered, one true character error — a doubled degree sign standing in for a minutes prime — plus two harmless word slips, "arc"→"are" and "to a"→"toa"), which this session built targeted, unit-tested repair rules for; (b) a synthetic degraded-scan fixture (skew, noise, dropped contrast, resample blur — harder than his clean 1-bit CCITT scan) driven end to end in headless Chromium against the real shipped pipeline (`ui-audit/verify-ocr-scanned-deed.mjs`) — see V425920 for the measured recovery rate. The remaining gap only his real file (or a live click-through on planyr.io) can close.
- **Architecture (new modules, all client-side, all lazy-loaded — nothing here rides the boot bundle):**
  - `src/shared/files/deedOcrRepair.js` — pure, Node-tested text repair (THENCE/COMMENCING/BEGINNING fuzzy correction, DMS punctuation normalization, quadrant-glyph VV→W / F→E repair scoped to a bearing token only, the doubled-degree-sign-is-a-misread-prime fix, "toa"/"are"→"arc" word-merge fixes, and `flagSuspectDistances` — a lost-decimal-point flag that is surfaced, never silently guessed at).
  - `src/shared/files/imagePreprocess.js` — pure pixel-array preprocessing (grayscale, local-mean adaptive threshold, skew estimation + deskew) Node-tested against synthetic arrays; `isEffectivelyBitonal` detects an already-black-and-white source (measured: the owner's real deed is a 1-bit CCITT-G4 scan) and skips the threshold pass entirely rather than risk fraying a clean edge.
  - `src/shared/files/pdfRaster.js` — browser-only PDF page → canvas render at ~300 DPI (a SEPARATE pdf.js setup from `pdfText.js`, which is text-extraction-only and needs none of the render assets).
  - `src/shared/files/ocrConfidence.js` — pure, Node-tested: locates each Tesseract word's confidence in the (possibly repaired) text, and `culpritCalls` correlates a bad closure with the specific courses most likely to blame (the closure safety net, item (f)).
  - `src/shared/files/deedOcr.js` — the orchestration (dynamic-imports `tesseract.js` + the above; per-page progress + `AbortSignal` cancellation; multi-page scan-all-and-concatenate with a per-page picker).
  - `src/workspaces/site-planner/components/OcrDeedTextarea.jsx` — the paste box with an optional low-confidence highlight overlay (a plain `<textarea>` when there's nothing to highlight — every non-OCR path is untouched).
  - `readDeeds`/`ocrScannedPdfInto` in `SitePlanner.jsx` wire it up: catch pdfText.js's new `.scanned` error flag, run OCR with a progress/cancel UI, and feed the SAME downstream call-parsing/closure code every other path already uses.
- **AUDIT-FIRST finding, per the owner's explicit ask ("go and check whether the EXISTING .docx and paste paths already mishandle these same constructs"):** the owner's real deed exercises non-tangent curves (radius/central-angle/arc/chord), "passing at … for a total distance of" governing-distance clauses, parenthetical offset notes, a monument "bears" tie call, a SAVE AND EXCEPT second tract, and a numbered "following N courses" sub-list. Built a construct-coverage fixture reproducing all of these (geometry-exact, closing to sub-foot tolerance — `test/deedRealDeedAudit.test.js`) and ran it through the REAL, already-shipped `deedParse.js` (used by every path, not just OCR): **all six constructs parse correctly and the boundary closes.** One real, pre-existing, unrelated bug WAS found and fixed: a SAVE AND EXCEPT tract's label picked up the ORIGINAL tract's acreage (the first-mentioned figure in its header prose, e.g. "out of the above described 94.53 acre tract a 12.584 acre tract…") instead of its own — cosmetic only (never affected the parsed geometry/closure), fixed by preferring the LAST acreage mention in the tract's own text over the first.
- Origin: filed 2026-08-25 from chat

### B758545 — Cloud tool PHASE 2: Markups List panel, threaded replies, tool presets `[Site Planner / markup]` (feature) #site-planner #markup #ui #export  *(owner chat block 2026-08-25, explicit PHASE 2 of the Cloud markup tool brief — filed as its own item per the brief's own instruction ("PHASE 2, file explicitly if not shipped") after PHASE 1 shipped this session as B758544. Minted **B758545** from this branch's reserved block B758544–B758559 against `origin/main` 825a7c0. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open/⏳Verify/Done for `Markups List`, `tool chest`, `tool preset`, `threaded repl`, `markup panel list`: no prior item — the shared markup engine (`shared/markup/`) has a `PropertyPanel` for ONE selected object at a time, nothing that lists every markup on the plan. Net-new.)*
`[ ]` Three sub-features, all deferred out of the PHASE 1 session as explicitly too large to ship alongside the draw/edit/style/metadata/z-order/PDF-parity work:
- Verify: live — PDF/export parity (the CSV/PDF summary table) and zoom-/data-density-dependent rendering (the panel row list) are both mandatory LIVE-VERIFY classes.
- **The Markups List** — a sortable, filterable, groupable panel (type, subject, author, date, colour swatch, comment, status) listing every markup on the plan (not just clouds — Bluebeam's own Markups List covers every annotation type, and this app's shared markup family already spans line/rect/ellipse/polygon/cloud/callout/text/measure). Clicking a row zooms to that markup (reuse the existing "zoom to feature" plumbing measurements/parcels already have). Exports to CSV and to a PDF summary table (reuses `exportSheet.js`'s document-composition path, never a second PDF pipeline). **The Review tab is its natural home** per the brief.
- **Threaded replies** — a markup (starting with Cloud, generalizable to any kind once the Markups List exists to display a thread) carries a reply thread: author + timestamp per reply, same shape as the metadata this session already added (`cloudMetaDefaults`'s author/createdAt pattern generalizes directly). Needs its own small data shape (`replies: [{id, author, text, createdAt}]`) and a compact panel UI — natural to build alongside the Markups List since a reply is what a list row expands into.
- **Tool presets (Bluebeam's Tool Chest)** — save a configured cloud (colour, weight, arc size, subject) as a reusable named tool, plus a recent-tools row. This session's `mkCloudStyle` sticky-style mechanism (kept deliberately separate from every other markup's shared `mkStyle` — see `MK_CLOUD_DEFAULT` in `SitePlanner.jsx`) is the natural seam: a preset is just a NAMED, PERSISTED snapshot of that same shape, plus a small picker UI. Store presets per-account (mirrors `userPrefs.js`'s account-level Standards store) so they follow the user across plans/devices, not just per-device localStorage.
- Depends on nothing PHASE 1 didn't already ship — the shared markup engine, the metadata fields, and the sticky-style seam are all in place; this is new UI + a new small data shape, not a prerequisite refactor.

### B758546 — Cloud tool PHASE 3: revision delta tag (numbered triangle), flatten-on-export, iPad touch drawing `[Site Planner / markup]` (feature) #site-planner #markup #ui #export #mobile  *(owner chat block 2026-08-25, explicit PHASE 3 of the Cloud markup tool brief — filed per the brief's own instruction ("PHASE 3, file explicitly"). Minted **B758546** from the same reserved block against `origin/main` 825a7c0. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open/⏳Verify/Done for `revision delta`, `revision triangle`, `flatten`, `Cloud+`, `pinch`, `#1149`: **#1149** (touch pinch-zoom on the canvas, cited by the brief itself as the precedent to respect) is a generic gesture fix, not cloud-specific drawing support — the brief explicitly says "respecting the native pinch handling shipped in #1149," i.e. don't break it, not that it already covers drawing. Net-new.)*
`[ ]` Three sub-features, all explicitly deferred as PHASE 3 by the owner's own brief (revision-set tooling, not core annotation):
- Verify: live — PDF/export parity (flatten-on-export) is a mandatory LIVE-VERIFY class; touch drawing needs a real iPad (`Blocker: real-data` — no touchscreen in this sandbox).
- **Revision delta tag** — the numbered triangle every drawing-set convention attaches to a cloud, standard on construction documents. Moves with the cloud (bond it the same way an inline label rides a line — see `inlineLabelEls`/`labelSpacing` precedent in `SitePlanner.jsx`), auto-increments per revision (needs a per-plan "current revision number" concept that does not exist yet — the closest analog is `Version history`'s device-local snapshot ring, a different mechanism), filterable and colour-codeable by revision number (natural fit for the PHASE 2 Markups List's filter/group UI once it exists — build this AFTER B758545, not before).
- **Flatten on export** — bake the delta tag (and arguably the cloud itself, if the export target is a static archival PDF rather than a working drawing) into the exported sheet as static ink rather than an editable object. `exportSheet.js` clones the live SVG (see B758544's PDF-PARITY note) so "flatten" here likely means: nothing extra for the cloud's own scalloped path (it's already plain SVG in the export, not a special editable widget), but the delta TAG's own future interactivity (if any) needs the same clone-not-rebuild discipline.
- **Touch drawing on iPad** — the three Cloud draw gestures (polygon click-path, rectangle drag, freehand drag) all need to work with a finger/Pencil, respecting the pinch-to-zoom gesture #1149 already shipped (two-finger pinch must not be captured as a one-finger cloud draw). No touch-specific code exists yet for ANY markup draw tool in this codebase (confirmed during PHASE 1 research — `touchCountRef.current >= 2` gates pinch, but single-finger draw gestures were never specifically tested on a touch device); this is a testing/hardening pass across every draw tool, not just Cloud, so scope it as a real iPad session before committing to "Cloud-only."
- Depends on B758545 (the delta tag's filter/colour-code UI is the Markups List's own filter mechanism, not a second one) for its first sub-feature only; flatten-on-export and touch drawing are independent and could ship first.

### B765984 — Remove the .json project-file export and import from the File menu `[Site Planner]` (task) #site-planner #ui  *(owner chat block 2026-08-25, verbatim: "get rid of the json print feature, no one should really be using that." Measured live on production: the File menu had exactly four items — Export project file (.json), Import project file… (.json, replaces the current canvas), Export PNG, Download PDF / pick frame…. Minted **B765984** from this branch's reserved block B765984–B765999 against `origin/main` 825611a1. **DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open/⏳Verify/Done for `exportJSON`, `importJSONFile`, `Export project file`, `Import project file`:** no prior removal item; B1042 verified this pair still worked post-lazy-load-split, which is the closest prior touch and is not a duplicate. Net-new.)*
`[x]` **SHIPPED — both the export and the import removed from the File menu; the underlying serialiser was audited and is NOT shared with any other path, so nothing else was touched.**
- Verify: sandbox
- **BOTH removed, not just export, and here's why the import mattered more.** The import's own tooltip admitted it "replaces the current canvas" with no confirmation dialog anywhere in its path — a destructive whole-plan overwrite one row below a harmless PNG download, in a project that has already had a real data-loss incident (57 of 95 elements wiped on a real plan, `BACKLOG-DONE.md`). An import with no way to produce its own input file is also just dead weight once export is gone. Removing this pair is a safety win, not only decluttering.
- **AUDITED FIRST, per the task's own instruction: is the serialiser shared with autosave / plan duplicate / templates / the Library?** No. `exportJSON` (in `lib/exportSheet.js`) built its own standalone `Blob` from the live collections and was called from nowhere but this menu button. `importJSONFile` (in `SitePlanner.jsx`) parsed a dropped file through `createSiteModel` — the SAME model funnel autosave/cloud-save/duplicate/Library all use — but it was the ONLY caller that fed it a user-picked file; autosave, `duplicatePlan`, and the Library's file browser all call `createSiteModel`/`storage.js` directly on already-in-memory or already-fetched data, never through this import path. So `createSiteModel` (the shared funnel) was left completely untouched — only the menu entries and their two dedicated functions were removed.
- **What was removed:** the two `<button>` menu items and the hidden `<input type="file">` in the File ▾ menu (`SitePlanner.jsx`); `importJSONFile` + its `importRef` (`SitePlanner.jsx`); the `exportJSON` wrapper (`SitePlanner.jsx`) and the underlying `exportJSON` function + its entry in the returned API (`lib/exportSheet.js`). Export PNG and Download PDF / pick frame… are untouched, same code, same position.
- **Housekeeping so nothing rots green:** removed the now-stale `exportJSON` row from `lib/hiddenContentReads.js`'s DECLARATIONS table (a declaration naming code that no longer exists fails `test/hiddenContentReads.test.js`'s "no declaration outlives its binding" check) and the two now-dead destructured bindings (`callouts`, `markups`) it left behind in `exportSheet.js`'s `ctx` destructure, which `test/deadStores.test.js` (B1128) caught as new computed-but-never-read values. Updated the historical audit comments in `test/kmzExport.test.js` and `test/opEnvelopeSeedCoverage.test.js` that named the removed functions, and dropped the removed feature's step from the live-verify harness `ui-audit/verify-b1042-export-lazy.mjs`.
- **Verified:** full unit suite green (12,552 tests; the 2 pre-existing failures — `hiddenContentReads.test.js`'s mutation check and `docReviewLayerVisibility.test.js`'s mutation check — are a shallow-git-clone artifact in this sandbox unrelated to this change, confirmed identical on the unmodified tree via `git stash`), lint 0 errors, build green.
- Files: `src/workspaces/site-planner/SitePlanner.jsx`, `src/workspaces/site-planner/lib/exportSheet.js`, `src/workspaces/site-planner/lib/hiddenContentReads.js`, `test/kmzExport.test.js`, `test/opEnvelopeSeedCoverage.test.js`, `ui-audit/verify-b1042-export-lazy.mjs`.

### B724256 — Audited: "Already in front of everything" is TRUE, not the reported forward-direction twin of B548064 `[Site Planner / markup]` (task) #site-planner #markup #testing  *(owner chat block 2026-08-25, arrived as a proven-false claim with production evidence — callout `e1454866xdbcen` on Richfield (`smsdrvzr9gzx`) at z=25,600, the max among the plan's 8 callouts, vs. buildings up to z=78,848 — and framed as "the message compares within the element's own TYPE BAND and describes the result as the whole drawing," an unfixed mirror of the B548064–B548066 Send-to-Back defect. Minted **B724256** from this branch's reserved block B724256–B724271 against `origin/main` 98cfd3e. **DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open/⏳Verify/Done for `arrangeAcrossBands`, `Already in front`, `Already behind`, `B548064`, `B548065`, `B548819`, `paintOrder`, `EL_BANDS`:** B548064–B548066/B548819 shipped `arrangeAcrossBands`/`arrangeBandFlags`, which already handle BOTH directions (front and back) symmetrically for all three annotation families — read in full, not re-derived. This item does not reopen them; it is the requested audit of a NEW claim against that code. Net-new.)*
`[x]` **AUDITED — the toast is CORRECT. No code defect found; a real test-coverage gap was closed instead.**
- Verify: sandbox
- **THE CLAIM, reproduced against real production data.** Pulled `e1454866xdbcen` and its 7 sibling callouts from Supabase (`lyeqzkuiwngunutlkkmi`, `site_elements` where `site_id='smsdrvzr9gzx'`): all 8 have `behindEls: null` (the "above" band, the default), and `e1454866xdbcen`'s z=25,600 is genuinely the max among them. Running the shipped `arrangeAcrossBands(callouts, id, "front")` on that exact data returns `null` — a true no-op — confirming the app's own logic, not just the message, agrees it is a no-op.
- **WHY IT IS STILL TRUE, not a lie: `paintOrder.js`'s ladder is RUNG-based, never a shared raw-z comparison across families.** A callout in the "above" band (rung 9) paints in a DOM group rendered unconditionally AFTER every element — `elements → …forced elements… → callouts(above)`, confirmed by reading the actual render order in `SitePlanner.jsx` (`drawElsZ.above` at line 21083, `calloutBands.above` at line 21379) — so it draws over EVERY element regardless of that element's raw `z`. The 78,848 vs. 25,600 comparison in the report treats `z` as one shared stacking coordinate across families; it is not, by design (z only orders peers within one family+band), and this is exactly the design B316864/B548819 already shipped and tested (`test/paintOrder.test.js`, `ui-audit/verify-paint-order-contract.mjs`).
- **LIVE-DRIVEN PROOF, not just a read of the code.** Ran `verify-paint-order-contract.mjs` against the real built app on the real Richfield fixture (`smsdrvzr9gzx`): `paint order observed, back to front: reference → parcel → element → markup → callout → measure`, `pairs: 30 observed · 0 FAILED · 0 unobserved`, `✅ PASS`. The callout family paints above the element family, full stop, on this exact plan.
- **WHAT WAS ACTUALLY MISSING, and the one real gap this item closes:** `test/arrangeAcrossBands.test.js` had six `"front"`-mode assertions against sixteen `"back"`-mode ones — the ORIGINAL fix (B548064–B548066) was implemented symmetrically but tested asymmetrically, which is exactly the shape that let a plausible-sounding "the forward direction was never covered" theory form. No new production code changed. Hardened `test/elementBandForce.test.js` instead (see B724257, which reuses the same audit) and left `arrange.js`/`arrangeAcrossBands.js` untouched — they were already correct.
- **AUDIT-FIRST discrepancy, stated plainly per house rule:** the task's framing does not match the code's behavior. Flagging rather than silently fixing a phantom bug — manufacturing a "fix" for correct code would be the actual defect.
- Files: none (audit only; no production code changed for this item — see B724257 for the test hardening this audit fed into).

### B724257 — A Bluebeam-style stack picker (Alt+click cycles the hit stack) + the missing "Force underneath everything" mirror `[Site Planner / selection]` (feature) #site-planner #selection #ui  *(owner chat block 2026-08-25, verbatim: "A 'force on top' affordance exists; there is no 'force underneath'." Concrete case: road `e1454053brxkkr` geometrically inside pond `e1454052brxkkr` on Richfield, unreachable because both are already at the bottom of their own type-layer band (B316864) so Send-to-Back has nowhere left to send either. Minted **B724257** from the same reserved block. **DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open/⏳Verify/Done for `stack picker`, `alt+click`, `force underneath`, `EL_BANDS`, `featureStack`, `featuresBeneath`, `B548065`:** B548065 built the annotation-specific "Behind this" menu (reach a markup/measure/callout sent behind an element) — this generalizes reaching ANY buried feature, of any kind, without requiring the covering object be selected first, and adds the element-band mirror B548065's own family never needed. Net-new.)*
`[x]` **SHIPPED — both halves. Verified live against the real Richfield plan (headless Chromium, logged out — no GIS/auth needed, per ATTEMPT-BEFORE-YOU-PARK).**
- Verify: sandbox — the mechanism is deterministic and fully unit-tested (`test/featureTarget.test.js`, `test/elementBandForce.test.js`); additionally driven live this session against the real dense Richfield fixture headlessly, so no signed-in click-through is owed. A short live check of the GESTURE ITSELF (does Alt+click feel discoverable/natural) is worth Michael's five minutes whenever convenient, but nothing is blocked on it.
- **THE PICKER.** Hold Alt and click: resolves to the TOP of the hit stack at that point, exactly like a plain click. Alt+click AGAIN at the same point (within a few px) steps one deeper — the object underneath, then the one under that — wrapping back to the top so it can never dead-end. Click anywhere else and the next Alt+click starts over at the top: this is a way to REACH something, not a mode you can leave engaged by accident. A brief flash names how many objects are stacked here ("2 of 3 here — Alt+click again to go deeper").
- **BUILT ON THE EXISTING RESOLVER, not a second hit-test.** `lib/featureTarget.js` already had `featureStack`/`stackEntries` (the exact primitive `resolveDoubleClickTarget` and the B548065 "Behind this" menu use) returning every feature under a point, top-most first, chrome/handles skipped, deduped. Added `stackAtPoint` (a thin composition of those two) and `nextPickIndex` (the pure cycle rule — same-point-within-tolerance advances and wraps, anything else resets to 0). Wired via `handleStackPick` into the SVG root's EXISTING capture-phase press handler (the same one `notePress`/the double-click anchor already use), because a capture-phase listener is what lets the picker win over whichever feature's own bubble-phase pointerdown would otherwise take the press first.
- **THE BAND-VS-Z FIX: `EL_BANDS.back = -100`, the mirror of the existing `EL_BANDS.front = 100`.** An element's right-click menu now offers **"Force on top of everything"** and **"Force underneath everything"** (collapsing to one "Use the normal layer order" row once either is set, per PANEL-BREVITY — never three rows at once). `zOrder`/`drawElsZ`/`arrangePeers` needed NO changes beyond the one constant: `zOrder` already resolves `bandForce` generically, and `drawElsZ` already splits on a plain `zOrder(el) < BUILDING_Z` threshold sorted ascending, so `-100` falls into the "below" half and sorts first there (bottom of the whole drawing) for free, exactly as `100` already fell into "above" and sorted last.
- **PROVEN LIVE, not just in a pure-function test.** Seeded a pond geometrically containing a road on the real Richfield fixture (124-element dense plan) and drove real pointer events against the real built app: a plain click resolved to whichever real fixture element already painted topmost there; Alt+click same point → same top; Alt+click again → the seeded pond; Alt+click again → the seeded ROAD underneath it; Alt+click again → wrapped back to the top. Separately, forcing the pond's band to `"back"` and clicking a point covered by the pond's body but not its area label: a PLAIN click now resolves directly to the road, no picker needed.
- **ONE NUANCE FOUND AND NOT FIXED, named rather than silently left:** an element's LABEL/dimension chrome renders in a pass that does not individually respect that element's own forced band (verified by planting the road directly under the pond's centered area-label anchor — the label still won the plain click even with the pond forced back; offsetting the road away from the label's anchor made the plain click resolve correctly). This is pre-existing label-layout behavior (labels declutter globally, not per-object z), out of scope for this item, and does not affect the picker (which still reaches the correct feature by identity regardless of which sub-node was hit) or the common case (a body-vs-body occlusion, the reported one).
- **CHROME-NEVER-EATS-A-PRESS respected:** the picker only engages on a plain Alt+click (no Shift/Ctrl/⌘ — those are already claimed by vertex-insert and other gestures) in the select tool, and falls through to the ordinary background press untouched when nothing is under the cursor.
- Files: `src/workspaces/site-planner/lib/featureTarget.js` (`stackAtPoint`, `nextPickIndex`, `PICK_SAME_POINT_PX`), `src/workspaces/site-planner/lib/planStyle.js` (`EL_BANDS.back`), `src/workspaces/site-planner/SitePlanner.jsx` (`handleStackPick`, `stackPickRef`, the capture-phase wiring, the two-row Arrange-menu escape hatch, the inspector's forced-band note). Tests: `test/featureTarget.test.js` (+15), `test/elementBandForce.test.js` (+7, symmetric to the existing "front" suite).

### B724259 — Keyboard shortcuts could be swallowed by a component's own `stopPropagation()`, outside the app's one keyboard router `[Site Planner / keyboard]` (bug) #site-planner #keyboard #selection  *(owner chat block 2026-08-25: "Keyboard undo does nothing on some plans while the toolbar Undo button works, and a Delete keypress was reported landing in a text box the owner was not typing in." The referenced project doc (`claude/finding-2026-08-20-keyboard-shortcuts-route-by-dom-focus-not-selection-three-symptoms-one-cause.md`) could not be located in this repo, its git history, or the connected Google Drive — this item's diagnosis is this session's own independent AUDIT-FIRST investigation, not a confirmation of that doc's specific claim. Minted **B724259** from the same reserved block. **DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open/⏳Verify/Done for `keyScope`, `keyContract`, `stopPropagation`, `B464048`, `B3296`, `B3297`:** B464048–B464050/B3296/B3297 (2026-08-17) already shipped a thorough DOM-focus-vs-canvas-intent router (`shared/keyboard/keyScope.js` + `site-planner/lib/keyContract.js`) that this item does NOT reopen — read in full; Ctrl+Z/Redo/Escape are already `scope:"app"` and already survive every chrome/latch state except a literal focused text field, by design. This item is a DIFFERENT, narrower defect: four components bypassed that router entirely. Net-new.)*
`[x]` **SHIPPED and headlessly proven live this session — closed the bypass; the router (already shipped, already correct) is now the ONLY keyboard-routing decision in the site-planner workspace.**
- Verify: sandbox — per ATTEMPT-BEFORE-YOU-PARK, drove the exact reported sequence headlessly (logged out, no GIS/auth needed) rather than parking it for a signed-in pass; see the live proof below.
- **AUDIT-FIRST: what the missing doc's title claims ("routes by DOM focus rather than canvas selection") is not what the shipped B464048 system does** — it already routes by a LATCH tracking the user's last real canvas-vs-chrome touch, not by raw focus, and undo/redo are already `scope:"app"` (always allowed except while literally typing in a text field). Rather than re-diagnose a fix that was already shipped and independently verified 56/56 in `test/keyContract.test.js`, this session searched for a DIFFERENT way the reported symptom could still occur despite that system.
- **THE FOUND DEFECT: four `onKeyDown` handlers called `e.stopPropagation()` UNCONDITIONALLY, before checking which key was pressed** — `ParcelRecordPanel.jsx`'s two record fields, `SetLocationDialog.jsx`'s address search box, the "Add by address" field, and — the one that matters most, because it is the single most-used free-text control on the canvas — the callout/text-box editor (every plan with any callout or text box reaches it). A `window`-level bubble-phase listener (the planner's `onKey`, where keyScope/keyContract actually live) never sees a key stopped upstream, for ANY reason, whatever the shared router would have decided. That is a SECOND, undocumented, per-component keyboard-routing decision — exactly the "routes around the one place this app decides who owns the keyboard" failure mode named in the task, even though the specific missing-doc diagnosis could not be confirmed.
- **THE FIX IS THE SAME SHAPE IN ALL FOUR PLACES: stop only the key(s) the component actually answers itself** (Enter to commit, Escape to cancel/revert, Alt+Z to autosize) **and let everything else bubble.** This is safe by construction, not by luck: `keyScope`'s FIELD scope already refuses every plan-mutating shortcut while a text control is genuinely focused (`keyScopeVerdict`'s `if (scope === SCOPE.FIELD) return { allow: false, … }` — checked BEFORE the "app"-scope carve-out, so even Ctrl+Z stays correctly blocked while truly typing), so nothing here needed a second copy of that rule. The only behavior this changes is the case where one of these controls holds focus PAST the point a shortcut is pressed — which is exactly the class of bug B464048 exists to close, arriving through a door that system could not see because the event never reached it.
- **LIVE PROOF, driven headless against the real running app on a fresh "Start blank" plan (no sign-in, no GIS):** drew a building, moved it (one canvas action), then armed the Callout tool, placed one, typed "hello world" — and, critically, clicked DIRECTLY ON THE BUILDING to select it, never pressing Enter or Escape (the exact "believes he's left the box" sequence from the report). Confirmed `document.activeElement` moved to `BODY` (not the textarea) and the callout's `<textarea>` unmounted. Pressed Ctrl+Z **once**: the callout ("hello world") was removed from the canvas — proof the keystroke reached the app's global undo instead of being silently absorbed by the (no-longer-focused, but formerly `stopPropagation`-guarded) callout editor. Before this fix, the same sequence would have left that keystroke unable to even reach the window listener.
- **MACHINE-ENFORCED so it cannot regress:** `test/keyContract.test.js` gained a source sweep (`BANNED` regex) over the whole site-planner workspace that fails the build if `onKeyDown={...}` ever again calls `stopPropagation()` before its first `if`, plus a mutation-proof (the exact pre-fix shape is asserted to MATCH the banned pattern, so the guard is proven to bite before proving the fix clears it).
- **NOT CLAIMED:** this may not be the exact mechanism the referenced (unlocated) finding doc describes — flagged per AUDIT-FIRST rather than silently assumed. `doc-review/DocReview.jsx` and `workspaces/notes/Notes.jsx` carry the same blanket-`stopPropagation` smell (found while sweeping) but are a DIFFERENT workspace and out of scope for this Site-Planner-scoped report; noted here rather than silently left, not fixed in this item. The Parcel-Record-field variant of the same sequence (type an acreage value, click a building, press Delete) was not separately re-driven live — the mechanism is identical and the same source guard covers it, but it is worth a five-minute spot-check if this ever resurfaces.
- Files: `src/workspaces/site-planner/components/ParcelRecordPanel.jsx`, `src/workspaces/site-planner/components/SetLocationDialog.jsx`, `src/workspaces/site-planner/SitePlanner.jsx` (the callout editor + the "Add by address" field). Tests: `test/keyContract.test.js` (+3, one proven red against the exact pre-fix shape).

### B647392 — `verify-schedule-row-move.mjs` check I (zero re-render during a drag) has NO discriminating mutation `[Schedule]` (task) #scheduler #testing #selection  *(self-discovered during the B646272 close-out audit, on the owner's direct question "of the 20 checks, how many have a mutation proven to turn them red — name the ones that do not." Minted **B647392** from this branch's reserved block B647392–B647407 against `origin/main` 7c5fb69c. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open / ⏳ Verify / Done for `verify-schedule-row-move`, `check I`, `zero re-render`, `MutationObserver`, `childList`: no prior item; B646272 shipped the harness this gap is IN, and did not itself notice the gap. Net-new.)*
- Verify: sandbox
- **THE GAP, stated exactly, not rounded up.** `ui-audit/verify-schedule-row-move.mjs` check I asserts that dragging a row across a ~540-row fixture (auto-scroll engaged) produces zero `childList` DOM mutations on the rows container — i.e. the row list is never re-rendered mid-drag. That measurement is real and was taken correctly. But `grep -c "await runMutation" ui-audit/verify-schedule-row-move.mjs` returns **8**, covering checks A through H only — there is no `runMutation("I", ...)` call anywhere in the file. Nothing proves this check would go red if a future edit reintroduced a per-mousemove `setData`/re-render. **That makes it a one-time measurement wearing the costume of a check — defensive code, not a check**, per the standing instruction that a check which never goes red must be called that rather than counted.
- **THE INTENDED FIX IS ALREADY KNOWN — don't re-derive it.** The B646272 session's own plan was to reuse mutation F's scenario (wiring `moveRows` into the per-frame paint loop, `computeAndPaint`/`onMove`, instead of only `onUp` — the exact B1121-shaped regression mutation F already constructs) and additionally assert against the SAME mutated build that the `MutationObserver` on the ~540-row fixture now reports `childList > 0`. That verification was planned, never wired in, and the gap shipped anyway. Whoever picks this up should extend `runMutation("F", ...)` (or add a sibling `runMutation("I", ...)` sharing the same needle/replacement) to also run check I's MutationObserver assertion against the mutated build and confirm it flips red.
- **ADJACENT, RECORDED HERE SO IT ISN'T RE-DISCOVERED THE HARD WAY:** the predecessor-LIVENESS claim for a moved task (does a cross-parent move keep the link genuinely driving the date, not just coincidentally unchanged) is **still unmeasured**. A same-session attempt at this test edited the moved task's OWN duration after the move to see if a downstream successor's date would shift — but by that point in the fixture the moved task had already become a PARENT (gained children from an earlier step in the same script), so the edit silently no-op'd against the pre-existing parent-date-lock guard (`isParentDateLocked`), and "before equals after" would have been reported as proof of liveness when it was actually proof that nothing happened at all. **The correct construction edits a LEAF's duration** (a task with no children, so the cell is genuinely editable) that a downstream task's date depends on, post-move, and confirms the downstream date actually shifts. Not yet built.
- **ALSO UNCHARACTERIZED: moving a task to a row position ABOVE its own predecessor.** One ad hoc, unmutated live check (not part of the shipped harness) moved a successor above its FS predecessor and observed the date stayed correctly derived (schedule computation is dependency-graph-driven, not row-order-driven, so this is not expected to be a data problem) with no visible warning indicator anywhere in the UI. That single observation was never turned into an asserted, repeatable check, and no search was done for whether this app has ANY "out-of-sequence dependency" warning mechanism that should be firing here and isn't. Undefined until someone actually characterizes it.

### B647393 — No NAMED regression check asserts row-range-select still works after the B646272 drag-grip change `[Schedule]` (task) #scheduler #testing #selection  *(self-discovered during the B646272 close-out audit, on the owner's direct observation that his drag-grip regression "matters more than it sounds" since row-range-select is a feature he has complained about twice in the last week. Minted **B647393** from the same reserved block against `origin/main` 7c5fb69c. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open / ⏳ Verify / Done for `rowRangeSelIds`, `range-select`, `dragAnchor`, `rowgrip`, `B463921`, `B646272`: **B463921** is a DIFFERENT mechanism (a floating menu leaking a press into the grid underneath it) and is closed; this is about the ID-column drag-select gesture itself, which B463921 never touched. Net-new.)*
- Verify: sandbox
- **THE SHAPE OF THE RISK, not just the gap.** During B646272 (shipped), the drag-and-drop row-move feature's first implementation gave its grip handle `inset:0` over the FULL id cell with `pointer-events` gated on CSS `:hover` — and because `:hover` is true for the entire duration of a mousedown (the cursor must already be over an element to press it), that silently ate every ordinary mousedown in the ID column, breaking the pre-existing row-range-select drag outright. It was caught and fixed in the same session (final geometry: an 8px permanently-interactive strip at the cell's left edge, `pointer-events` never gated) — but **the only reason it was caught is that a developer happened to build an ad hoc diagnostic script to chase down an unrelated multi-row-move test failure.** Nothing in the shipped, checked-in test suite would have caught it on its own.
- **WHAT EXISTS TODAY, PRECISELY.** `ui-audit/verify-schedule-row-move.mjs` check D (and its mutation) both call a `selectRowRange` helper that depends on the ID-column drag-select gesture working correctly — so if range-select broke again, check D would very likely fail too, as a SIDE EFFECT. But there is no check under its own name asserting "a real mouse drag across two ID cells produces a genuine multi-row `selRange`" — the property is only ever exercised as a precondition of a check about something else. A future refactor of check D (or a rewrite that stops using `selectRowRange`) would quietly stop covering this at all, with nothing to notice.
- **WHAT "CLOSING" THIS MEANS.** Add a small, standalone, named check (and its own mutation — e.g. temporarily reintroducing a `pointer-events:auto` full-cell overlay, or reverting the grip to `inset:0`) that asserts the range badge and the selected-range background color appear after a real two-row ID-column drag, independent of anything else in the file. The diagnostic technique already exists and worked (`document.body.innerText` for the "N × M" badge text, `getComputedStyle(...).backgroundColor` on the ID cells for the `rgb(219, 234, 254)` selected-range color) — it just was never turned into a permanent, named assertion.

- **THE GAP, stated as the weaker truth, not the comfortable one.** `ui-audit/verify-successor-complete.mjs` — Sections A/B/C (the original 27 checks) and Section D (the seven-width sweep + 2 mutation proofs added in B605840, 102 checks total) — is **not invoked anywhere in `.github/workflows/build.yml`**. Neither is the pre-existing A3 pixel-equality check. The dialog EXISTS in a permanently-checkable state, but the check is **not enforced** — it only runs when a person, or a future Claude session, types `npm run verify:successorcomplete`. A regression here (buttons going unequal, the footer overflowing at a narrow width, the interaction silently breaking) would ship, deploy, and stay broken indefinitely with every other CI check green, until someone happens to run this script by hand.

This item is filed narrowly against the one harness just extended, not as a mandate to wire the whole suite into CI — that would be a real headless-Chromium-in-CI infrastructure decision (cost, runtime, flakiness surface) worth its own item if picked up, not an incidental fix.
- **What "closing" this would mean, so it's actionable rather than just documented:** either add a CI job that runs `verify-successor-complete.mjs` (accepting the real-Chromium-in-CI cost for this one dialog), or accept the gap explicitly and say so in this file rather than let a "permanent check" read as a "permanent guarantee."

### B603841 — MasterView's health-cell renderer has no `|| HEALTH.gray` fallback (crashes on an unknown health key) `[Scheduler]` (bug) #scheduler #ui  *(self-discovered 2026-08-17 while mutation-testing B603840's Automatic-clear guard — NOT an owner report. `🔲` **Open — found, filed, NOT fixed (out of scope for the item that found it, per its own "smallest correct change" brief).**
- Verify: sandbox
- **THE DEFECT.** MasterView's `renderCell`, case `"health"`, reads `const h = HEALTH[dispHealth];` with no fallback — every OTHER `HEALTH[...]` lookup in this file guards it (`HEALTH[value] || HEALTH.gray`). If `dispHealth` is ever a key `HEALTH` doesn't recognize, `h` is `undefined` and the very next line (`h.dot`) throws, taking down MasterView's whole render (caught by the app's `ErrorBoundary`, so the failure is a broken Dashboard tab, not a blank page — still a real crash).
- **HOW IT WAS FOUND — and this is the ONLY confirmed trigger.** A deliberately-broken build (testing B603840, `--mutate-automatic-grid`) let the internal sentinel string `"__auto__"` leak into a task's stored `.health` field — something the real, unmutated code can never do (the sentinel is always intercepted before it reaches storage). This trigger is NOT reachable in production; it exists only inside that mutation test.
- ~~**THE REAL, REACHABLE TRIGGER:** a task holding a CUSTOM health status (`data.settings.customHealth`) that the user later renames or deletes from Standards. `HEALTH` is rebuilt from `customHealth` on every settings change (`rebuildHEALTH`); a task's stored `.health` is not migrated when a custom status disappears, so any task still carrying the old key would hit this exact crash the next time MasterView renders it.~~
- **⛔ CORRECTION (2026-08-17, same day, before this item was ever picked up) — the struck claim above is WRONG and was filed without checking the deletion code first.** The delete-a-custom-status path is **already guarded**: `removeOption` (`public/sequence/index.html` ~line 8246) reassigns every task still carrying the status being deleted to `"gray"` **before** removing it from `customHealth`, specifically to prevent this exact crash — its own comment says so verbatim (`"...so no view dereferences a now-missing HEALTH key and crashes (B1)"`). So that is not the reachable path either. **No genuinely reachable real-product trigger has been found, and none has been ruled out — this is UNPROVEN in both directions.** Recommendation: leave filed, do NOT dispatch, until someone actually finds a real path in (a multi-device/sync race around a status deletion is the one untested candidate, not confirmed).
- **STOPPING RULE:** closes when MasterView's health-cell lookup guards the same way every other `HEALTH[...]` read in this file already does (`HEALTH[dispHealth] || HEALTH.gray`) — that fix is cheap and safe regardless of whether a real trigger is ever found — **or** when a genuinely reachable real-product trigger is found and confirmed, whichever comes first. A repro via `removeOption`'s delete path is NOT a valid closing test (see correction above); anyone attempting one will find it already passes for the wrong reason.

### B820 (×2) — RE-OPENED: "Send to Back" silently does half the job against a BUILDING, then greys itself out as if it worked `[Site Planner / markup]` (bug) #site-planner #markup #selection #ui  *(Recurrence: 2026-08-14 — the owner has reported "send to back / layers never work" SIX times and it has been "fixed" FOUR times (B421, B820, B671, B293072/B293073). **Every one of those fixes was correct and every one tested MARKUP AGAINST MARKUP, which already worked.** Nobody pointed a markup at a BUILDING and pressed the command he would actually press. Per DEDUPE-FIRST this re-opens THIS number — B820 is the item that shipped this very menu — rather than taking a new one.)*
`[ ]` **REPRODUCED AND RED-PROVEN, driven on the owner's Richfield plan with an opaque markup over building `e1454886kaaymz` (`ui-audit/diagnose-band-ordering.mjs`):**

    stack BEFORE  markup:zzM1 → el:e1454886kaaymz      (markup above the building)
    Send to Back  clicked, ran, reported success
    stack AFTER   markup:zzM1 → el:e1454886kaaymz      IDENTICAL — nothing moved
    menu BEFORE   Send Backward ENABLED   · Send to Back ENABLED
    menu AFTER    Send Backward DISABLED  · Send to Back DISABLED

- **THE CAUSE.** `arrangePeers` scopes the peer set to same-family-same-band (`markups.filter(m => (m.behindEls === true) === (t.behindEls === true))`), so the command reaches the bottom of the MARKUP layer and `arrangeFlags` then correctly reports `atBottom` — of a band the user cannot see. **This is a LOUD-FAILURE violation of the worst kind: not silence, but a confident report of success for a DIFFERENT operation than the one requested.**
- **⛔ THE MEASUREMENT HALF OF THE REPORT DID NOT REPRODUCE, and the design must not be built on it.** It was reported that an area measurement drawn over an opaque markup "vanished completely" and that nothing can bring it forward. Driven on the same plan with TWO deliberately opaque markups over a building: the family paint order back-to-front is **`parcel → el → markup → callout → measure`**, so a measurement is TOPMOST of the four by construction, and its outline, its edge labels and its acreage chip all render clearly over both markups (screenshot in the run). A measurement therefore cannot fall behind a markup by default, and its cross-band toggle is a REVERSIBLE pair ("Send behind the plan" / "Bring above the plan"), so a forward command does exist — it is simply not offered while the measurement is already in front. **The one state that would produce the reported symptom is a measurement previously sent behind the plan; that is an open question with the owner and must not be guessed.**
- **⛔ CONFIRMED AND SEPARATE: ONE CONCEPT, TWO VOCABULARIES.** The markup menu says **"Send behind buildings"**; the measurement and callout menus say **"Send behind the plan"**. Both observed in the same run, minutes apart. This is exactly the parity drift **B293072** was built to kill, and it survived because `e2e/elementCapabilities.table.js` declares `crossBand: "yes"` for every type — a cell that any escape hatch satisfies REGARDLESS of what it is called or which direction it travels. The table needs to declare the cross-band CONTRACT (name + both directions), not merely its existence.
- **⚠ FOUND WHILE DRIVING, not in the report: a measurement's LABEL CHIP eats presses aimed at a markup underneath it.** The chip is far wider than the measurement itself and answers `elementsFromPoint` well outside it; a right-click aimed at a markup opened the MEASUREMENT's menu. That is CHROME-NEVER-EATS-A-PRESS in the wild and is adjacent to the reported "cannot right-click a markup back" case.
- **⛔ NOT YET FIXED, deliberately.** The brief's design instruction is to write the ordering CONTRACT across every pair of types as committed data and render the menus from it — and one of the three band-pair behaviours it was to be built around does not exist. Designing the contract around a refuted premise is the exact failure this item is made of. **Blocked on one owner question:** should a measurement ALWAYS outrank decoration, or may it be tucked under a callout deliberately? The contract is a one-line change either way, which is why it is worth waiting for rather than guessing.
- **Instrument:** `ui-audit/diagnose-band-ordering.mjs` — drives the PAIRS rather than the family (markup↔markup as the control, markup↔building, measure↔markup, callout↔markup), and measures what PAINTS, what a right-click RESOLVES to, and what the commands actually DO. It never accepts "the z changed" as evidence; the paint order has to move.
- Verify: live
- Origin: filed 2026-08-14 from chat

- **PRIOR RECORD — the original B820 entry, kept verbatim so the four-correct-fixes history is not lost:**
  `[x]` **IMPLEMENTED — the whole job.** Net-new for Site Planner *elements* (B421 = Doc Review markups, B461 = overlays only, B671 = the z plumbing). New pure engine `lib/arrange.js` (`reorderByZ`/`arrangeFlags`/`ARRANGE_MODES`) computes a minimal `{id→z}` patch over a PEER SET, reusing the B671 `zOrder.js` z field + `Z_GAP`/`nextZ`/`normalizeZ`. Elements reorder WITHIN their `Z_LAYER` type-band (planStyle `zOrder`) so the guardrail holds — a building can never drop under a road/parking; markups reorder within the markup layer. Wiring in `SitePlanner.jsx`: `arrangeSel(mode, target)` (pushHistory + per-kind setter — undoable; dual-write persists via the existing blob + `site_elements.z_index`), the element right-click menu gains an **Arrange** section, the markup right-click menu gains the four ops + a **Send behind buildings / Bring in front of buildings** toggle (new additive `behindEls` markup flag, group-aware for a deed + its exceptions), and the `onKey` handler gains ⌘/Ctrl+] (forward, ⇧=front) / ⌘/Ctrl+[ (backward, ⇧=back) via `e.code`. Render: the markup layer now paints in z order (`byZAsc`) split into a BEHIND-els pass + a front pass; new markups get `nextZ` on creation (`withStackZ`) so a freshly-drawn markup still lands on top. Hit-testing is native SVG DOM order, so it follows the new paint order for free. PDF/print export clones the live SVG (`buildExportSvg`), so z-order + behind-buildings carry into exports with no separate change (PDF-PARITY).
  - Verify: live → **V309** (signed-in cloud `z_index` round-trip survives a reload; a PDF/print export visually reflects the new stacking + a behind-buildings markup)
  - Origin: filed 2026-07-13 from chat.
  - Sandbox: 16 unit tests `test/sitePlannerArrange.test.js` (four modes, no-op at ends, band isolation, minimal-patch, ambiguous-z repair, no mutation); headless `ui-audit/verify-b820-arrange.mjs` (12 checks, all green: keyboard front/back reorders buildings, right-click Arrange menu, band isolation vs parking, send-behind-buildings moves the markup below the elements + persists to localStorage + survives reload). Full suite + build green, lint 0 errors.

### B540768 — Split lineage: the invariant is EXACTLY ONE ACTIVE GENERATION, and the rule as requested would have failed correct data `[Site Planner]` (bug) #site-planner #parcel #testing  *(owner audit block 2026-08-13, arrived as the "fourth case" alongside a counting trap. Minted **B540768** from this branch's reserved block B540768–B540783 against `origin/main` f0213ff. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open / ⏳ Verify / Done across `split`, `parentId`, `lineage`, `active`, `B651`, `B472049`, `B280704`, `parcelSplit`, `supersede`: **B651** built the mutual-exclusion guard this vindicates and is NOT re-opened — it is working; **B472049** (merged #1031) stops NEW splits leaving a drawn parent and audits ONE split at the moment it happens. Neither looks at a plan's lineage AT REST, which is the orientation here. Net-new.)*
`[ ]` **`lib/splitIntegrity.js` — `lineageAudit` / `ancestorChain` / `parentCycles`; `test/splitIntegrity.test.js` +13 (33 total), two mutation checks.**
- **⛔ THE ASSERTION AS REQUESTED IS REFUTED, AND THAT IS THE FINDING.** The ask was *"a parent with live children must NOT be active, and a split's children must not ALL be inactive. Assert both directions."* The second half **fires on correct data on his own live plan**, so shipping it would have reported a working feature as a defect.
- **RICHEY / Concept A (`smrdl6frtt6r`) is NOT an inverted split and needs NO cleanup.** Rows: `psmrdl6frtt6r_2` active=TRUE 7.874 ac · `e666fqvqmq` active=false 6.606 ac · `e667fqvqmq` active=false 1.268 ac; 6.606 + 1.268 = 7.874, residual −0.0002 ac, **all three written at one identical microsecond** (2026-07-13 15:48:35.91822+00). That is `toggleParcelActive` — **B651's mutual-exclusion guard** — doing exactly its job: turning a parcel back ON deactivates its ancestors AND descendants in the SAME `setParcels` call, which is why one action yields one flush and three rows sharing a microsecond.
- **THE ROWS SAY WHICH PATH WROTE THEM.** The parent carries an **explicit `active:true`**, and the tree has exactly two writers of that value — the Active toggle (`SitePlanner.jsx:10641`) and a split's own CHILDREN (`:6600`). A split's PARENT is only ever written `active:false`. So this was a deliberate user action, not the split tool, and not an undo (an undo restoring the pre-split snapshot would have minted DELETES for the children; they are not deleted).
- **⛔ AND THE STATED RISK IS REFUTED BY THE SAME GUARD:** *"the moment anyone toggles those children on, RICHEY double-counts by 7.874 ac."* It cannot — turning a child ON runs `lineageConflicts` and switches the parent OFF in the same update. **Swept across the whole account: ZERO lineages have an active ancestor and an active descendant.**
- **SO THE INVARIANT IS ABOUT GENERATIONS, NOT ABOUT PARENTS.** Along any ancestor chain exactly one member may be active: **more than one is a DOUBLE COUNT** (the failure that costs a number), **zero is VANISHED LAND** (geometry held, ground counted nowhere). Both directions asserted. WHICH member is active is the owner's business and is a defect in neither direction.
- **⛔ THE COUNTING TRAP, which would have been destructive.** Nineteen parcels across eight plans carry `active:false`; only **three** have live descendants. The other sixteen are parcels deliberately excluded from the active set — same flag, opposite meaning — on plans in daily use. `supersededParents` is therefore `active:false` **AND at least one live descendant**, and nothing else may drive a cleanup. Mutation-proven: keying on `active:false` alone turns two tests red.
- **A TWO-LEVEL CHAIN IS ONE LINEAGE.** Bain / Concept A - Quiddity DIA is `e1454855gyzzln` (off) → `e1455071mkspvo` (off) → `e1455075mkspvo` (ON) — **one chain with one active member, correct.** A parent-keyed grouping splits it in two and manufactures a false "no active member" finding; the audit walks to the maximal TREE instead. Mutation-proven: an immediate-parent-only walk misses a grandparent double count.
- **CYCLE-SAFE BY CONSTRUCTION** — a `parentId` cycle is reported, never walked. None exists in production; a hung planner is worse than a finding.
- **THE ACCOUNT-WIDE RESULT, measured 2026-08-13 against `planyr_production`:** three multi-member lineages exist (4050 CR 50 JOHNSTOWN / Concept A · Bain / Concept A - Quiddity DIA · RICHEY / Concept A) and **all three carry exactly one active member.** Zero double counts, zero vanished lineages, zero cycles. ⚠ A fourth apparent case (Woods Road, one id in two trees) is an artefact of grouping by plan NAME — two distinct plans are both called "Concept A PRINT" — not a data defect.
- **NO CLEANUP IS PROPOSED OR RUN.** The only remaining leftover is cosmetic: **two** superseded parents still drawing (both on Bain, one chain), not three — RICHEY is not one of them, and 4050 CR 50's parent is a legitimate superseded parent whose sibling piece the owner switched off himself. Automated repair of live data remains unauthorised.
- Verify: sandbox — pure module, 33 tests, both invariants mutation-proven.

### B500576 — Group CAS: three more ways one bad bet refused every save on a building, found by a second ordinary hour — and the flag is now ON `[Site Planner / persistence]` (bug, DATA LOSS) #site-planner #sync #testing  *(owner instruction 2026-08-13: re-run the trial hour on the fixed build and flip it on if quiet, with the prefix-pair case covered rather than missed. Minted **B500576** from this branch's reserved block B500576–B500591 against `origin/main` 1da150a. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open / ⏳ Verify / Done across `groupsFor`, `assemblyOf`, `groupConflict`, `assemblyDigest`, `attachedTo`, `rootIdOf`, `B1341`, `B484336`, `B447472`, `B1117`, `B1124`, `bondRemap`: **B484336** is ORDERING and **B447472** is MEMBERSHIP-BY-KIND — both are the digest disagreeing on the same member set; these three are the client claiming the WRONG SET, which no prior item covers. **B1124/bondRemap** is `attachedTo` remapping on COPY, a different path. **Net-new.**)*
`[x]` **SHIPPED, and the build flag is flipped ON for everyone.**
- Verify: sandbox — 20 seeded ordinary hours through the real write engine, each fix mutation-proven red when reverted, plus discriminating unit tests.
- Origin: filed 2026-08-13 from the owner's chat instruction.
- **⛔ THE ARGUMENT FOR DRIVING ORDINARY EDITING RATHER THAN A TARGETED REPRO, in one line: a
  re-bond produced 865 SPURIOUS REFUSALS ON THE CLEAN BUILD — a third distinct cause the first trial
  hour never reached, for one reason only, that the first run never performed that action shape.**
  No amount of re-reading the code found it; adding the gesture found it in one run. A repro can only
  ever confirm a defect someone already suspects.
- **THE ROOT CAUSE IN PLAIN TERMS.** The expected digest was built from the CANVAS's bonding rather
  than the SERVER's, so this tab's belief about which assembly a row belongs to can go stale while
  its revision is current — and a refusal does not teach it otherwise. One variant is a genuine
  **DEADLOCK**: a conflict naming an EMPTY assembly carries no members, so it teaches the client
  nothing at all and the identical wrong claim is re-derived forever.
- **WHAT `expected` IS A CLAIM ABOUT, which is the one idea behind all three.** It says *"refuse me unless this assembly is STILL exactly this"* — a statement about the **server's** current state. The canvas holds the state we are trying to **create**. Those coincide for a move, a resize or a delete and diverge for exactly one ordinary gesture: **re-bonding a child to a different host** (indent/outdent), the only edit that touches `attachedTo`, which is the generated `assembly_id`'s sole input.
- **THE THREE, each proven necessary by reverting it:**
  1. **Membership was read off the CANVAS.** A pending re-bond put the mover in its DESTINATION's expected digest while the server still had it in the SOURCE — two digests wrong in opposite directions, call refused whole, retry re-derived the identical wrong claim from the same unchanged canvas. **383 refusals, 865 spurious, 50 of 433 calls applied.** Fixed: bucket by the SHADOW's bond, and stake BOTH ends of a re-bond.
  2. **A conflict taught the assembly of members this tab had never seen, and nothing about the ones it had.** The shadow's rev can be advanced past its own json by the monotonic guard, so a tab holds a CURRENT rev beside a STALE bond — and the refusal could not correct it. Measured: client bucketed `e107` under itself, server under `e2e-bldg-1`, same rev 5, forever. Fixed: `assemblyOf` is recorded for EVERY member a conflict names, preferred over the json, and cleared the instant anything fresher lands (our own accepted commit, or a remote row).
  3. **A bond it could not state was guessed at.** On a `stale` entry with no server statement the bond is a guess; a bet built on one is refused forever when the server considers that assembly empty, because an empty conflict payload names no member to learn from. Fixed: the member is WITHDRAWN, degrading that group to the per-row rev guard — never to no guard. **Appeared on ONE of twenty hours (seed 14)**, which is why that seed is pinned in CI beside its unit test.
- **THE FLIP, and the one-line undo, written out.** `groupCas.js`'s build default is now ON (absence of `VITE_GROUP_CAS` means on). **Per device:** `localStorage.setItem("planarfit:groupCas","0")` then reload — beats the build flag, no deploy. **Everyone:** `VITE_GROUP_CAS=0` in the Cloudflare Pages build env, redeploy. **The database needs no rollback** — the 4-arg overload is inert for a client that stops sending `p_groups`.
- **THE RUN THAT JUSTIFIED IT:** 20 seeded hours · **8,042 commits · 3,880 group bets · 312 refusals, every one caused by a real concurrent edit and every one converged · 0 spurious · 0 stuck · 0 lost.** `--mutate order` and `--mutate membership` still go red on DIFFERENT assemblies.
- **THE HOUR IS GENUINELY ORDINARY NOW, and the coverage is MEASURED.** Added the two shapes the first run lacked: **re-bond** (the indent/outdent analogue — the only action that moves an element between assemblies, and the one that found defect 1) and **non-geometric field edits** (owner / status / label). The prefix-pair traps are planted in the two characters that actually invert a token sort — a DIGIT (`b1` ⊂ `b11`) and a HYPHEN — after the first fixture used `b1x`, where `x` (0x78) sorts ABOVE `:` and does **not** invert; and one trap uses the owner's OWN live ids, `e2e-bldg-1` ⊂ `e2e-bldg-11`. The run REPORTS which traps it staked a bet on and FAILS if it missed one.
- **⛔ THE HARNESS CONVICTED WORKING CODE TWICE MORE, both kept as comments.** It modelled `create` over a tombstone as a rev reset to 1, and `delete` against a tombstone as a conflict; `site_elements.sql` continues the rev on the first and returns idempotent `ok` on the second. Both produced confident, permanent "spurious refusals" that the real server cannot generate. When the instrument and the code disagree, the instrument is on trial.
- **⛔ AN INSTRUMENT THAT GETS CORRECTED IS WORTH MORE THAN ONE THAT WAS NEVER QUESTIONED.** Twice in
  this run the driver reported a confident, permanent spurious refusal that the real server **cannot
  produce**, and both times the correct move was to put the instrument on trial rather than the app:
  a `create` over a tombstone CONTINUES the rev (it does not reset to 1), and a `delete` against an
  already-tombstoned row is **idempotent success**, not a conflict (`site_elements.sql`). And the LAST
  failing seed was the oracle mis-attributing — not a defect at all. Every one of those was a step
  toward the real finding, not away from it.
- **⛔ A GUARD THAT A COMMENT CAN SATISFY OR BREAK IS NOT GUARDING ANYTHING.** The stage-1 assertion
  *"no client code may reference `assembly_id`"* went red on a COMMENT explaining that very rule — so
  it was forbidding the code from documenting its own invariant. It now strips comments and asserts
  CODE, with the stripper itself proven non-vacuous. Same family as the panel-brevity check that
  counted question marks in source and caught a ternary: a guard whose subject is text rather than
  behaviour eventually measures the wrong thing.
- **AND THE ORACLE ITSELF WAS CORRECTED, in the open:** a foreign write now marks BOTH assembly keys the element can be counted under (its host's and its own id), because a stale client bets under the latter; and "stuck" now means *kept trying and kept failing*, not *never bet on again*. Both corrections were re-proven not to hide anything — all three defects and both mutants still go red with them in place.
- **⛔ THE BATCHING BOUNDARY, written down so the next session does not rediscover it the hard way.**
  Group bets ride the ATOMIC gate, and `batchSpansAssembly` opens that gate only for a batch carrying
  MORE THAN ONE member of one assembly. So a **LONE re-bond makes no group claim at all** — and so
  does an OUTDENT that empties its host, because the batch stops spanning one assembly the moment the
  child leaves. Both are guarded by the per-row rev check exactly as before stage 2, which is correct
  and is stage 3's territory (retire the per-row expectation for bonded elements). It is asserted in
  `test/assemblyGroupCas.test.js` rather than left implicit, so nobody reads the re-bond tests beside
  it as covering the lone case.

### B484336 — Group CAS would have refused EVERY save on a building, forever, over a sort order `[Site Planner / persistence]` (bug) #site-planner #sync #testing  *(found 2026-08-13 driving the first ordinary editing hour through the real write engine with group CAS forced on, per the owner's "collect the evidence yourself, then flip it for everything". - Origin: filed 2026-08-13 while collecting rollout evidence for B1341 stage 2.
- **THE MECHANISM.** Sorting the finished token compares the separator `:` (0x3A) against the longer id's next character, and every digit (0x30–0x39) and the hyphen (0x2D) sort below it. So the two sides disagree the moment one member's id is a PREFIX of another's. Uniqueness — which the old comment cited — is not the property that makes those orders agree; PREFIX-FREEDOM is.
- **⛔ THE CONSEQUENCE, WHICH IS THE POINT — NOT THE MECHANISM.** The naming pattern that triggers
  this **ALREADY EXISTS IN THE OWNER'S DATA**. Had the switch gone on with one of those two ids
  bonded into the same assembly, **every save on that building would have been refused,
  permanently**, with no escape available to him — not a reload, not re-drawing it, not a different
  browser. The only exit is a code fix. That is the concrete reason the careful route — collect the
  evidence first, park the flip on a spurious refusal — was worth what it cost: it turned a silent,
  unrecoverable data-loss bug into a one-line ordering change made before anyone was exposed to it.
- **NOT YET BITING, and one bond away.** Across the owner's 403 client-named assemblies and 1,104 ids there are ZERO prefix pairs inside a single assembly — but there is already one on a site (`e2e-bldg-1` ⊂ `e2e-bldg-11`). Group CAS was about to be switched on for everyone.
- **THE FIX, both sides.** Client sorts by the ID through a code-POINT comparator (`compareIds`); SQL says `order by t.id collate "C"` — byte order STATED rather than inherited, because the database default is `en_US.UTF-8` and a linguistic collation may reorder on a version bump. Applied to production 2026-08-13.
- **THE INSTRUMENT IS THE DELIVERABLE** (DANGEROUS-MEANS-UNOBSERVABLE). `ui-audit/session-group-cas.mjs` drives an ordinary hour — moves, resizes, child edits, adds, deletes, undo/redo, saves, idle gaps, a second tab writing, realtime dropping a quarter of its rows — through the real `elementSync` against a server model EVALUATED OUT OF THE SHIPPED MIGRATION. Clean build, 20 seeds: 8,389 commits · 366 refusals · every one genuine and converged · **0 spurious, 0 stuck, 0 lost**. `--mutate order` and `--mutate membership` re-introduce this defect and B447472's; both go red on DIFFERENT assemblies, and the fixture plants both shapes or the check is vacuous. Pinned by `test/sessionGroupCas.test.js`.

### B477808 — The inspector can hand back a different number than you typed, and says nothing `[Site Planner / inspector]` (bug) #site-planner #ui  *(found 2026-08-13 answering the owner's question "check whether the Depth and Length inputs silently round, clamp or otherwise alter a number"; measured rather than assumed. `[x]` **SHIPPED.**

- **TWO DIFFERENT FACTS, and the first guess about the second one was WRONG — which is why they are stated apart.**
  - **CLAMP (a real alteration).** `clampNum` floors at `min` and ceils at `MAX_DIM` (100,000 ft). Typing `200000` into Depth committed **100,000** and said nothing. The stored dimension genuinely was not the one typed.
  - **DISPLAY ROUNDING (not an alteration).** Every dimension call site passes `value={Math.round(...)}`, so typing `613.7` shows **614** afterwards — and it looked like the field silently rounds. **It does not: the model stores 613.7 exactly** (verified by reading it back out of the saved plan). What is rounded is the DISPLAY, so the number on screen stops being the number in the drawing. A smaller problem than a swapped dimension, and a real one.
- **LOUD-FAILURE:** both now report in the moment, in their own words and with their own icon — *"✎ Using 100000"* for a clamp, *"✎ Showing 614"* for a display that disagrees with the model — and neither is dressed as a rejection (`aria-invalid` stays keyed on a genuine refusal alone). **Nothing was prevented and no rounding was removed**: the clamp and the round are both correct behaviour; they were merely silent. The display half is detected by watching what the CALLER hands back, so no call site changed.
- **⛔ AND THE DEFECT THIS WORK ITSELF INTRODUCED, caught by the browser and pinned by a test.** The first cut rendered the message by returning a bare row when there was nothing to say and a wrapped column when there was — so the moment a message appeared React saw a different tree shape, **REMOUNTED the `<input>`, and the field lost focus mid-keystroke**: typing `-5` left `-` in the box and dropped the `5`. A control that stops accepting input the instant it has something to tell you is a crueller version of the complaint this whole strand began with. The wrapper is unconditional now; the MESSAGE changes, never the tree. Invisible to every unit test (MODULE-SCOPE-COMPONENTS' family).
- **Guards:** `test/fieldFocusVsInvalid.test.js` (22 — incl. the constant-tree-shape and no-second-focus-colour regressions) · `ui-audit/verify-field-focus-vs-invalid.mjs` (**20 checks, both themes, computed styles off the live element, model read back from storage**), with crops in `ui-audit/screens/field-{focused,rejected,altered}-{light,dark}.png`.

  - **Doc Review had the identical defect** (its guard read `e.target`, `<body>` after any dismissal) and is closed the same way — a stray Backspace there destroyed the selected MARKUP.

Both regressions have named test cases.
- **LOUD-FAILURE:** a refused key that would have changed the plan flashes *"The keyboard is still on the panel. Click the plan, then press Delete."* once per episode, and a refused Delete reports `delete-attempt` telemetry with its reason.
