### B464049 (×2) — The Depth box "wasn't letting" him type. Nothing was rejecting it — and the app had NO error state at all `[Site Planner / UI · a11y]` (bug) #site-planner #ui  *(owner chat 2026-08-13, arrived with NEW-1 as its second symptom, and confirmed by him as its own item: "The field was never broken — it just looked broken, and that is a real defect worth its own item, not a footnote." Minted **B464049** from the same reserved block. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open / ⏳ Verify / Done across `focus ring`, `--accent`, `--danger`, `invalid`, `aria-invalid`, `contrast`, `B316`–`B320`, `B341`, `B433`, `B926`, `B927`: **B927** ADDED the focus-visible outline (this re-colours it), **B433** is the status palette and its "red is reserved for genuine alert/error" rule — which this restores rather than changes — and **B341** is the hardcoded-colour-in-chrome trap, a different failure. Nothing owns the focus-vs-error collision. **Net-new.**)*
`[x]` **SHIPPED — and then CORRECTED. Read the correction first; the first fix was the wrong end of the problem and is reverted.**
- **Recurrence: 2026-08-13 — owner researched the three options rather than picking one, and none of them was right.** Verbatim: *"THE DEFECT IS THE ERROR STATE, NOT THE FOCUS RING. Orange-red is Planyr's brand accent — it is on the Select tool, the 'Select parcels: on' pill, everywhere. A field you are typing in glowing in the accent colour is normal and correct, and restyling every text box in the app is a large visible change to fix something that is not the cause."* He is right, and the shipped restyle is **reverted**: `--focus-border` is gone, `--focus-ring` / `--focus-ring-soft` are back to their accent-derived values byte-for-byte, and the focused input's border reads `var(--accent)` again. A guard test now fails the build if a separate focus colour reappears.
- **⛔ WHAT THE FIRST PASS GOT RIGHT AND WHAT IT GOT WRONG.** Right: nothing was rejecting his input (that finding stands, unchanged and re-verified). Wrong: it read the accent-vs-danger ΔE00 of ~14 as *the focus ring is impersonating an error* and moved focus. The accent IS the brand; the real fault is that **this app had no invalid state whatsoever** — an unusable value was reported by nothing at all: no colour, no icon, no message. **That is a WCAG 1.4.1 (Use of Color) failure in its own right, independent of the bug that surfaced it**, and — per Deque's guidance — a bare coloured border would not have satisfied it either, because the user must be able to tell WHICH field is wrong and WHAT is wrong with it.
- **WHAT SHIPS NOW.** A rejected value carries **four** cues, with colour last: a **short text message** naming the problem (*"Smallest allowed is 1"*) · **`aria-describedby`** tying that message to the input so a screen reader is handed it · an **icon** · and a border that differs from focus in **WEIGHT (2px vs 1px) as well as hue**, so the two never read alike before the words are read. A bare accent ring with no message is then unambiguous: you are simply typing.
- **PANEL-BREVITY:** the message is ONE line, ≤ 60 chars, and exists ONLY while there is something to say — every panel's default view is byte-identical. `panel-copy-budget --check` before and after: **all regions within budget, unchanged** (the note is not static copy and never renders at rest).
- Verify: sandbox — proven on the RENDERED element in both themes (ATTEMPT-BEFORE-YOU-PARK: this is a logged-out UI check and was driven here, not filed as pending).
- Origin: filed 2026-08-13 from chat.
- **⛔ SAY IT PLAINLY: NOTHING WAS REJECTING HIS INPUT.** Driven every way it can be driven on his own Depth field — select-all-and-type · clear-with-Backspace-and-type · type-a-partial-and-Tab-away · type-and-click-away — **the field took the value every single time** (613 → 500, → 5, → 450, all committed to the model). There was no validation, no revert, no blocked keystroke. The screenshot he sent showed Depth outlined in red and Length normal because **Depth was FOCUSED and Length was not.**
- **THE MEASUREMENT.** The focused-input border was `--accent` (#C2410C light / #F26B3A dark) with a soft accent halo. Against this app's own error colour `--danger` (#E24B4A / #F2706F) that is **ΔE00 14.4 (light) and 13.4 (dark)** by the repo's own CIEDE2000. A plainly different hue measures ~49 on the same scale. Red universally means rejected, so **a focused field was an error message.**
- **⛔ SUPERSEDED — the blue-focus fix described here was REVERTED (see the correction above).** It is left in the record because the blast radius it measured is the reason the revert mattered: those are BARE ELEMENT SELECTORS in `src/index.css` reaching **~194 inputs, selects and textareas** across Site Planner (138), Review (14), Notes (15), Library (11) and shared chrome (16), plus the Scheduler's own 66 — one edit restyling every text box in the product.
- **AND `--danger` NOW HAS A REAL STATE TO MEAN.** There was no invalid state in this control at all, which is why the focus ring was the only red on screen. `NumInput` now refuses a genuinely unusable value (unparseable · below `min` · above `max`) — and ⛔ **an EMPTY field is never an error**, because clearing it is the first half of retyping it and flagging that instant would recreate the exact impression this removes.
- **⛔ COLOUR IS NEVER THE ONLY CUE** (owner requirement — blue-vs-red is precisely the pair a red-green colour-blind reader cannot separate). Four independent signals: **`aria-invalid="true"`** on the input · **`aria-errormessage`** carrying the reason · a visible **⚠ glyph** whose accessible name is *"Invalid: Smallest allowed is 1"* · and the colour, last.
- **⛔ THE DEFECT THAT ONLY THE ON-SCREEN CHECK COULD SEE, and the reason the owner was right to demand it.** The first cut set every token correctly, put `aria-invalid` on the element and rendered the ⚠ — **and the border stayed blue.** `!important` does not arbitrate between two `!important` declarations; SPECIFICITY does, and the focus rule's three `:not()` arguments (0,4,1) out-specify a bare `input[aria-invalid]:focus` (0,2,1) wherever it sits in the file. A stylesheet reading would have passed it.

### B464050 — "Undo re-spaces every element's layer key" — IT IS NOT UNDO. Legacy duplicate `z`, repaired at load `[Site Planner / undo]` (bug → **not a bug; diagnosis corrected**) #site-planner #selection #sync  *(found 2026-08-13 while verifying B464048's undo restoration; the owner has not reported it. Minted **B464050** from that branch's reserved block. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open / ⏳ Verify / Done across `zOrder`, `normalizeZ`, `ensureZ`, `B671`, `B820`, `B316864`, `arrange`, `applySnapshot`, `undo`: **B671** IS this mechanism — it introduced the explicit `z` and its migration — and what was filed here turns out to be that migration firing, not a new defect.)*
`[x]` **CLOSED — the filed diagnosis was WRONG, and the correction is the deliverable. No fix was built, deliberately; the sizing is stated below.**
- Verify: sandbox.
- **WHAT WAS FILED.** Deleting Building 1 on his FM 359 plan and pressing Ctrl+Z restored all 18 elements with every property byte-identical **except `z`**, which was re-spaced on the 17 elements the undo did not touch (`1024 → 2048`, `0 → 1024`, …).
- **⛔ UNDO IS NOT WHAT DOES IT — measured, not reasoned.** Driven in a browser on the same fixture, **one arrow-key nudge** — no delete, no undo — produces the identical re-spacing. The chain is: his saved plan carries **9 DUPLICATE `z` VALUES** (both buildings are `z: 0`; each assembly is numbered 0…8192 independently — legacy rows from before B671 gave elements an explicit `z` at all) · `createSiteModel` calls `ensureZ` on **LOAD**, which repairs them in memory · the next **SAVE of any kind** persists the repair. Undo was simply the first save that happened. B671's designed migration, doing its job.
- **THE THREE SIZING QUESTIONS, ANSWERED BEFORE ANY CODE:**
  1. **Does anything consume these keys for ORDER?** **Yes** — `byZAsc` (z, then id) *is* the draw order within a type layer, so a re-space would be a live hazard the moment two elements landed in a new relative position. **It cannot:** `ensureZ` is `normalizeZ(sortByZ(list))` — it assigns `index × Z_GAP` in the order produced by **the very comparator the renderer sorts with**. One function at both ends, not two numbers that happen to agree.
  2. **Does it persist?** Yes, on the next save — but **exactly once**. `ensureZ` is idempotent *by identity* once the duplicates are gone (`needsZ` false → the input array is handed straight back), so this is one migration write, not a mutation on every undo. It is also deterministic, so two people undoing the same action produce the same file — no divergence, nothing for a diff or a sync to see after the first pass.
  3. **Can an element end up with a DIFFERENT key than it had?** Yes, at that one migration — and it does not matter, because **nothing identifies an element by its `z`**. Bonds are `attachedTo` (id), selection is by id, `bondRemap`'s id-bearing inventory (B1124) does not list `z`. Only ORDER is expressed, and order is preserved.
- **SIZING, STATED: hygiene, not a hazard — so no fix was built.** Building one would be churn against a value nothing depends on. **⛔ And the pixels matching is NOT the reason** (the eight-group-headers case is the counterexample: right by accident because two numbers happened to agree, with nothing maintaining the agreement). The reason is that the agreement here is *structural* — and it is now **pinned as a property rather than argued**.
- **AND THE THING THAT COULD MAKE IT PERPETUAL WAS CHECKED, because "nothing maintains it" is the real risk.** Driven in a browser: creating a building, **Ctrl+D duplicating** one, and **copy/pasting** one all assign distinct gapped `z` (`nextZ` lands above every peer). **Nothing in the app creates a duplicate today**, so the migration fires once per legacy plan and then never again.
- **Guards:** the repo-root `test/` suite **zOrderStability** (22 — the order-preservation invariant over a battery of hostile inputs *including the owner's real duplicate-z assembly shape verbatim*, the idempotent-by-identity property, a source sweep that no bond or selection field is keyed on `z`, and the three creation paths; **mutation-proven — dropping the `sortByZ` from `ensureZ` turns 6 red, his plan's shape among them**) and one added check in the ui-audit harness **verify-delete-undo-restores** (33/33), which measures the nudge-does-it-too fact on the real plan so the corrected diagnosis cannot decay back into the filed one.

### B472049 — A notch split left the superseded parent drawn, so it read as a duplicate `[Site Planner]` (bug) #site-planner #parcel  *(owner chat 2026-08-13, arrived as NEW-9. Minted **B472049 / V266993** from this branch's block B472048–B472063 against `origin/main` 22be185. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched `split`, `polygonSplit`, `B651`, `B652`, `parentId`, `supersede`: **B651** SHIPPED the supersede-and-retain model this reverses, on the owner's own decision. Not a recurrence — a reversal, with his reasoning on the record.)*
`[ ]` **⏳ SHIPPED 2026-08-13. `Verify: live` → V266993.**
- Verify: live → **V266993** (`Blocker: real-data`).
- **⛔ TWO CLAIMS IN THE REPORT ARE REFUTED, AND A THIRD WAS WITHDRAWN BY THE REPORTER.** (1) *"it wrote the remainder to a NEW parcel instead of back onto the parent"* — that IS the design, and the through-cut that works did exactly the same: `e1455073` is a NEW 41-point parcel, and `e1454855` is still present at 35 points. (2) *"209.597 acres of parcel sitting on 105.122 acres of land"* — no; the superseded parent is `active:false` and counts nowhere. (3) The **data-loss** framing was withdrawn: the owner confirms **he deleted both slivers himself** (0.647 ac and 3.883 ac), deliberately. **There is no geometry bug and no data-loss bug.** The engine's through-cut residual is 0.000 ac and it was not touched.
- **WHAT WAS REAL, AND IT IS A DRAWING DECISION.** On a notch cut the remainder is 99.4% of the parent (104.475 of 105.122 ac), so the retained parent and its own remainder are two near-identical outlines and the tool reads as having duplicated rather than cut.
- **THE OWNER DECIDED IT, AND HIS REASONING IS BETTER THAN EITHER OPTION PUT TO HIM:** *"no because the two new parcels would have the same exterior outline."* The union of a split's children REPRODUCES the parent's outline exactly — that is what a split is — so the retained parent adds no information, only a second coincident boundary. **The parent is now REMOVED and tombstoned.** The dimmed/dashed/superseded-styling route was considered and rejected on the merits.
- **⛔ THIS REVERSES B651 IN TWO PLACES, BOTH DELIBERATE:** the parent is no longer retained `active:false`, and it IS tombstoned — B651 expressly said not to, correctly, *while the parent stayed a live record*; now that it is gone the tombstone is what stops a merge from another device resurrecting it over its own children.
- **LINEAGE SURVIVES WITHOUT A DRAWABLE PARCEL, and nothing is lost:** the HCAD facts (`addr`/`acct`/`attrs`) were already COPIED onto every child at split time and were never read back off the parent; `parentId` stays as a historical stamp, and `siteModel.childrenByParent` already ignores a child whose parent is absent, so the nesting stops rather than dangles.
- **MIGRATION, ANSWERED EXPLICITLY: NO, existing plans are NOT fixed automatically.** Parents superseded by earlier splits are already on disk as drawable `active:false` rows and keep drawing. Measured against production: **3 such parents across 2 plans** (Bain `smsqi16s9ej4` holds `e1454855gyzzln` and `e1455071mkspvo`). ⛔ **Not repaired here** — the owner ruled out automated repair of his live data; the count and the ids are reported for him to choose.
- **THE GUARDS (`lib/splitIntegrity.js`), all measured across ACTIVE **AND NOT DELETED**:** area conservation · **union-outline equality** against the parent (his argument, turned into the assertion — and stronger than area alone, since it catches a cut that balances the books while leaving a gap or a slit) · no pairwise overlap · and whether a split's emitted pieces survived its own operation. ⚠ **The column that makes it honest is `deleted_at`**: reading `active` alone the reported case sums to 105.122 and passes green while a piece has vanished; reading `!deleted` alone the superseded parent joins in and the sum doubles. Both mutation checks are in the suite. The survival guard **names no culprit** — it says outright that the rows cannot tell who deleted a piece.
- **CUT-TOPOLOGY FIXTURES, through the REAL engine:** through-cut (edge A→B) · **notch (both endpoints on the SAME edge — the reported case, and the one that had no coverage)** · corner clip across two adjacent edges · multi-vertex curved chain · endpoints landing exactly on existing vertices.
- Sandbox: `test/splitIntegrity.test.js` (20). Full suite 11,169 green, lint 0, build green.

### B454480 — "Tab sometimes doesn't work": instrumented, and the answer is one sentence `[Notes]` (bug) #notes #ui #testing  *(owner chat block 2026-08-13, NEW-1, with his screenshot of a Richfield "Utilities" note — a bulleted list with a nested sub-list and an autolinked email in it. Minted **B454480–B454481 / V249424** LATE via `git fetch origin main && npm run next-id -- --against-main`, from this branch's reserved block B454480–B454495 · V249424–V249439. **DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open / ⏳ Verify / Done across `Tab`, `notesTabKey`, `indent`, `outdent`, `sinkListItem`, `B1392`, `B291536`, `B36051`.** **B1392** and **B1392 ×2** own this key and are the direct ancestors — the second one wrote the context table this item extends. Neither had driven the FIRST-ITEM case, which is the whole of "sometimes". Not a recurrence: those items fixed contexts that were failing; this one measures which contexts fail now and finds the answer is one, for a structural reason. Net-new.)*
`[ ]` **⛔ SHIPPED as an INSTRUMENT plus a written rule — and the honest answer is that Tab is right everywhere except one case, which cannot be "fixed" without putting litter in his documents. That trade-off is his call and is flagged in the session reply.**
- Verify: sandbox (`ui-audit/audit-notes-tab.mjs`, 29 pinned rows)
- Origin: filed 2026-08-13 from chat.
- **HIS INSTRUCTION WAS NOT TO GUESS**, and it was the right instruction: *"Do not fix a guess — INSTRUMENT IT… Then report the failing set, not a theory."* The harness drives a REAL Tab in fourteen contexts × Tab and Shift+Tab, records the caret's node chain, list depth, offset, selection state and what is either side of it at the moment of the press, and judges by the STORED document.
- **THE FAILING SET IS THREE ROWS AND THEY ARE ONE FACT.** The first top-level bullet · the first bullet of the nested list · a range whose START is a first item. Everything else — mid-word, end of line, an EMPTY item, an already-nested item, immediately after an autolinked email, immediately after an autolinked URL, inside a table cell, the LAST cell of a table (adds a row, as Word does), inside a positioned box, and the page title — does the right thing.
- **⛔ AND IT IS STRUCTURAL.** A `listItem`'s content is `paragraph block*`, so a bullet is nested by becoming a child of the bullet ABOVE it; the first bullet has none. The only way to fake an indent is to mint an empty parent bullet — a bullet with no words in it — which is precisely the litter this module has spent six rounds removing. **So the rule, written into `notesTabKey.js`'s header as he asked: a bullet tucks under the bullet above it; the first bullet has nothing to tuck under.**
- **THE OPEN PRODUCT DECISION, stated rather than guessed:** accept the no-op (today), or accept an empty parent bullet in exchange for OneNote-style first-item indent. I have NOT taken this one — it puts a visible artefact in his real notes, which is his call and not mine.
- **⛔ THE INSTRUMENT NEEDED CORRECTING TWICE BEFORE IT COULD BE BELIEVED, which is the sub-finding.** Its first run reported TEN failures; five were the app being CORRECT and the instrument unable to see it. It could not tell *"did nothing"* from *"moved the caret"*, so Tab between two table cells and Tab out of the title — both of which move the caret and change no document — were filed as defects. And its node column read `p` for all twenty-eight rows, because `closest` with a selector list returns the NEAREST match, so a paragraph inside a cell inside a list always answers "p".
- Tab is also asserted REVERSIBLE where it inserts: in a plain paragraph Tab adds a tab character and Shift+Tab takes it back, so "Shift+Tab did nothing" is only ever reported when there was nothing to undo.

### B434416 — A text box had no SELECTED state at all, so "click it and press Delete" could not work `[Notes]` (bug/feature) #notes #ui  *(owner chat block 2026-08-13, arrived as NEW-1 of the second block and named by him as the parent of the other two: *"if I click on the box, I should be able to just press delete, but it doesn't seem like I can ever even click on the box."* Minted **B434416–B434418 / V229360** LATE via `git fetch origin main && npm run next-id -- --against-main`. **DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open / ⏳ Verify / Done across `noteAnchor`, `selected`, `data-selected`, `anchor-del`, `hover`, `OneNote`, `B342993`, `B350000`, `B357008`, `B391073`, `B400177`, `B421494`.** The closest is **B421494** (marquee multi-select), shipped in this same PR — it built a selection MODEL for several boxes at once, and this is the single-box half of the same concept, which is why it is a small extension rather than a rewrite. **B391073** added the delete and width controls that this makes reachable. Net-new.)*
`[ ]` **⛔ SHIPPED. Adversarially verified per his instruction — 88 checks in `verify-notes-box-selection`.**
- Verify: live  (V229360 — the two-stage gesture and the resize persistence on his own account)
- **HIS MEASUREMENT, WHICH IS THE WHOLE ITEM IN ONE FACT.** After a press, the element carried the class `planyr-anchor` and **nothing else** — no selected, active or focused state anywhere on the box, before or after clicking. There was no such thing as a selected box, so Delete had nothing to act on and every affordance had to hang off the pointer happening to be over it.
- **THE MODEL, OneNote's, in four steps.** Press 1 on an unselected box **selects** it — the caret does not enter, so the BOX is the thing you have hold of and Delete removes it in one undoable step. Press 2 **enters** it and it is an ordinary text box again. Escape backs out to selected; Escape again deselects. Arrow keys nudge a selected box; click-away clears it. A press on empty page still places a new box, unchanged.
- **TWO DEFECTS FOUND BY THE ADVERSARIAL PASS ITSELF, both invisible to a confirming test.** (a) The selection ring is an attribute on an element the EDITOR owns, and blurring the editor rebuilt the node view and dropped it — so "Escape backs out to the box being selected" silently did not happen. It is repainted on every transaction now. (b) The rule was bound in TWO places, so one Escape ran it twice and left editing *and* cleared the selection in the same keystroke, which made the two-stage model unusable. One binding now.

### B434417 — Resizing a box never saved: the gesture committed the width the box already had, while rendering the one you dragged to `[Notes]` (bug) #notes #ui #persistence  *(owner chat block 2026-08-13, NEW-2, flagged HIGH and measured by him on his account — rendered 300, stored 180, 180 after a reload. His words for the experience: *"it just is really dog shit, honestly."* Minted **B434417** from the same reserved block. DEDUPE-FIRST — **B400177** is the same control's STALE-ORIGIN defect, fixed the round before and genuinely fixed; this is a different mechanism in the same handler, found only because he measured the persistence path that item never checked. Not a recurrence of B400177 — a second, independent defect it was masking.)*
`[ ]` **⛔ SHIPPED. This is the one that produced his "review adversarially" instruction, and he was right.**
- Verify: live  (V229360)
- **WHY IT IS WORSE THAN "IT DOES NOT WORK".** The box goes on RENDERING at the size you dragged it to, so the gesture looks like it worked; the size evaporates on the next reload. You do the work, you watch it happen, and it is gone.
- **THE MECHANISM.** `endSize` committed `parseFloat(dom.style.width)` — and the DOM is not the gesture's memory. Anything that re-renders the node view between the last pointermove and the release rewrites that style from the node's CURRENT attrs, after which `num(w, ANCHOR_WIDTH)` falls back to the 180px default. On a signed-in account a sync tick does exactly that. **The commit now reads the gesture's own record**, and the MOVE drag — which had the identical `parseFloat(dom.style.left)` hazard and would have been the next report — was fixed in the same pass.
- **⛔ AND THE REASON THE HARNESS THAT SHIPPED THIS WAS GREEN, which is the lesson rather than the excuse.** It read storage AND reloaded, so it looked like a document-level check. It passed because a signed-out sandbox has nothing that re-renders a node view mid-gesture: the check was correct and the CONDITIONS were unreachable. Reproduced here by forcing one interfering re-render mid-drag — which now runs on every pass, at three window sizes, at a zoom other than 100%, on a box that was moved first, and on the last box of a crowded page.

- **⛔ ATTEMPT 2 FOUGHT THE RESIZE DRAG IN REAL TIME**: the fit re-derives the rendered width from `data-anchor-w` on a ResizeObserver, so while the handler wrote only the STYLE, every frame of a drag was immediately overwritten with the old stored width and the handle appeared dead.   | `e56` | parcel | 4 | 14:57:34.590193+00 | 14:57:34.590193+00 | `b147d90d…` |
  | `e1454594huuiov` | parcel | 4 | 14:57:34.590193+00 | 14:57:34.590193+00 | `b147d90d…` |
  | `e1454919qhgshe` | parcel | 1 | 14:57:34.590193+00 | — (created) | `b147d90d…` |

  Two deletions and one creation at the **identical microsecond**, same account, **nothing tying them together**. That is a parcel MERGE and it is unreadable as one: the only honest reading available from the database is "77 − 2 + 1". I came one query away from hand-writing an UPDATE to un-delete two parcels the owner had deliberately consumed, which would have resurrected them overlapping his new merged parcel.
- **⛔ WHY IT DID NOT SHIP THIS SESSION — three reasons, all specific:**
  1. **It requires a SCHEMA MIGRATION on the live production table holding every plan he owns**, applied BY HAND (this repo has no migration runner — see the convention in `db/`), while two sessions were actively editing that very database during this session. That is the class of action that gets confirmed, not performed at the end of a long run alongside two other items.
  2. **It touches the ELEMENT WRITE PATH**, which is this repo's most dangerous surface by record: the bonded-assembly family alone took **eight merged PRs** before B1340 closed it, and every one of those was a subtle multi-writer interleaving that passed its tests. `opFor` is four lines and reaching them is easy; being sure an envelope survives `freshen`, the atomic group commit, the unload keepalive, the PGRST202 fallbacks and the realtime echo path is not.
  3. **It is five deliverables, not one** — envelope, presence naming, activity view, undo ownership, and merge/split/paste fixtures — and shipping two of five under one number is exactly the half-job the house rules forbid.
- **WHAT WAS ESTABLISHED THIS SESSION, so the next one starts from measurement rather than from scratch:**
  - **⛔ THE OWNER'S QUESTION ABOUT THE EXISTING CLOCK CONTROL IS ANSWERED, AND THE ANSWER IS "EXTEND THE SHELL, NOT THE DATA".** There IS a clock: `HistoryIcon` → **Version history**, and it is a row in the **Plans ▾ header menu**, not in the map control cluster (the canvas cluster is Undo / Redo / Zoom-to-fit only). Its data is `storage.js`'s `planarfit:sites:history:v1` — a ring of **15 whole-plan snapshots, per DEVICE**, `{ at, buildings, summary, sig }`, never pushed to the cloud, **with no actor and no operation**. So it is the wrong grain and the wrong scope for a plan-activity feed: reuse the dialog chrome and the menu affordance, source the list from the rows, and do NOT try to widen the version ring.
  - **A PER-TAB SESSION ID ALREADY EXISTS AND SHOULD BE PROMOTED, NOT MINTED.** `elementJournal.journalSessionId()` is `sessionStorage`-backed — per TAB, surviving a reload, which is exactly the lifetime `actor_session_id` needs. (Two weaker candidates exist and should not be used: `randomIdSalt()` at `SitePlanner.jsx` is per-page-load and already baked into element ids, and `multiTab.js`'s `tabId` is per-realm and shared by every workspace header in one tab.)
  - **`updated_by` / `deleted_by` ARE NOT DECORATIVE — the owner's word, and it is worth correcting.** They are stamped server-side from `auth.uid()` on all five write statements and are load-bearing today: `elementSync.foreignAuthor()` reads them for own-echo suppression (B1116) and for the conflict-toast name resolver. The gap is real but narrower than stated: they carry an ACCOUNT, and both live sessions authenticate as the same account, so they cannot answer "was that my other tab". **Session granularity is what is missing, not attribution.**
  - **THE MERGE ALREADY LANDS IN ONE BATCH, incidentally rather than by design.** `mergeParcels` does `setParcels(...)` + `tombstone(goneIds)` in one React handler, so the autosave diff produces the deletes and the create in one `commit_elements` call. It is NOT atomic (`batchSpansAssembly` is about bonded buildings, and parcels are not), and nothing marks the three ops as one logical act. So `op_id` + `op_kind:"merge"` is a labelling change on a batch that is already whole — which is the cheap half.
  - **`reconcile` already carries a `direct` flag** (real user touch vs cascade relayout) — the closest existing thing to an `op_kind`, and the natural seam to widen.
- **THE PLAN, in the order it should be built:**
  1. **Envelope on the wire.** Extend `opFor` (`elementSync.js`) with `op_id` / `op_kind` / `actor_session_id` / `client_ts`; a 5-arg `commit_elements` overload; **columns on `site_elements`, not a separate `operations` table** — the rows are already the record, a side table would be a second copy of a fact the rows can carry (the mistake the `group_rev` column would have been), and every read path already selects from this one table. Follow the `site_elements_assembly_id.sql` precedent for the DDL and the `elementApi` PGRST202 latch precedent so an unapplied migration degrades instead of failing.
  2. **One op per user-visible action.** Mint the `op_id` where the gesture is (`pushHistory` is already the one-per-action seam) and thread it through the diff, so a merge's deletes and create share it.
  3. **Presence names names.** `ch.track({ uid, name })` gains `sessionId`; `presencePill` keys names by session and marks which is ME.
  4. **Activity view**, reusing the Version-history dialog shell, reading grouped ops.
  5. **Undo ownership.** `history.js` frames gain a meta sidecar (`push(current, meta)`); Undo names what it will undo and refuses / requires explicit confirmation when the top frame is not this session's.
- **SCOPE FENCE, from the owner verbatim: no full CRDT, no audit-log UI, no per-keystroke history.** The bar is that a human or agent looking at the plan five minutes later can answer "who did this, and what were they doing" without reading the database.
- **⚠ ALSO FROM THE SAME REPORT, AND IT IS THE UNCOMFORTABLE PART:** he pressed Undo six times on Bain (`smsqi16s9ej4`) while a second presence was in the plan. The geometry survived, but it cannot be proven that none of the other session's property edits were reverted — remote upserts mutate the canvas WITHOUT pushing a history frame, so an undo already reaches past them. **That uncertainty is the bug**, and step 5 is what closes it.


### B420257 — "create hit a live row (should be impossible)" fired twice in 36 hours, and it is NOT the duplicate-id collision `[Site Planner]` (bug) #site-planner #sync #persistence  *(filed 2026-08-13 from the B420256 audit block, which asked whether the two share a root cause. Minted **B420257** LATE via `git fetch origin main && npm run next-id -- --against-main`, from this branch's reserved block B420256–B420271 against `origin/main` 01f66ec. **DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open / ⏳ Verify / Done across `create-collision`, `create hit a live row`, `exists`, `B591`, `B377888`, `B757`, `B1113`, `elementSync`.** Neighbours, none of them this: **B377888** is delete-vs-create (a delete outliving the row it was about — the opposite direction, and its guard is about deletes); **B591** is the per-tab id salt this assertion is written against; **B1113** is which ledger wins on a seed. No item covers a CREATE being minted for a row the server already holds live. Net-new.)*
`[]` The engine emits `element-create-collision` — an op sent as `create` whose row is already LIVE on the server — which `B591`'s per-tab salted ids are supposed to make impossible.
- Verify: live  (needs a signed-in two-tab / reload-under-edit repro on a real plan)
- Origin: filed 2026-08-13 from the B420256 audit block.
- **THE EVIDENCE, from `client_errors` on production.** Twice in 36 hours — `sms69x8rb2qk` / `e1455040epkkus` (2026-08-12 18:50:17) and `smsdrvzr9gzx` / `e1454919cgzlnc` (2026-08-12 13:35:36) — and 19 rows in all since 2026-07-06, across seven different sites. Every one is `kind: el`.
- **⛔ IT DOES NOT SHARE B420256'S ROOT CAUSE, and that was checked rather than assumed.** B420256 is the (site_id, kind, id) composite key colliding inside one batch. A `select … group by site_id, id having count(*) > 1` over the whole live table returns **exactly one** such pair — Katz `e6327` — and **neither** reported id is in it: `e1455040epkkus` and `e1454919cgzlnc` each have exactly one row. A kind collision cannot produce a mis-paired result for an id that names only one row, so the two are independent. B420256's fix will not close this one.
- **THE LIKELY SHAPE, stated as a hypothesis and not as a finding.** `create` is minted for exactly one reason (`reconcile`: the canvas holds an element the SHADOW does not), so a `create` against a row the server already has means the shadow lost an entry the server still holds — a re-seed from a snapshot older than the create, a `shadow.delete(key)` on a `missing`/`deleted` branch that then re-diffs, or a refetch-replace landing between the two. The `exists` branch already recovers correctly (it adopts the row as an update), so **this is not currently known to lose data** — it is an assertion firing that says a state we believe unreachable is being reached, and that belief is load-bearing for other reasoning in this engine.
- **STOPPING RULE (STANDING RULE #2 clause 5):** closes when either the shadow-loss path is reproduced and fixed, or the telemetry carries enough context (the preceding settle path per id) to prove which of the three shapes above it is. It may not be closed on "could not reproduce".

### B400176 — A renamed note left the sidebar until a reload, because the stored tree lagged the screen by 400 ms `[Notes]` (bug) #notes #sync #persistence  *(owner chat block 2026-08-13, arrived as NEW-1 after the #1009 live pass, with his own caveat that he drove the rename synthetically. Minted **B400176 / V202272** LATE via `git fetch origin main && npm run next-id -- --against-main`, from this branch's reserved block B400176–B400191 · V202272–V202287. **DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open / ⏳ Verify / Done across `persistTree`, `writeTree`, `treeDirty`, `debounce`, `rail`, `sidebar`, `rename`, `stale`, `B134`, `B342992`, `B342996`, `B357011`, `B364016`, `B391072`, `B1291`.** Four neighbours, none of them this: **B342996** is the merge's TITLE rule under staleness — a different fact, and it is re-opened and half-shipped in this same PR (see it); **B342992** is the merge losing a page's HOME; **B357011/B364016/B391072** are the purge tombstones; **B134** is the planner's own stale-load, a different module and a different store. Not one of them is about the two readers of the Notes tree disagreeing for 400 ms. Net-new.)*
`[ ]` **⛔ SHIPPED. Reproduced with a REAL keyboard, fixed, mutation-proven both ways.**
- Verify: live  (V202272 — two windows on his account; a rename in one is not undone by the other)
- Origin: filed 2026-08-13 from chat.
- **HIS REPORT.** Rename a loose page from "Untitled page" to "PROBE13 TITLE". The stored tree updated immediately and correctly, **and the rail stopped showing the note at all** — only "Recovered — …" remained. A reload put it back in the right place. His caveat, stated plainly and correctly: he drove it with a synthetic `input` event, so the re-render path might not be the real one. What made it worth chasing anyway is the **asymmetry** — the commit path ran while the list did not update.
- **REPRODUCED WITH `page.keyboard`, and the caveat was not the story.** `ui-audit/verify-notes-rename-live.mjs`, three assertions, two window sizes including his short one. After typing a new name: the screen read **"PROBE13 TITLE"** and the STORED tree read **"Untitled page"**. After making a new page: the rail had **three** notes and the stored tree had **two**. 11/15 before, **15/15** after.
- **THE CAUSE — TWO READERS OF ONE TREE, READING DIFFERENT COPIES.** The rail renders from React state; the cloud sync reads `localStorage`. `persistTree` wrote the stored copy on a **400 ms debounce**, and the sync does not merely READ that copy, it decides from it:
  - `seed()` asks `sync.treeDirty` — only true once `writeTree` has run — to decide whether this device owes anything. Inside the window it is FALSE, so the seed concludes this device is clean and **adopts the account's tree wholesale**, a tree that cannot contain an edit this device has not written down yet. It hands that back through `onTree`, which is the row leaving the rail.
  - `pushPending` pushes `readTreeRaw()`, so an edit made in the window is not merely late to the account — it is **skipped**.
  - A page that exists only in memory is therefore one sync tick away from never having existed. That is the version of the failure that matches what he SAW.
- **THE FIX, and it is a correctness rule rather than a performance one: THE STORED TREE IS NEVER STALER THAN THE SCREEN.** `persistTree` writes through. The debounce bought nothing — the write it delayed is LOCAL, and the network push is debounced separately inside `writeTree` (`schedulePush`), unchanged — so removing it adds no traffic.
- **THE COST IS MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED** (`ui-audit/measure-tree-write.mjs`, budget chosen before the run: 2 ms/keystroke against a 16.7 ms frame). His notebook today: **0.007 ms** median. Ten times his: **0.052 ms**. Fifty times his (500 notes × 5 subpages, 500 binned, 352 KB): **1.167 ms**. The debounce was protecting a rename from seven-millionths of a second.
- **AND THE SAME DEFECT ONE LAYER UP, fixed in the same pass.** Every tree mutator was a `useCallback` closing over the render's `tree`, so an edit made after the store replaced the tree underneath us wrote the older copy back over the newer. **Two of the sixteen already read the ref and fourteen did not** — exactly the split that survives review. All sixteen now go through `treeNow()`, which also makes the rail's handlers referentially stable instead of rebuilt on every keystroke of a rename.
- **GUARDS, both mutation-proven.** `test/notesTreeWriteThrough.test.js` — 11 cases through TWO REAL STORE INSTANCES against an in-memory server that owns `rev` like the deployed trigger: the loss DEMONSTRATED (so the cost is on the record, not asserted), then rename / new page / move / delete each surviving a seed, plus ten interleaved write-then-sync rounds with the other computer editing between each. `test/notesModule.test.js` adds the source guard — no timer between `persistTree` and the disk, `TREE_SAVE_MS` gone rather than unused, and every one of nine mutators reading `treeNow()`. Reverting one mutator to the render's copy turns it red with the exact call named.
- **WHY A SOURCE GUARD AS WELL AS A BEHAVIOURAL ONE.** A reintroduced timer looks correct to every test that waits a moment before reading, which is nearly all of them. The shape is what rots quietly, so the shape is what is pinned.

### B400177 — The box width handle resized against a STALE left edge, so resizing a box you had moved gave the wrong width `[Notes]` (bug) #notes #ui  *(found 2026-08-13 by driving the control with a real mouse, after the owner reported it as "PRESENT but not behaviour-verified by me — my synthetic drag does not register on this build". He was right to flag it. Minted **B400177** from the same reserved block. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open / ⏳ Verify / Done across `noteAnchor`, `anchor-size`, `setNoteAnchorWidth`, `ANCHOR_MIN_WIDTH`, `nodeView`, `update(`, `B350000`, `B350001`, `B357008`, `B391073`: **B350000** is the placement CLAMP and the stylesheet floor that fought it — a different owner of the same attribute, already closed; **B391073** shipped this control and is the item this defect was introduced by, so this is its follow-up rather than its recurrence (a different mechanism, found by exercising it rather than by re-reading it). Net-new.)*
`[ ]` **⛔ SHIPPED, and it is a defect in code this cohort shipped one round earlier.**
- Verify: sandbox (`ui-audit/verify-notes-box-drag.mjs`, 43/43)
- **THE MECHANISM.** A ProseMirror node view is built once; its `update(next)` re-styles the element but **never rebinds the closure's `node`**, so `node.attrs` describes the box as it was when the view was BUILT. The width handle computed against `num(node.attrs.x)`. Resize a box you had already dragged and the width was measured from its OLD left edge: on a ten-box page, a drag asking for **90 more** produced **34 less**.
- **AND A SECOND, SMALLER ONE FOUND BY THE SAME PASS.** The box's right edge JUMPED to the pointer on grab, so asking for 90 gave 86 — a silent re-seat, which is precisely what the move drag's own comment forbids. The handle now keeps its grab offset the way the move drag keeps `grabX`. Exact to the pixel afterwards: asked 90, got 90; at zoom, asked 72, got 72.
- **THE DEAD FIELDS ARE GONE, not left unused.** The move drag's `from` object still carried `x`/`y` read from the same stale `node.attrs`; nothing read them, which makes them a trap for whoever edits this next.
- **WHAT THIS SAYS ABOUT THE PREVIOUS ROUND.** The control was shipped with a test that found it in the DOM and never drove it. "The button is there" and "the button works" are different claims, and only the second one is worth making. The harness now drives it with a real mouse in both directions, asserts the box does not MOVE while it resizes, and reloads to prove the width is stored rather than styled.

The numbers above are from the same snapshots with ids normalised. **Normalising the id at the diff is a one-line fix and is NOT shipped here** (it belongs to B266084, which owns the attribution tool); flagged so the next reader does not re-derive it.
- **STEP 2 — WHAT ATTRIBUTION NAMES, AND WHY IT IS NOT CHEAP.** `notesRouteJsBytes` is **no longer past its ceiling** — main has moved since the item was written, and it now sits +11.3 KB inside a 32 KB band. It PASSES; the one-lazy-boundary fix the brief describes is not needed to clear the red. Of the three that remain, the site route's +60.2 KB is boot-path app code across a dozen modules — **B1064 already took the lazy tranche** (`SetLocationDialog`, `ParcelRecordPanel`, `SiteAnalysis`, `StandardsBar`, `PondSection`, `StoragePanel` are all `lazy()` today), so there is no dialog or panel left to move.

Replacing it with a direct `fetch` would take ~144 KB off `totalJsBytes` — most of the 167.7 KB the metric needs. **It was not done: the repo's `claude-api` skill forbids exactly this substitution** ("Never mix the two — don't reach for `fetch` in a TypeScript project just because it feels lighter"), and bundle weight is the reason it names. The architecturally correct version — move the call server-side to a Pages Function, which is ALSO what this repo's own KEY DECISIONS say about third-party API keys — is real work with a live-feature security model attached, and is filed as **B393173** rather than shipped at the end of a long session.
- **STEP 3 — NOT TAKEN, BY THE ITEM'S OWN RULE.** Three metrics are red. The brief says: *"If you find yourself typing the third `--allow-raise`, STOP and report."* Ratcheting two of three would burn two baselines and leave main red anyway. **Nothing was ratcheted; no baseline was edited.** `test/perfBudgetPolicy.test.js` exists to prevent exactly the shape this would have been.
- **STEP 4 — WHAT A RED MAIN PUSH BUILD NOTIFIES TODAY: NOTHING OF ITS OWN.** `.github/workflows/build.yml` was read first, as instructed. It is 92 lines, has **no `if: failure()` step, no issue creation, no Slack, no notification of any kind** — the only signal is GitHub's built-in one: the red ✗ on the commit, and GitHub's default "workflow run failed" email to the run's ACTOR. On this repo the actor for a main push is whoever/whatever completed the auto-merge, which for automation-merged PRs is not a human inbox anyone reads. So the honest answer the brief allows is close but not exact: **it is not that "it already notifies and nobody looked" — it is that the only notification goes to the actor of an automated merge.** No mechanism was added; that is a decision, not a gap to fill blind.
- **⛔ NOT RE-SUGGESTED, as instructed:** "Require branches to be up to date" is not proposed. The `pull_request`-relative vs `push`-absolute asymmetry is deliberate and documented in the audit's own output.
- **THE DECISION THAT IS NOW THE OWNER'S**, stated plainly rather than left implied: optimize-first was tried and attribution says the cheap wins are gone; the only large one is policy-blocked and filed. Either **(a)** raise the three bands with a stated reason per metric — a product decision about download weight — or **(b)** fund B393173 + B1064 and leave main red until they land. **B329408 remains OPEN and keeps its stopping rule.**

### B393173 — The Anthropic SDK ships 144 KB to the browser for one API call, with the user's key in the page `[Site Planner / build · security]` (task) #infra #perf #files  *(found 2026-08-12 while attributing B393171's bundle drift; the owner has not reported it. Minted **B393173** from the same reserved block. Nothing owns this dependency's weight or its key handling.)*
`[ ]` Filed, not started.
- Verify: sandbox
- Origin: found 2026-08-12 during B393171's attribution.
- **THE MEASUREMENT.** `@anthropic-ai/sdk` is **144.4 KB** of the built bundle — the fourth-heaviest dependency, behind `pdfjs-dist`, `pdf-lib` and `leaflet`. It is reached from exactly one place (`lib/titleReader.js`, itself dynamic-imported) and makes exactly one call. It also drags a `node:fs` externalisation warning into every build.
- **TWO REASONS, and the second is the stronger one.** (1) It is most of the 167.7 KB `totalJsBytes` is over. (2) It runs `new Anthropic({ dangerouslyAllowBrowser: true })` with a key the user pastes and this app stores — `lib/titleKey.js`. It is the USER's own key rather than ours, so it is not a breach of the "server-side only" KEY DECISION, but it is the same shape, and the repo already has the right pattern next door: **B299** does the Tier-2 filing read server-side behind a Function.

That option was considered and rejected during B393171; do not re-derive it.


### B329408 — `main`'s required build is RED on the performance budget, and it has been for at least three commits `[Infra / CI · perf]` (task) #infra #perf #testing  *(found 2026-08-09 while landing B326416–B326419. Minted **B329408** from this branch's reserved block via `git fetch origin main && npm run next-id -- --against-main`. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open + ⏳ Verify + Done across `bundle`, `budget`, `perf:bundle`, `siteRouteJsBytes`, `largestChunkBytes`, `ratchet`, `B1064`, `B266084`: **B1064** owns closing the real Site-route gap and **B266084** built the base-ref attribution that DIAGNOSED this; neither is "main is red right now", which is what this item is. Filed rather than left as a note in a merged PR body, because a diagnosis with no B# is un-owned.)*
`🔲` **Open.**
- Verify: sandbox (`npm run perf:bundle` is the whole check)
- **THE STATE.** On the `main` push builds for `81f7725`, `1c41514` and `80fb475` (the last being B326416's merge), every step passes — lint, all five drift guards, the mint gate, the tests, the build — and **only** step 16, *Performance budget*, fails. Four metrics are over: `siteRouteJsBytes`, `notesRouteJsBytes`, `totalJsBytes`, `largestChunkBytes`.
- **IT IS NOT A REGRESSION FROM ANY ONE BRANCH, AND THE AUDIT SAYS SO ITSELF.** B266084's attribution line on the `1c41514` run reads: *"4 metric(s) arrive ABOVE BASELINE before this branch adds a line — that drift belongs to main, not to this pull request."* At that point main carried **+58.0 KB** (site route), **+33.9 KB** (notes), **+196.0 KB** (total) and **+53.8 KB** (largest chunk) above their baselines. It is accumulated drift across many merges.
- **WHY IT LOOKS INVISIBLE AND KEEPS GETTING MERGED PAST.** A `pull_request` run judges a branch RELATIVE to its base ref, so a PR adding a few KB is green; a push to `main` is judged **ABSOLUTELY**. That asymmetry is deliberate and documented in the audit's own output (*"main cannot drift past its own band without going red there"*) — it is the design working. The consequence nobody owns is that **every PR can be green while `main` is permanently red**, so the signal has stopped meaning anything and the next session will assume it is background noise.
- **WHAT THIS ITEM IS NOT.** It is not a licence to ratchet four baselines to make the red go away. Raising a baseline is a product decision about download weight and needs the same justification as any other; doing it to silence accumulated drift is exactly what `test/perfBudgetPolicy.test.js` exists to prevent. The two honest paths are **optimize back inside the band** (B1064 owns the real Site-route gap) or **ratchet with a stated reason per metric** — and someone has to choose, per metric.
- **STOPPING RULE (STANDING RULE #2 clause 5):** closes when a `main` push build goes green on step 16 — either by optimization or by a per-metric ratchet with its reason recorded in `ratchetLog`. If neither is judged worth doing, the item closes by an explicit owner decision to raise the band, recorded on the item — never by the check being ignored into permanence.

### B298759 — Version history is DEVICE-LOCAL, so losing the machine loses the history `[Notes]` (feature) #notes #persistence #sync  *(filed 2026-08-09 alongside B298754, which shipped the feature. This is the half that did NOT ship, stated as an item rather than left implied.)*

What it does not cover is losing the device: a new laptop signs in to the notes but to none of their history.

Device-local needs no schema change and cannot fight anything. Shipping the 90% that answers the stated risk beat shipping nothing this session.

Retention already exists and is pure (`planRetention`), so the server side is a mirror of a decision that is already made and tested.

- **✅ SHIPPED 2026-08-09 — `scripts/resolve-ledgers.mjs` (`npm run resolve-ledgers`).** Union the conflicting append sections, **but check the precondition instead of assuming it**, then regenerate the derived pair. This is what makes it not `merge=union`:
  - **THE PRECONDITION: within a conflict hunk, no `B#`/`V#` heading may appear on BOTH sides.** Disjoint ids = two independent appends, and concatenating them loses nothing. The same id on both sides = two sessions edited one item (or an edit raced a lifecycle move) — a genuine disagreement, so it **REFUSES, names the id and the line, leaves every conflict marker untouched, and writes nothing.** It never guesses.
  - **It catches the trap a naive check misses:** when git WIDENS a hunk to swallow an untouched neighbour, that neighbour's id shows up on both sides and the whole hunk is refused rather than silently double-written. Proven as its own case.
  - **AND A POST-CONDITION, because a precondition that is subtly wrong must not be able to write a broken ledger.** After unioning, the result is re-checked with **CI's own detectors** (B308704 same-file + B780 cross-file). Any new duplicate → **the entire resolution is rolled back** and the markers are restored. Two independent chances to catch the one failure mode that matters — which is the direct answer to *"make sure the bridge cannot silently duplicate a concurrent amendment."*
  - **The GENERATED pair is never unioned** — `BACKLOG_OPEN.md` and `MAP.md` are regenerated from the merged inputs, the only correct answer and one concatenation cannot get wrong.
  - **Refuses partially, never partially resolves:** if ANY hunk in a file overlaps, the whole file is left alone. A half-resolved file looks handled and is not.
  - Sandbox: `test/resolveLedgers.test.js` (12 cases — 9 pure, 3 end-to-end against a REAL `git merge` conflict in a throwaway repo), covering the amend-the-same-item refusal, the widened-hunk refusal, diff3-style conflicts, unterminated markers, and byte-identical pass-through of a clean file.
  - **It is also the INSTRUMENT that decides whether (c) is worth its cost**, which was the argument for a bridge in the first place: every run appends a line to `.planyr-ledger-merges.log` (gitignored). If the "ids overlap on both sides" branch never fires in a month of merges, the conflicts really are 100% arrival-order and (c) is justified by data rather than by argument.
- **⛔ (c) — ENTRIES AS DATA THE GENERATOR ASSEMBLES — IS NOT STARTED, AND WAS NOT HALF-STARTED.** The owner's instruction was explicit: *"do not half-migrate the file that is the single source of truth for what is open."* Nothing about `BACKLOG.md`'s format changed; it is still hand-edited exactly as before. **The remaining scope, unchanged and costed:** one file per item (`backlog/items/B<id>.md`, front-matter for status / `Verify:` / tags / module, prose for the body), `BACKLOG.md` + `BACKLOG_OPEN.md` + `BACKLOG-DONE.md` all becoming generated views, and a one-time migration of ~1,400 items across two files. **The generator becomes load-bearing** — if it is wrong the entire ledger is wrong — so it needs the same mutation-proven treatment as any guard here. That is its own session, and it should be taken only after the bridge's log has said whether the conflicts really are pure arrival-order.
- Verify: sandbox (the bridge) — V107264 tracks the one thing a sandbox cannot show: the bridge resolving a REAL `dirty` PR against real `origin/main` divergence.
- Origin: filed 2026-08-09 on owner instruction, from PR #974
- **THE MEASUREMENT, from the incident that produced this.** #974 was pushed with a green build. Five PRs merged while it sat — **#969, #970, #971, #973, #976, #977** — and it went `mergeable_state: dirty`. Resolving it by hand required inspecting **4 conflict hunks across 3 files** and regenerating 2 more. **Every hunk was "both sides prepended a new item to the top of the same section", with ZERO id overlap on either side.** There was no disagreement to resolve. There was nothing to decide. It was pure arrival-order collision, twice in one session (an earlier merge against `f797f8c` had the identical shape).
- **⛔ WHY THIS IS THE B6864 FAMILY AND NOT A HOUSEKEEPING GRUMBLE.** B6864–B6867 diagnosed a livelock where seven PRs were open and none was mergeable, and the fix was to make the contended resource a **pure function of the branch name** so two sessions cannot contend at all. That fixed the *numbers*. **The TEXT those numbers live in was left as one shared append target**, so the same shape survived one level up: the ids no longer collide and the paragraphs still do. A concurrency defect fixed for the identifier and not for the record it identifies is fixed for the easy half.
- **THE ASYMMETRY THAT POINTS AT THE ANSWER, and it is a measurement rather than a preference.** Of the five files, **two are GENERATED** (`BACKLOG_OPEN.md` from `BACKLOG.md`, `MAP.md` from `src/`) and **three are hand-maintained**. The generated pair conflicted just as violently — and resolving them cost **nothing and required no judgement**: take either side, run the generator, done. The three hand-maintained files are where all the reading, checking and risk was. **The files that are a function of data were free; the files that ARE the data were not.**

**THE THREE FIXES, and what each actually costs.**
- **(a) PER-SESSION APPEND FILES reconciled by the generator** — each branch writes `backlog.d/<branch>.md`; the generator concatenates. Kills the conflict outright (different files never conflict) and is the smallest conceptual change. **⛔ But it breaks on the two operations this repo performs most.** The lifecycle is a **MOVE** (🔲 Open → ⏳ Verify → ✅ Done, and Done means moving the block to another file) — that is not an append. And the **recurrence rule** re-opens the ORIGINAL `B#`, which by definition lives in some *other* session's append file: the edit is cross-file again, and now it is a conflict in a file whose owner never expected one. It solves the case we have and fails the cases we rely on.
- **(b) A UNION MERGE DRIVER on the append-only sections** — `.gitattributes` marking these files `merge=union`, which git concatenates both sides of. **By far the cheapest: one line, no per-clone configuration (union is a built-in low-level driver), and it would have landed #974 with no human step at all.** ⛔ Its hazard is exactly proportional to its convenience: union **cannot tell an append from an edit**, so two sessions amending the SAME item — which happened twice in this very session (#976 amended B1349; this branch corrected its own B287057 cross-reference *because* of #976) — are silently DUPLICATED instead of stopping anyone. In the file that is the single source of truth for what is open, a silent duplicate is a correctness failure, not an untidiness. Good bridge, wrong destination.
- **(c) ENTRIES AS DATA THE GENERATOR ASSEMBLES** — one file per item (`backlog/items/B287056.md`, front-matter for status / `Verify:` / tags / module, prose for the body), with `BACKLOG.md`, `BACKLOG_OPEN.md` and `BACKLOG-DONE.md` all becoming GENERATED VIEWS. Two sessions filing two items touch two different files → **no conflict**. A lifecycle move is a one-field edit in one file → **no conflict**. A recurrence is an edit to one existing item → conflicts **only** with another session editing that same item, which is a genuine disagreement that SHOULD stop you.
- **⛔ I WOULD PICK (c), AND SHIP (b′) AS THE BRIDGE. The reason is the property, not the tidiness: (c) is the only option where the conflict rate tracks REAL DISAGREEMENT instead of ARRIVAL TIME** — which is precisely the property B6864 established for ids, applied one level up to the text. Three things make it the cheap choice rather than the grand one: the repo **already runs this pattern** (`BACKLOG_OPEN.md` and `MAP.md` are generated, `--check` already fails CI on drift, and both were free to resolve in this incident — that is evidence, not analogy); prose cross-references (*"see B1349"*) are plain text and keep working untouched; and the archives are already declared **write-only**, so turning them into generated views costs nothing anybody reads.
- **THE PRICE OF (c), NAMED RATHER THAN GLOSSED.** It is a one-time migration of ~1,400 items across two files, `BACKLOG.md` stops being hand-editable and every session's habit changes with it, and **the generator becomes load-bearing** — if it is wrong the entire ledger is wrong, so it needs the same mutation-proven treatment as any guard here. That is a real cost and it is why the bridge matters.
- **(b′) THE BRIDGE TO SHIP FIRST, and it is small: `scripts/resolve-ledgers.mjs`,** encoding exactly the resolution performed by hand in this incident — union the conflicting append sections, **but FIRST assert that no `B#`/`V#` appears on both sides**, refuse loudly and leave the conflict for a human if one does, then regenerate the two derived files. It gets (b)'s automation with none of its silent-duplication hazard, because it checks the property that makes union safe instead of assuming it. It is also the honest way to prove (c) is worth doing: if the "ids overlap on both sides" branch never fires in a month of merges, the conflicts really are 100% arrival-order and (c)'s migration is justified by data.
- **⛔ ONE THING THIS ITEM MUST NOT BECOME.** Do not "fix" this by relaxing the drift checks (`build-backlog-index --check`, `build-map --check`) or by removing `BACKLOG_OPEN.md`/`MAP.md` from version control. Those are guards; they caught nothing wrong here and they are not the cause. The cause is that three files are a shared append target.

### B295168 — The site-route chunk guard snapshots AFTER its own gesture, so it reports input-driven chunks as boot-path ones `[Infra / Testing]` (bug) #infra #testing #perf  *(found 2026-08-06 while closing out B1349's owner gate — the guard was still red on `terrainLayers` after B1442 removed the only trigger this repo had recorded for it, and the discrepancy turned out to be the instrument. Minted **B295168** via `git fetch origin main && npm run next-id -- --against-main`. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open + ⏳ Verify + Done across `siteRouteChunks`, `bootChunks`, `BOOT_SETTLE_MS`, `lazyChunksAfterBoot`, `B1163`, `B1344`, `B1349`, `B1358`, `B1431`: **B1358** fixed this metric's RACE (the snapshot was taken before React's mount effects had fired, so a fast machine reported clean) and its 4 s settle window is still correct and still load-bearing; **B1163** is the allowlist's own defect; **B1349** owns the chunks the guard names. None of them is about WHERE in the run the snapshot is taken relative to the harness's own pointer. Net-new, and deliberately NOT a B1358 recurrence — B1358's fix holds and this is a second, independent way the same number can mean something other than what it says.)*
- **THE DEFECT.** `ui-audit/perf-harness.mjs` defines `siteRouteChunks` as "which JS chunks a PLAIN SITE ROUTE fetched — the boot path", and takes the snapshot **after** the time-to-first-drag gesture plus a 4 s settle. That gesture moves the mouse across the canvas. So any chunk a POINTER MOVE can pull lands in a list whose name and whose failure message (*"Something is warming a route-irrelevant workspace at boot again"*) both say boot.
- **PROVEN, on `main` at `1d2f31a`, with the reference plan seeded:** idle page, **no mouse, no click, eight seconds** → `terrainLayers` is **absent**. One mouse move over the canvas → `terrainLayers` arrives (the cursor ground-elevation readout, `useGroundElevation` → `terrainLazy.loadTerrain()`). The harness reports it as a boot chunk in both worlds.
- **WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND TIDINESS:** it cost B1349 a false red for a defect that was genuinely fixed, and the next reader's obvious move — widening the allowlist — would have hidden a real regression on the six chunks that ARE on the idle path.
- **FIX SHAPE, and why it is not a one-line move.** The snapshot cannot simply move earlier: B1358's settle exists because a boot-path `import()` fired from a mount effect is only in the list if it has been REQUESTED by the moment of the read, and that is machine-speed dependent. The honest shape is **two page loads in one run** — one that gestures immediately (time-to-first-drag) and one that never receives input at all (the chunk guard, after its settle) — or an initiator-aware split reporting `chunksBeforeFirstInput` / `chunksAfterFirstInput` as two named numbers. Either changes what a guard other sessions read, so it wants its own before/after rather than a drive-by edit.
- **⛔ Until it is fixed, do NOT widen `bundle.siteRouteAllowlist` to quiet it** — the six genuinely-at-boot names on B1349 are what it is correctly catching.
- Verify: sandbox
- Origin: found 2026-08-06 while closing B1349's owner gate

- **THE TARGET IS A BOUNDARY, NOT A SMALLER FILE.** Two stores split by who WRITES them — a VIEW store (pan, zoom, cursor, hover, size) and a MODEL store (elements, parcels, ponds, settings) — so that **a write to the VIEW store cannot invalidate a memo whose inputs are MODEL + SETTINGS.** That is the invariant B217538's guard asserts from outside, moved inside the architecture so it holds by construction. Roughly 150 of the 206 cells are neither: UI-local menu/draft/status state that should never have been in this component.

Acceptance is `after ≤ before` on every counter from `perf:recompute`'s four arms, at least one strictly lower, `perf:viewindep` green throughout, and **the registry grown** — a slice that relocates state without registering the promise it just made has bought a refactor and no guarantee.

- **⛔ SLICE 6 DOES NOT START UNTIL B217540 IS FIXED.** One building drag re-migrates and re-serialises the entire plan dozens of times; that is a persistence-layer invalidation defect a state split would inherit and hide. **ROWS-CANONICAL-ON-SEED**, **TOMBSTONE-DELETES** and **LOUD-FAILURE** all bear on it and none may be relaxed to make a slice land.

- **THE FACT.** There are exactly **two** Web Workers in this repo — `lib/terrainWorker.js` and `lib/dxf/dxfWorker.js`. - **WHY MEMOISATION IS NOT THE END OF IT, in the owner's framing and it is correct.** B236592 cut the CALL COUNT by ~99% (275,184 `offsetInward` calls in one pan). It did not move a single millisecond off the main thread, so **the next bad input reintroduces the whole problem** — a pond with a denser ring, a larger plan, a new caller. A memo bounds frequency; it does not bound worst case.
- **⛔ WHY IT DOES NOT SHIP BLIND, AND THE ARBITER IS NAMED.** This math sizes the owner's **detention basins for permitting**. Any move off-thread must be **byte-identical**, and the arbiter is **`test/pondStorageGoldenMaster.test.js`** — **78 tests, exact equality, no tolerance anywhere** (verified green on this branch, 8.9 s). Its own header states the bar: *"the stored volumes did not move. Not close. EQUAL."* **No engineering number may be changed to make anything pass.** A failing golden-master assertion is a failed port, never a threshold to revisit.
- **THE ASYNC RIPPLE, SCOPED HONESTLY — this is the real cost of the item and the reason it is not small.** A worker boundary makes a currently-synchronous answer a promise, and the callers are in the RENDER PATH:
  - `pondStageModel` / `pondSplitFor` / `usablePondVolume` / `bandedStorage` are read **synchronously from the render body** (the `pondLedgerEntries` build, `SitePlanner.jsx` ~L10533 — see **B221763**). A promise there means the panel must render a PENDING state, which is a **product** change: the yield/pond panel would show "computing" where it now shows a number.
  - **PANEL-BREVITY and honesty collide here** and the resolution has to be decided before any code: a pending detention volume must not read as a computed zero, and it must not add a line to the default view.
  - **PDF-PARITY** applies — the export path reads the same numbers and must not be allowed to race a pending result.
  - The pond LABEL FIT (**B221761**) and the drainage facts pass sit downstream of the same geometry.
- **THE SHAPE THAT AVOIDS MOST OF THAT, recorded as the candidate rather than the decision:** keep a synchronous LAST-GOOD result (the memo B236592 already maintains) and let the worker refresh it, so the render body always has a number and the pending state is a staleness marker rather than a blank. Whether that is acceptable for a permitting number is the owner's call, not an implementation detail — **and it is the one question this item must not answer on its own.**
- **NOT STARTED. No worker written, no call site changed, no dependency moved.**

  were also re-run in full AFTER the split, not only before it.

### B280402 — The parcel acreage badge is armed by the cursor merely RESTING on it, so it takes press 2 of a double-click `[Site Planner / selection]` (bug) #site-planner #selection #ui #parcel  *(filed 2026-08-09 — diagnosed from the owner's live `__plannerHitWhy` read on cf4f77b and then REPRODUCED in the sandbox. Minted **B280402 / V78961** from this branch's reserved block B280400–B280415, against origin/main cf4f77b. **DEDUPE-FIRST — this is CHROME-NEVER-EATS-A-PRESS's SIXTH instance and the acreage badge's THIRD appearance** (B1327 gated it on selection; B1327/NEW-4 re-gated it on HOVER so it could be dragged; this is that hover gate biting). Searched Open / ⏳ Verify / Done across `acreage`, `badge`, `chip`, `hoverChipId`, `polylabel`, `B1186`, `B1327`, `B233153`, `B278576`, `B280400`: **B278576** is the anchor rule and is intact — his FIRST gesture passes because of it; **B280400** is the repeat symptom and is CLOSED BY THIS. Net-new number.)*
`[x]` **Shipped — reproduced, fixed at the resolver, and the audit row he predicted goes red on cf4f77b.**
- Verify: live → **V78961** (`Blocker: real-data` — his re-run of the exact table).
- Origin: diagnosed 2026-08-09 from his live instrument read; shipped the same session.
- **HIS READING, which is the whole diagnosis.** Same point (673,414), nothing selected, `grips === 0` in both states — only the stack differs: after touching the POND, `target el:e79463haroul`, stack `["el:e79463haroul"]`; after touching the STUB, `target parcel:e79379lfxyni`, stack `["parcel:e79379lfxyni", "el:e79463haroul"]`. **The parcel does not move above the stub — IT ENTERS. The stub is still there, second, unchanged.**
- **⛔ AND IT IS NOT THE DOM, which he ruled out directly:** the stub's node is index 99 of 521 in BOTH states, computed `pointerEvents` is `"auto"` on the node AND its parent in BOTH, same total node count. Not paint order, not re-parenting, not a pointer-events flip on the stub. **The parcel BECOMES hit-testable.**
- **THE CAUSE.** The acreage badge renders `pointerEvents={draggable ? "auto" : "none"}` where `draggable = tool === "select" && hoverChipId === pc.id`. **`hoverChipId` is a HOVER latch** — B1327/NEW-4 moved the gate from selection to hover precisely so the badge could be dragged (the selection gate was unreachable: the badge sits at `polylabel`, on top of a building, so pressing it selected the building and the lot never became selected). But **a cursor resting on a point is exactly what a cursor does between the two presses of a double-click.** So the badge arms itself mid-gesture, and because it paints after the element bands it wins the hit test — over a feature smaller than its own chrome, there is nothing else to win it. That also explains every discriminator: the pond click **moves the cursor away** and disarms it; a six-second wait does not, because the cursor never moved.
- **THE FIX — the badge is a GRIP, so it is identity-transparent, exactly like the handle layer.** New `data-chrome` marker (`lib/featureTarget.js` `CHROME_ATTR`), flagged by `stackEntries` alongside `data-handle-layer`, so the resolver looks THROUGH it. **DELIVERY IS UNTOUCHED:** the badge keeps its own `pointerEvents`, its own `onPointerDown` and its own drag — only "which feature was double-clicked" changes, the same B233153 rule one layer out. The lot is still reachable by its own body underneath, so double-clicking a lot still opens the Parcel panel.
- **REPRODUCED, then proven both ways.** Sandbox fixture: a lot whose `polylabel` puts its badge on a 6-px road stub. Pre-fix the stack reads `["parcel:zzlot", "el:zzstub"]` and the gesture selects the lot; post-fix both gestures read `["el:zzstub"]` and open Properties. **The audit row he predicted goes RED on cf4f77b** and names the cause in its own message — *"with the cursor merely hovering, this point resolves to parcel:zzlot1 instead"*.
- **THE GUARD — a HOVER-ARMED-CHROME invariant, run for every feature.** Park the cursor on the probe point, let it arm whatever it arms, and re-ask the resolver: it must still name this feature. **Nothing in the suite read the DOM after a plain HOVER before** — every other check reads after a click, which is why this was invisible. Audit **266/266** (pre-fix: 7 red). Counted as OBSERVED so it cannot rot into a silent pass.

### B280403 — The instrument that answers "why did it fail on HIS machine" could not be armed on his machine `[Infra / Testing]` (task) #infra #testing  *(filed 2026-08-09 from the owner's note against the instrument this program shipped him one round earlier. Minted **B280403** from this branch's reserved block. **DEDUPE-FIRST** — searched `__PLANYR_E2E`, `hook`, `gated`, `E2E`, `diag`, `B233153`, `B278576`: every planner probe uses the same mount-time gate and this is the first time one needed to answer on a PRODUCTION tab, so it is a new item rather than a recurrence.)*
`[x]` **Shipped.**
- Verify: sandbox — 11 unit tests incl. the hostile-environment cases, plus source guards that the gate cannot move back onto the effect.
- Origin: filed 2026-08-09 from chat; shipped the same session.
- **The gap, in his words and it is exact.** `__plannerHitWhy` is gated on `window.__PLANYR_E2E`, which is FALSE in production — **so as shipped it could not diagnose the owner's live session, which is the only place the bug exists.** He got in by setting the flag by hand and then forcing a `SitePlanner` remount by switching plans and switching back, because the hook's effect has `[]` deps and reads the flag at mount. **That worked, and it is folklore, not a feature:** it requires knowing the dependency array.
- **THE FIX, two halves.** The gate is read at **CALL time**, not at mount — the hooks are installed unconditionally and answer `null` until armed, so arming can never require a remount. And there is a way in that needs no console and no source dive: **`?planyrDiag=1`** on the URL, which **latches into `sessionStorage`** so an in-app plan switch (the planner navigates by hash) does not disarm it mid-diagnosis. `window.__PLANYR_E2E` still works, so every existing harness is untouched.
- **⛔ THE SAFETY BOUNDARY, and it is the whole argument:** arming exposes READ-ONLY resolution diagnostics — what a double-click at a point would address, and the facts behind that answer. It writes nothing, changes no behaviour, and is SESSION-scoped so it cannot leak into a later visit. **It is not a debug mode and must never gate anything that mutates.** Pure half in `lib/diagArm.js`, so the rule is testable without a browser.
- Recorded beside FOREGROUND-OR-VOID in `/CLAUDE.md`.

Two full cycles, no exceptions.
- **THE DISCRIMINATORS, and they are what make this a latch rather than a race.** `A` stub first → PASS. `B` stub repeat after a **six second** wait → **FAIL** (so it is NOT a time-based expiry). `C` stub repeat after **one single click on the pond** → **PASS** (so touching ANOTHER FEATURE resets it). `D` stub repeat immediately → FAIL. **Deselecting to empty canvas does NOT reset it** — every run above verified `grips === 0` first, which clears the SELECTION but not whatever the gesture is keyed on.

Both are now structurally impossible: **no dependency array** (it runs after every commit, so no press can be missed) and **a cleared selection clears the anchor**. "Press 1 keeps the anchor" is now decided by the PRESS — if the held anchor is still live for this press it stands, whoever it names — rather than by the old `held.key !== key` clause, which could only ever hold an anchor against a *different* feature.
- **⛔ SCOPE, STATED PLAINLY BECAUSE IT IS THE DIFFERENCE BETWEEN A FIX AND A HOPE: THIS SANDBOX DOES NOT REPRODUCE HIS SECOND-GESTURE FAILURE.** The new repeat-gesture row passes on the very build it fails on for him — on the seeded stub, on the tiny-paving, and on all 28 fixture features. So the latch above is a REAL defect that is proven red-then-green here, but it is **not proven to be his cause**, and this item is not closed on it. Shipping a confident "fixed" on that evidence is the B1434 blind-fix failure; the honest disposition is **fix what is provable, instrument the rest, and let his re-run be the verdict** (NEVER-PARK: the disposition taken is **INSTRUMENT IT SO IT CAPTURES ITSELF**, plus a live V#).
- **THE INSTRUMENT, which is the real deliverable here.** `window.__plannerHitWhy(x, y)` (E2E-gated, read-only, nulled on unmount) returns the three facts that DECIDE the verdict rather than the verdict alone: **what the anchor names and how old it is** (`{key, ageMs, dx, dy}`), **whether it still applies**, **what the selection is**, and **the top of the hit stack**. If his re-run still fails, that call names the cause in one line instead of costing another round of reconstruction. Asked before or after the gesture — never between the presses (see below).
- **THE GUARD HE ASKED FOR — a REPEAT-GESTURE row, run for EVERY feature**, not just the stub: double-click, verify, deselect (verified `grips === 0`), double-click the same point again. Nothing in the suite repeated a gesture on the same target before, which is why a live check that clicks each element ONCE passes 36 of 36 and ships green through exactly this. Audit **237/237**; the e2e spec adds a deselect-clears-the-anchor case that is **mutation-proven RED on 697e5e0**.
- **STOPPING RULE:** closed when his re-run of the exact table above passes twice in a row on two features, or when `__plannerHitWhy` names a cause that this session's fix does not cover — in which case that cause is filed and fixed on its own number.
