- **WHAT THE OLD BAR COST.** B1345's bar — byte-identical, or one unit of 255 on one channel — is a measurement of the FILE. It refused B1350's 424-node dock-door fold twice, the second time (PR #921) for a cause that turned out to be that Chromium does not rasterise a `<rect>` and a rectangular `<path>` to the same antialiased edge **at any zoom**, so no gate could ever have satisfied it.
- **THE CONSTRUCTION, and it is the substance of the item.** A raw diff cannot tell **the same ink moved a sub-pixel** (invisible) from **a line of ink removed** (a downgrade) — both read ~23/255, and refusing both is exactly what byte-identity did, at the price of refusing every representation change forever. So both renders are low-pass filtered **at two scales** before comparison: one near visual acuity (which bounds how far any single sample may stray) and one inside the eye's high-sensitivity band (which is what the eye actually receives after it integrates). The colour metric is **CIEDE2000**, not a channel delta — 10/255 in a dark blue and 10/255 in a light yellow are nothing alike to a viewer, which is the second reason "23/255" was never an answer to "can he see it".
- **THE BAR, three magnitudes:** detail ΔE00 ≤ **6.0** · perceived ΔE00 ≤ **1.0** (the classical just-noticeable difference; the figure usually quoted for ordinary viewing is ~2.3 and we deliberately took the strict end) · perceived frame-mean ΔE00 ≤ **0.10**. **Coverage is REPORTED but does not gate** — an earlier draft capped the share of the frame allowed to differ and it was removed before shipping, because for an antialiasing-class change the pixels touched scale with the total EDGE LENGTH IN THE DRAWING, i.e. with how much is drawn rather than how much changed; a dense plan would have failed for being dense.
- **THE VIEWING GEOMETRY IS STATED, NOT ASSUMED.** 20/20 acuity (1 arcmin), 600 mm viewing distance, 0.50 mm per CSS pixel (a 27″ 2560-wide panel at his measured dpr ~2.15) → **one CSS pixel subtends ~2.9 arcmin**. All three are parameters, every run prints the ones it used, and the two this repo cannot measure from a sandbox — his panel's physical width and how far he sits from it — are on `OWNER-TODO.md`.
- **WHAT SHIPPED.** `ui-audit/lib/perceptualDiff.mjs` (pure: sRGB→linear→Lab, CIEDE2000, separable Gaussian **in linear light** — averaging gamma-encoded values is not averaging light, and the whole claim rests on ink averaging back) + `ui-audit/verify-perceptual-parity.mjs`, which drives two builds at a zoom ladder and prints every number plus the geometry, never a bare verdict. The **engine is unchanged**: the same dependency-free PNG decoder (`lib/pngDiff.mjs`) B1345 built.
- **⛔ THE FIRST REAL USE REJECTED THE CHANGE IT WAS INTRODUCED FOR, and the bar was left alone.** B1350's fold came in at perceived ΔE00 **1.20–2.19** against 1.0. The one modelling parameter the verdict turns on (`PERCEIVED_ARCMIN` = 6, the half-period at the contrast-sensitivity peak; 12 would roughly halve every figure) was chosen **before** the measurement and deliberately not touched **after**. Picking a threshold to suit a result you have already seen is not a measurement — and a bar that rubber-stamps the first thing put in front of it would be worth nothing.
- **Guard.** `test/perceptualParity.test.js` (37): CIEDE2000 against **Sharma/Wu/Dalal's published test vectors** — that formula has more special cases than anything else in this repo (the hue-average wrap, the zero-chroma branch, the blue-region rotation) and a subtly wrong one would still return plausible small numbers, the most dangerous shape a metric can have — plus the discriminator itself (ink moved a sub-pixel PASSES, the same magnitude of ink REMOVED fails, and the two separate by more than 3×, with a companion assertion that a raw channel diff ranks them the wrong way round), and all three thresholds pinned by value.
- **The rule is written into `/CLAUDE.md` as PERCEPTUAL-PARITY**, naming that it supersedes B1345 for LOD-class changes, that the threshold is chosen before the measurement, and that every picture-altering change records a before/after crop.
- **Tests.** `npm test` 8,266 green · lint 0 errors · build green · `perf-bundle-audit` inside the band (this item is dev tooling only — no app bytes).

- **THE PREMISE, and it was a good one:** the symptom (appears only after interaction, clears on reload, ~278 MB tab) fits a compositor/raster problem, and a JS CPU profile — every instrument the speed program had — would never see it. So the browser side was measured explicitly.
- **⛔ THE BLOCKER THAT HAS ENDED EVERY MEMORY INVESTIGATION IN THIS REPO IS NOW REMOVED.** Every external tile host is unreachable here, so Leaflet created its tile `<img>` elements but **nothing ever decoded** — no bitmap, no texture upload. `ui-audit/lib/fakeTile.mjs` now serves a real, decodable PNG for every tile request (`--fake-tiles`), so Chromium does the actual work: decode, bitmap allocation, texture upload, compositing, eviction. **Every tile's bytes are UNIQUE by construction** — Chromium caches decoded images by content, so one shared fixture would have meant ONE decoded bitmap shared N ways and a tile cache that looked free. That false negative is the exact failure this file exists to avoid, and it is unit-tested (`test/fakeTile.test.js`, including a real CRC walk of the PNG chunks — a malformed PNG fires `error` instead of `load` and would silently reproduce the blocked-host run it replaced).
- **(a) COMPOSITOR LAYERS AND RASTER MEMORY — measured, FLAT.** Read from CDP `LayerTree`, not inferred. With imagery absent: **7 layers**, flat 0 → 1000. With tiles decoding at dpr 1: **43 → 45**. At **dpr 2: 112 → 114**, raster proxy **35.62 → 36.12 MB**. Layers are numerous — and they do not multiply with interaction.
- **(b) RETAINED vs GARBAGE — CLASSIFIED, which is what the item said mattered most.** The owner measured the heap climbing 35 → 114 MB over 600 gestures without forcing GC and could not tell garbage from retention. Forced-GC readings plus full heap snapshots at both ends: **retained heap grows 0.9–2.1 KB per gesture and PLATEAUS** (16.96 → 17.33 → 17.48 MB over the last 850 gestures). The snapshot diff is **+0.75 to +1.46 MB total**, and **every top class is a JIT artifact** — `[code]`, `system / TrustedByteArray [code]`, `system / WeakArrayList`, instruction streams. That is V8 compiling hot functions: self-limiting, and the opposite of a leak. **No application object class appears anywhere in the growth list.** So the owner's ~130 KB/gesture was **garbage, not retention**.
- **(c) DETACHED DOM — REFUTED OUTRIGHT, and not by a proxy.** `lib/heapSnapshot.mjs` reads V8's own per-node `detachedness` flag: **0 detached nodes, 0 KB**, in all three regimes. (The probe also carries a `detachedApprox` counter — renderer-wide nodes minus attached nodes — which is an UPPER BOUND that also catches shadow and adopted trees, so it can clear a suspect but never convict one. The snapshot is the answer; the counter is the cheap screen. The parser **refuses to quote a detached figure at all** from a snapshot with no detachedness column, because a zero meaning "not measured" is exactly the reassuring number that must never be printed.)
- **(d) TOTAL INTERACTIONS vs SINCE-LAST-IDLE — neither.** The `idle` control arm holds time-since-load, probe count and GC opportunity equal at zero gestures. Cost is flat on both axes; there is no cleanup that never runs, because there is nothing accumulating for it to run on.
- **(e) THE B65 GHOST AND THE TILE CACHE — bounded, and now demonstrated rather than reasoned about.** **7,943 tiles were served, decoded and uploaded** across 1,000 retina gestures and **107 were retained at the end** (105 at N=0). At dpr 1: **6,084 served, 38 retained**. Leaflet's pruning plus `capTileCache` / `boundTileCache` are doing exactly their job. No eviction, teardown or lifetime change is warranted, and none is made — the authorisation to cap retained memory is not a licence to cap something that is already flat.
- **THE OWNER'S "LEAFLET TILE RETENTION LOOKS WRONG" IS EXPLAINED, AND IT IS NOT A LEAK.** He saw ~164 tiles on a fresh load. Measured here: **36 at dpr 1, 105 at dpr 2** on the identical scene. The multiplier is `detectRetina` — on a HiDPI display Leaflet fetches one zoom level DEEPER, roughly four times the tiles for the same ground, which is the sharp-aerial trade `lib/tileBudget.js` `retinaForZoom` makes deliberately and which the owner's standing constraint protects. 36 × ~4 ≈ 144, against his 164. **The count is high by design and it is FLAT with pan/zoom count** (+2 over a thousand gestures).
- **⚠ WHAT THIS STILL CANNOT SETTLE, stated rather than implied.** The tile BYTES are synthetic and the network is local: real imagery over a real connection is a different load (transfer, cache pressure, decode of far more varied content), and this reference plan is a floor, not a match, for the owner's heaviest signed-in plans. What is now proven is the MECHANISM — decode, bitmap, texture, eviction — not the magnitude on his machine. `Blocker: real-data`.

See **B1434** for where it can still live, in order, and for the decision not to ship a fix against a table that named no mechanism.
- **Report.** Working in the Site map, memory climbs and interaction degrades; **Ctrl+Shift+R** (a hard reload, confirmed with the owner — not spacebar pan) restores speed only briefly. That the fix is a fresh document is load-bearing: the degradation **accumulates over the session**.

- **CONSTRAINT CHANGE, recorded exactly as the owner stated it.** He now authorises capping **RETAINED MEMORY** — tile eviction, ghost lifetime, overlay teardown. He does **NOT** authorise any drawing-quality or drawing-quantity downgrade: no blanket retina downgrade, no geometry decimation at working zooms, no spinner gating, no removing the B65 ghost buffer. **V483(a) passed precisely because retina was not traded away, and the aerial sharpness matters to him.** Evict aggressively, render at full quality.
- **FOUND AND FIXED — the coarse z13 BACKFILL layer had no ceiling at all.** `SitePlanner.jsx` bound `boundTileCache` to the DETAIL layer only. The backfill was created with `preserveTilesAcrossSetView` **and a keepBuffer two rings LARGER** than the detail layer, and nothing ever capped it — so its `_tiles` map grew for the length of the session, shedding only when Leaflet's incidental pruning happened to fire. At z13 each tile covers a large area, so panning a metro accumulates them steadily. This is retained decoded-image memory: **invisible to the instrument the previous verdict was based on.** It now carries its own ceiling, computed from its own (larger) keepBuffer. `capTileCache` never evicts a CURRENT tile, so this cannot punch a hole in the view or cost a pixel of sharpness — it is squarely inside the authorised scope.
- **Checked and found already correct (AUDIT-FIRST, so the next session doesn't re-investigate):** the detail layer's cap IS wired and detached on teardown; `releaseLayer` IS called on both layers when the basemap is toggled/switched; the ghost clone is bounded at one instance (`dropGhost()` precedes every spawn) with a 5 s backstop plus a `load` release.
- **⚠ WHAT I COULD NOT MEASURE, stated plainly rather than implied.** The owner asked for retained-tile counts and estimated decoded bytes over a multi-minute session. **That measurement cannot run in this sandbox: Chromium here cannot reach ANY external host, so aerial tiles never paint and there are no retained tiles to count.** `measureUserAgentSpecificMemory()` is separately unavailable on planyr.io. So the backfill fix is proven by reading the code and by unit tests over the budget maths — **its magnitude in MB is unknown**, and it is entirely possible it is not the whole of (a). The remaining suspects the owner named and I could not weigh: dynamic image overlays that re-fetch a full-view PNG per pan, and cumulative detached DOM. `Blocker: live-GIS`.
- **Tests.** `test/tileBudget.test.js` gains a NEW-1 block: a larger keepBuffer earns a larger but still FINITE ceiling; eviction never sheds a `current` tile (so capping cannot degrade the aerial) and sheds furthest-first; plus a source guard that BOTH tile layers are capped and both caps are detached.
- **Sandbox evidence.** `npm test` 6261 green (371 files) · lint 0 errors · build green.

And an explicit read on complaint **(b)**, which nothing here addresses.

### B1431 — The four seconds nobody could account for, ATTRIBUTED: a boot timeline with named phases `[Infra / Testing]` (task) #infra #testing #perf #site-planner  *(filed 2026-08-06 from the owner chat block as NEW-1 of the speed program's phase 3, whose instruction was explicit: **DO NOT FIX ANYTHING IN THIS ITEM — the deliverable is the BREAKDOWN.** Minted **B1431 / V710** LATE via `git fetch origin main && npm run next-id -- --against-main`, as the last step before push; the code, tests and commits keep the provisional `NEW-1` label. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open + ⏳ Verify + Done across `timeToFirstDrag`, `boot`, `TTFD`, `perf-harness`, `B1121`, `B1344`, `B1349`, `B1358`, `B1086`, `B1163`: **B1344** rebuilt the SCENE and the GESTURE the harness measures and is the direct predecessor, **B1358** fixed that harness's boot-chunk race, **B1086** its hidden-tab trap, **B1349** owns the chunks fetched at boot, **B1121(b)** is the owner's original *"still sluggish immediately after a reload"* report. Every one of them measures or fixes ONE thing inside the boot; not one of them attributes the WINDOW. Net-new.)*
- **THE DELIVERABLE IS THE BREAKDOWN, and nothing in this item is a fix — that was the dispatch's explicit instruction.** What shipped is the instrument: `--boot-timeline` in `ui-audit/perf-harness.mjs`, driven by `ui-audit/lib/bootTimeline.mjs` (+ `ui-audit/lib/sourceMapIndex.mjs`, a dependency-free source-map reader, so a production profile names `lib/roadGeometry.js` instead of `SitePlannerApp-BxMJopPJ.js:7`). Unit-tested in `test/bootTimeline.test.js` (17 assertions); protocol + limits in `docs/PERF-BUDGETS.md`.
- **THE HEADLINE, and it kills the framing the whole question was asked in: THE FOUR SECONDS ARE NOT WAITING. THEY ARE WORK.** Across the boot window the main thread is **idle 116 ms out of 8,076 ms — 1.4%**, and every wall segment after the HTML arrives measures **98–100% busy**. There is no network stall, no timer gap, nothing to overlap. (This sandbox blocks every external host, so the tiles/GIS/Supabase are ABSENT rather than slow — which makes every figure below a LOWER BOUND, and makes everything found here local work the owner's machine pays too.)
- **THE WALL SPINE** — median of 3 interleaved reps at 4× throttle, time-to-first-drag median **7,927 ms** (per-rep segments sum exactly to that rep's own total; these are per-row medians, so they sum a little differently):

  | ms | segment |
  |---:|---|
  | 37 | navigation → HTML received |
  | 23 | HTML → the first app script starts |
  | **1,201** | first script → **first contentful paint** |
  | **3,573** | first paint → **the planner canvas element exists** |
  | 339 | canvas exists → canvas finished drawing |
  | **1,421** | canvas drawn → **the press is delivered to the page** |
  | **1,638** | press delivered → the release is delivered |
  | 124 | release → drag serviced (TIME TO FIRST DRAG) |

- **THE ATTRIBUTION** — the same window by named phase (median ms · % of 8,076 ms of samples). Anything no rule can name is charged to an explicit UNATTRIBUTED row, which came in at **0.8%**:

  | ms | % | phase |
  |---:|---:|---|
  | 1,659 | 20.5% | V8 `(program)` — script parse / compile / VM |
  | 1,587 | 19.6% | React render & commit |
  | 1,415 | 17.5% | Planner render body (`SitePlanner.jsx`) |
  | 534 | 6.6% | Geometry vendor (Clipper) |
  | 504 | 6.2% | browser native (DOM · layout · style) |
  | 465 | 5.8% | Model load & normalisation |
  | 436 | 5.4% | Planner app & panels |
  | 378 | 4.7% | Basemap (Leaflet / Esri) |
  | 244 | 3.0% | garbage collection |
  | 238 | 2.9% | Site geometry (roads · ponds · contours) |
  | 208 | 2.6% | Label layout & collision |
  | 156 | 1.9% | App shell & routing |
  | 154 | 1.9% | GIS layers, fetches & basemap wiring |
  | **116** | **1.4%** | **idle — main thread free** |
  | 65 | 0.8% | **UNATTRIBUTED** |
  | 49 | 0.6% | Map finder |
  | 1 | 0.0% | Supabase client |

- **EVERY CANDIDATE IN THE DISPATCH, MEASURED — five of the six are small or absent:**
  - **(a) THE FOUR-SECOND COINCIDENCE — REFUTED, and it is a coincidence.** Control arm `no-drainage` seeds `settings.drainage.autoFacts = false`, which is exactly what `drainAutoEnabled` reads; the arm demonstrably fires (GIS requests during boot drop **75 → 34**). Two independent interleaved A/B runs, 3 reps each: run 1 **−1.6%** against a ±6.1% floor (INCONCLUSIVE), run 2 **−13.5%** against a ±9.6% floor (clears it). **Pooled, 6 boots per arm: baseline median 7,744 ms (7,420–8,370) vs 7,224 ms (6,772–7,445) — about −0.5 s, with the two ranges overlapping.** So the load-time drainage pass is worth a few hundred milliseconds, NOT four seconds. The arithmetic settles the coincidence on its own: B1349's idle callback is armed **after a 1,200 ms timer** with a 4,000 ms ceiling, so it can only fire between 1.2 s and 5.2 s — and with it disabled the boot still measures ~7 s with the **same shape** (first-paint → canvas 2,851 ms vs 3,573 ms). Phase 2 did NOT move this cost somewhere else; it is not this cost.
  - **(b) parcel-snapshot hydration from IndexedDB — NOT FOUND HERE, and the reason is stated rather than hidden.** All model work together (`Model load & normalisation`) is **465 ms / 5.8%**, and this scenario is a fresh profile with **no stored snapshot to hydrate**, so the durable side is unexercised. Its ceiling in this run is that 465 ms; sizing it properly needs a scenario seeded with a cached county snapshot, which does not exist yet.
  - **(c) the element-sync seed + `normalizeBondedChildren` / `normalizeStrandedZones` / `rowsToModel` — inside that same 465 ms row**, and 163 ms of it lands before first paint. Not the four seconds.
  - **(d) the first roadNet dissolve + pondContours — REAL and the largest named app cost: Clipper 534 ms + site geometry 238 ms = 772 ms (9.5%)**, essentially all of it inside the first-paint → canvas-exists segment (Clipper alone is 491 ms of that 3,573 ms). This is the one candidate that survived.
  - **(e) the first label layout / collision pass — 208 ms (2.6%).** Real, small.
  - **(f) Supabase auth + the initial site fetch — 1 ms.** Logged out and blocked: absent here, unmeasured for a signed-in load.
- **WHAT IS ACTUALLY IN THE FOUR SECONDS, in one sentence: the planner's FIRST RENDER (3.6 s, 100% busy — `SitePlanner.jsx` 968 ms · React 812 ms · Clipper 491 ms) and then THREE MORE SECONDS OF CONTINUED RE-RENDERING after the canvas is already drawn** (V8 390 ms · React 281 ms · `SitePlanner.jsx` 210 ms · Leaflet 190 ms in the first of those two segments, and the same shape in the second). The app does not stop working when it looks finished.
- **WHAT TO ATTACK, with a predicted saving each — proposals, not decisions:**
  1. **The post-draw tail (≈3.0 s, 38% of time-to-first-drag).** Nothing should be re-rendering the whole planner for three seconds after the canvas is drawn. Attribute it further with the same instrument (the boot-order of the map mount / layer sync / overscan settle are the named suspects). **Caveat that has to be settled first:** 350 basemap tile requests are BLOCKED in this sandbox, and failed-request handling is inside this window — a run on a live network could look different. Predicted saving unknown until attributed; largest addressable block by far.
  2. **The road dissolve off the first-paint critical path (Clipper 534 ms).** Predicted **≈400–500 ms**. ⚠ Deferring it changes the FIRST FRAME's picture (roads unwelded for a beat), so it is bound by the B1345 pixel bar; persisting the dissolve across a reload is the version that is not.
  3. **Parse / compile, 1,659 ms (20.5%).** The only lever is fewer boot-path bytes (B1064 / B1130 territory). A 20% cut ≈ **330 ms**.
  4. **The first React commit, 1,587 ms.** ~1,000 canvas nodes on first mount; deferring non-canvas chrome to after first interaction. Predicted **100–300 ms**, and it is the riskiest of the four for what the user sees.
  5. **The load-time drainage pass, ≈0.5 s** — already an owner decision on **B1349**, now with a measured price against it.
- **⚠ TWO LIMITS ON EVERY NUMBER ABOVE.** (i) The last two spine segments include the harness's own CDP round trips for the press and the drag; the page was 98% busy through them, so the lag is real in kind, but the millisecond figure is instrument-shaped. (ii) Source-map naming needs `npx vite build --sourcemap`; without it the run degrades to chunk granularity and says so.
`[~]` **AMENDED 2026-08-06 (NEW-4) — THE POST-DRAW TAIL, MEASURED WITH AND WITHOUT THE PRIME SUSPECT. IT SURVIVES.**
- **Why this run exists.** Residue item 1 above named the post-draw tail as "the largest addressable block by far" and named the load-time drainage pass among the suspects. The owner's amendment then removed that pass entirely (**B1442**) and instructed the measurement be taken **both ways anyway** — *"if the cliff survives the removal we need to know that, and if it does not, that is the answer to the whole thread."*
- **The two arms**, `--boot-timeline`, 4× CPU throttle, one rep each: `main` (facts pass auto ON) vs this branch (manual only, nothing fetched on open).

  | segment | auto ON | manual | Δ |
  | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
  | first script → first contentful paint | 933.8 ms | 863.7 ms | −70 |
  | first paint → canvas element exists | 2,542.0 ms | 2,472.8 ms | −69 |
  | canvas exists → canvas drawn | 364.7 ms | 328.7 ms | −36 |

- **⛔ THE CLIFF SURVIVES, and that is the finding.** With no timer, no idle ceiling and nothing fetched on open, the app still spends **2.2 seconds working after the canvas is already drawn**. Both post-draw segments measure **98–99% busy** — V8 parse/compile at 254–389 ms and the rest inside the planner's own re-rendering. It is continued re-rendering, not waiting. **The drainage pass is not the cliff.**

It **amends B1008** — specifically the widening of its `collapseFt` from a flat 1.5 ft to `max(1.5, travelW/4)` — without reopening it: that widening is correct for a FRESH connect and is left byte-for-byte intact.
- **The mechanism, measured on his rows rather than inferred.** Of the four candidate causes in the brief it is the fourth, produced by the first: **the junction re-solves on release and reverts.** A tee is stored as a control point spliced into the HOST road's alignment, and `planRoadConnect` routed every tee — including one that already existed — through `insertRoadVertex`'s reuse rule. That rule's tolerance scales with the host's width, and his host (`e1454717dshobp`) is a 100 ft aisle, so it is **25 ft**. The endpoint being dragged was already welded to that node, so any drop within 25 ft "reused" it and the endpoint was welded straight back to where it started. **The ghost tracked the cursor the entire drag**, which is why it reads as "stuck" rather than as "nothing is grabbable". Past 25 ft it did move — and spliced a SECOND node in, leaving the original behind (host 9 pts → 10).
- **The correction he wants is ~18 ft. The dead zone was 25 ft.** So his adjustment did literally nothing, every attempt.
- **A SECOND stuck mechanism, found while reproducing and fixed with it.** `findRoadConnect` ranks candidates by distance to the pavement EDGE (`max(0, d − halfW)`, B961), which **saturates**: on a 100 ft road that is 0 for every point within ~50 ft of the centerline, so a strict `<` comparison resolved a 50 ft-wide band of ties by SCAN ORDER, not proximity. Sliding along a wide host that way kept resolving to the first segment scanned — whose clamped projection is the shared vertex itself. `dist` stays edge-relative (B961's cross-target fairness is untouched); ties now break on the raw centerline distance, which does not saturate.
- **Fix.** New pure `teeNodeIndex` (which host control point is this endpoint already welded to — interior only; an endpoint meet is a WELD and must not move the host's extent) + `slideTeeNode` (drop the held node, re-project onto what is left so a slide PAST a neighbour re-sequences instead of folding the alignment back on itself, splice it in at its new home). `planRoadConnect` takes `opts.fromPt` — the endpoint's pre-drag coordinate — and `startRoadVtx` stashes it. The reuse tolerance on a SLIDE is the tight `ROAD_VERTEX_COLLAPSE_FT`, never the width-scaled one: a slide is a deliberate repositioning of a node that already exists, so the only thing worth collapsing onto is a true coincidence.
- **Result on his geometry:** the tee slides continuously in both directions and stays where it is dropped, at every distance tested from 1 ft to 80 ft; the host keeps its 9 control points at every one of them (the debris path is gone, not just the dead zone).
- **Sandbox-verified:** new `test/roadTeeSlide.test.js` (28 cases on his real rows, incl. two that pin the PRE-FIX behaviour explicitly) — mutation-checked twice, disabling the slide branch and removing the saturation tie-break each turns it red. New `e2e/road-tee-slide.spec.js` (11 specs) drives the REAL app: select the connecting road, press its tee handle, drag along the host, release, read the committed model back — proven red on a pre-fix build. Fixture `ui-audit/fixtures/goose-creek-tee-slide.json` (all six roads: the load-time simplify only protects a host control point another road PINS, so a partial road set silently deletes one and the plan stops being his).
- **Live-verify (V674):** on his signed-in Goose Creek plan, grab the tee where the road between the buildings meets the 100′ aisle and slide it a few feet along that aisle — it goes where he puts it and stays there, and the 100′ aisle grows no extra grips.

A perpendicular snap had been designed against the wrong reading and was **discarded unbuilt**. Minted **B1383 / V675** (renumbered from a provisional B1380/V673) via `--against-main`, LATE; code/tests keep the provisional `NEW-2` label. Same branch. Same real plan as B1382.)*
`[ ]` **⏳ merged — V675 PENDING (Verify: live — `Blocker: real-data`).**
- **The owner's hypothesis, CONFIRMED on his geometry.** The connecting road's far end is anchored (a drive junction into a truck court), so the tee is the free end and **its position along the host is exactly what sets the road's absolute bearing**. Measured: the leg the tee governs sits **9.4° off the cardinal axis**; the cardinal is **18.4 ft south along the host** — and the B1382 dead zone was 25 ft. So the stuck tee was not merely inconvenient, it was the whole reason he could not get the bearing he wanted. Bearings here are TRUE bearings: the feet frame is axis-aligned to north (`mapLock.feetToLatLngPair`), no rotation.
- **AUDIT-FIRST, question 1 — was a bearing readout already there? NO.** Every `bearing`/`azimuth` in the workspace belongs to metes-and-bounds deed parsing or the deed basis-of-bearings check; nothing in the road tools reported one. So a few degrees off north was pure eyeball — exactly the frustration described. **Added:** a live bearing readout on the road-vertex drag, transient (drag only, so it costs the default view nothing — PANEL-BREVITY), reading degrees clockwise from north.
- **AUDIT-FIRST, question 2 — was a cardinal/angle snap already there? YES, and it was DEAD here.** Holding Shift while dragging a road vertex already locks the leg to 45° increments (`snap45` — due N/S/E/W plus the diagonals). On a junction drag it computed a locked point and the connect magnet then **overwrote it**, so the lock silently did nothing at exactly the moment it was wanted. **Made to apply** rather than newly invented: `cardinalTeePoint` composes the two — round the leg's bearing to the nearest increment, intersect that ray with the host, and slide the connection to the crossing, so the leg lands on an exact cardinal AND stays welded to the host. Releasing Shift is the override; Alt still bypasses connecting entirely.
- **The subtlety that made a first attempt refuse to fire:** the cardinal crossing routinely lands on a DIFFERENT leg of the host than the cursor is over (on his plan the crossing is one control point back from where his cursor was), so the ray is intersected against the host's WHOLE alignment and the crossing nearest the free point wins. The reported segment index travels with the point, because that index is what the tee is spliced into.
- **Scope held deliberately.** The owner asked to be able to place the road where he wants it; he did not ask for a bearing-constraint system. No perpendicular snap, no per-road bearing field, no constraint solver.
- **Sandbox-verified:** covered by `test/roadTeeSlide.test.js` (the NEW-2 group: true-compass bearings, the confirmed tee↔bearing dependency, the named 18.4 ft slide, the cross-leg crossing, the honest refusals) + 4 specs in `e2e/road-tee-slide.spec.js` (the readout appears on drag and clears on release; Shift reports `cardinal`; the leg lands on a true cardinal and is still a tee; without Shift the lock does not fire).
- **Live-verify (V675):** on his signed-in Goose Creek plan, drag that tee and watch the bearing number follow the road; hold Shift and it snaps to the cardinal and says so; let go of Shift and it is free again.

### B1359 — The drawing↔basemap registration layout effect is the largest named item in a zoom frame `[Site Planner / UI]` (task) #site-planner #perf #ui  *(found 2026-07-31 by `ui-audit/diagnose-zoom-cost.mjs --profile`, the instrument built for the phase-2 speed block. **Filed deliberately, NOT fixed** — it is a change to the code B1122 / B1141 / B1189 have each already had to correct, and the effect's own comment names the change as deliberately unshipped; it needs its own verification and its own item. Minted via `--against-main`. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open + ⏳ Verify + Done across `regShift`, `registration`, `mapLock`, `B1122`, `B1141`, `B1142`, `B1189`: **B1122** moved the write into a layout effect, **B1141/B1142** made the shift measured rather than assumed, **B1189** stopped it re-running on state identity. Every one of those is about the effect being CORRECT; none is about it being expensive. Net-new.)*
- A CPU sample profile across a 40-event wheel gesture at 4x throttle puts the registration layout effect at **9.2% of all script self-time** with the inspector closed and **12%** with it docked — the largest single named entry after V8's own unattributed `(program)` bucket. `setAttribute` and a synchronous `getBoundingClientRect` inside it account for several points more.
- Its own source comment already names the fix: *"The larger win — taking `regShift` out of React state entirely and writing both transforms — DELIBERATELY unshipped."* That is still the shape.
- **⛔ Read `B1122` / `B1141` / `B1189` before touching it.** It is load-bearing for the drawing sitting on the imagery, it must stay pre-paint (VIEWPORT-STABLE), and it has taken the planner down once (B1189's fifty-render abort).

`[~]` **AMENDED 2026-08-06 (speed program phase 3, NEW-2) — the MECHANISM is now measured, one half of phase 2's diagnosis is REFUTED, and the fix is deliberately NOT shipped. Nothing in the render path changed.**
- **The instrument got better first.** `ui-audit/diagnose-zoom-cost.mjs --profile` now resolves its frames through the build's source maps (shared with the boot timeline's reader), and a new `--profile-tree <substring>` opens a named frame up into its own call tree. Phase 2 could say "the registration layout effect is 9.2% of script"; it could not say which line, what it called, or where the time went inside it.
- **CONFIRMED, and it is the largest single app frame in a zoom profile.** Interleaved A/B, 3 reps each way at 4× throttle (closed · Yield docked · closed · …): the effect (`SitePlanner.jsx` → the `useLayoutEffect` at line 2751) measures **11.3% of script self-time closed and 13.1% docked**, in absolute terms **1,471 ms → 1,776 ms across a 40-event gesture (+21%)**, with the two arms' ranges NOT overlapping (closed 1,383–1,586 · docked 1,690–1,957).
- **REFUTED — `setAttribute` does NOT rise with a panel docked.** Phase 2 recorded 4.9% → 8%; measured again here it goes the other way, **1,480 ms → 1,312 ms (11.4% → 10.0%)**, with the arms' ranges heavily overlapped. Half of phase 2's stated mechanism does not reproduce. (What DOES rise on the panel arm besides the effect: number formatting, 3.3% → 5.2% — the panel re-formats its numbers every frame.)
- **⚠ AND THE HEADLINE ITSELF IS INCONCLUSIVE TODAY.** The +20% panel-open frame penalty phase 2 reported comes out **+6.7% (closed median 250 ms · docked 267 ms) against a ±6.6% noise floor measured on the closed arm's own repeats** — it does not clear its floor. The mechanism below is confirmed; the headline it was meant to explain is not, on this machine on this day. Both are reported rather than the convenient one.
- **WHY IT COSTS — a FORCED SYNCHRONOUS LAYOUT, not the state dispatch.** The effect reads `wrap.clientWidth` / `wrap.clientHeight` (and, in the tile branch, `getBoundingClientRect`) *inside a layout effect*, i.e. immediately after React has mutated the DOM — so every run flushes a full layout of the just-dirtied tree. Chrome's own counters make the case quantitatively: **`LayoutCount` is flat between the arms (97–110 closed · 91–100 docked) while `LayoutDuration` rises 881 ms → 1,276 ms (+45%)**, with every docked rep above every closed rep. The effect's own self time rises by **+305 ms** while layout rises by **+395 ms** — the same money. The panel does not make the effect run more often; it makes each forced layout more expensive, because there is 142 nodes more to lay out. **That is what the "+20% panel penalty" is.**
- Its children are minor by comparison: the tile scan 136 ms, the commit path 199 ms, everything else under 20 ms.
- **THE FIX THAT WOULD WORK, costed and NOT taken this session.** `cw`/`ch` exist only to decide `sizeChanged`. React already knows every input that can change them (`size`, `geoOverscan`), so the synchronous read can be gated to the frames where a resize is *possible* and skipped entirely on a pure view gesture — the measurement is unchanged wherever it is taken, which is the property that protects the weld. Predicted saving **≈8–11% of a zoom frame**, and most of the panel-open penalty with it.
- **WHY IT IS NOT SHIPPED HERE, plainly: THIS SANDBOX CANNOT VERIFY THE WELD.** Every external tile host is blocked, so `tileRef()` never finds a loaded tile and the registration falls to its projection fallback on every run — the exact path the change would alter is the one that cannot be exercised. Shipping a change to the effect that B1122 / B1141 / B1189 each had to correct, un-verifiable, on a predicted saving, is the trade this program exists to refuse. It needs a session with a live basemap (V710).
- Verify: live
- Origin: found 2026-07-31 (speed program phase 2) · mechanism measured 2026-08-06 (phase 3, NEW-2)

### B1360 — The wheel zoom cannot reach 30 fps without taking the VIEW out of every coordinate `[Site Planner / UI]` (task) #site-planner #perf #ui  *(filed 2026-07-31 as the honest residue of the phase-2 speed block, whose stated target was a 33 ms wheel-zoom median at 4x throttle. **NOT reachable in that block, and said so loudly rather than reported as progress.** Minted via `--against-main`. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open + ⏳ Verify + Done across `memo`, `reconcil`, `transform`, `LOD`, `f2p`, `worldToScreen`, `B1345`, `B1352`: **B1345** cut how much there is to reconcile, **B1352** put a boundary around it. Neither changes the fact below, and this is a different KIND of change from either. Net-new.)*
- **THE MEASURED FACT.** `f2p` is `worldToScreen(view, …)`, so every element's pixel geometry is a function of the view. A pan or a wheel zoom therefore changes the rendered output of **every element**, and no memo can bail: `ElNode`'s memo (B1352) misses on 100% of elements during a view gesture **by construction**, which is why B1352 moved the number by less than the noise floor. Attribution of a zoom frame at 4x throttle: **script ~72%**, recalc-style ~8%, layout ~6%, paint/raster residual ~13%. There is no single item inside that 72% worth 5×.
- **THE ONLY SHAPE THAT GETS THERE** is a representation change: draw the plan in a view-INDEPENDENT space and let the view be an SVG group transform, so a gesture writes one attribute instead of re-emitting ~1,200 host elements. Then B1352's boundary becomes the mechanism by which nothing re-renders.
- **WHY IT IS NOT A ONE-SESSION CHANGE, stated so the size is not rediscovered:** stroke widths, label sizes and every LOD gate in this renderer are functions of `ppf` and would scale with the group unless individually counter-scaled; the pixel bar is byte-identical (B1345's standard); and the canvas has many sibling layers (parcels, markups, measurements, handles, GIS bands, furniture) which would all have to move together or visibly detach mid-gesture — the exact failure B1122 exists to prevent.
- **A PAN, unlike a zoom, has an EXACT version of this** (a pan is a pure translation at constant `ppf`, and a translate composes exactly), so it could land first and independently. The pan median is already 16.8 ms; its **p90 is 133 ms**, which is what that would fix.

`[~]` **AMENDED 2026-08-06 (speed program phase 3, NEW-3) — THE COSTED ROUTE TO 33 ms. No code; the dispatch asked for the plan, and the plan's honest conclusion is that the target is reachable for a PAN and is a multi-session component split for a WHEEL ZOOM.**
- **Derived from the profile already taken, re-run with source-map naming rather than re-derived.** A wheel frame at 4× throttle, panel closed, 3 interleaved reps: **script ~65% · recalc-style ~9% · layout ~8% · paint/raster residual ~15%**, and inside the script half: V8 `(program)` 25% · `setAttribute` 11% · the registration layout effect 11% (**B1359**) · react-dom + jsx-runtime ~12% · number formatting 3.3% · `getBoundingClientRect` 1.2% · label layout 1.1% · `renderElPx` 1.0% · roadNetwork 1.1% · Clipper 0.8%. **679 DOM mutation records per commit.**
- **CONSTRAINTS THAT BOUND THE PLAN, stated so no increment is costed against a cheaper bar than it has to clear:**
  - Canvas / WebGL are **rejected**, with reasons that are structural rather than aesthetic: `buildExportSvg` CLONES the live SVG, 54 of 65 e2e specs read `planner-canvas`, 39 `data-*` names are the test contract, and the accessibility tree is the SVG.
  - The B65 ghost buffer, retina, and drawing quantity are **off the table** (owner constraint: capping retained memory is authorised, a downgrade of drawing quality or quantity is not).
  - Anything that changes the picture must clear the **B1345 pixel bar**: byte-identical, or one unit of 255 on one channel.
- **THE INCREMENTS, in the order they would land:**

  | # | change | predicted | risk | what it would break |
  |---:|---|---|---|---|
  | 1 | **PAN as a group `translate`** — draw in a view-independent space for translation only; a pan writes ONE attribute instead of re-emitting ~1,200 host elements | pan p90 **133 ms → ~20 ms**; pan median already 16.8 ms | **medium** | hit-testing must add the offset; the basemap registration transform must compose with it; `data-view-offx/offy` must keep being written (harness + e2e contract). A translation cannot change any LOD gate or stroke width, so the picture is exact by construction — this is the increment whose pixel bar is free |
  | 2 | **ZOOM as a group `scale` between rungs** — re-emit geometry only when the scale crosses a threshold or the gesture settles | wheel median **~250 ms → ~40–60 ms** (the only increment that is worth a multiple) | **high** | every stroke width, label size and LOD gate is a function of `ppf` and would scale with the group. Counter-scaling strokes is `vector-effect`; counter-scaling text and re-deciding LOD is per-element work, which is the cost being removed. **Mid-gesture the picture would differ from the shipped one — the pixel bar has to be re-stated for "during a gesture" or this cannot ship** |
  | 3 | **The registration layout effect's forced layout** (B1359) | **8–11%** of the frame | medium | the drawing↔basemap weld; not verifiable in this sandbox |
  | 4 | **Memoise the panel's number formatting** (3.3% closed / 5.2% docked) | **2–4%** | low | nothing user-visible; the strings are pure functions of values that mostly do not change per frame |
  | 5 | **Cache the tile scan** in `tileRef` instead of re-querying every tile every run | **1–2%** here, more on a machine where tiles actually load | low | the "deepest z wins" rule exists to avoid sampling the coarse backfill layer — it must become structural (skip that layer) rather than a max-scan |
- **THE ARITHMETIC, said plainly: increments 3–5 sum to roughly 12–17%, which takes a 250 ms frame to about 210 ms. The target is 33 ms. Only increments 1 and 2 are worth a multiple, and only increment 2 touches the wheel.**
- **THE SIZE OF INCREMENT 2, so it is not rediscovered as a surprise.** It is a component split, not an optimisation: the canvas has many sibling layers (parcels, markups, measurements, handles, GIS bands, furniture) which must move together or visibly detach mid-gesture (the exact failure B1122 exists to prevent); `f2p` is threaded through every renderer; and the counter-scaling policy above is a product decision about what the plan looks like DURING a gesture, which is the owner's call and not an engineering one. **Estimate: increment 1 is one focused session with its own live verification; increment 2 is a multi-session project with a design decision at the front of it.** An honest "not this quarter" is a legitimate answer to it.
- Verify: live
- Origin: filed 2026-07-31 (speed program phase 2, the target it could not reach) · costed 2026-08-06 (phase 3, NEW-3)

### B1341 — One assembly, one revision: make a partial apply unrepresentable in the DATABASE, not only in the client `[Site Planner / Persistence]` (task) #site-planner #persistence #sync #infra  *(spun out of B1340, 2026-07-31, and flagged LOUDLY there and in the session reply rather than left implicit. Minted via `--against-main`. DEDUPE-FIRST: B1117 shipped the all-or-nothing GROUP COMMIT (`db/commit_elements_atomic.sql`) — that is one CALL being atomic. This is the different, larger thing: one REVISION for the assembly, so two calls cannot each be internally atomic and still disagree.)*
`[⚠]` **Open — STAGE 1 OF 3 IS NOW SHIPPED AND APPLIED TO PRODUCTION (2026-08-12). Stages 2 and 3 remain open, and the reason they were not attempted in the same session is below, not buried.**
- **⛔ AMENDMENT 2026-08-12 (owner chat block, arrived as NEW-5: "B1341 AMENDMENT, not a new item"). No new B# was minted — this is a recurrence-shaped intake and DEDUPE-FIRST governs it: the item exists, it was filed-not-built, and this is that item HAPPENING TO THE OWNER.**
  - **THE INCIDENT, as measured evidence rather than as an argument.** On plan `smsdrvzr9gzx`, a stale delete from a second tab re-applied onto rows 1.75 s old and killed two members of a five-member bonded assembly (**B377888**); the load-time heal then fabricated a physically impossible layout out of what was left and reported success (**B377890**). Both fixes shipped in the same session and both are **CLIENT-SIDE GUARDS**. They make the partial apply harder to reach. They do not make it unrepresentable, which is what this item is for — and the session watched a live tab undo a correct repair four seconds after it landed, which is the same class arriving through a door no client guard can close.
  - **STAGE 1 SHIPPED: `db/site_elements_assembly_id.sql`, applied to production 2026-08-12 and verified against the owner's own rows** (Building 3's assembly reads 5 members, 3 live — exactly the deficit B377889 is about). A nullable `assembly_id` naming the host id for a bonded element and the element's own id otherwise, plus a partial index on `(site_id, assembly_id) where deleted_at is null`. Read by nobody, written by nothing, no behaviour change. Measured before applying: 2,457 rows / 1,832 kB, so the table rewrite is milliseconds.
  - **⛔ ONE DELIBERATE DEVIATION FROM THIS ITEM'S OWN WRITTEN PLAN, recorded rather than left implicit.** The plan says *"backfilled from `attachedTo`, written by the client"*. It shipped as a **STORED GENERATED column**, so it is neither backfilled nor written by anyone — Postgres derives it from `data` on every insert and update, forever. That is strictly better for the one property stage 1 exists to establish, which is that **the grouping cannot DRIFT from the bonds it names**: a client-written column has exactly the failure mode this whole bug family is made of — two copies of one fact, written by different paths, disagreeing under a race. There is no "the client forgot to set `assembly_id`" to defend against, because the client cannot set it. The cost is that changing the expression needs another migration; that is the right trade for one `coalesce`. Guard: `test/assemblyIdColumn.test.js`, which reads the migration AND `elementSync`'s `rootIdOf` and fails if the two definitions of "assembly" drift apart.
  - **⛔ STAGE 2 SHIPPED 2026-08-12, in the same session, and applied to production. The blocker this item named for it turned out not to exist.** The stated reason to defer was that stage 2 "needs its own session with its own rejection-path self-test (the `mintGateE2E` shape)" — i.e. that a SQL guard could not be proven here. That was wrong: the repo already had the pattern, in `db/test/team_share_scope.test.sql` — a **self-rolling-back** test that runs against the real database, raises at the end to discard every fixture, and writes nothing. DANGEROUS-MEANS-UNOBSERVABLE applies exactly as written: the thing missing was an instrument, and the instrument already existed.
    - **What ships.** `db/commit_elements_group_cas.sql` — a FOURTH, defaulted parameter `p_groups jsonb`, an array of `{assembly, expected}`. Every named assembly's digest is checked BEFORE any op is applied; on any mismatch the call returns `{applied:false, groupConflict:[{assembly, expected, actual, members}]}` and **writes nothing**. Null/empty `p_groups` delegates to the 3-arg form, so no client in the wild changes behaviour. Client half: `lib/assemblyDigest.js` (the twin), `lib/groupCas.js` (the kill switch), `elementApi` (the 4-arg call + a PGRST202 latch that degrades to the 3-arg ATOMIC call, never to the per-row path), `elementSync` (`groupsFor` + `onGroupConflict`).
    - **⛔ THE GROUP REVISION IS DERIVED, NOT STORED, and that is the load-bearing choice.** The obvious design is a `group_rev` column bumped by a trigger. It was rejected for the reason this whole family exists: a stored group revision is a SECOND copy of a fact the row revs already carry, maintained by a different path, and two copies of one fact disagreeing under a race IS the defect. The digest is `string_agg(id || ':' || rev, ',' order by id)` over LIVE rows — it cannot drift from the revs because it IS the revs. Kept a plain STRING rather than a hash so a mismatch names which member moved, straight off the wire.
    - **⛔ AND THE MUTATION CHECK EARNED ITS KEEP — one of these tests was VACUOUS and passed on a deliberately wrong build.** The first "the digest covers every member" test moved the WHOLE assembly, so every member was also a written op and a digest over the written SUBSET produced the identical string. The test now spans the assembly while leaving one member unwritten, which is the only shape that can tell *the assembly's revision* from *the revisions of the rows I happen to be writing* — the distinction the item is entirely about. Three mutants now go red: written-subset digest, a fixed-arity transport that drops `p_groups` (the B1120 shape), and an ignored kill switch.
    - **Evidence.** `db/test/commit_elements_group_cas.test.sql` — **9/9 against the real production database, nothing left behind** (verified by count afterwards), and **mutation-proven**: with the digest comparison disabled the stale call is ACCEPTED and the host row moves to rev 2. `test/assemblyGroupCas.test.js` (23) covers the digest, the switch, the engine and **the real request body through the real transport** (never a mock `commit` with wider arity than the shipped adapter — the exact mismatch that shipped B1116/B1117 dead).
    - **⛔ AND A DEADLOCK IT NEARLY SHIPPED WITH, found by asking "how could turning this ON go wrong?" rather than by a failing test.** The server digests every LIVE row of the assembly; the client digests every row in its SHADOW. A member another writer CREATED that this tab's realtime has not yet delivered makes the two disagree PERMANENTLY — the same omission recomputed on every retry, ending in `client-stale` and a tab that has stopped saving. Recoverable by a reload, but reachable by exactly the two-writer case the feature exists for, which is the worst possible place for a stuck state. The conflict payload carries id/kind/rev, which is enough to converge with no refetch: an unknown member is ADOPTED (json `""`, `stale`), **`assemblyOf` records the assembly the SERVER named** (without it the member buckets under its own id and drops straight back out of the next digest — the fix looked right and did nothing until a test caught it), and it is marked **`remoteOnly`**, or B377888 fires on our own repair since the shadow now holds a row the canvas has never shown. Both halves are mutation-proven — and the second mutant initially PASSED because that test never re-ran the diff, which is fixed and red now.
    - **⚠ WHAT THIS IS NOT, so the record cannot overstate it.** It closes the window between two CALLS. It does not make a torn assembly unrepresentable in the store — a writer that never sends `p_groups` still commits per row — and **the switch ships OFF, so nothing in production exercises it yet**. Turning it on is stage 2's live-verify (**V179984**), and stage 3 remains open.
  - **Stage 3 is NOT started, and this is not a soft deferral.** It retires the per-row expectation for bonded elements and deletes the bookkeeping that made it necessary — `shadow` / `revOf` / `ownRevs` / `maxOwnRev` / `maxDeleteRev` / `reconcileSeedRows` / the journal's `baseRev`. It should follow stage 2 running clean live, which is what V179984 is for.
- **AMENDMENT 2026-08-09 (from the B298560–B298563 chat block, recorded at the owner's instruction — NOT built in that block, and he did not ask for it).** This now has a MEASURED number from his own signed-in Bain plan: **the gap between the last GIS response and the save is 1,029 and 1,654 ms of the app's OWN work on the main thread**, on two consecutive runs of the flood/drainage check. ⚠ Read it precisely: that is a **GAP IN THE NETWORK TIMELINE**, which is solid, and NOT a main-thread blocking measurement, which would not be — his tab was `document.visibilityState === "hidden"` while it was captured (`/CLAUDE.md` → FOREGROUND-OR-VOID; Resource Timing is unaffected by visibility, message-loop gaps are). B298563 now records this leg as `calc` on every check in production, so the next reading is a query rather than an expedition.
- Verify: live
- **What it is.** Today every element row carries its own `rev`, and a bonded assembly's coherence is a property the client maintains. The end state is a **shared revision per assembly**: a host and its bonded children CAS against one number, so a write that touches part of an assembly is rejected by the database rather than merely re-derived by the client. Then the partial apply is unrepresentable in the STORE, not just unobservable in the app.
- **Why B1340 did not do it, stated plainly.** It is a schema change (`group_rev`, or an assembly-keyed row), a rewrite of `commit_elements_atomic` to CAS on the group instead of per row, a migration for every existing row with a rollback, AND a rewrite of the client bookkeeping — `shadow` / `revOf` / `ownRevs` / `maxOwnRev` / `maxDeleteRev` / `reconcileSeedRows` / the pending-edit journal's `baseRev` — every one of which the last eight fixes are built on top of. Landing that badly is worse than the bug it closes. B1340's invariant makes the tear invisible and unpersistable TODAY, which is what the owner actually needs; this makes it impossible, which is what the data model deserves.
- **Staged plan (three sessions, each shippable and reversible on its own):**
  1. **Name the assembly on the row.** Add a nullable `assembly_id` (the host's id, or the element's own when unbonded), backfilled from `attachedTo`, written by the client, read by nobody. Pure additive; no behaviour change; gives the database the grouping it currently cannot see. Ships with a backfill + a drift test.
  2. **Group CAS behind a flag.** Extend `commit_elements_atomic` with an optional `p_group_rev`: the call succeeds only if every row of the named assembly is still at the expected group revision, and bumps them together. Client sends it for assembly batches only, behind a kill switch, with the per-row path untouched underneath. Ships with the rejection path self-tested in CI the way `mintGateE2E` tests the mint gate.
  3. **Make it the only path, and simplify the client.** Once stage 2 has run clean live, retire the per-row expectation for bonded elements and delete the bookkeeping it made necessary. This is the stage that PAYS BACK — several of the eight prior fixes exist only because per-row revs can disagree, and they can go with it.
- **Do not start at stage 2.** Without stage 1 the server cannot name an assembly, and the client would have to send the membership on every call — which is the same trust-the-client problem in a new place.

- **The state.** B1197 made the handle layer the last child of the plan SVG, so a handle paints over and hit-tests ahead of every drawn element and every AREA-role GIS layer. B1205 added a LINE-role band hosted ABOVE the whole SVG, so a contour hairline can now cross a handle.
- **Bounded, and cosmetic.** The band is `pointer-events: none` and its strokes are hairlines: a handle can be crossed, never made unreachable, and B1197's `e2e/references-handle-layer.spec.js` still passes.

### B1126 — "Computed but never RENDERED" is a class, and the ratchet only catches half of it: the unmounted-JSX half has no guard `[Site Planner / Yield]` (task) #ui #yield #testing  *(minted via `git fetch origin main && npm run next-id -- --against-main`. Filed 2026-07-29 from the B1105 dispatch's sweep instruction. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open + ⏳ Verify + Done: **B1110** is one INSTANCE of the variable half (now Done, and its guard shipped as B1128); no existing item covers the REACHABILITY half or the 90-strong inventory. Net-new.)*
`[ ]` **Open — swept, counted and sized. The cheap half of the guard SHIPPED as B1128; this item is the expensive half plus the paydown.**
- Verify: sandbox
- **Why it was swept.** Three "computed on render, never reaches the DOM" defects surfaced in five dispatches: the invisible Buildability panel rows, the ParcelDrawing swatch row reported missing though B567 records it shipped, and **B1110**'s `detVerdict`/`detTone`/`detSub`. A fourth was found during this sweep and fixed as **B1127** (the verdict strip rendering every Colorado site as a permanent "checking flood data" spinner). Four in five dispatches is a class, not a run of bad luck.
- **THE CLASS SPLITS IN TWO, and conflating them is why it kept recurring.**
  - **(a) The VARIABLE half** — a local written and never read. Statically detectable. **Guard SHIPPED (B1128):** `ui-audit/dead-store-audit.mjs` + `test/deadStores.test.js`, a per-file ratchet over ESLint's `no-unused-vars` (assigned-but-never-used only). A new one now fails CI.
  - **(b) The REACHABILITY half** — a variable that IS read, feeding JSX that never mounts, renders zero-height, or sits behind a condition that is never true. **This is the Buildability-rows and swatch-row shape and it has NO guard.** No static rule can see it: the value is used, the element exists in the tree, and every unit test passes. It needs a headless assertion that the node is present **AND** has a non-zero box **AND** its text is non-empty — which is the point the dispatch made: *a passing test asserting an element EXISTS is not a test that it is REACHABLE.*
- **INVENTORY for (a), measured, so the paydown is scoped rather than vague.** 90 across 29 files (`node ui-audit/dead-store-audit.mjs`): **28** look like unused components/constants (cosmetic dead code — unused icon components, `LINE`, `Badge`), **62** look like unused VALUES (the B1110 risk shape). **`SitePlanner.jsx` holds 46 of the 90**, 37 of them value-shaped: `measureModeLabel`, `lookupBusy`, `lookupErr`, `lookupRes`, `setSearchMode`, `setSearchVal`, `setLotW`, `setLotD`, `addRectParcel`, `overlayCenter`, `onCountyChange`, `runLookup`, `importFeature`, `courtOnSide`, `addCourtTrailer`, `drainCityCount`, `pondTailwaterFt`, `buildingRules`, `calibrated`, `hdrTab`, `curHint`, `otherSites`, `drainRecomputing`, three `fill`/`stroke`/`fillOpacity` triples, and others.
- **⚠ Sizing, and the honest risk note.** The paydown is NOT a mechanical sweep and should not be done as one PR. Each of the 62 value-shaped ones is a fork: **either** the value was meant to render and does not (a real bug worth its own item — `drainRecomputing` and `pondTailwaterFt` in particular sound like they were meant to be seen), **or** it is a leftover whose surface moved (delete it). Only reading each one tells you which, and the second reading is what B1110 got right. Estimate: **~1 session for `SitePlanner.jsx`'s 37** (the only file worth a dedicated pass), ~1 session for the remaining 28 files, and any genuine "was meant to render" finding spawns its own item.
- **Scope for (b), the part with no guard yet.** A shared helper — `visibleText(page, selector)` / `assertRendered(...)` — asserting presence **+** a non-zero bounding box **+** non-empty text, adopted by the `ui-audit/verify-*.mjs` harnesses. `ui-audit/verify-b1105-mhfd-panel.mjs` (shipped with B1105) is the worked example: it reads `innerText` off the `data-surface="planner"` host, so a `display:none` or zero-height node fails. Retrofitting it across the existing harnesses is ~1 session; it is the only thing that would have caught the Buildability rows.
- **Gate:** `test/goldenMasterTexas.test.js` green, and the B1128 ratchet may only ever be lowered (`--update` refuses to raise a total).

### B1106 — Ground vs grid: a real project-coordinate transform (combined factor + project origin on the site model) `[Platform / geo]` (feature) #coordinates  *(minted via `--against-main`. DEDUPE-FIRST: B1112 shipped the SURFACING half; this is the transform half, deliberately split. Origin: filed 2026-07-29 from chat (NEW-4).)*
`[ ]` **Open — the half B1112 deliberately did not ship, flagged loudly on the item rather than half-applied.**
- Verify: sandbox
- Origin: filed 2026-07-29 from chat
- **The audited fact (docs/COLORADO-AUDIT.md §4).** Planyr measures in TWO feet frames and had never written that down. Drawn geometry lives in `mapLock.js` — a uniform scaling of spherical Mercator anchored at the site origin, so it is **ground-true at the site**. Screening distances go through the state-plane **grid** (`proximityScreen.js`, `coverage.js`, `fbcdWse.js`, `deedAlign.js`, `thoroughfare/ingestTransform.js`) and are treated as ground feet. So **yes, the app assumes grid equals ground wherever it measures on the grid.**
- **Correct by accident in Texas, wrong in Colorado.** Houston at ~50 ft: elevation factor 0.999998, about 0.01 ft/mile. Denver at ~5,280 ft: combined ≈ 0.99975, **~1.3 ft/mile, ~9 in across a 3,000-ft site**. A "within 1,000 ft" screen in Denver really measures ~1,000.25 ground ft — a bias, not noise.
- **Why it was NOT applied this session (the loud part).** A half-applied scale factor — some quantities corrected, others not — is strictly worse than none: the error stops being a known constant and becomes untraceable. B1112 therefore ships the honest reporting (`shared/coordinates/scaleFactor.js`: grid factor × elevation factor, what it is worth per mile and over any run, and `detectSurveyFrame` classifying a survey as grid / ground / other-scale / unknown) and applies nothing.
- **Scope when picked up:** carry a **project combined factor + project origin** on the site model (a persisted-schema change → additive field, bumped `SITE_MODEL_VERSION`, extended `migrate`), apply it consistently across every measuring path, and wire the deed/CAD import paths so a survey delivered in modified state plane reconciles. Front Range surveys commonly arrive in ground coordinates with the project factor printed on the sheet — read it rather than deriving it where it is available.
- **Needs its own golden master.** It touches every measuring path, so B1107's harness must be extended with a ground-frame section before the first line changes.

| module | in the chunk |
|---|---|

`SitePlanner.jsx` itself is **581.2 KB** of that chunk — still, by a distance, the dominant term and still unsplittable by any `import()`. So the honest ranking of remaining levers is: the component itself (581 KB) ≫ the analysis stack (139 KB) > everything else. Tranche (b) is worth doing; it is not worth doing *first*, and it is not worth 580 KB.

**TRANCHE (a) — the lazy-panel scaffold + a first tranche. SHIPPED 2026-07-30.**
- `components/LazyPanel.jsx` is the scaffold: a **height-reserving** Suspense fallback (the call site passes the panel's resting height, so a deferred panel cannot jump the content below it — a `fallback={null}` would have traded bytes for a flash) plus a **per-panel error boundary** that contains a failed chunk to that panel and, on the stale-deploy case `isChunkLoadError` recognises, offers the cache-busting reload. LOUD-FAILURE: neither path renders empty.
- Three panels moved, each confirmed genuinely conditional and **closed by default** first. Measured per panel, by rebuilding with each one reverted to a static import:

| panel | `siteRouteJsBytes` | `largestChunkBytes` | note |
|---|---|---|---|
| `SiteAnalysis` | **−7.6 KB** | **−7.6 KB** | takes `lib/siteAnalysis.js` with it; mounts only on `_pid === "analysis"`, and `leftPanel` starts `null` |
| `TeamPanel` | **−10.3 KB** | +0.1 KB | lives in the shared ENTRY chunk, so **every** route gains: Review −12.9 KB, Library −12.9 KB, Scheduler −12.9 KB |
| `StandardsBar` | **−2.6 KB** | **−2.6 KB** | renders only while the Standards panel is open, docked or floating |
| **tranche total** | **−20.5 KB** | **−10.2 KB** | (`largestChunkBytes` gains less because TeamPanel was never in that chunk) |

- **`LayerPanel` was CONSIDERED AND DELIBERATELY NOT MOVED**, which is the brief's own instruction applied rather than ignored. It is the biggest single candidate (43.6 KB of source, 14.1 KB in the chunk) and it *is* conditional in the planner (`layersOpen` starts `false`) — but `MapFinder.jsx` renders it under `(!narrow || layersPanelOpen)`, and `layersPanelOpen` initialises **true** on any viewport wider than 760 px. So on the map finder — the app's landing surface for a user with no site open — LayerPanel is on the **first-paint path**, and lazying it would trade bytes for a flash on the first screen anyone sees. It stays static until either the finder's panel defaults change or a skeleton is designed that provably does not shift; noting it here so the next session does not re-derive this.
- Evidence: `node ui-audit/verify-lazy-panels.mjs` (new, headless, logged out, cross-origin blocked) proves all three are **absent from the boot fetch set**, and that opening Standards fetches the `StandardsBar` chunk and renders all three of its footer actions, with no uncaught page errors. `npm test` 6483 green · lint 0 errors · build green · bundle audit green.
- **What that harness could NOT do, named rather than implied → V532.** Site Analysis needs a georeferenced plan (GIS hosts the sandbox blocks) and the Team tab needs a signed-in account (sign-in is CORS-blocked here). Their **deferral** is proven; their **render after the lazy load** is not.

**TRANCHE (b) — get the analysis stack off the synchronous render path. ⛔ NOT SHIPPED. The specific blocker, stated plainly:**
- The six modules are called **synchronously in the component's render body** — plain `const x = cond ? f(…) : null` at ~50 sites inside the body (e.g. `computeRequiredDetention` at 8776/8778/8782, `criteriaFor` at 9134/9917/10313/10684/10874/11595, `assessBuildability` at 9756/9883, `detentionStorage` at 8295/9300/18267/…), **204 reference sites across the six**. None is memoised; none is gated on the consuming panel being open.
- Deferring the MODULES requires those calls not to happen during render at all — i.e. the yield / pond / criteria derivations become asynchronous, which introduces an **interim state on engineering numbers the owner makes decisions from**. That is a LIVE-VERIFY change by every one of this repo's own criteria (it changes *when* a number appears), on a plan with real project data, and **neither half of that verification is reachable from this sandbox**: no signed-in session, no GIS hosts, no real plan. Shipping a 200-site async conversion of the detention/floodplain math with the numbers unverifiable is exactly the trade this repo's rules exist to refuse.
- **B1121(b) — "still sluggish immediately after a reload" — MEASURED 2026-07-31 (speed program phase 2), and it is now a number rather than a feeling.** Time-to-first-drag on the reference plan at 4x CPU throttle, which is the honest definition of "when could I actually start working": **4.6–4.9 s** on the unmodified base, **4.4–4.7 s** after B1349's boot-path fixes — a consistent but small ~5% improvement across three interleaved pairs, and the absolute figure is the story: **first-contentful-paint lands at ~0.7 s and the canvas does not answer a drag for another four seconds.** So the post-reload complaint is real, is NOT paint latency, and is not going to be fixed by moving one more import. What DID move it: the load-time drainage facts pass (a GIS pull plus a bare-earth DEM grid) was firing 1.2 s into a boot that is not finished for four; it now waits for a genuinely idle main thread. **Not closed** — the remaining four seconds have not been attributed, and that attribution is the next step here.
- **What IS now known, and should be the first move next time:** the derivations are not merely un-deferred, they are **un-memoised** — they re-run on every render of a 23,419-line component. That is a frame-time and allocation cost independent of bytes, and it bears directly on **B1121(b)** ("still kind of annoying immediately after a reload" — the baseline-cost half, still untouched). Memoising them changes no behaviour and needs no interim state, so it is the tranche-(b) step that can land without a live gate. It is deliberately NOT bundled into this session's PR: a missed dependency in a `useMemo` over the flood/detention inputs produces a **stale engineering number**, which is worse than a slow correct one, and it wants its own diff and its own review.
- **Runtime measured this session** (`ui-audit/perf-harness.mjs`, headless, tab visible, reference scenario): frame median **16.7 ms**, p90 **16.7 ms**, peak JS heap **53.4 MB** — all inside budget and **unchanged** by tranche (a), which is the "nothing regressed" reading, not an improvement claim. `aerialTileRequests` reads 513 against a 240 ceiling — **pre-existing and owned by B1063**, identical to the figure B1063 recorded on `origin/main`, so this session neither caused nor fixed it.
- **A separate finding, recorded so it is not lost:** `perf-harness.mjs`'s `siteRouteChunks` check compares chunks the browser actually FETCHED (dynamic ones included) against the STATIC allowlist, so it names `rasterIdentifyMap`, `rasterIdentify`, `featureHover` and `terrainLayers` as intruders when all four are lazy **by design**. That check can never pass as written. It is not CI-gated, so nothing was red; it is left alone here rather than "fixed" in passing, because loosening a guard nobody has diagnosed is how guards die.

### B916 — Project sharing model: one grant per grantee, module-visibility mask, viewer-only v1 `[Backend / Sharing]` (feature) #infra #auth #persistence  *(owner-dropped 2026-07-21 as "NEW-2", top-of-queue; minted **B916** via `npm run next-id -- --against-main`. Schema/RLS DRAFT written this session — see below.)*
`[ ]` A more granular sharing model than today's team-based share: the unit of sharing is the **project**, a grant is **(project → grantee)** where grantee is a user OR a team, exactly one live grant per (project, grantee), and each grant carries a **module-visibility mask** (which modules the grantee can see) rather than sharing everything. Default on share = every module the grantor can see; uncheck to redact. **v1 role = viewer only.**
- Verify: **live** — **⛔ BLOCKER: `auth` + concurrency.** This is a security-critical RLS change on REAL user data whose core acceptance ("**revoke is immediate and verified** — re-run the access check post-revoke and confirm it returns `false`, crash-severity if it doesn't") can ONLY be confirmed with **two signed-in accounts** in the live app. The sandbox blocks Supabase sign-in (proxy CORS) and has no second account, so this **cannot be shipped-and-verified in one session** and is NOT auto-applied to production — see "What's blocked" below. This is the STANDING-RULE-#1 "too large / hard-blocker → raise with a plan, don't ship half" case, flagged loudly.
- Origin: filed 2026-07-21 from chat ("NEW-2").
- **DEDUPE-FIRST (searched Open / ⏳ Verify / Done for shar*, grant, team, RLS, access, viewer):** related but NOT a dup of **B406** (the EXISTING team-workspace share — whole-project `sites.team_id`, all-or-nothing, teammate-can-edit) or **B714** (the B406 model's share-reverts bug). NEW-2 is a *new, additive, finer-grained* model (per-grantee, per-module mask, viewer-only) that sits ALONGSIDE the team model, not a rewrite of it — a `team_id`-shared project keeps working; a `project_shares` grant is a second, independent path. When both cover the same (project, user), access is the UNION (either grants read). **Design note flagged for the owner:** whether `project_shares` eventually SUPERSEDES `team_id` sharing is a product call to make later — v1 just adds it without touching the team path.
- **Schema (DRAFT written this session → `src/workspaces/site-planner/db/project_shares.sql`, NOT yet applied):** `project_shares` (id, project_id, grantee_type `user`|`team`, grantee_id, role, **modules text[]**, created_by, created_at, revoked_at) with a partial-unique index enforcing exactly ONE live (`revoked_at IS NULL`) grant per (project, grantee); `teams` / `team_members` (reuse the B406 tables if present, else create); `share_events` audit log (who granted/revoked what, when). **`modules` is a `text[]` of module keys, not boolean columns** — adding a future module (e.g. `notes`) is a data change, not a schema+policy rewrite.
- **RLS (one helper, called from every table):** a single SECURITY-DEFINER SQL function **`has_project_access(project_id, module, min_role) → boolean`** — true when the caller owns the project, OR has a live `project_shares` grant whose `modules @> {module}` and role ≥ `min_role`, OR (union) a live team share. Every project-scoped table's SELECT policy becomes a **one-line call** to it with that table's own module key. (Draft policies for `sites` / `doc_reviews` included in the SQL file, commented as illustrative until the live pass.)
- **Non-negotiables (all in the DRAFT):** default **private** (a new project = zero grants); **no god-mode / cross-user admin read**; **revoke is immediate + verified** (post-revoke access check must return false — the live gate); every grant/revoke **undoable as one step**; a failed share write **surfaces loudly** (LOUD-FAILURE — never optimistic-only UI). v1 grantee scope = **existing accounts only** (no invite-by-email flow yet — that's a separate follow-on: needs pending accounts + invite emails + an accept-flow, scoped once this lands).
- **Out of scope v1:** anonymous/public links; invite-by-email for non-accounts; commenter role (implies a per-module comments system that doesn't exist — a dead checkbox without it); editor role (blob-level cloud save makes two editors silent last-write-wins data loss until the per-element `site_elements` sync migration ships); element-level ACLs inside a module.
- **Grantee experience:** shared projects appear on the grantee's map with a visible "shared with you" distinction and are filterable.
- **What's shipped vs. blocked:** ✅ the reviewable schema + RLS-helper SQL DRAFT (delivered to the owner to run against Supabase). ⛔ applying it to production + the two-account live-verify (revoke-locks-out) → **needs the owner's 2nd test account** (`OWNER-TODO.md`) → **V387 in `VERIFICATION.md`**. The client dialog + read-only mode is **B917** (depends on this).

### B917 — Share entry points, unified project-level dialog, and read-only client (viewer) mode `[Global / UI]` (feature) #ui #infra #auth  — depends on B916  *(owner-dropped 2026-07-21 as "NEW-3", top-of-queue; minted **B917**. Uses the B915 ContextMenu primitive.)*
`[ ]` Two problems: sharing is only reachable from the map-pin right-click, and the app assumes every user can edit everything — there is **no viewer state**. This item adds the surfaces + the read-only mode on top of B916's schema/RLS.
- Verify: **live** — depends on B916 (⛔ same `auth` blocker: the read-only lockdown + "shared with you" distinction + cross-module gaps need two signed-in accounts to confirm). Ships AFTER B916's schema is live-verified. Not shippable-and-verified this session.
- Origin: filed 2026-07-21 from chat ("NEW-3").
- **DEDUPE-FIRST:** relatives (not dups) — **B464/B465** (read-only/locked-TAB persistence signal — a DIFFERENT read-only: single-writer lock, not a viewer grant), **B455** (conflict/at-risk lockout). This is a *permission-driven* viewer mode, distinct from the tab-lock class.
- **Primary surface:** a persistent **Share** button in the project header bar of **every** module (Site Planner, Schedule, Document Review, Cost Estimating, future Notes).
- **Also reachable from:** the map-pin right-click (existing — CONVERTED from the current one-click team-grant to opening this dialog) and the project list / Library row right-click. All via the **B915 `ContextMenu`** primitive.
- **Unified dialog contents:** project name; an explicit **"Private"** state when there are zero grants; a **"Who has access"** list (grantee, role, "All modules" or "3 of 5"); an add row (existing user or team → module checkboxes, all checked by default); revoke. **Contextual open:** launching from inside a module pre-highlights that module in the checklist but still shows the FULL project-level dialog — no module-only shortcut that grants without showing complete access.
- **Read-only client (viewer) mode (new work):** when a viewer opens a shared project, EVERY edit affordance across all modules — drag handles, markup tools, task-edit fields, layer edits — is **disabled or hidden, not merely rejected server-side after the fact.** RLS is the enforcement backstop; the UI must not let a viewer attempt an edit guaranteed to fail. (Threaded as a `canEdit`/`viewer` capability from the grant down through each module's editing surfaces.)
- **Cross-module access gaps:** if a grant excludes a module that another visible module references (e.g. a Schedule task links a Doc Review sheet), show an explicit **"you don't have access to this module"** state — never a broken/dead link.
- **Blocked-this-session note:** the dialog + viewer-mode wiring is real UI work that can be built, but it is **meaningless to ship without B916's schema live + verified** (a viewer mode with no grants to read, and no verified revoke, is untestable and unsafe). So it parks here behind B916; the plan + surfaces are fully specced above for the follow-on session that has the owner's 2nd account. → **V388 in `VERIFICATION.md`**.

### B908 — Scheduler indent→outdent round-trip leaves the task's Start/Finish shifted by one business day `[Scheduler]` (bug) #scheduler  *(owner-tested 2026-07-19 during the V327 live follow-up on Goose Creek; minted **B908**)*
`[ ]` On Goose Creek (signed in), right-click **Indent** on task 46 ("Staff producing reports", originally top-level alongside task 45) correctly nested it under task 45; right-click **Outdent** correctly promoted it back to top-level — the STRUCTURE round-trips cleanly. But the outdent step also recomputed task 46's **Start/Finish one business day later** than before the round-trip (07/20/26–08/20/26 → 07/21/26–08/21/26), even though nothing about the task's own inputs (duration, predecessors) was touched by the user. Reverted cleanly via 2×Ctrl+Z (screenshot-confirmed exact match to the pre-test ID/dates/indentation), so this is a **forward-path recompute drift**, not a data-loss bug.
- Verify: live (real-project-data + timing/recompute class — the exact drift depends on task 46/45's real `predecessors`/`duration`/`pinnedStart` fields on Goose Creek, which this sandbox can't see: the scheduler's own Supabase project (`ksetjztkplttbcehyicv`, see `docs/REFERENCE.md`) isn't one of the two Supabase projects reachable from this session, and the scheduler page itself can't run headless here — its CDN React/Babel is egress-blocked).
- Origin: filed 2026-07-19 from chat, surfaced as evidence during V327 live testing (not flagged by the owner as urgent — reported alongside a CONFIRMED PASS on the menu-driven indent/outdent — but real and reproducible, so filed rather than dropped).
- **Code-level investigation this session (no live repro possible):** both `indentTaskById`/`outdentTaskById` (`public/sequence/index.html:6281`/`6312`) end in `recomputeAfterStructureChange = rollupParentDates(cascadeDates(tasks))` — the same recompute used after any structural move. A task with an **FS (finish-to-start) predecessor and no `pinnedStart`** has its `start` re-derived every cascade pass as `addBD(pred.end, 1) [+lag]` (`constrainedStartFrom`, line 1918); when a task is briefly re-parented (indent), `rollupParentDates` (line 2209) can overwrite its **new parent's** own start/end to mirror the (now sole) child, and outdenting then re-derives the child's start from that parent-as-predecessor's mutated end — a plausible but **unconfirmed** mechanism for a same-day drift. Whether task 46 actually has task 45 as an FS predecessor (vs. a plain `pinnedStart` date that shouldn't move at all) can only be confirmed against the real stored task JSON. **Do not guess-fix this** against a mature, heavily-tested cascade engine (`test/schedulerEngine.test.js` et al.) without the real repro data — a blind change here risks a regression across every other predecessor-driven schedule.
- **Next step (live-only):** with the same two tasks on Goose Creek, open the row editor for tasks 45/46 before repeating Indent→Outdent and record their `predecessors`/`pinnedStart`/duration fields alongside the before/after dates, so the drift can be pinned to one exact line instead of a hypothesis.
- Cross-links (DEDUPE-FIRST, not dups): B255 (the indent/outdent dedup this drift was found while re-verifying — already shipped, unrelated defect class).
