Net-new for the Site Planner workspace, which is what the owner uses.)*
`[ ]` **⏳ IMPLEMENTED AND HEADLESSLY SELF-VERIFIED this session (33/33 checks, every draw mode, real minified production build) — parks in ⏳ Verify because PDF/export parity and zoom-dependent rendering are BOTH mandatory LIVE-VERIFY classes regardless of how thoroughly they were driven headlessly → V424368.**
- Verify: live — PDF/export parity (arc size is drawn in real feet, scaled through the live view exactly like every other markup's geometry) and zoom-dependent rendering (the same scale term) are both named mandatory-live classes in `/CLAUDE.md`.
- **SCOPE, PHASE 1 (the "must ship this session" bar) — every bullet in the owner's brief, confirmed shipped:**
  1. **Draw, three gestures behind one tool (Cloud ▾ picks the mode, sticky via localStorage like `easeMode`):** Polygon (click each vertex; close on the first dot within 12px, double-click, Enter, or Esc to cancel — reuses the SAME `mkPoly`/`finishMkPoly`/`finishActiveDrawing` machinery `mpolygon` already had, extended rather than forked) · Rectangle (press-drag OR click-to-start→click-to-finish, mirroring `mline`/`mrect`/`mellipse`'s existing dual gesture, extended into `commitMkRect`) · Freehand (new `mkFreehand` drag-accumulate state, distance-gated to ~2px-worth of feet per point so a slow drag doesn't pile up thousands of near-duplicate points, then Ramer–Douglas–Peucker-simplified on release — `simplifyPath` in the new pure lib). **Always a closed ring** regardless of gesture: rectangle mode builds a literal 4-vertex `pts` array (never a centre-box), freehand always closes the loop — a cloud is never anything but a vertex ring, which is what makes every downstream piece (reshape, hit-test, translate) generic instead of a fourth special case.
  2. **Scallops.** `lib/cloudGeometry.js` (new pure module, 21 unit tests, `test/cloudGeometry.test.js`) — `cloudScallopPath(pts, arcSize)` walks each edge of the closed ring, picks a WHOLE arc count per edge (`edgeScallopCount = max(1, round(edgeLen / 2·arcSize))`) and divides the edge length by that count for the real per-arc chord, so the gap between the requested size and the actual chord is spread evenly across every arc on that edge rather than dumped on one stunted last arc — the exact "remainder absorbed" behaviour the brief asked for, unit-tested directly (a 10ft edge at a 3ft arc size produces 2 arcs of exactly 5ft each, never 1 arc of 6ft + a 4ft stub). The sweep flag (which way each arc bulges) is decided ONCE from the whole ring's signed area, not per-edge, so it can't flip on a locally-reflex (concave) corner. Arc size is stored in **feet** on the object (`m.arcFt`) and only multiplied by the live view's `rppf` (the exact same render-body scale term every other markup's geometry already goes through via `f2p`, per the repo's VIEW-ANCHOR convention) at render time — so it is genuinely zoom-invariant in real-world terms and prints at true scale, never a fixed pixel radius. **Small/Medium/Large presets (1.5 / 3 / 6 ft) plus a numeric field** (0.5–30 ft clamp), in both the Cloud ▾ toolbar dropdown (sets the default for the NEXT cloud) and the Properties panel (per-object, for an already-placed one).
  3. **Style.** Line colour, weight, dash, opacity — plus fill with its OWN separate opacity — all in the Properties panel, reusing the SAME `<Field>`/`ColorField`/`NumInput` controls every other markup uses. **The default colour is `#2563EB`, never `rgb(194,65,12)`/`#c2410c`** — that exact value is the whole generic "markup" family's existing default fill/stroke (`MK_DEFAULT` in `SitePlanner.jsx`) and was ALSO a previously-shipped, previously-reported collision for a different pair of families (B548816 — a measurement rendering invisibly into a same-coloured markup). Cloud gets its OWN sticky style bucket (`mkCloudStyle`/`MK_CLOUD_DEFAULT`, deliberately never `mkStyle`, which every OTHER markup tool shares and which starts at `#c2410c`) so it can never silently inherit that colour from whatever was drawn last, and the new ink is registered in the shared `src/shared/theme/familyInk.js` collision table and proven ≥12.2 ΔE00 (CIEDE2000, the perceptual metric that table already uses) from every other drawn family's default AND every site-element's default paint — `test/familyInk.test.js`, 10/10 green including its own teeth-proof.
  4. **Edit after placement — the SAME vertex idiom as the building footprint tool.** Cloud joins `MK_VERTEX_KINDS` (`["line","polyline","polygon","cloud"]`, never `MK_BOX_KINDS`) — which means it falls straight through the EXISTING shared B230 vertex-editing system (`editablePath`/`hitEditPath`/`insertVtx`/`deleteVtx`) with zero new per-kind logic: drag a dot to move a vertex, Shift-click / right-click an edge to insert one, right-click / Shift-click a dot to remove one, all identical to a polygon markup. **Control points are HIDDEN UNLESS SELECTED — the hard house rule from B705200 (shipped in #1145)** — satisfied BY CONSTRUCTION, not by a new gate: `markupHandles` (the one function that renders every markup's grips) already returns `null` unless `sel?.kind === "markup" && sel.id === m.id`, so joining `MK_VERTEX_KINDS` is the only change needed and there is no code path that can bypass it. Move, multi-select (marquee/Shift/Ctrl-click), copy/paste/duplicate, delete, undo/redo, and lock/unlock are ALL fully generic across every markup kind already (`translateMarkup`'s `.pts` fallback, `CLIP_KINDS`, `deleteSel`, `pushHistory`) — confirmed with an architecture-mapping pass before writing any code, and zero new code was needed for any of them.
  5. **Metadata, Bluebeam parity — every field on every cloud** (`cloudMetaDefaults`, pure + unit-tested): Subject (defaults "Cloud", editable) · Comment (a real textarea) · Author (auto — defaults "You"; this app has no per-account display-name registry wired into the Site Planner canvas anywhere yet, a gap that predates this item and is not this item's to fix, so Author is honestly editable rather than falsely "auto-only") · Created / Modified timestamps (auto — Created stamped once at draw time; Modified auto-updates on every Properties-panel edit to style OR metadata via the new `setSelMarkupCloud`/`liveMarkupCloud` wrappers; a PURE canvas reshape with the panel closed does not currently bump it — wiring that means touching the one shared per-gesture history-arm point (`dragGate.js`'s `histOnArm`) every markup/element/parcel type depends on, which was judged too risky to touch blind in this session and is noted here rather than silently dropped) · Status (None/Accepted/Rejected/Cancelled/Completed, a `<select>`) · Label · Layer (a free-text tag, distinct from the app's existing "Markups" show/hide GROUP — see point 7; Bluebeam's per-object Layer property has no equivalent named-layer system in this app yet, and building one is exactly PHASE 2/3-shaped scope creep, so it's an honest text field for now).
  6. **Persistence + op_kind (B727936).** Stored in the same flat `markups[]` array as every other markup, through the SAME `KIND_TO_FIELD`/Supabase row sync every other markup kind already rides — zero new persistence code. **A real op_kind on create, edit AND delete:** every creation path (`commitMkRect`'s new `mcloud` branch, `finishMkPoly`'s new `mcloud` branch, the new `commitMkCloudFreehand`) calls `pushHistory()` before mutating state, matching the EXISTING, established convention every other markup shape's creation already uses (a bare `pushHistory()` defaults its `kind` argument to `"edit"` — a real, non-`"unknown"` value; B727936's own text is about paths that skip `beginOperation` entirely, never about this argument's semantic precision, and introducing a one-off `"create"` label for Cloud alone while every sibling tool stays `"edit"` would be a new inconsistency, not a fix); delete rides the universal `deleteSel` path, which already stamps `pushHistory("delete")` for any markup. No path exists that can leave a Cloud row `op_kind:"unknown"`.
  7. **Z-order + exclusion + layers.** Markups band (99-101), the force-on-top/underneath controls (#1151) — fully generic via `annotationFamily`/`arrangeSel`/`arrangePeers`/`arrangeAcrossBands`, zero new code (confirmed: the right-click menu, Arrange rows, and the cross-band "Send behind the plan" toggle are gated on `sel.kind === "markup"`, never on `m.kind`). **Excluded from every calculation** by construction — the area/yield/coverage/parcel metrics pass iterates `els`/`parcels`, never `markups`, and always has (confirmed, not merely assumed — this is the SAME invariant `contentVisibility.js`'s own header documents and a prior session's audit already covers). Shows/hides with the "Markups" View-menu row (`contentVisibility.js` already treats "a rect markup vs a cloud" as the SAME row by explicit design in its own header comment — zero new code). Also added to `ANNOTATION_KINDS` (`siteModel.js`), `CLOSED_MARKUP` (`multiStyle.js`, so a multi-selection including a cloud gets correct shared Fill controls + a closed selection outline), and `markupHitModel` (`lib/markupPick.js`, so Alt-click stack-cycling reaches a cloud stacked under something else) — three small, real gaps a full-repo sweep for every hardcoded markup-kind array found and closed.
  8. **PDF PARITY.** No second render path exists to keep in sync: `exportSheet.js` clones the LIVE `<svg>` wholesale (confirmed by reading it — zero markup-kind-specific logic anywhere in that file), so the same `renderMarkupNode` branch that paints a cloud on screen is exactly what a PDF/PNG export contains. Proven live this session (`window.__plannerExportSvg`, the same hook the app's own export-parity guards use) — see the verification note below, not merely argued from source.
- **NOT SHIPPED, EXPLICITLY FILED, NOT SILENTLY DROPPED — see B758545 (PHASE 2: Markups List, threaded replies, tool presets) and B758546 (PHASE 3: revision delta tag, flatten-on-export, iPad touch).** Per the brief's own instruction to file rather than skip.
- **THE REAL BUG THIS SESSION'S OWN HEADLESS VERIFICATION CAUGHT, worth recording because it is exactly the class of defect `npm run build` + `npm run lint` + the unit suite all missed.** `cloudMode`/`cloudArcFt`'s `useState` initializers were first placed ABOVE `lsGet`'s own `const lsGet = (k,d) => …` declaration in `SitePlanner.jsx` (mirroring `mkPoly`/`mkStyle`'s position) — a genuine JS temporal-dead-zone violation (a function-body `const` never hoists its value) that `npm run build`'s successful minified bundle did **not** surface as a build error, and only appeared as a runtime crash (`ReferenceError: Cannot access 'lsGet' before initialization`, caught by the app's own error boundary) the first time the component actually rendered in a real browser. ### B757920 — Roads categorically excluded their own ENDPOINTS from vertex deletion, and the disabled reason was FALSE `[Site Planner]` (bug) #site-planner #road #ui #testing  *(owner chat block 2026-08-25, verbatim: "i should be able to delete end points for roads, easements, anything similar that makes sense." Measured LIVE on production, plan `smsz866fuql0`: a 3-point road's MIDDLE vertex right-clicked to an ENABLED "Delete control point"; either ENDPOINT right-clicked to the same row DISABLED, labeled "(min reached)" — false, since a 3-point road sits above the true 2-point minimum. The owner flagged the label as misleading and instructed against chasing an off-by-one in a minimum-point counter; the actual defect is a rule that excludes endpoints from the deletable set entirely, regardless of point count. Minted **B757920 / V423744** from this branch's reserved block B757920–B757935 / V423744–V423759 against `origin/main` 4b28b82. **DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open/⏳Verify/Done for `canRemoveRoadVertex`, `removeRoadVertex`, `noEndpointDelete`, `endpoint`, `min reached`, `control point`:** **B718** (Done) is the item that ORIGINALLY SHIPPED this exact exclusion — its own verification note reads "right-click an endpoint → Delete disabled ('min reached')" as the EXPECTED, correct behavior at the time. This item does not reopen B718 as broken-then; it REVERSES that specific design decision per a fresh, explicit owner instruction that endpoints must be deletable like any other CAD/GIS polyline vertex. A separate item found in the same search, the stale-`selVtx`-wedges-Delete-key bug (`BACKLOG.md:9784`-area), is a DIFFERENT defect (a stale armed index, not a deliberate exclusion) and is untouched. Net-new.)*
`[ ]` **⏳ IMPLEMENTED and VERIFIED LIVE (headless) this session — parks in ⏳ Verify per the LIVE-VERIFY "anything whose repro cites real project data" class (the owner's repro named a specific production plan) → V423744.**
- Verify: live — repro cites real project data (plan `smsz866fuql0`). The mechanical claims below (endpoint now deletable, road shortens correctly, the 2-point-floor "Delete road/easement/etc." offer, no other element type regressed) were proven headless, logged out, this session, driving the real built app end to end — see V423744.
- **THE AUDIT, done first, as the report demanded.** Read every vertex-editable element type's `deleteVtx`/`editablePath` branch (`SitePlanner.jsx`): parcel boundaries, buildings/paving/sidewalk/parking/pond (all `layer:"el"`, closed rings, min 3), measurements (`layer:"measure"`, min 1/2/3 by mode), markups (`layer:"markup"`, polyline min 2 / polygon min 3), and easements (`layer:"ease"`, centerline/strip min 2 / boundary ring min 3) ALL already computed deletability as the generic `path.pts.length > path.min` — no endpoint singled out, INCLUDING for their own endpoints on open paths. **Only the road layer set `noEndpointDelete: true` and routed through `canRemoveRoadVertex`, which explicitly forbade `index === 0` and `index === pts.length - 1` regardless of point count** — that is the one and only place the false "min reached" label could ever fire above the true floor. Encumbrances (`markup.kind === "encumbrance"`) and 2-point `line`-kind markups are moved as one piece and are not vertex-edited at all (no control-point model, so no bug is possible there). Building footprints were explicitly left alone — their loaded-dock-wall-corner exclusion (`x.footEdit && dockLineAt(...)`) is a real, honest, unrelated rule and was not touched.
- **A SECOND removal path exists (Shift-click), and it was measured rather than assumed, per the report's instruction.** Reading `onCanvasVtxDownCapture`/every per-type vertex "start-drag" handler (`startVertex`/`startElVertex`/`startMeasureVertex`/`startMarkupVertex`/`startEaseVertex`) found NO branch anywhere that deletes on a Shift-click of a vertex — only Shift-click on an EDGE (away from a corner) inserts a point; the code's own comment at `startEaseVertex` confirms the design: "Shift-click … an edge to add; right-click a vertex or press Delete to remove." So the two paths did not disagree about endpoints specifically — one of them (Shift-click-to-remove) simply doesn't exist and never has; a Shift-click on a vertex just starts an ordinary drag. Three panel hint strings (the easement panel, the generic markup panel, and the pond inspector) nonetheless claimed "Shift-click removes one" / "click + on an edge to add a point; Shift-click to delete one" — false copy describing a feature that isn't there, the same class of lie STANDING RULE (c) asked to be audited for. Fixed to state the true mechanism (Shift-click an edge to add; right-click a dot to remove).
- **THE FIX.** `lib/roadGeometry.js`: `canRemoveRoadVertex`/`removeRoadVertex` now allow ANY control point — endpoint included — above the 2-point floor, matching the rule every other element type already used; deleting an endpoint on a 3+ point road SHORTENS the road (the adjacent vertex becomes the new endpoint), exactly as the report's EXPECTED (a) specified, and exactly what every CAD/GIS polyline editor does. Endpoints hold no curve treatment (`treatmentAt` only reasons about interior vertices 1..N-2), so removing one is pure geometry with nothing to migrate; road junctions/welds (`teeTargetOf`) are re-derived from live COORDINATES every render, not a stored index, so a shortened road simply stops matching a tee it used to weld to, with no dangling reference. `SitePlanner.jsx`: dropped the road-only `noEndpointDelete` special case from `editablePath`/`onCanvasVtxDownCapture`/`onCanvasVtxContextCapture` so every layer shares ONE `canDelete` rule (`path.pts.length > path.min`). At an OPEN path's TRUE minimum (2 points for road/easement-line/markup-polyline; mode-dependent for measurements), per EXPECTED (b), the context menu now offers **"Delete road" / "Delete easement" / "Delete measurement" / "Delete markup"** in place of the old dead disabled row — routed through the existing unconditional `deleteSel` (DELETE-PLAN's single decision point, so undo/redo + a real `op_kind` come for free, per EXPECTED (d) / B727936). CLOSED rings (parcel/building-shaped elements/polygon markups/easement boundaries) at THEIR true minimum keep the plain disabled "(min reached)" row unchanged — that message was never false there (a ring genuinely cannot go below 3 points), so nothing needed fixing on that side.
- **LIVE VERIFICATION, this session, headless Chromium, logged out, driving the real built app (`ui-audit/verify-endpoint-delete.mjs`, kept in the repo) — 12/12 checks passed.** Drew a 3-point road (start/turn/end, the owner's exact repro shape): right-clicking the START endpoint now shows "Delete control point" ENABLED (not "min reached"); clicking it shortens the road to 2 points, with the surviving start vertex's feet-coordinates proven byte-identical to the old middle "turn" vertex. On the resulting 2-point road, right-clicking its remaining endpoint shows "Delete road" (no dead disabled row); clicking it removes the road entirely (0 roads left). Repeated for a 2-point centerline EASEMENT (drawn fresh): the floor right-click shows "Delete easement" and removes it. Repeated for a 2-point Length MEASUREMENT (its permanent floor — a Length measurement is always exactly 2 points): the floor right-click shows "Delete measurement" and removes it. Screenshots in `ui-audit/screens/endpoint-delete/`.
- **Unit tests.** `test/roadGeometry.test.js` updated: the two tests that asserted the OLD (buggy) "blocks removing an endpoint" behavior now assert the endpoint IS removable and the road correctly shortens; `canRemoveRoadVertex` test updated to expect `true` for an endpoint above the 2-point floor. Full suite `npx vitest run` — 12550/12552, the same 2 pre-existing shallow-clone-only failures present before this session's changes (`docReviewLayerVisibility.test.js`/`hiddenContentReads.test.js`, both `git show <hash>` against history this shallow clone lacks — reconfirmed pre-existing via `git stash`). `deletePlan.js`'s `DELETE_ENTRIES` registry gained the new `vtxMenu:wholeDelete` entry point (the deletePlan self-test enforces that every `entry:` string used is registered). Build green, `node scripts/build-map.mjs --check` clean (no export/file changes needed it).
- **Live-verify (V423744).** On a real signed-in plan, confirm: (a) a multi-point road's endpoint can be right-clicked and deleted, correctly shortening the road; (b) a 2-point road/easement/measurement offers "Delete road/easement/measurement" at its floor rather than a dead disabled row; (c) the corrected panel hint text (Shift-click an edge to add, right-click a dot to remove) reads correctly in the easement/markup/pond panels.

### B742369 — A footprint corner drag could overshoot and write a self-crossing polygon that reached the database before the (release-only) revert guard ever ran `[Site Planner / footprintEdit]` (bug) #site-planner #ui #testing  *(owner chat block 2026-08-25, "NEW-2" — driven live on production, plan "ZZ TEST - reshape footprint - safe to delete" (site `smsz866fuql0`, Goose Creek), Building 2 `e1454729ykduhm`. The owner explicitly flagged browser zoom as a SUSPECTED, NOT PROVEN variable — at 100% zoom the identical gesture tracked 1:1 (20px → 156.9 ft vs 159 ft expected) and could not be re-triggered — and instructed: audit the pointer→world transform for devicePixelRatio/visualViewport scaling, prove the repro RED before fixing, and do not brief zoom as the cause downstream. Minted **B742369 / V408192** from this branch's reserved block B742368–B742383 / V408192–V408207 against `origin/main` a618d07. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open + ⏳ Verify + Done for `self-intersect`, `polySelfIntersects`, `reshape crosses`, `elVertex`, `dragGate`, `devicePixelRatio`: B233153/B278576 (CHROME-NEVER-EATS-A-PRESS) are a different double-click hit-testing family, untouched; no prior item covers a mid-drag geometry guard. Net-new.)*
`[ ]` **⏳ IMPLEMENTED this session — the DAMAGE this class of bug can do (a corrupted polygon ever reaching the database) is closed and self-verified live; parks in ⏳ Verify because the ROOT CAUSE (was it really zoom?) needs a real machine with real browser page zoom, which this sandbox cannot faithfully emulate → V408192.**
- Verify: live — zoom-/devicePixelRatio-dependent rendering (a mandatory LIVE-VERIFY class) for the root-cause question. The consequence half (guard-before-write, user notification, canvas/DB agreement) is `Verify: sandbox`-strength and was driven live in this session's own headless browser, not merely argued from source — see below.
- **THE AUDIT, DONE FIRST, AS INSTRUCTED — the pointer→world transform (`p2f` → `screenToWorld` in `shared/viewport/viewportTransform.js`) carries NO `devicePixelRatio` or `visualViewport` term anywhere in the chain.** It is `world = (screen − t) / scale`, fed by `e.clientX/clientY` (browser-reported) and `svgRef.current.getBoundingClientRect()` — both defined by the DOM spec in the SAME "visual CSS pixel" space at any browser zoom level, so their difference is invariant under a uniform page zoom by construction (both move together). A repo-wide grep for `devicePixelRatio`/`movementX`/`movementY` in the drag path found none — the one `devicePixelRatio` use in this file is for basemap tile retina selection, unrelated to pointer math. The drag-vs-click gate (`lib/dragGate.js`) measures travel in CSS px and rebases in world feet, also with no zoom term. **So the hypothesis handed in — browser page zoom as the direct cause — is NOT confirmed by this audit, and is not asserted as the cause; it is also not refuted with certainty, since this sandbox cannot drive Chrome's real Ctrl+/Ctrl− page zoom (which changes `window.devicePixelRatio`) the way a real browser session can — `document.body.style.zoom` was tried as a proxy and found NOT equivalent (it changes `getBoundingClientRect()` numbers but leaves `devicePixelRatio`/`visualViewport.scale` at 1, unlike real page zoom).** That specific question is parked below as V408192 for a live re-test at ~160% zoom on the deployed build.
- **THE FIX SHIPPED REGARDLESS OF ROOT CAUSE, because the DAMAGE — an invalid polygon reaching storage — is a defect independent of what triggers an oversized pointer delta.** The self-crossing/degenerate guard (`points.length < 3 || polyArea < 1 || polySelfIntersects`) used to run ONLY at pointer-up (release). It now ALSO runs on every `onMove` frame for a `footEdit` vertex drag, against the CANDIDATE points before they are ever written to state: if the candidate would cross or degenerate, the frame writes NOTHING — the vertex holds at its last valid position instead of following the cursor past the crossing — and a throttled (once-per-gesture) toast fires. The existing release-time guard is kept as a backstop for any other write path (a typed coordinate, say) and is now unreachable via a normal drag. Because a self-intersecting ring can no longer be CONSTRUCTED in local state at all, there is nothing invalid left to race a debounced flush against — closing the reported "canvas showed the old rectangle while the database held a bow-tie" split by construction, not by making the race narrower.
- **User notification, per part (c) of the report.** The per-frame guard flashes `"⚠ Reshape held — that move would cross the outline over itself."`; the release-time backstop's message also now carries the `⚠` prefix (see B742371) so a refusal can never again render in the same green pill as a completed action.
- **LIVE VERIFICATION, this session, headless Chromium, logged out (`ui-audit/verify-b872-round2.mjs`, kept in the repo).** A cross-dock 600×300 ft building seeded with 4 bump-outs, promoted to reshape mode via the real "Edit footprint" flow (B742368), its top-right corner (a dock-wall corner — the exact case that slides ALONG the wall via `projectOntoLine`, unbounded, matching the reported gesture) dragged 20 real pointer-move steps well past the point that would self-intersect. Read straight out of `localStorage` (ground truth, the same discipline `verify-bumpout-anchor-style.mjs` uses) after release: **the final ring is never self-intersecting, keeps a real positive area, and the dragged vertex was held at x≈−270 rather than following the cursor to the −400-and-beyond target** (left edge at −300) — and the red `⚠ Reshape held…` toast fired MID-DRAG with the error-pill background color (`rgb(127,29,29)`), not the success green. 4/4 checks in this item's group passed (screenshot `ui-audit/screens/b872-round2-new2-guard.png`).
- **What's left for a live pass (V408192).** On the owner's actual machine, at real browser page zoom (Ctrl+/Ctrl−, not this sandbox's `body.style.zoom` proxy) around 150–175%: drag a footprint corner a modest, ordinary distance and confirm it still tracks the cursor 1:1 (not 5×). Two possible outcomes, both fine: **(a)** it tracks correctly — the zoom hypothesis is refuted outright, and the corruption this session actually reached was some other, still-unidentified trigger for an oversized delta, now harmless regardless; **(b)** it still overshoots — the root cause is real and needs a second investigation pass, but critically it can no longer corrupt the plan (the corner will hold at the outline boundary and warn, exactly as the live check above proved), so the severity drops from a silent data-integrity bug to an annoying-but-safe input-tracking one.
- **TESTS.** `test/dogEar.test.js` (27), `test/dogEarReanchor.test.js` (5), `test/dragGate.test.js` (30), `test/footprintEdit.test.js` (23) — all pre-existing, all green, unchanged (the pure geometry these lean on was not touched; the guard is new code in the component's drag handler, not a library function). Full unit suite `npx vitest run` — 12500/12503 passing, the same 2 pre-existing shallow-clone-only failures (`docReviewLayerVisibility.test.js`, `hiddenContentReads.test.js` — both `git show <hash>` against history this shallow clone does not have; confirmed pre-existing by re-running on a clean `git stash`) present before this session's changes, plus `mapDrift.test.js` regenerated clean after `node scripts/build-map.mjs` (a new export in `ringMath.js`, see B742372). Lint 0 new errors. Build green.

### B734529 — "Find my location" spins forever in a policy-blocked browser, can fly to a 20-50 km IP guess, and has no cancel `[Site Planner / Map]` (bug) #site-planner #ui #mobile #a11y  *(owner chat block 2026-08-25: "the owner's COMPANY BLOCKS LOCATION SERVICES IN CHROME BY POLICY, so this button can NEVER succeed for him. Spinning then timing out on every click is wrong for a permanently-denied environment," plus a full steel-man of the failure set — enterprise no-prompt denial, an ignored permission dialog with no callback ever firing, POSITION_UNAVAILABLE, insecure context, a Permissions-Policy header, garbage IP-accuracy results (20-50 km) being flown to and drawn as a precise circle, a stale cached fix, no way back after flying far from the sites, concurrent/repeated clicks, no cancel, and the control sticking in spinner/error states. Minted **B734529 / V400352** from this branch's reserved block against `origin/main` bf7ee2f (fetched fresh at ship time). DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open/⏳Verify/Done for `locate`, `geolocation`, `Find my location`, `ACCURACY_CIRCLE_THRESHOLD`, `permissions.query`: **B725218** (Done, `V393761` still open) is the ORIGINAL "add the control" feature and is not reopened — its remaining open question is real-hardware GPS accuracy, a different fact from this item's permission-awareness and failure-handling defects, none of which existed as separate claims anywhere. Net-new. Branch `claude/map-view-control-defects-l6z64q`.)*
`[ ]` **⏳ IMPLEMENTED this session — every steel-manned failure case addressed in `lib/locateMe.js` + `MapFinder.jsx`; parks in ⏳ Verify because the last remaining fact (does the real defence actually fire cleanly on his machine) still needs his own click → V400352.**
- Verify: live — `Blocker: real-data`. The owner has since MEASURED the one fact this sandbox couldn't fabricate (see the correction below), which narrows the remaining live gap to "does it actually behave this way when he clicks it," not "which permission state does his browser report."
- ⛔ **CORRECTION, same day as the original ship (owner measurement) — READ THIS BEFORE the numbered list below, which describes the AS-CORRECTED design.** The first cut of this item's own text (and the code comments) claimed the `navigator.permissions.query` precheck was the defence against the owner's case. The owner then measured it directly on his real, policy-blocked Chrome, on the real deployed app: **`navigator.permissions.query({name:'geolocation'})` reports `'prompt'`, not `'denied'`.** An enterprise policy of this shape (Chrome's `DefaultGeolocationSetting`) blocks the geolocation REQUEST itself, silently — it does not pre-announce through the Permissions API. So the precheck reads his environment as available and a click proceeds exactly like anyone else's, which means the precheck was NEVER what would have fixed his report, and shipping it framed that way would have been a wrong claim standing in the backlog. **Demoted, not removed:** it stays for what it CAN see honestly (an explicit HTTPS/API absence, or a genuine 'denied' from a real per-site browser block — a different case from his) and is documented as such in both `lib/locateMe.js` and `MapFinder.jsx` now. **The actual defence — which was ALREADY built and shipped, just under-credited in the writeup — is items 2 and 4 below**, and a NEW harness arm (`ui-audit/verify-locate-me.mjs`, "THE CORRECTED SCENARIO") proves both together with `permissions.query` genuinely left un-mocked (reporting the real 'prompt', matching his measurement) and `getCurrentPosition` mocked to call back NEITHER way — 30/30 passing, including this arm. The explicit `map.locate()` timeout was also tightened from 12s to **10s** (the watchdog from 14s to 12s) to sit inside the "8-10s" the owner asked for, rather than leaving the original, already-explicit-but-untouched 12s.
- **AUDIT-FIRST — read the shipped control (`MapFinder.jsx`'s "create the map once" effect) before changing anything.** It already had a good, honest timeout message (`locateErrorMessage(3)`, kept verbatim), an already-EXPLICIT (never Infinity) `timeout` on `map.locate()`, and a same-tick in-flight guard (`locatingRef`) — but `map.locate({ setView: true, … })` unconditionally flew the camera and drew a marker for ANY reported accuracy (including a bare desktop IP guess), there was no independent backstop if neither `locationfound` nor `locationerror` ever fired (the browser's own timeout doing nothing for a provider a policy prevents from ever being asked), and there was no `navigator.permissions.query` pre-check for the states it CAN see.
- **Steel-manned, one by one, all in `lib/locateMe.js` (pure, unit-tested) + `MapFinder.jsx` (wiring):**
  1. **PERMISSION_DENIED / enterprise policy, no prompt ever shown.** `locateAvailability()` calls `navigator.permissions.query({name:'geolocation'})` at mount, BEFORE any click — but per the correction above, this catches only a GENUINE 'denied' (a real per-site browser block), not the owner's policy shape, which reports 'prompt'. Where it DOES apply: renders the control muted (opacity only — `btn.style.opacity`, never a hardcoded color, so it survives dark mode) with an anchored tooltip naming the reason, and a click neither spins nor ever calls `getCurrentPosition`; subscribed to the permission's own `change` event so a later-lifted block re-enables the control live, no reload.
  2. **⛔ THE ACTUAL DEFENCE — the prompt is ignored / the environment silently never resolves.** Two parts, both required: (a) `map.locate()` is now called with an EXPLICIT `timeout: 10000` (never the PositionOptions default of Infinity — an infinite timeout on a request that never resolves IS the permanent-spinner bug); (b) an INDEPENDENT wall-clock `setTimeout` watchdog (12s, a 2s margin past (a)) that fires on its own regardless of whether `navigator.geolocation` invokes EITHER callback — because a policy-blocked provider is free to invoke neither, which is exactly what makes (a) alone insufficient. Both force-stop the spinner and show the honest timeout message. Proven together, with `permissions.query` genuinely reporting 'prompt' (nothing mocked), by the new "THE CORRECTED SCENARIO" harness arm.
  3. **POSITION_UNAVAILABLE (code 2).** Already covered by the existing `locateErrorMessage` fallback sentence; unchanged, still reachable, still non-empty.
  4. **TIMEOUT (code 3).** Kept, tightened to 10s, and now PROVABLY cannot leave the spinner running even when the browser's OWN timeout mechanism does nothing (item 2's watchdog is the backstop for exactly that).
  5. **Insecure context / (6) a Permissions-Policy header or an iframe without `allow="geolocation"`.** `locateAvailability` checks `window.isSecureContext` first (wins over every other signal); a Permissions-Policy violation is handled at the reactive layer — the whole `map.locate()` call is wrapped in try/catch (a synchronous throw is treated exactly like a failed attempt) and a `permissions.query()` rejection is caught and silently falls back to the reactive path rather than being treated as a hard dependency.
  7. **A successful result that is garbage (20-50 km IP accuracy).** New `isAccuracyUsable()` / `ACCURACY_USABLE_THRESHOLD_M` (15 km — above ordinary Wi-Fi/cellular positioning, below a bare IP-lookup's range): `setView:true` was REMOVED from the `map.locate()` call entirely; the `locationfound` handler now decides for itself, so a fix beyond the threshold moves NOTHING and draws NOTHING — treated as a failure with an honest `garbageAccuracyMessage()` naming the accuracy and calling it what it is ("a rough network guess, not a real location"), never a multi-mile circle over half a county.
  8. **`maximumAge` returning an hours-old cached fix.** `maximumAge: 0` is now passed explicitly (Leaflet's own default, made a stated fact rather than an implicit one).
  9. **Far from every saved site.** Flying there is still correct (STEEL-MAN's own framing) — but a "◂ Back to your sites" action now appears in the app's standard bottom-left banner slot whenever the fix lands more than the SAME 50-mile market radius `landingView.js` already uses (`CLUSTER_RADIUS_MI`) from the user's own sites, re-running the exact derived landing view a fresh page open would use.
  10. **Repeated/concurrent clicks** and **(xi) no way to cancel.** Solved together: a 2nd click while a fix is in flight now CANCELS it (`map.stopLocate()` + immediate reset to idle) rather than being a no-op or racing a 2nd request; both async handlers check `locatingRef.current` first, so a late result from a cancelled or watchdog-timed-out request is silently ignored instead of reviving the UI.
  12. **Control state after an error.** Every exit from "locating" — found, error, cancel, watchdog — funnels through one `stopLocating()`, so retry always works; proven for all four paths headless, INCLUDING a fresh click actually re-spinning right after a corrected-scenario timeout (the "retry works" arm).
  13. **`watchPosition`.** Confirmed by source sweep: not used anywhere in this codebase (only the one-shot `getCurrentPosition` via Leaflet's `map.locate()`) — nothing to clear.
  - Aria-label and tooltip: confirmed always present (idle: "Find my location"; blocked: the reason appended), including on the muted state.
- **SELF-VERIFICATION, headless, logged-out, real built app.** `test/locateMe.test.js` — 27 pure-logic tests, all green. `ui-audit/verify-locate-me.mjs` — extended from 6 to **30 checks, 30/30 passed**: proactive genuine-denial (mocked `permissions.query`) never spins and never calls `getCurrentPosition`; a live permission `change` event re-enables a blocked control; a mocked 50 km fix shows the honest failure and draws nothing; an unanswered prompt (mocked `getCurrentPosition` that never calls back) is proven to stop the spinner via the watchdog within bounds; **the corrected scenario — `permissions.query` genuinely un-mocked and reporting 'prompt', `getCurrentPosition` never calling back either way — proves the actual defence (explicit timeout + independent watchdog) holds, then a fresh click retries successfully**; a 2nd click cancels immediately and a late stale resolution is proven ignored; aria-label/tooltip always present. RED proven first against the pre-fix build with an earlier cut of this harness — 13 of 24 checks failed (the new protections), confirming these are genuinely new defects closed, not pre-existing coverage.
- **WHAT IS NOT PROVEN HERE, stated plainly.** That the explicit-timeout + watchdog mechanism is sound is now proven against the owner's OWN measured permission state (a real fact, not an assumption) — what remains is whether his real machine's geolocation provider behaves like the mock (calls back neither way) or produces some other shape entirely (e.g. a slow but eventual error), and whether the honest message and retry read correctly to him in the running app. That is a plain click-through, not a mechanism question, which is why this parks rather than needing further design work.

### B719776 — A healthy, permission-clean overlay (Richfield/Quiddity site plan) does not render — the client fetch-and-rasterise path, not the data `[Site Planner / overlay]` (bug) #site-planner #persistence #perf  *(owner dispatch, 2026-08-25, established against production before a line of code was written: site `smsdrvzr9gzx` ("Richfield", plan "Concept A"), overlay `e1455071lxvizi` ("Richfield - Quiddity Site Plan 2026.08.13.pdf") — confirmed via direct read of `sites.data.sheetOverlays` and `storage.objects`: the record is intact, the storage object EXISTS (bucket `doc-review-files`, 5,723,266 bytes, `application/pdf`, created 2026-08-13), and the owner's own role can read it. 19 of 21 overlays across the whole account have healthy bytes and this is one of them, so the failure is neither the data nor permissions. Minted **B719776 / V388320** from this branch's reserved block B719776–B719791 / V388320–V388335 against `origin/main` 98cfd3e. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open / ⏳ Verify / Done across `rehydrate`, `idbPut`, `rasterizeStoredPdf`, `overlayLoadErr`, `B784`, `B785`, `B749`, `B251136`: **B784/B785** (Done) built the terminal missing/network classification this item extends with a THIRD reason (`render`) they never had; **B749/B251136/B251137** (Done) own the ZOOM-triggered hi-res re-raster, a different code path from the cold-load rehydrate this item fixes. Net-new — nothing prior backfills IndexedDB on rehydrate or distinguishes a rasterize failure from a network one.)*
`[ ]` **⏳ IMPLEMENTED this session — two real defects fixed in the client fetch-and-rasterise path (AUDIT-FIRST, read the actual rehydrate effect rather than guessing); parks in ⏳ Verify because the specific production PDF needs a real signed-in Storage round-trip to confirm end-to-end → V388320.**
- Verify: live — **LIVE-VERIFY class: real project data repro.** `Blocker: auth` — Supabase sign-in is CORS-blocked from this sandbox, so the exact Richfield/Quiddity 5.7 MB PDF can't be pulled through the real `doc-review-files` bucket and rasterized end-to-end here. Everything BELOW this line was verified in sandbox: the missing-backfill defect and the misclassification defect are both proven with mutation-checked source guards (RED confirmed against the pre-fix source, then GREEN), and the mechanism generalizes to any PDF/DXF/image overlay — it does not depend on the specific bytes of this one file.
- **AUDIT-FIRST — read the rehydrate effect (`SitePlanner.jsx`, the `[sheetOverlays, overlayLoadErr]` effect) end to end before writing anything**, rather than assuming the cause. Found TWO real, independently-provable gaps, neither previously flagged:
  1. **MISSING CACHE BACKFILL.** The other two places that produce a fresh raster — creating an overlay (`openOverlayFile`) and changing its page — both write the result back to IndexedDB (`idbPut(o.idbKey, r.src)`) so the next load is instant and offline-safe. The rehydrate-from-Storage path downloaded from cloud Storage and re-ran PDF.js/DXF, but never wrote the result back — so **every load on a device whose local cache doesn't already hold this overlay (a fresh browser, "clear site data", private mode, or a first `idbPut` that silently failed) re-pays the full download + re-rasterize forever**, never healing itself. Fixed: all three rehydrate branches (PDF/DXF/image) now backfill IndexedDB the same way the other two call sites already do.
  2. **A RASTERIZE FAILURE WAS SILENTLY MISCLASSIFIED AS "NETWORK."** `rasterizeStoredPdf`/`rasterizeStoredDxf` return `null` on ANY failure — a bad download, OR PDF.js/canvas throwing while decoding a page that DID download successfully (a real possibility on a 5.7 MB, 30×42 ARCH-E1 sheet). The caller could not tell these apart: a genuine rasterize failure was always recorded as `"network"` (implying a retry might help), with **zero telemetry** — the real bug is invisible even in production diagnostics, which is exactly the failure mode that would explain "healthy bytes, healthy permissions, still doesn't render, no error the owner can report beyond 'it doesn't render.'" Fixed: a raster-step failure now gets its own terminal reason (`"render"`, distinct from `"missing"`/`"network"`) and a `reportClientEvent("overlay-rasterize-failed", …)` row naming the site/overlay/key/byte-length — LOUD-FAILURE, so a recurrence of this exact production symptom is diagnosable from `client_errors` instead of a dead end. The on-canvas placeholder gained a matching "Couldn't render … — click to re-add the file" label (offering re-add, not an endless pointless retry on bytes that will decode the same way every time).
- **TESTS.** `test/overlayRehydrateCache.test.js` (12) — source guards on all three backfill branches + the `idbAvailable()` gate on each, the `rasterFailed` tracking and its LOUD telemetry, the terminal-reason ordering (rasterize failure classified BEFORE the generic missing/network fallback, never double-classified), and the placeholder's new label/action. **Mutation-proven both ways** — 9 of 12 real assertions confirmed RED against the pre-fix source (via `git stash` of just this file, re-run, then restored), the remaining 3 being the deliberate pre-fix-shape control assertions that are supposed to pass either way.
- **WHAT COULD NOT BE CONFIRMED HERE, STATED PLAINLY.** Whether THIS SPECIFIC production failure was the missing-backfill class, the rasterize-failure class, or both, cannot be distinguished without either a live signed-in session against the real Storage object or a `client_errors` read from after this fix ships (the new `overlay-rasterize-failed` event will say so directly if it recurs). Both fixed defects are real, provable bugs in the exact code path this overlay goes through on every load, and neither can make the situation worse — the backfill is strictly additive caching, and the reclassification only ever produces a MORE honest state than the "network" mislabel it replaces.
- Files: `src/workspaces/site-planner/SitePlanner.jsx`, `test/overlayRehydrateCache.test.js` (new).

### B711328 — Leasing Comps: a global comp layer (land / building sale / lease), pin-or-parcel anchored, team-visible & owner-editable, basis-normalized `[Site Planner / comps]` (feature) #site-planner #comps #gis #sync  *(owner chat block, driven with Jordan Bookstaff (Hillwood) on requirements, arrived alongside an unrelated "Graphic scale bar" brief that got paste-error-concatenated into one dispatch; the owner corrected this session mid-turn to build ONLY the comps half — the scale bar is a separate, already-dispatched session/branch and was deliberately not touched here. Minted **B711328 / V379872 · V379873** from this branch's reserved block B711328–B711343 / V379872–V379887 against `origin/main` 416a2e9. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open/⏳ Verify/Done for `comp`, `leasing`, `comparable`, `Bookstaff`: no prior item; the `public.comps` table, its RLS shape, and every module under `src/shared/comps/` are net-new. Phases 1–4 per the brief; KML import/export and the Jordan Bookstaff `team_id: null` gap are explicitly filed separately below (B711329, B711330), not built.)*
`[ ]` **⏳ merged — V379872 / V379873 PENDING (Verify: live).**
- Verify: live — two independent LIVE-VERIFY classes: **concurrency/multi-writer** (the team-read/owner-write RLS split — proven directly against the real database this session, see below, but never exercised through the actual signed-in UI) and **GIS endpoint behavior** (the parcel-anchor path depends on a live county identify service, egress-blocked from this sandbox).
- **STRUCTURE, decided and built exactly as specified.** A comp (`public.comps`) is its own entity, owned by the user who entered it — never a project type. `project_id` is a nullable FK to `public.sites`; a comp with no project at all is fully valid and equally visible ("I don't need to build on it to place a lease comp on it"). Every comp a viewer can access (their own + their team's, via `team_id`) is a map candidate regardless of which project it names or whether it names one.
- **ANCHOR: pin drop OR real parcel selection, never a drawn rectangle.** Built by REUSING `MapFinder.jsx`'s existing parcel-select flow rather than a second identify pipeline: the `+ Comp` button arms a small one-shot pin-drop mode (its own `placingCompPin` state/ref, mutually exclusive with `selectMode`); a `Comp here` button rides the EXISTING "+ Select parcels" selection bar, so a parcel anchor is exactly the parcel `selectMode` already resolved (its lon/lat `rings`, snapshotted into `parcel_geom` for the map layer — no re-derivation, no second query). `comps_parcel_anchor_has_identity` is a DB check constraint: a `parcel` anchor with no APN and no geometry is refused at the database, not just the UI.
- **SHARING — narrower than a shared site plan, DELIBERATELY, per the owner's own precedent for why: "that default cost this owner 57 elements off a live plan on 2026-08-21."** `public.comps` RLS composes two EXISTING precedents rather than inventing a third shape: the SELECT half is `team_sharing.sql`'s "own row OR a team you're in" verbatim; UPDATE/DELETE are `profiles.sql`'s plain owner-only shape (`user_id = auth.uid()`), with **no team-admin override** — not even a team admin can edit or delete a teammate's comp. Proven against the REAL production database (`lyeqzkuiwngunutlkkmi`), not just argued: a self-rolling-back RLS proof (`src/shared/comps/db/test/comps_rls.test.sql`) ran live via the Supabase MCP inside a `DO`/`RAISE EXCEPTION` block (nothing committed — confirmed after with a direct row-count read) and reported **9/9 PASS**, including the two negative controls that matter most — a teammate's UPDATE and DELETE against another member's team-shared comp both affect 0 rows.
- **THREE COMP TYPES, empty fields never render.** `compFieldRows(comp)` (`lib/comps.js`) is the ONE place that decision is made — a field with no value is simply absent from the returned row array, never an empty row or an em-dash, and the list, the detail view and (implicitly) the map tooltip all read the same function rather than re-deriving which fields apply per type. LAND's and BUILDING SALE's $/SF headline is DERIVED from price + size (`landPricePerSf`/`buildingPricePerSf`), never entered or stored twice — building SF, not land SF, for the building-sale figure. `comp_date` is the one field the database itself requires on all three (`not null`), matching the brief's "date REQUIRED" stated three times.
- **LEASE BASIS — stored as quoted, normalized only where the math is honest.** `lease_rate_period` (annual/monthly) and `lease_rate_expense` (NNN/gross) are both stored per comp, as quoted. `annualLeaseRate` converts period to annual with EXACT math (×12) and returns `null` — never a guessed default — when the period is unknown, because assuming annual on a comp quoted monthly would silently misstate it 12x in any aggregate. **NNN and gross are never blended into one number**: there is no honest conversion between them without the underlying expense figures this app doesn't have (an op-ex load), so `summarizeLeaseComps` keeps them as SEPARATE averages, defaults the headline to annual NNN (falling back to gross only when no NNN comps exist), and always NAMES the basis it's showing — a comp missing its rate or basis counts toward a reported `unknownCount`, never silently toward either average. This is the honest reading of "normalise to one display basis (annual NNN by default) and state which basis it is showing" — blending NNN and gross into one figure would itself be the "table that silently mixes monthly and annual figures" the brief explicitly ruled out, just on the other axis.
- **NOTES on every type**, free text, `compFieldRows` renders it last and only when non-empty.
- **UI**: `CompsPanel.jsx` (lazy-loaded, its own chunk — confirmed in the build output, not riding `SitePlannerApp`'s critical-path chunk) is a right-side panel — never a dialog (`window.prompt`/`confirm` stay banned) — that owns its own data (fetch/insert/update/delete) and self-fetches the current user + team list rather than threading them through `SitePlannerApp`. List view leads with the basis-normalized summary strip; detail view shows only the populated fields with Edit/Delete gated to the entering user; the create form opens pre-filled the instant a map anchor is picked. Map markers (`compMarkerIcon.js`) are a small colored tag, one hue per type, deliberately a different silhouette from `sitePinIcon` so a comp can never read as a project pin.
- **Sandbox-verified:** `npx vitest run` — **12,303 / 12,305 passing** (the 2 failures are pre-existing and unrelated to this branch — confirmed via `git stash`: both are `git show <hash>` mutation-check fixtures failing on a shallow clone missing that historical commit, identical on baseline). 34 new tests in `test/comps.test.js` (30) + `test/compMarkerIcon.test.js` (4) — every $/SF derivation, the NNN/gross non-blending rule (incl. the monthly→annual exact-math case and the "period unknown → excluded, never guessed" case), the empty-field-hide rule per type, anchor validation (pin/parcel/neither), and the row↔model round-trip (PostgREST numeric-as-string coercion). `eslint` on touched files: 0 errors (7 warnings, all matching this codebase's pre-existing "unused disable directive" pattern already present at baseline — confirmed via `git stash` diff). `vite build` green; `CompsPanel-*.js` confirmed as its own chunk. `MAP.md` + `BACKLOG_OPEN.md` regenerated.
- **⛔ WHAT THIS SANDBOX COULD NOT SEE, and what WAS driven headlessly instead of parked untried (ATTEMPT-BEFORE-YOU-PARK):** the parcel-anchor path needs a live county GIS identify (egress-blocked here) and the full signed-in insert/update/delete round trip needs Supabase auth (CORS-blocked here) — both genuinely need `Blocker: live-GIS` / `Blocker: auth` and are logged at V379872/V379873. Everything ELSE was driven live in a real headless browser rather than assumed: a new e2e spec (`e2e/leasing-comps.spec.js`, 2 specs) proves the `+ Comp` button arms, a map click opens the create form pre-filled, the armed prompt clears itself, and — LOUD-FAILURE — a signed-out save fails with a real, specific, non-silent message (this build carries no Supabase env at all, so the honest message is "Supabase not configured"; a configured-but-signed-out build says "Sign in to add a comp" instead, and the spec accepts either); a second spec proves the "Comps" toggle opens an honest empty-list state. Both pass against the real built app.

### B711792 — Deleting a building read the owner his own bonded assembly back as six "you just edited" banners (the SEVENTH round on the same-account-echo family) `[Site Planner / persistence · UI]` (bug) #site-planner #persistence #sync #ui  *(owner-reported live 2026-08-23: "I deleted one building and got this beautiful, um, abundance of banners to take over my screen." Two of HIS OWN tabs on one plan (presence chip "2 here" — no collaborator); one delete produced six stacked toasts, each reading "…you just edited changed in another tab of yours…" for a bonded-assembly member the owner never touched. Escalated three times in one session as the true mechanism was found. Minted **B711792 / V380336** LATE, `git fetch origin main && npm run next-id -- --against-main`, from this branch's reserved block B711792–B711807 / V380336–V380351 against `origin/main` be3f8e8. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open / ⏳ Verify / Done across `B673` (the matrix this amends — the row itself was always correct), `B757`/`B759`/`B811`/`B812` (single-tab self-echo, Done), `B846`/`B847` (the `isDirectEdit`/`direct` tagging this bug lived one branch away from), `B1116`/`B377888`/`B377891` (foreignAuthor + attribution wording, Done): every one of them closed an EDIT-cascade path; none of them ever classified a DELETE. Net-new — see the recurrence history below, which is the point of this entry.)*
`[x]` **SHIPPED — a solo user's own delete cascade produces zero banners; a genuine cross-account conflict still produces exactly one, naming the whole gesture rather than reciting each member. `Verify: live` → V380336.**
- Verify: live — a same-account/cross-tab notice, and a multi-element commit-batch coalesce, can only be *confirmed* by driving two real signed-in tabs (LIVE-VERIFY class: timing/concurrency/multi-writer).
- **⛔ RECURRENCE HISTORY — READ THIS BEFORE TOUCHING THE B673 MATRIX AGAIN.** The owner, verbatim, on being shown a coalescing-only fix: *"I thought I've addressed this at least twenty times with you… I don't think it's as simple as we just haven't figured out this simple root."* He was right. This is at least the **seventh** round on one family — same-account (or same-tab) traffic misread as a stranger editing the plan:
  1. **B757 (2026-07-11)** — five single-tab self-echo paths (the pending branch + `processResults`).
  2. **B759 (×2) / V301 (2026-07-13)** — the sixth path: the no-pending READ branch after a stale re-seed.
  3. **B811** — a resized building's bonded children snap back when a stale refetch re-seeds the shadow.
  4. **B812 (2026-07-13)** — `ownRevs` + a never-pruned rev high-water, after a refetch omitted an element.
  5. **B846 / B847 (2026-07-15)** — the TWO-TAB path: `direct` tagging so a cascade-DERIVED write never stamps `recent` (never claims "you just edited"); `semanticallyEqual`; the per-session journal.
  6. **B1116** — `foreignAuthor` (row `updated_by` vs the signed-in account) applied to `processResults`.
  7. **B377888 / B377891 (2026-08-12)** — `foreignAuthor` applied at another site; stopped naming a nonexistent teammate for a same-account echo.
  Every round closed ONE detection site for an EDIT cascade. **THIS bug is a DELETE cascade, and nothing above ever reached it** — which is the whole reason a seventh round was necessary and not a sign the family was mis-diagnosed six times.
- **THE ACTUAL HOLE, one line.** `SitePlanner.jsx`'s real `isDirectEdit` — `kind !== "el" || !el || el.attachedTo == null || isDirectTouched(kind, id)` — reads `el.attachedTo` to tell a bonded child (derived) from anything else (direct). A delete op carries **no element** (`elementSync.js` enqueues `{ cls: "delete", el: null, … }`), so `!el` short-circuited **every** delete, including every cascaded child's tombstone, to `direct: true`. `recent.set(...)` is gated on `direct !== false`, so every deleted child stamped its own authorship and answered `authoredRecently: true` for the whole ~15s window — the exact shape of the report: delete one building, and its bonded truck court / paving / parking field each individually claim "you just edited me" the moment any later activity touches them. **Fixed at the mechanism**, not at a new detection site: `elementSync.js`'s delete-enqueue now reconstructs the pre-delete element from the shadow's last-known json before calling `directTag`, so a delete is classified by the IDENTICAL rule an edit already was. Proven with a mutation check (the regression test fails red against the pre-fix source, green after).
- **THE SEPARATE HOLE `foreignAuthor` closes, defense-in-depth.** Independent of the above: `elementSync.js`'s no-pending `remote-upsert` emit (~1493 pre-fix) was the one B673 site that skipped `foreignAuthor(row)` — its sibling at ~1418 already had it (B1116). Added, and the same "would a SOLO user with two tabs ever see this" question was re-asked at every other self-attributable emit in the file (`remote-delete`, `remote-while-dirty`, `edit-vs-edit-lost-race`, `edit-vs-deleted`); each now toasts only when a genuinely different account wrote the row, OR this tab has an ACTIVE, DIRECT, uncommitted edit on the exact element being overwritten (the one same-account case that is real news — "your OTHER tab just overwrote what you're doing right now").
- **THE "COLLAPSE THE SIX SIGNALS" ASK — DONE FOR THE NOTICE LAYER, NAMED AS PARTIAL.** The owner asked for one authoritative `isOwnWrite(row)` used at all ~50 sites that ask some version of "did this row come from me" across `elementSync.js` (`recentSent`/`sentMatches`, `ownRevs`/`maxOwnRev`, `foreignAuthor`, `localEpoch`, `semanticallyEqual`, the `rev <= shad.rev` guard). **`foreignAuthor(row)` is now that one answer for the NOTICE layer** — every self-attributable B673 emit (the six above) is gated on it, uniformly, and `test/elementSyncOwnWriteGate.test.js` sweeps the real source (comments stripped, so it can't be fooled by a doc comment saying the function's name) and fails if a NEW `onEvent(...)` call carrying a `remote` row is added without either passing through `foreignAuthor` or being added to that test's documented EXEMPT table with a stated reason. **What this does NOT do:** migrate the other ~44 sites — the WRITE/CANVAS-correctness decisions (ignore vs. upsert, which rev to adopt, which json the shadow keeps) — onto one function. Those signals answer a materially stricter question (zero tolerance for a false positive OR negative, unlike a notice's fail-open-toward-silence), are each backed by their own dedicated guard tests from the six rounds above, and touching all of them blind in one session — with no live two-tab environment to verify against — is a correctness risk this session declined to take. **Flagged loudly, not silently dropped: a full sweep/consolidation of the write-path signals is real remaining work**, scoped and left for a session that can drive a live two-tab repro throughout. **⛔ AMENDMENT (2026-08-23, B712224):** that remaining sweep is no longer speculative hardening — **B712224 is the first measured, reproducible defect in this exact ~44-site remainder** (a stale `stateRef.current` read in `reconcileElems`, fed to `elementSync.reconcile()` after `drainRemote()`, resurrected three tombstoned bonded-assembly members under a second same-account tab). B712224 fixed that ONE site; the other ~44 are unaudited against the same class of race and should be treated as live work with a known repro shape to test against, not a hypothetical.
- **THE "DIRECTION 4" ASK — NAMED, PARTIALLY DELIVERED.** The owner cited a dropped handoff (`claude/handoff-2026-07-14-multiwriter-cascade-false-conflict.md`, in his own project, not this repo) whose fourth listed direction — "batch the cascade as one causal unit end-to-end so its derived members are never surfaced individually" — was never built; directions 1–3 shipped as B846/B847. This session delivers it for the **NOTICE layer**: `elementSync` already commits a bonded assembly (or any multi-element gesture — group delete, a parcel's bonded content, a multi-element undo, a paste) atomically, so every row in one commit shares a single `updated_at`/`deleted_at` to the microsecond — an EXISTING DB guarantee, not a new id to mint. `SitePlanner.jsx` now buffers sync events sharing (event type, that timestamp, the writer) for a short window and coalesces every surviving one into a SINGLE toast naming the group (`describeCoalescedLabel`, unit-tested) rather than reciting each member — group delete, parcel-cascade delete, multi-element undo, and paste all route through the same one-commit-per-gesture architecture, so they get this for free without gesture-specific code (structurally verified; not yet driven live on all four — see the live-verify steps below). **What this does NOT do:** thread a causal-unit id through the SERVER (a `commit`/`batch_id` column on `site_elements`, surviving echo and reload) — ~~that is a schema change touching `db/site_elements.sql` / `db/commit_elements_atomic.sql` / `db/commit_elements_group_cas.sql`, each with its own production-safety bar, and is out of scope for the same session as six other changes to this file.~~ **⛔ AMENDMENT (2026-08-23, B712225) — THAT CLAIM WAS WRONG, and a future session should not decline this work for a reason that turned out to be false.** The columns already existed on production `site_elements` (`op_id`/`op_kind`/`actor_session_id`/`client_ts`, confirmed via `information_schema.columns` against `lyeqzkuiwngunutlkkmi` — no committed migration ever created them) and the module that fills them (`lib/operationEnvelope.js`, B472048/B472049) already existed and was already tested — it had simply never been imported into a single write. **B712225 wired it**: `db/commit_elements_op_envelope.sql` (new) persists the four fields on every `commit_elements` branch, applied to production this session; `elementSync.js`/`SitePlanner.jsx` stamp `op_id`/`actor_session_id`/`client_ts` on every row from a per-tab `createOperationTracker`. So the correlation now DOES survive a page reload — no schema change was ever required, only wiring. (Owner-facing wish, unaffected: if the ORIGINAL owner ask here was for the correlation to survive a reload, that is now true.)
- **NEW-1 (round 2, SECONDARY per the owner's own correction — "the primary defect is that there should be ZERO"; this is the backstop for whatever residual traffic remains after the fixes above):** `TOAST_CAP` (`shared/ui/Toast.jsx`) dropped 4 → 2, so even an uncollapsed stack reads as a short strip pinned to the bottom edge rather than a wall reaching up the canvas. `Show` on a coalesced toast zooms/selects the UNION bbox of every named member (`zoomToElements`), never one arbitrary one.
- **Guards:** `test/elementSync.test.js` (97 tests total after this round, incl. the 8 NEW-0 same-account/foreign-account pairs and the 3 round-7 delete-classification tests — mutation-proven red pre-fix), `test/elementSyncOwnWriteGate.test.js` (21, the sweep guard above, itself mutation-proven against a comment-defeats-naive-regex false pass), `test/conflictToasts.test.js` (6, `describeCoalescedLabel`).
- **Steps for the live check, each with a named expected result** — logged at V380336.
- Files: `src/workspaces/site-planner/lib/elementSync.js`, `src/workspaces/site-planner/lib/conflictToasts.js`, `src/workspaces/site-planner/SitePlanner.jsx`, `src/shared/ui/Toast.jsx`, `test/elementSync.test.js`, `test/elementSyncOwnWriteGate.test.js` (new), `test/conflictToasts.test.js` (new).

### B709696 — A place missing from the food snapshot silently returned ten wrong restaurants, with no "no match" signal `[Food / search]` (bug) #food #testing  *(owner chat block 2026-08-23, "NEW-1" — searched "Cowboy Japanese BBQ&Sushi", a real 291-review Westheimer restaurant confirmed absent from `food_places` under any spelling, and got ten unrelated Japanese restaurants with no indication nothing matched. Minted **B709696 / V379280** from this branch's reserved block B709696–B709711 / V379280–V379295 against `origin/main` 1edf385. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open/⏳ Verify/Done for `food_places_search_by_name`, `no match`, `strong match`, `SearchBox`, `B632178`, `B634980`: no prior item addresses match QUALITY (as opposed to the search mechanism itself, which B632178/B634980 built). Net-new. Branch `claude/food-data-quality-search-crsd7e`.)*
`[x]` **SHIPPED — a genuinely non-matching search now produces zero results and correctly shows the "No matches" state with the live-search and drop-a-pin escape hatches, instead of ten unrelated results with no signal anything was wrong. `Verify: live` → V379280.**
- Verify: live — search-result quality is measured against the real 82,310-row production snapshot and can only be *confirmed* by driving the deployed app (LIVE-VERIFY class: GIS/data-endpoint behavior).
- Origin: owner chat block, 2026-08-23. Implemented and shipped this session (STANDING RULE #1).
- **AUDIT-FIRST — the escape hatches this item asks for already existed.** A prior session's own "NEW-1 (2nd owner block)" had already built the "No matches" state, the reused live-Overpass search offer, and the pre-filled drop-a-pin flow (`SearchBox.jsx`'s `showNoResults`/`showLiveOffer`/`onStartDropPinFor`, `FoodApp.jsx`'s `startDropPinFor`). **The actual defect** is that `showNoResults` gates on `results.length === 0`, and the RPC's own loose word_similarity threshold (0.3, deliberately loose for typo tolerance) let ten weak, wrong candidates count as "results" — so the no-match branch never fired and `showLiveOffer` (which needs `results.length < 3`) didn't either.
- **WHY A RAW SIMILARITY SCORE CANNOT FIX THIS — measured directly against production before choosing a design.** The Cowboy query's own top candidate ("Kansha Japanese Sushi Bistro") scores word_similarity 0.615 — no single cutoff separates that from a genuine match: a real typo'd match scores LOWER in a real case ("chiptle" → "Chipotle" scores 0.545) while OTHER garbage scores HIGHER ("chilis restaurant" → "El Viejo Solis Restaurant Corporation" scores 0.777, because 3,225 of the snapshot's 82,310 names contain the single word "restaurant"). word_similarity() rewards the best-matching SPAN of the query, so a query with one missing distinguishing word can still score high against a name sharing only its generic descriptor.
- **THE FIX — "strong match" is WORD COVERAGE, a named, tested, documented rule (`src/workspaces/food/lib/searchQuality.js`), not a magic number.** `isStrongMatch(query, name, address)`: strip generic restaurant-domain words (`GENERIC_NAME_WORDS` — measured: "restaurant" in 3,225 names, "grill" 3,533, "bar" 3,802, "kitchen" 1,847, "cafe" 3,131, "house" 1,452, "drive" 578), then require every (or, past 3 words, 75% of) remaining distinguishing word to appear — typo-tolerant (`EDIT_DISTANCE_TOLERANCE`, length-scaled Levenshtein) and prefix-tolerant ("mcdon" → "mcdonald's") — somewhere in the candidate's name OR address (so a location-qualified query like "fadis westheimer" still resolves against the street). Verified against every production case gathered this session: the Cowboy garbage (0 of 4 sampled candidates pass), "chilis restaurant"/"wendys drive thru"/"taco bell mexican" garbage (all correctly rejected, unlike a raw-sim cutoff would), and every genuine typo'd match this session found ("chiptle"→Chipotle, "mcdon"→Mcdonald's, "olive gardn"→Olive Garden, "whataburgr"→Whataburger, "bandito taco"→Bandito's Taco Grill, "panda expres"→Panda Express) all correctly pass.
- **A place he's already logged or flagged is EXEMPT from this filter** (`rankSearchCandidates`'s `protectedIds`) — a place he's personally vetted stays findable even on an odd fuzzy match; only the SNAPSHOT's own unvetted candidates are gated.
- Shares its implementation and its guards with **B709697** below (same file, same PR) — both ship together.
- **Sandbox evidence:** `npx vitest run test/foodModule.test.js` — 330/330 green (25 new tests in `searchQuality`'s own describe blocks, each pinned to a real production-measured case, not a synthetic one). Full-repo `npx vitest run` and `npm run build` run before push (see PR).
- **Steps for the live check, each with a named expected result** — logged at V379280.
- Files: `src/workspaces/food/lib/searchQuality.js` (new), `src/workspaces/food/components/SearchBox.jsx`, `test/foodModule.test.js`.

### B709697 — A low-confidence corrupted row (concatenated addresses, wrong coordinates) outranked two clean records for the same restaurant; corporate-filing names and duplicate source records pollute results `[Food / search]` (bug) #food #testing  *(owner chat block 2026-08-23, "NEW-2" — searched "fadis", picked what looked like the Westheimer location, and the map flew to a pin near Bellaire matching neither of the two real Westheimer addresses; the panel showed one place whose address read "12360 Westheimer Rd… and 6365 Westheimer Rd…, Houston, TX, 77077" — two real addresses concatenated into one field, coordinates matching neither. Minted **B709697 / V379281** from the same reserved block. DEDUPE-FIRST — same search as B709696 above: no prior item addresses `food_places.confidence`, registry-style names, or duplicate collapse. Net-new. Branch `claude/food-data-quality-search-crsd7e`.)*
`[x]` **SHIPPED — the corrupted row is excluded, registry-style names never outrank a real brand name, near-duplicate source records collapse to one, and every existing visit was checked to still resolve correctly. `Verify: live` → V379281.**
- Verify: live — GIS/data-endpoint behavior against the real 82,310-row production snapshot; only confirmable on the deployed app.
- Origin: owner chat block, 2026-08-23. Implemented and shipped this session (STANDING RULE #1).
- **CONFIDENCE IS A DE-RANK SIGNAL, NOT A HARD FLOOR — chosen from data, not vibes, per the brief's own instruction to sample before committing.** Sampled `food_places` directly across every confidence band from 0.50–0.60 (the very bottom — nothing scores lower) through 0.75–0.90: every band is dominated by completely ordinary real restaurants (Starbucks, Waffle House, Subway, Taco Bueno, Whataburger, Don Julios Mexican Restaurant, Doña Martha Comida Nicaragüense…) — there is no cut where "below this = bad" held up under inspection. A hard floor at the report's suggested 0.80 would have silently hidden 11,343 real rows (13.8% of the snapshot) for no measured quality gain. What confidence DOES do reliably: the "fadis" repro's own three exact-name candidates (sim 1.0) needed confidence to tell the clean meta/BrightQuery records (0.95–0.99) from the corrupted Foursquare one (0.77) — so it's used purely as a sort tiebreaker (`rankSearchCandidates` in `lib/searchQuality.js`), never a filter. Reported per the brief's ask: what was sampled (every 0.05-wide band from 0.50 to 0.90, ~20 rows per band eyeballed) and what was chosen (de-rank, not a floor) — with the reasoning above.
- **CONCATENATED ADDRESSES — detected and EXCLUDED (not repaired: the offending row's coordinates are also simply wrong, matching neither embedded address, so there is no safe text-only repair; excluding leaves the two already-clean duplicate records fully findable).** `CONCAT_ADDRESS_PATTERN` (`lib/searchQuality.js`) requires a real 5-digit zip immediately followed by "and" and a second house number — deliberately narrow so it never fires on a real Texas place name containing the word "and" ("Cut and Shoot, TX" and "Town and Country Way" are both common in this snapshot and were the first two false-positive shapes found and excluded while building the pattern). **AUDIT-FIRST discrepancy, recorded rather than silently matched:** the report estimated 37 rows of this shape; measured directly against production this session, only 2 currently match (the reported Fadi's row and one Dallas "Rise" record — confirmed to ALSO have high confidence, 0.985, proving confidence alone would never have caught it). The snapshot reloads periodically per this module's CLAUDE.md, so the counts can genuinely differ between samples; this is not claimed as a correction of the report, only as what THIS session measured. Applied both server-side (the RPC excludes these rows outright) and client-side (defense in depth).
- **REGISTRY-STYLE NAMES ("Fadis Express Binz Llc", "Fadis Signature Katy Inc") — measured 3,371 matching rows in production** (the report's manual count was 3,403 — same drift note as above) via the report's own `/\b(llc|inc|corp|holdings|management)\b/i` pattern (translated to JS). De-ranked, not excluded — some (like the Fadi's Binz St location) are real, otherwise-undocumented locations, so hiding them outright risked losing a real place with no clean-named duplicate; instead they NEVER outrank a non-registry match at any similarity score (`rankSearchCandidates` buckets non-registry names first, THEN by similarity/confidence/distance) — verified against the exact repro: "Fadis Signature Katy Inc" scores a higher raw similarity (1.0, no apostrophe) than the real "Fadi's Mediterranean Grill" (0.667, the apostrophe costs it trigram overlap) and is still correctly ranked below it.
- **DUPLICATE COLLAPSE — same brand, same real-world spot, different source, collapsed to one; genuinely distinct branches of the same chain stay fully separate and independently selectable.** Measured the actual geometry before picking a radius: the snapshot's two known same-location, multiple-source duplicates for this brand sit 25.8m and 38.9m apart (a Foursquare/BrightQuery record and a meta record for the identical Binz St storefront); the closest pair of genuinely DISTINCT same-brand locations sits ~3,540m apart. `DEDUPE_RADIUS_METERS = 150` sits in that gap. Verified: two Fadi's records at real, separately-measured production coordinates 39m apart collapse to one (the non-registry name wins); a set spanning three real, separate Fadi's addresses (Westheimer/Binz/Katy, km apart) all remain independently present in the result — Michael's own multiple Fadi's locations stay separately selectable and rateable.
- **VISITS CHECKED EXPLICITLY, per the brief's own instruction — nothing was silently broken.** Queried production directly: of his 173 existing `food_visits` rows, **3 point at a confidence-under-0.80 `food_places` row, 0 point at a registry-style-named row, 0 point at the 2 concatenated-address rows.** None of this matters anyway by construction — a visited/flagged place is drawn on the map and read in the List view via `fetchPlacesByIds`/`fetchAllVisits`, entirely separate code paths from the search RPC this item touches, and is additionally exempted from the new search filter/dedupe logic (`protectedIds` in `rankSearchCandidates`) so it also never disappears from a fresh SEARCH for it. **`food_places` itself was never written to** — filtering and ranking happen at query time only, matching this module's own "do this without deleting rows" instruction.
- **THE SQL CHANGE HIT A REAL PRIVILEGE WALL — recorded so a future session doesn't repeat the diagnosis.** Adding `confidence` to `food_places_search_by_name`'s output is a return-type change (needs DROP + CREATE), and re-issuing the function's existing `set pg_trgm.word_similarity_threshold = 0.3` clause — unchanged in VALUE, just re-stated — failed with `42501: permission denied to set parameter "pg_trgm.word_similarity_threshold"` from both the Supabase migration tool and a direct SQL session (confirmed live: this project's exposed `postgres` role has `rolsuper = false` on Supabase's hosted platform). Worked around by RENAMING the original, still-privilege-tuned function to `food_places_search_by_name_raw` (a rename never re-validates a SET clause) and wrapping it in a new, unprivileged `food_places_search_by_name` that adds `confidence` and the address exclusion. Applied directly to production and verified end to end (search "fadis": corrupted row gone; search "chiptle": the loose 0.3 threshold still returns "Chipotle" at sim 0.545 — proof the rename preserved the original tuning exactly). Full reasoning + the guarded, fresh-install-safe idempotent form is in `db/food.sql`'s own comment.
- Shares its implementation and its guards with **B709696** above (same file, same PR) — both ship together.
- **Sandbox evidence:** `npx vitest run test/foodModule.test.js` — 330/330 green. Full-repo suite + build run before push (see PR). Migration applied and verified directly against production `lyeqzkuiwngunutlkkmi` (see above).
- **Steps for the live check, each with a named expected result** — logged at V379281.
- Files: `src/workspaces/food/lib/searchQuality.js` (new), `src/workspaces/food/components/SearchBox.jsx`, `src/workspaces/food/db/food.sql`, `test/foodModule.test.js`. Production migration applied directly (see above).

### B688864 — "Map references" Aerial backdrop: Hide and Remove change nothing you can see, and Remove doesn't stick `[Site Planner]` (bug) #site-planner #gis #persistence #ui  *(owner chat, verbatim brief citing MEASURED production facts before a line of fix code was written: across all 54 production plans in Supabase project `lyeqzkuiwngunutlkkmi`, 48 carry `sites.data.underlay`, and ALL 48 have `fromMap: true` with an arcgisonline World_Imagery export `src` — every one auto-generated from the map, none a user-uploaded document.
