`[x]` **IMPLEMENTED this session — Hide and Remove now have real, persistent effects on the picture the owner actually sees; parks in ⏳ Verify (Verify: live — a real signed-in check against one of his own georeferenced production plans; the mechanism is otherwise proven end-to-end, live, in a headless browser against the real built app) → V362512.**
- Verify: live — V362512 (`Blocker: auth` — the whole mechanism is driven and proven headless below against a seeded plan with the exact production shape (`origin` set, `underlay.fromMap: true`); what the sandbox cannot do is sign in and confirm it on one of his own 48 real aerials)
- Origin: owner chat, 2026-08-22.
- **AUDIT-FIRST — established which of the report's two candidate causes was real, rather than assuming either (the brief explicitly required this).** Read `SitePlanner.jsx` end to end for how the row's three controls (eye / padlock / ✕) and the picture on screen actually connect, before writing anything:
  1. **The row draws through TWO independent techniques the owner cannot tell apart.** The captured `underlay` object (the padlock/opacity/calibration fields) is rendered as a plain SVG `<image>` — but ONLY `!(origin && basemapOn)`, i.e. only when the LIVE Leaflet basemap tile layer isn't already covering it. `basemapOn` is `basemapSrc !== "off" && !!origin`, and `basemapSrc` **defaults to `"esri"` (on) the instant a plan has a real `origin`** — true for every one of the 48 `fromMap` plans, since they were all captured FROM the map picker, which always sets one. So on every one of those plans, the picture on screen is the LIVE tiles, not the static image the row's opacity slider even claims to control (the row already said as much in a buried sentence: *"Hidden while the live map basemap is on — the basemap IS the aerial there"* — printed, but never acted on).
  2. **The eye (Hide) toggle — `showAerial` — never touched that live layer at all**, and was a bare `useState(true)`, not part of the saved plan. So on a `fromMap` plan (basemap on) it changed **nothing visible in the same session**, and even on the rare plan where it WOULD have mattered (basemap off), it reset to shown on every reload — never persisted, for any plan, ever.
  3. **Remove (✕) DOES clear the archived snapshot** (`underlay: null`, confirmed it writes and persists like every other site-model field) — the brief's option (b), "it writes and the underlay is regenerated," is **REFUTED**: nothing in `MapFinder.jsx`'s `fromMap: true` construction path runs again on an existing plan's reload, so a deleted underlay does not come back. What actually happens is worse for the owner's mental model, not a data bug: **the live basemap tiles were never touched by Remove either**, so the identical-looking aerial stays on screen — read, correctly, as "deleting it does nothing," even though the archived record genuinely is gone.
- **THE FIX — real, persisted hide/delete semantics (the brief's option (a)), implemented rather than the wording-only relabel B525632/B519152 already tried and which the brief explicitly forbade repeating.** New pure module `lib/aerialVisibility.js`: `settings.aerialHidden` (sparse — absent means shown, the same convention `settings.hidden`/content-visibility already uses) is now the ONE persisted fact behind the eye toggle, and `wantBasemapSrc(basemapOn, aerialVisible, basemapSrc)` is the corrected decision for the live tile layer's `want` — gated on that same fact, not just on `basemapSrc`/`origin` as before. `showAerial` in `SitePlanner.jsx` is now derived from `settings` (via `isAerialVisible`) with a `setShowAerial` that persists through `withAerialVisible`, instead of a throwaway `useState`. The background-grey/grid-line cosmetics (`SitePlanner.jsx` lines that painted the dark placeholder / suppressed the drafting grid) are gated the same way, so hiding the aerial also restores the ordinary grid rather than leaving a blank dark rectangle. Two reconciliation edges, so the row-1 Layers-panel "Basemap" dropdown (a separate, pre-existing control over `basemapSrc` itself) can't silently fight the References-panel Hide: picking a source there un-hides (an explicit direct pick wins), and loading a brand-new screenshot un-hides too (so a prior Hide/Remove can't silently suppress content the user just added).
- **THE SECOND COMPLAINT — "this row arguably shouldn't be in that panel at all."** Per the brief's own framing ("Implement ONE of" the two options), real hide/delete semantics (option (a), implemented above) is itself a complete, valid resolution — the row's controls now do exactly what a "Map reference" row's controls are supposed to do. Relocating the aerial out of the References panel (option (b)) was NOT also done: it would be a materially larger, separate UI-restructuring change, and the brief's explicit "Do NOT ship a wording change" was about not treating a copy tweak as a substitute for function — not a mandate to also relocate a working control. Filing a follow-up for (b) would itself be the kind of park-it-for-later this repo's STANDING RULE #1 exists to prevent when (a) already resolves the reported symptom; not filed separately.
- **AUDIT-FIRST, proved RED before the fix, twice — at both the correct unit-testable boundary and live, end to end:**
  - `test/aerialVisibility.test.js`'s "MUTATION CHECK" replays the exact pre-fix formula (`basemapOn ? basemapSrc : null`, blind to Hide) and asserts it disagrees with the shipped fix on the exact regression case (`basemapOn:true, hidden:true` → pre-fix wrongly keeps `"esri"`, fixed correctly returns `null`).
  - New live harness `ui-audit/verify-aerial-hide-delete.mjs` drives the REAL built app in headless Chromium: seeds a plan carrying the exact 48-plan shape (`origin` set + `underlay.fromMap: true`), and counts the live basemap's own `World_Imagery` tile nodes inside `window.__geoMap`'s container (the E2E-only hook `SitePlanner.jsx` already exposes) as the ground truth for "is the aerial actually on screen" — scoped past two false-positive tile sources found while building it: the tile pane's unrelated `World_Transportation` road-reference layer, and `MapFinder`'s own, independently-mounted picker map (`SitePlannerApp` keeps both hosts mounted at once, per the architecture notes). **Run against the UNMODIFIED pre-fix `SitePlanner.jsx` (via `git stash`, rebuilt, re-run, then restored): Hide left 49/49 tiles on screen — reproducing the bug exactly** — then green on the fix: known-good arm (aerial on by default, 49 tiles) → Hide removes all of them → **survives a reload** → Show restores them → Remove clears both the row AND the tiles → **survives a reload** too. 12/12 checks pass on the fixed build.
- **Sandbox result:** `npx vitest run` — **12,197 passed / 589 files**, 0 new failures (13 new tests in `test/aerialVisibility.test.js`, all passing; `test/mapDrift.test.js`/`test/deadStores.test.js` both green after regenerating `MAP.md` and avoiding a `no-unused-vars` rest-destructure trip in the new file). `eslint` on touched files: **0 errors**, same 10 pre-existing warnings as the pre-change baseline (confirmed via `git stash` diff — 0 new). `vite build` green. `node ui-audit/verify-aerial-empty-state-copy.mjs` (the current B525632 regression guard) still 6/6 — this fix does not touch the empty-state branch at all. `node ui-audit/diagnose-aerial-backdrop-row.mjs` was already stale before this change (last touched pre-B525632's reword; it checks for the OLD "Aerial backdrop" heading on the empty state, which B525632 deliberately renamed to "Add an aerial") — confirmed via `git log` that its failure predates this branch and is unrelated; not touched, per "smallest correct change."

### B683568 — The View card read a mid-load empty snapshot as "nothing to hide": a signed-in plan's real content vanished from the menu until its rows arrived `[Site Planner / view]` (bug) #site-planner #view #ui #sync #testing  *(owner-diagnosed report, 2026-08-22: the View tab shows a stripped-down control set — only Column grid/Dimensions/Element areas/Parcel acreage — on some plans, and B442688's full "hide a class of content" menu (the tri-state Elements master + per-type rows) on others, reading as being stuck on an old build. The brief's own hypothesis — the Content section gates on whether `settings.hidden` has ever been written, a chicken-and-egg — was tested against the SOURCE, per house rule, and **REFUTED**: `ViewMenu.jsx`'s Content section (lines ~169-204, pre-fix) is gated purely on `counts` (real element/parcel/markup/measure/callout presence via `groupsFor`), never on whether `settings.hidden` exists — `isHidden`/`groupState` handle an absent `hidden` map fine and only affect which boxes are CHECKED, never whether the section RENDERS. Confirmed against production (`lyeqzkuiwngunutlkkmi`, read-only queries) that `settings.hidden` presence/absence is uncorrelated with real content: queried `site_elements` directly for both the owner's account and jordan.bookstaff@hillwood.com's — every schemaVersion-12 and -13 plan checked (Bain, Silvestri ×4, Goose Creek ×5, Tsakiris, Katz, Turner JV Site, 7790 E 88th Ave, …) carries real rows (9 to 116 elements each), completely independent of whether `hidden` was ever set — Jordan's plans have real content too, contrary to what the `sites.data.els` blob alone suggests. The falsifiable prediction (the owner should see the same panel on his own schemaVersion-12 plans) doesn't confirm the hypothesized MECHANISM either — nothing in the render path branches on `schemaVersion`. **RE-DIAGNOSED, retracting the handed-in hypothesis rather than fixing to fit it:** a signed-in plan's cloud header (`slimForCloud`, `lib/cloudSync.js`) deliberately carries NO elements — they live in `site_elements` rows since B672's read cutover — so on every open of a signed-in plan, `els`/`parcels`/`markups`/`measures`/`callouts` read as genuinely EMPTY for the window between the plan opening and `elementSync`'s first successful `refetchReplace`. `ViewMenu`'s Content section read that transient empty snapshot as "this plan has nothing to hide" and rendered nothing at all, leaving only the Detail/Labels ornament toggles — structurally the PRE-B653 menu minus dock doors. The same open card, untouched by the user, silently grows the Content section once the rows land (typically under a couple of seconds; longer on a heavy plan or a slow connection) — exactly what reads as "stuck on an old build" to someone who glances at the card right after switching plans. Minted **B683568 / V357216** from this branch's reserved block B683568–B683583 / V357216–V357231 against `origin/main` 8f59326. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open/⏳ Verify/Done across `ViewMenu`, `contentVisibility`, `groupsFor`, `B442688`, `B653`, `B3296`, `B494048`–`B494051`, `elementsReady`, `refetchReplace`, `isSeeded`, `slimForCloud`: B442688 owns the content MODEL (correct, untouched) and B3296/B494048-51 own OTHER unfiltered-read seams found by a prior audit; none of them address `counts` itself being transiently wrong before the rows arrive. `[x]` **SHIPPED — the View card now distinguishes "still loading" from "genuinely empty" and never presents the reduced ornament-only layout as a settled state. `Verify: live` → V357216.**
- Verify: live (**LIVE-VERIFY class: timing/race** — the defect exists only in the window before a signed-in plan's element rows land, which this sandbox cannot reproduce: Supabase auth is blocked here. `Blocker: auth`.)
- **ROOT CAUSE, confirmed against real production data** (read-only `execute_sql` against `lyeqzkuiwngunutlkkmi` — no writes made): `slimForCloud` strips `els`/`markups`/`measures`/`callouts`/`parcels` from every signed-in plan's cloud header (`elementsInRows: true`); `SitePlanner.jsx`'s `[siteId]` effect only starts the rows engine when cloud-active, and its `refetchReplace` is the sole path that seeds real elements into React state.
- **THE FIX** (`SitePlanner.jsx`, `components/ViewMenu.jsx`): a new `elementsReady` flag — `false` while a cloud-active plan's rows haven't been seeded at least once (reusing `elementSync`'s existing `eng.isSeeded()`/`seed()` concept, now surfaced to React), `true` immediately for a signed-out/local-only plan (whose `els` is already complete synchronously from `loadSite`). `ViewMenu` renders a "Loading what's on this plan…" placeholder in the Content section's slot while `!elementsReady`, instead of omitting the section outright, so the card's shape never silently swaps between "looks like the old build" and "looks like the new one." Once ready, it renders exactly as B442688 built it — including correctly rendering nothing for a plan that truly has no content, which stays unchanged.

Queried production: 51 of 53 live plans read `true`, 2 read `null` (defaults `true`); **zero** currently read `false`, so the migration has already done its job for every plan touched since it shipped — it stays as cheap, already-documented insurance for any plan not yet re-saved, not removed.

Asserts by SHAPE: mid-load shows the loading placeholder and withholds the live rows; ready-with-content shows the live tri-state master + per-type rows; ready-with-genuinely-nothing still renders no Content section at all (unchanged pre-existing behaviour); the prop defaults to `true` for backward compatibility.

### B672115 — The planner must route a parcel click by WHERE IT IS, like the map already does `[Site Planner]` (bug) #site-planner #gis #ui  *(owner chat block 2026-08-22 — a real incident: a teammate, Jordan, on a Colorado site panned well away from the site inside the planner and could no longer select parcels, though the SAME point worked from the Map view. Root cause diagnosed by the owner off the actual code (`SitePlanner.jsx`'s `resolveCountyLayer`) and confirmed against the real source. Minted **B672115 / V345760** from this branch's reserved block against `origin/main` 7fbe151. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open/⏳ Verify/Done across `resolveCountyLayer`, `identify`, `candidateCountiesForPoint`, `B137`, `B383`, `B792`, `B36a`, `B130`, `siteCounty`: **B137** is the "outlines match what you can add" contract this fix keeps intact, not supersedes; **B792** heals a WRONG stored `siteCounty` after the fact (a data problem) and is orthogonal to this — routing by a frozen field regardless of whether it is right; **B383/B36a/B130** built the Map view's OWN point-based routing + statewide fallback, which this item makes the PLANNER's identify use too, rather than reinventing it. Net-new — no prior item addressed the planner's identify being pinned to one county for the life of the session.)*
`[x]` **IMPLEMENTED this session; parks in ⏳ Verify (Verify: live — needs a real signed-in browser against real county parcel GIS services, all egress-blocked from this sandbox) → V345760.**
- Verify: live — V345760 (`Blocker: live-GIS` — every county parcel service this needs is unreachable from Chromium in this sandbox)
- Origin: owner chat block, 2026-08-22 — filed and shipped the same session.
- **THE BUG, exactly as diagnosed.** `resolveCountyLayer` resolved the site's parcel-identify layer URL ONCE, on first use (`if (idLayerRef.current) return idLayerRef.current;`), keyed on `siteCounty` — the county recorded when the site was CREATED — with a `COUNTIES_MAP[siteCounty] || COUNTIES_MAP.harris` fallback. Three compounding defects: it never re-asked as the view panned across a county line; it cached the answer for the whole planner session even after crossing one; and an unconfigured/unresolved county silently fell back to querying **Harris County, Texas** forever — the identical wrong-but-plausible default `candidateCountiesForPoint` was already fixed against, surviving here in the ONE place the Map view's fix never reached. Because the SAME URL backed both the lit outlines and the click query (the B137 rule, deliberately preserved), the outlines went dark too — exactly the owner's "the parcels didn't show up," not merely "the click failed."
- **THE FIX (`SitePlanner.jsx`).** Replaced the single frozen `idLayerRef`/`resolveCountyLayer` with a per-county URL cache (`countyLayerUrlsRef`, `resolveOneCountyLayer`) shared by both consumers, and a `candidatesAtPoint(lat, lng)` helper that routes every click through the SAME `candidateCountiesForPoint` + `filterHealthyCandidates` the Map view already uses — re-asked fresh for every point, never pinned to the site's recorded county, and with **no county fallback of any kind**: an unconfigured area returns no candidates rather than a wrong-but-plausible one. The lit outline effect now lights up every configured county's outlines (mirroring exactly what `MapFinder` already does — resolve every county, add every one's display layer) instead of only the site's recorded one, so panning across a county line shows that county's lots instead of nothing, and the click routes to whatever the point is actually in.
- **B137 kept intact, deliberately.** Outlines and the click query still share one routing decision (`candidateCountiesForPoint`) and one URL cache — they cannot drift into "I can see it but I can't add it" by construction, the same guarantee the original comment described, just no longer pinned to one county.
- **Sandbox result:** lint 0 errors · new source-guard suite `test/parcelClickRouting.test.js` (4 — no `COUNTIES_MAP.harris`/`COUNTIES.harris` fallback anywhere in the identify path, no single frozen `idLayerRef`, both consumers route through `candidateCountiesForPoint`, the honest-cause error messaging is wired — see **B672114**) · `counties.test.js` / `arcgis.test.js` / `sourceHealth.test.js` unaffected (30/28/13 green, these are the pure functions this reuses, untouched) · full suite 12,086/12,088 green (2 pre-existing shallow-clone-only failures, unrelated — see B323424 (×2)) · build/lint green.
- **⛔ WHAT THIS SANDBOX COULD NOT SEE.** Every county parcel service (HCAD, the TxGIO/Colorado statewide composites, every county CAD) is unreachable from Chromium here, so the actual live "pan across a county line, click, get a lot" cannot be produced. The fix is proven at the wiring level (the frozen-county/Harris-fallback code is gone, the SAME routing function the Map view already relies on now drives the planner too) but not watched selecting a real lot across a real county boundary.

### B651872 (×4) — Selecting a search result leaves the food map blank until you zoom or pan `[Food]` (bug) #food #gis #ui #testing  *(owner report 2026-08-22, arrived as NEW-1, with extensive live DOM measurements already gathered on planyr.io/#/food (tile presence/opacity/positioning, the `.leaflet-tile-container` transform matrix, the post-interaction "band with grey margins" case) — see the full repro in the code comment at `FoodMap.jsx`'s flyTo effect. Net-new.)*
`[x]` **⏳ SHIPPED (×4) — the owner's own follow-up measurement was right: the flight itself fetches tiles at EVERY zoom level it sweeps through (owner captured a real request for zoom 5 mid-Maui-flight), and retina tiles cost 2-5x more than they're worth on a phone. A long jump now goes straight to the destination (no animation, no sweep) — measured 136 tile requests across 12 zoom levels before this fix, 7 requests all at the destination zoom after. `Verify: live` → V330864 (updated).**
- Recurrence: 2026-08-22 — B651872's fix cured the stale tile-grid ORIGIN but exposed a second bug in the SAME code path: after a search-select flyTo, tiles now position correctly but render as a washed-out ghost, frozen at ~30% opacity (measured live: 11 of 24 tiles stuck at exactly opacity 0, the rest spread 0.295–0.34, unchanged across repeated polls at t=0s/4s/8s). Re-opens B651872 per DEDUPE-FIRST — same underlying symptom class ("the map doesn't paint after a search jump"), not a new number.
- Recurrence: 2026-08-22 (×3) — the fade fix was genuinely complete (owner-measured: 27 tiles, all `naturalWidth>0`, computed opacity 1, unchanged at t=0s/3s/6s) but a Houston→Maui jump still painted flat grey for several seconds, with two `.leaflet-tile-container` levels present — one at a fractional scale (0.9118, not 1), one at 0 children. Owner's own hypothesis (a fractional landing zoom from a `zoomSnap`/bounds-fit issue) was checked and does NOT hold for this code path — see ROOT CAUSE below. Re-opens B651872 per DEDUPE-FIRST, same symptom class, not a new number.
- Recurrence: 2026-08-22 (×4) — owner's own follow-up measurement, on the live site, wired connection (a floor, not typical — his is cellular): during a Houston→Maui jump, tiles were requested at zoom 5 mid-flight (e.g. `World_Imagery/MapServer/tile/5/12/6`) before the camera ever reached zoom 16 — the (×3) duration cap made the sweep faster, it never stopped it. Separately measured: `@2x` retina tiles average 45.7 KB / 129 ms median per tile vs 21.4 KB / 23 ms for `1x`, cold — a full retina screen (12-20 tiles) is ~550-900 KB before a single pin draws, seconds over LTE, and lands at a fractional zoom anyway so the extra resolution gets resampled away. Re-opens B651872 per DEDUPE-FIRST, same symptom class ("the map doesn't paint promptly after a search jump"), not a new number. Separately reported in the SAME message: a clean horizontal grey band (top half grey, bottom half correct tiles) specifically on mobile with the new bottom sheet open — investigated as possibly the SAME root cause; see ROOT CAUSE below for the finding (not the same mechanism, but not left unaddressed either).
- Verify: live (`Blocker: live-GIS` — unchanged from the original ship: the sandbox's own egress proxy blocks the real CARTO/Esri tile hosts this needs outright, `403` on `a.basemaps.cartocdn.com`. None of the three bugs in this item's history could be reproduced or re-confirmed from here against real tile servers — this recurrence's mechanism was instead confirmed by instrumenting a real Leaflet map with synthetic tiles, see below.)
- **ROOT CAUSE, the (×2) recurrence — Leaflet's own tile fade-in, not the origin/reset mechanics B651872 already fixed.** Live proof the fade is the WHOLE problem and nothing else is wrong: the owner ran `document.querySelectorAll('.leaflet-tile').forEach(t=>t.style.opacity=1)` in the console on the live, broken page and the map rendered perfectly — correct location, correct zoom, selected pin ringed. `GridLayer._tileReady` (`node_modules/leaflet/dist/leaflet-src.js`) branches on `this._map._fadeAnimated`: when true, a loaded tile is set to `opacity:0` and handed to ONE shared `requestAnimFrame` handle (`this._fadeFrame`) that steps every tile's opacity up each frame — a single shared rAF chain that a burst of tiles loading in quick succession (exactly what a big flyTo jump triggers) can apparently leave orphaned partway, for reasons independent of the origin/reset fix. When `fadeAnimated` is false, `_tileReady` instead marks the tile `active` immediately with **no opacity manipulation at all** — nothing to ever get stuck. FIX: `fadeAnimation: false` at map construction — not a `setTimeout`/`setInterval` forcing opacity, which the owner explicitly asked NOT to do.
- **ROOT CAUSE, the (×3) recurrence — `flyTo`'s own distance-proportional duration, NOT a fractional landing zoom.** The owner's own hypothesis (check `zoomSnap`/`zoomDelta`, whether the target zoom comes from a `fitBounds`) was verified and refuted for this code path: both are Leaflet's untouched defaults (1), and the zoom passed to `flyTo` here is always a literal integer (`Math.max(map.getZoom(), FLY_TO_ZOOM)`), never a `fitBounds`-derived fraction — confirmed by instrumenting a real Leaflet map (not a paraphrase) and logging every `_move`/`_setView` call through a live Houston→Maui flight. **What's actually happening:** `map.flyTo` with no `duration` option computes one from real-world distance via Leaflet's own van-Wijk/Nuutinen curve — measured directly against the real formula: ~1.6s for a same-neighbourhood hop, ~2.4s Houston→Katy, ~4.2s Houston→Austin, **~7.8s Houston→Maui**. For a jump that long, the animation continuously sweeps through EVERY integer zoom between start and destination (12 down to ~5, back up to 16), and GridLayer creates/tears down a tile level at each one it passes through — the "two levels, one fractional-scale, one 0-children" snapshot the owner measured is not a stuck state, it's a NORMAL mid-flight frame of an animation that was still running when it was measured (its own natural landing was still several seconds away). Confirmed by instrumenting the identical flight to run to its true, natural end, repeatedly (4 trials, both with the tile server's baseline latency and realistic 150-350ms jittered latency): it always settles to exactly one level, `scale(1)`, an integer zoom — the existing hard-reset from the (×1) ship is not flaky. The bug is that the flight simply takes too long for the user to perceive as landed before it visibly is.
- **THE FIX, this recurrence: cap `flyTo`'s duration at a fixed 1.5s** (`FLY_DURATION_SEC`, `FoodMap.jsx`) — measured to match what a local jump already takes naturally, so a same-neighbourhood search feels unchanged, while a cross-metro/city/country jump no longer balloons to several seconds. Not a redraw or a timer patched over the symptom (the owner's explicit "do not paper over it" instruction) — it directly shortens the window the animation spends sweeping through unneeded intermediate zoom levels, so the destination's own tiles start loading sooner and the flight settles before the user is watching for it to.
- **SELECTED PIN, checked per the owner's explicit ask ("confirm whether the selected marker renders at the landing zoom, and if it does not, say so plainly rather than filing it as fixed") — it did NOT.** A place selected via search but never visited/flagged draws ONLY from the bounds-scoped reference snapshot (`places`, refetched only on 'moveend'), unlike `loggedPlaces`/`manualPins`/`wishlistPlaces` (none are bounds-gated). Right after a jump, before that refetch lands, the selected place genuinely had no pin at all. Fixed alongside the duration cap: `selectedPlaceInfo` (FoodApp.jsx) threads the selected place's own lat/lon/name through as a prop, and `FoodMap.jsx`'s marker-redraw effect draws ONE fallback pin for it whenever `selectedKey` isn't already covered by one of the always-drawn sets — verified against the real production `FoodMap.jsx` component (not a paraphrase), mounted via a scratch Vite entry with the selected place absent from every drawn set: the fallback pin rendered at the exact selected coordinates.
- **ROOT CAUSE, the (×4) recurrence — `flyTo`'s own zoom-level sweep, plus a real byte/latency cost the owner independently measured, neither previously addressed.** The (×3) fix capped duration but never stopped `flyTo` from sweeping through every intermediate integer zoom on a long jump — each level triggers a full screen of tile requests that get thrown away a few hundred ms later, all competing with the DESTINATION tiles for the browser's ~6 connections. Confirmed by reimplementing `flyTo`'s own van-Wijk/Nuutinen curve and finding the MINIMUM zoom each jump sweeps down to (`.scratch-repro/measure-zoom-depth.html` this session): Katy (~48km, same metro) only dips to z11.7 from z12 — negligible; Austin (~235km) dips to z9.6; Maui (~6128km) dips to z5 — matching the owner's own live capture exactly. Separately, Leaflet substitutes `{r}`→`@2x` in a tile URL UNCONDITIONALLY whenever `Browser.retina` is true (every iPhone) — confirmed from `TileLayer.getTileUrl`'s own source — regardless of any `detectRetina` option, so this app has been paying the full retina byte/latency cost on every phone regardless of viewport size.
- **THE FIX, three parts, each measured:** (1) **Stop the sweep** — `LONG_JUMP_METERS` (100km, measured per above) gates a DIRECT `map.setView(dest, zoom, {animate:false})` instead of `flyTo` beyond that distance — no animation at all, so the destination's own tiles are the FIRST thing requested. **Measured before/after** (`.scratch-repro/verify-tile-perf.mjs`, real Leaflet + a local tile server, driving the real `FoodMap.jsx` component): Houston→Maui went from **136 tile requests across 12 distinct zoom levels (5 through 16), first request at zoom 11**, to **7 tile requests, ALL at zoom 16, first request AT zoom 16** — a 95% reduction, and the wasted-fetch class is now structurally gone for any jump this far, not just slowed down. A short jump (Katy, under the threshold) is unchanged (51→50 requests, same zoom range) — the animation there was never the problem. (2) **1x tiles on a narrow viewport, street basemap only** (`STREET_TILES.url1x`, gated on the same breakpoint `VisitPanel.jsx` already uses) — Esri's satellite layer never had a `{r}` token to begin with. **Verified live** (`.scratch-repro/verify-retina.mjs`, `deviceScaleFactor:2` in both cases): the resolved URL template drops `{r}` entirely at 390px width, keeps it at 1400px. Not independently visually diffed against real CARTO tiles — this sandbox's egress proxy blocks the real hosts outright — flagged honestly rather than claimed proven. (3) **A real loading treatment** — a small "Loading imagery…" pill tied to the current tile layer's own `loading`/`load` events, so grey reads as in-progress, not broken; "keep the previous tiles" doesn't apply to a jump to a genuinely different place, so there's nothing relevant to keep.
- **THE MOBILE GREY BAND, investigated separately, per the owner's explicit "say so plainly, do not assume either way."** Could NOT reproduce the reported mechanism (a clean horizontal grey band, top half only, on mobile with the sheet open) from the bottom sheet mounting: `BottomSheet.jsx` renders `position:fixed`, which Flexbox does not allocate layout space for, so it cannot resize `FoodMap`'s own container by CSS mechanics alone. Confirmed by instrumenting the real `FoodMap`/`VisitPanel` pair at iPhone width through the exact real sequence (map mounts alone at full height → sheet mounts later on selection → snap settles): Leaflet's own `_size` and the container's real `getBoundingClientRect()` stayed IDENTICAL throughout, every sample, across two separate harness attempts. **Not the same mechanism as the (×4) sweep/retina fix, but not left unaddressed:** (a) the tile-loading fixes above are the better-evidenced explanation for a partially-painted screen at whatever moment a screenshot was taken (an iPhone on cellular is exactly where the intermediate-zoom-sweep + retina cost bites hardest — this is very likely what was actually captured), and (b) shipped a genuinely missing piece of hardening regardless: nothing in this file previously told Leaflet when its container's own size changed OUTSIDE of a flyTo/setView (the only `invalidateSize()` calls lived inside that one effect) — a device rotation or an iOS Safari dynamic-toolbar resize at any other moment would leave Leaflet's cached size stale with nothing to correct it. A `ResizeObserver` on the host div now calls `invalidateSize()` the instant the container's real size changes, never on a timer — closes that whole class regardless of what triggers it, and was verified live (`.scratch-repro/verify-resize-observer.mjs`): resizing the real browser viewport with NO flyTo/setView call in between still correctly updated `map.getSize()`.
- **What was verified here (sandbox, cannot reach real tile servers — see the Blocker above):** the (×2) fade fix — rebuilt the isolated Leaflet harness with the fade flag toggleable and the exact flyTo+hard-reset code path; `fadeAnimation:false` painted every jump fully opaque with zero tiles stuck at any intermediate opacity. The (×3) duration fix — instrumented a real Leaflet map (real `L.tileLayer`, a local HTTP tile server with realistic jittered latency) logging every `_setView`/`_pruneTiles`/`_updateLevels` call through the flight; with `duration: 1.5`, both a Houston→Maui long hop and a same-neighbourhood short hop settled in ~1.5s wall-clock, every run (3+2 trials), always ending at exactly one tile level, `scale(1)`, integer zoom. The selected-pin fallback — verified against the real `FoodMap.jsx` component mounted in a real browser, confirmed rendering. The (×4) fixes — all four verified live against real Leaflet/real browser instrumentation, detailed above. Full suite green (12,154), lint clean, build green.

`[x]` **SHIPPED (×5) — REPRODUCED, ROOT-CAUSED, AND FIXED, against the REAL app.** `Verify: live` → V330864 (updated).
- **HOW IT WAS FINALLY REPRODUCED, per the owner's own instruction on how the prior session's attempt fell short.** The prior session's harness used plain `page.setViewportSize()` at a narrow width — Chromium's `isMobile` device-emulation flag (which `page.setViewportSize()` alone does NOT set) changes viewport semantics in ways a plain resize doesn't. This session used Playwright's real device descriptor (`devices['iPhone 14 Pro']` — `isMobile:true, hasTouch:true` together) against the REAL running dev build (not a synthetic stand-in), drove the real "drop a pin" flow (search needs network, blocked in this sandbox; drop-a-pin needs none and exercises the identical `BottomSheet`/`FoodMap` mount path) to get the sheet open, then used `page.setViewportSize()` to grow/shrink the REAL viewport height — a genuine trigger of `index.css`'s real `100dvh` sizing (`html, body, #root { height: 100dvh }`, B168 — "so mobile browser chrome can't crop the bottom of the canvas"), which is exactly what Safari's own chrome collapsing/expanding does. Confirmed live: `#root`'s height genuinely changes; the map host's own `getBoundingClientRect().top` never moves (top-anchored, below the fixed-height `AppHeader`) while its height grows/shrinks — the real trigger, reproduced without needing real Safari.
- **ROOT CAUSE, traced into Leaflet's own source, not guessed.** `.leaflet-map-pane`'s CSS transform went from `matrix(1,0,0,1,0,0)` to `matrix(1,0,0,1,0,60)` after growing the viewport by 120px — Leaflet's own `invalidateSize()` (`leaflet-src.js`) pans the map by HALF the size delta (`oldCenter.subtract(newCenter)`) by DEFAULT, which assumes a resize is symmetric around the container's centre. This app's layout never is: a fixed-height `AppHeader` sits above a `flex:1, minHeight:0` map host, so the host's top-left edge is permanently anchored and only its BOTTOM edge ever moves. The half-delta pan shifts already-rendered tiles inside a container whose own top edge never moved — the pane's new top lands mid-container with nothing painted above it. That is the "clean horizontal line, grey on top" the owner described exactly: not a ragged tile edge (which a stale-size guess would produce), a precise, uniform offset (which a wrong PAN produces).
- **THE FIX, two parts, both needed — confirmed by testing each alone first.** (1) The B651872 (×4) ResizeObserver's own `invalidateSize({animate:false})` call gained `pan:false` — this app's layout is ALWAYS top-anchored, so the default symmetric compensation is never correct here. Tested alone: the grey band persisted. (2) `trackResize:false` at map construction — Leaflet's OWN default (`trackResize:true`) independently binds `window`'s `'resize'` event straight to `this.invalidateSize({debounceMoveend:true})`, with NO way to pass it `pan:false`. The ResizeObserver (which watches the real container, not just `window`, and is already fixed) fully supersedes what `trackResize` was for. Both together: `.leaflet-map-pane`'s transform stays `matrix(1,0,0,1,0,0)` through growth, shrink-back, AND a simulated rotation (width/height swap) — the tile container's real screen position tracks the map host's real position exactly, every time.
- **What was verified here — real Playwright `devices['iPhone 14 Pro']` context, real dev build, real `FoodMap`/`BottomSheet` components, not a synthetic harness** (`.scratch-repro/verify-grey-band-real.mjs`): before the fix, growing the viewport +120px left the pane transform at `translate(0,60px)`, tile-container's real top misaligned from the map host's real top by 60px. After: pane transform stays `matrix(1,0,0,1,0,0)` and tile-container top matches map-host top exactly, across growth (122→122), shrink-back (122→122), AND a rotation (107→107). Full suite green (299/299 in `foodModule.test.js`), lint clean, build green, no new console errors on a full interaction smoke pass (zoom, basemap toggle, pan).

### B707841 — Scale markers continuously during a zoom animation, not just at zoomend `[Food]` (feature) #food #ui #perf #testing  *(owner chat block, 2026-08-23, verbatim: "it seems like everything resizes as I zoom in or out... once the zoom is complete, when we could just resize stuff as it's going, assuming that doesn't bog stuff down too much." Minted **B707841 / V380065** from this branch's reserved block B707840–B707855 / V380064–V380079 against `origin/main` f0032e7. DEDUPE-FIRST — grepped Open/⏳ Verify/Done for `zoom animation`, `marker scaling`, `zoomanim`, `canvas renderer pop`: no prior item touched zoom-animation rendering behaviour. Net-new.)*
`[x]` **SHIPPED — pins hold their true constant on-screen size THROUGH a zoom animation instead of visibly ballooning then snapping at the end, with a measured, budgeted, two-tier graceful degrade.**
- Verify: live — LIVE-VERIFY class (zoom-/data-density-dependent rendering)
- **THE MECHANISM, traced into Leaflet's own source (`leaflet-src.js`'s `Map._animateZoom`/`Renderer._updateTransform`), not guessed.** An animated zoom (wheel, +/-, double-click, pinch) jumps the map's internal model to the FINAL zoom immediately — every pin's screen POSITION is already correct from frame zero. The visible transition is a pure CSS trick: Leaflet sets `transform: translate(...) scale(s)` on the canvas RENDERER'S OWN `<canvas>` element (not the shared map pane) and lets the browser's native `.leaflet-zoom-animated{transition: transform 0.25s ...}` interpolate `s` from the start/end ratio down to 1 over ~250ms. Pins are drawn at a CONSTANT pixel radius (never meant to scale with zoom), so for that whole window the ambient `scale(s)` stretches the already-correctly-drawn bitmap — every pin visibly balloons or shrinks in lockstep with the tiles — then SNAPS back to true size the instant the transition ends and Leaflet's own `_reset()` repaints at scale 1. That snap is the reported "pop."
- **THE FIX.** While `s(t) ≠ 1` — read directly from the canvas's own live `getComputedStyle().transform`, the REAL browser-interpolated value, so this never has to reimplement Leaflet's cubic-bezier easing curve — every marker's drawn radius is set to `trueRadius / s(t)` each animation frame (`CircleMarker.setRadius`, which Leaflet itself batches into ONE actual canvas repaint per frame via its own `_requestRedraw`/rAF coalescing), so the NET on-screen size after the ambient scale is applied stays the TRUE constant radius throughout. Positions are untouched — already correct, and the ambient transform is exactly what smoothly carries them, which was already working as intended; only the SIZE needed correcting. Restored to the true radius the instant the animation ends (`zoomend`, plus the loop's own natural exit on every path), so nothing is ever left scaled.
- **PERF BUDGET, measured against the REAL worst case — 2000 markers (PLACES_QUERY_CAP, `foodStore.js`; the owner's own "roughly 1,000" is in the neighbourhood, the real cap is larger), zoomed PAST `MIN_PIN_ZOOM` (a first pass measured from the map's DEFAULT zoom and got a false-good number — the reference snapshot draws NOTHING below that threshold, so that run was silently timing an empty loop; caught via a `setRadius` call-count proof before it was reported, see the code comment for the full trace).** `.scratch-repro/verify-zoom-scaling-perf.mjs`, real Playwright, real Chromium, the REAL `FoodMap` component with synthetic data (network to Supabase/CARTO is blocked from this sandbox): **median 1.1ms, p95 4.2ms, max 15.8ms, 2/98 sampled frames over the 8ms budget** — comfortably inside budget; before this item, ZERO per-frame JS ran during a Leaflet zoom animation at all (the pop was a pure CSS-transform artifact, not a perf cost), so this is the full added cost, not a regression delta.
- **TWO-TIER GRACEFUL DEGRADE, per gesture only (a fresh gesture always starts at full fidelity — conditions genuinely change, e.g. fewer markers once zoomed in past `MIN_PIN_ZOOM`).** `ZOOM_ANIM_DEGRADE_STREAK` (3) consecutive over-budget frames at full fidelity drops to redrawing every OTHER frame; the same streak still over budget at that tier BAILS entirely (restores true radii immediately, falls back to the old transform-then-settle look) rather than ever dropping frames. Stress-tested at 6x CPU throttle (`.scratch-repro/verify-zoom-scaling-degrade.mjs`, same 2000-marker worst case): individual frames reached 17-25ms, confirming real pressure — but only ~1.75 frames land per gesture at that throttle (Leaflet's own zoom-animation window is a fixed ~250ms regardless of device speed), too few for a 3-frame streak to complete within ONE gesture. Documented honestly rather than papered over: on a genuinely slow device a single heavy gesture may not fully degrade before it ends, but nothing runs away — the next gesture starts fresh, and `restoreTrueRadii()` always leaves every marker at its correct true radius regardless of which tier a gesture ended at.
- **THE DEGRADE DECISION IS A PURE, UNIT-TESTED FUNCTION** (`nextZoomAnimTier`, extracted to its own `lib/zoomAnimTier.js` — a live CPU-throttled proof alone can't fully exercise it, per the ~250ms gesture-window limit above), driven directly with scripted frame-time sequences in `test/foodModule.test.js`: stays at "full" while in budget (and a single in-budget frame resets the streak, so noise never creeps it toward "bailed"); "full"→"everyOther" only after exactly the full streak, never before; "everyOther"→"bailed" the same way; "bailed" is a hard floor for the rest of the gesture.
- **CROSS-FADING THE ZOOM-GATED DATA SWAP, checked and deliberately NOT done this session — said plainly, per the item's own instruction, rather than silently skipped.** The reference-snapshot pins popping in/out at `MIN_PIN_ZOOM` does NOT need a second query (the data is already fetched regardless of the `tooSmall` gate — it's a pure rendering-timing question, not a network one). What it DOES need is the same shape of custom rAF-driven redraw loop as the radius fix above, applied to a boolean state flip instead of Leaflet's own `'zoomanim'` hook — there is no equivalent Leaflet-native event to piggyback on for that trigger, so it would need its own tween state machine and its own separate perf-budget/measurement pass, genuinely feature-sized on its own. Left undone and flagged rather than half-built; a reasonable fast follow-up, not folded into this item to keep this session's already-large scope honest.
- **What was verified here.** Real Playwright, real Chromium, the real `FoodMap` component (`.scratch-repro/zoom-perf-harness.jsx`), a `setRadius`-call proof confirming the compensation actively fires (32,000 calls across one 16-frame gesture at the 2000-marker worst case, radii ranging 0.64–5.0 as the ambient scale swings up to ~8x and back, the LAST call settling exactly at the true base radius). A full interaction smoke pass (zoom, basemap toggle, pan) showed zero new console errors. Full suite green (307/307 in `foodModule.test.js`), lint clean, build green, bundle audit within ceiling.
- Guard: `test/foodModule.test.js` — the `nextZoomAnimTier` state-machine tests above, a source-scan confirming the effect wires `zoomanim`/`zoomend` to real Leaflet events with `restoreTrueRadii()` called on every exit path (natural loop exit, bail, `zoomend`, unmount cleanup — asserted ≥4 call sites), that compensation goes through Leaflet's own `setRadius` (never a hand-rolled canvas 2D reach-around), and that `readContainerScale` reads the live computed transform rather than reimplementing an easing curve.
- Sandbox: `npx vitest run` 307/307 green in `foodModule.test.js`, lint 0 errors, build green, bundle audit within ceiling.
- **Steps for the live check, each with a named expected result:**
  1. Cache-busted load at a zoom past the pin threshold with many pins on screen (a dense area, or a wide window at a city-scale zoom). Zoom in/out with the scroll wheel or the +/- buttons. **Expect:** pins hold a roughly constant visual size THROUGH the zoom motion — no visible balloon-then-snap.
  2. On the densest real area available (a downtown/midtown cluster), repeat the same zoom gesture several times in a row. **Expect:** no stutter or dropped frames; if the device is notably slow, the degrade may make individual gestures look closer to the old behaviour on a heavy gesture, but the app should never freeze or lag behind.
  3. Confirm the reference-snapshot pins (unlogged places) still pop in/out abruptly at the zoom threshold rather than fading — this is the known, deliberately-undone piece from above, not a regression to chase.
- **Result:** ⏳ pending — needs a live pass on the owner's own device/connection to confirm the perceived smoothness; the mechanism, the perf numbers, and the degrade path are all measured above.
- **Files:** `src/workspaces/food/components/FoodMap.jsx`, `src/workspaces/food/lib/zoomAnimTier.js` (new), `test/foodModule.test.js`.

### B668193 — Restaurant pins are too small to tap on mobile `[Food]` (bug) #food #ui #testing  *(owner report 2026-08-22, arrived as NEW-2, with live DOM measurement: canvas-rendered markers, zero `.leaflet-interactive`/`.leaflet-marker-icon` DOM nodes, so the tap target is exactly the drawn circle radius plus Leaflet's default zero canvas-renderer tolerance — ~10-12px against a ~44px finger. Minted **B668193 / V341841** from this branch's reserved block B668192–B668207 / V341840–V341855 against `origin/main` ff0c4d5. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open/⏳ Verify/Done for `food`, `tap target`, `touch`, `canvas renderer`, `tolerance`, `coarse pointer`: no prior item touched touch-target sizing anywhere in the food module. Net-new.)*
`[x]` **⏳ SHIPPED — a coarse-pointer-only nearest-centre tap resolver, widening the effective hit radius to a 44px-diameter floor without touching a single drawn pixel. Desktop/mouse is byte-identical. `Verify: live` → V341841.**
- Verify: live (no `Blocker:` — extensively verified headless with real Playwright touch/coarse-pointer emulation against the exact shipped algorithm, below; parked per house convention because a real finger on a real phone against the real Montrose cluster hasn't been checked)
- **WHY A TOLERANCE BUMP ALONE WAS REJECTED.** Leaflet's own canvas hit-test (`Canvas._onClick`) resolves overlapping candidates by DRAW ORDER — the topmost/last-added layer wins, never proximity — confirmed against a local repro of `_fireDOMEvent`'s `canvasTargets` filtering. Simply raising the renderer's `tolerance` option would make the WRONG pin win more often in a dense cluster, not less, which fails the report's own explicit requirement ("if two targets overlap, the nearest centre wins").
- **THE FIX.** On a coarse pointer (`matchMedia("(pointer: coarse)")`, reactive — mirrors `AppHeader.jsx`'s `useNarrow` pattern) — desktop mice are completely untouched, so precision there is byte-identical — circleMarkers skip their per-marker `click` listener (confirmed via a local repro that an `interactive:true` canvas layer with no listener attached does not consume the click; `map`'s own `click` event still fires normally) and instead get recorded into `pinIndexRef` with their real screen radius. ONE `map.on("click", …)` handler resolves the tap by picking whichever candidate's centre is CLOSEST to the tap point, among those within `Math.max(radius, TOUCH_MIN_TAP_RADIUS)` (22px, giving a 44px-diameter floor — the common minimum touch-target guideline). `TOUCH_MIN_TAP_RADIUS` only widens the invisible HIT area; the drawn circle's own radius is completely untouched, so the map's visual density at any zoom is unaffected ("must not turn to mush," satisfied by construction, not by tuning). The resolver stands down while "Drop a pin" mode is active, so a tap on an existing pin can't also drop a phantom manual pin at the same spot.
- **What was verified here (sandbox, real headless Chromium with Playwright's `hasTouch`/`isMobile` context emulation, driving the EXACT resolver algorithm mirrored from the shipped source):** 9 checks, all passed — desktop precision unchanged (a 15px-off click on a 7px pin still misses; dead-centre still hits); touch widens the hit radius correctly (an 18px-off tap on a 5px reference pin now hits, a 30px-off tap still misses — bounded, not infinite); genuine nearest-centre resolution in a dense 5-pin overlapping cluster (resolves to the geometrically closest candidate, not the last-drawn one, at two different tap points that shift which pin is nearest); pinMode gating confirmed. See V341841 for full detail.
- Guard: `test/foodModule.test.js` — 5 new tests covering the coarse/fine branch split, the reactive matchMedia wiring, the nearest-centre comparison logic (not "last match wins"), the hit-area-only widening (never feeding into the drawn `radius:`), and the pinMode stand-down.
- Sandbox: `npx vitest run` 12,037 green, lint 0 errors, build green, bundle audit clean.
- **Steps for the live check, each with a named expected result:**
  1. On a phone (or Chrome DevTools device emulation) at `planyr.io/#/food`, zoom into the Montrose/Museum District cluster in Houston (the honest dense-cluster test named in the report). **Expect:** you can reliably select a specific pin near where you tap, not a neighboring one.
  2. Tap slightly off a pin's visual centre, not dead-on. **Expect:** it still selects that pin.
  3. On desktop with a mouse, click precisely between two nearby pins. **Expect:** unchanged from before this item.
- **Files:** `src/workspaces/food/components/FoodMap.jsx`, `test/foodModule.test.js`.

### B851 (×2) — Schedule grid diverges from the route + a false "newer version — reload?" banner, same cause `[Scheduler / persistence]` (bug — data-loss hazard) #scheduler #persistence #ui  *(owner chat block 2026-08-22, minutes apart, verbatim: (1) "me hear it's doing its thing again where it shows the wrong site for the schedule" — breadcrumb "Dashboard / Goose Creek", grid showing Baytown/Chambers County tasks; (2) "And now it keeps saying that, like, a new site has new information or something and offers to reload." He has been told not to accept the reload. HIGH priority, live breakage with a data-loss hazard.)*
`[x]` **IMPLEMENTED — root-caused by a forced-ordering simulation (not assumed), mutation-proven, sandbox-verified. `Verify: live` → V326384.**
- Verify: live — V326384 (`Blocker: real-data` `Blocker: auth` — the race is timing-dependent on the owner's real ~338 KB `hs-v1` doc under his actual multi-project navigation pattern; it cannot be forced through the sandbox's egress-blocked signed-in Scheduler iframe)
- Recurrence: 2026-08-22 — same reported shape as B851's original report (route Goose Creek, grid showing another project's tasks) plus a new co-symptom (the false reload banner). Re-opens B851 per DEDUPE-FIRST rather than minting a new number.
- Origin: filed 2026-08-22 from chat (owner, two screenshots, minutes apart).
- **STEP 1 — what was actually on screen, measured from live `planyr_production` Supabase (read-only), not inferred from task names.** `sites`: `smqfy48tlk9j` = Goose Creek (confirms the crumb was correct). The current `hs-v1` doc has `aPid: 1` = "Goose Creek" (linked to `smqfy48tlk9j`) and `aPid: 2` = "Grand Port" (linked to `smqfy2r7pdec`) — i.e. it has since self-healed. The brief's own warning ("Goose Creek and Grand Port are both Baytown-jurisdiction, so Baytown task names prove nothing") held: "Baytown" tasks exist in BOTH pid 1 and pid 2, but **"Chambers County" tasks exist ONLY in pid 2 (Grand Port)** — so his screenshot is the exact SAME pair as the original report (route=Goose Creek, grid=Grand Port), confirmed by data, not by reading task names alone.
- **STEP 1b — the two suspects named in the brief, checked first, both REFUTED by measurement, not assumption.** (a) The no-op guard in the iframe's `planar:nav-select-by-site` handler (`public/sequence/index.html`, added by B560) is byte-identical to its original form — `git show` diffs of the three recent Scheduler-grid PRs (#1101 scroll-jump, #1103 indent/outdent, #1107 row move) touch zero lines anywhere in the nav bridge, the autosave effect, or `mergeCloudDoc`; grepped for every symbol in that region (`nav-select`, `attemptCloudSave`, `latestData.current`, `mergeCloudDoc`, `checkRemote`) across all three diffs — no match. (b) `carriedRef`'s "already carried" latch (B1342/NEW-2's reordering) does NOT leave the grid stuck: production `client_errors` (247 `module=scheduler` rows, going back weeks) contains **zero** `schedule-route-grid-divergence` events — the LOUD-FAILURE backstop B851 installed specifically to catch a non-converging re-drive has never once fired, meaning the carry-in always eventually reaches the right state in the iframe's own React tree. Neither suspect explains a PERSISTENT wrong grid with no telemetry trace.
- **STEP 2 — the real mechanism, found by forcing the load-time ordering the brief asked for, not by more static reading.** `Scheduler.jsx`'s carry-in effect has no `isActive` gate — by design (the "project-aware header tabs" cross-module payoff, B1342), it posts `planar:nav-select-by-site` into the always-kept-alive Scheduler iframe on EVERY app-wide routed-project change, even while the Schedule tab isn't visible. Browsing a few Site Planner projects before landing on Schedule can therefore put two or more REAL, distinct saves to `hs-v1` in flight at once (`attemptCloudSave`, `public/sequence/index.html:5825`, fires un-debounced on every `data` change — confirmed the `saveSeq` ref only gates the UI's "saving/saved" label, never the underlying `window.storage.set()` calls, which have no serialization at all). `window.storage.set()`'s optimistic-concurrency guard (`cloudRev > knownRev[k]`) is a plain client-side read-then-write check with no server-side compare-and-swap. **Simulated the exact real Layer-0 guard + the real `mergeCloudDoc` (the verbatim mirror already in `ui-audit/stress/scheduler-engine.mjs`, confirmed byte-identical to the live source) through three realistic network-timing interleavings of two overlapping same-tab saves (one stale/transient target, one the final correct one): 2 of 3 forced orderings silently persist the STALE `aPid` with `blocked: false` — no conflict ever detected, because the rev sequence still looks monotonic to the guard even though the writes landed out of order.** This is report (1), reproduced, not assumed. The remaining interleavings are the ones B851 itself already diagnosed as the false-banner mechanism ("the optimistic-save guard tripped against the tab's own in-flight write") — same missing-serialization gap, report (2)'s cause.
- **ONE bug, not two — and NOT a regression.** B851's original fix (killing REDUNDANT reposts of an already-active schedule) correctly closed its own narrower symptom and still works exactly as designed — the recurrence is a DIFFERENT slice of the same pre-existing gap in `window.storage.set()` (present since B560/B864, unrelated to any Scheduler-grid work) that fix never covered: overlapping saves to genuinely DIFFERENT targets (from browsing multiple projects), not duplicate reposts of the same one. So: **this is "never covered this path," not "the fix regressed."**
- **Fix (`public/sequence/index.html`):** `window.storage.set()`'s original body is renamed `_rawSet`; a new `set()` wrapper serializes writes per key — at most one `_rawSet` call is ever in flight for `"hs-v1"`. Two adjacent, not-yet-started AUTO saves (the fungible "here is the current `data`" saves `attemptCloudSave` issues) coalesce into one, sending only the latest payload; an EXPLICIT checkpoint save (`skipSanity: true` — pre-delete/pre-import/pre-restore/pre-recascade) always keeps its own slot in line and is never coalesced away or coalesced past. This closes the race at its root for every caller (task edits, retries, restores, and the carry-in) without touching the carry-in/nav logic at all — that logic was never wrong; the storage layer underneath it never guaranteed saves wouldn't overlap.
- **USER-FACING HAZARD, answered directly.** Accepting "Reload" while `saveStatus !== "saved"` DOES discard genuinely-unsaved in-memory edits (`window.location.reload()` has no pre-reload save) — the banner's own copy already half-admits this ("reloading replaces them with the other device's version"), though its claim that "your copy is kept in Version History either way" only holds for edits that had ALREADY been saved at least once, not for edits made since the last successful save. **This fix closes the hazard for the mechanism actually causing his repeated false prompts** (same-tab overlapping saves spuriously tripping the conflict guard) — with saves serialized, that spurious trip can no longer happen, so the banner stops appearing falsely and there is nothing false to accidentally accept. It does **not** change the Reload button's own behavior for a genuine cross-device conflict (a real second writer) — that path, and its pre-existing "kept in Version History either way" copy, are unchanged and out of this bug's scope.
- **Guards, mutation-proven both directions.** `test/schedulerSaveQueue.test.js` (new, 8 tests) — extracts the real queue wrapper from the shipped `index.html` (same live-extraction pattern as `test/ganttLabelAbove.test.js`, so it can never drift) and: (a) proves coalescing/ordering/isolation/error-propagation properties in isolation; (b) drives the SAME three forced interleavings through the real Layer-0/`mergeCloudDoc` logic twice — once calling `_rawSet` directly (asserts at least one interleaving clobbers the correct value — the reproduction) and once through the real extracted `set()` wrapper (asserts all three converge to the correct value — the fix). A check that can't fail on the unfixed code proves nothing; this one does, on real extracted source.
- Sandbox: `npx vitest run` 12,020 green (582 files), lint 0 errors (24 pre-existing warnings, untouched), `npm run build` green, `node ui-audit/stress/check-babel.mjs` (the Scheduler syntax guard) OK on both script blocks. No `ui-audit/verify-*.mjs` exists for this path and none is claimed as CI-enforced — this is sandbox-provable only; `npm test` is the enforced gate.
- **Steps for the live check, each with a named expected result:**
  1. Signed in, browse several Site Planner projects in quick succession, then open Schedule on one of them. **Expect:** the grid matches the routed project every time, with no visible flash of a different project's tasks lasting more than the ordinary ~1s load window.
  2. Repeat step 1 several times over a normal working session (the race is timing-dependent, not guaranteed every attempt). **Expect:** the false "a newer version was saved on another device" banner does not appear from this pattern; if it ever does, note whether it was genuinely a second device/tab (real conflict, not this bug) or not.
  3. If a divergence is ever seen again, check `client_errors` for `schedule-route-grid-divergence` (the LOUD-FAILURE backstop, unchanged by this fix) — its continued silence would say the re-drive itself is still converging and the recurrence, if any, is a new cause, not this one.
- **Files:** `public/sequence/index.html`, `test/schedulerSaveQueue.test.js` (new).

### B616673 — A teammate can see only one plan of a shared project though the database returns all of them `[Site Planner / sharing]` (bug) #site-planner #auth #sync #persistence  *(owner chat block 2026-08-17, arrived as NEW-1, with evidence already gathered: a rolled-back-transaction SELECT run as the non-owner teammate's real role + JWT confirmed the database correctly returns all 5 rows of the "Goose Creek" project (`group_id smqfy48tlk9j`) to him. Minted **B616673 / V314401** from this branch's reserved block, against `origin/main` 19f9643. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open + ⏳ Verify + Done across `plan switcher`, `plansHere`, `plansOfGroup`, `groupId`, `mergePulledSites`, `cloudList`, `B385042`, `B487601`, `B371361`, `B366384`, `B326416`–`B326419`: **B385042** fixed the switcher stating the CURRENT plan's name three times (over-counting a label, not dropping rows); **B371361** is the jurisdiction pill covering the switcher (a layout defect, not a data one); **B366384** is a different share-menu mislabel. None of them is "a shared row silently vanishes from the merge." Net-new.)*
`[x]` **⏳ SHIPPED — a real class of bug found, reproduced in a real browser, and fixed at the read boundary, with defense-in-depth instrumentation. Root cause NOT confirmed as the historical cause of Bryndan's specific report — see the honest caveat below. `Verify: live` → V314401.**
- Verify: live — V314401 (`Blocker: auth` `Blocker: real-data` — needs a real non-owner teammate's account on a real multi-plan shared project; the sandbox cannot sign in as one)
- **THE PIPELINE WAS AUDITED FIRST, EXHAUSTIVELY, AND FOUND CLEAN — stated so the next reader doesn't re-walk it.** Every pure function between a cloud fetch and the rendered switcher (`cloudList`, `mergePulledSites`, `loadSitesList`, `loadPlansOfGroup`, `plansHere`'s own filter, `reconcileGroupNames`, the map's `siteGroups` collapse — which is a *different*, correctly-designed one-pin-per-project list, not the plan switcher) was unit-tested against data shaped exactly like the real Goose Creek rows and returned all 5, correctly. A whole-`src/` grep for any `.filter(...ownerId...)`/`.filter(...user_id...)` "only mine" array filter came back empty. No service worker or client-side response cache exists in this repo.
- **THE DEFECT, found by driving the REAL APP in a REAL BROWSER as a fake signed-in non-owner teammate** (`e2e/new1-team-plan-count.spec.js`, `page.route()` intercepts every request to the configured Supabase origin and a `localStorage`-seeded session stands in for real sign-in — the sandbox's proxy CORS-blocks real Supabase auth, so this is how a signed-in path gets driven here at all): `cloudList()` (`cloudSync.js`) never selected a `sites` row's real PostgREST primary key (`id`) — only `data, version, team_id, user_id, share_locked` — and trusted the `id` embedded in the row's own jsonb `data` unconditionally. `mergePulledSites()` (`storage.js`) keys its **entire** merge map by that same jsonb id (`map[n.id] = ...`). Two *different* physical rows (real, distinct primary keys — Postgres enforces that) whose jsonb payloads happened to carry the *same* `data.id` would silently collapse to ONE surviving plan, with zero error anywhere — exactly the reported shape: not zero plans, not a random count, **one specific plan missing**. Reproduced live: the switcher showed 4 of 5 ("Concept B" gone, no trace) on the pre-fix build; git-stashing the fix and re-running confirmed it independently.
- **THE FIX, at the read boundary, same pattern B714 already uses.** `cloudList()` now selects `id` alongside `data` at every migration-fallback tier and corrects a drifted jsonb id to the row's real primary key *before* anything downstream sees it, reporting the correction loudly (`reportClientEvent("cloud-id-mismatch", …)`).
- **PLUS TWO DEFENSE-IN-DEPTH INSTRUMENTS (DANGEROUS-MEANS-UNOBSERVABLE) — belt-and-suspenders even though the primary fix already closes the reproduced path**, because a symptom this specific deserves a way to diagnose ITSELF if it is ever seen again, from any cause: `idCollisions` (`mergePulledSites` — two cloud rows sharing one id within a single pull) and `groupCountDivergence()` (new pure export — a project's plan count shrinking between what `cloudList()` fetched and what survived the merge, excluding a legitimate server-side soft-delete). Both are reported loudly from `pullCloud()` (`cloud-id-collision` / `cloud-group-count-diverged`, naming the exact ids/group), so a recurrence is a telemetry query, never a re-investigation.
- **⛔ THE HONEST CAVEAT (STANDING RULE #2 — a null does not close an owner-reported symptom, and this is the corresponding discipline in the other direction: a fix must not overclaim what it proved).** Re-querying the real Goose Creek rows AFTER building this fix (`select id as row_pk, data->>'id' as json_id, id = data->>'id' as matches from sites where group_id = 'smqfy48tlk9j'`) found **all 5 rows match — no drift present today.** So the SPECIFIC anomaly this fix corrects is a real, reproducible class of bug that produces exactly Bryndan's reported shape, and it is now closed and instrumented — but it is **not confirmed** to be the historical cause of his specific report (a stale prior state that self-healed on a later ordinary write is one plausible explanation; an as-yet-unfound second cause is another). This is disposition **(2) "instrument it so it captures itself when he hits it"** from STANDING RULE #2's three admissible dispositions — not disposition (1) "reproduce and fix the reported instance," which was not achieved against the current production row.
- Guards, all mutation-proven (git-stashed the source fix, confirmed red, restored, confirmed green): `test/cloudListIdIntegrity.test.js` (new, 4 tests — including the 5-distinct-real-PKs-with-one-colliding-jsonb-id repro), `test/storage.test.js` (+11 tests for `idCollisions`/`groupCountDivergence`), `e2e/new1-team-plan-count.spec.js` (new, 2 tests — Scenario A: 5 clean ids, must show 5; Scenario B: the collision, must still show 5 — independently re-run and reproduced red pre-fix / green post-fix in this session, not just accepted from the implementing pass).
- Sandbox: `npx vitest run` 11,847 green, lint 0 new errors, build green, `node ui-audit/perf-bundle-audit.mjs` — all budgets within ceiling (5 metrics sit inside their existing headroom band, none newly breached; the 4 pre-existing B329408 breaches are untouched and no ceiling was raised).
- **Steps for the live check, each with a named expected result:**
  1. Sign in as a real non-owner team member on a real multi-plan shared project (Bryndan on Goose Creek, or any equivalent). **Expect:** the Plan ▾ switcher lists every plan the project actually has, matching what the owner sees.
  2. If it does NOT — check `client_errors` for a `cloud-id-mismatch`, `cloud-id-collision`, or `cloud-group-count-diverged` event around that pull. **Expect:** one of them names the exact row/group at fault, turning any recurrence into a five-minute diagnosis instead of a re-investigation.
  3. If (1) passes cleanly, this closes as: not currently reproducing on real data, with the new instrumentation standing guard — per STANDING RULE #2, this is a legitimate close on disposition (2), not a null.
- **Files:** `src/workspaces/site-planner/lib/cloudSync.js`, `src/workspaces/site-planner/lib/storage.js`, `test/storage.test.js`, `test/cloudListIdIntegrity.test.js` (new), `e2e/new1-team-plan-count.spec.js` (new), `MAP.md` (regenerated for the new `groupCountDivergence` export).

### B576000 — planyr.io/food (no hash) 404s — the clean path he actually types `[Food]` (bug) #food #infra #testing  *(owner report 2026-08-17, confirmed live on his own browser, verbatim: "planyr.io/food -> Planyr's own 'That page isn't here' screen, planyr.io/#/food -> loads and works... His original words, from the very first brief: 'if I just make it up planner i o slash food, I feel like it won't actually mess anything up.' He types planyr.io/food. That is the entrance." Filed as NEW-3. Minted **B576000 / V306880** LATE via `git fetch origin main && npm run next-id -- --against-main`, from this branch's reserved block B576000–B576015 / V306880–V306895 against `origin/main` f6d66fa (the just-merged B575952). DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open/⏳ Verify/Done for `food`, `_redirects`, `hash rout`, `catch-all`, `B449`: B449 is the reason there is NO blanket catch-all (still respected below, not reverted); nothing prior added a clean-path entrance for any workspace slug. Net-new.)*
`[x]` **⏳ SHIPPED — Cloudflare now 302-redirects every known top-level slug (incl. /food) straight to its hash route, before the app's JS is ever requested. `Verify: live` → V306880.**
- Verify: live — **V306880** (`Blocker: live-deploy` — `public/_redirects` is Cloudflare Pages routing config; a local `vite preview` server does not process it at all, so the redirect chain itself can only be proven on the real deployed edge, not in this sandbox)
- **⛔ AUDIT-FIRST CAUGHT A WRONG DIAGNOSIS BEFORE ANY CODE WAS WRITTEN — flagged here rather than silently overridden.** The brief's own stated diagnosis (marked "already done for you, do not re-derive") was that this is a hash-router problem fixable entirely in-app: "index.html IS being served at /food... this is fixable in the app and needs no Cloudflare change." **That is not what's happening.** Reading `public/404.html` (the exact "That page isn't here" text the owner described, character for character) and `public/_redirects` (deliberately NO `/* /index.html 200` catch-all, per B449 — a stale content-hashed chunk must 404 cleanly, not silently serve HTML) proved Cloudflare answers `/food` with `404.html`, a small standalone static file with **none of the app's JavaScript**. The React app, `main.jsx`, `route.js` — nothing boots at that path today. An in-app boot-time shim cannot run in a request where the app's JS is never requested, so the prescribed fix was inert by construction. Root cause and fix both moved from "app code" to "the one place that actually sees the request before the app does": `public/_redirects`.
- **THE FIX, general per instruction, not food-special-cased.** `public/_redirects` gets one real HTTP **302** redirect per known top-level slug (`site`, `schedule`, `markup`, `library`, `notes`, `food` — every value in `route.js`'s `SLUG_BY_MODULE`, not just food), bare and trailing-slash forms both (Cloudflare's redirect matching is exact-path, not prefix — `/food` does not also match `/food/`), each straight to `/#/<slug>`. **A real redirect, never a `200` rewrite** — a 200 would serve the app at the bare path with the hash still unset, leaving the router with nothing to match. `/assets/* -> /404.html 404` is untouched, one line above the new block, so a stale chunk still 404s cleanly exactly as B449 requires — the new rules are the narrow, named exception the no-catch-all comment already anticipated, not a reversal of it.
- **ADDRESS BAR: settles on the hash form, deliberately.** A 302 (not a silent rewrite) means the browser's own address bar updates to `planyr.io/#/food` after the redirect — that's the URL the owner ends up looking at, and it's the one form that was already proven to reload correctly (nothing about `route.js`/`main.jsx` changed). Typing the clean path is still the entrance he asked for; the bar settling on the hash form is the one line item the brief asked to "decide and state" — chosen because it needs zero app-code changes and cannot regress `INITIAL_HASH_EMPTY`'s module-load-time capture in `route.js`.
- **ZERO APP-CODE CHANGES, and here's why that's not a shortcut.** By the time a 302 lands the browser at `/#/food`, `location.hash` is already the deep link — `route.js`'s `INITIAL_HASH_EMPTY` capture and `index.html`'s inline landing-page-redirect script (which already exempts `h && h !== "#"`) both do the right thing with no line changed. Neither `main.jsx` nor `route.js` was touched.
- **GUARD TEST, exactly as asked ("that test would have caught this before merge").** `test/foodModule.test.js`'s new "clean-path entrances" suite (22 tests) parses `public/_redirects` and asserts, for **every** slug in `SLUG_BY_MODULE` (not just food): a bare-path rule and a trailing-slash rule both exist, both target `/#/<slug>`, both carry a 3xx status; a round-trip check that `parseRoute("#/<slug>")` resolves back to the right module; that no slug is missing a rule and no stray rule names an unknown slug; and that `/assets/* -> /404.html 404` is untouched. A future workspace added to `route.js` without a matching `_redirects` line now fails the build instead of silently 404ing exactly as `/food` did.
- **BYTES: proven identical, not assumed.** This change touches `public/_redirects` (a static file Cloudflare reads directly — never part of the JS bundle) and a test file (never part of the production build) — no `src/` file changed. Built twice, once with these changes stashed and once with them applied: `FoodApp-SFmuNkFG.js`, `SitePlannerApp-BKaKJ3LI.js`, and `Notes-DE5TTmGz.js` came out with the **identical content hash both times** — byte-for-byte proof, not inference, that `siteRouteJsBytes`/`notesRouteJsBytes`/`foodRouteJsBytes` are unchanged from the B575952 post-removal baseline.
- **What was verified here (sandbox):** `npx vitest run` 11,786 green (65/65 in `test/foodModule.test.js`, up from 43 — the 22 new clean-path tests), lint 0 new errors (24 pre-existing warnings, none touching these files), build green.
- **⛔ AND, MID-SESSION, THE ACTUAL REDIRECT RULE ITSELF — LIVE, ON CLOUDFLARE'S REAL EDGE, NOT JUST THE FILE.** `vite preview` can't see `_redirects` at all, but once PR #1079's Cloudflare Pages **preview deploy** finished (`claude-food-place-tracker-rg.planyr.pages.dev`, this exact commit), a headless browser hit the same TLS-tunnel wall this file already documents for `*.supabase.co`/`hazards.fema.gov` — but a raw `curl` got through, straight to Cloudflare's edge: `GET /food -> HTTP/2 302, location: /#/food`; `GET /food/` → same; `GET /notes -> HTTP/2 302, location: /#/notes` (proving the general fix, not just food); `GET /assets/DefinitelyStale-<fake>.js -> HTTP/2 404` (B449 still intact). That is the redirect RULE proven live, not inferred from reading the file — see V306880 for the full response headers. Still open: whether the browser shows any visible flash before the redirect lands (a 302 is the very first byte back, before any page content, so there is nothing to flash — read off HTTP semantics, not watched in a browser) and whether `planyr.io` itself (vs. the PR preview) behaves identically once merged.
