### B576001 — Food pins look geographically lopsided at metro-wide zoom `[Food]` (bug) #food #gis #testing  *(owner report 2026-08-17, verbatim: "the loaded places look LOPSIDED. At a metro-wide view the pins are dense around Bellaire / Sharpstown / south-west Houston and thin-to-absent across Downtown, the Heights, Montrose, Katy, Baytown and the north side... Report the actual row count and its bounding box before changing anything — do not reload the dataset on a hunch." Filed alongside NEW-3 as a lower-priority, investigate-and-report-only item, then re-opened as NEW-4 once he chose the fix approach ("VIEWPORT-AWARE, not a bigger number and not an even global sample... Raising the limit alone just moves the cliff; an even global sample makes every zoom level wrong in a new way"). Minted **B576001 / V306881** from this branch's reserved block B576000–B576015 / V306880–V306895 against `origin/main` f6d66fa. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open/⏳ Verify/Done for `food`, `lopsided`, `fetchPlacesInBounds`, `LIMIT`: no prior item; B568400 loaded and reported the full dataset but never queried it at metro-wide zoom. Net-new.)*
`[x]` **⏳ SHIPPED (2nd generation) — the per-cell cap is now PROPORTIONAL to each cell's own true count, not a flat 1/64th share; the first generation's flat cap was ITSELF a biased slice. `Verify: live` → V306881.**
- Verify: live — **V306881** (`Blocker: real-data` — proven against the real production table below; needs a live pass over his actual signed-in map to confirm the visual spread and the capped notice render correctly)
- **⛔ THE FIRST FIX WAS INCOMPLETE, AND HE CAUGHT IT.** Generation 1 (below, for the record) partitioned the viewport into an 8×8 grid and gave every cell the SAME fixed cap (`p_cap / 64`). That fixed the ORIGINAL bug (a scan-order prefix bunched in one corner) but introduced a NEW, subtler one: **giving every cell an equal absolute count, regardless of how many places actually live there, systematically under-represents dense areas and over-represents sparse ones.** Measured on a real production viewport (a ~12mi box, 8,903 total matching places across a 4×4 analysis grid): the densest cell (1,959 real places) returned only **124 rows — 6.3% of its content**; the sparsest cell (114 real places) returned **100 rows — 87.7% of its content**. A >13x disparity in coverage fraction, cell to cell. That is a biased slice by any reasonable definition, and it is very likely what read as "focusing on the middle" — whichever part of his screen happened to be denser was proportionally the most under-filled.
- **THE FIX — weight each cell's share of the cap by its OWN true count** (`ceil(p_cap * cell_count / total_matched)`, both cheap window functions on the same scan). Re-measured on the identical viewport: coverage fraction flattened to a **near-constant ~22.6%–24.0% across 14 of 16 analysis cells** (the remaining two, at the extreme edge of the RPC's own grid, sit at 17.1% and 9.6% — a `width_bucket` edge-overflow artifact affecting only the very outermost sliver, not a "middle" bias). This is a genuinely representative sample now, not a shape that favors wherever a cell happens to be dense or centrally located.
- **⛔ AND THE MODEL ITSELF CHANGED — read the redesign entry below.** This query is now used ONLY once zoomed in past the threshold; below it, the reference snapshot doesn't draw at all (his own logged/rated places are the zoomed-out content instead, always visible, never sampled). So this fix matters for the "zoomed into a neighbourhood" case specifically, which is exactly where he observed it.
- **What was verified here (sandbox):** the fix proven directly against production Supabase (before/after quadrant measurement above, via `execute_sql`/`apply_migration`); `npx vitest run` 11,872 green (source guard confirming the proportional weighting formula is present and the OLD flat-cap formula is gone); lint 0 new errors; build green; bundle audit clean (see the redesign item for the shared bundle numbers).
- **Files:** `src/workspaces/food/db/food.sql` (RPC body, 2nd generation), `test/foodModule.test.js`.
- **Steps for the live check, each with a named expected result:**
  1. On planyr.io, signed in, zoom into any neighbourhood-scale view with a real mix of dense and sparse areas. **Expect:** pin density visually tracks real restaurant density everywhere in the viewport — a busy commercial strip shows visibly more pins than a quiet residential block a short distance away, not a suspiciously uniform count everywhere.
  2. If the viewport genuinely has more places than the cap. **Expect:** a small pill reading "Showing N of M here — zoom in for more."
- *(Generation 1, superseded but kept for the record: partitioned the viewport into an 8×8 grid, an even absolute share per cell, `total_matched` reported for the capped-notice pill. Fixed the original scan-order-prefix bug; caused the disparity above.)*
- **⛔ ADDENDUM, 2026-08-18/19 — re-checked at the zoom where the reference snapshot actually draws now (see B623728's `MIN_PIN_ZOOM` correction, above), per a colleague's live-check instruction to "verify it at the FIRST zoom where they DO draw."** The z12 "bottom-heavy" look the colleague also flagged is real HOUSTON DENSITY, not this RPC failing: raw `food_places` counts for Sharpstown (713) and Spring Branch (710) — one reported "dense", the other "nearly empty" — are nearly identical, and the RPC's own output over a box containing both preserved that ratio almost exactly (71 vs 65 rows). At the corrected z15 threshold this proportional-share logic doesn't even need to be fair, because it never engages: six real Houston locations checked directly against production (downtown/midtown 1,251, Sharpstown 574, Heights 483, Galleria 265, Spring Branch 197, Kashmere Gardens 58) are all under the 2,000-row cap, so every one of those views returns its full, uncapped, unsampled content. No code change to this RPC was needed as a result of this addendum — recorded here so the "still bottom-heavy" question isn't left open.

`[x]` **⏳ SHIPPED (2nd generation) — colourful key-less basemap and ZERO clustering are confirmed correct; the "only his own places at low zoom" threshold was still wrong and is now corrected. `Verify: live` → V314448.**
- Verify: live — **V314448** (`Blocker: real-data`/environment — see below; two of the four claims below are now confirmed by a colleague's OWN live check of the owner's real screen, not by this session reading its own code)
- **⛔ RECURRENCE, 2026-08-18/19 — CAUGHT BY A LIVE CHECK, NOT BY RE-READING THE CODE, exactly the standard the owner now requires.** The owner had a colleague load `planyr.io/#/food` on his real screen and report back precisely (pin count, banner text, zoom level) rather than accept another code-based summary — this is because three prior summaries from this branch had already been contradicted by his own screen. The colleague's report, verbatim in substance: **basemap colour and the 1-10 rating scale are correct — confirmed** live; but **"the threshold is two zoom levels too far out"** — at Leaflet zoom 12, the whole-metro view (Katy to Baytown, the exact view the owner screenshotted and rejected twice), the map still drew **1,000 unrated reference pins** with a "Showing 1,000 of 9,697 here" pill; the "only his own places" rule only engaged at zoom 10. Root cause, confirmed by re-reading this file's own generation-1 note: `MIN_PIN_ZOOM` shipped at **12** — identical to `DEFAULT_ZOOM` — so the rule that was supposed to keep the reference snapshot off the default whole-metro view never actually fired at that view. The colleague also flagged the bottom-heavy distribution as still visible at z12 and asked it be re-checked at whatever zoom the rule newly engages at, and asked that the unrated-pin style not read as "a flat grey blob" now that ratings give the map its only other colour.
- **THE FIX — `MIN_PIN_ZOOM` raised from 12 to 15, chosen by measurement, not by nudging a constant.** Three independent lines of evidence, all computed directly rather than guessed (full derivation in the code comment, `FoodMap.jsx`): **(a) ground scale is zoom-intrinsic** — at z12 one screen pixel covers ~33m at Houston's latitude, at z15 ~4m, the first zoom where a city block reads as more than a few pixels; **(b) miles-across a 1440px window** — z12 ≈29.7mi (the whole metro), z14 ≈7.4mi (several stitched-together neighbourhoods), z15 ≈3.7mi (one named neighbourhood, e.g. the Heights or Montrose); **(c) the decisive practical test, run directly against production** — at z15, even downtown/midtown (the single densest `food_places` cluster in the entire metro) returns only **1,251** places, under the reference-snapshot RPC's 2,000-row cap; at z14 the identical box already returns **2,641**, over the cap. So z15 is the tightest zoom at which the reference snapshot is unconditionally complete everywhere tested in the metro — nothing is ever sampled, so the proportional-share fairness question (B576001, below) becomes moot at the zoom people will actually reach it.
- **THE DISTRIBUTION CONCERN — measured, not assumed, and it is real density, not an algorithm bug.** Raw `food_places` counts for the areas the colleague named: Sharpstown 713, Spring Branch 710, Heights 498, Bellaire 161, Independence Heights 127, Kashmere Gardens 56. Spring Branch (reported "nearly empty") is in fact nearly as dense as Sharpstown (reported "dense") — 710 vs 713. Running the actual production RPC over a wide box containing both returned 71 rows in Sharpstown's footprint vs 65 in Spring Branch's — proportional to their true 713:710 ratio. The sparse areas really are sparse in the underlying data; this is not the proportional-cap algorithm failing. And at the corrected z15 threshold this is moot regardless: six real Houston locations checked directly against production (downtown/midtown 1,251, Sharpstown 574, Heights 483, Galleria 265, Spring Branch 197, Kashmere Gardens 58) all sit under the 2,000-row cap, so nothing is sampled at all at z15 anywhere tested — a distribution question about a sampling algorithm that never engages.
- **THE UNRATED-PIN STYLE.** Reference/unlogged pins now render smaller and more transparent (`radius: 5, fillOpacity: 0.7`) than the owner's own places (`radius: 7, fillOpacity: 0.95`, unchanged) — a deliberately quieter background layer rather than a uniform grey mass, and it never competes with his own coloured/rated places for attention.
- **WHAT THIS SESSION COULD AND COULD NOT OBSERVE, stated plainly per the new standard.** This sandbox's egress proxy returns a confirmed policy denial (403 on the CONNECT, logged by the proxy itself, not a timeout) for both `basemaps.cartocdn.com` (the map tiles) and `*.supabase.co` (the data) — re-confirmed this session via the proxy's own `/__agentproxy/status` log immediately before writing this entry. `planyr.io`'s shell itself does load (HTTP 200), but a headless Chromium load of `#/food` cannot render tiles or fetch places, so no rendered screenshot of the corrected threshold was possible from here. What COULD be done, and was: the exact zoom-to-count relationship was reconstructed directly against the real production database (the numbers above), which tells you precisely what the app's own query would return at each zoom — but that is a database measurement standing in for a screen, not a screen. The two behaviours the colleague verified as CORRECT (rating scale, basemap colour) are taken as confirmed on his authority, not re-verified here.
- **⛔ OWNER REJECTED THE WHOLE MODEL, NOT THE TUNING (2026-08-18) — read this before re-adding either half of what was removed.** The first ship ran clustering (grey numbered bubbles) plus a flat basemap over the FULL 34,000-place reference snapshot, even zoomed out. His words, verbatim: *"i dont think the idea is to show all the places at this zoom level, i also dont want to lump things together, the better thing would be to show places that we have rated at a more zoomed out level"* — followed by *"i want some color on the map, its too grey"* on the muted basemap specifically. Both halves of the first ship were wrong, not just imperfectly tuned.
- **CLUSTERING — REMOVED ENTIRELY.** `lib/markerCluster.js` is deleted; `FoodMap.jsx` draws one pin per point, at every zoom, no exceptions. There is no grouping mechanism left in the file to misconfigure.
- **THE ZOOMED-OUT MODEL — his places are the content, the 34,000-place table is a lookup, not something to sample.** Below `MIN_PIN_ZOOM` the reference snapshot (`places`, from Overture) does not draw at all — not sampled, not thinned, simply absent. What DOES draw, at every zoom with no threshold: every place he's logged (`loggedPlaces`, resolved from `placeNames` — already fetched independent of the current viewport, since the visit list needed it anyway) and every manual pin. **Honest consequence, not smoothed over:** with ~0 logged visits today, the metro view is nearly empty. The zoomed-out pill now reads "Zoom in to browse restaurants near you" (or, once he has logged somewhere, "Showing only places you've been — zoom in to browse everywhere else") — intentional-browsing copy, not a "why is this broken" dead end. Zoomed in past the threshold, the reference snapshot draws exactly as before (see B576001 ×2 above for the query-fairness fix that governs it there).
- **BASEMAP — CARTO Voyager, not Positron; checked the Site Planner's registry again first, same answer as before.** The first ship's Positron ("light_all") delivered "muted" so thoroughly it read as a flat grey wash — water, parks and built-up land all nearly one tone, nothing to orient by. `basemaps.cartocdn.com/rastertiles/voyager` is the SAME free, key-less CARTO service, same terms (https://carto.com/basemaps), same domain — just a different `style` parameter, confirmed against CARTO's own published URL scheme (`github.com/CartoDB/basemap-styles`) rather than guessed: real cartographic colour (green parks, blue water, warm building fill) with roads/labels still quiet. Esri/USGS (the Site Planner's own free sources) were re-checked and are still the wrong content type — aerial photography has no "muted" setting, it would reintroduce "too busy" in a different shape.
- **PINS — coloured by rating, not decoration.** `lib/ratingColor.js` is a 10-step warm ramp (cream → deep red-brown); a rated place/pin uses `colorForRating(avgRating)` (the mean of that place's rated visits), falling back to the flat logged/manual colour when visited-but-unrated. **Deliberately single-hue, never red/green** (this repo's own KEY DECISIONS already bans that confusion pair elsewhere) — verified by asserting the green channel never dominates red in any step. **Relative luminance falls STRICTLY step 1→10 (0.89→0.04, WCAG formula, computed not eyeballed)**, so the ramp still reads light-to-dark in grayscale or on a washed-out phone screen. Step 8 (`#BE3B22`) lands exactly on the module's own existing `--accent-food` token. Every step's paired label colour clears AA (≥4.5:1, the small-bold-text bar) — step 7 was nudged from a linear interpolation's `#D74A2A` (4.28:1, short of AA against either black or white) to `#CC4526` (4.72:1) specifically to close that gap.
- **RATING SCALE — 1-10, not 1-5** (see B623776 below for the full change; the map/ramp side is summarized here since it's the same redesign).
- **What was verified here (sandbox, 1st generation):** `npx vitest run` 11,872 green — new describe blocks for the redesigned zoomed-out gating (source-verified: his places drawn outside the `!tooSmall` gate, the snapshot/live-search inside it), the colour-fallback wiring, the empty-state copy, and a full `ratingColor.js` unit suite (10 steps, no green, monotonic luminance computed via the real WCAG formula, every step's AA contrast computed and asserted, brand-token match, clamping/rounding/null-handling); a positive assertion that `lib/markerCluster.js` no longer exists and nothing imports it; lint 0 new errors; build green; bundle audit clean (`foodRouteJsBytes` +3.2 KB inside its headroom band — see B623776 for the shared `bundle.totalJsBytes` note, which is ambient drift unrelated to this item). Headless Chromium against the built app: tile requests captured live and confirmed to hit `rastertiles/voyager` (never `light_all`, never the old raw-OSM host); zero `.food-cluster-count` elements exist anywhere, before or after a zoom sweep; the zoomed-out pill renders the new copy; no console error through a full zoom-out-then-back-in sweep.

Against production directly: z10-z15 whole-metro counts (31,439 / 24,344 / 13,011 / 5,991 / 2,641 / 1,251) computed for a realistic 1440×740 viewport; the neighbourhood density counts and the RPC-output comparison cited above; the downtown/midtown z14-vs-z15 cap-safety comparison that decided the threshold. **Not done here, and said so rather than assumed:** an actual rendered screenshot of `#/food` at any zoom — this sandbox's network policy blocks both hosts the map needs (see below).

- **SCHEMA — `numeric(3,1)`, not an integer half-point count.** Chose the representation that keeps the column self-explanatory: the stored value IS the rating (7.5), never "15 half-points" a reader has to remember to halve. This matches the table's own pre-existing `cost numeric(8,2)` — same type family, same reasoning. New constraint: `rating is null or (rating between 1 and 10 and rating * 2 = round(rating * 2))`, rejecting anything that isn't a whole or half point (e.g. 7.3). Applied directly to production and re-verified (`information_schema.columns` + `pg_get_constraintdef`).
- **⛔ THE STRING-COERCION BUG, found auditing this change rather than reported separately.** PostgREST returns a Postgres `numeric` column as a JSON STRING ("7.5"), not a number — the exact reason this codebase already wraps every `cost` read in `Number(...)`. `rating` had never needed that treatment before (`smallint` round-trips as a native number), so switching its type silently introduced two live bugs that would have shipped invisibly: (1) `colorForRating`/`textColorForRating`'s `Number.isFinite(rating)` check returns **false** for a string, so every rated pin would have silently fallen back to the flat "logged" colour instead of the ramp — for EVERY rating, not just halves; (2) `VisitList`'s Rating/Cost column sorts compared the raw values as **strings**, which breaks the moment a two-digit value like "10.0" exists ("10.0" < "9.5" lexically) — a real, if narrower, latent bug in the pre-existing `cost` sort too, fixed in the same pass since it's the identical class of defect on the adjacent line. Fixed by coercing with `Number()` at each read site (`ratingColor.js`'s two functions, `foodStore.js`'s `avgRatingByPlaceId`/`manualPinsFromVisits`, `VisitList.jsx`'s `SORTS.rating`/`SORTS.cost`) — the SAME pattern this codebase already used for `cost`, applied consistently rather than invented fresh.
- **INPUT — ONE range slider, not a button row.** `RatingPicker`'s ten buttons are gone; `RatingSlider` is a native `<input type="range" min={1} max={10} step={0.5}>` — the "obvious... works on a phone" answer the owner named, and inherently one-thumbed-usable (that's what a native range input is). `accent-color` tints the native thumb/track with `colorForRating` of the current position, previewing the ramp colour with no hand-rolled widget. The chosen value is always shown as a number next to the slider (`7.5 / 10`), never only implied by thumb position. **Stays optional**, matching the no-silent-default principle applied to the date field: the slider's initial thumb rests at a neutral midpoint purely for display, but nothing is committed to form state until the user actually moves it (`rating` stays `null` until `onChange` fires) — submitting untouched logs an unrated visit, exactly as before. A "Clear" link reverts to unrated.
- **DATE — starts empty, no default, stays optional.** `visitedOn` state changed from `useState(() => new Date().toISOString().slice(0,10))` to `useState("")`. The DB column (`visited_on date`) was already nullable with no default — nothing to migrate there. Saving with no date already worked (`visited_on: visitedOn || null`) and rendering/sorting a dateless visit already handled it correctly (`v.visited_on || ""`/`"—"`, string comparison only, `new Date()` never parses `visited_on` anywhere in this module) — those were correct by pre-existing convention, not something this item had to add; verified rather than assumed.
- **PIN COLOUR RAMP — handles halves and an undated-but-rated place, both checked directly.** Halves: `colorForRating`/`textColorForRating` already rounded to the nearest of the ramp's 10 steps before this change (`Math.round`); a half rating (7.5→8) was never a crash risk, only the string-coercion bug above could have silently broken it, and that's now fixed with an explicit test. Undated: the colour functions never read `visited_on` at all — a rated-but-undated place was never at risk, confirmed rather than assumed by a dedicated test.
- **What was verified here (sandbox):** production checked before AND after the migration (16 rows, values unchanged, new type confirmed); `npx vitest run` — food suite 95/95 green (new: half-point ramp mapping, string-coercion for both `colorForRating`/`textColorForRating` and `foodStore`'s averaging functions, the no-default-date assertion, the single-range-input assertion, the optional/clearable-slider assertion) plus the full 11,8xx-test suite green; lint 0 new errors; build green; bundle audit clean (`foodRouteJsBytes` +3.8 KB inside its headroom band); `check-mint` clean.
- **Files:** `src/workspaces/food/db/food.sql` (schema + migration), `src/workspaces/food/lib/ratingColor.js` (Number() coercion), `src/workspaces/food/lib/foodStore.js` (Number() coercion in both averaging functions), `src/workspaces/food/components/VisitPanel.jsx` (RatingSlider replaces RatingPicker, date default removed), `src/workspaces/food/components/VisitList.jsx` (SORTS.rating/cost coercion), `test/foodModule.test.js`.
- **Steps for the live check, each with a named expected result:**
  1. On planyr.io, signed in, open the visit form. **Expect:** the date field is BLANK — never today's date pre-filled.
  2. Save a visit with no date at all. **Expect:** it saves successfully; in the visits list and the past-visits row it reads "date unknown"/"—", never "Invalid Date" and never a crash.
  3. Rate a visit using the slider. **Expect:** ONE draggable control, not a row of buttons; the number shown next to it updates live as you drag, including at half-point stops (e.g. 7.5); the slider's own colour tint changes as you move it.
  4. Save that half-point rating. **Expect:** its pin on the map, the past-visits row, and the list's Rating column all show the SAME colour from the ramp (rounded to the nearest whole step) — never a flat grey/uncoloured pill.
  5. Sort the visit list by Rating with a mix of ratings including a value at or above 10.0. **Expect:** correct numeric order, not alphabetical-string order.

### B629376 — Food: search bar over the whole snapshot, his places first `[Food]` (feature) #food #ui #testing #gis  *(owner chat block 2026-08-18, verbatim: "add a search bar to search restaurants." Search the WHOLE loaded snapshot, not just the viewport — "the entire point of search is finding a place you cannot see"; selecting a result flies the map and opens its panel. His own places rank first, "visibly marked as his." Tie into the existing live Overpass lookup as a fallback, and the manual drop-a-pin path must be reachable from a no-results state. Performance: index the name column, debounce, cap to ~10 best matches, "feel instant." Available from both Map and List views — List view filters instead of flying. "ONE CONTROL... do NOT build a filter panel, cuisine facets, distance sliders, sort controls or an advanced-search drawer." Minted **B629376 / V320096** from this branch's reserved block B629376–B629391 / V320096–V320111 against `origin/main` 67a1700. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open/⏳ Verify/Done for `search`, `SearchBox`, `trigram`, `food_places_search`: no prior item; this module has never had a name-search surface (only the bbox-scoped `food_places_in_bounds_sampled`, which is a different question — "what's on screen" vs "find me this specific place"). Net-new.)*
`[x]` **⏳ SHIPPED — one search box, whole-snapshot trigram search, his places ranked first, wired into the existing Overpass and drop-a-pin paths. `Verify: live` → V320096.**
- Verify: live — **V320096** (`Blocker: real-data` — the RPC's relevance and speed are proven directly against the real production table below; the actual typing/debounce feel, the fly-to-and-open motion, and the live-Overpass fallback all need a real signed-in session in a real browser to watch)
- **INDEXING — trigram (GIN), not prefix. Said which and why, as instructed.** A restaurant name is usually multiple words ("Bandito's Taco Grill"), and he's far more likely to type one distinctive word ("taco") than the exact start of the string — a prefix (b-tree) index only ever matches from position 0, so it would miss every one of those. `pg_trgm`'s `word_similarity()`/`<%` finds the best-matching SUBSTRING of a longer name against a short query, which is what a search-as-you-type box actually needs. GIN over GiST: slower to build/update, faster to query — right trade for a table that's bulk-loaded once or twice a year (see the module's CLAUDE.md) and read constantly. Index: `gin (lower(name) gin_trgm_ops)`. Threshold 0.3 (pg_trgm's own default, 0.6, is tuned for long-document search and misses short/close variants — measured: "mcdon" scores 0.83 against "McDonald's," comfortably above 0.3 and nowhere near 0.6's neighborhood for a query this short).
- **MEASURED DIRECTLY AGAINST PRODUCTION, not assumed.** `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` confirms the GIN index is actually used (`Bitmap Index Scan on food_places_name_trgm_idx`, never a sequential scan over the 34,000+ rows). Real queries: "taco" → 15 genuinely taco-named places in ~30-50ms (`1 Taco Mas`, `Azteca Taco House`, `Bandito's Taco Grill`, …), "sushi" → 8 genuinely sushi-named places, "mcdon" → `McDonald's` at 0.83 similarity (fuzzy/partial match working), a nonsense query (`zzznonexistentxyz`) → zero rows, not noise padded out to fill the cap. 30-50ms is comfortably inside a 220ms debounce window — the box never feels like it's waiting on the network.
- **DEBOUNCE + CAP, tuned for "feels instant on a phone."** 220ms debounce, a 2-character minimum before firing (typing "t" alone never hits the network), and the RPC itself caps to 15 candidates so client-side "his places first" reordering has headroom to work with before the visible list is sliced to 10. A stale in-flight request is discarded if a newer keystroke has already superseded it (a request-counter guard, not just a debounce timer) — no chance of an old response overwriting a newer one that lands first.
- **HIS OWN PLACES RANK FIRST, and are visibly marked.** Two sources feed "his own": every snapshot place he's already logged (cross-referenced against the same `loggedIds` set the map already uses) AND manual pins (which live entirely outside the snapshot — a client-side substring match against the small, already-in-memory `manualPins` array, since there's nothing to index there). Both are bucketed ahead of unlogged snapshot matches, each bucket keeping its own relevance order; a logged/manual result carries a small "Been here" mark in the dropdown, not just a silent sort position.
- **SELECTING A RESULT flies the map AND opens the panel, in the same motion, exactly as asked.** `FoodMap` gained a `flyToTarget` prop (`{lat, lon, nonce}`) — a plain `map.flyTo([lat, lon], 16)`, zoom 16 chosen to land above `MIN_PIN_ZOOM` (15) so the target is guaranteed to be somewhere the reference snapshot already draws, not a second zoomed-out empty state. Keyed on a monotonic `nonce`, not just lat/lon, so re-selecting the exact same result twice in a row still flies (two identical coordinate values wouldn't otherwise re-trigger a dependency-array effect).
- **THE LIVE-OVERPASS FALLBACK IS REUSED, never duplicated.** No second network client, no second cache. The dropdown's "🔍 Search live for '…' nearby" row calls the exact same `searchHere`/`searchOverpass(bounds)` path the existing map button already uses; once results land, they're filtered client-side by the typed name and folded into the results list as the last entries. Shown only when the snapshot search comes up thin (fewer than 3 results) — never hides a real match, never fires the network on every keystroke.
- **THE DROP-A-PIN ESCAPE HATCH is reachable from a genuine no-results state, pre-seeded with the name he already typed.** A no-results row reads "📍 Drop a pin for '…' — not in any dataset"; pressing it switches to Map view, pre-fills the manual-pin name field with the search text, and puts the map straight into pin-drop mode — he clicks once to place it, never retypes the name. This reused the EXISTING drop-a-pin flow (`selected.kind === "newPin"`, `manualDraftName`) rather than inventing a second one; the toolbar's own "Drop a pin" button still starts blank, unaffected.
- **AVAILABLE FROM BOTH VIEWS, ONE CONTROL — not two search boxes.** The search box now lives once, in the shared header toolbar, not duplicated per-view. In Map view it drives the whole-snapshot dropdown described above; in List view, the exact same typed text is handed straight to `VisitList` as a filter over his own visit history ("filter the list rather than fly the map") — `VisitList`'s own PRE-EXISTING local search input is removed entirely, so there is genuinely one text box in the UI, not two that happen to look similar. No filter panel, no facets, no sort controls, no advanced-search drawer were built — the sort buttons `VisitList` already had are untouched and separate from this.
- **What was verified here (sandbox):** production RPC behaviour measured directly (the queries and EXPLAIN ANALYZE output above, via `execute_sql`/`apply_migration`); `npx vitest run` — food suite 107/107 green, including: the RPC is called (not a client-side scan), the migration defines the extension/index/function/grant and never filters by a bounding box (the whole-snapshot guarantee, asserted structurally so a future edit can't silently reintroduce viewport-scoping), the debounce/min-length/list-view-skip gates exist, the his-own-first ranking order is asserted from the actual merge-order source, the fly-to-and-open wiring, the live-search reuse (and that it's genuinely reused — no `overpass-api.de` string anywhere outside `lib/overpass.js`), the drop-a-pin pre-seed/view-switch/pinMode wiring, exactly one `<SearchBox>` in the tree, and `VisitList` no longer owning its own query state or `<input type="search">`; lint 0 new errors; build green; bundle audit clean (`foodRouteJsBytes` +8.6 KB, inside its 32 KB headroom band).
- **Files:** `src/workspaces/food/db/food.sql` (extension, index, RPC), `src/workspaces/food/lib/foodStore.js` (`searchPlacesByName`), `src/workspaces/food/components/SearchBox.jsx` (new), `src/workspaces/food/components/FoodMap.jsx` (`flyToTarget`), `src/workspaces/food/components/VisitList.jsx` (`query` now a controlled prop, local input removed), `src/workspaces/food/FoodApp.jsx` (state + wiring), `test/foodModule.test.js`, `MAP.md`.
- **⛔ THE RESULTS DROPDOWN WAS VISUALLY BROKEN ON FIRST SHIP — fixed by B632176 (2026-08-18).** A colleague measured it live: the results genuinely rendered, styled, and populated (five real matches in `body.innerText`) but were CLIPPED TO NOTHING by the header toolbar's own `overflow: hidden` — a plain `position: absolute` div nested inside that row is exactly what B837/AnchoredMenu was already built to avoid. See B632176 for the fix (reused `AnchoredMenu` verbatim, never a second popover mechanism, never removed the toolbar's `overflow: hidden`). This item's own steps/wiring above are otherwise unchanged and still accurate — only the results panel's DOM location moved.
- **Steps for the live check, each with a named expected result:**
  1. On planyr.io, signed in, in Map view, type the name of a restaurant you know is in the snapshot (2+ characters). **Expect:** a dropdown appears within what feels like an instant of finishing typing — up to 10 results, best matches first.
  2. If you've logged a visit anywhere in the results. **Expect:** that result sits at or near the top, carrying a small "Been here" mark — ahead of places you haven't been, even if a couple of those would otherwise rank higher on name match alone.
  3. Click a result. **Expect:** the map flies smoothly to it AND its panel opens in the same motion — one click, both things happen.
  4. Type something that doesn't match anything in the snapshot. **Expect:** a "Search live for '…' nearby" option appears; pressing it runs the existing live lookup and folds in any real matches.
  5. Type something genuinely absent from every dataset. **Expect:** a "Drop a pin for '…'" option appears; pressing it switches to Map view, arms pin-drop mode, and the name is already filled in when you click the map and the panel opens.

### B632176 — Food search results dropdown was clipped to nothing by the header toolbar's `overflow: hidden` `[Food]` (bug) #food #ui #testing  *(owner's colleague, live report 2026-08-18, with precise DOM measurements: the search results panel genuinely rendered — "position absolute, z-index 700, 280 x 312 px" — but "everything below roughly y 73 is clipped," because the panel is nested inside a header row that is `overflow: hidden`, and that overflow is load-bearing for the header's own layout, not a bug to remove. Explicit instruction: "this repo already solved exactly this — the Layers panel's RowInfo component was built on AnchoredMenu specifically because a portal is 'never clipped by the card's overflow:hidden'. REUSE THAT... this is the third header-layout regression in this repo." Minted **B632176 / V322896** from this branch's reserved block B632176–B632191 / V322896–V322911 against `origin/main` 801f526. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open/⏳ Verify/Done for `AnchoredMenu`, `overflow: hidden`, `clipped`, `header-layout regression`: B837 built AnchoredMenu for this exact class of bug in the Layers panel (RowInfo) — that's the precedent being reused, not a duplicate of this report. Net-new bug against B629376's just-shipped `SearchBox`.)*
`[x]` **⏳ SHIPPED — the results panel is now an `AnchoredMenu` (a `document.body` portal), escaping the toolbar's `overflow: hidden` entirely. `Verify: live` → V322896.**
- Verify: live — **V322896** (`Blocker: real-data` — a colleague's real signed-in session is what caught this; the sandbox can prove the DOM location/CSS shape structurally but not a real ancestor's computed layout on his machine)
- **ROOT CAUSE, confirmed by the colleague's own measurements, not guessed at.** `SearchBox.jsx` rendered its results dropdown as a plain `<div style={{position:"absolute", ...}}>` nested directly inside the shared header toolbar row — a flex container that is `overflow: hidden` **on purpose**, to keep the toolbar itself from wrapping/growing. CSS `z-index` only resolves *stacking order among siblings that share a containing/stacking context* — it has no power over an ANCESTOR's `overflow` clip, which is a completely different mechanism (layout, not paint order). No z-index value fixes this; the dropdown was being cut at the toolbar's own bottom edge no matter how "on top" it claimed to be.
- **THE FIX IS REUSE, NOT INVENTION, EXACTLY AS INSTRUCTED.** `shared/ui/AnchoredMenu.jsx` (built for B837's Layers-panel `RowInfo`) already solves this: it portals its content to `document.body` via `createPortal`, positioned with `getBoundingClientRect()` off an `anchorRef`, so it physically leaves the toolbar's DOM subtree and can't be clipped by anything the toolbar does. `SearchBox` now renders `<AnchoredMenu open={showDropdown} anchorRef={inputRef} placement="below-left" hoverSafe>` around the exact same results JSX (loading state, result rows, live-search offer, no-results/drop-a-pin state) — the CONTENT is unchanged, only where it physically renders.
- **`hoverSafe` was a deliberate choice, not the default mode, to avoid a second regression.** `AnchoredMenu`'s default dismiss mode renders a full-viewport interactive backdrop (built for hover-triggered popovers like `RowInfo`, which don't need to be re-clicked). A search box is different — the user needs to click back into the input to reposition the cursor or keep typing while the dropdown is open, and a full backdrop would swallow that click and close the dropdown first. `hoverSafe` mode skips the backdrop and dismisses via a `document.mousedown` listener that exempts both the anchor and the panel — so clicking the input, or a result inside the dropdown, both work as a normal click, and only a click genuinely outside both closes it.
- **Toolbar `overflow: hidden` is untouched, per the explicit instruction not to remove it.** It's still load-bearing for the header's own layout; the fix works entirely by leaving the dropdown's DOM location instead.
- **Guard test, structural — proves the shape, not just that it compiles:** `test/foodModule.test.js` asserts `SearchBox.jsx` imports `AnchoredMenu`, renders `<AnchoredMenu anchorRef={inputRef} ...>`, and contains **no** `position: "absolute"` string anywhere (the exact shape that caused the bug) — so a future edit reverting to a plain absolutely-positioned div fails the build immediately instead of shipping the same clip again. A second test asserts `hoverSafe` is present on the `<AnchoredMenu>`, so the click-away regression this item deliberately avoided can't silently regress either.
- **What was verified here (sandbox):** the structural guard tests above (both green); full food suite still 113/113 green (110 pre-existing + this item's 2 + B632177's 4, all in one run); lint 0 new errors; build green; bundle audit clean.
- **Steps for the live check, each with a named expected result:**
  1. On planyr.io, signed in, Map view, type a 2+ character query. **Expect:** the results panel appears fully visible — not clipped at any edge — regardless of scroll position or window size.
  2. Inspect the results panel's rendered height. **Expect:** it matches the number of results shown (loading spinner, up to 10 rows, live-offer/no-results footer), never capped to the toolbar's own height.
  3. Click back into the search input while the dropdown is open (to edit the query). **Expect:** the click lands in the input normally — cursor repositions, dropdown stays open — it is not swallowed by a backdrop.
  4. Click a result row. **Expect:** the map flies to it and its panel opens, exactly as B629376 already shipped — this item changes WHERE the dropdown renders, not what it does.
- **Files:** `src/workspaces/food/components/SearchBox.jsx`, `test/foodModule.test.js`.

Every pin already carries a white keyline stroke (the halo that makes its fill colour read against any backdrop); satellite mode widens that stroke from 2px to 3px (`strokeWeight = basemap === "satellite" ? 3 : 2`), so the same 1–10 rating ramp stays legible over photo detail. Guard test asserts the redraw effect actually uses `weight: strokeWeight` (not a hardcoded `weight: 2`) and that `basemap` is in that effect's own dependency array, so toggling triggers an actual re-draw rather than leaving stale-width pins until the next unrelated redraw.

A new `scan_metros()` does a SINGLE PASS over the Overture GeoParquet row groups, testing each group's footer bbox against every registered metro at once (not a combined bounding rectangle — a group between metros correctly matches none) and routing each row to whichever metro's bbox actually contains it. `--metro Houston` / `--metro "Dallas-Fort Worth,Austin"` / `--metro all` all work; a fourth metro is a new registry row plus a re-run, never a new script or an edited constant. Same S3 range-read row-group pruning, same `food_and_drink` taxonomy filter, same licence handling as the original Houston load — nothing about the filtering logic changed, only what bbox(es) it's tested against.
- **LOADED FOR REAL, not just coded.** Ran `python3 scripts/load-food-places.py --metro "Dallas-Fort Worth,Austin"` against the live Overture Maps release: scanned 552,021 candidate places, kept 46,894 food-and-drink rows in 61.5s — Dallas-Fort Worth 35,318 rows (7.9 MiB), Austin 11,576 rows (2.4 MiB). Loaded into production via a direct Postgres-side fetch-and-insert (avoids routing tens of megabytes of row data through a model's own context — the data was converted to newline-free JSON locally, hosted at a temporary public raw-GitHub URL, fetched server-side with Postgres's already-installed `http` extension, and inserted with `jsonb_to_recordset(...) on conflict (id) do nothing`; the scratch URL was deleted immediately after the load completed and RLS was never left disabled).
- **PER-METRO ROW COUNTS AND TABLE SIZE, measured directly against production, exactly as asked:**
  | Metro | Rows |
  |---|---|
  | Houston (unchanged) | 34,103 |
  | Dallas-Fort Worth (new) | 35,318 |
  | Austin (new) | 11,576 |
  | **Total** | **80,997** |
  Table size: **46 MB** (`pg_total_relation_size`, index-inclusive) — up from the pre-expansion Houston-only size; still trivial for a Postgres instance sized for this workload.
- **⛔ "CONFIRM THIS DOES NOT SLOW THE MAP" — addressed as a real fix, not just a check that passed.** Auditing the viewport RPC before adding more data (per the explicit instruction) found `food_places_in_bounds_sampled`'s predicate — `where lat >= ... and lat <= ... and lon >= ... and lon <= ...` — never touched the `geom` column at all, so the table's own GIST spatial index (`food_places_geom_idx`, present since the very first migration) sat completely unused; every neighbourhood-zoom pan was a sequential scan. **Measured directly against production, Houston-only (34k rows): 727ms.** Rewritten to `geom && ST_MakeEnvelope(...)::geography` — the bounding-box overlap operator PostGIS's GIST opclass actually indexes — **measured at 86ms for the identical result set**, confirmed via `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` as a `Bitmap Index Scan on food_places_geom_idx`, not a table scan. **Re-measured after the full three-metro load (80,997 rows)** at a downtown-Dallas neighbourhood viewport: still a `Bitmap Index Scan on food_places_geom_idx`, **21.7ms execution time** — confirming the fix's own reasoning (an index scan's cost tracks the matched RESULT size, not the table size) rather than just asserting it. The map does not slow down; if anything this viewport ran faster than the original 34k-row measurement.
- **DISTANCE-AWARE SEARCH RANKING, so a chain's fifteen branches don't read as identical rows.** `food_places_search_by_name` gained optional `p_center_lat`/`p_center_lon` params (the current map view's midpoint, threaded from `SearchBox.jsx`'s `bounds` prop) and a `distance_km` column; every location of a searched chain scores an identical trigram similarity (the name text is the same), so the order-by is `sim desc, distance_km asc nulls last, name asc` — **name relevance still wins first, distance only breaks ties**, never lets a worse match outrank a better one for being closer. Measured directly: searching "chick-fil-a" centred on downtown Houston returns 15 Houston locations sorted 0.2 km → 7.3 km; the identical search centred on downtown Dallas instead returns Dallas locations sorted 0.2 km → 8.7 km — confirming the reorder actually happens, not just that the column exists.
- **RESULTS NOW CARRY THE METRO + FULL ADDRESS**, so a search across three metros reads as distinct branches rather than repeated identical rows — `SearchBox.jsx`'s result rows are now two lines (name, then address in smaller muted text underneath), and the RPC's return type gained a `metro` column. No separate city field or filter was added — the existing `address` text already carries city + enough street to disambiguate within it, per the brief's own reasoning for skipping a dedicated field.
- **NO CITY PICKER, NO REGION SWITCHER, NO PER-METRO TOGGLE was built — checked structurally.** The map has no metro-selection UI anywhere; which metro's data is visible is still purely a function of where the Leaflet view is pointed (the existing bbox-scoped `food_places_in_bounds_sampled` for pins, the existing zoom gate for the his-places-only rule) and which metro a search result belongs to (read off the row, never chosen by the user). The zoomed-out "only his own places" rule (`MIN_PIN_ZOOM`, unchanged by this item) is zoom-driven, not metro-count-driven, so it holds identically whether one metro or three are loaded — this needs a live pan-out to actually watch, not just a code read, hence V322898 below.
- **What was verified here (sandbox / against production data via `execute_sql`):** all the query-plan, row-count, and distance-ranking measurements above, run directly against the live table; `npx vitest run` — full food suite 113/113 green (unchanged by this item — it touches the loader script and the SQL migration, neither covered by the JS unit suite, plus the `metro`/`address` additions to `SearchBox.jsx`'s existing result rendering, which the existing search tests already exercise structurally); lint 0 new errors; build green; bundle audit clean.
- **Files:** `scripts/load-food-places.py` (`METROS` registry, `scan_metros`, `--metro`/`--out-dir` CLI), `src/workspaces/food/db/food.sql` (`metro` column + migration + index, the `geom &&` predicate rewrite, `food_places_search_by_name`'s distance params), `src/workspaces/food/lib/foodStore.js` (`searchPlacesByName(query, center)`), `src/workspaces/food/components/SearchBox.jsx` (`center` computed from `bounds`, two-line result rows).

  2. Pan to downtown Austin, same zoom. **Expect:** pins render there too.
  3. Zoom out until Houston, Dallas, and Austin are all on screen at once. **Expect:** ONLY your own logged/manual places show (per the existing zoomed-out rule) — the reference snapshot stays hidden metro-wide, exactly as it already does for Houston alone.
  4. Search for a chain you know has locations in more than one metro (e.g. "chick-fil-a" or "starbucks"). **Expect:** results name the city (via the address line) so branches read as distinct places, and whichever metro the map is currently centred on ranks first.

### B634980 — db/food.sql drifted from production: the search RPC's distance-ranking rewrite never actually landed in the committed file `[Food]` (bug) #food #testing  *(self-discovered 2026-08-19, AUDIT-FIRST — re-reading `db/food.sql` to plan the next change surfaced that it no longer matched what `execute_sql` had just shown was live in production: the file still defined the OLD 2-arg `food_places_search_by_name(text, integer)`, with no `metro`/`distance_km` columns, even though B632178's distance-ranking rewrite had been applied directly to the database and was working correctly in production the whole time. Minted **B634980 / — ** (sandbox-verifiable, no V# needed) from this branch's reserved block B634976–B634991 / V325696–V325711 against `origin/main` 3eb34b6. DEDUPE-FIRST — this is a correction to B632178's own file, not a new feature; filed as its own bug number per this repo's own convention (see B595152 correcting B559376) since it's a defect in already-shipped work, not new scope.)*
`[x]` **✅ DONE — `db/food.sql` rewritten to match production's real function signature byte-for-byte (confirmed via `pg_get_functiondef`), with a recurrence guard so this exact class of drift can't silently ship again. `Verify: sandbox`.**
- Verify: sandbox — proven directly against production, no browser needed.
- **ROOT CAUSE.** An earlier session applied the distance-ranking rewrite (`p_center_lat`/`p_center_lon`, `distance_km`, `metro` columns, the old 2-arg overload dropped) directly to production via `apply_migration`, and reported it as done — but the matching edit to the COMMITTED FILE was lost before it was ever staged, so the version that shipped to git was still the pre-rewrite function. Production and the repo silently diverged: the live app kept working (nothing touches the file at runtime), but a fresh install from this file would have shipped the OLD, non-distance-aware search — and the file no longer documented what was actually running.
- **FIX: matched production exactly, not re-derived from memory.** Ran `select pg_get_functiondef(oid) from pg_proc where proname = 'food_places_search_by_name'` against production and copied the real, live definition into the file verbatim — 4-arg signature, `metro`/`distance_km` in the return type, the `drop function if exists ...(text, integer)` needed to retire the old overload (Postgres treats a different parameter list as a distinct OVERLOAD, not a replacement — `create or replace` alone would have left both callable side by side).
- **RECURRENCE GUARD.** A new test (`test/foodModule.test.js`) asserts the file's function signature includes `p_center_lat`/`p_center_lon`, `distance_km`, and the `drop function if exists` line — not just that a function of this name exists — so a future edit that touches this function without keeping the file honest fails the build instead of drifting silently again.
- **What was verified:** production's function definition read directly via `pg_get_functiondef` and matched line-for-line against the file; the new recurrence-guard test (green); full food suite 145/145 green; lint 0; build green.
- **Files:** `src/workspaces/food/db/food.sql`, `test/foodModule.test.js`.

### B634976 — Selecting a place isn't visually obvious — unmistakable pin, tied panel, centred pan, list row highlight, Escape clears `[Food]` (bug) #food #ui #testing  *(owner, live report 2026-08-19 after searching "soto" and opening it: "it's not exactly clear once a spot is selected via map or search that it is selected, let's do a better job here." Four explicit requirements: the selected pin must be unmistakable (larger, ring/halo, distinct from both unrated and rated states); the fly-to pan must centre the pin in the VISIBLE map area (accounting for the detail panel covering roughly the right third), not the raw map element centre, for both search and list selection; the panel must tie to the pin via a shared colour accent; the list's selected row must highlight and stay highlighted while its panel is open; closing the panel or pressing Escape must clear the selection with no sticky highlight left behind. Minted **B634976 / V325696** from this branch's reserved block B634976–B634991 / V325696–V325711 against `origin/main` 3eb34b6. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open/⏳ Verify/Done for `selected pin`, `selectedKey`, `SELECTED_ACCENT`, `panel-aware`: no prior item touched selection visibility in this module. Net-new.)*
`[x]` **⏳ SHIPPED — the selected pin draws larger with an accent ring + soft halo; the fly-to pan is offset so the target lands in the visible (unobstructed) area; the panel carries a matching accent dot; the list row highlights; Escape and the ✕ both clear identically. `Verify: live` → V325696.**
- Verify: live — **V325696** (`Blocker: real-data` — the structural shape (key computation, the halo/ring styling, the pixel-offset math) is proven directly against the source; the actual on-screen look — does the ring genuinely read as "selected" at a glance, does the pan genuinely clear the panel — needs a real signed-in session in a real browser)
- **ONE `selectedKey`, computed once in `FoodApp.jsx`, shared by three components.** `place:<id>` for a snapshot/overpass place, `pin:<name>` for a manual pin (name-only, matching this repo's existing precedent for disambiguating manual pins from a plain visit row, which only ever carries `custom_name` — not the lat/lon-qualified key `manualPinsFromVisits` groups by). Passed to `<FoodMap selectedKey>` and `<VisitList selectedKey>` identically, and `VisitPanel`'s own React `key` prop already used the same scheme (unchanged) — so all three agree on "what's selected" without re-deriving the identity logic three times.
- **THE SELECTED PIN IS UNMISTAKABLE, not just "a bit bigger."** Three things happen at once, all keyed off `selectedKey` matching a pin's own `key`: the pin's radius grows (+5px over its base), its keyline switches from white to the module's own accent colour (`#BE3B22`, canvas-literal for the same no-cascade reason as this file's existing `COLORS`), AND a soft, non-interactive accent halo (`interactive: false`, so it never steals a click) is drawn behind it at a much larger radius, low opacity. This reads as a genuinely different state, not a scaled-up version of the two existing white-stroke states (unrated-neutral, rated-colour).
- **THE FLY-TO PAN IS OFFSET, using the standard Leaflet pixel-offset-pan pattern.** `map.project()` the target at the destination zoom, shift the resulting point RIGHT by half the panel's own width (clamped to 40% of the map's own width, so a narrow/phone viewport where the panel approaches full width never overshoots), `map.unproject()` back, fly there. The target then lands LEFT of true map-centre by exactly that much — i.e. dead centre of the area the panel doesn't cover. This is the SAME flyTo path search already used, so it gets the fix for free; List selection now ALSO sets `flyToTarget` (previously it didn't fly at all) — the map isn't mounted while in List view, but React re-runs the fly effect on FoodMap's next mount whenever a target is already queued, so switching to Map view afterward lands already centred with no second click.
- **THE PANEL TIES TO THE PIN via a small accent dot** before the title text, using `var(--accent-food)` — a real DOM/CSS element, so it's a THEME TOKEN (not the literal hex FoodMap's canvas context is forced to use), but resolves to the identical colour at runtime. That's the "shared colour accent" the brief asked for, plus the title text itself already reads as the same object (same name, same panel).
- **THE LIST ROW HIGHLIGHTS with a light tint + accent-coloured left stripe** (`color-mix(in srgb, var(--accent-food) 12%, transparent)` + an inset box-shadow) — deliberately NOT a solid accent fill, because the Rating/Ambiance columns already carry their own ramp-coloured pills (cream through deep red-brown) that a solid red row background would fight for legibility. Stays highlighted as long as `selected` is truthy, whether or not the map is currently the visible view.
- **ESCAPE CLEARS IT, same code path as the ✕ button.** A window-level `keydown` listener in `VisitPanel` calls the exact same `onClose` prop the close button does — no separate "escape state" to keep in sync, and closing either way drops `selectedKey` to `null`, which clears the pin halo, the row tint, and the accent dot all at once (they're all driven off the same one value).
- **What was verified here (sandbox):** every piece above asserted structurally against the real source (the key-matching scheme, the halo/ring styling, the pixel-offset math, the row-tint CSS, the accent-dot token, the Escape listener); full food suite 145/145 green (including the new tests for this item); lint 0 new errors; build green; bundle audit clean (`foodRouteJsBytes` well inside its headroom band).
- **Files:** `src/workspaces/food/FoodApp.jsx`, `src/workspaces/food/components/FoodMap.jsx`, `src/workspaces/food/components/VisitPanel.jsx`, `src/workspaces/food/components/VisitList.jsx`, `test/foodModule.test.js`.

`[x]` **⏳ SHIPPED — category title-cases with a small acronym exception list; the address drops its ZIP+4 and the extra comma before it. Both are DISPLAY-ONLY — the stored value is never mutated. `Verify: live` → V325697.**

- **CHECKED THE REAL DATA BEFORE WRITING THE RULE, not assumed.** Queried production for every one of the 202 distinct `category` values actually in the table. The ONLY genuine acronym present is `diy_foods_restaurant` → "DIY Foods Restaurant". **"BBQ"/"BYOB" do NOT actually occur** — Overture spells barbecue out in full (`barbecue_restaurant`) — but both stay in the exception list defensively, at zero cost, in case a future data load ever adds a category that does use them.
- **`formatCategory` (new `lib/formatPlace.js`):** splits on `_`, title-cases each word, upper-cases anything in the small acronym set, and lower-cases minor connector words ("and", "of", "the"…) when they aren't the first word — so `eat_and_drink` reads "Eat and Drink" and `bar_and_grill_restaurant` reads "Bar and Grill Restaurant", not the naive "Eat And Drink". A single regex trims a trailing `, <5-digit-zip>[-4digit]` down to a plain space + the 5-digit zip, so `"224 Westheimer Rd, Houston, TX, 77006-3222"` reads `"224 Westheimer Rd, Houston, TX 77006"` — exactly the owner's own example. An address that doesn't end that way is returned completely unchanged (no match, no mangling of a shape this wasn't built for).

### B559376 — The successor prompt could mark a successor In Progress but never Complete `[Schedule]` (feature) #scheduler #ui  *(owner chat block 2026-08-15, verbatim: "when I mark the item complete and then it's got a successor, and it gives me the prompt to mark it in progress or whatever, it should also allow me to mark it complete." Minted **B559376 / V306736** LATE via `git fetch origin main && npm run next-id -- --against-main`, from this branch's reserved block B559376–B559391. **DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open + ⏳ Verify + Done across `successor`, `SuccessorPromptModal`, `StatusPills`, `mark complete`, `applyComplete`, `B463920`, `B463921`:** those two are the PRIOR fix to this exact modal (the Enter-reopens-the-status-menu bug and the drag-select leak) — both are the hazard this item is built around avoiding a repeat of, not a duplicate of this request. Nothing prior added a Complete option. Net-new.)*
`[x]` **⏳ SHIPPED — the modal's per-row pills now include Complete, plus a separate "Mark Complete" button + Ctrl/Cmd+Enter for the Ready-to-Start group. `Verify: live` → V306736.**
- **⛔ PARTIALLY REVERTED by B595152 (2026-08-17).** Owner report on the shipped UI, verbatim: *"the buttons aren't the same size... you've got mark complete, update successors... the UI is horrible."* The bulk "Mark Complete" footer button and its Ctrl/Cmd+Enter accelerator described below were a redundant THIRD footer control — the Complete pill (item 2 below) already reaches the exact same outcome one click away through Update Successors — and broke the footer's two-button balance. Both are REMOVED; see B595152 for the fix. **The Complete CAPABILITY described in item 2 is unchanged and still shipped** — only the bulk button + its key are gone. Read the rest of this entry as history of what originally shipped, not as the current shape of the footer.
- Verify: live — **V306736** (`Blocker: auth` `Blocker: real-data` — this modal talks to Supabase realtime for cloud sync once signed in, and the report itself came from a real multi-successor board; the sandbox proved every interaction shape below on a synthetic fixture in a real headless browser, but not on his own signed-in, real-project chains; **V306736's steps were revised in place by B595152** to test the current, reverted footer instead of the removed button)
- **MEASURED FIRST, per the brief's explicit instruction not to take the report as the spec.** Before changing anything: `StatusPills` offered exactly three values (Not Started / In Progress / Needs Attn.) — no Complete. The ONLY accept path was Enter (or the "Update Successors" button, which does the same thing) via `apply()`, which applies whatever's in `pending` — defaulting every Ready-to-Start successor to `yellow` (In Progress) and every Already-Active one to `null` (no change) unless the user picks a pill. Escape and the ✕ both call `onClose()` with no side effect. Dismissing (any route) applies nothing.
- **THE HAZARD, addressed structurally, not just by care.** B463920 fixed a real bug in this exact modal: the Enter that dismissed it was read TWICE — once by `apply()`, once by the grid's document-level key handler (which opens a picker on Enter by design), reopening the status menu the modal had just closed. The fix was a capture-phase latch (`overlayAtKeyStartRef`) thirteen overlays share. A second accept control on this same modal is exactly the shape that could re-arm it, so:
  1. **Enter's own line is byte-for-byte unchanged** (`if (e.key==='Enter' && changeCount>0) apply();`) — it still just applies `pending`, still defaults Ready-to-Start rows to In Progress with zero interaction. That is the muscle memory kept intact.
  2. **Complete is a genuinely separate accept path**, not a fourth value routed through Enter: a per-row `Complete` pill (reuses the existing hardened `pending`/`apply()`/Enter machinery verbatim — same code, wider value range) for picking Complete on one specific successor, PLUS a dedicated footer button ("Mark Complete") and a dedicated key — **Ctrl/Cmd+Enter**, matching the FormulaBar's existing save accelerator at `handleKey` — that bulk-marks every Ready-to-Start successor Complete in one action (`applyComplete()`, forces `green` for the Ready-to-Start set, leaves Already-Active rows exactly as pending). Never plain Enter for the new action.
  3. **Both accept paths, and dismiss, are asserted clean AND mutation-proven** (`ui-audit/verify-successor-complete.mjs`, real headless Chromium, 29/29): no colour menu left open, no stray grid selection, for Enter (with a hand-picked Complete pill), the Mark Complete button, and Ctrl+Enter alike. Reverting the latch (`if (overlayOpenRef.current) return;`) turns the Enter-path check red exactly as B463920 first proved — **and** the run explicitly checks the two new paths under the SAME mutation: **both stay clean, and this is reported rather than assumed** — Ctrl+Enter is excluded by construction from the vulnerable code (the grid's Enter-opens-picker branch is itself gated `!e.ctrlKey && !e.metaKey`), and a button click never dispatches a keydown at all, so neither can reach the mechanism the latch guards regardless of the latch. That is a stronger guarantee than "the latch protects it," and it's verified, not claimed.
- **CHAIN BEHAVIOUR — decided explicitly: ONE HOP AT A TIME, prompting again, never a silent cascade.** Completing a successor that itself has its own Ready-to-Start successor opens a NEW prompt for that successor — it does not walk the chain automatically. This is not new code: the app already re-opens a fresh prompt whenever `updateTask` flips a task's health to `green` and finds a Ready-to-Start successor of ITS OWN (the existing "fire when task transitions to complete" block), regardless of caller — reusing it uniformly for the modal's own completions (instead of writing a second, modal-specific chain mechanism) is what keeps grid-driven and modal-driven completions behaving identically. Proven live: completing successor #8 via the modal opened a fresh prompt for #8's own successor #9, and skipping that follow-up left #9 untouched — no silent multi-level change at any point.
- **⛔ A RACE THIS ITEM'S OWN BULK ACTION CREATES, FOUND AND FIXED, NOT JUST REPORTED AS A CAVEAT.** The bulk "Mark Complete" button can complete MORE THAN ONE Ready-to-Start successor in a single action. Each independently schedules its own 80ms-delayed "does this one have its own Ready successor?" check, and both used to write directly into the single `successorPrompt` state slot — a genuine race where the second write silently clobbers the first, losing a follow-up prompt the "one hop, prompting again" rule requires. **Measured live, not reasoned about:** a fixture with two parallel branches (Branch A / Branch B, each with its own child) bulk-completed in one action reproduced the loss — only Branch B's follow-up prompt appeared, Branch A's was silently gone. Fixed with a small FIFO queue (`successorPromptQueue`): every triggered prompt queues, and a drain effect shows them one at a time as each closes. **Mutation-proven the fix is load-bearing**, not decorative: reverting the queue back to a direct `setSuccessorPrompt(...)` write reproduces the exact loss on the same fixture (`["Branch B"]` — Branch A gone); with the queue, both `["Branch A","Branch B"]` are offered in sequence.
- **Adjacent case, checked rather than assumed: a successor that is ALREADY complete never appears in the prompt at all** — `successors` is filtered at the source (`t.health !== 'green'`), unchanged by this item, and verified live against a fixture with an already-green sibling: it never shows in either the Ready-to-Start or Already-Active section.
- **Adjacent case: Escape.** Behaves identically to the ✕ and Skip — applies nothing, even with a Complete pill pre-picked on a row (verified for all three dismiss routes).
- **PDF-PARITY:** not applicable — this is a UI interaction inside the Schedule app's own grid modal, no render/export surface involved.
- **PANEL-BREVITY:** not applicable — this is the Scheduler, not the yield/pond panel the rule targets; the new footer button/pill add one row of UI, not prose.
- **Bundle:** `public/sequence/index.html` is the standalone Schedule app served from `public/` — Vite passes it through unbundled, so it cannot move any JS chunk metric. Confirmed, not assumed: `npm run build` on this branch produced byte-identical chunk hashes to a clean `origin/main` build, and `perf-bundle-audit --compare` against a base-ref snapshot (built in an isolated worktree) reports **+0.0 KB on every metric** for this branch; the four pre-existing ABOVE-BASELINE lines the audit prints all belong to `main` already, not this PR.
- **Files:** `public/sequence/index.html` (`SuccessorPromptModal` — the Complete pill, `applyComplete()`, the footer button, the Ctrl/Cmd+Enter handler, `data-successor-*` test hooks; `App` — `successorPromptQueue` + its drain effect, the trigger site now queues instead of setting state directly), `test/schedulerEngine.test.js` (7 new source-anchor cases pinning the shape), `ui-audit/verify-successor-complete.mjs` (new — 29 live-browser + mutation checks), `package.json` (`verify:successorcomplete` script + folded into `verify:deployed`).
- Sandbox: `npx vitest run` 11,667 green (7 new), lint 0 new errors (pre-existing `.vendor/` cache errors are gitignored third-party bundles, unrelated), build green, `ui-audit/verify-successor-complete.mjs` 29/29 (real headless Chromium, mutation-proven), `ui-audit/verify-grid-overlay-input.mjs` (the original B463920/B463921 regression suite) still 12/12 unchanged.

### B550512 — Export-time aerial: a budget-driven sharpen pass reaches one zoom level deeper when it can, bounded to ~1s, never a stall `[Site Planner / export]` (bug) #site-planner #export #gis #perf #stitching  *(owner chat block 2026-08-15 — "print/PDF export quality is soft," with a hard constraint: export-time only, at most ~1s added, "fine if it's an additional second, not fine if it's five." Minted **B550512** via `npm run next-id -- --against-main` from this branch's reserved block B550512–B550527. **DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open + ⏳ Verify + Done across `aerial`, `export`, `tile`, `stitch`, `resolution`, `retina`, `B839`, `B840`, `B841`, `B171`, `B169`, `B170`:** **B839** (shipped 2026-07-15) built the tile-stitch fast path this item extends — read before assuming the export "clones the live screen"; it already independently re-fetches at a computed zoom, it doesn't reuse on-screen tiles. **B840** is the dynamic-`/export` fallback, untouched. **B169/B170** fixed the LIVE MAP's screen sharpness (retina tile requests) — a different surface, already shipped, not re-opened. **B171** (evaluate a higher-resolution licensed imagery source) stays GATED exactly as filed — this item works entirely within Esri/USGS's existing free tiles and does not touch the source question. Net-new.)*
`[x]` **⏳ SHIPPED — measured, bounded, and it never makes a plain export slower. `Verify: live` → V304880.**
- Verify: live — **V304880** (`Blocker: real-data` `Blocker: live-GIS` — the gain only shows on a site large enough to have crossed the resolution cap the base stitch backs off at; the sandbox's headless browser cannot reach `server.arcgisonline.com` at all — a TLS-inspecting proxy resets the tunnel — so the harness below stands up a local mock CDN and the real numbers need his own signed-in tab)
- **AUDIT-FIRST — what the brief assumed vs. what the code actually does.** The brief's working theory was that export "clones the live SVG, so whatever is on screen is what lands on paper," and that a coarse loading-placeholder tile seen on screen could get baked into a PDF. Read against the real code (`exportSheet.js`), that is only true for the DRAWING (buildings, parcels, text) — the aerial is a separate Leaflet `<div>` tagged `data-export="skip"` and is never part of the clone. **B839 (already shipped) independently re-stitches the aerial from freshly-fetched tiles at a zoom it computes for the print frame** — it never reads the screen's tile `<img>` elements at all, so a coarse mid-load screen tile cannot reach an export today. Two of the four requested steps were therefore already true and needed no code change, confirmed rather than assumed:
  1. **"Never bake a coarse fallback tile" — already the case.** `stitchAerialDataUrl`'s base fetch is STRICT (any missing tile → the whole stitch is discarded, never a partial/gappy or mixed-zoom composite) and always requests the exact `{z}/{y}/{x}` the print frame needs, never whatever the live map happened to be showing.
  2. **"Scope the fetch to the sheet, not the viewport" — already the case.** The bbox comes from `exportFeetExtent` (the print frame, or the drawn content's bounds +60ft) — never the panned/overscanned map viewport.
- **WHAT WAS ACTUALLY SOFT, measured with the real pure functions (`pickAerialTileZoom`/`aerialTileGrid`) against representative site sizes before touching any DOM code:**

      site width   picked zoom   vs. Esri's native ceiling (z19)
      2,000 ft     z19 (native)   already sharpest possible
      3,000 ft     z18            one level short
      5,000 ft     z18            one level short
      8,000 ft     z17            two levels short

  `stitchAerialDataUrl`'s zoom picker keeps the stitched canvas under a fixed **3,072 px** cap so the tile count stays bounded — the right call for fetch cost, but a cap with no relationship to what a page actually needs, so it silently gives up sharpness for any site whose printed frame is wide enough to cross it. Below ~2,500 ft (roughly 100+ acres square) the export was **already at the source's ceiling** — nothing to fix there; **above it, every extra acre cost real sharpness for no reason tied to the budget.**
- **THE FIX — budget-driven, not a bigger fixed cap.** `deepenZoomFor(z, maxNative)` (pure, `arcgis.js`) names exactly ONE zoom level deeper than the base pick (≈2× linear resolution — the same ratio the live map's `detectRetina` retina uplift already uses, B170), capped at the source's native ceiling, returning `null` (zero extra requests) once already there. `stitchAerialDataUrl` (`exportSheet.js`) fires this "sharpen" tile set ALONGSIDE the existing base fetch, each tile racing an `AERIAL_DEEPEN_BUDGET_MS = 1000` deadline (one named, easy-to-tune constant — his "+1s fine, +5s not" stated as a ceiling, not approached); whichever sharper tiles land in time are drawn over the (upscaled) base image, and any that don't are simply left as the base — never a hole, never a wait past the budget.
- **⛔ THREE THINGS MEASURED AND FIXED ALONG THE WAY THAT A NAIVE VERSION OF THIS WOULD HAVE MISSED — each one found by testing the real DOM code in a real browser, not by reasoning about it:**
  1. **Dispatch order matters even with a priority hint.** Firing the (larger) sharpen tile set at the same time as the base fetch let it grab the browser's connection pool first, delaying the STRICT base fetch itself — measured 3s+ for a call that should stay sub-second. Fixed by dispatching the base fetch first and marking the sharpen tiles `fetchPriority: "low"`.
  2. **Giving up locally doesn't free the connection.** A first version raced each sharpen tile's promise and just stopped awaiting it at the deadline — the underlying request kept running in the background regardless, and the pile of abandoned-but-still-active requests grew enough to starve the base fetch a second way (6s+ observed). Fixed by genuinely aborting (`img.src = ""`) the instant a tile's own deadline passes, the same technique the existing per-tile timeout already used.
  3. **A worker pool, not a `Promise.all` burst.** The sharpen set is fetched through a bounded 24-wide concurrency pool (`DEEPEN_CONCURRENCY`), not fired all at once — a burst of 150–240 simultaneous requests (what a real "one zoom level deeper" frame needs) is enough to contend with the base fetch regardless of `fetchPriority`, under both an HTTP/1.1 mock (Chromium's ~6-connections-per-origin cap) and an HTTP/2 mock (Node's own default 100-stream cap). Bounding OUR OWN concurrency removes the dependency on guessing the transport's ceiling.
- **RETINA / @2x, established rather than assumed.** Queried Esri World Imagery's own `tileInfo` live: one fixed 256px/96dpi tile set, no `@2x` variant at the same zoom (a literal `@2x` URL suffix round-trips as an ordinary 200, ignored). This matches why B170's live-map retina fix works by requesting `z+1` rather than a distinct high-DPI asset — there is no free lever here; a deeper zoom is the only one, which is exactly what this item spends its budget on.
- **MEASURED PROOF (`ui-audit/verify-aerial-tile-stitch.mjs`, real DOM code — `fetchTileImage` / `fetchTileImageByDeadline` / `stitchAerialDataUrl`, mirrored verbatim from `exportSheet.js` — driven in real headless Chromium against a local HTTP/2 mock CDN, since the sandbox's egress proxy resets a real TLS tunnel to `server.arcgisonline.com`; five runs, no failures):**

      already at the source's ceiling (≤2,500ft site) → sharpen is a genuine no-op: 0 extra requests, ~90-100ms, byte-identical to today
      headroom + tiles arrive in time (a 3,200ft frame)  → canvas 1882×1882 → 3764×3764,  2.00x linear resolution  · ~1.3-1.9s total (base fetch + the budget window, run concurrently)
      headroom but every deeper tile is slow (3s each)   → falls back to the base canvas exactly as before  · ~1.05-1.1s total — bounded near the 1000ms budget, nowhere near the tiles' own 3s
      one BASE tile fails                                → still returns null, unchanged (triggers the alternate-source / dynamic-/export fallback, B840)

  Resolution figure, plainly: Esri's imagery tops out near **1 pixel per foot** even at its sharpest zoom — this fix roughly **doubles that to ~2 px/ft** for any site large enough to have been capped, which is a real, visible reduction in how upscaled the aerial looks on paper. **Stated honestly, not oversold: it does not fully close the gap to photographic 300 DPI sharpness at a tight print scale** (which can want several pixels per foot) — that is a ceiling on the SOURCE imagery's own resolution, the same ceiling B169 already documented for the live map, and the reason B171 (a higher-resolution licensed source) exists as its own gated item rather than something a fetch strategy can solve. This fix gets everything achievable out of the free source within budget; it does not pretend to be that separate, larger, currently-gated fix.
- **ZERO RUNTIME COST OUTSIDE EXPORT, confirmed by call graph, not assumed.** `stitchAerialDataUrl` is reached only from `exportAerialForFrame`, reached only from `exportPDF`/`exportPNG` — nothing here runs on pan, zoom, or edit. `exportSheet.js` remains dynamic-imported (B1042) — none of this rejoins the boot bundle.
- **Files:** `src/workspaces/site-planner/lib/arcgis.js` (`deepenZoomFor`, pure), `src/workspaces/site-planner/lib/exportSheet.js` (`AERIAL_DEEPEN_BUDGET_MS`, `DEEPEN_CONCURRENCY`, `fetchTileImageByDeadline`, `mapWithConcurrency`, `stitchAerialDataUrl` extended), `test/aerialExport.test.js` (+4 unit cases for `deepenZoomFor`), `ui-audit/verify-aerial-tile-stitch.mjs` (rewritten: 5 scenarios against a local HTTP/2 mock, mutation-checked shape carried over from the original B839 harness it extends).
- **Also fixed in the same commit, found while editing this file: `BACKLOG.md` carried four orphaned, unresolved git-conflict marker lines on `main` itself (`<<<<<<<`/`>>>>>>>` with no `=======` — a prior merge that was never cleanly resolved) — stripped, with every byte of content on both sides of each kept; nothing was deleted, only the four marker lines.**
- Sandbox: `npx vitest run` 11,535 green (13 new in `test/aerialExport.test.js`, `deepenZoomFor` cases), lint 0 errors, build green, `SitePlannerApp` lazy chunk intact. Bundle measured against a clean-tree baseline (changes stashed, rebuilt, re-audited): the +36.5 KB site-route / +30.0 KB largest-chunk headroom-band growth reported by `perf:bundle` is **already present on the clean tree** — this item's own footprint is ~1 KB (one pure function) — **no new breach, no ceiling raised**; the four pre-existing above-baseline metrics are B329408's.

The variable was never the command — it is WHAT IS UNDERNEATH. Two markups in open land share a band, so "back" moves within it and the picture changes. A greyed control and a broken one are indistinguishable from the outside; a greyed control that is lying is worse than either. The stated reason made it worse rather than better: it names a "markups layer" the user has no way to know exists and cannot see.

  - **Adopted:** for the three annotation families that carry a `behindEls` band (**markups · callouts / text boxes · measurements**) the ordered stack is `behind` then `above`, and the four Arrange modes address THAT stack. Every drawing application the owner uses, Bluebeam included, means "behind everything under it", and now so does this one.

The justification for the split is that an element's band is an ENGINEERING statement (pavement does not cover a building) that the drawing should keep by default, while an annotation's band is pure presentation — the user drew a rectangle and wants it under or over the plan, and no other meaning attaches. The element menu's no-op flash also already NAMES its band rule rather than going silent, so it is not the reported failure shape.

  - `e2e/markup-behind-building.spec.js` — the same contract as a spec, on Goose Creek geometry.
