### B548065 — A markup sent behind a building could not be right-clicked back: the send-behind door was one-way `[Site Planner / selection]` (bug) #site-planner #markup #ui #selection  *(owner chat block 2026-08-14, arrived as provisional NEW-2, reproduced by him on his own account. Minted **B548065 / V302433** from the same reserved block. **DEDUPE-FIRST — the owner named the lineage to check and it was checked: B310** (accidental parcel selection while panning) is about a press reaching the WRONG thing during a pan; **B420** (parcel grabs only by its boundary) and **B155** (grab unfilled markups by their interior) are both about a feature's own HIT AREA, and both are intact — this markup's hit area is correct and it is simply painted underneath; **B1188** is the inspector's open/closed state being derived from the selection. **B316865** is the nearest sibling and the reason the resolver this reuses exists at all — but it is chrome painting ABOVE a feature and answering as itself, whereas here the annotation is below BY THE USER'S OWN INSTRUCTION and the element on top is answering correctly. None is this; net-new rather than an amendment.)*
`[x]` **⏳ SHIPPED — two ways back, neither of which depends on finding uncovered geometry. `Verify: live` → V302433.**
- Verify: live — **V302433** (`Blocker: auth` — driven here on his real plan data; his signed-in tab is the configuration this sandbox cannot reach)
- Origin: filed 2026-08-14 from chat (provisional NEW-2)
- **THE SYMPTOM, measured.** After sending a markup behind the plan, right-clicking it anywhere it overlaps a building opens the **BUILDING's** menu, which mentions the markup nowhere. Paint order is hit-test order in SVG, so the element on top answers every press across the whole overlap. The markup is grabbable only on a sliver no element covers — and on one drawn to COVER a building, on nothing at all. **B548064 makes this worse rather than better on its own**, because it makes crossing the band the ordinary thing to do; the two had to ship together.
- **THE FIX — two mechanisms, because the two states need different answers.**
  1. **A SELECTED annotation in the behind band keeps the right-click wherever it paints.** The selection survives the send, so the way back is available in the very next gesture. Narrow on purpose: it fires only for an annotation that is BOTH already selected AND actually painted under this point, so nothing changes for an element that merely overlaps something. Sibling of `gestureAnchorTarget` — same idea (what the user is working on wins the hit test), different trigger.
  2. **The covering element's menu NAMES what is underneath, with one row to reverse it and one to select it.** `Behind this ▸ Bring the markup back in front` · `Select the markup underneath`. This is the answer for the DESELECTED state, which is the one the owner was stuck in, and it needs no uncovered geometry at all — right-click anywhere over the overlap.
- **⛔ THE STACK IS READ AT MENU-OPEN TIME, not at render.** The menu is about to paint over the very point the user aimed at, so asking again during render would hit the menu instead of the plan.
- **Scoping that keeps an ordinary menu ordinary:** only annotations in the BEHIND band are listed. An element under another element has always been reachable through its own uncovered geometry, and listing everything would turn a right-click menu into a scene graph. A control building with nothing underneath renders no extra rows — asserted.
- **Reuse rather than a fifth copy:** `featureTarget.js` gains `featureStack` / `featuresBeneath` / `stackHoldsFeature` (pure, same skip-the-chrome rule the double-click resolver already uses), and the reversal calls the three existing band setters.
- **GUARDS.** `test/markupBehindReach.test.js` (20 — the pure stack reader plus source guards on both mechanisms, incl. that the priority check runs BEFORE the element claims the selection). Live half is the same `ui-audit/verify-markup-over-building.mjs`, whose NEW-2 arms are mutation-proven red on the pre-fix build — including its own precondition that, deselected, an ordinary press at that point really does reach the building rather than the markup, so the arm cannot rot green if the overlap ever stops being real.

### B519907 — An undo rebuilt the entire basemap, because `origin` came back as a new object `[Site Planner / Map]` (bug) #site-planner #perf #gis #view  *(the FIX for B1121 ×4, found and shipped 2026-08-14. Minted **B519907 / V295136**. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open / ⏳ Verify / Done across `B1121`, `B1189`, `B1439`, `B1440`, `origin`, `pushHistory`, `applySnapshot`, `map.remove`, `preserveTilesAcrossSetView`, `boundTileCache`: **B1189** is the same CLASS on a different effect (it fixed the registration layout effect by listing `origin.lat/lon` in its deps) and **B385040** is the same class again on `overlays` identity through `applySnapshot` — neither owns the map-creation effect, and neither stabilises the VALUE. **B1121** is the SYMPTOM this is the mechanism for and stays open on its residual. Net-new.)*
`[ ]` **`pushHistory` snapshots the WHOLE app state, so an undo restored `origin` as a fresh object holding identical numbers — and the Leaflet map-CREATION effect keys on it with `map.remove()` as its cleanup. React runs a cleanup before re-running, so every Ctrl+Z destroyed and rebuilt the whole basemap.**
- **Measured per action on the owner's Richfield plan:** click 0/0 · drag 0/0 · **undo 272 tile `<img>` added + 272 removed** · pan 14/0 · Escape 0/0, with the retained count never leaving 274. Each undo paid 272 element destructions, 272 image decodes and 544 Leaflet subscriptions **for a basemap that had not moved**. ⛔ The tile COUNT is identical either side of the defect — which is exactly why every existing instrument here was blind to it, and why the guard counts CHURN.
- **The fix:** the state is held as `originRaw` and `origin` is derived through a `useMemo` keyed on the two SCALARS, so an equal-valued restore is the SAME object and none of the ten effects keyed on it re-runs.
  - **⚠ NOT a per-effect fix, and B1189 is why.** That item hit this exact class and fixed ONE effect by listing `origin.lat/lon` in its deps — leaving nine others and every future one to remember. Stabilising the VALUE closes all of them at once.
  - **⚠ NOT a tolerant compare.** `sameOrigin`'s 1e-12 is right for *"is this the same site?"* and wrong here: it would pin a genuinely MOVED origin to its old object and strand the basemap at the previous location.
- **PROOF — controlled A/B, same build config, same plan, same 12-round × 6-edit sequence, fix stashed and restored:** listeners **1544 → 1616, +6 EVERY round, 12/12, no plateau** → **1544 → 1656 (one step) then 1656 flat for 11 rounds**; retained heap **+1.66 MB/round → +0.65 MB/round**; renderer RSS delta **457.2 → 241.2 MB**; undo churn **272/272 → 0/0**, redo likewise, map alive with all 274 tiles.
- **⚠ WHAT IS NOT FIXED, stated rather than rounded off.** The listener leak is GONE. The retained-heap slope is CUT BY ~60%, NOT ELIMINATED, and the after-curve is still decaying at round 12 rather than provably flat. The after run also STARTS higher (45.6 vs 25.9 MB) — with the map no longer torn down, more is legitimately retained at load; **the SLOPE is what was fixed, and the slope is what makes a long session degrade.** That residual keeps **B1121** open.
- **Guards, both mutation-proven:** the repo-root `test/` suite **originIdentityStable** (source guards incl. the no-tolerance rule) and the ui-audit harness **verify-undo-tile-churn** (`npm run perf:undochurn` — **exit 0 on the fixed build, exit 1 with the fix stashed**). It carries two CONTROLS — the map must be alive and still holding tiles — because a build that simply never rebuilt the map would otherwise score a perfect zero while being badly broken.
- **⚠ Also fixed: a real defect in the NEW harnesses, caught by this repo's own guard.** They stranded an `ElementHandle` from `waitForSelector` — **B1439**, a strong GC root that inflates every later memory reading. In an instrument whose whole purpose is measuring retention that is contamination, not style. Now `waitForSelectorReleased`.
- Verify: live
- Origin: filed 2026-08-14 from chat


### B520560 — The owner's two split decisions, shipped: every piece kept, and the pieces numbered off the original `[Site Planner / parcels]` (feature) #site-planner #parcel #geometry #ui  *(owner chat block 2026-08-13, answering the two judgement calls B455360 filed. Minted **B520560** LATE via `git fetch origin main && npm run next-id -- --against-main`, from this branch's reserved block B520560–B520575 (origin/main 55dcdb5). **DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open / ⏳ Verify / Done across `parcel name`, `parcelDisplayInfo`, `parcelOutline`, `lineage`, `label`, `situs`, `addr`, `sliver`, `B455360`, `B651`, `B682`, `B1415`.** This is the SECOND HALF of **B455360** (⏳ Verify, same branch, same V###) — its own number rather than a re-open, because it changes shipped behaviour rather than repairing it. **B651** owns the parent-supersede model this rides on, unchanged. **B1415–B1418** own the PROJECT name and are a different axis entirely (a plan's `site` field), deliberately untouched. `parcelDisplayInfo`'s lineage chain is PRIOR ART and is named as such below. Net-new.)*
`[x]` **SHIPPED.** `siteModel.parcelDisplayInfo` (names) + the canvas acreage badge + `polygonSplit` (keep every piece).
- Verify: **live** — folded into the EXISTING `V250304` rather than a new entry; see the note there about who is driving it.
- Sandbox evidence: `test/siteModel.test.js` **+7 naming tests** (two proven RED against the rule each replaced) · `test/polygonSplit.test.js` **31** · `e2e/parcel-split-complex-cut.spec.js` **8/8 in the real app**, incl. re-splitting a piece · unit **11,098 passing** · lint 0 errors · build green · PANEL-BREVITY audit clean · bundle +0.9 KB against a clean-tree baseline, no new breach.

**(1) THREE OR MORE PIECES — KEEP THEM ALL. This CHANGED something, which the answer's phrasing hides.** Keeping every piece was already true of the ENGINE, and the toast already said how many were made — both confirmed unchanged. But B455360 also dropped any piece under a hundred-thousandth of the parent and *reported the loss*, which his instruction forbids: *"Nothing may be discarded silently — if a cut produces a sliver, he gets it as a parcel rather than losing the acreage."* That drop is **gone**. Every traced face with measurable area is now returned as a piece; the only faces still discarded are those with no area at all (one part in a billion, dropped at the trace), which are numerical noise rather than land. On his Bain tract that takes the result from 3 pieces + a reported 8 sf loss to **5 pieces with nothing lost**. The two crumbs are still NAMED in the toast — *"2 pieces are too small to see (8 sf) — kept, not dropped"* — because an eight-square-foot lot on a hundred-acre plan is invisible and he should know it is there to delete. A notice, not a removal.

**(2) NAMING — AND THE PRIOR ART IS THE HEADLINE (AUDIT-FIRST).** The scheme he asked for **already existed and already matched his answer exactly**: `siteModel.parcelDisplayInfo` has long derived `Parcel 1` → `1A`/`1B`/`1C` → `1A1`/`1A2`, alternating letters and digits by depth, with spreadsheet carry past Z (`birthLetter`: …Y, Z, AA, AB). It is derived from `parentId` lineage, never stored, so it cannot go stale and two siblings cannot draw the same suffix. **So his answers to the three design questions were already the shipped behaviour of the model layer, and none of them was re-litigated:**
- **A piece split again → `1A1` / `1A2`**, not `1A-A` and not a re-letter. Chosen because it is the alternating chain the model already used AND the convention his own appraisal districts use in a legal description (`TR 3A1`), so it is the least surprising of the three by both tests.
- **Past Z → `AA`, `AB`, …** Nothing wraps, nothing collides; asserted at 28 children.
- **No name on the original → `Parcel <n>`**, its position among the roots. That is what an unnamed lot is already called everywhere in the app, so the chain starts from the name he already sees rather than from nothing.

**⛔ WHAT WAS ACTUALLY BROKEN, then — three defects, none of them the numbering scheme.**
1. **THE CANVAS IGNORED IT.** The acreage badge hardcoded `` `Parcel ${acres} ac` `` for every lot. The Parcel panel showed the derived names; the drawing — which is where he looks — showed the word "Parcel" on all of them. From his seat the pieces genuinely were unnamed, and no unit test on the naming function could see it. The badge now reads the resolved name (`Parcel 1A 63.46 ac`). PANEL-BREVITY: this REPLACES the word, it does not add a line.
2. **AN INHERITED ADDRESS NAMED EVERY PIECE THE SAME.** The rule was `label || addr || "Parcel <tag>"` at every depth, and a split COPIES the parent's situs `addr` onto each piece — so cutting an addressed tract in three produced **three parcels displaying one identical name**. Exactly the collision he asked about, and it was live. An inherited address is now ignored for a CHILD; only a name the user TYPED on that piece still wins.
3. **A TYPED NAME DID NOT REACH ITS OWN PIECES.** A parent called "Creek Tract" had children named "Parcel 3A" — the letters restarted off the positional tag instead of extending the name he gave it, which is the one thing his instruction was explicit about. A child's name is now `<parent's name><suffix>`: Creek Tract → Creek Tract A → Creek Tract A1.

**THE SEPARATOR IS TRACKED, NOT GUESSED, and that is worth one line because the obvious rules both fail.** Appending with no space is right after a generated suffix (`Parcel 1A` → `Parcel 1A1`) and wrong after a typed name (`The Wooded Half` → `The Wooded Half 1`). Depth cannot decide it — a typed name can appear at any depth and restarts the question — and neither can the text, since a trailing letter may be a suffix or the last word of a real name. So `nameOf` returns `{ name, suffixed }` and the separator reads the flag.

**LOUD-FAILURE ON A COLLISION.** Derived names cannot collide with each other by construction, but a name the USER typed can duplicate one. `parcelDisplayInfo` publishes `nameCollision` per parcel, and the split reports it against the plan the cut actually produced — *"heads up: "Creek Tract" is now the name of two parcels on this plan — rename one"*. **Reported, never silently renamed:** renaming a parcel he named is not the app's decision.

**COST.** +0.9 KB on the Site route against a clean-tree baseline measured on this machine; no new breach, and the four metrics above baseline were above it on the clean tree too (pre-existing, B329408 / B1064).
### B512672 — Tab on the FIRST item of a list now INDENTS IT, and never invents an empty parent bullet `[Notes]` (feature) #notes #ui  *(owner chat block 2026-08-13 — his ANSWER to the open question B454480 raised, with the instruction "do not ask him again, he considers this asked and answered". Minted **B512672 / V294385** LATE via `git fetch origin main && npm run next-id -- --against-main`, from this branch's reserved block B512672–B512687 · V294384–V294399, against origin/main 768f8c4. **DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open / ⏳ Verify / Done across `Tab`, `indent`, `outdent`, `sinkListItem`, `liftListItem`, `listItem`, `notesTabKey`, `B1392`, `B454480`, `B291536`.** **B454480** is the parent and is the INSTRUMENT — it measured which contexts fail and wrote the rule that Tab could not indent a first item; it is shipped and closed. **B1392 / B1392 ×2** own the key itself and are untouched except for the header rule and one dead branch. This is the BEHAVIOUR CHANGE that instrument's finding asked for, not a recurrence of it. Net-new.)*
`⏳` **Verify — shipped and merged (#1050). Parked for V294385, which is a COURTESY pass: the keystroke check ran here, logged out, so this is a spot-check on a signed-in note rather than a doubt.**
- Verify: sandbox — the document rule in `test/notesListIndent.test.js` (17 cases, real schema + real command) and the KEYSTROKE in `ui-audit/audit-notes-tab.mjs` (33 pinned rows, real Tab, judged by the stored document). Both green. The live pass is V294385 and is a courtesy, not a gate.
- **HIS DECISION, VERBATIM:** *"Tab on the first item of a list INDENTS IT, and does NOT invent an empty parent bullet… build the indent as a level change on the item, not as 'nest under a fabricated parent'."* Rationale he gave: he has twice asked for this to work more like OneNote, where the list renders one level deeper and the user never sees a bullet they did not type.
- **THE RULE, NOW THE MODULE HEADER'S FIRST SENTENCE, as he asked:** **Tab changes the level of the current item; it never creates a node the user did not type.**
- **WHY IT COULD NOT BE DONE BEFORE, and why the model turned out to be able to represent it after all.** A `listItem`'s content is `paragraph block*`, so ProseMirror nests a bullet by making it a CHILD of the bullet above it — and the first bullet has none, so `sinkListItem` declines. He asked to be told LOUDLY if the list model genuinely could not represent a first-item indent without a parent node. **It can, and the answer is not to change the shape at all:** `indent` is a small integer attribute on `listItem` / `taskItem`. Same nodes, same order, same parents, one number different.
- **THAT MAKES HIS CONSTRAINTS TRUE BY CONSTRUCTION RATHER THAN BY CARE.** Nothing is created, so there is no empty parent to assert the absence of. Shift+Tab is `n − 1`, so returning to the original level is exact rather than a repair. At `n === 0` the attribute renders **nothing**, so an indent/outdent pair leaves the stored document byte-identical.
- **THE OPTION THAT WAS REFUSED, recorded so it is not re-proposed:** mint an empty parent bullet and sink into it. It gets the picture right and puts a bullet with no words in it into the document — which then has to be exported, printed, counted, outlined, searched and eventually deleted by hand. This module has spent six rounds removing exactly that litter.
- **REAL NESTING IS NOT REPLACED, it is completed.** Where `sinkListItem` CAN act it still does, and the result is a real nested list exactly as before. The extension asks `can().sinkListItem(...)` and declines — that question IS the boundary between the two mechanisms, answered by the editor rather than by a rule someone wrote down.
- **IT SITS ABOVE THE LIST KEYMAP (priority 200), and that is load-bearing.** `notesTabKey` is a FALLBACK at 50, which is right for Tab and wrong for Shift+Tab: an item at level 2 by attribute is, to ProseMirror, an ordinary first item, so `liftListItem` would lift it clean out of its list while it still owed two outdents.
- **PDF-PARITY, MEASURED NOT ARGUED.** The level is written into the markup (`margin-left` on the ITEM, so the bullet moves with its words), so the print sheet and the HTML export carry it through the one serializer they already share. The harness opens the printed sheet and reads its first bullet — `indented-on-paper`. Markdown carries the level as indentation, which is how Markdown spells nesting, so the export is **not lossy** (asserted: the lossy list is unchanged).
- **FILES.** `lib/notesListIndent.js` (the rule and the two keys) · `lib/notesIndentLevel.js` (the pure reader — split out because `lib/notesMarkdown.js` is on the Notes route's STATIC path and may not pull the engine, the same shape as `lib/notesFileMeta.js`) · `lib/notesTabKey.js` (header rewritten; its list branch is now a backstop) · `lib/notesMarkdown.js`, `lib/notesExtensions.js`.
- **⛔ AND TWO DEFECTS IN THE HARNESS, BOTH OF WHICH FIRST REPORTED THE WORKING FEATURE AS BROKEN.** It named a string the fixture does not contain and **threw away `placeCaret`'s return value**, so a caret that was never placed read as `TAB-DID-NOTHING`; and it asked *"is any bullet empty?"* when the claim was *"did Tab ADD one"* — the fixture deliberately contains an empty nested bullet, so a working feature measured as `NODE-INVENTED`. Both are now in `ui-audit/TRAPS.md` (see B512673).

### B342996 (×3) — A device whose tree is 98 revisions STALE is also flagged dirty, so a merge lets it overwrite newer titles `[Notes]` (bug) #notes #sync  *(owner side-observation, 2026-08-10, read off his live workspace. **Recurrence 2026-08-13: hit independently while building B400176's two-client suite.** **Recurrence 2026-08-13 (×3): the OWNER re-opened it himself — "SECOND OPEN DECISION — B342996, the rename-timestamp question" — and overruled the stamping choice the ×2 pass made.** DEDUPE-FIRST: this takes the ORIGINAL number, not a new one — he named the number, and the promise is unchanged.)*
`⏳` **Verify — shipped and merged (#1050). The title travels, the project travels, and a rename no longer moves "Last edited". Parked for V294384: two signed-in computers is the one thing this sandbox cannot do (`Blocker: auth`).**
- Verify: live  (V294384 — two real computers, his account: rename on one, watch the other)
- Recurrence: 2026-08-13 — reproduced in `test/notesTreeWriteThrough.test.js` against two real store instances, not inferred. A rename pushed from window A was reverted by window B and pushed back up, so the account ended holding the name the owner had just replaced. **A rename could not travel between two machines in either direction.**
- **⛔ THE OWNER'S DECISION (×3), VERBATIM, AND IT OVERRULES THE ONE BELOW: *"stamp renames with their OWN timestamp, separate from the edit timestamp… 'Last edited' keeps meaning what it says: the text changed. A rename must not move it, and the label he sees must not change because someone renamed a note."*** He was right and the ×2 argument was wrong: it reasoned that renaming a note IS editing it, which is defensible in the abstract and false on screen — the page header renders `updatedAt` as **Last edited**, so a note nobody had written a word in for months began claiming it was edited today because somebody fixed its title.
- **WHAT SHIPPED FOR IT.** Three independent stamps, each answering exactly one question: `updatedAt` (the TEXT changed — rendered, moved only by `touchPage`), **`renamedAt`** (the TITLE changed) and **`filedAt`** (the PROJECT changed). The last two are never rendered and are read only to settle their own conflict, in `mergeTrees` rule 3. His other constraints, each as a case: **newest rename wins**; **absent is OLDEST, never newest**, so a machine that has never renamed anything cannot win by default; **when NEITHER side has a stamp the old rule stands (local wins) and the code says so.**
- **⛔ AND THE DEFECT THIS FOUND, which was nowhere near the merge and is the reusable lesson.** `migratePageNode` rebuilds every node from a **named field list**, and every read of the tree goes through it. It did not name the two new fields — so they were written correctly, **destroyed on the next read**, and the merge then compared two absent stamps, called it a tie and kept local: **indistinguishable from the old behaviour, in total silence.** Seven cases went red at the merge; the cause was in the reader. A per-node field must be added to `migratePageNode` in the same commit.
- **GUARDS (×3).** Eight new cases in `test/notesTreeWriteThrough.test.js`: a rename does not move Last edited · a re-file does not either · both stamps survive `migrate` · an older node reads back with no stamps rather than zeros · **his test — two clients, one stale, A renames and B pushes an older tree, in BOTH directions** · a machine with no stamp cannot win by default · **and the mutation check he asked for.** Mutation-proven twice against the real source: restoring `updatedAt` stamping turns **8 red**; making an absent stamp read as *newest* turns **9 red**.
- **THE DECISION THE ×2 PASS TOOK, KEPT AS THE RECORD BECAUSE IT WAS OVERRULED.** The filing named a real either/or: stamp renames (which changes what `updatedAt` means) or add a per-field revision. Stamping `updatedAt` was chosen, on the argument that renaming a note IS editing it. See above for why that was wrong.
- **THE MERGE RULE, AMENDED.** `mergeTrees` rule 3 was an unconditional "the local title wins", justified by the merge only running when this device owes an edit. That does not survive contact with a second page: owing an edit on page X says nothing about page Y's name, and even for X the account may hold a NEWER name typed elsewhere since this device last synced. **The name now comes from whichever side was edited LAST**; a tie or a missing stamp still resolves to LOCAL — the conservative answer, because the copy in front of someone is the one they can see is wrong.
- **THE PROJECT BINDING — was open after ×2, closed by B421493 and given its own `filedAt` stamp here.** The 2026-08-10 filing correctly noted rule 3 covers a page's `projectId` too; ×2 left it deliberately unchanged. Where a page SITS — its parent, its order and its project — stays on rule 4 (local placement wins), which the reachability fuzz (`notesReachability`), `notesProjectIntegrity` and `notesTwoClientConflict` are all built around. Recency is the right rule for a VALUE; it is not obviously the right rule for a STRUCTURE, and changing both in one pass is how a merge's hard-won rules get quietly re-litigated. So: re-filing a note on one computer still does not reach the other. That is the remaining work on this number.
- **GUARDS.** Three cases in `test/notesTreeWriteThrough.test.js` — a rename reaching the other computer and not being undone by it; the LATER of two rival renames winning whichever machine typed it; a tie resolving to the copy in front of you. Mutation-proven: restoring "local always wins" turns three red.
- Origin: filed 2026-08-10 from chat (side observation).
- **THE MEASUREMENT.** His LOCAL tree is at rev **812** with `treeDirty: true` while the CLOUD tree is at rev **910**. Local is 98 revisions behind AND owes the cloud a push at the same time.
- **IS THAT STATE REACHABLE? YES, AND LEGITIMATELY.** `sync.treeRev` records the server rev the last completed seed saw; `treeDirty` records that this device has unpushed structural edits. A device that edits while offline — or whose pushes keep losing the guard — sits in exactly this state. It is not corruption.
- **DOES IT "PUSH BACKWARDS"? NO — AND THAT PART IS REFUTED.** With `treeDirty` set, the seed MERGES rather than adopting (`seed()` → `mergeTrees`), and the merge is a union: nothing on the server side is dropped. The push that follows carries the merged tree guarded on the server's own rev. So the structure cannot regress.
- **WHAT IS GENUINELY AT RISK IS THE TITLE.** `mergeTrees` rule 3 says *"for a node on both sides, the LOCAL title wins"* — reasonable when local is a few seconds stale, wrong when it is 98 revisions stale: a rename made on another device is silently reverted by a device that has not caught up. Same for a page's project binding, which rule 3 also covers.
- **WHY IT WAS NOT FIXED IN THE FIRST PASS (2026-08-10), kept as the record.** The obvious repair — take the LATER edit — could not be done with what the model stored: `renameNode` did not stamp `updatedAt` (only body saves did, through `touchPage`), so there was no timestamp to arbitrate a title with. That diagnosis was exactly right, and the decision it was waiting on is taken above.
- **THE HAZARD IT ACTUALLY CAUSED IS ALREADY CLOSED.** The stale-merge condition is what made B342992's two holes reachable in practice; both are fixed and property-tested. This item is the remaining, narrower risk.


### B371362 — The header offered a centred slot the jurisdiction pill could not use, so the pill went blank with room beside it `[Site Planner / UI]` (bug) #site-planner #ui  *(filed 2026-08-13 while shipping B367298; owner instruction 2026-08-13: "Ship it… but your reason for NOT blind-patching it is exactly right and must survive into the fix." **DEDUPE-FIRST** — this is inside **B371361**'s centring work and deliberately does NOT re-open it: that item's symmetric bound is CORRECT, is untouched here, and is now asserted as geometry in the same run. Not B367298 either — that item's rung ladder behaves correctly given the width it is granted; this is about the width being granted.)*
`[ ]` **⏳ IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-13 — rides V162864.**
- Verify: live → **V162864** (`Blocker: auth` + `browser-egress`)
- **⛔ FIRST, THE GUARD THAT HAD TO SURVIVE, because patching around it is how this repo breaks the same thing twice.** `headerCenterFit` exists because the chip was centred inside its SLOT while the slot was `flex: 1 1 0%` leftover space between the breadcrumb and the account controls — so the chip's position was a function of how long the project and plan names were (measured 94 px right of true centre at 1600 px). B371361 pinned the slot OUT OF FLOW at the row's midpoint so the side groups keep their natural widths and NAVIGATION WINS is untouched. Out of flow, nothing stops the pill running over the plan chip's ▾ caret — the defect it had just closed — so `centerSlotMaxWidth` is the replacement bound: the slot is SYMMETRIC about the midpoint, so its width is limited by the WIDER side group plus a gap. Below `CENTER_SLOT_MIN` it returns `tight` and the slot goes back in flow, off-centre but readable.
- **⛔ SO NEITHER SIDE WAS AT FAULT, AND THAT IS THE FINDING.** The bound is right. The pill's fallback to pin-only is right. **The verdict BETWEEN them was decided against a CONSTANT while the quantity it stands for is a VARIABLE:** `CENTER_SLOT_MIN` is 120 px — the width of the word "Unincorporated" — and the least width at which a pill can still say something TRUE depends on the label. Measured on the real header with the owner's own side groups:

  | width | mode | offered | pill needs | shown |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | 1100 | centered | 236 | 200 | `Part in City of Baytown limits +2` |
  | **1000** | **centered** | **136** | **199** | **(blank — pin only)** |
  | 980 | tight | in flow | 199 | the WHOLE label |

  A slot the content cannot use is not a centred chip; it is an empty space where a chip used to be — and one band lower the fallback the same work already built shows everything.
- **THE FIX: the content declares the threshold.** The pill publishes the width of its shortest true rung on `data-center-min-fit` (a function of its TEXT, never of the width it is granted, so it cannot feed back on the layout that reads it); `AppHeader` passes it to `centerSlotPlan` as `min`. `centerSlotPlan` already took `min` as a parameter — **its shape did not change, and `centerSlotMaxWidth` was not touched.** Anything that declares nothing gets the constant and behaves exactly as before. Result: 1040 and 1000 now go `tight` and show the whole label; 1100 stays centred with a rung that fits.
- **⛔ MEASUREMENT CORRECTED FROM THE B367298 REPORT.** That item recorded "38 px beside a 453 px spacer at 980 px". Re-measured against current `main`, 980 px is now `tight` and shows the full label — the 38 px was the zone's CONTENT width with the pill already blank, not the offer, and the band moved as the centring work landed. The real starvation band is **~1000–1040 px, offering 136 px**. The earlier number is superseded; the symptom the owner reported was real.
- **BOTH RULES ASSERTED IN THE SAME RUN, and each mutation-proven** (`npm run verify:jurbadge`, **129/129** across 8 widths × 2 themes × 8 labels): ignoring the declared minimum → *"header stayed CENTRED offering 136 px while the pill declared it needs 199 px"* · replacing the symmetric bound with the NARROWER side (i.e. buying the pill's room back from the crumb) → *"the pill OVERLAPS the plan switcher by 63.8 px — B371361's defect is back"*. The check that fails a pill going blank **with room to spare** is kept and still green.
- Guards: the repo-root `test/` suite **headerCenterSlot** (5 new, incl. a value-pin so "just give the centre a bit more" cannot be done quietly, and a both-ends wiring check) + the ui-audit harness **verify-jurisdiction-badge-shapes**.

### B505664 — NO-ONE-OWNS-A-COMPOSITE: name the pattern that produced three defects in one day `[Docs / rules]` (task) #infra #testing  *(owner instruction 2026-08-14, after the Doc Review audit: "that pattern deserves a named entry in the repo's rules if it does not have one yet." Minted **B505664** from this branch's block B505664–B505679 against `origin/main` 2999b1e. **DEDUPE-FIRST — checked all 19 existing named rules in `/CLAUDE.md`: LOUD-FAILURE · AUDIT-FIRST · PDF-PARITY · MODULE-SCOPE-COMPONENTS · VIEWPORT-STABLE · CHROME-NEVER-EATS-A-PRESS · FOREGROUND-OR-VOID · DRIVER-SCROLL-IS-NOT-APP-SCROLL · COUNT-EVERY-KIND · SYNTHETIC-KEYS-DONT-EDIT · PERCEPTUAL-PARITY · DEDUPE-FIRST · TOMBSTONE-DELETES · TIER-BY-REBUILDABILITY · ROWS-CANONICAL-ON-SEED · DANGEROUS-MEANS-UNOBSERVABLE · LIVE-VERIFY · PANEL-BREVITY · VIEW-INDEPENDENT-ONCE.** None covers it. **COUNT-EVERY-KIND is the closest and is the INSTRUMENT half** — the rule that certified the road pavement green. Net-new.)*
`[x]` **SHIPPED.**
- Verify: sandbox — the entry is prose; its guard is a source assertion, mutation-proven two ways.
- **THE PATTERN, named because it surfaced THREE times in one day and each instance was found by accident rather than by looking.** A surface built from several objects at once — a dissolved region, a merged outline, a union, a **cached raster** — is owned by NONE of them, so no per-object predicate can reach it and no feature census can see it.
- **THE OPERATIVE LINE: the guard is INK OR PIXELS, never REGISTRATIONS.** A census counts things that registered themselves (`data-feature` keys, `[data-el-id]` nodes, model entries); a composite registers nothing, so it is invisible to every count by construction.
- **⛔ WHY IT IS NAMED BESIDE `COUNT-EVERY-KIND` RATHER THAN FOLDED INTO IT.** That rule guarantees you counted every FAMILY of object and is the closest thing the repo had, so the next reader reaches for it and believes they are covered. They are not: it is the instrument half, and it is *the very rule that certified the road pavement green* — every road's own node correctly left the canvas, `4 drawn → 0`, ✓, while four unbroken grey ribbons stayed on the drawing.
- **THE THREE INSTANCES carry the entry's own evidence:** **B3296** the dissolved road pavement · **B494050** the export crop framing the printed sheet from the whole model · **B503184** Doc Review's cached sharp tile holding **579,121** blue pixels of a switched-off PDF layer, exactly that shape's share of the page.
- **⛔ THE SHAPE THEY SHARE, and it is why each survived review: IN EVERY ONE THE PER-OBJECT SIDE WAS CORRECT AND LOOKED CORRECT.** The filter was applied, the predicate asked, the object's node left the DOM, the unit tests passed. "I checked the filter" is not evidence for this class.
- **AND THE PREFERRED TEETH PROOF, recorded from B503184:** point the new check at UNTOUCHED code and require it to go RED there BEFORE writing the fix — stronger than planting a synthetic defect, which only proves the check can see the thing you built it to see.
- **⚠ PROSE, WITH PER-INSTANCE GUARDS, and the entry says so plainly rather than implying a detector exists.** "Is this surface a composite?" is not decidable from source. `test/compositeSurfaceRule.test.js` (15) guards the ENTRY: the rule is still stated, its operative line survives, it still names where COUNT-EVERY-KIND stops, it still carries its three instances — and **every guard it cites still exists and is non-trivial**, because a rule whose evidence has been deleted reads as covered. Mutation-proven both ways (strip the operative line → red; rename the COUNT-EVERY-KIND relationship → red).


### B503184 — Doc Review's Layers toggle hid nothing you could see: the sharp tile painted over the backdrop was never re-rendered `[Doc Review]` (bug) #doc-review #ui #testing  *(owner instruction 2026-08-14: run the B3296/B494048 audit on Doc Review, but establish first what "hidden" MEANS here rather than transplanting the planner's model. Minted **B503184 / V287376** from this branch's block B503184–B503199 against `origin/main` 09d9cf9d. **DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open / ⏳ Verify / Done across `B490`, `ocg`, `optionalContentConfig`, `renderDetail`, `tileCovers`, `B415`, `B489a`, `detailTile`, `contentVisibility`, `B3296`, `B494048`.** **B490** SHIPPED this feature and its own unit tests (`ocg.js`) pass on the broken build, because the config really is mutated correctly and only the raster is stale. **B415** introduced the backdrop/detail split and **tileCovers** with it; this is that cache meeting a content change it was never told about. Net-new.)*
`[x]` **SHIPPED.**
- Verify: **live** — `V287376`, `Blocker: real-data`.
- **⛔ THE PRIOR QUESTION FIRST, because the planner's model does NOT transfer.** Doc Review's markups carry **no visibility concept at all** — the shared markup engine has no `hidden`, no per-object filter, no layer assignment — so the planner's question ("which reads of our collection forget the predicate") is **degenerate here: there is no predicate to forget.** What markups have instead is the PAGE, and every path that matters is already page-scoped deliberately: `pageMarks` is the draw set, `eraseInBox` guards `m.page !== page`, B569's net drops off-page selection ids, and `arrange.js` takes the global array on purpose and derives same-page peers internally. Those are **correct and are recorded as correct** in `lib/layerVisibilityReads.js`, beside the ones that are correctly WHOLE-document (the takeoff `rollup`, the saved snapshot, the undo state).
- **FOUR OF THE SEVEN ARTEFACT CATEGORIES DO NOT EXIST IN THIS WORKSPACE, and that is the answer, not a gap:** Doc Review has **no export or print path**, **no thumbnails** (the sheet rail is text rows and skeletons), and **no text search** (`jumpTo` walks detected CHANGES in Compare; `goToPage` is sheet navigation). Nothing to audit in any of them.
- **THE ONE REAL HIDE is the PDF optional-content ("layer") toggle (B490)**, and it is a different mechanism: it hides part of the immutable PDF **backdrop**, pdf.js performs the hiding through the `OptionalContentConfig` passed to `page.render`, and nothing is persisted (the group ids are per-load refs). So the only way our code can get it wrong is to render without that config — **or to serve a CACHED raster made before the toggle.** It was the second.
- **THE DEFECT, measured on a two-layer PDF.** `renderDetail` opens with `if (tileCovers(detailTileRef.current, reg.visible, v.scale)) return` — a cache check that asks *"does the tile I already have cover this view at this scale"* and knows nothing about the drawing's CONTENT changing underneath it. Toggling a layer off re-entered it and it returned immediately. **The detail tile paints ON TOP of the backdrop, so the layer the user just switched off was still what they were looking at — at rest, not only on zoom.** The backdrop correctly dropped to **0** blue pixels while the tile above it held **579,121**, which is 12.2% of the tile and exactly the hidden square's share of the page.
- **THE FIX IS THE FILE'S OWN EXISTING RULE, applied to the case it missed.** Every other change to what the tile should contain already invalidates it — a new document, a page or size change, a clear. Visibility was the one mutation that did not. `toggleLayer` now drops the retained tile; `tileCovers(null, …)` is false, so the next render is forced.
- **⛔ THE TEETH PROOF IS AGAINST A REAL SHIPPED DEFECT, NOT A SYNTHETIC MUTANT.** The harness was written before the fix and ran **RED on unmodified `origin/main`** — 2 of 10 arms, naming the pixel counts. Both guards are then mutation-proven by reverting the one line: the browser harness goes 10/10 → 8/10 and the source guard 10 → 8. Every setup arm is a **vacuity guard** that exits rather than scoring if the fixture cannot show the effect (no Layers control · no listed groups · no blue at baseline · a detail tile that never rendered).
- **⚠ THE HONEST LIMIT, and it bounds how much this matters:** whether the owner's OWN drawings carry optional content is **unknown from here** — his 30 source PDFs live in Supabase Storage / Drive and the bytes are not reachable from this sandbox (SQL reaches the metadata rows, never the objects). If none of them has layers, the Layers control never appears for him and this surface is empty in practice. **That is the first step of `V287376`, not something any code here can answer.** The fixture is therefore a hand-built two-layer PDF, which is legitimate because the question — does OUR render path honour the config — is a property of our code, not of his files.
- **Bundle:** against the base ref `09d9cf9d` built from a clean worktree — site route 2488.4 → **2488.1 KB**, largest chunk **unchanged at 1566.3 KB**. The four metrics above baseline are identical on the base ref; no new breach.
- **Guards:** `test/docReviewLayerVisibility.test.js` (10 — the invalidation source guard, the render-path declaration table covering every `page.render` call site, and a mutation check reading the REAL pre-fix body from the pinned commit `09d9cf9d` rather than a paraphrase) · `ui-audit/verify-pdf-layer-hiding.mjs` (`npm run verify:pdflayers`, 10/10, mutation-proven).

So the guard is now INK: `ui-audit/lib/inkCensus.mjs` walks every painted node in the drawing and attributes it to the feature it draws for, reading `data-road-cluster` so unowned ink is attributable at all, and reporting anything it CANNOT attribute by selector rather than dropping it.

The KMZ path is deliberately untouched and is **not** a gap — a model-built export decides its own contents and never inherits a canvas display toggle (`kmzExport.js`'s own rule, guarded by `test/kmzExport.test.js`).

### B3297 — Delete did nothing on a selected area measurement: a slider and a dropdown were eating the key, and the second press said nothing at all `[Site Planner / keyboard]` (bug) #site-planner #keyboard #selection #ui #testing  *(owner chat 2026-08-13, arrived as NEW-2: "I was pressing delete on it, and it was not deleting." An AREA measurement, inspector open (MEASUREMENT · AREA, 98,501 sf / 2.26 ac), handles drawn. Minted **B3297 / V2577** LATE against fresh main. **DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open / ⏳ Verify / Done across `keyScope`, `keyContract`, `focusScope`, `B464048`, `B746`, `V258`, `B1215`, `deletePlan`, `B743`, `B154`, `SYNTHETIC-KEYS-DONT-EDIT`, `B304178`.** **B464048** shipped the scope model hours earlier and was the leading suspect — **it is NOT the cause, proven by measurement below.** **B746/V258** is the closest relative: it carved undo/redo out of the slider guard for precisely the reason that generalises here, and stopped one key short. **B743/deletePlan** made delete unconditional and never silent INSIDE `deleteSel`; this key never reached `deleteSel`. **B1215** made a field-swallowed Delete audible, and its once-per-episode rule is half of what is fixed here. Net-new.)*
`[x]` **SHIPPED.**
- Verify: **live** — `V2577`, `Blocker: real-data` (his signed-in tab).
- **⛔ NOT A REGRESSION FROM TODAY'S WORK, and this was established BEFORE anything was changed, because the brief named it as the leading hypothesis.** The pre-#1010 build (`609eb6f^`) was checked out, built and driven through the identical arms: the slider refusal reproduces **identically** there. The old guard asked `tagName === "INPUT" || "SELECT" || "TEXTAREA"`, and a range input and a dropdown are both in that list — B746/V258's own comment states it outright ("Every OTHER shortcut … still respects the guard while a slider has focus"). The scope model INHERITED this defect; it did not introduce it. **B464048's own data-loss fix is intact and re-proven dead in the same run.**
- **THE MEASUREMENT, on his plan, with the measurement selected and its inspector open:**

      after touching…                        press   focus          result
      nothing / a plain button in the panel   Delete  BUTTON, BODY   ✓ deleted
      the Fill opacity SLIDER                 Delete  INPUT[range]   ❌ refused ("belongs to the slider")
      the Line style DROPDOWN                 Delete  SELECT         ❌ refused ("the box you're typing in")
      a value row's text box                  Delete  INPUT[text]    ✓ correctly refused — you ARE typing
      the same, pressed a SECOND time         Delete  INPUT[text]    ❌ refused in TOTAL SILENCE

- **THREE DEFECTS, one report.** (a) A range input does nothing at all with Delete or Backspace, and a closed `<select>` does not either — so the keys went nowhere and the object stayed on the drawing. (b) The dropdown's refusal named *"the box you're typing in"* about a control with no text in it. (c) **The second press was silent**, because the hint is keyed once per episode — so a user who did not catch the first toast experiences a key that does nothing, repeatedly, without explanation. That is the LOUD-FAILURE violation the hint was added to close, surviving inside the hint's own de-duplication, and it is exactly what *"I was pressing delete"* — plural — describes.
- **THE FIX INVERTS THE DEFAULT.** The old rule was "refuse everything, with an allow-list of exceptions" (`allowOnSlider`, added by B746 for undo/redo alone) — the wrong default, because every key a control cannot use has to be added by hand, one bug report at a time. Now each control scope declares the SHORT list it genuinely consumes (`CONTROL_CONSUMES`: a slider takes the arrows; a dropdown takes arrows, Enter, Space, Escape and the type-ahead letters) and everything else passes. **B746/V258's carve-out is not lost — it stops being a carve-out**, because a slider does not consume ⌘Z under this rule either. `<select>` became its own `SCOPE.PICKER` and left `TEXT_ENTRY_TAGS`. A destructive key now explains itself on **every** press; everything else keeps the once-per-episode rule.
- **AND THE LATCH, which is why the fix holds after focus moves on.** The `FIELD` latch outlives the field's focus by design (that is B464048's whole insight) but it was keyed on the ROW — and `data-field-group` marks every value row, including rows whose only control is a slider or a dropdown. Touching one latched *"the user is typing a number"* about a control with no digits in it. A row is a typing row only if it holds something you can type in; the Depth row does, and is unchanged.
- **⛔ THE CONTROLS ARE THE POINT, and they are in the same run.** Narrowing a guard built to stop a Backspace destroying the owner's building is only safe if that defect is re-proven dead: **Enter-, Escape- and Tab-out-of the real Depth (ft) row, each followed by Backspace, all leave the building and its bonded elements untouched (43 → 43 features).** Nothing in this change reaches the text-field scope.
- **Guards:** `test/keyContract.test.js` (**53**, incl. the property "neither a slider nor a dropdown may swallow Delete", the non-typing-row latch cases, and B746/V258 re-asserted as a consequence rather than a special case) · `ui-audit/verify-delete-key-scope.mjs` (`npm run verify:deletescope`) — **10/10 arms**, real key events per SYNTHETIC-KEYS-DONT-EDIT, re-read until settled, and **7 of those 10 red on the pre-fix build**.


### B487600 — Deleting a picture from one plan DESTROYED it in every plan sharing it — a ref-count that could only see the current plan `[Site Planner / storage]` (bug, data-loss) #site-planner #persistence #files #sync  *(found 2026-08-13 from the owner's report "it's saying that it's not available"; the bytes for his Woods Road overlay are GONE. Minted **B487600** from this branch's reserved block B487600–B487615 against `origin/main` 79be535. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open / ⏳ Verify / Done across `overlay`, `storageKey`, `idbKey`, `deleteOverlayObject`, `B72`, `B461`, `B474`, `B784`, `B785`, `B1427`, `TOMBSTONE-DELETES`, `orphan`: **B461** introduced the SHARED reference on Duplicate/Paste and added the current-plan ref-count that is the defect; **B474 #23** added the idb half of that same wrong-scoped count; **B784/B785** classify a MISSING object on READ (the symptom this produced) and never ask who else holds it; **B1427** is the tiering rule, not ownership. No item owns cross-plan asset ownership. Net-new.)*
`[x]` **SHIPPED — ⏳ awaiting live confirmation (V278320).**
- Verify: live — real Supabase Storage + a signed-in account with two plans sharing one source file. `Blocker: auth`.
- **⛔ THE BYTES WERE ALREADY LOST WHEN THIS WAS FILED. This is not a hypothetical.** Plan `smsrrlk9u576` ("Concept A 1M SF", Woods Road) still carries an overlay record naming `…/site-overlays/smsrrlk9u576/e1454691snsene.png` with `src: null`; `storage.objects` holds **zero** rows for it. There is no bucket versioning and database point-in-time restore does not cover storage bytes, so it is unrecoverable from the cloud. **Six further plans were armed the same way at fix time — Goose Creek (FOUR plans sharing one site-plan PDF) and Bain (two).**
- **THE MECHANISM.** `⧉ Duplicate plan` does `saveSite({ ...src, id })`, copying each overlay record WHOLESALE — `storageKey` (cloud object) and `idbKey` (device raster) included. Two plans then point at ONE set of bytes. Every delete path ref-counted that share against `sheetOverlays`, **the current plan's overlay list**, which by construction cannot see the sibling. So removing the picture from the duplicate hard-deleted the original's image out of **both tiers at once**.
- **EVERY OPERATION THAT PRODUCES A SHARED REFERENCE, enumerated — the fix covers all of them, not just duplicate:** `duplicatePlan` (sheetOverlays, both tiers) · `newPlanSameParcel` (`underlay: src.underlay` — the aerial backdrop, whose delete path had **no ref-count at all**) · `copyOverlay`/`placeOverlayCopy` (B461, within and ACROSS plans). **RENAME does not** — `renameSiteGroup` patches `{ id, site, siteRenamedAt }` on the same plan and creates nothing; it was checked because the owner thought he may have renamed rather than duplicated. Sharing can only arise from the three copy paths.
- **⛔ THE BIGGER BLAST RADIUS, same bug one tier down.** `deleteSite` evicted `raster:<siteId>:*` by PREFIX, and a duplicate carries the SOURCE plan's `idbKey` — so deleting the SOURCE plan wiped the device copy for every plan copied from it. The sweep is kept (it is what evicts genuine orphans) but now SPARES every key a surviving plan names (`idbDeleteByPrefix(prefix, { keep })`).
- **THE FIX, three rules** (`lib/sharedAssetRefs.js`): the ref-count spans EVERY plan, never the current one · an UNKNOWN answer releases nothing (an orphaned object costs storage, a destroyed one costs the owner's work) · both tiers are released together or neither.
- **⛔ AND THE DATABASE IS THE AUTHORITY, because the client's list is only ever best-effort.** It knows what THIS DEVICE has hydrated; a stale tab, a second device or a direct Storage API call all reason from an incomplete list and would orphan the bytes exactly as before. `db/overlay_object_release_guard.sql` is a `BEFORE DELETE` row trigger on `storage.objects` that REFUSES while any plan still references the key (soft-deleted plans COUNT — a binned plan is restorable). **Applied to production 2026-08-13 and proven on the real path:** Supabase's own `protect_delete` blocks direct SQL, so the probe set `storage.allow_delete_query` exactly as the Storage API does — the guard refused and named all four Goose Creek plans; the CONTROL (an unreferenced object) passed through. Neither probe committed anything.
- LOUD-FAILURE: a refusal reports `overlay-asset-retained` / `underlay-asset-retained` / `plan-delete-raster-retained` naming the holders — a kept file is never silent.
- Guards: the repo-root `test/` suite **sharedAssetRefs** (17 — the pre-fix rule REPLAYED verbatim as the mutation check, so the suite fails if the old scope ever passes again, plus source guards on all three call sites and the SQL).
- **Full incident record: `docs/INCIDENT-2026-08-13-shared-asset-delete.md`** — the three sharing paths, the prefix blast radius, how the database guard was proven on the real Storage API path with a discriminating control, the fresh-id restore that dodges the 30-day tombstone, the controlled negative on the owner's own browser, and the two method lessons (a UA string is not a device identity; the version ring is the better first-party witness).
- **Owner data restored in the same session:** the plan he could not find (`smsrpaiqu5sv`) was soft-deleted, intact, and is back as `smt0rwoodsa1` "Concept A (restored)" — **a NEW id deliberately, because his device holds a durable 30-day delete tombstone for the old one that would have re-issued the delete on his next pull.** 30 elements, the 1,675' × 613' building included. It carries **no roads — it never had any**; the four deleted roads belong to `smsrrlk9u576` and were left deleted at the owner's explicit instruction.
### B367298 — The pill cut a jurisdiction MID-WORD on the two longest labels, and its shortener could not save them `[Site Planner / UI]` (bug) #site-planner #ui  *(filed 2026-08-11 as the residual of B367296; owner instruction 2026-08-13, verbatim: "Do not leave it filed and unbuilt… trailing off into an ellipsis is still the app deciding, silently, that you do not need to see something. A truncated jurisdiction is missing information wearing the costume of a complete label." **DEDUPE-FIRST, and it matters here: B371361 shipped a fix for this surface WHILE this item was open** — the "navigation wins" layout plus `abbreviateJurisdiction`, from a different owner report (the pill covering the plan switcher). That work is correct, is kept, and is NOT re-opened; this item is the case it does not cover, found by driving it in a browser. Re-typed (task) → (bug) on the owner's instruction.)*
`[ ]` **⏳ IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-13 — rides V162864, which covers B367296 and this on one live look.**
- Verify: live → **V162864** (`Blocker: auth` + `browser-egress`, both measured — see the note there)
- **THE DECISION, STATED, AND WHAT WAS REJECTED.**
  - **CHOSEN — a LADDER of complete-facts forms, ending in nothing.** Rung 1 the full line · rung 2 the governing fact + "+N" (B371361's form) · rung 3 the same without its parenthetical qualifier · rung 4 the bare governing identity + "+N" · rung 5 **nothing but the pin**. Every rung is a true, whole statement; the complete label is always in the tooltip and in `data-jurisdiction-full`.
  - **Rung 5 is deliberate.** Below a certain width no true statement about a split jurisdiction fits, and the alternatives are a fragment ("Part in City of Bayto…", which reads as a different answer) or dropping the qualifier that carries the meaning ("City of Baytown", which claims the WHOLE site is in it). Showing nothing is the only one of the three that cannot mislead, and it costs nothing — the hover still has every word. It is "navigation wins" followed to its end.
  - **REJECTED — wrap to a second line** (the row's height is fixed and B1173's two-row header is hard-won; a tag that reflows the chrome while a window edge is dragged is a worse trade than a hover). **REJECTED — a CSS ellipsis on the whole line** (that IS the defect). **REJECTED — per-priority spans with graded `flex-shrink`** (built and measured: a heavily-shrunk band collapses to ZERO width and renders no ellipsis at all — a shorter label with no sign anything was left out, i.e. this item's own defect from the other direction).
- **⛔ THE DEFECT, MEASURED IN A BROWSER, AND WHY THE SHIPPED GUARD COULD NOT SEE IT.** `test/headerNavPriority` reads the SOURCE, and the source was right. The failure is a property of ONE label SHAPE: a split site's governing chain was built as a single pre-joined slot (`"Part in City of Baytown limits (full purpose, 6 of 14 lots) · rest in its ETJ"`), so `abbreviateJurisdiction` had nothing to drop and its "short" form was ~330 px in a ~150 px box. The pill fell back to a CSS ellipsis and cut it mid-word, on the owner's two longest labels — **Goose Creek and Tsakiris, at 761 and 860 px**.
- **TWO FIXES, AND ONLY THE SECOND MAKES A FRAGMENT IMPOSSIBLE.** (1) a split contributes its two governing facts as two SLOTS — the label text is byte-identical, the shortener finally has something to drop, and the "+N" count is right for the first time (it read "+2" for three hidden facts); (2) the rung ladder above.
- **THE MEASUREMENT THAT COST THE MOST, recorded so it is not rebuilt three more times: "how much room do I have" must not be a function of the text.** Three readings failed first — `host.clientWidth` while the zone is `flex: 0 1 auto` (the zone IS its content, so the comparison degenerates to `shown <= shown` and the label **ratchets down and never comes back**: shortest rung at 860 px, still shortest at 1440 px) · row width minus the siblings' content (content-independent, but not what flex grants once the row is over-subscribed — too generous, the pill overflowed) · step DOWN a rung on each clip (terminates, but every step changes the layout, so it overshot and sat blank with room to spare). The shipped reading asks the ZONE: its measured `max-width` when it is out of flow (centred mode), and its granted width with the span briefly filled with the FULL label when it is in flow.
- **PROVEN, in a real browser** (`npm run verify:jurbadge` — the real `AppHeader` + `JurisdictionBadge` over the real identify chain, 6 widths × 2 themes × 8 labels incl. Goose Creek and Tsakiris, down to **761 px**, the width just above `AppHeader`'s phone gate below which the row scrolls and nothing clips): **97/97**. **Mutation-proven**: restoring B371361's binary shortener reproduces the mid-word cut on exactly the labels the audit flagged (split · Tsakiris · Goose Creek at 761 and 860). The harness also asserts the floor is honest — a blank pill is allowed ONLY when the granted width is smaller than its shortest true form, so "give up early" is a failure, not a style.
- **⚠ THE TWO-SLOT HALF IS NOT MUTATION-PROVEN AND SAYS SO.** Re-joining the slots does not turn the harness red, because the ladder's later rungs absorb it; it is right on its own terms (a correct "+N", and one more rung of information at narrow widths), not because a check would catch its loss.
- **⛔ AND ONE FINDING THAT IS NOT MINE TO FIX, FLAGGED RATHER THAN SILENTLY LEFT — see B371362.** Between roughly 940 and 1000 px the header's centring measurement grants the badge almost nothing while the row is half empty: measured at 980 px, zones `[398, 38, 453, 128]` in a 980 px row — the pill squeezed to **38 px** with a **453 px** spacer beside it. The pill then correctly falls to pin-only, for the wrong reason. That is the centring measurement in `AppHeader` (B371361's own work, with its own guard), not the label, and blind-patching another session's freshly-shipped layout guard is how this repo breaks things twice.
- Guards: the repo-root `test/` suites **jurisdictionBadgeRungs** (17) and **headerNavPriority** (three of its assertions AMENDED, each with its reason recorded in the test itself — the rule is unchanged, the premise about a split's pre-joined lead is what was wrong), plus the ui-audit harness **verify-jurisdiction-badge-shapes**.
### B484337 — The tab stops saving and the screen says "synced" `[Site Planner / persistence · UI]` (bug, DATA LOSS) #site-planner #sync #ui  *(found 2026-08-13 answering the owner's "prove a refusal is genuinely visible on the running app rather than from the code — this repo's signature defect is a mechanism that looks right and never fires". It never fired. Minted **B484337** from the same reserved block. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open / ⏳ Verify / Done across `client-stale`, `conflictToasts`, `saveState`, `elemSync`, `LOUD-FAILURE`, `B671`, `B673`, `B465`, `B209`, `B595`, `B610`: **B671** wired the engine into the save badge and named `failed`/`syncing`/`retrying` — it never named `stale`; **B673** built the toast matrix including this row, and the row was correct. Nothing owns the delivery. **Net-new.**)*
`[x]` **SHIPPED** — parks in ⏳ Verify (V273520) for the signed-in click-through.
- Verify: live — the stale state needs a signed-in cloud session, and this sandbox's proxy answers `403 to CONNECT` for the Supabase host, so no browser here can reach it.
- Origin: filed 2026-08-13 from the owner's chat instruction.
- **⛔ THIS WAS PRE-EXISTING AND USER-FACING. IT IS NOT A SIDE EFFECT OF THE GROUP-CAS WORK, AND
  THAT IS WHAT MAKES IT THE MOST VALUABLE THING IN THIS BATCH.** The silence sits on the
  already-shipped NEW-3 rejected-op streak (`elementSync.js:768`), which has been live in the
  product the whole time; group CAS merely adds a second door into the same state. It was FOUND
  while arming that feature — because the owner asked for proof that a refusal is visible on the
  running app rather than read out of the code — but it was not CAUSED by it, and it would have
  gone on losing saves silently whether stage 2 ever shipped or not.
- **⛔ AND IT IS THE WORST SHAPE A DEFECT TAKES IN THIS CODEBASE: NOT AN ERROR, AN ANSWER THAT IS
  CONFIDENTLY WRONG.** A visible failure gets investigated; a green "synced" badge over a tab that
  has stopped writing gets trusted. Same family, and the list is long enough now to be a pattern
  rather than a coincidence: the scheduler group header reading **0d** for a real span (B463072),
  the Layers panel showing a green **loaded** light over a map drawing nothing (B323424 — *"those
  rows showed a green loaded dot over an empty map, which is worse than the case that was
  reported"*), the jurisdiction label being CHOPPED and its lead re-parsed to pick a floodplain rule
  (B367297), and `deriveZoning` asserting Texas law in Colorado (B290240). Every one of them
  answers, and the answer is wrong. LOUD-FAILURE exists for exactly this.
- **TWO INDEPENDENT SWALLOWS, and neither is in the sync engine.** (1) `SitePlanner.jsx`'s sync-event handler opened `if (!kind || !id) return;` — correct for every row of the B673 matrix, all of which are about one element, and fatal for the one event that is about the whole plan: `client-stale` carries neither. The toast was built, mapped, unit-tested and dropped before `pushToast`. (2) The save badge named `failed`, `syncing` and `retrying` and not `stale`, so a tab that had GIVEN UP landed on the resting case and painted green "synced".
- **`stale` IS WORSE THAN `failed`, which is the part that was missed.** `failed` means a commit did not land and the engine is still trying; `stale` means it issues no further commit until `retryNow()` or a reload.
- **LIVE TODAY, not a group-CAS bug.** The same silence sits on the already-shipped NEW-3 rejected-op streak (`elementSync.js:768`); group CAS merely adds a second door to it.
- Guard: `test/staleVisible.test.js` — the engine half is BEHAVIOURAL (the real engine is driven to `stale` and its event caught, asserting it carries no kind/id); the rendering half is a source check, stated as weaker than a click-through rather than passed off as one. Both halves mutation-proven.

### B463920 — The Enter that accepted the successor prompt re-opened the status menu it had just closed `[Scheduler]` (bug) #scheduler #ui  *(owner chat block 2026-08-13 from a live screenshot, Permitting/Entitlements → SIA. Minted **B463920 / V258864** LATE against fresh main. **DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open / ⏳ Verify / Done across `overlayOpenRef`, `successorPrompt`, `HealthPicker`, `StatusPicker`, `picker`, `Enter`, `B456208`, `B443536`: nothing owns overlay key ownership.** Net-new.)*
`[x]` **SHIPPED.** `public/sequence/index.html` — the key guard latches in capture.
- Verify: **live** — `V258864`, `Blocker: auth` + `real-data`.
- Evidence: `ui-audit/verify-grid-overlay-input.mjs` **12/12** · `test/menuPortalIsolation.test.js` (9).

**⛔ BOTH REPORTED HYPOTHESES ARE WRONG, and the measurement is the item.** The menu is not "never told to close" and the prompt does not "steal the closing event". The menu **closes correctly** — control: with no prompt in play, picking a swatch left a menu up **0/9**. What happens is that the **Enter which dismisses the prompt is handled twice**: the modal applies and closes, and the same keystroke then reaches the grid's document-level handler, which by design opens the picker on a picker column (`Enter on a picker column opens its picker`) and fires a **synthetic click on the dot** — captured as `HTMLDocument.onKey → HTMLElement.click()`, `isTrusted=false`. The menu in the screenshot is **a second menu**, opened by the keystroke that dismissed the prompt. The signature is the proof and is now a test: **Enter 7/7 left a menu open · Escape 0/7 · ✕ 0/7**, because only Enter maps to a picker action.

**THE GUARD EXISTED AND ASKED THE WRONG QUESTION.** `overlayOpenRef` bails while an overlay is open, but it reads **false** for the one keystroke that dismissed it — the modal has already closed itself synchronously by then. Fixed by **latching the answer in capture** (`window` capture runs before React's root handler and before the document handler), so the question becomes *"did this keystroke BEGIN while an overlay owned the keyboard?"*.

**WHY NOT "THE MODAL SWALLOWS THE KEY" (option a).** That fixes `SuccessorPromptModal`. **Thirteen** overlays feed that ref, and the next one added arrives with the same hole — the defect is in the question the guard asks, not in one modal's manners. The latch covers all thirteen by construction and needs nothing from any modal.

**THE FEATURE SURVIVES, ASSERTED AS LOUDLY AS THE BUG.** With no overlay in play, Enter on a picker column still opens the picker. Mutation M3 (killing the cell's mousedown to "fix" NEW-2) turns that assertion **red**, so it is load-bearing rather than decorative.

**MUTATIONS: revert the latch → Enter back to 4/4 with Escape and ✕ still 0/4** (the asymmetry reproduces exactly) · unit: live-ref-only guard · latch on bubble instead of capture → one distinct assertion red each.

### B456208 — The Owner field turned any typo into a person, silently `[Scheduler]` (feature) #scheduler #ui #persistence  *(owner chat block 2026-08-13, arrived as the answer to a question this session raised off the B443536 sweep — his instruction, verbatim: *"YES - make it ask before adding a new contact.
