That is the same shape as everything else this repo keeps producing: something that looks like an answer without anyone having decided it."* Minted **B456208 / V251152** LATE via `git fetch origin main && npm run next-id -- --against-main`, from this branch's reserved block B456208–B456223 · V251152–V251167; code and tests keep the provisional `NEW-1` label. **DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open / ⏳ Verify / Done across `ContactPicker`, `commitTyped`, `ensureContacts`, `contacts`, `registry`, `auto-add`, `confirm`, `B443536`, `B291538`, `B865`, `B418`.** **B443536** is the parent — it fixed the CARET in this same component and its data sweep is what exposed this — but it is a different defect (a character eaten by a selection) and is NOT re-opened; this is the create-on-commit behaviour beside it. Nothing else owns contact creation. Net-new.)*
`[x]` **SHIPPED.** `public/sequence/index.html` — `ContactPicker` asks before creating.
- Verify: **live** — `V251152`, `Blocker: auth` + `real-data`. Narrowly scoped: the whole interaction is proven here (21 browser assertions, mutation-proven). What the sandbox cannot settle is whether it NAGS in real use against his own 17-contact registry — and a guard that nags gets switched off, which would leave things worse than before.
- Sandbox evidence: `ui-audit/verify-contact-confirm.mjs` **21/21** in a real browser · `test/contactCreateConfirm.test.js` (9) as the CI-runnable half. Eight mutations, every one proven red — see below.

**THE ENTRY-POINT AUDIT, done BEFORE choosing where to fix (the #948 lesson).** Create-on-type lives in exactly **one** component — `ContactPicker.commitTyped()` — serving **two** call sites, the grid Owner cell and the master-table Owner cell. That component IS the shared ancestor, so the guard sits there and both routes are covered by construction. The other two ways a contact can come into being are deliberately untouched: **`ContactsPanel.addContact()`** is the explicit "Add contact" form (already a decision — asking again would be the nag), and **`ensureContacts`** is a load-time repair pass, not typing. **The main app (`src/`) has no contact registry at all** — zero matches for `ContactPicker` / `responsibleParty` / `settings.contacts` — so there is no cross-module ancestor and no other cell to fix. Reported rather than assumed.

**⛔ THE FACT THAT DECIDED WHAT "DECLINE" MEANS, and it is not a preference.** `ensureContacts` runs on **every load** and re-derives a contact for **any task owner name missing from the registry**. So "commit the owner but don't create the contact" does not avoid the creation — it defers it to the next reload, where nobody is asked. The owner field and the registry are already **one decision**; this makes that visible instead of changing it. Hence: **confirm = assign AND create · decline = neither, and you are returned to the text.** `test/contactCreateConfirm.test.js` pins `ensureContacts`'s behaviour so a future reader knows the coupling was deliberate and can relax the decline path if it ever stops being true.

**THE ROUTES, and which ones stay silent — because a guard that nags on a normal selection gets turned off within a day and then it has made things worse.** ASKS: unrecognised text committed by Enter/Tab, and unrecognised text on click-away. DOES NOT ASK: an exact registry match · picking a person from the filtered list · the ghost-prefix completion · clearing the field · and the dropdown's own **`+ Add "X" as new contact`** row, which is already an explicit, self-describing choice — double-confirming it would be pure nag. Every one of those is a separate assertion in the harness.

**BLUR WAS DECIDED, NOT INHERITED.** The old handler committed on click-away, which is exactly what would have made the prompt theatre. Committing silently defeats the item; discarding silently throws away typing. So click-away with unrecognised text **raises the question and keeps the editor open** — the one option that neither writes nor loses. Recognised text and an empty field commit on blur exactly as before.

**DECLINING RETURNS THE TEXT UNHARMED, and that is guarded twice** — because getting it wrong would re-introduce the very class B443536 just fixed. `declineNew()` never touches `query`, restores focus, and places the **caret** (never a selection — a selection would let the next keystroke eat the text again). Proven in the browser: decline, then Backspace, and the field reads `Jason Berca` rather than an empty box. Typing while the question is up dismisses it, so it can never sit there quoting a name the field no longer says.

**PANEL-BREVITY.** One plain sentence in the space the dropdown already occupies — `No match — add "Jason Bercaw" as a new contact?` — plus two short buttons. No heading, no paragraph, no dialog wall; saying no is a button AND Escape AND where a stray click leaves you. The unit test measures the VISIBLE copy against a character budget (the first version of that assertion counted `?` in a source slice and caught a ternary — it was measuring the wrong thing and was fixed).

**MUTATIONS RUN — eight, every one proven RED, then restored.** Browser: revert to silent auto-create → 5 red incl. `Jason Bercaw` written with no question asked · decline wipes the text → 3 red · ask on an exact match (the nag) → 2 red. Unit: create directly again · nag on exact match · decline wipes the text · blur re-asks on every stray click · Escape no longer declines → one distinct assertion red each.

**AND THE OLDER HARNESS WAS UPDATED, NOT WEAKENED.** `verify-owner-first-char.mjs` encoded the OLD contract (a new name + Enter commits silently) and went 14/18 the moment this shipped. It now answers the question and re-asserts the same committed values — back to **18/18** — and the original caret mutation still drives it to **9/18**, so the update did not soften it.

### B455360 — Parcel split only accepted trivial cuts; it now takes a general polyline cut `[Site Planner / parcels]` (feature) #site-planner #parcel #geometry #ui  *(owner chat block 2026-08-13, arrived as NEW-1, verbatim: "I tried to split a parcel, but it seems like it only allows very simple cuts. And I'd like to split a parcel with a more complicated cut. So let's fix this." Minted **B455360 / V250304** LATE via `git fetch origin main && npm run next-id -- --against-main`, from this branch's reserved block B455360–B455375 · V250304–V250319 (origin/main c378cc8); code, tests and commits keep the provisional `NEW-1` label. **DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open / ⏳ Verify / Done across `parcel split`, `split parcel`, `splitPolygon`, `polygonSplit`, `concave`, `acreage`, `deed`, `promote`, `parcel drawing`, `B128`, `B416`, `B628`, `B651`, `B652`, `B682`.** Six neighbours, none of them this, and NOT a recurrence of any: **B128** (Done) made a STRAIGHT cut correct on a concave lot by pairing all crossings along the infinite line — that work is intact, still tested, and is now the independent ORACLE the general engine is cross-checked against; **B416** (Done) made the Split control reachable from the Parcel panel — discoverability, not geometry; **B628** owns the canvas/parcel menu the tool is armed from; **B651** (⏳ Verify) made a split a REPLACEMENT (parent superseded, children active) — that model is unchanged and this rides on it; **B652** is the active-parcel overlap warning; **B682** is the acreage-label duplication defect. The limit reported here was never filed by anyone: the engine had no representation for a cut that bends or crosses the boundary more than twice. Net-new.)*
`[x]` **SHIPPED.** `src/workspaces/site-planner/lib/polygonSplit.js` — `splitPolygonByCut`, a general polygon-split-by-polyline — wired as the Split tool's only caller.
- Verify: **live** — `V250304` (a signed-in pass on his own cloud plans; `Blocker: auth`). The logged-out half is proven HERE and is unusually strong for this class — see the evidence below.
- Sandbox evidence: `test/polygonSplit.test.js` **31 passing**, incl. the pre-fix pipeline reproducing his exact toast on two of his own production parcels, and mutation-proven three ways · `e2e/parcel-split-complex-cut.spec.js` **5/5 driving the REAL app on his recorded 95-acre Goose Creek tract** · unit **11,059 passing** · lint 0 errors · build green · bundle audit passes (see the cost note).

**WHAT WAS ACTUALLY WRONG, and it is worse than "the message is unhelpful".** Two splitters shipped, and between them they covered only trivial cuts. A 2-point cut went to `splitPolygonByLine`, which is correct. Anything with a bend went to `splitPolygonByPath`, which projected the first and last cut vertex onto the NEAREST polygon edge, refused outright when both landed on the same edge, and then emitted exactly TWO rings by walking the boundary between them. Three consequences: it could not represent a cut crossing the boundary more than twice (so three or more pieces was unreachable BY CONSTRUCTION); it never checked that the cut stayed inside the lot; and on a concave lot the two rings overlapped or omitted a wedge, at which point a downstream area guard refused the whole thing with `That cut crosses the parcel ambiguously (concave shape) — try a straight cut between two opposite edges.` **That refusal is measured, not recalled**: `test/polygonSplit.test.js` runs the pre-fix pipeline verbatim and reproduces it on his Goose Creek and Bain tracts.

**THE FIX IS ONE ENGINE WITH NO CASE ANALYSIS.** `splitPolygonByCut` builds the PLANAR ARRANGEMENT of the boundary and the cut and enumerates its faces: node every intersection into a shared tolerance-snapping registry, emit boundary sub-edges plus the cut sub-edges whose midpoints are strictly inside the lot, prune degree-1 nodes, trace faces, keep the ones that are land. Both readings of "more complicated" fall out of it rather than being handled — a multi-segment cut, and a cut crossing the boundary 2k times giving k+1 pieces — as do a cut that re-enters and a cut that closes a loop inside the lot. There is no crossing-count branch anywhere, which is the point.

**⛔ TWO CONDITIONS IN HIS REAL RECORDED PARCELS BROKE THE FIRST DRAFT, AND NEITHER IS A TEXTBOOK POLYGON. Do not "simplify" either guard away.**
1. **Goose Creek's ring is PINCHED.** It runs out to a point, clockwise around an interior exclusion while the rest of the lot runs counter-clockwise, and back through that same point — a hole reached by a zero-width slit. Under an even-odd containment test that hole reads as LAND and the split invents ~13,400 sf the parcel does not own. Faces are therefore classified by the WINDING rule, which is also what the shoelace acreage the whole app quotes already assumes; getting the two to agree is what makes "the pieces sum to the acreage" a real check rather than a coincidence. Mutation-proven: keep every bounded face and the two Goose Creek tests go red.
2. **Bain's ring self-overlaps.** It runs 1,296 ft out along a zero-width prong and back, and the returning leg clips the outgoing one about two tenths of an inch above its base. Left un-noded, that hairline crossing has no node and the face walk runs straight through it, so the boundary is now noded against ITSELF before anything else. Mutation-proven: drop that pass and the Bain test goes red. Its consequence is also handled rather than hidden — the shoelace figure counts an 8 sf crumb twice, so the pieces cannot sum to the STATED acreage, and rather than refuse his largest parcel over 8 sf on 109 acres the engine reports `outlineDrift` and the app says so on screen.

**LOUD-FAILURE, in four places.** Nothing is silent. (a) Every refusal names what is wrong with THAT cut — never crosses the parcel · runs along the property line · stops inside the parcel · doesn't separate it · the pieces don't add up · the parcel's own outline crosses itself — and a unit test fails if any refusal message is generic, duplicated, or contains the retired "try a straight cut" advice. (b) A cut producing three or more pieces SAYS how many. (c) A scrap under a hundred-thousandth of the parent is not made into a parcel, and its count and area are reported. (d) A parcel whose own outline overlaps itself is named, with the discrepancy in square feet. The one hard refusal that remains is a genuine area mismatch with no crossing to explain it: nothing is written.

**ATTRIBUTES, and what is RECOMPUTED rather than copied.** Address, account and the attribute bag ride onto every piece. Acreage and the badge were already derived from `points` at render, so they are right for free. The per-edge vectors are the ones that would have gone stale invisibly — a piece has different edges from its parent — so `setbacks`, `roleOverrides` and the legacy dense `roles` are REMAPPED through the engine's own edge provenance (`edgeSrc`: for each edge of the new ring, the parent edge index it came from, or -1 for an edge the cut created), and a cut edge takes the plan's default setback and no role assignment rather than a neighbour's value. `label` is deliberately NOT carried — see the owner questions.

**HOLES.** The parcel model is single-ring (`pc.points`), so there are none to preserve today; the pinched-hole case above is the nearest thing the data actually contains and it is handled. The engine is ring-topological rather than boundary-walking, so real interior rings would be fed into the same arrangement — not a rewrite.

**⛔ JUDGEMENT CALLS FOR THE OWNER — NOT DECIDED HERE.** Both are on `OWNER-TODO.md`.
1. **A cut making THREE OR MORE pieces.** Shipped behaviour is KEEP THEM ALL, because it is the only option that cannot lose acreage, and the toast says how many were made. The open question is whether he wants that, or the two largest kept with the rest discarded, or to be asked at the moment of the cut.
2. **NAMING the pieces.** Shipped behaviour is UNCHANGED from before this item — pieces carry no label. Copying the parent's name onto three parcels would pre-empt his answer, and dropping it is what the app already did, so this is the neutral hold. The question is Parcel 1A / 1B / 1C, or the original name staying on the largest piece with the rest named after it.

**COST, stated rather than left to be found.** The engine adds **6.4 KB** to the Site route and the largest chunk against a clean-tree baseline measured on this machine. It stays: it replaced a ~1.5 KB special case that refused the cuts the tool exists for, all four bundle metrics remain inside their headroom band and PASS, and the four metrics already above baseline were above it on the clean tree too (pre-existing, B329408 / B1064).

- **⛔ THE OWNER'S OWN LEADING HYPOTHESIS IS REFUTED. The date did not come from the clock.** His framing —
  "adding a predecessor STAMPS THE CURRENT DATE onto the successor start" — was the single most likely
  mechanism and it is wrong. `updateTask` handles `predecessors` correctly: it normalises the list, clears
  any manual pin so the cascade can take effect, and `touchesSchedule` fires a full recompute. Nothing on
  that path reads `NOW`. **2026-08-10 is a DERIVED date** — it is the next working day after Friday
  2026-08-07, and its resemblance to the day of the edit is a coincidence.
- **WHAT IT WAS DERIVED FROM — the predecessor's START, because the predecessor's FINISH had been silently
  discarded.** Read straight off his live document: task 228 "Mobilize" (0d, FS after 106 and 108); task
  **108 "CCID3: Lift Station & Force Main Approval" is a SUMMARY row** with three children running to
  2026-10-02, stored `duration: 40` and `durValue: 0`. A parent gets `duration` written by
  `rollupParentDates` and never gets a `durValue` — but `cascadeDates` resolved every row as a leaf, so
  `resolveTaskSpan` read `durValue: 0` and **collapsed a 40-working-day summary into a 0-day milestone
  sitting on its own start, 2026-08-07.** The FS successor then computed the next working day after that:
  Monday **2026-08-10**. `rollupParentDates` restored 108's finish to 2026-10-02 immediately afterwards —
  which is exactly why the wrong date was **a STABLE FIXED POINT**: re-running the recompute reproduced it
  byte for byte, and `detectCascadeDrift` (stored vs engine) could never see it because the engine agreed
  with the stored value. Correct answer, confirmed on his data: **2026-10-05**.
- **This is NOT the "mechanism that exists and never fires" class (hypothesis 1 — refuted).** There is a
  real scheduling engine, it does re-run on a predecessor edit, it is a full topological recompute, and it
  propagates transitively. It supports FS / SS / FF / SF with lag in working OR calendar days (hypothesis 5
  — answered: all four types, both lag units). Both predecessors WERE resolvable (hypothesis 2 — 106 and
  108 are both real rows in the same project; 106 simply has no dates).
- **THE RED "Needs Attn." DOT IS NOT A DEPENDENCY VERDICT (hypothesis: refuted).** It is
  `computeDisplayHealth`'s `cf.overdueRed` rule — finish in the past, 0% complete. The app did not know
  anything was wrong with the dependency; it only knew a date had passed.
- **THE PADLOCK ANSWER (hypotheses 6 + 7).** The padlock is a pinned start (or a locked finish); a pinned
  date WINS over predecessor logic, and adding a predecessor deliberately clears the pin. Rows 26/27/30/42/43
  wear one because their dates were typed by hand; Mobilize does not, because adding predecessors unpinned
  it — so it was exactly a row the engine was supposed to be computing, and it computed off a collapsed
  input. The difference between rows 28 and 42 is real but it is not the cause. Row 42 also happens to have
  a LEAF predecessor, so it was never exposed to this defect.
- **THE FIX.** `cascadeDates` no longer derives a span for a row that is a parent — a summary's dates are
  owned by `rollupParentDates`, full stop (parents never took a predecessor-driven start either, because
  the rollup overwrote it in the same breath, so the skip is behaviour-preserving for the parent itself).
  And the cascade/rollup pair — hand-written at nine call sites — is now the single `recomputeSchedule`,
  which seeds with a rollup so the first cascade reads real parent finishes and then **iterates to a fixed
  point**, so one call propagates a move transitively down a chain of any depth.
- **EXISTING SCHEDULES RECALCULATE, AND SAY SO.** The cloud load path already routes through
  `recascadeWithDrift`, so every saved document is re-derived on open and the B836 drift banner NAMES each
  corrected row. Measured against his live Grand Port document: **exactly one row moves — Mobilize,
  2026-08-10 → 2026-10-05** — and it arrives named, not swapped in silence. Across all six of his projects
  there are **9 predecessor links pointing at a summary row** (Goose Creek 4, 8 South 3, Grand Port 2), so
  that is the full population exposed to this class.
- Guards, all four MUTATION-PROVEN RED: `test/schedulerEngine.test.js` (removing the summary skip → 5 fail;
  dropping the fixed-point iteration → 1 fail) and `ui-audit/verify-summary-pred-dates.mjs` /
  `npm run verify:schedpreds`, which drives the REAL Grid on his exact row shape and reads the Start cell
  off the screen. With the skip reverted the harness reads **08/10/26** — his screen, reproduced.
- Bundle: **zero delta, byte-identical** (`dist/assets/index-*.js` gzip identical with and without the
  change). The Schedule module is the standalone `public/sequence/index.html`, never part of the main
  bundle, so the ceiling is untouched.
- Files: `public/sequence/index.html`, `ui-audit/stress/scheduler-engine.mjs` (verbatim mirror),
  `test/schedulerEngine.test.js`, `ui-audit/verify-summary-pred-dates.mjs`, `ui-audit/lib/vendorCdn.mjs`.

### B443249 — A predecessor that drives NOTHING looked identical to one that does `[Schedule]` (bug) #scheduler #ui  *(owner chat 2026-08-13, the "unresolvable predecessor" half of the Grand Port report. Minted B443249 / V238193.)*

  at all** (its one child is blank too). `cascadeDates` filtered it out — correctly, it can drive nothing —

  fabricated-date-looks-exactly-like-a-real-one failure this repo keeps paying for (LOUD-FAILURE).

  so it can never disagree with what the engine actually ignored.

  explanation replaces the existing cell hover rather than adding one. No new banner.

### B447472 — `assembly_digest()` had no kind predicate, so the two sides of the group revision digested DIFFERENT MEMBER SETS `[Site Planner / Persistence]` (bug) #site-planner #persistence #sync #infra  *(adversarial review of B1341 stage 2 + a steel-man pass, 2026-08-13. Minted **B447472 / V242416** LATE via `git fetch origin main && npm run next-id -- --against-main`, from this branch's reserved block B447472–B447487 · V242416–V242431 against `origin/main` 2396734. **DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open / ⏳ Verify / Done across `assembly_digest`, `digestsByAssembly`, `groupCas`, `p_groups`, `groupConflict`, `assembly_id`, `kind`, `B1341`, `B1340`, `B1117`, `B420256`, `B377888`, `B377890`.** Neighbours, none of them this: **B1341** is the staged feature this defect lives inside — stage 2 is SHIPPED and unchanged in every other respect, this corrects one predicate in it; **B420256** is the same ROOT CAUSE (an id is unique only per KIND) in the commit-RESULT pairing path, and is why this one was looked for; **B1117** is the atomic call; **B1340/B377890** are the client-side integrity heals. Net-new.)*
`[ ]` **⏳ SHIPPED 2026-08-13. `Verify: live` → V242416 (MERGED ≠ LIVE).**
- Verify: live → **V242416** (`Blocker: auth` + `real-data` — the DB half is proven only by running `db/test/commit_elements_group_cas.test.sql` against the real database, and the repro assembly is on a signed-in plan).
- **THE DEFECT.** `assembly_digest()` in `db/commit_elements_group_cas.sql` filtered on `site_id`, `assembly_id` and `deleted_at` — and **nothing else**. Its client twin `digestsByAssembly()` (`lib/assemblyDigest.js`) opens with `if (e.kind !== "el") continue`. So for an affected assembly the two sides digest different member sets and **can never agree**: every commit is refused with a `groupConflict` whose retry recomputes the identical disagreement, until `maxRejectStreak` declares the tab stale. That assembly simply cannot be saved.
- **⛔ THE ROOT CAUSE IS NOT "THE SERVER FORGOT A FILTER" — that reading was steel-manned and replaced, and the better one is the whole value of this item.** `assembly_id` **INHERITS THE ID NAMESPACE'S NON-UNIQUENESS.** The PK is `(site_id, kind, id)`, so an id is unique only per KIND (**B420256**); stage 1 sets an unbonded element's `assembly_id` to its OWN id, so that non-uniqueness passes straight into the assembly key and **two unrelated SINGLETON assemblies of different kinds collide on the name**. Verified on production: `markup:e6327` has `attachedTo = NONE` and `assembly_id = e6327`; `el:e6327` has `attachedTo = NONE` and `assembly_id = e6327`. The markup is **not a member of the building's assembly at all** — it is its own assembly that happens to share the NAME. Read it that way, or the next person rediscovers it through a callout instead of a markup.
- **LIVE INSTANCE, read-only against production 2026-08-13.** Site `smqh3au6aeb4` (Katz / Plan 1), assembly `e6327` = **28 `el` members + 1 unrelated `markup`**. Server digested 29 tokens, client 28. A sweep of the whole table finds **exactly one** such assembly today — and with `kind = 'el'` filtered, the count of assemblies containing a duplicate id drops to **ZERO**. ⛔ **The Katz plan was NOT touched and nothing was written to `public.site_elements`** — that data is legitimate and the code must tolerate it (same standing as B420256).
- **LATENT ONLY, and that is why it was worth fixing now rather than later.** Group CAS is OFF (`elementSync.js` `groupCas = null`; `groupsFor` returns `[]` when unset), so nothing is broken today. It bites the instant stage 2 is switched on — i.e. it is a defect that would present as "the flag we just enabled broke saving", at the worst possible moment to be diagnosing it.
- **THE FIX.** `and t.kind = 'el'` in `assembly_digest()`, and the same predicate on the `groupConflict` **members** subquery — the client ADOPTS every member that payload names into its shadow, so a membership disagreement there deadlocks the retry exactly as one in the digest does. **⛔ THE CLIENT IS RIGHT AND DOES NOT MOVE:** a markup has no host, so it is a member of nothing but itself. Settled, not an open choice — never make the two agree by folding non-`el` rows in on the client side. The false claim in `assemblyDigest.js`'s header (that the database's `assembly_id` "never groups them with it") is **deleted and replaced with the namespace explanation**, not reworded.
- **APPLIED TO PRODUCTION this session**, because the stage-2 migration was already deployed and the DEPLOYED function was the broken one — a repo-only fix would have left the live database wrong. `create or replace` on both functions plus the re-`grant`s; additive, idempotent, no client behaviour change (the flag is off). Post-apply check on the live database: `assembly_digest('smqh3au6aeb4','e6327')` now returns **28 tokens, naming no markup**, while 29 rows still share the assembly key — the data is intact, only the question changed.
- **⛔ THE TEST GAP MATTERED AS MUCH AS THE FIX, AND IT IS CLOSED STRUCTURALLY.** `test/assemblyGroupCas.test.js:50` asserted the SQL matched a regex of the `string_agg` EXPRESSION. That pins the shape of the PROJECTION and is **structurally blind to the WHERE clause beside it** — both sides can agree character-for-character on how to build a token and still disagree about who is in the set. Its neighbour asserted "a markup is never in an assembly", **a claim about the DATABASE tested only against the client**. Both are replaced by a **PARITY suite** (`test/helpers/sqlDigestParity.js`): it reads the real migration, parses the projection AND the filter, EXECUTES both over one row set, and compares against the client twin over the same rows — with a kind-collision fixture drawn from the live `e6327` assembly (28 real ids at their real revs + the colliding markup), plus controls (an ordinary assembly, a tombstone, another site's rows, the empty group) so the suite cannot pass by answering empty. The interpreter **THROWS on any construct it cannot model** rather than skipping it, so a future edit that moves the SQL outside what it understands fails loudly instead of passing vacuously.
- **PROVEN RED BEFORE THE FIX: 4 of the new parity cases failed against today's SQL** — the kind collision (server 29 tokens vs client 28), the markup-is-its-own-assembly case, the conflict-members set, and the predicate readback — while the other 28 cases in the file stayed green, so the suite is not merely asserting the new implementation. **32/32 green after.**
- The real-Postgres half gains matching checks 9 and 10 in `db/test/commit_elements_group_cas.test.sql` (a markup inserted at the host's own id: it must collide on `assembly_id`, stay out of the digest, and stay out of the members payload). Self-rolling-back as before.
- **DELIBERATELY NOT DONE, offered and declined as out of scope:** `db/site_elements.sql`'s per-op loop reads `jsonb_array_elements(p_ops)` with no `ORDER BY`, which B420256's positional pairing rests on. Postgres preserves array order in practice and `pairCommitResults` VERIFIES the pairing and falls back loudly, so it is hardening, not a defect — not inflated into this trip.
- **Housekeeping:** `BACKLOG.md` carried three committed **merge-conflict markers** (`<<<<<<< HEAD` / `=======` / `>>>>>>> origin/main`) around the B442688 and B435536 blocks, landed by an earlier bad merge into the ⏳ Verify section. Removed, keeping BOTH sides per this file's own rule. No item content changed.
- Sandbox: `test/assemblyGroupCas.test.js` 32 green (4 proven red pre-fix), full suite + lint + build green.
### B443536 — The Owner cell ate the character that opened it: typing `Scott` saved `cott` `[Scheduler]` (bug) #scheduler #ui  *(owner chat block 2026-08-13, arrived as the Schedule / Owner-column report, verbatim: *"we type a person's name into the owner column … it uses the first letter for searching the contact list or the registry, but after that, it forgets that first letter. Test it and figure it out."* Minted **B443536 / V238480** LATE via `git fetch origin main && npm run next-id -- --against-main`, from this branch's reserved block B443536–B443551 · V238480–V238495. **DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open / ⏳ Verify / Done across `ContactPicker`, `editStartChar`, `initChar`, `responsibleParty`, `type-to-edit`, `first letter`, `first character`, `select()`, `setSelectionRange`, `seed`, `B291538`, `B865`, `B212`, `B583`.** One near neighbour, and it is NOT this: **B291538** is also "the first letter typed goes nowhere", but its cause is a bare `f` being swallowed as a global fullscreen command in the SHELL, a different module and a different mechanism — it is not re-opened and does not take this number. **B865** (NO_AUTOFILL) and **B212** (Tab through visible columns) touch the same editors without owning caret behaviour. Net-new.)*
`[x]` **SHIPPED.** `public/sequence/index.html` — `ContactPicker` gains a `seeded` prop; both call sites wire it.
- Verify: **live** — `V238480`, `Blocker: auth`. Narrowly scoped: the INTERACTION is fully proven here (see below); what the sandbox cannot reach is the **signed-in cloud round-trip** — type an owner on a real cloud project, reload, confirm the whole name came back. The scheduler falls back to its baked seed when Supabase is unreachable, which is the proxy's CORS wall, so that half is genuinely blocked.
- Sandbox evidence: `ui-audit/verify-owner-first-char.mjs` **18/18** in a real browser with real key events · `test/ownerPickerSeed.test.js` (5) as the CI-runnable half. Both mutation-proven — see below.
- **Confirmed on LIVE PRODUCTION and on the DEPLOYED branch build** (2026-08-13, logged out). The sandbox browser cannot reach `planyr.io` or `*.pages.dev`, but Node can, so the deployed bytes were fetched and driven: `planyr.io` reproduces the owner's report exactly — trace `["S","c","co","cot","cott"]`, committed `"cott"` — and this branch's Cloudflare preview gives `["S","Sc","Sco","Scot","Scott"]`, committed `"Scott"`. V238480 stays open for the signed-in round-trip only.
- **DATA-DAMAGE SWEEP OF THE REAL SAVED DATA (2026-08-13, read-only, via the Supabase MCP): ZERO rows damaged, ZERO contacts damaged.** Scope: all **6 projects · 734 tasks · 30 owner values · 17 contacts** in `public.planar_data`, **plus all 1,062 `planar_history` snapshots spanning 2026-06-03 → 2026-08-13** (19 distinct owner values and 19 distinct contacts ever recorded). Four independent signatures were run, and the registry was swept as well as the assignments — a name auto-added through the broken field would make a damaged task look internally consistent, which is the case a naive assignment-only check cannot see: (a) an owner value starting LOWERCASE — the truncation removes the leading CAPITAL, so this is close to unambiguous; (b) a CONTACT starting lowercase; (c) an owner value that becomes an exact contact when one char is prepended; (d) a contact that is another contact minus its first char. All four: **NONE**, now and at every point in the history. The only two entries ever removed from the registry were `Can give up trailer parlking` (a note mistyped into the field) and `chris@gaiadevelopment.com` (an email used as a name) — both full strings, neither a truncation, both already cleaned up by the owner.
- **THE DETECTOR WAS PROVEN RED BEFORE THE NULL WAS BELIEVED** (STANDING RULE #2 — when the instrument and the report disagree, the instrument is on trial). The same four queries were run against a synthetic damaged copy and correctly reported `cott Kitrell | ercaw` as lowercase owners, `ercaw` as a truncated contact, and `cott Kitrell -> Scott Kitrell` as a prepend match. A clean number from an instrument that could not have seen the effect is not evidence of absence; this one can see it.
- **AND THE MECHANISM THAT EXPLAINS THE CLEAN RESULT, measured on the PRE-FIX build rather than reasoned about.** The picker filters by SUBSTRING (`c.name.toLowerCase().includes(q)`), and `cott` **is** a substring of `Scott Kitrell` — so on the broken build the dropdown still listed the right person. Driven live against the pre-fix bytes: field holds `"cott"`, dropdown still offers `Scott Kitrell`, and clicking that row commits **`Scott Kitrell`** in full, because `onCommit` takes the CONTACT's name and not the box's text. The damage only lands when the raw text is committed instead — the same run typed a genuinely new name and stored **`ephyr`**. So the defect was real and visible (which is exactly what the owner saw and reported) but self-correcting for anyone who picks the person out of the list, and his saved data reflects that habit. **This is an explanation, not an excuse: the bug is fixed, and a name not already in the registry would have been stored mangled.**

**THE MEASURED CAUSE, and it is none of the three shapes the report proposed.** The keystroke trace, read out of the real input after EVERY key, was `["S","c","co","cot","cott"]`. So the character is **captured**, **written into the field**, and **used to filter the registry** — it is present and correct after keystroke 1. It dies on **keystroke 2**. `ContactPicker`'s mount effect ran `inputRef.current?.select()` **unconditionally**, so the seeded character was left SELECTED; the next key replaced the selection instead of appending to it. Not a seed written before mount, not a stale re-render, not a `preventDefault` that ate the key — the character was destroyed by a caret decision one keystroke later, which is exactly why the search legitimately sees the letter the field has lost.

**AND IT WAS DATA DAMAGE, NOT A DISPLAY GLITCH.** `cott` is what `commit()` stored on the task, and `commitTyped()` then auto-added **`cott` as a new contact** — so one mistyped-looking edit both mis-assigned the task and polluted the registry that every later autocomplete reads from. The harness asserts the COMMITTED value (read back off the task model through the closed cell, never off the input that was typed into), not just the rendered one.

**NOT A RACE — MEASURED, not assumed.** The report asked whether typing speed matters, because a mount/keystroke race needs a different guard. Typed with **no delay between keys** the field reads `anda` for `Wanda` on the broken build and `Wanda` on the fixed one: the loss is deterministic, so the guard is a plain assertion and needs no timing tolerance.

**THE "IT MIGHT BE SHARED" HYPOTHESIS IS REFUTED BY MEASUREMENT.** Predecessor, Task name and Duration all keep their opening character (`["1","12"]`, `["Z","Ze","Zet","Zeta"]`, `["3","37"]`) — every other type-to-edit editor is UNCONTROLLED with `defaultValue`, and none calls `select()` on mount. `NotesModal` already documents the correct behaviour in its own comment (*"caret at end so an initChar keystroke continues seamlessly"*). `ContactPicker` was the lone outlier, so the fix belongs IN it rather than at a shared ancestor. It does serve **two** call sites, though — the grid cell and the master-table cell (which seeds via `localEdit.initChar`) — and both were affected and are both fixed.

**THE FIX IS ONE FLAG BECAUSE THERE ARE TWO CORRECT BEHAVIOURS.** `seeded` says where the opening `value` came from. Type-to-edit → caret AFTER the character. Click / double-click on an existing owner → select-all, so typing a new name REPLACES the old one rather than appending to it. Deleting the `select()` outright is the tempting one-line fix and it is **wrong**: the inverse mutation (never select) makes replacing `Scott` with `Dana` produce `ScottDana`, and that case is asserted so the over-fix cannot ship either.

**MUTATIONS RUN (every assertion proven RED, then restored).** Browser harness: revert the branch to an unconditional `select()` → **8 red**, reproducing `cott` and `riya` verbatim · never-select (the over-fix) → the two double-click REPLACE checks red at `ScottDana` · drop `seeded=` at the grid call site only → **8 red**. Unit test: unconditional `select()` · drop the grid prop · hardcode `seeded={true}` · drop the `= false` default → one distinct assertion red each.

**AN UNMATCHED NAME IS AN EXPLICIT OUTCOME, and that is now asserted rather than assumed.** A free-typed name that matches no contact already shows a visible `+ Add "Priya" as new contact` row before commit and is accepted as a real owner; the harness reads that row's text. No new copy was added (PANEL-BREVITY: net zero lines).

**THE GROUPING, argued rather than picked.** The owner floated both shapes ("buildings and pond and roads … but maybe that should just get grouped into elements"), so this does BOTH, in the shape the app already has next door: a tri-state **Elements** master over per-type rows, which is precisely the Layers panel's "Show all flood & drainage" row — same `{ all, any, onCount, ids }` object, asserted against `LayerPanel`'s own `floodMaster` by a test so the two cannot drift into two mechanisms. **⛔ HIDE NEVER DELETES, AND IT IS STRUCTURAL RATHER THAN CAREFUL.** The filter is applied ONLY where `cullToView` is already applied — `drawEls`, `drawParcels`, `drawMarkupsZ`, `measureBands`, `calloutBands`. Viewport culling has always meant "drawn ≠ exists" in this codebase and has never moved a number; hiding is the same operation at the same seam with a different predicate. The metrics pass (`els.forEach` → bldg/paving/parkArea/trailArea/pondArea/stalls/trailers/providedDetCf, and `dissolvedParcelSqft(parcels…)`) iterates the MODEL and never a draw set. Nothing is tombstoned, nothing syncs, no geometry is touched.

**THE FOUR OLD TOGGLES, each decided rather than preserved.**
- **Show dock doors → REMOVED.** He is explicit. **The hazard of deleting a shipped control is STRANDING a plan saved with it off** — the doors would be off forever with nothing left to turn them back on — so `normalizeRetiredToggles` restores a stored `false` on load, once, and reports it. It returns null when there is nothing to do, so an ordinary plan is not dirtied on open.
- **Column grid → KEPT** (under *Detail*). His own block calls it "genuinely a drafting aid", and it is the one of the four about the WORK rather than about clutter.
- **Dimensions → KEPT** (under *Detail*) — worth suppressing for a clean look before a print.
- **Element areas → KEPT, MOVED** (under *Labels*) beside the parcel acreage master, because "the sf line on an element" and "the acreage chip on a lot" are one idea that lived as two unrelated controls in two unrelated places.

**THE ACREAGE CHIP — NOT re-implemented, made DISCOVERABLE.** The block's own note is right: `chipHidden` shipped in B1404 and is reachable only from a parcel's right-click menu, which is why he did not know it existed. The per-lot control is untouched; a plan-wide **Parcel acreage** master joins it in *Labels* and the two compose with OR in `parcelAcreageHidden`. **⛔ The master deliberately does NOT write `chipHidden` on every parcel** — that would be a model mutation dressed as a view toggle, it would sync, and turning it back off could not know which lots he had hidden by hand. Asserted both ways.

**WHAT THE HARNESS FOUND, which is the part worth reading.**
1. **A real bug in this very work: hiding Parcels left every acreage badge on screen.** The badges are built from `parcels`, not `drawParcels`, so the draw-seam filter never reached them — and the badge carries `data-feature="parcel:<id>"`, so by every reading the parcel was still on the plan. A group that hides an object must hide its chrome, or "hidden" means "mostly hidden". Fixed at the chip list.
2. **The harness's own first cut was measuring the wrong thing, and it failed LOUDLY rather than passing.** `panelText` scoped to `[data-surface="planner"]`'s nearest `div`, which resolved to most of the page — so the "numbers" being compared included canvas element labels, the acreage badges and the View menu's own chrome. Six checks went red on a working implementation. The metrics region is now `data-testid="yield-metrics"` and the read returns **null** when it is not on screen, so "the panel was not open" can never masquerade as "the numbers did not move" (two nulls compare equal — that trap is closed by an explicit setup check, which then caught the *next* one: the left dock starts CLOSED on every load, so 25 checks had been comparing `null === null`).
3. **The mutation proof.** Move the filter one seam earlier — filter `els` before the metrics pass instead of at the draw set — and the canvas is **pixel-identical** while `Buildings 62.13 ac · 24%` becomes `Buildings 0.00 ac · 0%` and open space silently gains 62 acres. The harness goes 33/33 → 28/33 and names the moved number. No visual test in this repo could see it.

**Also closed:** hiding a group now clears any selection into it (the handle layer renders from `sel`/`multi`, not the draw sets, so grips would otherwise float over ground with nothing under them), and a MARQUEE cannot catch what he cannot see (the three box-select passes read the raw model, so a box over a plan with markups hidden would have handed back invisible objects — and the next Delete would have taken them).

**Persistence:** `settings.hidden`, a SPARSE map naming only what is hidden, so a plan saved before this gains no keys and renders byte-identically, "show everything" is a DELETE of keys rather than eight `false`s, and an unrecognised key from a newer build degrades to visible.

**Glanceable, as he required** ("a plan that silently hides half its content is worse than one that never hid anything"): the collapsed View header turns amber with a struck-through eye and NAMES what is hidden — `Buildings, Markups hidden`, degrading to `4 groups` past three — and the open card repeats it with a one-click **Show all**.

**Bundle:** +6.6 KB on `largestChunkBytes`, inside the headroom band, attributable and owned by B1064.

Driving the pre-fix build here measured **199.5 px of label over 10.3 px of feature** — his number, reproduced.
- **⛔ ONE CORRECTION TO THE DIAGNOSIS, and it matters for where the fix goes.** The item's stated likely root was that the easement kind carries none of `labelSize` / `labelSpacing` / `labelPlace` / `labelInside` / `labelHalo`. **It carries all of them** — verified against the four real easement rows on that plan and against `inlineLabelEls`, which the easement render calls at `SitePlanner.jsx`. An easement has TWO labels: the repeating INLINE label (fully controlled, and not the reported one) and the CENTROID label built from `labelOverride`, which had no controls at all. **And no markup label anywhere is in world units** — the others ride a clamped zoom ramp. His five measured neighbour sizes are `base × 0.34` exactly (labelSize 7 → 2.38, 8 → 2.72, default 11 → 3.74, 12 → 4.08), which is what identified the ramp.
- **⛔ THE ANSWER TO "IS A SHARED LEGIBILITY GATE THE RIGHT ABSTRACTION": IT ALREADY EXISTED, BUILT THREE TIMES, AND THIS LABEL WAS USING NONE OF IT.** B149's `detailLabelVisible`, B911's `dimFontPx` and the pond-parameter tier each pair the same two defences — a VISIBILITY gate keyed on the measured feature's on-screen size, and a SIZE riding `dimFontScale`. So **no fourth threshold was introduced**: the floor IS `dimCalloutVisible`, the ramp IS `dimFontScale`, and nothing in the new code is tunable. B371360's `featureEditFloorPpf` was considered and is deliberately NOT reused — it answers "is an EDIT legible" from an absolute px/ft floor and a viewport cap, which is a different question from "is this label smaller than its feature".
- **WHAT IS GENUINELY NEW is the third question none of the three existing tiers asks: is the LABEL narrower than its FEATURE?** The others gate on the feature alone, which suffices for short generated numbers ("300′") and not for arbitrary user text: this 513 ft easement clears `detailLabelVisible` at ppf 0.0585, where 30 characters still measure ~64 px against 30 px of feature. A long name now waits longer than a short one on the same feature.
- **⛔ THE SELECTION BYPASS WAS PART OF THE DEFECT.** The label only drew when selected, via `(isSel || dimCalloutVisible(ppf))` — `isSel` short-circuited every gate, which is exactly why a 199 px label sat over a 21 px object. - **"the feature's length" is its GREATEST extent**, not its horizontal one — otherwise a vertical easement of the same length would wait far longer for its name, which is a size rule masquerading as an orientation rule.
- **SCOPE: the same fix was applied to the two SIBLINGS with the identical shape** — the `traced` overlay label (9.5 px constant) and the `encumbrance` deed-boundary label (11 px constant), found by the same audit. ### B435537 — Baytown's flood ordinance, transcribed: the higher of the 500-year and BFE + 24 in `[Site Planner / drainage]` (bug) #site-planner #floodplain #gis  *(owner chat amendment 2026-08-13, arrived as NEW-8, with the ordinance text pulled from Municode in his own browser. Minted **B435537 / V230481** from the same reserved block. Not a new number for the same problem: B393170 shipped the honest UNKNOWN, this ships the rule. Also searched `baytown`, `110-102`, `RULE_KEY_ALIAS`, `limitedPurpose`, `shaded X`, `moderate flood hazard`: net-new work.)*
`[ ]` **⏳ SHIPPED 2026-08-13. `Verify: live` → V230481.**
- Verify: live → **V230481** (`Blocker: real-data` `Blocker: auth`).
- Origin: filed 2026-08-13 from chat; shipped the same session.
- **CITATION:** City of Baytown, TX, Code of Ordinances, Subpart B — Land Development Code, Ch. 110 (FLOODS), Art. II (Flood Damage Prevention). Version JUL 2 2026, codified through Ord. No. 16,449 enacted 2026-04-23. Owner-read via Municode 2026-08-13 — the same provenance route as the Waller record (B986) and the Harris / Fort Bend records (owner-read PDFs, PR #594). This sandbox's egress proxy still refuses both `library.municode.com` and `baytown.org`.
- **THE RULE, Sec. 110-102(2): FFE ≥ the HIGHER OF the 500-year floodplain elevation and BFE + 24 in.** Modelled as a max-of over two bases (`wse02pct +0`, `wse1pct +2`), the Waller/Fort Bend shape. Dry floodproofing to the same elevation is an accepted alternative for nonresidential — recorded as copy, never as a number.
- **⛔ IT CORRECTS THE OWNER'S RECOLLECTION, WHICH IS WHY HE ASKED FOR IT TO BE CHECKED RATHER THAN CONFIRMED.** His version was "~2 ft above the 500-year". The ordinance is **not** 500-yr + 2, and his version is wrong in BOTH directions: where the 500-yr sits ≥2 ft above the BFE (the ordinary case in flat Harris and Chambers floodplain) it is **2.0 ft HIGHER** than the code requires; where the 500-yr falls below BFE + 2 it is **LOWER** (worked case: BFE 50.0 / 500-yr 49.5 → ordinance 52.0, recollection 51.5).
- **THE NONRESIDENTIAL PARAGRAPH IS NOT SPLIT BY HAZARD AREA — the non-obvious part, and it is asserted structurally.** Residential (1) IS split into a. special and b. moderate; nonresidential (2) is a single paragraph under the section preamble, so the SAME elevation applies in a moderate flood hazard area. Sec. 110-26 defines that as shaded Zone X / Zone B, so **Baytown regulates shaded X** — a site outside the 100-year but inside the 500-year still gets a Baytown floor. Neither basis carries a `when`, and a test fails if one acquires a hazard-area condition.
- **HOW MANY FEET THE PADS MOVE: NONE ON GOOSE CREEK, and the reason is the finding.** Harris County is 500-yr WSE + 2 (§4.07(b)(1), verified); Baytown is the higher of the 500-yr and BFE + 2. Wherever the 500-yr sits ≥2 ft above the BFE, **Baytown's number IS the 500-yr — 2.0 ft BELOW Harris's** — so the strictest-wins resolver keeps Harris and no pad moves. Measured across three surface pairs: −2.00 / −1.00 / −2.00 ft. On **Grand Port** Chambers County has no modelled rule at all, so Baytown's is the only number available — and its reach there is unresolved (below).
- **⛔ APPLICABILITY BEYOND THE CITY LIMITS: THE ORDINANCE IS SILENT, AND SILENT IS A FINDING.** Sec. 110-31 in full is *"This article shall apply to all moderate and special flood hazard areas within the jurisdiction of the city"*; Ch. 110 contains no occurrence of extraterritorial, limited-purpose or industrial district. So `limitedPurposeScope` moves from `"unknown"` (not read) to **`"silent"`** (read, does not say) — deliberately different values. Neither a yes nor a no was inferred. ⚠ ONE piece of textual evidence is recorded and LABELLED AS AN INFERENCE, never as the rule: Sec. 110-32 adopts the **Chambers County** FIS by reference alongside Harris's, and Chambers is where Baytown's limited annexation — and Grand Port — sits. Suggestive, not dispositive. (Sec. 110-32 also adopts FEMA-issued **PRELIMINARY** maps by reference, recorded as `adoptsPreliminaryMaps`.)
- **THE NEW STATE: `unresolvedApplicability` — rule known, REACH unknown**, kept deliberately separate from `unmodelledCandidates` (rule unknown) because they are different problems with different remedies (ask the city vs transcribe the ordinance). Such a candidate is refused the governing slot and blocks `settled`, so the panel shows Baytown's number ALONGSIDE the county's, labelled unresolved, and never silently picks one. **It is DECLARED BY THE RULE RECORD (`limitedPurposeScope`), never inferred from the candidate kind** — so Houston's Ch. 19 ETJ rule, which sixteen of the owner's sites depend on, is provably unaffected (asserted).
- **ONE FACT, ONE HOME:** the applicability clause lives in `floodplainRules.LIMITED_PURPOSE_SCOPE` and the buildability record IMPORTS it; a test asserts the two agree. Two copies of one clause is the shape that drifts.
- **A REAL FINDING REPORTED RATHER THAN SILENTLY CHANGED:** inside Baytown's full-purpose limits the resolver still ranks Harris County above Baytown (strictest-wins), so the county's number prints on land the city administers. That is the existing deliberate design (B209508) and it errs conservatively — but it is not obviously correct, and changing it would move numbers across the whole portfolio. Pinned by test, raised for the owner, not altered under a Baytown ticket.
- **PARTIAL BY DESIGN:** the excerpt read was the ELEVATION standard, so `trigger` is transcribed (it follows from Sec. 110-31 + Sec. 110-26) while `ratio` / `floodwayPolicy` / `offsetScope` were NOT in that text and stay null. The record NAMES both halves (`partial.transcribed` / `partial.notTranscribed`); `test/floodplainRules.test.js`'s old UNREADABLE class is replaced by a PARTIAL class asserting the two are disjoint and that every claimed-transcribed field is non-null.
- Sandbox: `test/baytownFlood.test.js` (23). Texas golden master regenerated — **all 14 differing paths proven to be under a `baytown` key; no other Texas value moved.** Full suite 10,969 green, lint 0 errors, build green.


### B420256 — One id can name TWO live rows, and the commit results were keyed by id alone `[Site Planner]` (bug) #site-planner #sync #persistence  *(audit finding with a live reproducer, 2026-08-13. Minted **B420256 / V215200** LATE via `git fetch origin main && npm run next-id -- --against-main`, from this branch's reserved block B420256–B420271 · V215200–V215215 against `origin/main` 01f66ec. **DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open / ⏳ Verify / Done across `byId`, `pairing`, `results`, `skey`, `unique within a batch`, `B1116`, `B1117`, `B1341`, `B377888`, `B1113`.** Neighbours, none of them this: **B1117** owns the atomic-rollback PATH this fix corrects inside, but is about all-or-nothing semantics, not about which result belongs to which op; **B1341** is the group CAS; **B377888** is the same CLASS (a kindless decision about a composite key) in the DELETE path, and is the reason this one was looked for. Net-new.)*
`[]` **⛔ SHIPPED 2026-08-13. `Verify: live` → V215200 (MERGED ≠ LIVE).**
- Verify: live → **V215200** (`Blocker: auth` + `real-data` — the collision exists on one signed-in plan, and the pairing only runs on a real multi-op commit against the live RPC).
- Origin: audit finding 2026-08-13; shipped the same session.
- **THE DEFECT.** `site_elements`' primary key is **(site_id, kind, id)** — deliberately, because legacy pre-salt ids are reused verbatim across collections. `elementSync.js` keyed a commit batch's per-op results by **`r.id` alone**, in two places (`processResults` and `onAtomicRollback`), under the comment *"ids are unique within a batch"*. **That comment is false in production.** With two ops for one id in a batch the second `byId.set()` overwrote the first, and every lookup for that id handed one element the OTHER's result — wrong rev, wrong status, silently. Every other lookup in the file goes through `skey(kind, id)`; these two forgot the kind.
- **THE REPRODUCER IS THE OWNER'S OWN DATA.** Site `smqh3au6aeb4` (Katz / Plan 1) holds `e6327` **twice, both LIVE** — kind `el` (a building, rev 2) and kind `markup` (rev 2) — and both rows carry the **identical `updated_at` of 2026-06-29 15:36:02.112**, i.e. they were written by ONE batch, which is exactly the collision condition. Confirmed against production this session. **The plan was NOT touched** and nothing was written to `public.site_elements`: `e6327` under two kinds is legitimate live data and the code must tolerate it (same reasoning as B384432 — make the ambiguity safe, do not destroy it). A sweep of the whole live table finds exactly one such pair, plus the ordinary `tombstone`-beside-a-real-kind pairs the schema has always produced.
- **⛔ THE OBVIOUS FIX IS NOT AVAILABLE, AND SHIPPING IT WOULD HAVE BROKEN EVERY WRITE.** The audit prescribed `skey(r.kind, r.id)`. **There is no `r.kind`.** `commit_elements` builds each result from `v_id` alone (`db/site_elements.sql`): `{id, status, rev}`, plus `row` on a miss. Keying by a field the server never sends misses on **every** op, so every op would fall to the `element-no-result` branch and be requeued forever. What the RPC **does** guarantee is ORDER — it loops over `p_ops` appending exactly one result per op — and `flush()` builds `ops = batch.map(opFor)`, so `results[i]` belongs to `batch[i]`; `elementApi`'s own contract already documents it ("same order as `ops`").
- **THE FIX.** One helper, `pairCommitResults`, used by both settle paths and nothing else. It pairs **positionally** and **VERIFIES** the pairing rather than trusting it: the ids must agree, and so must the kind whenever a returned `row` names one. A response failing that check falls back to a per-id **FIFO** that consumes each result once (preferring one whose row names this op's kind) and reports `element-results-unaligned` (LOUD-FAILURE — a pairing we cannot justify must never look like a clean one). An empty response is unchanged: it still reports `element-no-result` per op and requeues. The false comment is **deleted**, not reworded.
- **PROVEN RED BEFORE THE FIX.** `test/elementResultPairing.test.js` — 7 cases driving the real engine over the Katz collision: **5 failed, 2 passed** on the unfixed code (the two that passed are the deliberate controls — distinct ids, and a missing result — so the test is not simply asserting the new implementation). All 7 green after. The five that were red: a conflict on `el` beside an `ok` on `markup` (and its mirror), a `deleted` result tombstoning the wrong kind, the B1117 atomic rollback adopting the wrong fresh rev, and the out-of-order response.
- **THE SWEEP THE AUDIT ASKED FOR — every other id-alone lookup in the element-row path, and what it is.** These two were the only kindless lookups over the composite key. `elementRows.js`'s `rowsToModel` is already explicitly aware of this class (its comment names *"the legacy e6327 class"*) and subtracts live ids of ANY kind from `deletedIds`; `foldJournal`'s `find`/`filter` by id run **inside `out[field]`**, where the kind is already fixed by the field, so they are correct; `assemblyDigest.js` reasons only over `kind: "el"`. The other `byId` maps in the tree (Library files, Notes sketch boxes, folder rows) key domains whose real identity IS the id. No further change needed.
- **Verified here:** the 7 new tests · the full suite green (**542 files / 10,931 tests**, incl. `elementSync` 65, `assemblyTear` 54, `assemblyGroupCas` 23, `deleteVsCreate` 7) · lint 0 errors · build green · bundle audit **passes** (`siteRouteJsBytes` +0.7 KB and `totalJsBytes` +0.7 KB, both inside the headroom band — the helper replaces two inline loops, so the growth is its comment-free code, not a new dependency). **Bundle TARGETS untouched** (B414480 raised baselines on the owner's decision and left targets deliberately).
- **NOT this item, filed separately as B420257:** the `element-create-collision` assertion that fired twice in 36 h. Checked, not assumed — neither reported id has more than one row, so a kind collision cannot explain it.

### B407328 — The screening hydrology engine rode the boot path of every page load `[Site Planner / perf]` (task) #site-planner #perf #floodplain  *(owner ask 2026-08-13: "take a pass" at putting the app on a diet, after main's push build was found red on three bundle budgets for 12+ consecutive merges. Minted **B407328 / V209424** LATE via `git fetch origin main && npm run next-id -- --against-main`, from this branch's reserved block B407328–B407343 against `origin/main` d320e02. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open / ⏳ Verify / Done across `bundle`, `boot path`, `lazy`, `screeningBfe`, `siteRouteJsBytes`, `largestChunkBytes`, `B1042`, `B1095`, `B1130`: the prior splits are the export path (B1042), terrain (B1095) and the hover/identify pair (B1130) — the screening engine has never been split and no item covers it.)*
`[ ]` **⏳ SHIPPED 2026-08-13. `Verify: live` → V209424 (MERGED ≠ LIVE).**
- Verify: live → **V209424** (`Blocker: real-data` + `live-GIS` — the study only runs on an unstudied Zone A site, and needs FEMA / 3DEP / SSURGO / NOAA-PFDS, all egress-blocked in the sandbox).
- Origin: owner ask 2026-08-13; shipped the same session.
- **THE DEFECT.** The app's only real hydrology + hydraulics derivation — `screeningBfe.js` + `screeningBfeSite.js` + `upstreamArea.js` + `channelSection.js` — runs in exactly ONE place: `checkDrainage`'s async block, gated on an unstudied Zone A site with no published or manual 1% surface. Every byte of it was nevertheless on the Site route's critical path, downloaded on every load of every site, because a handful of CONSTANTS and three pure COPY functions were exported from the same modules and are read by the RENDER BODY. **A static import of one export pulls the whole module** — tree-shaking drops unused exports, never an export a sibling still uses — so the render body's need for `screeningBfeHeadline` was enough to hoist the entire engine.
- **THE FIX** is the `terrainGate.js` / `terrainLazy.js` shape already used twice in this folder: a dependency-free LEAF (`screeningBfeCopy.js`) holding the words, the constants and the acres/lots threshold test, with `screeningBfe.js` / `screeningBfeSite.js` re-exporting all of it so **no importer changed**. `SitePlanner.jsx` keeps the leaf statically and reaches the MATH through `import("./lib/screeningBfeSite.js")` inside `checkDrainage`.
- **MEASURED, before → after:** `siteRouteJsBytes` 2471.0 → 2457.7 KB · `largestChunkBytes` 1554.3 → 1541.0 KB (**−13.3 KB each**) · 43.6 KB of source moved into its own lazy chunk · `totalJsBytes` 4969.9 → 4970.7 KB (**+0.8 KB of chunk overhead — splitting moves bytes, it does not delete them**).
- **NO WALL-CLOCK COST on the branch that uses it:** the engine's `import()` is started BEFORE the `await` on the three data pulls it needs and awaited only at first use, so the module download overlaps network round-trips that were already happening. A failed chunk fetch rejects at that await and lands in the existing `catch`, reporting the named LOUD-FAILURE "could not run" state like any other outage.
- **THREE THINGS NOT TO UNDO** (all three re-open the defect while lint, tests and build stay green): the leaf may never import the engine or anything that does; the constants in `screeningBfe.js` are IMPORTED-then-re-exported rather than forwarded with a bare `export … from`, because its own functions reference them in scope (the trap `titleReader.js` documents); and `floodplainMitigation.js` — also on the boot path — takes its two constants from the LEAF, never from the engine.
- **Verified here:** full suite green (541 files / 10,917 tests, incl. `test/screeningBfe.test.js` driving the engine through the re-exports) · lint 0 errors · build green · headless boot on the built app confirms the planner paints and **the engine chunk is not among the 13 scripts fetched on load**.
- **⛔ WHAT THIS DOES NOT FIX, stated plainly: main's push build is STILL RED, and one more split will not fix it either.** Remaining after this change: `siteRouteJsBytes` −41.0 KB · `largestChunkBytes` −35.6 KB · `totalJsBytes` −183.4 KB. The first two are reachable with ~3 more splits of this size (candidates, measured source in the chunk: `proposedSurface.js` 30.7 KB · `pondRouting.js` 25.4 KB + `outletStructure.js` + `stageStorageDischarge.js` · `detentionCriteria.js` 46.0 KB · `roundabout.js` 19.0 KB · `planClipboard.js` 17.0 KB — each imported by `SitePlanner.jsx` alone, so each is a self-contained job). **`totalJsBytes` is NOT reachable that way at all** — it counts every emitted chunk, so moving bytes between chunks is a no-op for it, and closing 183 KB means deleting ~12% of the app. Audited for the usual suspects and there is no fat: **zero modules duplicated across chunks**, **zero dead code in the bundle** (27 unreferenced source files exist but none is bundled, so deleting them saves 0 bytes), and every heavy dependency is genuinely used and already lazily chunked (`pdfjs-dist` reads PDFs, `pdf-lib` writes them, `@anthropic-ai/sdk` is behind two dynamic imports, `clipper-lib` is core planner geometry). **That makes `totalJsBytes` an owner decision — optimize further, or ratchet the baseline with a reason on the record — not an engineering task**, and `docs/PERF-BUDGETS.md` says raising a baseline needs the same justification as any other product decision. Raised with the owner 2026-08-13.

### B393172 — A plain selection click pushed an undo entry that changed nothing `[Site Planner]` (bug) #site-planner #selection #ui  *(owner chat amendment 2026-08-12, arrived as NEW-5, found live on planyr.io. Net-new.)*
`[ ]` **⏳ SHIPPED 2026-08-12. `Verify: live` → V195265.**
- Verify: live → **V195265** (`Blocker: real-data` — the signed-in half: no `site_elements` row is written by a selection click).
- Origin: filed 2026-08-12 from chat; shipped the same session.
- **THE REPRO, reproduced here.** Load `smsqi16s9ej4` fresh — Undo correctly DISABLED — single left-click inside Building 3, no drag, no modifier, pointer does not move: Undo turns ENABLED while the database is byte-identical (md5 over all 50 `site_elements` rows `e6c520d7dba3b5fa7520aae3012545a9` before and after; `updated_at` does not advance). **Reproduced in this session on the pre-fix rule, on the owner's real Bain plan, by the new e2e spec.**
- **WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN IT LOOKS:** Undo-enabled is the only signal a user or an operator has that a plan has been modified. Once selection alone arms it, a plan you merely LOOKED at is indistinguishable from one you edited — which cost real time, six clicks and six entries, and an unwind to be sure.
- **THE FIX IS AT THE PREDICATE, NOT AT THE 210 `pushHistory()` CALL SITES.** A press handler pushes the pre-mutation snapshot BEFORE it knows whether a mutation follows — that is the transaction model, and unpicking it per call site would be 210 chances to get the drag threshold wrong, which the item expressly rules out. `canUndo` now asks the question the button claims to answer: **does any frame DIFFER from the live state?** `undo()` has always asked exactly that (its `keyOf` dedup); the button never did.
- **IT IS A REFERENCE SCAN, NOT A STRINGIFY.** `keyOf` is a JSON.stringify of the whole plan and this is read on every toolbar render. React replaces the collection arrays on every real mutation, so an identical set of references is proof nothing was committed. The component pays the exact check once per real change (`canUndoNow`, memoised on the drawn collections + the history tick), never per frame.
- **THE SIBLING, CHECKED AND ANSWERED: Redo's state was always right; the CONTROL was mislabelled.** A disabled `<button>` carries no `aria-disabled` attribute at all, so a checker reading that attribute got null and reported the empty Redo control as enabled. Both buttons now carry `aria-disabled` beside `disabled`. Not a state bug — `canRedo()` is `future.length > 0` and the future is empty on a fresh load.
- Sandbox: `test/history.test.js` (+6, incl. the six-clicks case and the reallocated-but-equal frame) and the e2e spec **undo-selection-only**, which asserts BOTH directions and is **mutation-proven** — restoring the old predicate turns it red at exactly the reported symptom.

### B391072 (×3) — A purged note reappeared in the LIVE list hours later, because rule 0 was CONDITIONAL `[Notes]` (bug) #notes #sync #persistence  *(owner chat block, 2026-08-12 — NEW-0, flagged HIGH and as a recurrence of an item twice reported fixed, with revisions: purged and verified absent at tree rev 1061, back in the live list at rev 1211, gone again at 1274. Minted **B391072** from this branch's reserved block B391072–B391087 against origin/main a8c52bd. **DEDUPE-FIRST — this takes the THIRD count on its own number rather than a new one**, because it is the same guarantee failing for a third distinct reason: B357011 shipped the rule, B364016 found `migrate` wiping the ledger it wrote, and this is the rule never running on one of the two paths that adopt a tree. Same promise, same item, `(×3)`.)*
`[ ]` **⏳ IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-12 — awaiting V193168 on his own account, HOURS later, not minutes.**
- Verify: live → **V193168** (`Blocker: auth`)
- Origin: filed 2026-08-11 from chat · recurrence 2026-08-12.
- Recurrence: 2026-08-12 — purged and verified absent across three reloads at rev 1061; back in the LIVE page list at rev 1211 with `deleted_at`, `purged_at` and a NULL `doc` still on its row; gone again at 1274.
- **⛔ THE CAUSE: RULE 0 ONLY EVER RAN ON THE MERGE PATH.** The seed has two ways to take the server's tree. When this device owes an edit it MERGES — and that path honours the tombstones. When it owes nothing it ADOPTED THE SERVER'S TREE WHOLESALE — no tombstone filter at all, **and this device's own ledger discarded in the same breath**. So any client still holding a pre-purge tree could put the page back on the server, and every other device would then adopt it and forget it had ever known better. It healed itself at 1274 once a dirty merge finally ran, which is exactly what a conditional rule looks like from outside — and is why "it cleared itself" was the clue rather than the reassurance.
- **THE FIX MAKES IT UNCONDITIONAL.** The adopt path is now expressed as a merge against a local side that is NOTHING BUT THE LEDGER, so it reuses rule 0 and rule 5 rather than growing a second copy of them: the server's structure wins in full, every tombstoned id is refused, the two ledgers are carried forward as one — and **if the filter actually removed something the correction is pushed back up**, because a purge that has to be re-applied on every device on every load is not a purge.
- **AND A LIVE PAGE WHOSE BODY IS PURGED IS LIFTED OUT AND TOMBSTONED**, which is the half that speaks to the account he has right now: a page the SERVER says is purged has nothing behind it, so rendering it offers a note that cannot be opened, restored or explained. Its children are RESCUED, never destroyed.
- **HIS FOUR ACCEPTANCE CONDITIONS ARE FOUR TESTS**, each named for the condition it answers: (1) a reload · (2) **a second client pushing a tree that predates the purge** — the ghost, and the one that had no protection at all · (3) no sweep prunes the ledger, proven across reads, writes, merges and adopts · (4) **hours later**, six adopt cycles deep, because the ledger's own expiry is 400 days and not a session. Plus: the live-side heal, and that a child added under a purged page is rescued.
- **⛔ WHAT IS OWED (V193168), AND IT MUST NOT BE CHECKED THE SAME WAY TWICE.** He said it plainly: *"Do not close this on another same-session test."* The check is a re-look HOURS after a purge, on his account, with another window in play.

- Verify: live → **V187136** (`Blocker: live-GIS` + `auth`)
- Origin: owner chat block 2026-08-13, NEW-1. Verbatim: *"the screen flashes on every ctrl z, that doesn't seem necessary."*
- **THE CAUSE, exactly as the block diagnosed it.** `applySnapshot` ran the layer restore UNCONDITIONALLY on every undo and every redo, and `applyOnOverrides` (`lib/layerPrefs.js`) built `const out = {}` and returned it every call — it carefully preserved each INNER layer state's identity and then threw that away by allocating the map around them. Three effects key off the `overlays` identity: the layer staging/sync effect (whose cleanup clears its intervals and idle callbacks and then re-stages and RE-ADDS the entire Leaflet overlay stack), the coverage recompute, and the persist. So an undo of a plain geometry edit rebuilt every GIS layer on the map.
- **FIXED AT BOTH ENDS, deliberately, because either alone leaves a way back in.** (a) `applyOnOverrides` **and** its `applyAboveOverrides` twin now return the INPUT object when nothing moved — the guard lives with the value, so no caller present or future can trip this by being written carelessly, and React bails out of the setState on its own. (b) `applySnapshot` compares `overridesSig`/`aboveSig` against `prevLayerSig`/`prevAboveSig` (the signatures the persist effect already keeps at "currently accounted for") and skips `setOverlays` / `setLayerOverrides` / `setLayerAbove` entirely on a match, so React is not even asked.
- **⛔ THE INSTRUMENT IS HALF THE ITEM, and without it this defect is unobservable** (DANGEROUS-MEANS-UNOBSERVABLE). The layer SET is byte-identical either side of the bug — the existing `window.__plannerLayers` hook reported `ids` and `on`, both unchanged — so **every check in this repo passes on a build that rebuilds the stack on every Ctrl+Z**. The hook now also reports `identityEpoch`, incremented by the very effect whose deps are `[overlays]`, so "an undo that touched no layer rebuilt no layer" is a NUMBER rather than something a human has to catch out of the corner of their eye. Read-only, same `__PLANYR_E2E` gate, and free (the effect already ran exactly when the identity changed). **MUTATION-PROVEN:** restoring the pre-fix rule takes the epoch from 2 to 4 across two undos and turns that spec red.
- **THE SECOND HALF THE BLOCK ASKED ME TO JUDGE — a still-valid selection now SURVIVES an undo, and it is a deliberate call, not a silent one.** `applySnapshot` did `setSel(null)` unconditionally, so undoing a nudge also closed the Properties panel you were working in — a second thing moving on screen for an edit that only moved geometry. A selection is a POINTER at a feature, and a snapshot that still holds that feature has not invalidated it, so `sel` and `multi` are now FILTERED against the restored collections instead of blanked: a feature the undo deleted drops out, everything else stays put. What is STILL cleared unconditionally, and why: `selVtx` / `splitPath` / `drillId` / `typeMenu` address internal structure (a vertex index, a cut path, a group drill, an open menu) that a restore really can renumber or dissolve. **B743's invariant is stronger, not weaker** — nothing stale can survive a filter that tests membership — and its source guard was REWRITTEN to assert that property rather than the old literal.
- Guards: the repo-root `test/` suite **undoLayerStability** (14 — identity stability both ways, the signature guard, every layer writer proven to be inside it, every selectable kind covered, and the real layer-toggle case proven to still revert) · **deletePlan** (38, its applySnapshot assertion rewritten) · the e2e spec **undo-dock-plan-menu** (`B385040` — the epoch across undo AND redo, selection survival driven through a real nudge, and the deleted-selection case; mutation-proven).

### B385041 — A building's dock walls moved because you resized it `[Site Planner / dockZones]` (bug) #site-planner #ui  *(owner chat block 2026-08-13, arrived as NEW-2 with the offending line quoted. Minted **B385041 / V187137** from this branch's reserved block; code, tests and commits keep the provisional `NEW-2` label. Net-new.)*
`[ ]` **⏳ IMPLEMENTED + PROVEN HEADLESS 2026-08-13 (real drags, mutation-proven 4/4 red) — awaiting V187137 on his own cross-dock plan.**
- Verify: live → **V187137** (`Blocker: real-data` — the repro he described is on a signed-in plan of his)
- Origin: owner chat block 2026-08-13, NEW-2. Verbatim: *"if I had a cross-dock and I shrink it lengthwise, it almost seemed to recompute where the docks went versus where the parking went, when I made it deeper than it was long. I don't really want it to do that. Let me just play around instead of correcting it for me — it doesn't help if I'm just trying to figure out what will and won't fit."*
- **THE CAUSE IS ONE LINE, and the block found it.** `dockZones.js` opened `dockSidesFor` with `const longSides = el.w >= el.h ? ["top","bottom"] : ["left","right"]` — which walls are loaded was a LIVE function of whichever dimension was larger AT READ TIME. Shrink a cross-dock building past square and the entire dock assembly (truck courts, trailer parking, buffers, sidewalks, dog-ears) rotated 90° MID-DRAG; and because the comparison is `>=`, one foot either side of square flipped it and flipped it back, so dragging THROUGH square did it twice.
- **THE FIX — derive by default, preserve once established, the pattern already used for dog-ears, side parking, trailer length and zone spans.** `el.dockAxis` (`"x"` = the top/bottom pair, `"y"` = left/right) is stamped when the orientation is first established and a resize can never re-derive it. Three stamping points, chosen so no plan changes appearance: **creation** (from the box he just drew) · a **load-time heal** (`healDockAxes`, run before the stranded-zone prune, stamping the axis a plan CURRENTLY RENDERS — so a record saved before this field existed keeps its walls exactly where they are and merely stops re-deriving them) · and **`refitChildren`**, the one funnel every building resize goes through (grip drag, edge drag, typed Length/Depth, the on-canvas dimension editor), stamped from the PRE-resize footprint so a row seeded mid-session by the sync engine is covered too. Pure aspect-ratio derivation survives only for a building with no established orientation.
- **A STORED `dockSide` NOW WINS, ALWAYS.** It was honoured only `if (longSides.includes(el.dockSide))`, i.e. an explicit user choice was discarded by an implicit one the instant the aspect ratio flipped. A named wall names an axis, so on an established building it is the more specific statement and it decides. **The `established` gate is not ceremony:** a legacy record can carry a `dockSide` that disagrees with what it RENDERS (that is what the old validation did for a living), and honouring it unconditionally on load would strand — and therefore prune — the zones bonded to the walls the plan actually shows. The heal normalises such a `dockSide` to the wall the plan is really docked on rather than enshrining the stale one.
- **A DELIBERATE WAY TO TURN THE DOCK FACE, since it can no longer happen by accident** — a `Dock face` row in the building's Loading group stating the current walls plus a `turn ⟳` action (`rotateBuildingDockFace`): stamp, prune the apron the old walls owned, relay the stack onto the walls that are loaded now, one undo frame. One row, no explanatory prose (PANEL-BREVITY; the panel-copy budget is unchanged — this is the Properties panel, not a budgeted yield/pond region, and it replaced nothing because nothing said this before).
- **B548 HOLDS AGAINST THE STORED VALUE.** `footprintAxes`, `footprintDepth`, `footprintLength`, the massing panel, the column grid and the dock-door count all read `dockSidesFor`, so they follow the stored orientation for free: past square, depth stays perpendicular to the loaded wall and length parallel to it, which is exactly the "it recomputed where the docks went versus where the parking went" he saw.
- **THE OWNER PRINCIPLE, ENCODED — and the audit he asked for, with an honest result.** *"Let me just play around instead of correcting it for me."* I swept the other resize-time re-derivations in `refitChildren` / `relayoutAllSides` / `relayoutWallKids` / `siteModel`'s heals for the same overreach. **Finding: this was the last one of its kind, and that is because the previous three were already fixed** — `alongLen` (B1123: a pin now requires a gesture aimed at that field), a bonded child's position and span (B1340 ×2: derived unless stamped, and the stamp is written only by a gesture aimed at it), and the along-wall anchor (B1356). Every remaining resize-time derivation is of a value that is DERIVED BY DEFINITION (a bonded child's offset from its host, a zone's depth from its box, the column grid) and none of them can overwrite a stored intent. **What made this one survive the previous three passes is worth recording:** those all guarded a value that has a stored field to protect, and each fix asked "may this gesture write it?". Dock orientation had **no stored field at all**, so there was nothing for those audits to find — the failure was an absent field, not a bad write rule.
- Guards: the repo-root `test/` suite **dockOrientation** (14, several of which REPLAY the pre-fix rule verbatim and require the stored answer to differ, so a tidy back to an aspect-ratio read goes red) · **dockZones** (65, unchanged and still green — the derived path is byte-identical for an un-established building) · the e2e spec **undo-dock-plan-menu** (`B385041` — a real edge-grip drag in FEET taking a cross-dock building down past square and back, the dock face read off the painted `data-dock-apron` band rather than off the record, plus the single-load choice, the readouts and the deliberate turn; **mutation-proven: restoring the live derivation turns all four red**).
- Before/after: `ui-audit/shots/b385041-before-shrunk-past-square.png` (identical 250 × 300 geometry, docks flipped onto the left/right walls, dimension reading the 250 axis) vs `…-after-…png` (docks still on top/bottom, dimension reading the 300 depth).

It cannot feed back on itself: an out-of-flow slot changes neither side group's width.
