- **THE REPORT.** A second tab of the owner's own account produced ~5 banners naming a collaborator who was never there.
- **⛔ THE MECHANISM WAS NOT THE UID COMPARISON, which is why reading the report literally would have found nothing.** `createNameResolver` already answered *"you (another window)"* for `uid === selfUid`. `selfUid` was **SNAPSHOTTED** from `activeUid()` when the sync engine was built — and that is null until the auth session resolves, so on any load where the planner mounted first it stayed null for the WHOLE plan session. Every row then fell past the comparison to the final fallback, **"a teammate"**, which invented a person out of a missing value.
- **Two changes, and both are needed — fixing either alone still leaves a way to invent a person.** `selfUid` is now a GETTER, read at resolve time, so a late sign-in is picked up. And the fallback is no longer a person: an actor we cannot PROVE is a different account resolves as this account in another tab. A roster MISS on a real team site still resolves as *a teammate* — that one IS a proven different account, and staying silent about it would be the opposite error.
- **The wording is a MODEL fact, not a string.** The resolver returns `{ name, self }` and `toastForSyncEvent` takes `self`, so every attributing row of the matrix has a sentence that names a TAB — *"…was deleted in another tab of yours"* — with no name in it. `self` defaults to TRUE, so a caller that forgets it gets the unattributed wording: wrong in the harmless direction.
- **The same snapshot bug was in `elementSync`'s own `selfUid`**, where it silently disabled B1116's and B1099's foreign-author gates for the session. Fixed in the same commit; it fails open exactly as before when there is genuinely no id to compare.
- **Sandbox evidence.** `test/editorNames.test.js` +3 (incl. the pre-fix construction asserted directly), `test/conflictMatrix.test.js` +3 (every attributing row × both directions, plus the forgotten-`self` default). Full suite green.

- **⛔ AND THE THING BOTH DERIVATIONS MISSED, which may be the actual cause of the feel: A GATE THAT IS PURELY ABSOLUTE IN px/ft PUTS A BIGGER SHARE OF A SMALLER SCREEN UNDER THE BUILDING.** At 0.359 Building 3 was **283 px — about a third of the ~945 px canvas inside his 1600 px monitor, but closer to HALF of the ~566 px canvas inside the 1191 px laptop viewport he now works on.** SITE-size independence was the property #990 was asked to protect and it is protected here unchanged; SCREEN-size independence was never checked and is not the same variable.
- **⛔ SO THE GATE IS NO LONGER PURELY ABSOLUTE, AND THAT IS SAID PLAINLY RATHER THAN SLIPPED IN.** The floor is the EARLIER of **(a)** the owner-set `FEAT_EDIT_MIN_PPF` 0.25 px/ft and **(b)** a **VIEWPORT CAP** — the zoom at which a reference industrial span (`FEAT_EDIT_REF_SPAN_FT` 800 ft, a CONSTANT) would reach a quarter of the canvas width. **It is still SITE-size independent, which is the property that was actually asked for:** nothing in it reads the plan, the site, the selected building or any drawn geometry, so a 30-acre and a 900-acre site on the same screen arm at the identical zoom. What it now reads is the canvas.
- **MEASURED, on his two real screens.** ~945 px canvas → the cap is 0.295, so the absolute floor governs at 0.25 → **B3 is 197 px, 21% of the canvas**. ~566 px canvas → the cap arms first at 0.177 → **B3 is 139 px, 25%**. Against **30% / 50%** at the superseded 0.359. The two screens now agree about SHARE, which is what he was reacting to. Arithmetically the cap binds on any canvas narrower than **800 px** and on none wider.
- **⛔ THE ORIGINAL B312544 DEFECT CANNOT RETURN THROUGH THE VIEWPORT TERM, at any canvas width, and that is a proof rather than a hope.** Whole-site zoom is itself `canvasW ÷ siteSpanFt`, so both sides scale with the canvas and their ratio is a CONSTANT: the cap sits `siteSpanFt ÷ 3200` tighter than whole-site zoom — 1.48× on his ≈4,725 ft Bain frontage, on a phone exactly as on a monitor. A narrower screen moves the floor and the overview zoom together. Asserted across seven canvas widths.
- **THE TWO PROPERTIES #990 GOT RIGHT ARE KEPT AND STILL ASSERTED.** (1) It is a ZOOM question, never a fraction of the drawn object. (2) **CLICKABLE THROUGHOUT THE FADE** — and this is now proven by a real HIT TEST rather than by a computed style: the e2e spec asks `elementFromPoint` at each faded control disc's own centre and requires the answer to be inside the control group.
- **GUARDS — the mutation checks moved to the new value, both of them, and a THIRD was added.** `test/featureEditZoom.test.js` (24) replays all three superseded rules verbatim: the pre-B312544 rule (no gate) must arm across his whole-site band on every canvas · the **#990 44 px rule must refuse** every zoom in the band this opens · **and so must #994's 0.359**. Plus: the floor asserted NOT to equal either failed derivation (a third re-derivation goes red on the spot), the crossover width, the two real canvases, the SHARE agreement between them with the purely-absolute rule replayed as the counter-example, the constant cap-to-overview ratio, the clamp, an unreadable canvas falling back to the stated floor rather than guessing, monotonicity and the no-invisible-but-clickable band on all three canvas cases.
- **⛔ AND THE E2E SPEC HAD TO CHANGE ITS PREMISE, which is worth knowing:** a blank plan opens at 0.35 px/ft, which is now ABOVE the floor, so "the default view shows nothing" is no longer true and asserting it would have been asserting the old number. The spec now wheels OUT to an overview first, and asks the library for the floor **in force on the canvas Playwright actually opened** rather than for a constant — the viewport half of the gate is a function of a measured canvas, which no source reading can evaluate.

The zones are now one-directional: **LEFT `0 1 auto` (max 60%)** takes the width it needs and shrinks only after the centre has already collapsed · **CENTRE `1 1 0%`** takes what is LEFT OVER, so its width never depends on its own content · **RIGHT `0 0 auto`** — the account controls were never the contended pair. ### B366384 — Sharing an ALREADY-SHARED project reported "this project isn't in the cloud yet" — a row COUNT read as EXISTENCE `[Site Planner / teams]` (bug) #site-planner #auth #sync  *(arrived 2026-08-11 as provisional NEW-1 in an owner chat block. Minted **B366384–B366386 / V161952** LATE via `git fetch origin main && npm run next-id -- --against-main`, from this branch's reserved block B366384–B366399. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open + ⏳ Verify + Done across `share`, `sharing`, `team`, `team_id`, `set_project_team`, `B406`, `B486`, `B714`, `B326416`: **B406** built the manual share flow, **B714** made `team_id` insert-only on the content path, **B326416–B326419** added default-share for NEW projects and the deny-by-default Postgres guard. None of them is "the share control lies about an already-shared project". Net-new.)*
`[x]` **⏳ SHIPPED, and the fix is PROVEN AT THE SOURCE against the production database.**
- Verify: live — V161952 (`Blocker: auth` — the sandbox proxy CORS-blocks Supabase sign-in, so the signed-in *click-through* cannot be driven here. The database half is NOT pending: it was verified directly, see below.)
- Origin: owner chat block, 2026-08-11 — filed and shipped the same session.
- **THE REPORT, verbatim.** *"when I tried to share 8 South it gave me this pop up at the bottom left, which is obviously not true because it's been in cloud for weeks, if not a month already."* The popup: *"This project isn't in the cloud yet — open it once to sync, then share."*
- **GROUND TRUTH (read from production, not assumed).** `8 South` = group `smqiljx5fngg`, **version 587**, `team_id` already `454aa114…` (team **HIP Houston**, 3 members). Exactly **2 of 34** projects carry a team: 8 South and RICHEY (`smraxmrwiyzk`). So the project was both unambiguously in the cloud AND unambiguously already shared.
- **THE MECHANISM.** `set_project_team`'s UPDATE carries `and team_id is distinct from p_team_id`, so re-sharing to the team it ALREADY has legitimately writes **0 rows** and returns 0. `MapFinder.doShare` read that as `if (teamId && r.sites === 0) → "isn't in the cloud yet"`. **"0 rows changed" is not "0 rows exist"** — and the message therefore fired precisely in the case where it was most wrong.
- **AND IT WAS WORSE THAN REPORTED: on this database that string was UNREACHABLE-WHEN-TRUE.** The genuine not-in-cloud case never got as far as the `return` — the RPC raises `No project of yours with that id.` first. So post-migration a 0 could only ever mean *already in that state*, and the sentence was false **100% of the time it was shown**.
- **THE CODEBASE ALREADY KNEW THIS IDIOM BITES.** `storage.js` documents that `cloudDelete` returning `removed:0` means **RLS REFUSED**, not "nothing was there". The share path never got the same care; it does now.
- **THE FIX — three answers at the source, no integer for the caller to interpret.** New RPC `set_project_team_state` (`db/team_share_state.sql`, **applied to production 2026-08-11**) returns `{outcome: not-found|changed|already, matched, changed, already, plans, foreign, mismatched}`. `lib/sharing.js` normalises all three tiers (state RPC → the older integer RPC, which RAISES for not-found so a 0 from it can only mean `already` → the pre-migration direct UPDATE, the one tier where 0 really does mean none exist). `doShare` branches on `outcome`; **only `not-found` may show that message.**
- **VERIFIED ON HIS REAL ROWS**, impersonating the owner, writing nothing (all three answered `changed:0`): re-sharing 8 South to its current team → `outcome:"already", matched:1, mismatched:0` (was: the false popup) · a non-existent group → `outcome:"not-found", matched:0` · Goose Creek (4 plans) private→private → `outcome:"already", matched:4, plans:4`.
- Guards: repo-root `test/` suite **shareMirror** (18 — incl. a mutation check that `r.sites === 0` is gone from `doShare`, and that the message's nearest enclosing condition is the `outcome` test).

### B366385 — The sharing pointer never SURVIVED a pull, so every "is this shared?" indicator was blank at once `[Site Planner / teams]` (bug) #site-planner #auth #sync #persistence  *(arrived 2026-08-11 as provisional NEW-2 in the same owner chat block. See B366384's provenance for the DEDUPE-FIRST sweep.)*
`[x]` **⏳ SHIPPED. This is the root cause of the whole complaint — the other two are only visible once this one is fixed, which is why the owner sequenced it first.**
- Verify: live — V161952 (`Blocker: auth`)
- Origin: owner chat block, 2026-08-11 — filed and shipped the same session.
- **THE REPORT, verbatim.** *"It's not very clear when a site is shared. I don't really know how to know if a site is shared… And when I do click, it isn't clear that it has been shared, and options still pop up to share it. So it makes it seem like it hasn't been."*
- **⚠ THE CHAT BLOCK'S DIAGNOSIS WAS CLOSE BUT NOT THE MECHANISM, and the fix location differs.** It said *"grep teamId storage.js returns NOTHING, so it never persists into the local site model."* The grep is accurate; the inference is not. `teamId` **is** a Site Model field (`siteModel.js`, schema v8) and it **does** round-trip a local save. The real defect is one function further on.
- **THE MECHANISM.** `mergeSiteContent(a, b)` resolves scalars by taking the copy with the newer `updatedAt` — correct for CONTENT, wrong for a server-owned column. B458's immediate mirror write advances the **LOCAL** `updatedAt` on every edit while the cloud push lags (stated verbatim in `storage.js`'s own B460 note), so on `pullCloud` the local copy is routinely newer and `...newer` took its **stale `teamId: null`**, discarding `sites.team_id`. Every pull, every project. Three surfaces read `s.teamId` and so went blank together: the list row's icon, the share menu's checked state, and TeamPanel's shared-projects count.
- **SAME DEFECT SHAPE AS THE RENAME SPLIT (B1415–B1418), and it takes the same rule: ⛔ never re-derive the winner from `updatedAt`.** There `siteRenamedAt` is the deciding fact; here the deciding fact is simpler — the COLUMN is the authority, so the mirror is COPIED, never voted on.
- **THE FIX, at both seams.** `cloudList` stamps an explicit `shareMirror` (so *"the cloud says private"* is distinguishable from *"the cloud did not say"* — a pre-migration DB has no such column and must be left alone, or every project silently unshares). `mergePulledSites` re-stamps it AFTER the merge; `saveSite` refuses to let a content save move it for a record that already exists (a stale in-memory model carries `teamId: null` EXPLICITLY, and an explicit key wins a spread — that autosave was re-blanking the mirror seconds after the pull set it). A brand-new record keeps its birth team, which is B326416's INSERT path and the one legitimate local writer.
- **⛔ READ-ONLY BY CONSTRUCTION, so B714 is intact.** Nothing here writes a share value outward: `siteRowFor` still strips all three fields from every content UPDATE, `team_id` still moves only through the explicit share path, and the Postgres guard still refuses any other write. B714's rule is WHY this bug existed (the pointer was deliberately kept off the content path), so the fix had to make the READ direction authoritative and nothing else.
- **THEN THE LEGIBILITY HALF** (the owner's actual bar: 35 projects, 2 shared, he could not tell which). The list row now NAMES it — `Shared with HIP Houston` on the existing metadata line, in the accent, rather than an accent glyph whose meaning lived in a hover title. The share menu STATES its state before offering an action (`Shared with HIP Houston` / `Private — only you can see this`), and an already-shared team row reads `✓ Unshare` instead of looking like a fresh invitation, which is exactly what *"options still pop up to share it"* was.
- Guards: repo-root `test/` suite **shareMirror** (18 — incl. a mutation check that replays the pre-fix `mergeSiteContent` behaviour and asserts it loses the team, the pre-migration no-mirror case, the cross-device unshare, and the stale-autosave case).

### B366386 — Sharing a MULTI-PLAN project keyed on the drifting `group_id` COLUMN — the rename bug's shape, still latent `[Site Planner / teams]` (bug) #site-planner #auth #sync  *(arrived 2026-08-11 as provisional NEW-3 in the same owner chat block, filed there as "FLAG TO VERIFY (NOT PROVEN)". See B366384's provenance for the DEDUPE-FIRST sweep.)*
`[x]` **⏳ SHIPPED as a fix, not just a check — the defect is REAL in mechanism and was LATENT for his data. Both stated plainly below rather than one overclaimed as the other.**
- Verify: live — V161952 (`Blocker: auth`)
- Origin: owner chat block, 2026-08-11 — filed and shipped the same session.
- **WHAT THE BLOCK ASKED.** *"Confirm it sets team_id on EVERY plan row in the group AT THE SOURCE OF TRUTH… This is the same shape as the rename bug that half-landed and left stale rows in the cloud."* Correct instinct, and it was checkable statically.
- **THE DEFECT.** Both `set_project_team` and its pre-migration fallback matched `coalesce(group_id, id)` — the group_id **COLUMN**. `db/rename_site_group.sql` exists *because that column is a denormalised mirror known to drift from the jsonb*, and its header says outright: *"matching on it would rename the wrong set. Do not 'optimise' this onto the column."* Sharing was matching on exactly that column while the CLIENT passes a group id read out of the **jsonb** (`groupOf()` → `data->>'groupId'`). Wrong in both directions: a plan whose column disagrees is MISSED (a "shared" project only partly shared; on unshare, a collaborator keeps access the owner believes he revoked), and a foreign plan whose column names the group is swept IN.
- **THE DRIFT IS REAL IN THIS DATABASE TODAY** — row `e2e-fixture-testfit` has `group_id = 'e2e-fixture'` against `data->>'groupId' = 'e2e-fixture-testfit'`. So the mechanism is live, not theoretical.
- **AND THE HONEST LIMIT: it is LATENT for every one of the owner's real projects.** Measured across all 34 groups — Bain 2, Clay & Porter 2, Gessner 2, Goose Creek 4, Houston ColdPort 2, Silvestri 5 — **both keys select the identical row set**. The only disagreement in the whole database is that e2e fixture pair. So this fix is PREVENTIVE; it did not repair a currently-broken share, and it is not claimed to have.
- **THE FIX.** Both functions now key on `coalesce(data->>'groupId', id)` — byte-identical to `rename_site_group.sql` and to the client's own `groupOf()`, so all three read one grouping. Sharing already reached un-hydrated plans (it is ONE server-side UPDATE over the group, not a client loop — that is what half-landed the rename), so this changes WHICH rows that statement selects, never whether it is atomic.
- **PLUS A COMPLETENESS SELF-CHECK, both directions (LOUD-FAILURE).** The RPC re-counts its own group AFTER writing and returns `mismatched`; a non-zero value is surfaced as *"Only part of this project was shared — N of M plans didn't take"*, and on the unshare side as *"N of M plans are STILL shared"* — named rather than softened, because a half-unshare is the dangerous direction. A group holding a teammate's plan reports `foreign` and says so instead of claiming a clean success.
- Guards: repo-root `test/` suite **shareMirror** (a source guard on BOTH function bodies — the jsonb key required, `coalesce(group_id, id)` forbidden).

### B366388 — The switcher's second rename, and the hover-gated kebab that made removing it unsafe `[Shared UI]` (task) #ui #testing  *(arrived 2026-08-11 as provisional NEW-2 in the same owner chat block. See B366387's provenance.)*
`[x]` **⏳ SHIPPED — including the PRECONDITION the block insisted on, which was the real work here.**
- Verify: live — V161953
- Origin: owner chat block, 2026-08-11 — filed and shipped the same session.
- **THE REPORT, verbatim.** *"And I don't need a rename Clay & Porter right there. If anything it should be via the three dots, or I guess there already is the option for the three dots, so I don't need a second option there."*
- **⛔ THE BLOCK'S OWN WARNING WAS CORRECT AND WAS THE BLOCKER: "The owner asked for one rename entry point, not zero."** The crumb-level rename existed because the per-row kebab was hover-revealed — its removed comment said *"invisible, and dead on touch"*. Confirmed in the source: `active = hoverRow === p.id || menuFor?.id === p.id`, and `hoverRow` is set **only** by `onMouseEnter`; the sole alternative route is `onContextMenu`, a right-click. So on a touch device there was **no rename and no delete at all** — and for a KEYBOARD user the button was not merely invisible, it was **absent from the DOM**, so it could not be tabbed to either.
- **SO THE KEBAB WAS FIXED FIRST, and only then was the duplicate removed.** It is now always rendered; hover only BRIGHTENS it (`--text-tertiary` → `--text-secondary`), because opacity/colour is presentation and must never be the hit-test gate. - **THE FIX — ONE CANONICAL FORMATTER (`lib/jurisdictionLabel.js`), and a three-level grammar where each level means exactly one thing:** `·` joins GOVERNING slots, always leading with the governing authority (authority · ETJ · county · ISD) · `+` joins co-equal peers inside one slot (two cities, two counties, two districts) · `—` introduces the non-governing tail, and nothing after it regulates anything. `jurisdiction.js` keeps the DERIVATION and hands over a structured model; the strings live in one place.
- **THE FOUR SHAPES, exactly as he stated them** (`split` and `unknown` are STATES, not shapes — a straddle has two governing answers, a failed lookup has none):

  2. `City of Humble · Houston ETJ · Harris County`
  3. `City of Houston ETJ · Harris County`  ← was `Unincorporated / City of Houston · ETJ`
  4. `Unincorporated · Harris County — touches City of Katy`
- **THE WHOLE PORTFOLIO, LIVE, BEFORE AND AFTER** — 28 sites through the real identify against the real TxDOT / TxGIO / H-GAC services: **27 correct → 27 correct**, 0 mislabelled, 0 unresolved, 1 site with no drawn geometry, both runs. 16 sites moved `Unincorporated / City of Houston · ETJ` → `City of Houston ETJ`; Bain `Unincorporated / City of Houston · ETJ / City of Katy · edge only · Fort Bend County` → `City of Houston ETJ · Fort Bend County — touches City of Katy`; Will Clayton → `City of Humble · Houston ETJ · Harris County`; Goose Creek and Tsakiris keep their measured split, now joined by `·` because both halves really do govern; Goose Creek still does **not** claim Baytown outright. Full table on **V162864**.

Measured in a browser at 980 px: Bain's label went **464 px → 349 px**. What changed structurally is that the governing authority now sits FIRST, so a clip can only ever eat the demoted tail — pre-fix a narrow header cut off the ETJ, i.e. the jurisdiction that actually sets the finished floor, and left the word that says nothing. The harness asserts that property. Residual tail ellipsising at ≤1100 px is the header's width budget and is filed as **B367298**, not swallowed.

### B364016 (×2) — Delete forever STILL did not stick, and now the purged note came back into the LIVE list `[Notes]` (bug) #notes #sync #persistence  *(owner chat block, 2026-08-11 — STILL BROKEN #1, flagged by him as the priority and as a REPEAT: it was reported fixed and it was not. Minted **B364016** from this branch's reserved block B364016–B364031 against origin/main 73c5011. **DEDUPE-FIRST — this deliberately does NOT re-use B357011's number even though it is the same symptom.** B357011's fix is CORRECT and is still in the code; what failed is a different defect one layer away — the ledger it writes was being destroyed on every read. Re-opening B357011 would have said "the tombstone rule was wrong", which is false and would have sent the next reader to the wrong file. `Recurrence:` is recorded on B357011 in the archive instead.)*
`[ ]` **⏳ IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-11 — awaiting V159584 on his own account.**
- Verify: live → **V159584** (`Blocker: auth`)
- Origin: filed 2026-08-11 from chat.
- Recurrence: 2026-08-11 — B357011 shipped the tombstone rule; the purge still did not survive a reload, and the note came back LIVE rather than into the bin.
- **HIS SEQUENCE, MEASURED.** Created `pg_msp3ucx811rq9ao`, typed in it, binned it (trash 23 → 24), pressed **Delete forever** on that row (trash 24 → 23, row gone — correct), **reloaded** → local rev 1018: trash still 23, **live pages 8 → 9**, the page back in the sidebar. Cloud rev 1018 agreed. Its body key does not exist and its `notes_pages` doc is gone, so what came back is a **ghost**: a note with nothing in it and nothing recoverable. **Worse than the bug it replaced**, which at least put things back in the bin.
- **⛔ THE CAUSE IS ONE MISSING ARGUMENT, AND IT IS NOT IN THE TOMBSTONE RULE.** `migrate` — which EVERY read of the tree goes through — built a fresh object and then asked *that* object for its tombstones: `withTombstones({ v, pages, trash }, [])`. It found none and returned an empty ledger. **So the ledger was destroyed the instant it was written**, the merge fell straight back to a plain union, and a server that had not yet seen the bin still had the page LIVE — which is exactly where it came back. Reproduced in eleven lines before anything was touched:
  ```
  after purge, tombs: [ tr_…, pg_x ]
  after a reload, tombs: []          ← the whole defect
  merged live pages: [ pg_x ]
  ```
- **⛔ AND THE REAL FAILURE IS THAT THE TESTS COULD NOT SEE IT — he called this exactly right** (*"the two-client fuzz clearly does not cover purge-then-reload-same-client"*). The whole suite, including a 6,000-merge fuzz, worked on **in-memory trees** and never once went through `migrate` or through storage. A purge-then-RELOAD on ONE client was not a case anybody had. Every case now round-trips through the real store, the fuzz **reloads between rounds**, and there is a dedicated three-reloads-deep case that also syncs against a server still holding the page live. **Mutation-proven:** restoring the missing argument turns 5 of 19 rows red, including the fuzz — on the build that shipped, the fuzz was green.
- **HIS STOPPING RULE, ADOPTED VERBATIM:** purge → reload → the id is absent from BOTH `pages` and `trash`, locally and in the cloud, and stays absent across three reloads. That is now a test.

### B357011 — EMPTYING THE BIN DID NOT STICK: a stale window resurrected every purged entry and pushed it to the cloud `[Notes]` (bug) #notes #sync #persistence  *(owner chat block, 2026-08-11 — BIN NEW-1, flagged by him as HIGH and data-integrity, and caught IN THE ACT with revisions rather than inferred. Minted **B357011** from this branch's reserved block B357008–B357023 against origin/main af0d914. **DEDUPE-FIRST** — searched Open / ⏳ Verify / Done across `merge`, `union`, `trash`, `purge`, `bin`, `tombstone`, `B276`, `B342992`, `B342996`, `B1310`: **B342992** fixed the union's other side (a delete taking MORE than it named) and is intact and untouched — this is the same class on the OPPOSITE side, a delete surviving nothing; **B342996** is the stale-title risk and is a different fact about the same staleness; **B1310** built the bin's lifecycle, which works. Net-new.)*
`[ ]` **⏳ IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-11 — awaiting V152576 on his own account, where the 23 entries are sitting right now.**
- **⛔ RECURRENCE 2026-08-11, AND IT IS FILED AS `B364016` RATHER THAN RE-OPENING THIS ONE.** The live pass found the purge still not surviving a reload — and the page came back into the LIVE list, not the bin. **The rule below is correct and is unchanged;** what failed is that `migrate` was destroying the ledger it writes, on every read, so the merge fell back to a plain union. Re-opening this item would have said "the tombstone rule was wrong", which is false and would send the next reader to the wrong file. See **B364016** for the missing argument and for the test gap that hid it.
- Verify: live → **V152576** (`Blocker: auth`)
- Origin: filed 2026-08-11 from chat.
- **THE SEQUENCE, ALL MEASURED.** He emptied the bin → cloud `notes_trees` **rev 991, trash = 1**, live pages 8; his screen agreed, "1 deleted note". A tab still open was on **rev 966, `treeDirty` TRUE, holding all 23 entries**. It reloaded → local came back at **rev 992 with all 23**, including Entitlements and the whole Untitled run — and **pushed the resurrection up**, taking the cloud to rev 992 with 23. The stale tab did not merely fail to notice the purge; it overwrote the good state.
- **⛔ THE CAUSE IS STRUCTURAL, NOT A SLIP. The tree merge is a UNION: an ADDITION wins, and a DELETION is the ABSENCE of an entry. Absence loses to any copy that still has one.** So a purge could never survive a merge with a client that had not yet seen it. This is what TOMBSTONE-DELETES exists for, and Notes did not implement it.
- **THE FIX IS A DEFINITION: a purge is a FACT.** `purgeTrashEntry` records the entry id and every page id it named in a tombstone ledger carried in the tree itself, so it merges like everything else. **Rule 0** of `mergeTrees` honours it before any other rule — deliberately first, because rule 1 lifts a live node out when a bin entry names it, and a resurrected entry would do exactly that to a page somebody had since restored.
- **⛔ THE FUZZ FOUND A SECOND HOLE THAT NO HAND-WRITTEN CASE WOULD HAVE.** Two devices that delete the SAME note mint two DIFFERENT entry ids, so purging one tombstones its id and the other sails through the union untouched — **still naming pages whose bytes are destroyed**. That is precisely his zombie state: 15 of 24 rows with `purged_at` set and `doc` NULL, back in the bin offering a restore that could only produce an empty note. An entry is now filtered by the ids it NAMES, not only by its own.
- **AND A PURGE STILL TAKES ONLY WHAT IT NAMED** — a child another device added under a purged parent afterwards is RESCUED, not dropped. Rule 0 shares rule 5's body deliberately, so B342992's defect cannot arrive through the new door.
- **THE ZOMBIES ARE CLEANED UP ON SIGHT:** a bin entry every one of whose pages the SERVER reports purged is purged locally and tombstoned. ⛔ **The server's `purged_at` is the ONLY evidence accepted** — "no body on this device" is a different claim (a signed-in device legitimately has not downloaded every binned body), and conflating them would destroy recoverable entries.
- **THE BIN NOW TELLS THE TWO APART.** *"Empty — nothing was ever written in it"* and *"Its writing was permanently deleted and cannot be brought back"* are opposite facts and it was showing the first for both.
- **ON THE REBASE HALF OF HIS ASK:** the push is ALREADY rev-guarded (`.eq("rev", base)`), so a client behind the server cannot write blind — its update fails and it merges first. That is what happened here: the rebase ran correctly and the MERGE was wrong. Stated rather than adding a second mechanism that would do nothing.
- **TESTED THE WAY HE ASKED:** two clients, one stale and dirty, in `test/notesBinPurge.test.js` — his exact sequence, both directions, a second equally-stale window, a restore racing a purge — **plus a 6,000-merge fuzz across five seeds** with zero resurrections. **Mutation-proven:** removing rule 0 turns 6 of the 12 rows red, including the fuzz.
- **⛔ WHAT IS STILL OWED (V152576).** His account is carrying the resurrection RIGHT NOW — 23 entries that he emptied and the app put back, and 15 of them with their content already destroyed. This build will clean them up on his next load; that has to be watched happening, and it needs a signed-in session the sandbox cannot have.

The double-click that followed asked "was this blank space?" against the edge **its own first press had just moved**, decided it was on content, and declined: **no block at all, and the added line left behind.** Found by the sweep, not by reading. The question is now asked against the document as the person FOUND it.

### B342992 — A real note is unreachable: a body with no tree node, in local AND cloud `[Notes]` (bug) #notes #sync #persistence  *(owner chat block, 2026-08-10, with forensics read off his live workspace and Supabase)*
`[⏳]` **Root cause found and fixed: `mergeTrees`, twice. The note itself is recovered in his account.**
- Verify: live
- Origin: filed 2026-08-10 from chat (NEW-1).
- **THE ROOT CAUSE IS NOT THE CONFLICT RESOLVER — that hypothesis is REFUTED.** The resolver parks a copy and never rebuilds the tree. The two holes are both in `mergeTrees`, and neither is visible in a hand-read; both were found by a randomised sweep over thousands of merges:
  1. **A DELETE TOOK MORE THAN ITS ENTRY NAMED.** `deleteNode` stamps the cascade the DELETING device could see. The merge lifted out every id in that entry and returned BEFORE recursing — so a page the other device had added under the deleted parent was neither kept live nor carried into the bin. Dropped, body intact. **Rule 5** now scopes a delete to exactly the ids its entry names; anything else is RESCUED to the top level of its branch's project and REPORTED.
  2. **THE OTHER SIDE'S COPY WAS LOOKED UP BY POSITION.** Re-parent a page on one device and the merge went blind to that page's copy on the other, losing every child it had gained there — **with no bin involved at all**: one `move` and one `add` were enough. Counterparts are now found by **id, anywhere in the tree**.
- **THE TITLE HYPOTHESIS IS REFUTED, and the observation it came from is explained.** A node with a null / undefined / empty / whitespace title survives all eleven paths (save, load, migrate, cloud round trip, two-window merge ×3, sibling delete/rename/move, bin-and-restore). The reason all 56 of his nodes carry a title is that **no path can mint one** — and since this item that is true at the ONE constructor rather than at each caller, which is what previously let `"   "` through `addPage`. Written into the store header as a standing rule: **a title is never load-bearing for identity or reachability; identity is the id.**
- **THE NOTE IS BACK.** `pg_msgaajbf1o61rit` was given a tree node in `notes_trees` (rev 910 → 911, guarded), titled from its own first line and filed in no project — nothing guessed. A full re-audit of his account afterwards returns **zero** bodies without a node.
- **AND IT IS SELF-HEALING NOW.** `sweepOrphans` refuses to destroy a body that still has words in it (it used to delete it every load while the next seed re-downloaded it — the loop that hid this for days); `unreachableNotes` looks for the violated property on every load; `adoptUnreachable` gives it a node automatically. The banner NAMES each one (first line, size, the date recovered from the id itself), opens it, and offers **File under a project… / Keep as loose / Move to bin** inline. **There is deliberately no title-keyed "Recovered" container** — that would make a title load-bearing in the one path whose job is repairing reachability.
- Guards: repo-root `test/` suite **notesReachability** (minimal cases for both holes, a 6,000-merge property across five seeds, all five falsy titles × eleven paths, and the adoption rules) + **verify-notes-project-integrity** (43 rows, real browser).

### B326419 — An existing project can never become shared by any ordinary write path — deny-by-default in Postgres `[Site Planner / teams · RLS]` (task) #auth #infra #persistence #testing  *(the hard safety requirement of the owner's block: "NOTHING that already exists may change visibility on release… Treat any ambiguity here as DENY." See B326416 for mint provenance.)*
`[x]` **⏳ SHIPPED and PROVEN — the security property is verified; only the UI pass is pending (V124976).**
- Verify: live — V124976 covers the UI only. The RLS property below was verified against the production policies this session and is NOT awaiting anything.
- **THE HOLE THIS CLOSES.** `guard_team_rehome` (B486) let the row OWNER change `team_id` on ANY update. That is right for a deliberate share, but it means a client bug, a stale in-memory model, a replayed cache write or a future refactor could flip an existing private project to shared through an ordinary content save — silently, with the owner's own credentials, and RLS would allow it. Client-side care (B714's INSERT-only rule) is a convenience, never the guarantee.
- **THE FIX.** `guard_team_share` REFUSES any UPDATE that changes `sites.team_id` unless it arrives inside `set_project_team()`, the only thing that sets the transaction-local `planyr.share_intent` flag. Ordinary writes cannot set it (PostgREST sends no `set_config`, and `is_local` stops it leaking on a pooled connection). INSERT is untouched — a brand-new row may be born shared, which is why **"new projects only" is a consequence of the schema rather than a rule the client is trusted to follow.**
- **PROVEN RED, not asserted.** `db/test/team_share_scope.test.sql` runs as a real `authenticated` role with a real JWT subject against the real policies, and is self-rolling-back (it raises at the end, so every fixture is discarded and it writes nothing that survives). Clean: **15/15 pass.** Re-pointed at the OLD permissive guard: **3 FAIL** — the ordinary owner UPDATE shares the pre-existing project, the teammate can then read it, AND can read its `site_elements` drawing. Restoring the guard turns them green. That mutation was run on 2026-08-09 and the guard restored + re-verified in the same session.
- Also covered by the same suite: a solo user sees their own project and nobody else's · a teammate has full edit while unlocked · a locked plan is readable but not writable, drawing included · a teammate cannot unlock · the owner CAN still deliberately share an old project through the RPC · a non-owner cannot share a project they do not own.
- `lib/sharing.js` now calls the RPC (with a pre-migration fallback so shipping the client before the SQL degrades rather than breaks) and no longer touches `doc_reviews` / `file_facts`.

- **THE REPORT, verbatim.** He checked *"Contour lines (1 ft)"* while zoomed out below the z16 terrain gate. The checkbox rendered fully ON, the map drew nothing, and he sat for a full minute believing the feature had failed before realising it was a threshold: *"it should be more obvious that that's what's going on… it's not clear to me that it's failing, I guess."*
- **⛔ THE PANEL ALREADY CARRIED AN EXPLANATION AND THAT IS THE DEFECT, NOT THE FIX.** The row showed `Zoom in to ≥ 16 to load (1-ft detail needs close zoom)` — **static helper text that renders identically whether the layer is currently drawing or not**, sitting under a checkbox that says ON. A sentence describing a rule is not a report of a state. Making that sentence louder was explicitly ruled out.
- **⛔ AND THE AUDIT FOUND A STRICTLY WORSE CASE THAN THE ONE HE REPORTED, which is why this is generalized rather than patched.** `featureLayerOptions` passes `minZoom: cfg.minZoom ?? 10` to Leaflet, so **EVERY `esriFeature` layer is gated at zoom 10 whether or not its registry row says so** — and Leaflet simply declines to draw, reporting nothing at all. Those rows showed a confident **green "loaded" dot over an empty map with no sentence to decode**. Contours at least had a sentence.
- **THE MODEL.** New pure leaf `lib/layerZoomGate.js` (imports only `terrainGate.js`, which imports nothing — the B1095 discipline). `layerMinZoom(cfg)` answers the gate for every KIND: the registry's declared `minZoom`, the `esriFeature` implicit 10, `TERRAIN_MIN_ZOOM` for contours/flowdir, the OSM (14) and Mapillary (16) evidence gates, and an explicit **null** for a raster export, which is never gated. `layerVisibility()` returns **four states, which are the four he has to be able to tell apart**: `off` · `drawing` · `dormant-zoom` · `dormant-blank`. `combineVisibility()` does the same for a merged row (City limits & ETJ, Water & sewer, Electric, Fire hydrants) — dormant only when EVERY on member is, offering the SHALLOWEST gate, because clearing that is what puts something on the map.
- **THE GATE IS ASKED BEFORE COVERAGE, deliberately.** Below the gate the layer never asked the source anything, so *"no data in this area"* would be a fabrication. The same ordering suppresses the flood group's `emptyReason` under a closed gate.
- **THE ROW (a), NO LEGEND AND NO KEY** (owner rule, 2026-07-30 — *"whatever an apple or a google would do"*). A dormant row looks like neither of its neighbours: the status dot goes **HOLLOW** (every live state is a filled dot, so an outline reads as *nothing is coming out of this one*), the label mutes, the row dims — and the checkbox stays checked, because it honestly is. Nothing anywhere explains the convention.
- **THE LINE IS LIVE (b) AND IT IS THE FIX (c).** `Not showing at this zoom — zoom in 3 levels`, computed from the ACTUAL current zoom and counting down as he zooms; clicking it takes the map just past that layer's gate. It **REPLACES** the static sentence rather than joining it (PANEL-BREVITY rule 2 — the removed sentence is the pipeline's own `Zoom in to ≥ 16 to load (1-ft detail needs close zoom)`; the full rule still lives behind the row's ⓘ, which is exempt). Net visible lines: unchanged.
- **BOTH SURFACES, ONE MECHANISM.** The planner passes the DRAWING's own zoom (live during a gesture, rather than one basemap commit behind) and zooms about the canvas centre — the same anchor the ＋/－ buttons use — and refuses to zoom OUT to "fix" a row. The map finder passes its Leaflet zoom and `setZoom`. Its zoom state was also seeded on map creation: it started null and only `zoomend` wrote it, so before the user's first zoom the finder's panel had no idea what zoom it was looking at.
- **(d) GENERALIZED, AND MACHINE-ENFORCED SO IT STAYS THAT WAY.** The kind-gated rows now DECLARE their `minZoom` in the registry (contours · flowdir · both OSM rows · Mapillary · the assumed pipeline corridor), and `evidenceLayers.js` imports its two constants from the shared leaf instead of keeping private copies. `test/layerZoomGate.test.js` (24) reads the REAL registry, the REAL `terrainLayers` gate, the REAL `vectorLayers` `minVectorZoom` and the REAL `featureLayerOptions` default and fails if any declared number drifts from the runtime one — the dangerous failure here is not a wrong pixel, it is the panel and the map holding two different numbers.
- **(e) THE BLANK STATE** — checked, past the gate, and the source's data does not reach here — gets the same dormant treatment and an honest line, with no fake action offered, because no zoom fixes it.
- **PROVEN RED FIRST, in a real browser.** `e2e/layer-zoom-dormant.spec.js` (6 cases) on the pre-fix build fails behaviourally on a selector that exists on BOTH builds — the panel really does render `Zoom in to ≥ 16 to load (1-ft detail needs close zoom)` under a checked box — and passes on the fix. It covers checked-below-gate, the click-to-fix (asserting the view really moved), checked-above-gate, unchecked, a DIFFERENT kind with a DIFFERENT gate source (`jur_road_authority`, the silent Leaflet case), and the map finder.

### B685200 — A Colorado sub-source is offered on a Texas site (and vice versa) inside a merge group `[Site Planner / Layers]` (bug) #gis #site-planner #ui  *(arrived 2026-08-22 as provisional NEW-2 in the same owner chat block as B323424 (×3), self-verified live on a THROWAWAY DUPLICATE of the Tsakiris site (Waller County, TX). Minted **B685200** from this branch's reserved block (B685200–B685215 / V358848–V358863) via `git fetch origin main && npm run next-id -- --against-main`. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open + ⏳ Verify + Done across `mergeGroup`, `water_sewer`, `outOfState`, `siteState`, `states:`, `B898`, `B1206`, `coloradoRegions`: **B898** built the merge-group consolidation this bug lives inside and is UNCHANGED (every member's own fetch/URL/kind is untouched); the "NEW-2 — the STATE gate" comment block in `components/LayerPanel.jsx` (`outOfState`/`slotOutOfState`) is the mechanism that should have caught this and didn't — nothing prior filed the gap in how it composes a MERGE row's member list. Net-new.)*
`[x]` **⏳ SHIPPED. `Verify: live` → V121984 (folded into the SAME item as B323424 — same report, same session, same "Water & sewer" row on the same throwaway site).**

- **THE REPORT, verbatim (from the same owner chat block as B323424 ×3).** On a Waller County, Texas site, the "Water & sewer" row surfaces "Water & sanitation districts (Colorado)" as a sub-source — a provider that can never apply there.
- **⛔ AUDIT-FIRST: THE DATA WAS ALREADY CORRECT — THIS WAS A RENDERING BUG, NOT A REGISTRY GAP.** Every member of `MERGE_GROUPS.water_sewer` already declares its own `states` in `lib/layers.js`: `co_water_districts: states: ["CO"]`; `ccn_service`/`jur_mud`/`coh_water`/`coh_ww`: `states: ["TX"]`. `LayerPanel.jsx` already HAD the exact predicate needed — `outOfState(cfg)` — and already used it correctly for two things: demoting a SOLO row entirely, and demoting a merge SLOT to the collapsed "N not available in {state}" block **only when EVERY member is out of state** (`slotOutOfState`, deliberately — the MERGE_GROUPS header comment is explicit that a group must stay INCLUSIVE of neighbouring jurisdictions, e.g. a CCN extension just across a city line, so a slot may never be demoted wholesale over one out-of-region member). **What NOTHING did: drop a single out-of-state member from an otherwise in-state group's ACTIVE member list.** `mergeGroupRow` (the component that renders the checkbox, opacity, combined status, and the ⓘ provider list) and `slotAnyOn`/`slotLowRel` (the group-header "N on" count and the low-relevance fold) all iterated the FULL, unfiltered `members` array regardless of site region.
- **AUDIT OF THE OTHER TWO MERGE GROUPS, as asked.** `electric` (`osm_power`/`hifld_tx`/`hifld_substations`) and `fire_hydrants` (`osm_hydrants`/`coh_hydrants`/`mapillary`) have **no Colorado (or any cross-state) member today** — none of their rows declare a conflicting `states` — so neither currently exhibits this defect live. The fix is at the shared rendering root (`mergeGroupRow`/`slotAnyOn`/`slotLowRel`), not per-row, so any future state-scoped member added to either group is covered automatically rather than needing its own patch.
- **THE FIX (`components/LayerPanel.jsx`).** A single `inState = members.filter(([, cfg]) => !outOfState(cfg))` computed once at the top of `mergeGroupRow`, and used everywhere the function previously read `members` directly: the checkbox's `anyOn`, the opacity control, the combined status (`combineLayerStatus`), the toggle-all handler (`setAll`), the ⓘ provider list (`mergeGroupInfoSections`), the "Show above plan" row, and `visForMembers` (the B323424 state machine). `slotAnyOn`/`slotLowRel` (the group-header count and the low-relevance fold) filter the same way, so the header's "N on" count can never disagree with what the row itself renders. `groupRows` already guarantees any slot reaching these functions has at least one in-state member (`slotOutOfState` routes a fully-out-of-state slot to the collapsed block first), so the filter is never vacuous here and the INCLUSIVE-across-neighbouring-jurisdictions guarantee for members that ARE in the same state is completely unchanged.
- **THE INTERACTION WITH B323424 (×3), NAMED RATHER THAN LEFT IMPLICIT.** Once `co_water_districts` is excluded from a Texas site's active member list, that site's "Water & sewer" checkbox no longer ever attempts to build it — so the specific row the owner saw (a Texas row admitting a Colorado registry gap) can no longer occur. But the underlying registry gap this exposed (no `VECTOR_SOURCES` entry for `co_water_districts`/`co_city`/`co_isd`/`co_metro_districts`) is real and independent: a genuine Colorado site checking "Water & sewer" hits it directly, with `co_water_districts` as its ONLY in-state member. That is exactly B323424 (×3)'s fix, and the two are proven together in the same e2e case below — a Colorado site's row resolves, synchronously, to the honest dormant-blank treatment rather than a phantom "drawing".
- **PROVEN RED FIRST, in a real browser** (`e2e/layer-zoom-dormant.spec.js`, two new cases, stashed the fix and re-ran to confirm): pre-fix, a Texas site's "Water & sewer" ⓘ popover names "Water & sanitation districts (Colorado) — Source: Colorado DOLA"; pre-fix, a Colorado site's row reads `data-layer-state="drawing"` (the TX-only members' immediate `"loading"` status wins `combineVisibility`'s `some(state === "drawing")`) instead of `dormant-blank`. Post-fix: the Texas popover lists only its four Texas-scoped providers by their exact `label — Source:` line and never the Colorado one; the Colorado row resolves to `dormant-blank` with the plain fallback sentence and its popover lists only the Colorado provider, never CCN/MUD/City-of-Houston.
- **Sandbox + real-browser result:** lint 0 errors · full `npx vitest run` green (see B323424 ×3's count — this fix has no dedicated unit suite of its own; its observable is the rendered panel, so it is proven in the e2e spec) · `e2e/layer-zoom-dormant.spec.js` 8/9 (auth-setup skipped, no seeded account) including both new cases and zero regressions on the 5 pre-existing NEW-1 cases · build green · MAP.md unaffected (no files added/removed/renamed, no primary export changed).

### B323425 — Contours paint, then disappear about two seconds after load `[Site Planner / Layers]` (bug) #gis #site-planner #perf  *(arrived 2026-08-09 as provisional NEW-2 in the same owner chat block, from the same session on his own site. Minted **B323425 / V121985** from this branch's reserved block. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open + ⏳ Verify + Done across `paint then`, `flash`, `disappear`, `viewreset`, `ghost`, `B65`, `B183`, `B821`, `B837`, `B933`, `B1122`, `B1189`: every one of those is about the BASEMAP flashing or lagging during a gesture; none is about a GIS layer being admitted at one zoom and cleared at another. Net-new, and deliberately NOT filed as a duplicate of B323424 — a paint that is WITHDRAWN reads as a crash, not as a threshold.)*
`[x]` **⏳ SHIPPED. `Verify: live` → V121985 for the owner-visible paint itself, which cannot be produced in this sandbox. The CAUSE is measured here, on the real app, and the fix is measured with it.**
- Verify: live — V121985 (3DEP is ERR_CONNECTION_RESET from Chromium in this sandbox, so no contour line can be made to paint here at all)
- Origin: owner chat block, 2026-08-09 — filed and shipped the same session.
- **THE CAUSE, DIAGNOSED RATHER THAN ASSUMED — and it is neither of the two candidates the brief listed.** New instrument `ui-audit/diagnose-layer-gate-flash.mjs` samples the backdrop map's zoom continuously from plan-open to settle, stamps every terrain DEM request with **the map zoom at the moment it was issued**, and counts contour polylines on the same clock. Measured on the pre-fix build, twice: the map holds **17.25**, then **15.08**. Four DEM grid pulls went out at **+290 ms, at map zoom 17.25**, while the plan settles at **15.08 — below the z16 gate**.
- **STATED PLAINLY: the gate was answered at a zoom the plan was never at.** A plan opens on the default view (ppf 0.35 ≈ Leaflet zoom 17.25 at this latitude, comfortably past the gate), and the whole-site framing — `requestFit`, 120 ms after the workspace becomes active — then drops it to whatever the tract needs. Every layer admitted in that window fetched, traced and painted, and the terrain pipeline then **CORRECTLY** cleared it on the first post-fit `moveend`. **Nothing was broken and no paint was wrong; the TIMING OF THE QUESTION was.** The brief's two candidates were "painting at the initial map zoom before the view settles" (right in shape, wrong in mechanism — it is not the map's zoom that is stale, it is that nothing waited for the framing) and "cached tiles drawing ahead of the gate" (refuted — the cache is what makes the paint INSTANT on his machine, but a cold run reproduces the wrong-zoom question with no cache involved at all).
- **THE FIX — one latch, not a timer.** No layer is ADMITTED until the backdrop map has committed the FRAMED view. `viewFramed` alone is not enough (it goes true one render BEFORE the commit lands), so the test is that the committed zoom has caught up with the drawing's own; `layerGateReady` is a one-shot latch, which is what keeps a zoom gesture from re-entering the overlay sync every frame. It gates ADDS only — a removal, an opacity change and a lift are untouched, exactly as with the staging gate it composes with. The backdrop map is also now born at the drawing's own zoom instead of a hardcoded 17.
- **MEASURED BOTH WAYS on the real app: six wasted DEM grid pulls at the wrong zoom → ZERO.** The same harness reports `the gate was answered ONCE, at the plan's real opening zoom`.
- **⛔ AND WHAT THIS SANDBOX COULD NOT SEE, reported as a blocker rather than as a pass.** Every `elevation.nationalmap.gov` request from Chromium here returns **ERR_CONNECTION_RESET** (curl succeeds — it rides the agent proxy), so the terrain layer can be observed ASKING but never ANSWERING and **no contour line can be made to paint**. The harness's third pass says exactly that and refuses to score itself. A harness that could not have seen an effect must never report its absence as a pass.
- **THE GUARD.** `e2e/layer-zoom-dormant.spec.js` asserts ZERO terrain grid pulls on opening a plan that settles below the gate — a blocked request is still an OBSERVED request, so it holds here exactly as it would with 3DEP reachable. **The reload in that case is load-bearing and is commented as such:** opening cold from the site list happens to mount the map AFTER the framing, so the gate is answered correctly by accident and a spec written that way **passes on the broken build**; re-entering on a remembered plan — how the owner arrives at a site he has been working on — mounts the map first. Proven red pre-fix (4 pulls) and green after.
- **Sandbox result:** as B323424 above; plus the diagnosis harness red on pre-fix and green on the fix.

- **THE REPORT.** *"if I'm in the settings just to change my password, and I don't want it to be right there… let's build out a more professional settings menu."* Settings was one tab of three whose entire body WAS the change-password form, so the most consequential control in the account greeted you before anything else.

A left nav on a desktop-width modal, wrapping to a row of chips under a phone width, in CSS with no measurement hook.
- **THE FRONT DOOR IS INTERFACE, NOT SECURITY, and that is the item.** The account dropdown's "Settings" row now lands on the ordinary app preference; the password is one click away in a section that says what it is. `SECTION_ALIAS` is the one place that decides, and the Shell's `initialTab` contract ("profile" / "team" / "settings") is unchanged, so no wiring outside this file moved.
- **⛔ THE RECONCILIATION THE OWNER ASKED TO BE STATED EITHER WAY: PROFILE AND TEAM FOLD IN.** They were already tabs of this same modal — what made them read as a third parallel surface is that "Settings" sat BESIDE them as a peer, as though profile and team were something other than settings. They are now sections OF Settings, and the account dropdown's three rows became DEEP LINKS into those sections rather than routes to different places. Nothing was duplicated and nothing was orphaned.
- **⛔ AND WHAT DELIBERATELY DID NOT SHIP: an "active sessions" list.** Enumerating a user's sessions needs the service-role admin API, which may never reach the browser (`CLAUDE.md` → KEY DECISIONS). A section that could only ever have listed *this* device would be furniture pretending to be a security feature. So Account & security carries the action that IS real — **Sign out on all devices** (`supabase.auth.signOut({ scope: "global" })`, which revokes every refresh token server-side) — and nothing else. An empty section never ships, and neither does a fake one.
- **LOUD-FAILURE on that action specifically.** Unlike the plain `signOut()` beside it, `signOutEverywhere()` RETURNS its outcome and the panel renders the error: a security action that fails silently is worse than one not offered, because the user believes they are safe.
- **PANEL-BREVITY.** Each section is verdict-first with no explanatory paragraphs; the one cloud-sync sentence that used to sit under the password form moved into Interface, where it is about the app rather than about the password, and it is the only prose in the panel. No section gained copy.

### B315712 — A synced note can be written into a different project than the one it belongs to `[Notes]` (bug) #notes #sync #persistence  *(owner chat block, 2026-08-09 — his own forensics, verified against `planyr_production`)*
`[⏳]` **Verify — the rule and every guard are implemented; the CONFLICT PATH itself needs a signed-in, two-window pass (V114272).**
- Verify: live
- Origin: filed 2026-08-09 from chat (NEW-1).
- **THE RULE, and it is the whole item: A PAGE'S `projectId` IS A PROPERTY OF THE PAGE, NEVER OF WHOEVER HAPPENS TO BE LOOKING AT IT.** If the sync engine keeps both sides of a conflict, the kept copy stays in the same project as its source, is named as a copy, and is surfaced at the moment it is made.
- **AUDIT-FIRST — what the audit actually found, including where it contradicts the reported premise.** Every write path was walked: the conflict park (`Notes.jsx` `handleConflict`), `mergeTrees` rules 3 and 4, `movePage`, `restoreNode`, `planAdoption`, `settleQuietly`, the seed's adopt/upload plan. **No path in the CURRENT code takes the viewer's project.** The park already read `hit.root.projectId`; the merge already carries each side's own record. What it DID have was the shape that makes the defect re-arrivable at any time — an `addPage(...)` call site with a `projectId:` argument sitting right next to the component's own `projectId` prop. So the fix is structural rather than a patch: `copyPageWithin` is now the ONE copy op and **has no project parameter at all**, so a caller cannot pass the wrong one even by accident. An unknown source is REFUSED and named rather than filed somewhere plausible, and the resolution does not proceed (parking is what makes "never a lost edit" true).
- **⛔ AND THE FORENSICS NEED ONE CORRECTION, stated because it changes what to look for.** The Colorado page `pg_ms8z7vik4vejfpp` was **not minted on 3 Aug**. Its id encodes `Date.now()` in base 36, and it decodes to **2026-07-31 13:26:38 UTC — eight hours BEFORE** Grand Port's `pg_ms9gfprm2viq50r` (2026-07-31 21:28:38). Its section `sec_ms8z7vik5yj3mf1` carries the SAME millisecond and the next sequence number, which is the signature of an ordinary "add section" in the Colorado project. Its title is still the default **"Page 1"**. So no page was ever copied INTO another project: a page that legitimately belonged to Colorado had **Grand Port's document written into its body key** on 3 Aug, 17:52–17:53 (rev 1→4). The second "orphan", Colorado's "Bonding", is a genuinely EMPTY page (0 characters against Grand Port's 151) that merely shares a name — not a copy at all.
- **WHAT THAT MEANS FOR THE RULE:** it is still right and is now enforced, but the 3 Aug event was a **body written under the wrong page id**, not a tree-level copy. The remaining live check is therefore the conflict path itself.
- Guards, all mutation-proven (reverting the copy op to take a viewer's project turns **9 rows red** with the exact reported fingerprint — same text, different projects): `test/notesProjectIntegrity.test.js` (32 rows), `test/notesTwoClientConflict.test.js` (two real store instances against an in-memory server that owns `rev` like the real trigger — asserts the exact page count AND every page's project), `test/notesModule.test.js` (the park may not reach for a `projectId` at all), `ui-audit/verify-notes-project-integrity.mjs`.


### B315716 — A note whose tree node is lost is swept off the device on every load and re-downloaded on every sync, reachable from nowhere `[Notes]` (bug) #notes #persistence #sync  *(found by the NEW-4 detector while it was being built, in the owner's own production account)*
`[⏳]` **Verify — implemented and proven headless; the CLOUD half of the recovery needs a signed-in pass (V114272).** Filed as its own item rather than folded into B315715, because it is a different failure with a different cause.
- Verify: live
- Origin: filed 2026-08-09 from chat (found while building NEW-4).
- **THE REAL ROW.** `pg_msgaajbf1o61rit` in `planyr_production` — created 2026-08-05 16:11 UTC, **rev 123**, 1,909 characters of real content (channel improvements to slow conveyance, Willow Point MUD water/sanitary, the $3–4/SF vs $10/SF pricing note, the Hilcorp blanket easement). It appears in **no tree node at all** — not live, not in the bin. It is unreachable in the app and has been for days.
- **THE MECHANISM, and why nothing could ever have said so.** `sweepOrphans` deleted the local body of any page not in the tree — correct for an interrupted delete, catastrophic for a page whose NODE was lost. The next seed then re-adopted the row (`planPageSeed` downloads any row this device does not have), the sweep deleted it again on the next load, and the loop ran indefinitely with the note reachable from nowhere and nothing ever mentioning it.
- **THE FIX, two halves.** `sweepOrphans` now **refuses to destroy a body that still has words in it** and returns `{ removed, kept }`; `unreachableNotes` (`lib/notesScan.js`) surfaces what it kept, and the workspace offers to put it back — into the named **"Not in a project"** home and nowhere else, because an orphan's project is exactly the fact that was lost and guessing one is B315712's defect.
- Proven: `ui-audit/verify-notes-project-integrity.mjs` §2/§4 (the recovery is read back out of the STORE, and survives a reload), `test/notesTwoClientConflict.test.js` (an empty stray is still swept; a body with words is not).

### B298756 — Notes took pictures and nothing else; a PDF, an XLSX or a DWG could not be attached `[Notes]` (feature) #notes #files #persistence #export  *(filed 2026-08-09 from the owner's Tier-1 chat block, item 5: *"We take images only. Dropping a PDF, an XLSX or a DWG into a note is table stakes everywhere."* See B298752 for the block's full provenance and dedupe.)*
`[ ]` **⏳ SHIPPED — drag-drop, paste and a toolbar button all attach any file; the chip downloads it; it survives Markdown and Print. `Verify: live` → V97312 (`Blocker: auth` — the cloud half needs a signed-in account).**
- Verify: live → V97312
- Origin: filed 2026-08-09 from chat; shipped the same session.
- **⛔ IT RIDES THE PICTURE TIER RATHER THAN A SECOND BLOB TIER, and that was the load-bearing choice.** The owner offered both — *"either a new bucket or a relaxed policy plus a row per file"* — and the second is what shipped. The picture tier already owns a sync plan, a purge cascade, an orphan sweep and a per-notebook ceiling; a parallel tier would have meant a second copy of every one of those, and a second way to leak bytes. An attachment is a picture that is not a picture, not a new subsystem.
- **THE MIGRATION, APPLIED — nothing on the owner's plate.** `notes_attachments_new5` on `planyr_production`, 2026-08-09, via the Supabase MCC: `notes_images` gains `name` and `kind` (`'image' | 'file'`, DEFAULT `'image'`, so every existing row is already correct and nothing is backfilled), plus a two-value check constraint; the private `notes-images` bucket stops refusing non-image types and its per-object ceiling goes to 50 MB. Verified after applying: both columns present, `allowed_mime_types` null, `file_size_limit` 52428800, security advisors show **no new findings**. Committed as a record at `src/workspaces/notes/db/notes_attachments.sql`.
- **⛔ THE BUCKET IS STILL CALLED `notes-images` AND MUST STAY THAT WAY.** Renaming it orphans every object already in it — every picture in every existing note — for the sake of a more accurate word. The table comment says what it really holds.
- **⛔ `assetIdsInDoc`, NOT `imageIdsInDoc`, IS WHAT EVERY DELETE PATH MUST NOW ASK.** The purge cascade and the orphan sweep both moved to it. A cascade that asked only for image ids would leave a deleted page's attachments on the device and in the account forever — bytes nothing can reach and nothing will ever free, which is the exact leak TOMBSTONE-DELETES exists to prevent, one layer down.
- **A MIXED DROP DOES NOT LOSE HALF OF ITSELF.** Two plugins watching one drop is a race the first to `return true` wins outright, so a screenshot dragged in beside a PDF would have landed the picture and dropped the PDF with no message anywhere. The attachment intake runs first, DECLINES a pictures-only drop (leaving the image path exactly as it was) and claims a mixed one whole, routing both halves.
- **EXPORT — named always, embedded when small.** Markdown embeds up to 2 MB and NAMES anything larger, reporting it as lossy; the print sheet carries name · type · size, because paper cannot carry bytes and a survey that vanishes silently out of a PDF is the worst class of export bug. Both are asserted against real downloads in the harness.
- **The ceiling is enforced at the STORE** (`MAX_FILE_BYTES`, 34 MB of stored data URL ≈ 25 MB of file), so no future intake path can slip past it, and an oversize file is a NAMED refusal in the app rather than an opaque 400 from storage (LOUD-FAILURE).
- Sandbox: `ui-audit/verify-notes-tier1.mjs` §6 — 7 rows, driving a REAL file through the picker and asserting the chip, the stored node, that the document does NOT hold the bytes, that the bytes ARE in IndexedDB marked `kind: "file"`, the Markdown download and the print sheet. `test/notesTier1.test.js` — the description layer and the cascade. Full suite green, lint 0 errors, build green.

### B298758 — A note had no way to say "this bit matters", and no way to fold a section away `[Notes]` (feature) #notes #ui #export  *(filed 2026-08-09 from the owner's Tier-1 chat block, item 7. See B298752 for the block's full provenance and dedupe.)*
`[ ]` **⏳ SHIPPED — a callout with five tones and a toggle that folds its children; both round-trip through Markdown, and a folded toggle prints EXPANDED. `Verify: live` → V97313 (`Blocker: real-data` — a real save-as-PDF from the browser's own dialogue).**
- Verify: live → V97313
- Origin: filed 2026-08-09 from chat; shipped the same session.
- **⛔ A CALLOUT STORES A TONE **NAME**, NEVER A COLOUR.** The node carries `info | tip | important | warning | danger` and nothing else. Three surfaces then draw that one name their own way — the screen from theme tokens, paper from print ink, Markdown from GitHub's own alert syntax. Storing a colour would have frozen the first of those three into the document forever, and would have printed a dark box on a light sheet the day the theme changed.
- **THE FIVE TONES ARE GITHUB'S FIVE, DELIBERATELY.** `> [!NOTE]` / `[!TIP]` / `[!IMPORTANT]` / `[!WARNING]` / `[!CAUTION]` is a real rendered construct in GFM, so the export is the same thing with a different spelling rather than an approximation — which is why a callout adds **nothing** to the lossiness report. A sixth tone would have no marker to map to; adding one means deciding its fallback first, and both files say so.
- **A TOGGLE IS THE BROWSER'S OWN `<details>`.** Folding is then something the browser does — no measuring, no animation frame, no height cache to go stale — and a printed sheet inherits the same element, so there is no second implementation on paper to drift (PDF-PARITY by construction). The fold is an ATTRIBUTE in the document, so it persists, syncs and survives a reload; a small plugin claims the marker press and writes the attribute rather than letting the browser flip a DOM property ProseMirror would immediately overwrite.
- **⛔ A COLLAPSED TOGGLE PRINTS AND EXPORTS EXPANDED, UNCONDITIONALLY.** `docToHtml` opens every `<details>` before it serialises — not behind an option a caller can forget, because this file has exactly two callers and both are the print path. Paper has no disclosure triangle, so a folded section written out folded is simply missing text, and nothing about the resulting sheet looks wrong. That is the whole reason it is not a flag.
- **ONE BUG THE HARNESS CAUGHT AND NO UNIT TEST COULD HAVE.** `setNoteToggle` read `state.selection`, but the slash menu runs it at the end of a chain that has already deleted the typed `/toggle` — so its positions were stale by exactly the length of the command the user typed, and the result was a toggle with an EMPTY title and the title's words in its body. A command that reported success and produced the wrong document. It reads `tr.selection` now.
- Sandbox: `ui-audit/verify-notes-tier1.mjs` §8 — 14 rows against the real built app, including the tone change asserted on the NODE (not the button), the fold recorded in the document, and the print sheet's **laid-out text** (`innerText`, not `innerHTML` — a closed `<details>` still carries its contents in the markup, so a check written against the HTML passes on a sheet that prints a blank box). `test/notesTier1.test.js` — every tone's marker, a callout holding a list, and a closed toggle exporting identically to an open one.

- **THE MEASUREMENT, his, and it is what makes this a bug rather than a tuning note.** Three samples of a query whose geometry parameter is **byte-identical run to run** — a 126-character 9-sample polyline transect, `sampleCount=9`, `RSP_BilinearInterpolation`, derived from the site's georeference; he captured it, re-ran the check and compared the strings — came back at **997 / 5,761 / 7,702 ms**, i.e. **68–90% of a 3.6–8.5 s check**. The existing 512 KB/entry · 3 MB budget is B1162's, unchanged. TTL **180 days**.

A press that blocks on USGS cannot deliver the second. So the press forces the network call AND publishes the held value immediately, patching the fresh answer in when it lands — the stale-while-revalidate shape /CLAUDE.md already mandates for every screening fetch. Both of his requirements are true: a wrong cached value is still one press from correction, and the press no longer costs up to eight seconds.
- **LOUD (his condition, verbatim: "a cache hit must be visible in the freshness hover, never silent").** `groundElevNote` states it with the value's age — *"held from an earlier USGS 3DEP elevation read (2mo old); bare-earth ground does not move"* — plus whether a refresh is running underneath it. `[ ]` **⏳ SHIPPED — one row per check, through the production sink, with the delivery outcome kept. `Verify: live` → V97121.**

- **WHAT IT RECORDS.** Per leg, in milliseconds: `elev` · `ctx` · `flood` · `bfeLines` · `xs` · `siteGrid` · `wse` and **one `wse:<raster>` row per county water-surface service** (the granularity his own PerformanceResourceTiming timeline had and the app did not — a group total cannot say WHICH county layer went slow) · `ebfe` · `maapnext` · `screening` · `gis` · `calc` · `save` · `total`. Plus the ground-elevation state, whether it came from cache, and whether it timed out.
- **`calc` IS A GAP IN THE NETWORK TIMELINE, NOT A BLOCKING FIGURE**, and the distinction is deliberate (`/CLAUDE.md` → FOREGROUND-OR-VOID): it is the interval between the last network leg settling and the publish. A gap is sound whatever the tab's visibility was doing; a main-thread blocking figure would not be, which is exactly why the owner declined to quote one.
- **THE SAVE LEG IS ATTRIBUTED, NEVER ASSUMED.** The Supabase write is not issued by the check — it rides the plan's own debounced cloud push — so it is stamped from there and only inside an 8 s window. Outside it, a save is just a save.
- **NO SILENT SINK (B265536's rule, applied to our own report).** `reportDrainageTiming` keeps the sink's OUTCOME: "we called send" is not "the server took it". A refused row is recorded as a failure with its reason, readable via `drainageTimingDelivery()` without a database round trip. A check whose save never arrives still emits its row after the window, because an absent report and a zero-cost save must not look the same.
- **PRIVACY: an ALLOWLIST, not a habit** (`perfCapture.js`'s discipline). A leg name can come from a GIS service key, so a row is BUILT from `DRAIN_LEG_KEYS` plus sanitised, length-bounded `wse:` names; anything else is dropped. Values are milliseconds. Nothing about the site, its geometry, its owner or its address is in the row.
- Sandbox: `test/drainageTiming.test.js` (26) · `test/fbcdWse.test.js` (+5 per-raster hook cases) · full suite green.
### B298401 — The flood layer can draw from a baked per-county archive instead of calling FEMA on every pan `[Site Planner / GIS]` (feature) #gis #floodplain #perf #site-planner  *(filed 2026-08-09 from the owner chat block "Planyr — floodplain performance, Phase 1", item NEW-2. None of them bakes anything. Net-new.)*
`[x]` **⏳ SHIPPED behind `VITE_FLOOD_TILES` (default OFF), fully proven headless, and parked in ⏳ Verify (`Verify: live` → V96960) for the one measurement this sandbox structurally cannot take.**

- Origin: filed 2026-08-09 from chat; shipped the same session.
- **WHAT IT DOES.** When the flag is on and the plan's county has a baked archive, the FEMA row renders from `public/flood/flood-<state>-<county>.pmtiles` — range-read off the same Cloudflare Pages origin that already serves the app — instead of calling FEMA's `/export` on every pan and zoom. **Same panel row, not a second one:** a second row would double-paint and would ask the owner a question about our plumbing.
- **⛔ THE FAIL-SOFT GUARANTEE IS THE LOAD-BEARING PART, AND IT IS A PROPERTY OF A PURE FUNCTION.** `floodTiles.resolveFloodSource` answers `live` for EVERY way the fast path can be unavailable — flag off · no county on the plan · county with no archive · an archive that failed earlier this session · called with nothing at all — each with a stated `reason` on the status channel. The runtime half is one terminal `_die()` in the layer: a 404 or an unparsable header disarms it ONCE, tears the slot down through `layers.js`'s existing shared `release` helper, and re-enters `syncOverlayLayers`, which then takes the raster branch exactly as it does today. A per-TILE miss is deliberately NOT that — most of a county has no polygon in it, and an empty tile is the ordinary case.
- **⛔ PARCEL-SCALE AUTHORITY IS UNCHANGED, AND THAT LINE DOES NOT MOVE.** A tile is generalised — simplified per zoom, quantised to a tile grid — so it is the right source for the FAST PICTURE and the wrong source for any number a user acts on. The screening / mitigation math still queries live FEMA; every tile identify card carries *"the parcel's authoritative zone and acreage still come from the live FEMA query."* Fast picture from tiles, exact number from FEMA.
- **⛔ AND THE ABSENCE RULE IS NOT THE SAME ON BOTH SOURCES, which is a trap worth naming.** The build DROPS unshaded Zone X, so on tiles "no polygon here" means **outside the mapped floodplain** — a real finding. On the LIVE layer it means **no effective flood map at this point** (the honest gap `layers.js` opts into with `identifyGap: "flood"`), which is the opposite risk position. `floodAbsenceKindFor(source)` is the one place that decides which wording applies; showing the live layer's absence wording over a tile answer would turn a clean result into a scare.
- **BUNDLE, MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSUMED.** The vector-tile stack (`pmtiles` + `@mapbox/vector-tile` + `pbf`) is reached ONLY by a dynamic `import()` at layer-switch-on, so it lands in its own **38.1 KB** chunk (`floodTileLayer-*.js`) and no visitor downloads it unless the flag is on AND their county has an archive. The site route pays **+5.0 KB** for the pure decision / manifest / normaliser code — measured by running the bundle audit against this branch's base with the tree stashed (site route 2387.1 KB → 2392.1 KB; largest chunk 1495.3 → 1499.6 KB). The four "above baseline" warnings the audit prints are inherited from main and reproduce identically on the stashed build.
- **⛔ WHAT IS DELIBERATELY NOT WIRED, so it is not read as an oversight.** The **map finder** stays on live FEMA: it has no plan county, and the county under the viewport changes on every pan, which would rebuild the layer mid-gesture. Phase 2 can pass `countyForView` if the fast path is wanted there; the fail-soft path makes that a one-line change with no new risk.
- **Sandbox evidence.** `npm test` green · `npm run lint` 0 errors · build green · bundle audit within ceiling. New suites: `test/floodTiles.test.js` (48) and `test/floodTileRender.test.js` (22) — the second drives the REAL committed Harris archive rather than a synthetic tile, because the two properties worth guarding (a floodway painting on top of the SFHA it sits inside; the identify naming the feature that was drawn) are both properties of real data and a hand-built fixture would satisfy them by construction. `test/layerAbovePlan.test.js`'s teardown census went 2 → 3 with the new call site named.
- **Headless evidence — `npm run verify:floodtiles`, 10/10.** Tiles paint in **286–320 ms** over **3 range requests / 27,392 bytes**; **zero** agency requests for the picture; the vintage stamp renders; a **404 archive hands the row back to live FEMA** (6 agency requests where the working archive made 0). The full harness is `ui-audit/verify-flood-tiles.mjs`.
- **⛔ THE PLAN'S CENTRAL MECHANISM WAS REFUTED BY MEASUREMENT AFTER THIS PR OPENED, AND THE FIX IS IN THE SAME BRANCH: CLOUDFLARE PAGES DOES NOT DO HTTP BYTE SERVING.** The brief's design is *"read by the browser with HTTP range requests."* Measured against a REAL Pages deployment of this branch (`claude-planyr-floodplain-pha.planyr.pages.dev`, `server: cloudflare`, `cf-ray` present): a ranged GET returns **`HTTP 200` with `content-length: 6246238`, no `accept-ranges`, no `content-range`.** Repeated (not a cold-cache artifact) and reproduced on the 665 KB Adams archive, on `manifest.json`, and on a plain `/assets/index-*.js` — so it is a property of the HOST, not of these files. **The control rules out the sandbox's egress proxy:** the identical ranged request through the same proxy returns `206` + `content-range` from `raw.githubusercontent.com` and `registry.npmjs.org`.
- **⛔ AND IT WOULD HAVE SHIPPED GREEN.** `pmtiles`' own `FetchSource` REFUSES a 200-with-full-body — *"Server returned no content-length header or content-length exceeding request. Check that your storage backend supports HTTP Byte Serving."* — so the layer would have thrown on its FIRST read in production and fallen back to live FEMA, permanently and silently. Nothing here would have caught it: **the Vite dev server DOES honour Range** (verified: 206, 127 bytes), so `verify-flood-tiles` 10/10, every unit test and every local run stay green over a feature that cannot work where it ships. That is the "green on a build that cannot work" class this repo keeps naming, and it was found only because the Cloudflare preview URL made a real host reachable.
- **THE FIX — ADAPTIVE, NOT A SWAP** (`lib/floodArchiveSource.js`). The first read asks for a range like any other client: a **206** keeps the cheap path (a few KB per tile, nothing held); a **200 with the whole body** means the host ignored the range, so that body is KEPT and every later read is a memory slice — the archive is fetched exactly **once**. No host detection, no configuration, a future Cloudflare that enables byte serving is picked up for free, and the dev server keeps its ranged path. Concurrent cold-viewport reads are deduped, so N tiles do not become N whole-file downloads.
- **⛔ AND THE WHOLE-FILE PATH IS NOT A CONSOLATION PRIZE AT THIS SIZE.** The largest archive is 5.96 MiB and measured **0.65 s** to fetch complete from Pages; after that every tile in the county is a memory slice with zero network, and static assets on Pages are **unmetered**. What it costs is one held ArrayBuffer per open county (dropped by `forgetArchive`) and a slower FIRST paint on a cold cache — which is why `public/_headers` now gives `/flood/*` `max-age=3600, stale-while-revalidate=86400`, and gives the MANIFEST the same policy so a refreshed vintage can never appear over stale tiles.
- **✅ AND THE FIX IS PROVEN ON THE REAL HOST, not only in a simulation of it.** The shipped reader was driven from Node against the live Cloudflare Pages deployment of this branch: **Harris — header + 5 z13 tiles decoded (38 / 70 / 19 / 60 / 52 features) in ONE request, 5.96 MiB, 1,094 ms total**; **Waller — 1 request, 0.69 MiB, 231 ms.** That is the same code path the browser takes, against the same host the app is served from, so the whole-file behaviour is measured end to end rather than inferred from the header dump that found it.
- **GUARD.** `test/floodArchiveSource.test.js` (9) drives the REAL committed Harris archive through BOTH measured host behaviours and requires them to decode the **same tile, feature for feature** — plus: exactly one whole-file fetch however many tiles are read · the held buffer is released · a short read and an error status both throw LOUDLY rather than feeding an error page to the tile decoder · three concurrent cold reads produce ONE request.
- **⛔ THE GAP, STATED PLAINLY — this is why the item parks.** Every `hazards.fema.gov` request **from Chromium** in this sandbox dies with `ERR_CONNECTION_RESET` (Node reaches the same host fine — that is how the archives were built). So the harness can prove the live path is ENGAGED and can NEVER prove it PAINTS, which means the tiles-vs-live first-paint comparison — the number the owner actually asked for — has no live half here. The harness DETECTS the block and says so rather than reporting the sandbox's egress policy as a defect in the app. V96960 owns the remaining steps.
