- **HIS TWO REPROS, and what they do NOW.** Setup: a paragraph "para one", a top-level bullet "bullet one", and "bullet two" nested under it. **A —** caret at the very start of "bullet two", one Backspace: it **outdents one level and does nothing else**; it no longer also merges into its parent. **B —** caret at the very start of "bullet one", one Backspace: it **becomes a plain paragraph keeping its text**; no merge into the paragraph above, **no empty orphan bullet**, and only a SECOND press joins it upward.
- **⛔ HIS EXACT SYMPTOMS ARE NOW REPRODUCED, BY A SWEEP RATHER THAN BY A GUESS — and the first pass at this item was wrong to ship without them.** `ui-audit/find-backspace-symptoms.mjs` (NEW) presses a real Backspace once at **every textblock start in 99 list-shaped documents — 414 probes** — and reports either symptom by name.   - **"bullet onebullet two" as ONE item** — a list that FOLLOWS another list of a different type. Caret at the start of the second list's first item, one press, and the two items merge: `taskItem > "A1A2"`. That is his sentence, reproduced.

- **⚠ THE HONEST RECORD OF THAT FIRST PASS, kept rather than quietly corrected.** It shipped a harness whose 37 rows asserted a SPEC — and **26 of them stayed green with the fix reverted.** A row that passes on the broken build is not evidence. The harness now labels every row **defect** (red on a revert to main — 11 of them) or **pin** (a boundary main already gets right, kept as a regression guard and never presented as proof), and `DEFECT_ROWS_EXPECTED` fails the run if a defect row is quietly downgraded.
- **⛔ AUDIT-FIRST — THE MECHANISM. Beyond the two symptoms above, his exact repro on a plain bulleted list did NOT reproduce in this sandbox** (a nested item outdented cleanly on the pre-fix build, and a top-level one converted without an orphan). What DOES reproduce, and produces his symptom exactly, is a document that **MIXES a checklist with a bulleted list** — which an Outlook paste routinely makes. Tiptap's `ListKeymap` runs its Backspace handler **once per list type** (`listItem`, then `taskItem`) over a `forEach` that does not stop at the first one to act, so pass two runs against the state pass one already changed. **Measured on the pre-fix build:** one press at the start of a bullet nested inside a checklist left `task one` AND `bullet two` as plain paragraphs — **both levels of the list dissolved by a single keystroke.** Both orders (checklist-in-bullets and bullets-in-checklist) do it. That is the class he reported, and it is now a permanent, mutation-proven row.
- **⛔ AND THE BOUNDARY NOBODY HAD LOOKED AT WAS WORSE THAN EITHER: one press at the start of a paragraph that follows a PICTURE DELETED THE PICTURE** — `joinBackward` removes a leaf it cannot join into. Same for a SKETCH. Found by the enumeration in B291537, not by a report. It now SELECTS the picture, so the destructive step is a second, deliberate press. (This is B1392 ×2's Tab defect — "a selected picture was REPLACED by a tab character" — arriving at a different key, which is the argument for enumerating a key rather than patching the case that got reported.)
- **THE FIX.** `lib/notesBlockKeys.js` is now a TABLE, not a special case: a pure `blockStartAction(state)` decides which single step applies, and the extension claims Backspace at a priority **above** `ListKeymap` so position zero is decided by that table and by nothing else. `ListKeymap` still owns Delete, Mod-Backspace and every press that is not at position zero, and typing `- ` then Backspace still takes the bullet back (`undoInputRule` keeps its first refusal).
- **⚠ ONE THING THE SCHEMA WILL NOT GIVE HIM, stated rather than buried.** He asked that a top-level item becoming a paragraph keep "its children where they are". A sub-list cannot exist in this document model without a parent list item, so when the parent stops being one, the children necessarily render at the first list level — one indent step left. The alternative is an empty parent bullet, which is precisely the litter he forbade. **What the fix does guarantee:** the children keep their text, their bullets, their order and their nesting *relative to each other*, and nothing merges. If the indent step matters to him, say so and it becomes its own item.

All three are Done and all three are about MAKING the recovery work; **not one of them records what it chose.** Also searched `chunkReload`, `recoveryStage`, `preloadError`, `client_errors`, `B279`, `B468`, `B265536`, `B270912`, `B270913`: **B265536** made the telemetry SINK report its own outcome and is the direct model for this — it is the same defect one layer up, and this is not a recurrence of it (that one was about whether a row was delivered; this is about a row that was never built). Net-new.)*
`[ ]` **⏳ SHIPPED — the outcome, the attempt count and whether the page came back all go on the wire. `Verify: live` → V85616.**
- Verify: live → V85616 (`Blocker: real-data` — the only place these branches fire is a real deploy against a real open tab; the sandbox has no deploy)
- Origin: filed 2026-08-09 from the owner's speed-review chat block
- **⛔ THE DEFECT, IN HIS WORDS AND CONFIRMED AGAINST THE TABLE:** `chunkReload.js` picks between `reload`, `stuck` and `cooldown`, and **not one of the 361 rows records which.** Verified by query, not assumed — every row's `url` had already had the `?_r=` cache-buster stripped by `stripReloadParam` at install, long before the error was reported, so **`with_r` is 0 across all 361**: even the one incidental trace of a rescue was gone. 82 silent successful rescues and 82 users at a wall wrote byte-identical evidence.
- **⛔ AND THE ANSWER TO HIS QUESTION IS NOT THE ONE THE ROW COUNT SUGGESTS — 361 ROWS ARE 54 EPISODES, NOT 361 INCIDENTS.** Grouped by `(build, chunk)`: **54 distinct first-failures**, of which **37 are a lone row followed by five quiet minutes** (consistent with a rescue that worked) and **17 kept failing inside 90 seconds** (the rescue did not take). **301 of the 361 rows are a repeat within 90 s of an identical predecessor.** So **90% of the volume comes from 31% of the episodes**, and the deploy-day spikes he flagged are not crowds:
  - **2026-08-06 (82 rows)** — build `53d1bac`, chunk `terrainLayers-aE2wQGtV.js`, **ONE tab, 2 h 20 m, 81 rows spaced exactly 10 s apart.** 10 s is `DUP_MS`, the telemetry dedupe window — so that cadence was the INSTRUMENT's, not the failure's, and the true attempt rate is unknown and higher. One wedged tab is **22% of every preloadError row this app has ever written.**
  - **2026-07-21 (132)** — two episodes, 15:45 and 20:01, four chunks each, both over inside two minutes.
  - **2026-07-05 (76)** — one episode, four chunks, **over in 10.3 seconds.**
- **⛔ WHAT THAT DOES NOT LICENSE, stated because the temptation is exactly here.** "37 episodes went quiet" is **not** proof of 37 recoveries. A tab that gave up and closed also goes quiet. The inference is the best the existing data supports and it is still an inference — which is the whole argument for shipping the record rather than a better query. From now on the answer is READ, not reconstructed.
- **THE SHIP — a paired event (`source='event:chunk-recovery'`), because the recovery row cannot be the failure row.** A rescue's mechanism is that the page NAVIGATES: the tab that would report success is destroyed by the fix. So an EPISODE record rides `sessionStorage` across the reload (`RECOVERY_KEY`), and the page that comes back says so itself. Six outcomes: `reload` · `stuck` · `cooldown` · **`landed`** (a `?_r=` page booted — the reload delivered a document that runs) · **`recovered`** (landed, and nothing failed in the 15 s that followed) · **`left`** (an episode was open and the tab escaped some other way — the user rescued themselves, which is not the guard working). Each carries `n` reload ATTEMPTS, `f` failures, the chunk, and the build it came from and landed on.
- **⛔ THE LADDER, and it is a correctness property rather than tidiness.** A paired event carrying a rising counter has a fresh signature every time, so it slips `decideReport`'s 10 s dedupe **entirely** — a naive version would have written a row per cursor move and manufactured the noise it was built to explain. Rows go out on a 1-2-5 ladder (1, 2, 3, 5, 10, 25, 50, 100, 250…) with the true count riding each one: the 2 h 20 m episode costs **about ten rows instead of eight hundred**, and its last row still states its real size.
- **⛔ THE EPISODE EXPIRES (30 min).** Without that, one long-lived tab ratchets the attempt counter forever and every number after the first is a lie.
- **`RECOVERY_SETTLE_MS` IS 15 s, NOT 2.** The chunk that fails is fetched by a route mount or a first interaction, not by the entry script — a page that has merely booted has not yet re-attempted the import it died on, and a short window would call every episode recovered before the failing import was tried. Silence for the settle window is the weakest claim the data supports and it is the one made.
- **THE MECHANISM BEHIND THE WORST EPISODE IS ITS OWN ITEM — B287060**, and it is why 08-06 looked like a crowd.
- Sandbox: `test/chunkRecovery.test.js` (21) — including that all six outcomes stay distinguishable, that `n` counts reloads while `f` counts failures, that the ladder stays sub-linear on the real 800-failure storm, and that a normal boot puts NOTHING on the wire. `test/chunkReload.test.js` (19) unchanged and green. Full suite **9,716 green across 492 files** · lint 0 errors · build green.
- **BUNDLE, MEASURED BOTH WAYS rather than claimed — the B217537 standard.** This branch's OWN contribution, measured by building its tree and `main`'s tree back to back: **+1.9 KB site route · +1.7 KB Notes route · +3.3 KB total · +0.3 KB largest chunk.** The recorded baseline is **already +22.3 / +26.4 KB behind main on its own**, so reporting the raw delta would have charged these items for a drift they did not cause; that drift is **B1064**'s and **B1178** remains open. **No ceiling raised and no baseline re-recorded.** The Notes route pays 1.7 KB for a recorder it will never fire — `chunkReload.js` is in the entry chunk every route downloads, by design (the guard must be armed before any lazy chunk is requested), and the alternative is a lazy import that cannot be loaded when the thing that is broken is lazy imports. **It stays, and this is the sentence that says why.**
- **⛔ NO ROW IN `public.client_errors` WAS DELETED, TRUNCATED OR MODIFIED.** Every number above comes from read-only `SELECT`s.

- **THE MECHANISM.** `loadTerrain()` clears its cached promise on failure so a network blip cannot wedge every later call — right, and unbounded. Its caller is `useGroundElevation`'s **per-`pointermove` cursor sample**. So a chunk that is genuinely gone got a fresh `import()` per mouse movement, forever.
- **MEASURED, not theorised.** Build `53d1bac`, chunk `terrainLayers-aE2wQGtV.js`, 2026-08-06, 15:32:55 → 17:53:27: **one tab, one dead import, 2 h 20 m**, arriving as 81 rows at exactly the 10 s dedupe cadence. **This one tab is 22% of every `vite:preloadError` row in the table**, and it is the entire reason his "82 on a deploy day" looked like a crowd.
- **AND THE CHUNK WAS NOT STALE.** The tab picked up `53d1bac` at 15:32:51 and the chunk failed **four seconds later**, on the freshest build — a mid-deploy edge skew, not the stale-hash case B221 was built for. The guard then correctly chose `stuck` (a `?_r=` page that fails again must not reload-loop) and correctly disarmed itself. Nothing surfaced that state, because a LAYER import failure never reaches the `ErrorBoundary` — so the app kept running, and kept hammering, for over two hours.
- **⛔ RECONCILED AGAINST #976 (b830000) BEFORE RESOLVING THE REBASE — NOT A TWIN, AND IT RE-OPENS NOTHING.** #976 landed *"B1349's owner gate is CLOSED (B1442 answered it), the terrainLayers half is proven resolved, and the residual red is the instrument (B295168)"*, and its evidence path is **exactly** the call chain this item changes: `useGroundElevation` → `terrainLazy.loadTerrain()` → `warmCursorGrid`. Read in full before resolving. Three findings, three verdicts:
  - **B1349's `terrainLayers` half asks WHEN the chunk is fetched on a HEALTHY page** — idle → absent, first mouse move → arrives, which #976 calls "the correct on-demand pattern this item itself prescribed". **This item asks what happens when that fetch FAILS**, which #976 does not address at any point. Different question, same module. **Not a duplicate.**
  - **⛔ AND IT CANNOT CONTRADICT #976's MEASUREMENT, which is the claim that actually needed checking rather than asserting** — a backoff on the very path #976 just measured is exactly how a close-out gets silently re-opened. `retryDelayMs(0) === 0`: **the first attempt waits ZERO**, so on a healthy page the first mouse move still pulls `terrainLayers` immediately and #976's idle-then-move result is unchanged. That is now a NAMED REGRESSION TEST citing B1349 and #976 by number (`test/terrainLazyBackoff.test.js`), not a sentence — because the next session to widen this backoff into the success path would re-open a closed item with nothing to notice.

- **THE FIX — a DELAY, never a CAP.** Exponential backoff, 2 s doubling to a 60 s ceiling, reset on success. A cap would cost terrain for the rest of the session over one blip, and a blip is the common case. `terrainNow()` keeps returning null inside the window, which every caller already treats as "not yet", so **no caller learns a new state**. Modelled against the real episode: ~840 attempts over 8,431 s becomes **under 150**.
- **LOUD-FAILURE holds.** The in-window refusal REJECTS (it does not resolve to a fake success), and all four call sites were re-checked to have a rejection handler — an unhandled rejection would have fed `window.onunhandledrejection` straight back into `client_errors` and traded one noisy source for another. `[x]` `newBlankSite` created a site with no origin and the planner read `const origin = restored?.origin || null` — read-only, with no writer anywhere in the app. With no origin the basemap is forced off and every geo effect early-returns, so the aerial, FEMA flood, contours, ground elevation, cursor lat/lon and county detection — and therefore jurisdiction, setbacks and drainage rules — were dead for the life of the plan.

SLIDE moves only the anchor, so not one drawn coordinate changes. Both are ordinary undo frames.

It survives a reload. **8 mutations proven red**, including the one that mattered: deleting `ensureBasemapOn()` left the map created and the first version of the spec GREEN, which is the B1422 shape (observing the mechanism instead of the payoff) — the spec now asserts the tile layer, not the map.

### B290240 — Unincorporated land was told "Texas counties have no zoning" in every state, including Colorado `[Site Planner / entitlements]` (bug) #site-planner #entitlements #gis  *(filed + shipped 2026-08-09 from the Colorado missing-data audit. `[x]` `deriveZoning`'s unincorporated branch asserted Texas law verbatim wherever the site was — and on Colorado ground it asserted the OPPOSITE of the law.

- **Why this leads the audit's ranking.** Every other finding here is a number that is wrong by a measurable amount. This one is a false ENTITLEMENT answer, and entitlement is the fact that decides whether an industrial building is by-right or a 6–12 month rezone. C.R.S. 30-28-111 et seq. gives Colorado counties zoning authority and every Front Range county exercises it: unincorporated Weld is zoned under the Weld County Code, agricultural by default, with industrial reached by a rezone or a Use by Special Review. A developer reading *"Unincorporated — Texas counties have no zoning"* on the owner's own raw Weld ground prices a by-right development on land that needs an entitlement.

Texas is byte-identical. Colorado states the real rule and points at the district / by-right / rezone / USR question. An **unidentified** state asserts no state's doctrine at all. The card's caveat also stopped naming City of Houston to a Colorado reader.
- Keyed rather than branched on purpose: a third state cannot be added without stating its own doctrine.

### B290243 — The Colorado 72-hour drawdown statute returned a soft pass on a plan with no pond at all `[Site Planner / pond]` (bug) #site-planner #pond #floodplain  *(filed + shipped 2026-08-09 from the Colorado missing-data audit. Minted from this branch's block. **DEDUPE-FIRST** — B1103 shipped `drawdownStatute.js` and its three-valued verdict; this is a missing PRECONDITION on that gate, not a failure of the verdict vocabulary, so it takes its own number rather than re-opening B1103.)*
`[x]` `assessStatutoryDrawdown` evaluated C.R.S. 37-92-602(8) against a zero stored volume and reported the site inside both statutory limits.
- Verify: **live** · `Blocker: live-GIS` — the line renders inside the Yield → Stormwater group, which only mounts once the drainage/flood context resolves. **V88801.**
- **The defect, and it is the #1423 shape exactly: a gate that passes when its input is missing.** `drawdownTime.drawdownHours` guards on `v < 0`, so a zero volume returns 0 hours (its own header says it must never return a zero — *"a zero would read as drains instantly, the exact opposite of the truth"*). 0 hours is inside both limits, so a Colorado plan with a release rate entered and **no pond drawn** rendered *"Inside Colorado's 72/120-hour drawdown limits (C.R.S. 37-92-602(8)) — screening, not compliance"*: a water-rights screen reading green on a facility that does not exist. Reproduced: `verdict: "not-ruled-out"`, headline *"Colorado drawdown statute not ruled out"*.

### B295008 — A click that drifts a pixel MOVES the element — up to a couple of feet once the flush-snap catches a neighbour `[Site Planner / interaction]` (bug) #site-planner #selection #ui  *(filed 2026-08-09 from the owner chat block as NEW-1, with his own diagnosis attached and confirmed correct in full. No prior item gates the MOVE path on travel. Net-new.)*
`[ ]` **⏳ SHIPPED — gated, mutation-proven both ways, and driven live logged-out. `Verify: live` → V93568.**
- Verify: live → V93568 (timing/interaction class + a real-project-data repro)
- Origin: filed 2026-08-09 from chat; shipped the same session.
- **THE OWNER, verbatim:** *"sometimes when I intend to just click on something to select it, it actually also moves it, like, a couple feet or, like, a pixel or two just because my click is too slow even though, like, to me, it feels like an instantaneous click, and it shouldn't move. Maybe I hold it for a couple milliseconds, and it accidentally moves the element. And I'd like it to stop doing that."*
- **HIS DIAGNOSIS WAS RIGHT, ALL FOUR PARTS.** (1) `SitePlanner.jsx`'s `move` branch computed `dx = fp.x - d.fx` and wrote new positions on the FIRST pointermove — no travel test anywhere. (2) The app already had the constants and the pattern: `PARCEL_CLICK_SLOP_PX` / `PARCEL_CLICK_MS`, used four times (B310 · B735 · B383 · the tap-to-clear), **every one of them on the `pan` branch**. (3) `pushHistory()` fired on pointer DOWN — see B295009. (4) The size: with snap on, the branch runs an ambient `edgeSnapCenter` at up to a **20 ft** tolerance, so one pixel of tremor enters the move path and the flush-snap then aligns the element to a neighbour's edge. That is the "couple of feet", and it is why it is intermittent — it only bites when a neighbour edge is inside tolerance.
- **THE FIX IS ONE GATE, APPLIED ABOVE EVERY BRANCH — not a patch on the branch he named.** `lib/dragGate.js` + `startGate(e)` spread into every `drag.current` that moves existing geometry; the test runs once at the top of `onMove`, so a press that has not travelled past the slop returns before any branch and writes **nothing at all** — no geometry, no history, no row write. **28 drag starts** are gated: element and parcel moves, group moves, markup move/resize/rotate, callout move + width, measurement move + chip, the acreage chip, the dimension slide, all five vertex layers, element resize / edge-resize / rotate, road ends and road vertices, the underlay, sheet-overlay move / scale / rotate, and the print frame. `pan` / `draw` / `mkDraw` / `marquee` are deliberately UNGATED and named in the guard, so the exemption is a decision on the record: a slop gate would change what a click-to-place draw or a tap-to-clear pan MEANS.
- **⛔ TRAVEL ONLY, AND THE MODULE HAS NO CLOCK — his second clause, and he was right that copying the pan test verbatim ships the mirror-image bug.** A slow, deliberate press that never moves is still a click; a fast flick that travels far is a drag however brief. `test/dragGate.test.js` fails if `dragGate.js` ever reaches for `Date.now` / `performance.now` / `timeStamp` / `setTimeout`, and asserts a gate held for 5,000 moves at zero travel is still a click.
- **⛔ THE NO-JUMP CLAUSE SPLIT IN TWO, AND THAT IS THE ONE THING THE OWNER'S SPEC COULD NOT HAVE KNOWN.** Rebasing the pointer by the swallowed travel is right for a MOVE (it carries a grab offset, so nothing downstream can tell) and **WRONG for a drag that AIMS AT A POINT**: a vertex written to `snapPt(fp)` then trails the cursor for the whole gesture, and a road endpoint released on another road's endpoint lands **outside the snap-and-connect magnet and never welds**. Caught by `e2e/road-connect-radius`, not by reasoning. So the rebase is opt-out and the seven point drags (`vertex` · `elVertex` · `measureVertex` · `mkVertex` · `easeVertex` · `roadVtx` · `roadEnd`) pass `{ rebase: false }` — their only "jump" is the one that design has always had, five pixels of travel later than before. Resize / rotate / scale keep the rebase: they aim at a dimension, so starting from the current size is what reads as no jump there.
- **RELEASE PATHS ARE GATED TOO** (`dragArmed(d)`): a plain click on a resize handle no longer prunes a stranded apron, a click on a road vertex no longer welds a junction or flashes a civil-radius warning about a curve nobody touched, and a click on a reshaped building's vertex no longer re-derives its dock frame.
- **AUDITED BEYOND THE PLANNER, as instructed.** Doc Review's markup move **already had** a travel gate (B293, 3 px, travel-only — the pattern the planner never got, which is itself evidence for the diagnosis); its missing half, the arm rebase, is added here so a Review markup no longer hops when its drag begins.
- **PROOF, both directions.** `test/dragGate.test.js` (30) — the pure rule plus a wiring guard that reads every `drag.current` in the planner; **mutation-proven**: removing the gate from the element move, and restoring `pushHistory()` on the press, each take it red (the first version of the history guard passed on a broken build and was rewritten because of it). `e2e/click-never-moves.spec.js` (4) drives the real app logged out — **all four proven red on the pre-fix build**, where the tremor click moved the building **cy 771.43 → 774.29 ft** and the slow press moved it **cx 1028.57 → 1034.28 / cy 771.43 → 774.29**. Full suite 9,702 green; lint clean; build green.
- **NOT claimed green in this sandbox, and not caused here:** `road-branch-and-label`, `wall-kid-drift` and `dock-zone-host-run` fail on the UNCHANGED tree too (measured by stashing the change and re-running), and the latter two flip which cases fail run to run on one build. They are flaky/red here already; nothing in this change touches their paths.

### B276576 — The app booted behind a render-blocking Google Fonts stylesheet; the landing page's fix was never carried across `[Infra / UI]` (bug) #infra #ui #perf #testing  *(filed 2026-08-08 from the owner chat block as NEW-1, re-verified against main @ #959. Minted **B276576 / V73584** from this branch's reserved block B276576–B276591, against origin/main bacae4b. **DEDUPE-FIRST — this is a RECURRENCE-BY-OMISSION of B1384, not a duplicate of it:** B1384 fixed `public/landing/index.html` only and is correctly Done; the root `index.html` was never touched. Searched Open / ⏳ Verify / Done across `fonts.googleapis`, `webfont`, `Inter`, `render-blocking`, `preconnect`, `FCP`, `firstContentfulPaint`, `B1384`, `B758`, `B1040`, `B1041`: **B1384** is the landing-page instance (different file, already shipped); **B1040/V477** owns re-seeding the paint ceilings from production and is referenced, not duplicated; **B758** owns the boot watchdog in the same file and is untouched. A grep of `BACKLOG_OPEN.md` for `fonts.googleapis` returned nothing — the app-entry instance had never been filed. Net-new number, deliberately: the original B1384 shipped and stuck for the file it named.)*
`[ ]` **⏳ SHIPPED — Inter self-hosted, the boot path is free of cross-origin render-blocking resources, and the A/B proving it is mutation-checked in both directions. Parks for the one thing no sandbox can see: what the deployed edge serves. `Verify: live` → V73584.**
`[ ]` **Every load of the app waited on a third-party round trip before any of its own code could run — and two instruments had recorded the defect and responded by MUTING the metrics it spoiled.**
- Verify: live → V73584 (the deployed edge's `content-type` on `/fonts/*.woff2`, and the production paint number; `Blocker: live-deploy`)
- Origin: filed 2026-08-08 from chat (NEW-1)
- **THE DEFECT.** `index.html:176` carried `<link href="https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Inter:…" rel="stylesheet" />`. A stylesheet is render-blocking, and — the part that actually bit — **a script cannot EXECUTE until every preceding stylesheet has resolved**, including `<script type="module" src="/src/main.jsx">`. So the whole app boot queued behind `fonts.googleapis.com`, and that host's latency passed through one-for-one. Anyone with an ad-blocker, a filtering resolver or a slow link paid it on **every single load**. `public/landing/index.html:93` had been fixed for this in B1384 (DOMContentLoaded 12,964 ms → 149 ms); the app entry was never carried across.
- **⛔ THE PART THAT MATTERS MORE THAN THE BUG: TWO INSTRUMENTS SAW IT AND MUTED THEMSELVES.** `ui-audit/perf-harness.mjs` downgraded every load-sensitive metric to *MEASURED BUT NOT JUDGED*, and `docs/PERF-BUDGETS.md` wrote the behaviour up as expected. Both were **correct at the time** — the sandbox blocks the font host, FCP went ~330 ms → ~13 s, and crying wolf is worse than silence. But the mute outlived its cause and nothing was watching for that. A budget muted for a bug we have since fixed is a budget nobody is enforcing.
- **THE FIX — SELF-HOSTED, not merely deferred.** The landing page's `media="print"` + `onload` promotion makes the request non-blocking; self-hosting removes the second origin outright, so there is nothing left to be slow, blocked or filtered. Google's own subsetted variable WOFF2 files now ship from our origin (`public/fonts/`), declared with `@font-face` at the top of `src/index.css`, with a `crossorigin` preload of the latin subset in `index.html`.
- **THE COST, AND A CORRECTION TO THE ITEM'S PREMISE.** The chat block asked me to cost this against the bundle ceilings and warned headroom was tight (largest chunk 17.3 KB of 32 KB, total JS 85.2 of 93.9 KB). **Those ceilings do not apply: all four committed bundle metrics — `siteRouteJsBytes`, `notesRouteJsBytes`, `totalJsBytes`, `largestChunkBytes` — measure JS bytes only.** A WOFF2 in `public/` is neither JS nor CSS-inlined (Vite's 4 KB inline limit is far below these files), so **self-hosting spends zero of that headroom.** Transfer size is unchanged at **47.1 KB** (identical bytes, from our origin instead of Google's); `latin-ext` (83.1 KB) is declared but `unicode-range` means it is fetched only if such a character appears, which for this UI is never. Five static weights collapse into one **variable** file (`font-weight: 400 800`). Cyrillic/Greek/Vietnamese deliberately not shipped — the `system-ui` fallback in `--font` covers them.
- **NEGATIVE CONTROL, RED FIRST — `ui-audit/verify-font-blocking.mjs` (`npm run perf:fontblock`).** One build, one server, two documents, same injected latency: **arm A** is the pre-fix build with the removed `<link>` re-injected, **arm B** is what we ship. Arm A **must stall or the harness fails**, because an instrument that cannot see the bug it was built for is not evidence of anything. Measured at a 2,000 ms delay: **first paint 2,372 → 384 ms · app mounted 2,058 → 81 ms** — a **1,988 ms pass-through eliminated** on a 2,000 ms delay, reproducing the owner's one-for-one finding almost exactly. At `--delay 0` (a *perfectly fast* font host — the best possible case for the pre-fix build) it is still **596 → 448 ms first paint, 152 → 98 ms mount**, so the win is not only about slow hosts.
- **THE INSTRUMENT IS UN-MUTED, and the mute now asks the right question.** The old gate was `failedExternal.size === 0 && !NO_TILES` — "did any external host fail" — which is a *different question* from the one that governs paint. A failing aerial **tile** host does not delay first paint by a millisecond. Split into two: **paint-sensitive** (`firstContentfulPaintMs`, `timeToFirstDragMs`) gated on the document carrying zero cross-origin **render-blocking** resources, measured live from the DOM so the mute **returns automatically and names the culprit** if one is reintroduced; **tile-sensitive** (`firstAerialCoverageMs`) keeps the original gate and is **not** un-muted. Immediate payoff: **`timeToFirstDragMs` is judged for the first time and PASSES at 1,435 ms against its 4,200 ceiling.**
- **⚠ WHAT UN-MUTING EXPOSED, AND THE CEILING I REFUSED TO MOVE.** The first judged run reports **FCP 688 ms against the 500 ms ceiling**. It is **not** a regression from this change and the ceiling was **left untouched**: the same harness on the **unmodified pre-fix tree** reports **668 ms** on the same container (run-to-run noise — it was always there, hidden by the mute), and the 500 ms figure was seeded on **production planyr.io on the owner's machine** (measured 328 ms, dpr 2.15, signed in) while this is a shared sandbox container. Re-seeding from a sandbox number, or nudging the ceiling to 700 so the run goes green, would be choosing a threshold to fit a result. **Answering "is 500 right?" needs a production run, which is already logged as V477.** Recorded in `docs/PERF-BUDGETS.md` rather than quietly absorbed.
- **GUARDS, two kinds on purpose.** `test/bootRenderBlocking.test.js` (11 cases, in `npm test`) forbids the static property — no cross-origin render-blocking tag, no third-party font host, preload present with `crossorigin`, both WOFF2 files valid and un-truncated, `font-display: swap` on every face. **Mutation-proven:** re-injecting the removed `<link>` turns it red (2 failures), restoring it turns it green. The browser harness measures; the unit test forbids.
- **ALSO CARRIED ACROSS: `public/sequence/index.html`** had the identical defect and now uses the same self-hosted files (no new bytes). **Stated honestly and asserted in the test rather than hidden:** that page still pulls two *other* render-blocking third-party resources (the jsdelivr icon webfont stylesheet and a synchronous supabase-js script), so removing the font host does **not** make it third-party-free the way it does the app entry. Those are a functional-dependency question, not a font question, and were deliberately left alone.
- **✅ THE EDGE CHECK WAS ATTEMPTED, NOT ASSUMED — and it came back clean.** V477 records that `curl` reaches these hosts even though Chromium is socket-reset, so the highest-risk unknown was reachable and was tested against the **real Cloudflare edge** (PR #961's branch preview): **both WOFF2 files return HTTP 200 with `content-type: font/woff2`**, byte-exact (48,256 / 85,068), valid `wOF2` signature, self-declared length matching actual length. That is the failure mode that fails *silently* — a wrong MIME type falls back to `system-ui` with no console error — and it does not happen. Also confirmed on the deployed document: **zero live tags naming `fonts.googleapis.com`/`fonts.gstatic.com`** (the one textual match is the explanatory comment), preload present with `crossorigin`, and the hashed app CSS really carries both `url(/fonts/…)` references.
- **✅ CONFIRMED ON PRODUCTION `planyr.io` after #961 merged (2026-08-08).** Both WOFF2 files: **200, `content-type: font/woff2`, byte-identical to the repo copies** (compared byte-for-byte, not just by length). Deployed document on `/`, `/?app` and `/#/`: **zero live tags naming a third-party font host**, preload present, and the hashed app CSS carries both `url(/fonts/…)` references. *(`/landing/` still shows four — B1384's intended non-blocking pattern, expected and allowed by the test.)*
- **⚠ DEPLOY PROPAGATION IS NOT ATOMIC, recorded because it nearly produced a false failure.** For the first minutes after the merge the edge served the **new font files** alongside the **old HTML** (Google link still present, preload absent). A post-merge check run in that window reads as a broken deploy when it is a half-finished one. Both settled within minutes. **MERGED ≠ LIVE cuts both ways: don't call it live off the merge, and don't call it broken off one early probe.**
- **PENDING LIVE (V73584), and it is now narrow:** re-tested this session against **both** the preview host and `planyr.io` itself, Chromium dies with `ERR_CONNECTION_RESET` either way, so what remains is only what a **real browser on a real network** can see — `document.fonts.check('16px Inter')` true, the latin file fetched **once** (a `crossorigin` mismatch on a font preload silently doubles the fetch while looking perfect), `latin-ext` **not** fetched on an English session, type visually unchanged, and the production `firstContentfulPaintMs` now reported as JUDGED with a value worth re-seeding the 500 ms ceiling from. Overlaps V477 — do both in one pass.
- **A defect that is invisible until it is slow is invisible to a screenshot.** Nothing about this changes a pixel when the font host is fast, which is why it survived months of visual checks and why the guard is a timing A/B, not an image diff.
### B276752 — Containment is a WHOLE-SITE question, and the badge was asking one lot `[Site Planner]` (bug) #gis #site-planner #floodplain  *(filed 2026-08-08 from the owner chat block as NEW-1, verbatim: "Go and check every site I have, the labels are generally hit or miss on accuracy". Minted **B276752 / V73760** from this branch's reserved block B276752–B276767 · V73760–V73775, against freshly-fetched `origin/main` bacae4b. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open / ⏳ Verify / Done across `jurisdiction`, `badge`, `ETJ`, `edge only`, `unincorporated`, `containment`, `cityCentroid`, `B763`, `B764`, `B792`, `B793`, `B823`, `B1091`, `B209502`, `B209506`–`B209509`: **B209506 is the closest and is AMENDED below, not duplicated** — it replaced "does a city TOUCH the ring" with "does the CENTROID sit in a city", which is the right question asked of the wrong geometry; this item is the first to notice the centroid it used belongs to ONE parcel. **B793** owns the edge-only demotion and is untouched. Net-new mechanism.)*
`[ ]` **⏳ SHIPPED — implemented, and driven against the LIVE agency services across all 28 of the owner's Texas sites. `Verify: live` → V73760.**
- Verify: live → V73760
- Origin: filed 2026-08-08 from the owner chat block (NEW-1)
- **THE PORTFOLIO SHAPE IS THE FINDING, and it is why this was never a Bain oddity.** Queried live at all 28 Texas origins: **8 inside city limits · 16 unincorporated inside the Houston ETJ · 4 unincorporated with no ETJ.** Twenty of twenty-eight — 71% — are unincorporated, and **17 of those 20 have a city polygon within a kilometre**, so the frontage-sliver trap is loaded on nearly all of them.
- **ROOT CAUSE, and it is not the one that was filed.** The header identify reduces a site to `representativeRing` — the single LARGEST active parcel — and asks which city THAT lot's centroid is in. **Twelve of the 28 sites are assemblages** (Goose Creek 16 parcels, 8 South 19, Martini 14, Tsakiris 9, Schiel 9, Will Clayton 6…), so on those the governing jurisdiction was decided by a coin flip weighted by lot size. Measured: at **Tsakiris** two of the nine parcels sit inside Katy's limits, the biggest happens to be one of them, and the pill printed a bare **"City of Katy · Waller County"**. At **Goose Creek** the opposite: the biggest lot is outside Baytown so the boundary query returned NO city at all, while **six of the sixteen parcels are inside Baytown** — a fact the app could not see from one ring.
- **FIXED — containment is asked of EVERY active parcel** (`parcelProbePoints`, largest first until the tested lots cover 98% of the drawn area, hard cap 16), and the answer is now FOUR states rather than two: **`in`** (a city holds the whole site → it leads, unqualified) · **`partial`** (it holds some parcels and not others → *"Part in City of X / part unincorporated"*, ⚑ straddle) · **`none`** (→ **Unincorporated**, the answer 20 of 28 sites need) · **`unknown`**. Cost is unchanged for the common case: one MULTIPOINT query replaces the one centroid query, and the per-parcel attribution pass only runs when a city is actually involved.
- **AND THE HOLE THE OWNER PREDICTED, closed exactly as he stated it.** With containment `unknown`, `formatJurisdictionBadge` fell back to leading with the RING UNION — so a failed containment lookup rendered as a positive containment answer, with no qualifier. That is the reported *"City of Baytown"* shape. A city may now lead ONLY on a positive containment answer; an unknown says **"City limits · couldn't check"** and every ring city is demoted to **"· touches"**, never the site's jurisdiction. The test that asserted the old behaviour (`B793 — NO centroid answer … keeps the pre-B793 behavior`) was the assertion that let it through and is replaced.
- **⚠ ONE CORRECTION TO THE BRIEF, and it is load-bearing.** Goose Creek and Tsakiris were filed as *"unincorporated, no ETJ, city within 1 km"*. At the site ORIGIN that is right, and the sweep confirms it. Across the DRAWN SITE it is not: Baytown holds 6 of Goose Creek's 16 parcels and Katy holds 2 of Tsakiris's 9, per TxGIO. The origin is one point and the site is many — the same confusion that produced the bug. Both now read as genuine splits, which is neither "City of X" nor a flat "Unincorporated", and in both the city is never presented as the site's jurisdiction — the property the owner asked for.
- **A `partial` city is still passed to the floodplain administrator as a candidate** (`cityLabel`), because `resolveAdministrator` picks the STRICTER rule: dropping it would let a site half inside a city be priced entirely on the county's laxer standard.
- Sandbox: `test/jurisdiction.test.js` (96 incl. the new `parcelProbePoints` block) · `test/jurisdictionShapes.test.js` (10, mutation-checked) · full suite 9187 green · lint 0 errors · build green · `npm run perf:bundle` within ceiling.
- **Live, all 28 sites, before → after: 18 correct / 1 mislabelled / 8 unresolved → 27 correct / 0 mislabelled / 0 unresolved** (the 28th, GREEN RIVER, has no active parcel geometry so the app shows no badge). Full table on V73760.
- **⛔ CORRECTED 2026-08-09 BY THE OWNER — the Goose Creek line above is WRONG and B280704 replaces it.** He wrote: *"For goose creek part of the site is in city limits and part is in ETJ, so it should clarify."* This item's sweep found the straddle but described the remainder as "part unincorporated" — a string that was hardcoded, never measured. Re-measured per parcel: 6 of 14 tested lots inside Baytown's city limits, **the other 8 inside Baytown's ETJ, none unincorporated**. The `partial` state and the per-parcel probe this item shipped are correct and are what made the correction possible; the remainder LABEL was a guess, and the ETJ behind it was invisible because the H-GAC layer does not carry Baytown at all (**B280705**). Do not read the "Goose Creek" row of the table above as current.

### B276753 — An unresolved jurisdiction must be first-class END TO END, not just in the badge `[Site Planner]` (bug) #floodplain #gis #yield  *(filed 2026-08-08 from the owner chat block as NEW-2. Minted **B276753** from the same reserved block. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open / ⏳ Verify / Done across `unresolved`, `settled`, `administrator`, `FFE`, `pending`, `B209507`, `B209508`, `B1089`, `B1127`: **B209507/B209508 are AMENDED below, not duplicated** — they made a FAILED role first-class inside `formatJurisdictionBadge` and `assessAdministrator`; this item closes the three seams where that signal never reaches them at all. Net-new.)*
`[ ]` **⏳ SHIPPED — implemented and measured live. `Verify: live` → V73760.**
- Verify: live → V73760
- Origin: filed 2026-08-08 from the owner chat block (NEW-2)
- **The stake, restated with the portfolio behind it:** on **16 of 28 sites** the Houston Ch. 19 rule (500-yr WSE + 2 ft) is the load-bearing floodplain fact, and one dropped ETJ lookup silently hands the site the county rule (BFE + 2 ft), commonly **1–2 ft LOWER** in flat Harris and Fort Bend floodplain. Sixteen sites, not one.
- **THREE SEAMS where B209508's signal never arrived, each fixed:**
  1. **The swallowed `catch`.** `SitePlanner`'s badge effect ended in `.catch(() => {})`, leaving `jurBadge` null — indistinguishable from "not looked up yet". `assessAdministrator` then received an EMPTY `unresolvedRoles`, reported `settled: true`, and the Yield panel printed a finished FFE off the county rule. A rejected identify now produces a badge that SAYS "Jurisdiction · couldn't check" and carries all three roles as unresolved (LOUD-FAILURE).
  2. **The pending window.** Before the first lookup returns there is no ETJ candidate at all, so the panel printed a settled FFE and then silently changed it a second later. `jurisdictionPending` is now a first-class signal; `assessAdministrator` reports `pending` with its own wording ("still being looked up"), distinct from a failure, and refuses to settle either way.
  3. **The cache pinned failures.** `jurBadgeCache` is keyed on parcel geometry and lives for the session, so a badge whose ETJ lookup failed pinned that site to "couldn't check" until a reload — on a source measured flaky at exactly this. An unresolved badge is still SHOWN (it is the honest state) but no longer REMEMBERED, so the next activation asks again.
- **A FOURTH defect found while measuring it, and it silently cost the ETJ on four sites.** The ETJ was deduped against `cities` — every city the boundary TOUCHES. At **Kennedy Greens, JFK, Katz and Pinnacle** a Houston sliver clips the parcel edge while the site is unincorporated land inside the Houston ETJ, so **the sliver suppressed its own ETJ** and the pill read "City of Houston · edge only": a jurisdiction the tooltip itself calls "unlikely to govern" shown INSTEAD of the Ch. 19 authority that sets the finished floor. An ETJ is now deduped only against the city limits that genuinely HOLD the site, and once named as an ETJ a city's edge sliver is not given a second slot.
- **Also:** a containment probe that fails while the boundary query succeeds now adds `city` to `unresolvedRoles`, so the gap reaches the administrator rather than stopping at the pill.

### B276755 — The identify query 404s past a URL ceiling, and a 404 reads as "nothing here" `[Site Planner]` (bug) #gis #site-planner #floodplain  *(filed 2026-08-08 — NOT from the owner's block; found while measuring NEW-1/NEW-2 across the portfolio, and it turned out to be the single largest cause of his "hit or miss" report. Minted **B276755** from the same reserved block. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open / ⏳ Verify / Done across `simplifyRing`, `query url`, `404`, `maxRecordCount`, `truncat`, `exceededTransferLimit`, `B366`, `B369`, `B1079`, `parcelTruncation`: **`parcelTruncation.js` is the closest and is a DIFFERENT defect** — it detects a RESPONSE cut short by `maxRecordCount`; this is a REQUEST rejected before any query runs. Net-new.)*
`[ ]` **⏳ SHIPPED. `Verify: live` → V73760.**
- Verify: live → V73760
- Origin: discovered 2026-08-08 while running the portfolio sweep for B276752
- **MEASURED, on the owner's own parcels, on the same service seconds apart:** Will Clayton's county query built to **2325 characters → HTML 404**; Bain's, at **1512 → 200**. `services.arcgis.com` (IIS) rejects a /query whose URL runs past roughly 2 KB of query string, and **a 404 decodes as "this layer has nothing here."**
- **So the county and the ETJ came back EMPTY on any site whose boundary was finely digitised — deterministically, as a function of how many vertices the surveyor drew, while looking exactly like "no ETJ here."** This is what B209507 recorded as the ETJ source being *"measurably flaky — 0 at three of six points"*: it was never flakiness. Before the fix **8 of 27 sites** could not resolve their county or ETJ; after it, **none**.
- **Root cause:** `simplifyRing` bounded the VERTEX COUNT (80), which is the wrong quantity — 80 lon/lat pairs at full double precision is ~2.5 KB of query string.
- **Fixed, two bounds:** coordinates are rounded to **6 decimal places** (~4 inches, far finer than any boundary layer's own precision, and most of the saving on its own), and the vertex count then walks a ladder down until the built URL fits `MAX_QUERY_URL`, never below a triangle. A coarser intersect test beats no test at all. POST would remove the ceiling outright but the B445 same-origin cache proxy is GET-addressed, so a POST body would silently bypass the cache — bounded GET keeps both.
- Sandbox: `test/jurisdiction.test.js` NEW-4 block (5 cases incl. the untouched-small-ring and point-query paths).

### B276448 — The one genuine cross-lane e2e failure was a spec B50010 had deliberately obsoleted the day before `[Site Planner / Canvas]` (bug) #testing #infra #site-planner  *(minted from this branch's reserved block B276448–B276463 · V73456–V73471, against freshly-fetched `origin/main` 294c0ce. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open / ⏳ Verify / Done across `dim-callout`, `B912`, `B50008`–`B50011`, `dblclick-properties`, `chrome-swallows-press`, `B592`, `B1174`, `B1327`, and the whole double-tap family: **B50010 is the CAUSE and is shipped and correct — it is not re-opened**; B266081 owns the ledger row and is AMENDED, not duplicated, per the dispatch. No item records this spec being stale. Net-new.)*
`[ ]` **⏳ SHIPPED — fixed, driven green in a real browser (logged-out local lane), and off BOTH lanes of the ledger. Parks for the one lane no sandbox can drive: `ci` is signed in against production. `Verify: live` → V73456.**
- Verify: live → V73456 (the `ci` lane — signed in, against production — cannot be driven from this sandbox; `Blocker: auth`)
- **Local-lane evidence:** 3 consecutive green runs of the full `dim-callout-edit` spec locally, plus the four red runs that established determinism first.
- **THE ROW #956 SINGLED OUT, and it was real.** `dim-callout-edit.spec.js:90` sat on the local ledger and had never once appeared in a production run until #42 — visible only because the two lanes are recorded separately. It was the most likely real defect of the three, and it was the only one whose *behaviour* had genuinely changed.
- **WHAT CHANGED, EXACTLY.** Until 2026-08-07 a double-tap on a building's dimension number at its DEFAULT position opened the inline length editor. **B50010 (commit `acd99a0d`, PR #932, 2026-08-07)** reversed that in `onDimNumberDown` — *"WHEN THE NUMBER SITS ON THE BODY, THE BODY WINS"*. The report behind it was a centreline road whose width number is anchored to the centreline midpoint and therefore painted ON the pavement, so a double-click aimed at the road could not miss it and the width chip swallowed a gesture the click contract says opens Properties. B50010 fixed it *"once in the shared dispatch for every type, not special-cased for road"* — and a building is caught by the same rule because **B592 clamps its number ONTO the footprint**. The case went red in BOTH lanes on 2026-08-08, the day after that merged.
- **WHY THE SPEC WAS THE STALE SIDE, not the code.** `CLAUDE.md`'s **CHROME-NEVER-EATS-A-PRESS** now cites B50010 as the standing rule (*"chrome sitting over its own object's BODY forwards the press to the body, asked once for every type"*), and `dblclick-properties.spec.js:210` already asserts the same contract for a road. Two specs were asserting opposite things; the contract is settled and this one had not been updated.
- **⛔ RETARGETED, NOT REWRITTEN — the coverage GREW.** Deleting the assertion, or reducing it to "Properties opens", would have quietly killed B912's feature and duplicated `chrome-swallows-press`. B50010 kept the inline editor *"exactly where the number is genuinely the only thing there"*, and that path had no guard anywhere. So the case is now TWO tests pinning both halves of B50010's rule: **(a)** number at its default position, on the footprint → Properties opens and the numeric editor does **not**; **(b)** number slid clear of the footprint → the editor opens and the building resizes to the typed depth, exactly as B912 always asserted.
- **THE MECHANISM THAT MAKES (b) REACHABLE, measured rather than assumed.** The number renders OUTBOARD of the dimension line (6 px beyond it, `textAnchor="end"`) and `dimSlideRange` lets the line slide to the end of the footprint — so sliding the dimension along parks the NUMBER in clear space. Measured on this build: it moves from x≈264 to x≈175 against a footprint whose left edge is x≈204, i.e. fully clear, `dimOffset.x = −252`, and the editor opens. Test (b) asserts that clearance explicitly, so if a future change re-clamps the number onto the body it fails **there**, loudly, instead of silently becoming a duplicate of (a).
- Origin: B266081 ledger row, dispatched 2026-08-08.

### B276450 — The contour hover's worst-case ceiling was never well-posed: replaced with the invariant it was reaching for, not loosened `[Site Planner / Terrain]` (bug) #testing #grading #site-planner  *(minted B276450 from this branch's reserved block. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open / ⏳ Verify / Done across `contour-hover`, `B1087`, `B1095`, `B1096`, `B1140`–`B1143`, `B1205`–`B1207`, `hitContour`, `HOVER_TOL_PX`, `terrainLayers`, `demGrid`: no item records this assertion being wrong, and no terrain defect is implied — the code is proven right below. B266081 owns the ledger row and is amended. Net-new.)*
`[ ]` **⏳ SHIPPED — fixed, driven green in a real browser (logged-out local lane), and off BOTH lanes of the ledger. Parks for the one lane no sandbox can drive: `ci` is signed in against production. `Verify: live` → V73456.**
- Verify: live → V73456 (the `ci` lane — signed in, against production — cannot be driven from this sandbox; `Blocker: auth`)
- **Local-lane evidence:** 3 consecutive green runs of the full `contour-hover-elevation` spec against the real USGS 3DEP DEM (relayed through Node, the app's own fetch/decode/worker/paint all running for real).
- **⛔ THE POND RULE APPLIED — a contour number, so which side was right was settled with EVIDENCE before either was touched. THE CODE IS RIGHT.** The assertion was `worst line-vs-readout disagreement ≤ 2.5 ft`; it failed at **`2.8000000000000114` on four consecutive runs — bit for bit**, so it was never flake.
- **THE EVIDENCE.** Probing the raw ground around the one offending sample shows it sits **in the bottom of a drainage channel**: 140.2 ft at the cursor, rising to ~147 ft within eight pixels on **both** sides — 11.3 ft of relief across a sixteen-pixel box. The 143-ft line the hover named **genuinely passes ~3 px from that cursor** (the raw grid crosses 143 ft between +2 px and +4 px), i.e. well inside the 6 px `HOVER_TOL_PX`. The trace is in the right place and the readout is right; they answer **different questions** — "the level of the nearest line within the tolerance" versus "the ground under the cursor". **59 of the 60 samples were within 1.7 ft** (median 0.6, p90 1.4): one channel bottom moved the MAX, nothing moved the distribution. No code in either grid has changed since the spec was written — the only commit to touch `terrainLayers.js` since (`609b0304`) is a z-order/pane change.
- **WHY IT WAS REPLACED RATHER THAN NUDGED.** A fixed FOOT ceiling on the max was never well-posed: the honest bound is `HOVER_TOL_PX × local relief per pixel`, which is **unbounded in a channel**. Moving 2.5 → 3.0 is precisely what the pond rule forbids, and it would re-break on the next sweep that clips a steeper bank.
- **WHAT REPLACES IT IS STRICTLY STRONGER.** Two guards, each with one job: **(a)** median disagreement ≤ **one contour interval** — the systematic-mismatch guard, since a units/datum/wrong-tile error shifts *every* sample while terrain shifts only the tail; **(b)** **the hovered line's level must be ATTAINED by the raw ground within the hover tolerance of the cursor**, checked on the three worst-disagreeing samples. (b) is what the max was reaching for, stated directly — and it catches a line traced in the wrong **PLACE**, which a foot ceiling never could. Measured: all reachable, **zero slack needed**. `HOVER_TOL_PX` is imported from `lib/contours.js` so the guard moves with the constant instead of silently going stale.
- **A REJECTED APPROACH, recorded because it looked right.** A per-sample derived ceiling (`tolerance × relief estimated from the neighbouring sweep steps`) was tried first and **refuted on its own evidence**: it cannot see relief PERPENDICULAR to the sweep, so it mis-fired on samples running along a contour (8 violations at 0.5 ft slack, still 1 at 1.0 ft). Discarded rather than tuned.
- Origin: B266081 ledger row, dispatched 2026-08-08.

### B270912 — The recorder was drowning its own signal: 89% of production telemetry came from automated runs `[Platform / Infra]` (bug) #perf #infra #testing  *(filed 2026-08-08 from the owner chat block. Minted **B270912 / V67920** LATE via `git fetch origin main && npm run next-id -- --against-main` from this branch's own reserved block **B270912–B270927 · V67920–V67935**, against origin/main 422cb3d; the code kept the provisional label through the renumber. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open / ⏳ Verify / Done across `telemetry`, `client_errors`, `perfcap`, `sink`, `noise`, `retention`, `e2e`, `fixture`, `B279`, `B468`, `B1215`, `B255200`, `B265536`, `B266080`: **B265536** is the parent and its opposite — it proved a row DOES travel and left the sink loud; this is the first item about rows that should NEVER have travelled. **B279** built the sink, **B468** its event tier, **B1215** and **B255200** are two of the loudest producers and inherit the fix unchanged. Nothing has ever asked WHO is writing to this table. Net-new.)*
`[ ]` **⏳ SHIPPED, both directions proven headless and both mutants proven red. Parks for the one thing no sandbox can see — the production row RATE after the deploy. `Verify: live` → V67920.**
- Verify: live
- Origin: filed 2026-08-08 from chat
- **THE MEASUREMENT.** `public.client_errors` took 679 rows in 24 hours; of 98 `event:perf` rows **87 were automated and 11 were the owner's — 89% noise**. Non-perf was the same story (`assembly-orphan-pad-repaired` 154 · `map-registration-out-of-range` 119 · `assembly-tear-persisted` 91 · `assembly-tear-detected` 65 · `county-healed` 47, all carrying e2e fixture ids), and #954's new logged-out CI lane had just multiplied the rate. Re-measured from the database this session: **5,162 rows · 410 in the last 24 h · 2,174 in the last 7 days · 3.2 MB · oldest 2026-06-20.**
- **WHY IT IS NOT TIDINESS.** #951's recorder exists so the owner pressing *"that felt slow just now"* reaches somebody. That capture was arriving as one row among several hundred synthetic ones a day, separable only by a READ-SIDE filter on his display signature — a workaround, not a design. **An instrument that buries the signal it was built to catch** is the class this repo has now caught six times: the swallowing sink (B265536), the frame-count sustain window, the packed track that emptied on real stalls (B265541), the drift gate's invented fixture (B266086), the growth harness whose plan B was plan A halved. A genuine production incident would have arrived buried the same way.
- **⛔ THE PREMISE OF THE BRIEF WAS FALSE IN THE FIELD, AND THE FIX TURNS ON IT (AUDIT-FIRST).** The dispatch said to gate on `window.__PLANYR_E2E`, citing `docs/PERF-PLAN-SWITCH.md` §1 — *"every performance harness in this repo sets"* it. For the **ui-audit perf harnesses that is true**; for the **e2e suite it is not**, and the e2e suite is where the measured noise comes from: **62 of the 81 specs in `e2e/` never set it**, `assembly-tear-detector.spec.js` — the top producer of three of the five loudest sources — among them. **A flag-only gate would have silenced 19 specs, left every top row untouched, and reported success.** So the primary detector is **`navigator.webdriver`**, which the browser sets itself under any automation protocol, is never true for a real user, and needs no per-spec discipline — it therefore holds for harnesses nobody has written yet. `__PLANYR_E2E` stays as a second door.
- **THE FIX.** `clientErrors.networkReportSuppression(win)` — a pure, exported, unit-tested decision (`automated && !optIn`), checked at SEND time in `sink()`. It **FAILS OPEN**: every unreadable branch returns "not suppressed", because silencing a real user over a throwing property read is strictly worse than one extra test row. Only a strict `true` counts, in either direction.
- **⛔ THE TRAP, WHICH IS THE WHOLE DIFFICULTY.** `verify-capture-pipe` proves the row reaches the wire, and its `rejected`/`offline` arms are the anti-rot half that proves a BROKEN delivery is LOUD — and **both run under automation**. Suppress unconditionally and that verification is disabled by its own fix, passing forever while observing nothing: the sixth instance of the class this closes. So the harness opts in DELIBERATELY (`window.__PLANYR_TELEMETRY_NETWORK`), and **both directions are asserted**.
- **THE LOCAL CAPTURE IS UNTOUCHED** — only the network write is suppressed. `pfTelemetry.recent()`, the IndexedDB capture store and the Storage panel all still work under test, which is what `verify-telemetry` and `assembly-tear-detector.spec.js` read (both re-run green).
- **SUPPRESSED IS NOT UNDELIVERED, and they never share a counter.** `_delivery.suppressed` / `pfRec.state().suppressed` are their own; `undelivered` keeps meaning *the server never acknowledged*. Folding them together would make every harness run look like a delivery failure, which is how a real one stops being noticed. The owner's button gains a third state, **`local`** — an automated run must not tell him the server is unreachable about a pipe that is working.
- **PROVED BOTH DIRECTIONS, AND PROVED THE GUARD CAN FAIL** (DANGEROUS-MEANS-UNOBSERVABLE (b)):
  - clean run — **all 5 arms green**, 12 perfcap rows on the wire from the opted-in arms, **0 writes to `client_errors`** from the suppressed one;
  - **MUTANT A**, suppression made unconditional (the opt-in ignored) → **7 assertions red** across `manual`, `manual-cold`, `rejected`, `offline` and `row` — the pipe guard cannot be blinded silently;
  - **MUTANT B**, suppression removed → **4 assertions red**, including **5 telemetry rows reaching `client_errors`** (a `window.onerror` among them — so error rows are covered, not just perf).
- **A REAL IMPRECISION THE ARM CAUGHT IN ITS OWN FIRST RUN, recorded rather than quietly loosened:** it asserted *"no request of any kind"* and failed on `/auth/v1/health`. Supabase is also this app's DATA backend — an automated run legitimately signs in and reads plans — so the claim is about **`public.client_errors`**, and every other request the page made is now PRINTED rather than ignored, so a future write to some other sink cannot hide behind the narrower claim.
- **⛔ NOTHING WAS DELETED, AND NO READ-SIDE FILTER WAS ADDED** — both were explicitly out of bounds. The table was READ only. Retention is a separate item and a separate decision: **B270913**.
- **A finding for whoever reads the table next:** 0 of the 410 rows in the last 24 h are identifiable as automated by `user_agent` or `url` (CI drives a real Chromium under xvfb against the deployed origin). **There is no server-side way to tell a test row from a real one**, which is why the read-side workaround had to key on his display, and why a client-side gate is the only correct fix — no cleanup query could ever have separated them.
- **Also seen while reading, NOT actioned here (out of scope, flagged not buried):** the owner's own signed-in session at 2026-08-07 19:07 fired `map-registration-out-of-range` **15+ times in 4 seconds** on his real plan. Once the synthetic rows stop, whatever remains on that source is real signal about his drawing/basemap registration — worth a look, on its own number.
- Files: `src/shared/telemetry/clientErrors.js` (the gate, the sink check, the `suppression()` handle) · `src/shared/telemetry/perfRecorder.js` (the suppressed/undelivered split) · `src/workspaces/site-planner/SitePlanner.jsx` (the button's `local` state) · `ui-audit/verify-capture-pipe.mjs` (the `suppressed` arm + the opt-in) · `test/clientErrors.test.js` (9 cases) · `test/capturePipe.test.js` (2 source guards).
- Guards: the repo-root `test/` suites **clientErrors** and **capturePipe** (the CI-runnable half — the browser half cannot run in this repo's CI), plus the ui-audit harness **verify-capture-pipe** (`npm run perf:capturepipe`), whose five arms now guard BOTH directions and are mutation-proven in both.
- Green: `npx vitest run` **9,168 passing** · `npx eslint .` **0 errors** · `npm run build` clean · `perf:capturepipe` ✅ all arms · `verify-telemetry` ✅ all checks · `e2e/assembly-tear-detector.spec.js` ✅ 3/3.

### B265536 — The recorder's production path, PROVEN — and the telemetry sink that swallowed every write failure `[Platform / Infra]` (bug) #perf #infra #testing #persistence  *(filed 2026-08-08 from the owner chat block, ITEM 1, verbatim: "does a capture written by the deployed build in the owner's signed-in browser actually REACH Supabase, survive RLS, and come back readable?" Minted **B265536 / V62544** LATE via `git fetch origin main && npm run next-id -- --against-main` from this branch's own reserved block **B265536–B265551 · V62544–V62559**, against origin/main c6a4b94. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open / ⏳ Verify / Done across `perfcap`, `recorder`, `telemetry`, `sink`, `client_errors`, `RLS`, `delivery`, `B279`, `B468`, `B1121`, `B1215`, `B255200`: **B255200** BUILT the recorder and is the parent — it proves an induced stall produces a capture IN CI and says nothing about the capture travelling; **B279** created the sink and is the code this fixes; **B1215** instruments deletes through the same channel and inherits the fix. Net-new: nothing here has ever checked that a telemetry row ARRIVES.)*
`[ ]` **⏳ SHIPPED and proven to the database. Parks for the one link no sandbox can reach — a real row from his own signed-in browser. `Verify: live` → V62544.**
- Verify: live
- Origin: filed 2026-08-08 from chat
- **⛔ THE DEFECT, and it was aimed at the highest-value signal in the programme.** `clientErrors.sink` handed the insert promise two empty handlers, under a comment stating the consequence: *"swallows all errors (including a missing-table / RLS rejection) so a telemetry failure is itself invisible."* Downstream, the owner's **"that felt slow just now"** button showed **✓ "Recorded — thanks"** off the LOCAL capture succeeding. So the one signal that comes from the person who actually has the symptom was also the one best able to vanish without trace — and B1121's whole disposition (*"instrument it so it captures itself"*) would have failed quietly for a week before anyone asked why no data had arrived. That is precisely the rot the NEVER-PARK stopping rule exists to prevent, so **the stopping rule was only sound once the pipe was proven.**
- **THE PROOF, link by link — full record in `docs/CAPTURE-PIPE.md`.** Deployed build `c6a4b94` carries the recorder chunk and arms it · an induced stall produces captures against the real trigger · each becomes a real POST to `/rest/v1/client_errors` · every row 1,687–1,765 of the 2,000-char cap, parsed back and its packed frame track decoded (64–128 frames) · **the RLS policy was executed for real against the production table as BOTH `anon` and `authenticated`** (with a live JWT claim), the row landing attributed to the caller's `user_id`, then selected back and parsed in SQL · **the `manual` kind round-trips**, warm (128 frames) and cold.
- **⛔ THE ONE HOP THIS SANDBOX CANNOT MAKE, stated rather than glossed.** The egress gateway answers **403 to CONNECT** for `*.supabase.co`, so no browser here can complete the real request. It is bridged, not skipped: the harness INTERCEPTS at the network layer (so what is asserted is the production bundle's actual POST, not a mock's) and the exact intercepted row is then inserted server-side under the real roles. What remains is his machine, his session, his network — V62544.
- **⛔ AND A TRAP WORTH KEEPING.** `INSERT … RETURNING` FAILS under this policy — `RETURNING` needs a SELECT policy and there deliberately is none — and it fails with wording that reads exactly like a rejected insert. The client must never `.select()` on this insert, and it does not. Consequence: a browser can only ever prove *the server accepted the write*. **A SELECT policy was considered and deliberately NOT added** — the write-only posture is a stated decision in `CLAUDE.md`, and changing a security posture to make a test easier is the wrong trade.
- **WHAT SHIPPED.** `sink` returns its outcome and keeps `lastSend` / `delivery` on `window.pfTelemetry` (readable live, no database round trip), with **one** bounded retry — one, not a queue: a telemetry channel that retries forever becomes the load. It still never throws into the app and never reports its own failure through itself. The recorder tracks delivery per capture and counts the undelivered. **The button's ✓ now means DELIVERED**: *sending* → ✓ on acknowledgement, or a warning saying the capture is kept on the device and could not reach the server.
- **THE ANTI-ROT ARM.** `ui-audit/verify-capture-pipe.mjs` (`npm run perf:capturepipe`) runs five arms; `rejected` answers the same insert with 401 and requires the button and `lastSend` to say so. **Before this item that arm was un-failable** — nothing in the app could observe a rejection, so no assertion about one could ever have gone red. CI-runnable half: `test/capturePipe.test.js` (27).
