### B236592 — A static pond re-derived its whole stage-storage model 156 times per pond per pan `[Site Planner / UI]` (bug) #site-planner #perf #pond #yield #ui  *(owner chat 2026-08-07, and his refusal of the premise is what made this correct, verbatim: "I don't really understand how a static pond, how the calculation should slow anything down at all. And you can give me the reason, but I still don't think it should." Arrived as the B227888 FOLLOW-ON brief, which named `interiorFitter` as the landing zone and a superlinear per-vertex law as the mechanism — both refuted below. Minted **B236592 / V33600** LATE via `git fetch origin main && npm run next-id -- --against-main`, as the last step before push, from this branch's own reserved block (B236592–B236607 · V33600–V33615). DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open + ⏳ Verify + Done across `pond`, `ring`, `vertex`, `interiorFitter`, `pondStageModel`, `offsetInward`, `clipper`, `drainFacts`, `B227888`, `B227477`, `B221761`, `B221763`, `B1440`, `B1352`, `B1437`: **B227888** is the MEASUREMENT that located this and stays open on its own live-verify terms — this is its fix, not a recurrence of it; **B221761** owns the pond LABEL-FIT memo and is **exonerated and confirmed working** by this profile (0.5 ms of a 55,760 ms gesture), not duplicated; **B221763** owns the pond LEDGER's render-body rebuild and is amended below rather than closed; **B1440 / B1352 / B1437** are the same VIEW-INDEPENDENT-ONCE class in different code and are the explicit model. Net-new.)*
`[ ]` **The owner was right and the brief was wrong: the defect is RECURRENCE, not complexity. 55,760 ms → 505 ms per pan (−99.1%) with his surveyed rings untouched, and nothing drawn changed.**
- Verify: live — V33600 · `Blocker: real-data` + `Blocker: auth` (same bound as B227888)
- Origin: filed 2026-08-07 from chat
- **⛔ TWO REFUTATIONS FIRST, because both were named in the brief and both are wrong.** (a) **`interiorFitter` is EXONERATED** — it runs 312×/gesture and costs **0.5 ms total**; B221761's memo hits exactly as designed, so the brief's landing zone was not the cost. (b) **THERE IS NO SUPERLINEAR PER-VERTEX LAW.** §5.5 decimated the rings and preserved the *bounding box* — but a bounding box is not a shape, and decimation removes **concavity**, which is what loads clipper's intersection sweep. **Collinear midpoint insertion** (same area, same perimeter, same bbox, same drawn path — only vertex count rises) measures an exponent of **0.20**: 16× the vertices for 1.75× the cost, and `maxInwardOffset` gets *cheaper* (−0.21) because clipper's `CleanPolygon` drops collinear points for free. §5.5's "920 ms per vertex" was `49,806 ÷ 54` — a whole recurrence attributed to the one variable that arm happened to name. **§5.5's headline needs re-reading exactly the way it re-read §5.4's Finding 3.**
- **CAUSE, counted rather than timed.** A JS self-time profile put **55,631 of 55,760 ms** in clipper-lib's intersection sweep; an invocation count on the probe build said why — **`offsetInward` ran 275,184× in ONE pan** (137,592 per pond), `maxInwardOffset` 8,736×, `pondElevations` 5,616×, **`pondStageModel` 312× = 156 per pond**. Two stacked defects, neither a formula: **(1)** `drainFacts()` in `SitePlanner.jsx` is *deliberately* GATING rather than memoising, so with the Yield panel docked the whole bundle rebuilds every render — 156 rebuilds per pond per pan, 155 of them bit-for-bit identical to the first; **(2)** `pondElevations` was re-derived **inside its own consumer** — `stageTable` asks once and twice more *per band* via `areaAtElev`, so a 7-band pond paid the 29-clipper-execute pinch-off search 15 times for a constant. That is the term that *looked* superlinear: a constant re-derived a linear number of times.
- **FIX — memoisation only, NO formula touched.** `offsetInward` / `maxInwardOffset` (`pondOffset.js`) and `pondElevations` / `pondStageModel` (`pondStageModel.js`) keyed on the ring's **identity** (the planner replaces `points` wholesale on edit, never mutates in place) plus det/opts by **value**. The key IS the inputs, so the cache cannot serve a stale engineering number — which is the exact property `drainFacts`'s gating-not-memoising comment exists to protect. `identityCache` gained a `cap` parameter (default 16 unchanged); one ring is legitimately asked for ~28 offsets by the binary search, and an under-sized cap clears on every call and pays the keying for nothing.
- **RESULT — the same 4 arms × 6 reps interleaved, same regime as §5.5:**

  | arm | work ms | vs §5.5 | vs `quiddity` | nodes | text |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | `quiddity` (**REAL 68-vertex rings**) | **505.1** | **−99.1%** (was 55,760) | — | 752 | 30 |
  | `simple-ponds` (decimated to 7) | 503.7 | −91.5% (was 5,955) | −0.3%, **p=0.688 NOT separated** | 752 | 30 |
  | `one-pond` | 479.1 | −98.8% | −5.1%, p=0.219 | 742 | 29 |
  | `original` (FAST) | 561.8 | −88.6% | +11.2% | 598 | 23 |

  **Acceptance was "quiddity with real rings must land near the simple-ponds number." It did better: ring complexity has ceased to be a variable** — the arm that recovered 89.3% now recovers nothing measurable, and the plan he calls slow is marginally *cheaper* on work than the one he calls fast.
- **⛔ NOTHING DRAWN CHANGED, PROVEN not asserted.** The rendered canvas was captured before and after on the real fixture and diffed: **752 canvas nodes · 30 text nodes · 52 elements · every element's vertex count and every bounding box byte-identical.** Both basins keep their surveyed 48 and 20 points. No fidelity is reduced at any zoom; no LOD decision was added.
- **THE THIRD QUESTION — "should we also make the pond math faster?" — answered "nothing further to do", with the number.** Measured **cold** (fresh ring identity every rep, exactly what a vertex drag produces): a full recompute of his **largest real basin is 15.4 ms**, inside one 16 ms frame; the second is 6.3 ms; and identity keying means only the *edited* pond recomputes. By the stated rule (under ~16 ms ⇒ stop) this is already fast enough and no formula is being rewritten. The constant factor improved anyway as a side effect of (2): one cold `pondStageModel` on the 48-vertex ring went **249.9 → 14.18 ms (17.6×)**. `pondFloodFacts` was never a suspect — it has had a content-signature LRU since B707.
- **GUARDS — all three count INVOCATIONS, never milliseconds**, because a time budget passes the moment a computation that should not run at all merely gets cheaper, and this programme has three cases on record of a cost class returning unnoticed behind a total. `test/pondViewIndependence.test.js` (16) — 156 identical rebuilds do **zero** additional clipper work · every input that can move an answer still does · per-vertex cost bounded on a **collinear-inserted** ring. `test/pondStorageGoldenMaster.test.js` (78) — **exact** equality (`toBe`, no tolerance, and the tolerance is not negotiable because these numbers size his basins) for every band, area, volume and split, on both real rings × 5 setting combinations × the full stage range. `ui-audit/count-pond-invocations.mjs --assert` — a pan recomputes **NO** pond geometry, **and** the cached lookups must be OBSERVED so an empty report cannot pass as a clean one. Mutation-checked: disabling the memos takes the unit guard 16 green → 4 red.
- **New instruments, kept:** `ui-audit/profile-pond-ring.mjs` (arm-vs-arm JS self-time diff) + `ui-audit/lib/cpuProfile.mjs` (CDP profile → self time per function) + `ui-audit/count-pond-invocations.mjs`. Bundle: **+0.2 KB site route, measured as zero attributable growth** (the three baseline overages reproduce identically without this change). Recorded in `docs/PERF-REAL-PLANS.md` §5.6.

### B230080 — The canvas clipboard is destroyed by a plan switch, so nothing could be copied between plans of one site `[Site Planner / UI]` (bug) #site-planner #selection #ui #coordinates  *(owner report 2026-08-07, verbatim: "I can't copy elements between pages of the same project. If I go to Silvestri, the print concept versus the same one just not the print concept, I can't copy a polygon over. And I'd like to be able to copy any kind of element over." Arrived as provisional NEW-1 with a source audit attached (`claude/handoff-2026-08-07-clipboard-dies-on-a-plan-switch-the-key-remounts-siteplanner.md`) — filed with a B# on sight per the 2026-07-15 intake rule. Minted **B230080 / V27088** LATE via `git fetch origin main && npm run next-id -- --against-main`, as the last step before push, from this branch's own reserved block (B230080–B230095 · V27088–V27103). Code, tests and commits keep the provisional `NEW-1` label. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open + ⏳ Verify + Done across `clipboard`, `paste`, `copy`, `CLIP_KINDS`, `planClipboard`, `overlayClip`, `B417`, `B461`, `B1059`, `B1124`: **B1059** (the NEW-2/NEW-6 general clipboard) built the COVERAGE and is correct and untouched — a polygon is a markup and was already in `CLIP_KINDS`; **B417** owns paste-at-cursor PLACEMENT and is kept; **B461** owns the overlay copy path; **B1124** owns bond remapping inside a copy. None of them owns WHERE THE PAYLOAD IS HELD, which is the entire defect. Net-new, and not a recurrence of any of them.)*
`[ ]` **AUDIT-FIRST, and it changed the shape of the fix: the clipboard's LIFETIME was the bug, not its coverage. Do NOT add kinds.**
- Verify: live — V27088
- Origin: filed 2026-08-07 from chat
- **CAUSE.** `SitePlannerApp.jsx` mounts `SitePlanner` with `key={`${activeSiteId}:${loadEpoch}`}`. Every plan of a site is its own record with its own id (plans of one site share a `groupId`; `activeSiteId` is the PLAN id), so a plan switch changes the key, React remounts `SitePlanner`, and `const clip = useRef(null)` inside it — the payload — is destroyed. `overlayClip` died the same way. The right-click menu then showed Paste disabled with "Copy a shape or drawing first", which is what the owner saw.
- **FIX.** The payload moved to **`lib/planClipboardStore.js`, at MODULE scope.** Deliberately not `SitePlannerApp` state: module scope is above EVERY remount boundary in the app at once — the plan-switch key, the `loadEpoch` bump, a workspace switch, a project switch, an error-boundary reset — rather than above the one that happened to be found. Reads are plain calls with no subscription, exactly like the `useRef` reads they replace, so nothing about React's render behaviour changes. Lifetime is the browser tab. **The overlay clipboard moved WITH it**, because leaving one behind is how the two Ctrl+V paths diverge again.
- **THE COORDINATE DECISION, stated: RE-PROJECT, and refuse loudly when re-projection would be a lie.** Clipboard geometry is feet in the SOURCE plan's frame, and `origin` is per-record — siblings usually share one (`New plan (same parcel)` copies it) but are not guaranteed to. So a cross-plan paste takes the payload out of the source frame to lat/lon and back into the destination frame through the SAME `mapLock` projection the planner is welded to (`resolveClipFrame`, `lib/planClipboard.js`), and **lands on the same GROUND POSITION it occupied on the plan it was copied from** — which is what "copy it over" means for two concepts of one parcel. **Real-world SIZE is deliberately NOT rescaled:** each plan's feet are ground-true at its own origin, so a 1,000 ft building is 1,000 real feet in either plan, and applying the Mercator grid-scale ratio between the two origin latitudes would shrink a copied building for no physical reason. That ignored scale term is therefore **measured, not assumed** — it appears as a positional smear across the copied set, and a paste whose smear would exceed `CLIP_FRAME_MAX_SMEAR_FT` (one foot, across the whole set) is **REFUSED by name** rather than landed in the wrong place. Two plans of one parcel never reach it; two plans in different cities do. The other refusal is `no-origin`: exactly one of the two plans is on the map, so the frames cannot be related at all. Both refusals carry owner-facing copy pointing at the cursor, and both are LOUD (LOUD-FAILURE). Two plans that BOTH have no origin are two abstract feet frames with nothing to reconcile — a clean no-op.
- **`lastPtrFt` — CHECKED, and the answer is that it stopped mattering.** It is a per-mount ref, so right after a plan switch there genuinely is no pointer history and the old fixed-nudge fallback would have fired. A cross-plan paste **never consults the cursor** — placement comes from the frame relation — so the fresh mount's empty pointer state is now irrelevant, and the paste is deterministic. It was left per-mount on purpose: a pointer position carried across a remount is stale by construction. A SAME-plan paste is untouched and still lands at the cursor (B417), nudge fallback and all. The cross-plan paste also takes NO nudge (there is no original here to sit on top of), and if the set lands outside the window the view pans to it (`revealPasted`) — "I pressed paste and nothing appeared" is the bug being fixed and must not become the cure's symptom.
- **Known and accepted:** a cross-plan overlay paste shares the source plan's `storageKey`, exactly as `⧉ Duplicate plan` already does — the reference points at the same stored file rather than re-uploading it.
- **ONE placement decision, not two.** The brief warned the two Ctrl+V paths would diverge the first time someone touched one, so `clipPlacement` (pure, in `planClipboard.js`) is the single decision both use: cross-plan-in-place → cursor → same-plan nudge → refuse. The drawn-object and reference-drawing paths now differ only in the wording of their toast.
- **PANEL-BREVITY:** not applicable (no yield/pond panel copy touched). `node ui-audit/panel-copy-budget.mjs --check` unchanged.
- **BUNDLE BUDGET — breached, optimized, then RAISED on the record.** The feature measures **+2.0 KB** on the Site route (2424.1 → 2426.2 KB). Optimized first: the duplicated placement logic collapsed into `clipPlacement`, the three refusal messages share one tail, and the modifier-label derivation was deduped onto the existing `MOD_LABEL`. That still breached the derived ceiling **by 0.7 KB — and clean main already measured 2367.3 KB, i.e. 45.1 KB of the 46.4 KB band was consumed by earlier merged work that never ratcheted, leaving 1.3 KB for the next feature of any size.** So `bundle.siteRouteJsBytes` was raised 2322.2 → 2369.3 KB via `npm run perf:ratchet -- --allow-raise` with that reason on the record (`ui-audit/perf-budgets.json` → `bundle.ratchetLog`). **This raise records accumulated reality, not this feature's cost.** `B1064` still owns getting the route back down.
- **Guards.** `test/planClipboardLifetime.test.js` (24: the store's lifetime, the frame decision incl. both refusals, `clipPlacement`'s four outcomes, and a SOURCE guard that the payload is not owned by the component again) + the e2e spec `e2e/clipboard-survives-plan-switch.spec.js` (4 cases). **NEGATIVE CONTROL, proven both ways in one session:** with the payload made to die with the mount (the pre-fix lifetime, injected), all four e2e cases go RED; with it removed, all four pass. Coverage is one of EACH kind — element · markup (the owner's polygon) · measure · callout · parcel — plus a mixed multi-selection, plus a workspace switch (Site → Sequence → Site) and a plan RENAME on the way.
- **Sandbox result:** lint 0 errors · `npx vitest run` **8,707 green across 468 files** · build green · bundle budgets green · the 4 e2e cases green against the built app. What is NOT proven here is signed-in behaviour → **V27088**.

### B779 — Concurrent-mint B#/V# collisions: catch loudly at PR time + prevent by late-binding (×3) `[repo / tooling · workflow]` (tooling) #infra  *(owner chat 2026-07-11 — "I thought I fixed the issue where branches use the same numbers … now you have to renumber your stuff?" after a concurrent floodplain/detention session (B763–B773) collided with this session's Layers-panel mints. Best-practice fix; sources: `scripts/next-id.mjs`, `test/idUniqueness.test.js`. `B779` late-bound against fresh main with `next-id -- --against-main`, the very rule this ships.)*
`[ ]` **DONE this session — `next-id` (B755) stops a session MISREADING the next-free number, but it can't stop two parallel branches (each branched from the same main, neither seeing the other's un-merged mint) from grabbing the SAME number — the distributed-counter impossibility. Made a collision RARE, AUTO-CAUGHT, and CHEAP without changing the id scheme or a big migration:**
- Verify: sandbox — 22 tests (`test/idUniqueness.test.js` + extended `test/nextId.test.js`); the guard was PROVEN to go red on an injected duplicate heading then green on revert; full suite **3577** green, lint clean, `next-id` output unchanged in default mode.
- Origin: owner chat 2026-07-11 (numbering collisions still forcing renumbers).
- **Guard (centerpiece):** `test/idUniqueness.test.js` fails the build if two ACTIVE items share a `B#` (in `BACKLOG.md`) or `V#` (in `VERIFICATION.md`) — so a colliding PR goes red BEFORE merge and renumbers then, instead of shipping silently (which is how ~50 historical archive dupes + a duplicate `V197` slipped onto main). `findDuplicateIds`/`findDuplicateIdsIn` added to `scripts/next-id.mjs`.
- **Prevention:** `next-id --against-main` folds in `git show origin/main:BACKLOG.md` etc., so a LATE mint (assign the number as the last step before push, `git fetch origin main` first — new CLAUDE.md rule) steps around ids merged after you branched. Collapses the collision window from a whole session to a few seconds; code/tests keep the provisional label so a rare clash renumbers only heading lines.
- **Scope (honest):** the guard enforces uniqueness on the LIVE files only. The write-only `*-DONE.md` archives carry ~50 historical cross-file collisions (genuine ones like B755=BFE-vs-next-id, V275=toggle-vs-thoroughfare, plus benign same-item re-listings) that predate the guard and can't be renumbered in place; `--against-main` prevents minting over them, and the full-pair audit stays available via `findDuplicateIds(REPO, B_FILES, "B")` for a future archive cleanup. Fixed the one live dup (`V197`→`V283`) as part of this.
- **Rejected (with reasons):** collision-proof ids (session/date tag or hashes) — repo-wide migration + loses "highest+1" ordering; auto-renumber-on-merge bot — fragile (must rewrite scattered prose + V#↔B# cross-refs). Both trade a rare, cheap, now-automated reconcile for a large or brittle system.

**Recurrence: 2026-07-30 (×2) — owner chat, "SIX in a row", handoff `claude/handoff-2026-07-29-backlog-id-collisions-assign-after-merge.md`.** Collided since the first pass: B1030/B1031 · B1032/B1036 · B1081/B1082→B1087/B1088 · B1093/B1094→B1095/B1096 · B1093/B1094→B1130/B1131→B1140–B1143 (renumbered TWICE in one PR, plus a merge-conflict redo). Owner's instruction was explicit: audit before redesigning, enforce the existing design rather than replace it, and do NOT rebuild the two things this item already rejected. **Both rejections re-examined and UPHELD — neither was re-litigated:** an auto-renumber-on-merge bot is still fragile for the stated reason (scattered prose + V#↔B# cross-refs), and hash/date/session-tag ids still cost a repo-wide migration and the "highest+1" ordering. Nothing in the audit weakened either.

`[x]` **DONE 2026-07-30 (second pass) — AUDIT-FIRST, and the audit overturned this item's own headline claim. The first pass was not being disobeyed; it was measuring the wrong window.**
- **THE ROOT CAUSE, reproduced (`(a)` answered — and the answer is NOT "sessions mint early").** Two clones, both branched from the same main, both `git fetch origin main`, both `next-id --against-main` as the last step before push — **both are handed the identical number**, same `provenance.sha`, both "fetched 0s ago". The late-bind rule was being followed *exactly* and still collided, because `--against-main` reads **one ref** and is structurally blind to the other branch. B1140's own note is the field evidence: its mint WAS late-bound with `--against-main`, and main took B1130/B1131 (#860) and B1132 (#862) while the PR was in flight. **The window that matters is `push → merge`** — PR open, CI nudge (often two), build, auto-merge — not `mint → push`. So this item's "collapses the collision window from a whole session to a few seconds" was **false as written**: minting later cannot close a window that opens after the mint. Corrected in place above and in CLAUDE.md.
- **`(b)` STALE `origin/main` — confirmed, and worse than suspected.** `git show origin/main:…` reads the local remote-tracking ref, and nothing verified a fetch had happened. Measured in a real session clone on 2026-07-30: `origin/main` sat **7 days / 169 ids behind** (maxB 974 vs 1143) while the banner still printed `[incl. origin/main]`. A stale `--against-main` is indistinguishable from a correct one.
- **`(c)` MORE SILENT DEGRADATION of the B898 shape — confirmed.** B898 fixed only the ENOBUFS path. A missing `origin/main` ref and a git-not-found both still hit `catch { return null }` with **no warning at all**, and `maxAgainstMain` folded the null into a local-only max that printed as success. `--json` carried no provenance whatsoever, so the degradation was invisible to any caller.
- **`(d)` The uniqueness guard is INNOCENT — it fires exactly as designed.** It went RED pre-merge on both B1140 renumbers (GitHub runs the required build on the PR's *test-merge* ref, so it sees the merged tree). B779's live guard and B780's cross-file guard are **deliberately untouched**: they are the backstop, and they work.
- **THE FIX — enforce the existing design; no new id scheme, no bot.**
  1. **Peer visibility (`scripts/next-id.mjs`).** `--against-main` now also folds in the ids **other in-flight branches have already claimed** — they are sitting on the remote and readable *now*, no merge required. `fetchPeers` mirrors remote heads into `refs/remotes/planyr-peers/*`; `peerClaims` reads them, deduped by blob sha and skipping any file a peer never touched (≈14 s fetch + ≈2 s scan over 499 branches / 35 in-window). This is what finally makes the "few seconds" claim TRUE: two sessions now collide only if both mint before either **pushes**.
  2. **Freshness is PROVEN, not assumed.** `--against-main` **REFUSES (exit 2)** on a missing, never-fetched, or stale `origin/main` (`--max-age`, default 300 s) instead of returning a plausible number, and reports the exact commit + fetch age it read (`[origin/main d5476d0, fetched 0s ago · 35 in-flight branches]`), in `--json` too.
  3. **No silent fallbacks left (LOUD-FAILURE).** `readOriginMain`'s null-on-anything is gone: `readRefFile` tolerates exactly ONE empty — "the ref is fine, the file isn't in it" — and reports every other failure, so no caller can mistake "couldn't read" for "nothing there". `GIT_MAX_BUFFER` is exported so the B898 regression test asserts the real value instead of scraping source.
  4. **Mechanically enforced, not a convention (`scripts/check-mint.mjs` + `.githooks/pre-push` + a required-build step).** The gate checks the **property** ("this id is unclaimed on main and on every in-flight branch"), never the ceremony ("was it minted late?") — a timestamp receipt would just be one more thing to drift. "Added" is measured against the **merge base**, not main's tip, which is what catches the B1140 case (main took the number mid-flight). A RECURRENCE mints nothing, so DEDUPE-FIRST never trips it. `npm run hooks:install`; `--ci` fails on a proven collision but only warns on an infrastructure problem, so a git hiccup can't wedge merges.
- **Verify: sandbox** — full suite **6,473 green / 383 files**, lint 0 errors, build green. Red-then-green proven end-to-end in a real multi-clone git lab (`scratchpad/repro.sh`): the gate exits **1** naming the claimant branch, and **0** after renumbering to the id it named — for BOTH failure shapes (an unmerged peer holding the number, and main having merged it mid-flight). Freshness refusal confirmed live (back-dated FETCH_HEAD → exit 2, no number printed). 30 new/updated unit cases in `test/mintGuard.test.js` + `test/nextId.test.js`, incl. gaps-stay-legal and recurrence-never-trips. The pre-push hook and the CI step were exercised on this item's own push/PR.
- **THE HONEST COST of the six collisions** (asked for explicitly, and it is lower than the "full CI re-run" framing): B780 established ids appear in code only as **comments**, so a renumber is a **few-line text edit of heading lines** — code, tests and commits keep their provisional `NEW-#` labels through any renumber. The real cost was the **extra push/CI cycle per renumber** (~2 min each) plus, on the worst one (B1140–B1143), a **merge-conflict redo** after a blanket resolution duplicated blocks. Roughly **eight wasted cycles and one manual conflict redo across six dispatches** — an ongoing tax and a genuine irritant, not rebuilt work. The guard never let a collision reach `main`.
- **The gate caught a bug in ITSELF, on its own PR — recorded because it is the failure mode that matters most.** The first CI run of the new step went RED with `V532 is ALREADY TAKEN on planyr-peers/claude/backlog-id-collision-recurrence-2z85n2` — **our own branch.** Cause: `actions/checkout` lands on the PR's test-merge commit in **detached HEAD**, so `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD` returns the literal string `"HEAD"`, the self-exclusion missed, and the branch read as its own rival. It passed locally (where the branch name resolves) and only failed in CI. Fixed two ways, belt and braces: `selfBranchNames()` also consults `GITHUB_HEAD_REF` / `GITHUB_REF_NAME`, and `dropContainedRefs()` drops any peer whose tip is an **ancestor of HEAD** — name-independent, so it holds even with no env vars. Pinned by a regression case in `test/mintGuard.test.js`. **A gate that cries wolf gets bypassed with `--no-verify`, so a false red is not a lesser bug than a missed collision.**
- **A second self-inflicted defect, found while fixing the first: the peer fetch was DAMAGING the clone it ran in.** `--depth=1` grafts every tip it mirrors into `.git/shallow` — including **our own branch**, which made git treat our own HEAD as parentless: `git merge-base` failed, `git log` went one commit deep, and the gate silently lost the merge base it needs for the B1140 case (falling back to main's tip, strictly weaker). Fixed with negative refspecs (`^refs/heads/main`, `^refs/heads/<self>`) so neither is ever mirrored, **plus a snapshot/restore of `.git/shallow`** so the file is byte-identical after a run — verified. Our own ancestry is now also resolved **before** any peer fetch touches the object store. A tool that inspects the repo must not modify it.
- **Residual, stated plainly:** the gate cannot see a branch that has minted but **not yet pushed**. That window is now seconds wide (mint immediately precedes push) instead of hours, and the B779/B780 uniqueness guards still catch anything that slips. Field behaviour across other sessions' dispatches → **V532**.

**Recurrence: 2026-08-06 (×3) — THE GATE IS NOW CORRECT AND UNSATISFIABLE. It has stopped being a rare renumber tax and become a LIVELOCK that halted every merge in the repo.** Filed from `claude/doubleclick-properties-bug-qijkn5` (PR #932) after **six** renumber passes in one session. This is a NEW failure mode, not a repeat of either prior pass — both of those were *collisions*; this is *starvation*.
- **Measured, not inferred.** `main` did not move for over two hours (`fee9a01`) with **16 branches in flight**. Peer build run `31128919262` (`claude/review-module-bugs-8236kb`) failed at **step 11, `Mint gate`** — steps 1–10 green, 12–15 skipped. Peers reach CI and die on the gate, so nothing merges; nothing merging means no branch's ids ever leave the in-flight set; which raises the mark for everyone still waiting.
- **The high-water mark, one evening:** B1478 → B1804 → B3219 → B3726 → B9004 → B25005 → B25017 → **B30007**. That is not sixteen sessions filing 23,000 items. It is each session reading the mark and minting defensively above it, and **every defensive mint raising the mark the next session must clear.** **The decisive measurement: this item's own filing then tried the opposite policy — MINIMUM next-free, no headroom, precisely so as not to feed the race — and the mark moved B25017 → B30007 in the ~3 minutes between reading it and committing.** So neither policy terminates: headroom accelerates the climb, and minimum-next is stale before a commit can be written. There is no number a session can choose, because the quantity being chosen is a function of what everyone else chose after you looked. That is the definition of a livelock, and it is why the fix has to be ALLOCATION (a reservation each session holds) rather than SELECTION (a number each session picks).
- **Headroom cannot outrun it, and headroom is the accelerant.** This branch minted B25000–B25003 with ~16,000 of deliberate headroom; `claude/notes-rail-hierarchy-bugs-26utv2` claimed **B25005 within four minutes** — and also **V9000**, the exact V this branch had just filed. The ×2 pass's own fix (`--against-main` reading in-flight peer branches) works **exactly as designed**; it is the *policy* built on top of it — "mint above the mark" — that has no fixed point when the mark is a function of everyone's mints.
- **Why the ×2 claim no longer holds.** ×2 closed `mint → push` and asserted the remaining window was minutes. True with a handful of branches. With sixteen branches and a jammed queue the window is *unbounded*, because a branch that cannot merge never stops being a claimant. B779's own "Rejected (with reasons)" list is now due a re-read: the objection to session-tagged ids was migration cost, weighed against "a rare, cheap, now-automated reconcile" — tonight that reconcile was neither rare nor cheap, and it did not converge.
- **DO NOT fix by weakening the gate.** The gate is catching a real property; a duplicate `V9000` genuinely existed tonight. The defect is in the allocation policy, not the check.
- **Owner has already approved the direction:** reserved B#/V# blocks per session, allocated up front, with the mint gate kept as the backstop — and asked for it to be steel-manned against regressions (block exhaustion mid-session, holes from abandoned sessions, a racing allocator handing out the same block, migration for the ~16 live branches, and whether id ordering is depended on anywhere). That dispatch is owed by another session; this item exists so the *diagnosis* is not un-owned (CLAUDE.md: a diagnosis reaching the repo without a B# is itself a protocol violation).
- Verify: **live** — this is a concurrency/multi-writer class by definition. It is confirmed fixed only when several concurrent sessions mint, push and merge without a renumber pass.

### B50009 — The native double-click fallback is dead for every feature: the first press re-renders the node, so the event retargets to the bare `<svg>` `[Site Planner / UI]` (bug) #site-planner #selection #ui  *(filed 2026-08-06 from the owner chat block as NEW-2; minted with B50008. DEDUPE-FIRST — same sweep as B50008 plus `onElDouble`, `onMarkupDouble`, `dblclick`, `retarget`, `common ancestor`: nothing in Open / ⏳ Verify / Done had ever looked at the native path's TARGET. Net-new.)*
`[ ]` **⏳ SHIPPED 2026-08-06. Parked in ⏳ Verify — `V17005`.**
- Verify: **live** — `V17005` · `Blocker: real-data`
- Origin: filed 2026-08-06 from chat (NEW-2)
- **MEASURED on his machine, ONE double-click on the easement:** `pointerdown#1 → polygon[easement hatch]` · `click#1 → polygon` · `pointerdown#2 → polygon` · `click#2 (detail:2) → svg` · `dblclick → svg`.
- **CAUSE:** a click's target is the **common ancestor of its down and up targets**. The first press selects the feature, React re-renders it, the node the browser was holding is gone, so the event collapses to the root `<svg>`. The `onDoubleClick` handlers on the easement/line/polyline `<g>` and on the three element groups were **UNREACHABLE in exactly the case they exist to cover**.
- **The source comments calling the native path "a fallback for when pointer capture doesn't suppress the native dblclick" were WRONG IN PRACTICE — corrected, at all four sites** (`onElDouble`, `onMarkupDouble`, the callout box, and the shared note). They are kept only for a harness dispatching a raw `dblclick` AT a node, where no point hit-test exists, and they now delegate to the same one action so they cannot drift.
- **CHOICE, and the other option was considered:** the gesture is resolved **AT THE `<svg>` ROOT by hit-testing the point**, not by keeping the hit node's identity stable across a selection re-render. Stabilising identity means promising that nothing in a feature's subtree remounts when it becomes selected — but selection is exactly when this canvas grows chrome (grips move to the handle layer, the dimension grab band appears, halos mount), so every future render change would silently re-break the gesture with nothing able to see it. The root is always there, and WHAT was double-clicked is answered by asking the browser what is under the point — **the same hit-test that decided the press targets**, so a second geometric hit-test can never disagree with it. `lib/featureTarget.js` is the pure half; every feature's outermost group now stamps `data-feature="<kind>:<id>"`.
- **ONE DECISION, NOT TWO.** The contract had two implementations and they had already drifted: `onElDouble` opened Properties for a LOCKED element while `startMoveEl` refused to, and nothing could notice because the native route was unreachable. Both routes now call `featureDoubleAction`, and the source guard checks **delegation** rather than an `openInspector()` at each call site — checking each site is what permitted the drift.
- **GUARD — the dblclick's own TARGET is asserted, not just that Properties opened**, so B50008's fix cannot mask this one: `e2e/dblclick-properties.spec.js` records every `pointerdown`/`click`/`dblclick` from a capture-phase listener and asserts a press that landed squarely on a feature was delivered as a click on the bare root. **WHICH event loses its target moves with machine speed** (his busy plan lost `click#2` and `dblclick`; an idle machine loses `click#1`), so the invariant is asserted rather than one trace — pinning a specific event would pin the machine, not the defect. A second case dispatches a `dblclick` whose own target IS the bare `<svg>`, with the reconstructed tap deliberately out of the picture, and asserts Properties opens: **proven RED with the root resolver removed.**
- Sandbox: `test/featureTarget.test.js` (26) · `e2e/dblclick-properties.spec.js` (4, all mutation-checked) · lint / suite / build green.

Containment now decides (`cityContainment: "in" | "none" | "unknown"`), the ring result is kept only as the "also touches" set, and `cityCentroid === null` now means UNKNOWN and nothing else (it previously ALSO meant "point query", which is why the ambiguity was invisible).

- **AMENDED 2026-08-08 with PORTFOLIO-WIDE evidence (B276752), not superseded.** This fix is correct and its Bain line still verifies live. What the 28-site sweep showed is that the CENTROID it reasons over belongs to `representativeRing` — the single largest parcel — so on the twelve assemblage sites the question was being asked of one lot. B276752 asks it of every active parcel and adds the `partial` state; the ordering rule and the `cityContainment` vocabulary this item introduced are unchanged and are what B276752 builds on. ### B208960 — Stitch: clicking a sheet row does nothing, silently, because a saved-set load holds a gate with no progress and no failure surface `[Doc Review / stitching]` (bug) #doc-review #stitching #ui  *(owner chat block 2026-08-06, provisional NEW-1. Minted **B208960 / V10608** LATE via `git fetch origin main && npm run next-id -- --against-main`, as the last step before push; the code, tests and commits keep the provisional `NEW-1` label. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open + ⏳ Verify + Done across `stitch`, `tray`, `addSheet`, `addGroup`, `loadStitch`, `silent`, `B51`, `B52`, `B536`, `B633`: **B51/B52** INTRODUCED the `loadingRef` gate this item is about and were right to (a load rebuilds `placed[]` wholesale); what is new is that the gate answered a user press with silence. **B536** fixed a group-drop that silently did nothing when one page failed to raster — same LOUD-FAILURE family, different call site, already shipped and untouched here. **B633** deduped placed sheets and is REUSED (moved earlier). Net-new.)*
`[ ]` **⏳ Shipped this session; V10608 PENDING.** Clicking a sheet row, or its plus button, did nothing at all — no sheet, no message, no console error, and a network trace showed zero requests, because the handler died before it could try.
- Verify: live
- Origin: filed 2026-08-06 from chat
- **AUDIT-FIRST, the cause, and it is one defect wearing two faces (this item and B208961).** `addSheet` and `addGroup` both opened with `if (loadingRef.current) return;` — a bare early return. `loadStitch` holds that gate for its whole run, and its whole run was: fetch every source PDF, then rasterise every placed sheet one at a time, committing NOTHING until the last one landed. On a real set that is minutes, over an empty canvas. So every click on every row in that window did nothing and said nothing. The gate itself is CORRECT — B51 added it because a load's blind `setPlaced` would clobber an added sheet — the defect was answering a user action with silence.
- **THE FIX — a press is never dropped on the floor.** A click during a load is QUEUED (`lib/stitchLoadState.js` `mergeAddQueue`, pure + unit-locked, dedupes a double-click to one) and REPLAYED against the fresh `pdfs[]` the moment the load lets go, and the user is told in the same beat (`deferredAddNotice`). A queued add whose file is no longer open is reported by name — never dropped quietly. Two more silent paths in the same handlers closed while here: a source with no `doc` now names itself instead of throwing an unhandled rejection past the handler, and a raster failure inside `addSheet` / `addGroup` is caught and SURFACED (LOUD-FAILURE — surfaced, not swallowed; the owner's "do not paper over it with a try/catch" is honoured by the fact that every catch here ends in a visible message, never a return). A drop of a non-PDF, previously an utter no-op, says so too.
- **AND the load got faster and visible while in there.** `dedupePlaced` moved BEFORE the raster loop — the owner's own JACINTOPORT draft is 14 entries / 8 unique (B633), so six full D-size sheets were being rastered purely to be discarded. Sheets now commit INCREMENTALLY, so the set builds up in front of you instead of appearing at the end. A source that won't download and a page that won't raster are each named rather than folded into one vague line.
- **Guards.** Unit: `test/stitchLoadState.test.js` (15). e2e: **stitch-row-adds-a-sheet** — the assertion is the owner's, verbatim: *click the sheet row → a sheet is actually visible on the canvas*, checked as a rendered `<image>` with a real blob raster behind it and a non-zero box, plus the app's own "Placed sheets · N" tally agreeing. A second row adds a second sheet. A press that cannot run right now produces a sheet OR a word, never neither. Located structurally (not by a testid this branch added) so it is mutation-checkable against the old build.
- **⚠ WHAT THE SANDBOX CANNOT SHOW, stated plainly.** The owner's trigger is a SAVED stitch being re-fetched from Drive, which needs a signed-in account — logged out, a fresh drop takes the fast path and the gate is never held, which is exactly why the headless suite passes on the OLD build for this one assertion. The queue/replay behaviour is proven by unit test and by reading the code; the LIVE confirmation is V10608.

- Origin: filed 2026-08-06 from chat
- **Cause.** The bar rendered `{err || "Rendering…"}` off a bare `busy` boolean. One string, no phase, no count, no name — so it could not move, and it could not distinguish "working" from "wedged". Because `loadStitch` committed nothing until the end (B208960), the canvas behind it was empty for the same window, which is what made it read as a hang.
- **THE FIX.** One honest status model: `prog = { phase, done, total, name }` and `loadStatusLine` (pure, unit-locked) — "Fetching saved drawings 2 of 3… (E2E SET.pdf)", "Drawing the saved set — sheet 4 of 8…", "Adding A227…". It counts, so a long job visibly moves; and it is ABSENT when nothing is happening, so it can never outlive the work it names. The bar carries `data-phase` for assertion.
- **Guards.** Unit: `test/stitchLoadState.test.js` — including the old bug in one assertion (the line at done=0 and done=3 must DIFFER). e2e: **stitch-row-adds-a-sheet** asserts the bar settles to gone/idle/error after a real add and that the literal string "Rendering…" is nowhere on the page. It stays in the **document model** — paragraphs, not a canvas — which is what keeps export, print, search and sync working with no new plumbing.
- **Single click and double click do the SAME thing.** The owner does not think of them as two gestures, and a page where one works and the other does not reads as intermittent, which is worse than neither working.
- **⛔ NOTHING IS LEFT BEHIND.** Paragraphs made this way are a CLAIM, not a commitment: typing releases it (they are the user's), and clicking away, blurring, moving the caret out, or leaving the page removes them. Word does the same, and without it every stray press would fatten the document forever. Asserted both ways — the orphan case AND the "a paragraph you typed into survives, including after a reload".
- **And a press ON text is still the browser's business**, so double-clicking a WORD still selects that word. Taking that away would be a worse bug than the one being fixed.

### B1427 — A re-fetchable cache was crowding the owner's saved work out of a 5 MB store `[Site Planner / storage]` (bug) #persistence #gis #site-planner #perf  *(owner chat block 2026-08-06 as NEW-1, with a MEASURED census from his own Chrome — the first diagnosis of this crisis blamed IndexedDB and was refuted by the reading. Minted **B1427 / V707** via `git fetch origin main && npm run next-id -- --against-main`, LATE, as the last step before push. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open + ⏳ Verify + Done across `gisCache`, `localStorage`, `quota`, `QuotaExceeded`, `IndexedDB`, `B473`, `B474`, `B483`, `B1162`: **B473** shipped the data-safety cure (cloud authoritative + the amber banner) and is Done; **B474** moved the version ring and the RASTERS to IndexedDB and is still Open for the site-payload tail; **B1162** BOUNDED this cache and that work stands untouched. None of them owns WHICH TIER the cache lives in — B474's Stage B explicitly scoped itself to rasters, and B1162 bounded the cache against the wrong ceiling. Net-new, not a recurrence.)*
`[x]` **Shipped 2026-08-06. Parked in ⏳ Verify — `V707` (a plan the size of Bain saving on a device that previously threw is a signed-in, real-data check).**
- Verify: **live** — `V707` · `Blocker: real-data`
- Origin: filed 2026-08-06 from the owner chat block (NEW-1)
- **THE MECHANISM, measured rather than reasoned.** `navigator.storage.estimate()` + a key census on the owner's Personal (CyberPower) Chrome on planyr.io: **IndexedDB 35.9 MB against a 10,275.9 MB quota (0.3%, persisted: true)** · **localStorage 3.88 MB across 156 keys against the hard ~5 MB per-origin cap (~78%)**. Largest localStorage keys: `planarfit:sites:cloud:<uid>` 523 KB · `planarfit:sites:history:v1` 416 KB · then **three `planyr:giscache:v1:terrain:dem:L16` tiles at 400 / 283 / 280 KB**. The site save writes to localStorage (`storage.js` — `SITES_KEY`, `cloudKey(uid)`, `AUTOSAVE_KEY`); `gisCache.js` lived there too with `maxTotalBytes = 3 MB`, and its own comment already said the budget existed "to keep our namespace from starving site data". 3 MB of cache out of a ~5 MB ceiling leaves under 2 MB for every saved plan plus the cloud index plus the history mirror plus the autosave — so on a Bain-sized plan `setItem` throws `QuotaExceededError`, the device save fails, and the B473 banner fires **while disposable, re-fetchable terrain tiles keep their space**. A priority inversion, with the two stores the wrong way round: the disposable data in the 5 MB box at 78%, the 10 GB box at 0.3%.
- **CAVEAT, stated because it matters:** the census is from the PERSONAL machine. The banner appeared on whichever machine the owner was on, possibly the Work Office PC. The design flaw is machine-independent and this machine is at 78% of the same ceiling.
- **THE FIX IS STRUCTURAL, NOT TUNING — gisCache's persistent tier moved to IndexedDB.** `localDb.js`'s store is already the app's durable KV home, already persisted, and had ten gigabytes unused. The cache keeps its own budget and eviction there, and **the budget did NOT change: 512 KB per entry and 3 MB total are exactly B1162's numbers.** Bounding this cache was always right — it was bounded against the wrong ceiling. Nothing got bigger; it stopped competing.
- **Migration: the legacy namespace is PURGED, not migrated** (the entries are one fetch away, so copying them would only delay the space we are trying to free). The purge runs **at module scope**, not on first cache use — on a device already at the cap the very next SAVE must find the room, and nothing guarantees a GIS layer gets touched first.
- **WHAT IT COSTS, said plainly: IndexedDB is asynchronous.** A cold lookup (nothing in the in-memory L1 yet — i.e. just after a reload) can no longer answer synchronously, so `swr()` returns `cached: null` on a cold L1 miss and delivers the stored copy through the `fresh` promise instead: a few milliseconds later, and still **with no network request**. Every consumer already handled that path — it is the same path an empty cache takes, and `fetchCached`, `terrainLayers` and `vectorOverlay` all await `fresh`. Hydration additionally warms the newest few entries back into L1 (bounded by count AND bytes) so a reload still paints from cache almost at once. The **one** caller that read the store synchronously was the PDF/PNG export, whose terrain branch is sync by contract; `exportSheet.js` now warms the frame's tiles first (**PDF-PARITY** — a wide view whose tiles had cycled out of the 48-entry L1 would otherwise have exported without contours).
- **WITH NO IndexedDB** (private mode, old browser, the node test env) there is now **no persistent tier at all** — L1 still serves the session and a miss is a live fetch. Deliberate, and it is the new rule again: with one store left, that store belongs to the user's work.
- **The L1 in-memory tier is exactly as B1162 left it** (48 entries, LRU by read-touch).
- **⛔ THE SITE PAYLOAD WAS DELIBERATELY NOT MOVED**, per the owner. That is the tempting follow-on and it is a much larger migration touching the exact path B473 exists because of — a device save that fails loses work. It is **B474**'s existing open sub-item, now carrying the risk statement; it did not get a new number (DEDUPE-FIRST).
- **MEASURED RESULT (headless, real browser, `e2e/storage-tiers.spec.js`):** seeded with the owner's own three tiles at their measured sizes, localStorage cache bytes go **986,247 → 0** on load, total localStorage drops to 194 bytes, and the saved plan + the version ring are untouched. Mutation-checked: disabling the purge turns the spec red.
- Guards: the repo-root `test/` suite **gisCache** (23, rewritten for the async tier — incl. the disk-hit-with-no-fetch case, the refused-write case where the index must not claim what is not stored, and a direct assertion that the cache never writes to localStorage however much it caches) + **renderBudgetMemos** (the durable-tier answer, now through `readAsync`) + the e2e spec **storage-tiers**.

### B1428 — The "Retry device save" button could not succeed `[Site Planner / storage]` (bug) #persistence #ui #site-planner  *(owner chat block 2026-08-06 as NEW-2. Minted **B1428 / V708** via `--against-main`, LATE. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open + ⏳ Verify + Done across `saveNow`, `Retry device save`, `localSaveFailed`, `savedToCloudOnly`, `B473`, `B507`: **B473** BUILT this banner and its button and is Done; **B507** fixed a rejected cloud push stranding the transient banner. Neither owns the fact that the button's action was incapable of changing the condition it was offered for. Net-new.)*
`[x]` **Shipped 2026-08-06. Parked in ⏳ Verify — `V708` (a genuinely full device is the only place the success path can be seen).**
- Verify: **live** — `V708` · `Blocker: real-data`
- Origin: filed 2026-08-06 from the owner chat block (NEW-2)
- **THE DEFECT.** `SitePlanner.jsx` wired the amber banner's Retry button to `onClick={saveNow}`. `saveNow` re-ran the same write **with nothing freed in between**, so while the store was full it failed every single time — an action offered for a condition it could not affect.
- **THE FIX.** `retryDeviceSave` now (1) frees the provably re-fetchable tier — oldest-first — (2) retries the identical verified write, and (3) reports **what it freed AND whether the save landed**, naming three distinct outcomes rather than one: `saved` ("cleared N of map data to make room"), `still-full` ("cleared N, but this plan still won't fit on this device — your work is safe in your account"), and `nothing-to-free`. The still-full case is the one the old button could not distinguish from "try again", and it is the one the owner most needs told. The decision layer is pure (`shared/storage/storageReclaim.js` — `reclaimThenRetry`), so all four outcomes are unit-tested with no DOM.
- **The explicit `Save now` does the same thing** before settling for the cloud-only story: one click should exhaust the safe options. The reclaim is awaited rather than raced against the cloud push, so the two can't contend over the banner state — it is a handful of `removeItem` calls plus an in-memory index clear, and it only runs when the device write has already failed.
- **⛔ THE HARD CONSTRAINT — no eviction may ever cost data that cannot be rebuilt.** Every reclaimable class must **declare a rehydration source** before anything is removed (`storageCensus.js`); a class that cannot name one for EVERY member is not reclaimable at any pressure, and the reclaim **refuses the whole pass** if any class claims to be reclaimable with no way back. B474 recorded the precedent — "a raster whose src had been dropped (idbKey set) was then unrecoverable" — so **reference images declare `rebuild: null` and are never bulk-cleared**: a raster with a `storageKey` has a cloud copy, one with only an `idbKey` is the user's ONLY copy, and the key alone cannot tell you which. Asserted directly in `test/storageReclaim.test.js` with exactly that record, under maximum pressure.
- Guards: the repo-root `test/` suite **storageReclaim** (24, incl. the four outcomes, oldest-first eviction, the limit-stop, the throwing-save case, and the two hard-constraint cases) + the e2e spec **storage-tiers**.

Audit green. The Notes route's 31.1 KB of above-baseline growth predates this change entirely and is untouched by it — someone should ratchet that metric deliberately, with the item that caused it.

Net effect: `sampleEbfePoint` had returned a permanent, silent `{null, null}` since B882 — read downstream as "outside InFRM coverage", everywhere, forever.
- **Live-proven end to end** (through the app's own same-origin proxy, 2026-08-05): Tsakiris tract 1% **154.8 ft** / 0.2% **156.0 ft**; north Waller 206.5 / 207.8; downtown Houston **NoData** — which is CORRECT and is now its own fixture, because Houston is studied and BLE deliberately maps only the unstudied gaps.

A new `nostore=1` proxy mode passes a point JSON read through without entering the Drive imagery cache, and **fails LOUD with a 502 instead of the imagery path's 302** — a redirect would send the browser straight back into the CORS wall the relay exists to avoid.
- **`hcfcdMaapnext` IS genuinely down, and the registry now says so instead of implying otherwise.** Its WSE endpoints were recovered from HCFCD's own ArcGIS-Online item catalog (they had been `null` placeholders since B882, so the sampler was a no-op by construction) — but the whole `fximgservices.hcfcd.org` host hangs ~20 s and is refused, **server-side from Cloudflare as well as in a browser**, while `www.hcfcd.org` answers in 1.3 s. - **So `availability` is a new registry axis, ORTHOGONAL to `tier`.** `tier` answers "is this the authoritative agency's production endpoint" (a design fact); `availability` answers "does it ANSWER" (an operational fact). Conflating them is exactly how a row sat at `production` with a fresh `lastVerified` while failing in its own home county. A `down`/`degraded` row **requires** a complete `outage` record — `{since, symptom, evidence, impact, replacement}` — and the sampler now **throws a named outage** instead of returning the null that read as "no coverage here". On the owner's core county those are opposite facts, and MAAPnext usually runs HIGHER than the effective FIRM, so the estimate a Harris site DOES get is likely low. That sentence is in `outage.impact`, and the drainage check renders it as a named `unavailable` state.
- **The verifier INVERTS for a declared outage**, which is what keeps this honest without keeping CI permanently red: a `down` row is asserted to be STILL down, and a row that starts answering again is reported as a **PROBLEM** — "recovered, flip it back to live". That is the one message worth having on the day it returns.
- **THE ROOT CAUSE OF THE SILENCE: twelve rows carried NO coverage fixture at all.** A fixture-less row gives the verifier nothing to assert, so it can never go red — which is precisely why both flood rows rotted for weeks behind a green weekly check. `auditRegistry` now FAILS a fixture-less row, and every one of the twelve has a live-measured fixture. Where the obvious point returns 0 the fixture records WHY: an ETJ is the ring OUTSIDE the city limits (downtown Austin measured 0), and the BKDD master-plan study area is **55 miles south** of where its own comment claimed — its published extent reprojects to 28.96°N, −95.93°, which is why the "TODO: bake an in-extent fixture" had never been done.

### B1423 — The Layers panel and the map chrome were fighting, and the chrome was winning `[Site Planner / UI]` (bug) #site-planner #ui #gis  *(owner report 2026-08-04 on the Goose Creek plan. Arrived as provisional NEW-3. Minted **B1423** via `--against-main`, LATE. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open + ⏳ Verify + Done across `zIndex`, `stacking`, `panel`, `overlap`, `scale bar`, `B1205`, `B1206`, `B837`, `B838`, `B734`: **B1205/B1206** own the MAP-LAYER stacking model (which pane a GIS layer paints into) — a different axis entirely; **B734** is the anchored-menu clamp; **B837/B838** are pan compensation. No item covers panel-vs-map-chrome. Net-new.)*
`[x]` **Shipped 2026-08-05 and VERIFIED HERE — headless, on the real render, mutation-checked both ways. `Verify: sandbox`.**
- Verify: sandbox — `e2e/layers-panel-legibility.spec.js` (4 specs), each proven RED on the pre-fix behaviour
- Origin: filed 2026-08-05 from the owner chat block (NEW-3)
- **The cause was not one bad number, it was the absence of a shared one.** Every floating thing over a map picked its own z-index at its own call site, months apart: the planner's Layers + View column **6**, the canvas furniture (north arrow, scale bar) **7**, the zoom stack **6 but later in the DOM**, and the map finder's panels **1000** — tying with Leaflet's own control containers, which are 1000 and later in the DOM. **A tie is resolved by document order**, which is why it read as random. `lib/mapChromeStack.js` is now the one model: passive furniture → map controls → **an open panel wins**, because a panel is the thing being read and operated and there is no case where a scale bar covering a slider is the right outcome. The View popover beside it is fixed by the same change rather than separately.
- **The panel is taller and wider, from the room that actually exists.** The height was a flat `62vh` (planner) and a flat `260px` (finder) — the owner saw about four rows of a twenty-eight layer list. Both are now derived from the space between the panel's top edge and the bottom furniture, and **group headers stick** so you can still tell which group you are in after scrolling. Measured after: **17 rows visible without scrolling**.
- **`minWidth: 0` is load-bearing, not tidiness.** A flex item will not shrink below its min-content width, so the row label refused to narrow, wrapped onto a second line, and pushed the agency chip past the panel's `overflow: hidden` edge — which is exactly why "FEMA flood zones" was on two lines with its chip clipped to "FEM". Every row is one line at any panel width now, with the full text on hover.
- **⛔ THE SPEC TOOK THREE ATTEMPTS TO BE HONEST, and that is worth recording.** v1 walked a grid and asked `elementFromPoint` who was on top — it **passed with the fix deliberately reverted**, because `elementFromPoint` honours `pointer-events: none` and the scale bar is exactly that: it never intercepts a click, it just paints over the panel. A hit-test is structurally blind to this bug. v2 asserted the rectangles must not intersect at all — too strict, and wrong: the panel now spans most of the map's height, so the scale bar sits inside its rectangle by construction. Overlap is not the defect; being painted OVER is. **v3** finds the chrome that paints AND overlaps, forces `pointer-events: auto` on each so the hit-test can see it, and asks who is on top at the shared pixels — isolating PAINT ORDER from pointer policy. Reverted, it fails and names the culprits: the scale-bar SVG and the `gbtn` zoom buttons.
- The sticky-header spec had the same problem in miniature (it passed with the rule removed, because a panel tall enough not to scroll leaves the header where it was) and now **proves the list actually scrolled** before asserting stickiness. A guard that cannot distinguish "sticky" from "nothing moved" is not a guard.

### B1425 — A reload lost the project, and a hash edit left the old project on screen under the new URL `[Site Planner / routing]` (bug) #site-planner #ui #auth  *(owner report 2026-08-04, two repros on production. Arrived as provisional NEW-5. Minted **B1425 / V706** via `--against-main`, LATE. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open + ⏳ Verify + Done across `route`, `deep link`, `bootResolved`, `mayReconcileUrl`, `V13`, `V28`, `B1419`, `B482`: **V13/V28** shipped `mayReconcileUrl`, the gate this defeats — and this is NOT a recurrence of it, because that gate works exactly as specified; the defect is that it gates on an EVENT having fired rather than on the DATA being known, which is a different property. Net-new.)*
`[x]` **Shipped 2026-08-05. Parked in ⏳ Verify — `V706` (both repros are signed-in-only; logged out they do not reproduce, which is itself the diagnosis).**
- Verify: **live** — `V706` · `Blocker: auth` + `real-data`
- Origin: filed 2026-08-05 from the owner chat block (NEW-5)
- **Repro A's mechanism, found by reading and then locked as a pure decision.** supabase-js emits `INITIAL_SESSION` with a **NULL user** while it is still restoring a stored session. `applyUser(null, …)` runs to completion and releases `bootResolved` — so the URL sync fires with the cloud sites still absent, `effGroup` is null, and that null is written straight over `#/project/<id>/site`. The deep link is gone before the real `SIGNED_IN` arrives, and the resume it would have driven now reads a route with no project in it. Worse: if the order is `INITIAL_SESSION(null)` → `TOKEN_REFRESHED(user)`, the handler ignores `TOKEN_REFRESHED` entirely, so the resume never runs at all.
- **Chasing the auth timing would close one sequence at a time, so the WRITER is honest instead.** `mayWriteRouteProject` refuses to clear a route-named project unless the user **deliberately left it**, and that intent cannot be inferred from state — "the project's data hasn't loaded" and "the user closed the project" both look like `effGroup === null`, and treating the first as the second IS the bug. Every deliberate exit (the Map crumb, Back to map, a sign-out, a discarded staging site) goes through one `leaveProject` / `goMap` seam that records it.
- **Repro B was two faults compounding.** `openProjectGroup` returned **silently** when a group had no plans on this device, so a hash edited to a not-yet-pulled project left the PREVIOUS project rendered under a URL claiming the new one — and because the effect only depended on `projectId`, the cloud pull landing a moment later never re-ran it, so it never self-corrected either. `routeProjectAvailability` replaces the silent return with three real states — **open / waiting / missing** — the effect now also depends on the site list and on `bootResolved`, and a genuinely missing project gets a named banner instead of someone else's plan.
- **On the duplicate panel:** driven headless, the invariant that actually matters holds — exactly ONE planner surface and at most one VISIBLE Layers panel, before and after a switch, with no duplicated rows. Counting raw checkboxes cannot distinguish a leaked second planner from the hidden keep-alive copy that is there **by design** (the inactive mode stays mounted so its Leaflet map is not rebuilt), which is why the original "64 vs 29" was hard to act on. `e2e/route-project-binding.spec.js` (4) asserts the real property, including that the fix did not make the URL un-leavable.

### B1420 — Collapse the Notes hierarchy: THE PROJECT IS THE NOTEBOOK, and a page can hold pages `[Notes / model · UI]` (feature) #notes #ui #persistence #sync  *(owner decision, 2026-08-05 chat block, verbatim: *"so i dont need a project to have multiple notebooks i dont think, like grand port being its own notebook is great as long as i can have subpages there."* — plus a mid-session AMENDMENT on a zoomed screenshot of the TOP of the rail: *"are we fixing this part too?"*, naming the primary-filled New-notebook button, the "Notebooks / Recent / Bin 2" tabs, and the stack of chrome above the tree.
