DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open + ⏳ Verify + Done across `notebook`, `section`, `notesModel`, `notesTree`, `subpage`, `nest`, `B1310`, `B1312`, `B1316`, `B1365`, `B1366`, `B1367`, `B1374`, `B1391`, `B1400`: **B1374** built the notebook→project binding this replaces, **B1316** wired the three move ops that become one, **B1365/B1367** cleaned the rail's rows, **B1310** built the bin. Every one of those fixed what it set out to fix and every one of their guarantees is CARRIED FORWARD here — none is re-opened as a recurrence. This is net-new because it changes the MODEL, not any of their behaviours.)*
`[x]` **Shipped 2026-08-05. Parked in ⏳ Verify — `V702` (the migration must be seen against the owner's REAL signed-in data, and the cloud round trip is auth-blocked here).**
- Verify: **live** — `V702` · `Blocker: auth` + `real-data`
- Origin: filed 2026-08-05 from the owner chat block + its amendment
- **THE MODEL, in one sentence: two concepts, a PROJECT and PAGES THAT CAN HOLD SUBPAGES.** There is no notebook layer to pick and no separate species called a "section" — "Entitlements" stops being a different KIND of thing and becomes simply a page that has pages under it. **Anything can have children, at any depth.** That is precisely what OneNote structurally cannot do (its sections and pages are different types and a page cannot nest under a page), so the distinction is not allowed back by the back door: no `kind` field, no depth ceiling, no "container" flag. `addNotebook` / `addSection` / `moveSection` / `moveNotebook` / `setNotebookProject` / `visibleNotebooks` / `notebooksInScope` / `notebookToMarkdown` are all **deleted**.
- **`projectId` LIVES ON THE ROOT PAGE AND NOWHERE ELSE.** A subpage's project is its root's, DERIVED (`projectOfPage`), never stored. Storing it per node would make one fact writable in N places — the redundancy that cost the Site Planner eight PRs to remove (B1340). `movePage` strips it on nest and restores it on lift, so the invariant is maintained by the one op rather than by discipline.
- **⛔ MIGRATION WAS THE RISK, AND IT IS PROVEN ON HIS OWN DATA.** Every SECTION becomes a top-level page **keeping its own id** (which is what lets a binned page whose `parentId` names its old section restore to exactly the right place); its pages become that page's subpages; **two notebooks bound to the same project MERGE by construction**, because `projectId` is the only grouping key there is — so no id can collide and nothing needs reconciling. A generic "Section 1" does not survive as a page name: a single-section notebook lends its own title instead, and where both titles are noise and there is one page, that page becomes the top level (`Untitled notebook › Section 1 › Load Study` → **`Load Study`**). A loose notebook lands in the named **"Not in a project"** home, same shape. The **bin comes with it**: a binned notebook or section converts to one page carrying its former contents, so a restore returns the branch whole, and every `pageIds` cascade set is copied verbatim.
- **It is IDEMPOTENT and it is PERSISTED.** The conversion only runs on a tree that has `notebooks` and no `pages`, so `migrate(migrate(x)) === migrate(x)` for every input — asserted by deep equality on the owner's data, three times over, and through a JSON round trip (which IS the sync path). It is also **written back on the first load that sees the old shape**, so the new shape rides the cloud tree blob to the other machine instead of being re-derived forever. **No schema change and no SQL — nothing lands on the owner.**
- **WHAT THE RAIL LOOKS LIKE NOW.** Inside a project: only that project's pages, nested, and **no project badge on any row** — everything on screen belongs to where you are standing, so a badge has nothing to say. From the Dashboard: **grouped by project name**, with a "Not in a project" group last, and that heading is the ONE place a project label belongs. A project id that no longer resolves still gets its own flagged group rather than being folded away.
- **⛔ B1374'S GUARANTEE IS UNCHANGED, by a different route.** Its in-rail scope switch is gone as duplicate chrome, because the DASHBOARD is now the all-projects view and its crumb sits at the top of every screen. The empty-rail state still offers that exact click explicitly ("See all your notes"), and — a defect caught by the harness — that button now **stays in Notes**: it was wired to the shell's Dashboard action, which switches to the Site workspace, i.e. it answered "where are my other notes?" by leaving the notes module.
- **THE AMENDMENT — the whole header block, not just the tree.** `＋ New notebook` was a **full-width primary-filled button for a concept that no longer exists**, and the loudest element in the panel for one of the rarest actions; it is now a quiet secondary **`＋ Page`** sharing the search field's row. The tabs read **Pages · Recent · Bin** — "Notebooks" stopped being true, and the **permanent Bin count is gone** (it lives inside the Bin view, where it answers a question you actually asked). The **scope switch** went with the Dashboard change. **Four rows of chrome became two.** The per-row **timestamp column** is gone as well — Recent already exists and is where recency is the point; it survives as the row's hover title, which costs the default view nothing.
- **AND THE TREE OPENS THE PATH TO THE PAGE YOU ARE ON**, leaving every other branch collapsed. It only ever ADDS to the open set: a branch you opened by hand stays open, because a rail that closes what you just opened is arguing with its reader.
- **PANEL-BREVITY — the WHOLE rail, header block included, measured on his own reported data (printed by the harness on every run).** Inside a project: **30 visible lines → 13 · 254 characters → 86 · 12 tree rows → 6** (for the same six pages). From the Dashboard: **38 → 16 lines · 335 → 128 characters · 15 → 7 rows**, while carrying MORE information than before (the project groupings). **What was removed, named:** the full-width New-notebook button · the two-segment scope switch · the Bin tab's count · the per-row timestamp · every per-row project badge · and, from the tree itself, the notebook and section rows that were containers for containers. Nothing that was removed took a FACT with it — every one is either reachable in one click (the Dashboard), on a hover (the time), or on the row's own menu. `node ui-audit/panel-copy-budget.mjs --check` green.
- **Kept working, and each one is driven headless rather than assumed:** creating a page inside a project files it there automatically · subpages created and re-parented by direct action (the row menu's **New subpage**, the Move panel, and **drag-to-nest**, with drag onto a project's heading as the way back out) · rename stays INLINE · delete bins for 30 days with the full **subtree** cascade and restores it whole · **no dialog boxes anywhere** · the sketch node, pictures, cloud sync, search, print and Markdown export all work against the new shape.
- **Markdown export is nesting as HEADING DEPTH, and lossless for content.** `pageToMarkdown` writes a top-level page as `#`, its subpages `##`, and so on. Markdown runs out at six levels and a note tree does not — past that the heading clamps and the page's place is carried by a **trail line**, which the exporter REPORTS as the one thing it could not spell. Not a page, title or byte of body is ever dropped.
- **PDF-PARITY.** There is no section heading to print any more, so paper carries each page's **trail** — the same "where does this sit?" the rail shows by indentation, which is what keeps a printed branch readable once the sheets are separated. Screen and paper were changed in the same commit.
- **A page may NEVER be moved into its own subtree.** That single move would detach a whole branch from the tree — every page under it still in the object graph and reachable from nowhere, which is the "renders in zero scopes" bug in its purest form. The model REFUSES it (returns the tree unchanged), the drop target does not light up for it, and both halves are asserted.
- Sandbox: `test/notesModel.test.js` **REWRITTEN** (80 cases — the old suite exercised the four-level ops and every one of its properties is re-asserted on the new shape rather than left passing against dead code) · `test/notesSync.test.js` merge + adoption fixtures rewritten (78) · `test/notesRoundTwo.test.js`, `test/notesMarkdown.test.js`, `test/notesModule.test.js` updated in place · full suite **7,975 passed** · lint 0 errors · `MAP.md` regenerated · doc-pointer audit + panel-copy budget + backlog index + mint gate green · build green.
- Headless, on the REAL build, logged out: **`ui-audit/verify-notes.mjs` — 244/244**, extended IN PLACE with a new **§25** that seeds the owner's four reported notebooks in the OLD shape with real bodies, boots the app onto them, and demands: every page survives · every body survives byte for byte · the two same-project notebooks merged with no id collision · "Section 1" did not survive as a name · sections' pages became subpages · **every migrated page is in exactly one project's rail** · a second boot is **byte-identical** (idempotent) · a migrated page opens with its words · drag-to-nest, drag-back-out and the refused self-nest · the subtree delete, its count on the confirmation, and the restore that brings the branch back whole · and the rail's before/after measurement. The old notebook/section structural checks were REPLACED, not left green.
- **What `V702` still covers:** the owner's REAL signed-in tree migrating on planyr.io (his ids, his bodies, his pictures and his 30-day bin), and the converted shape reaching his SECOND machine through cloud sync. `Blocker: auth` + `real-data`.

### B482 (×2) — A signed-in user's PROJECT LIST is empty on any route that never mounts the Site Planner, and every project name in that session is wrong `[Cross-module / projects]` (bug) #ui #sync #auth #notes  *(owner chat block 2026-08-04, provisional NEW-1, observed live on planyr.io signed in as the owner: the project picker read "No projects yet — start one below" while notebooks in the SAME rail were visibly bound to projects — and the OFFICE machine and the HOME machine gave different answers on the same account. **Filed as a RECURRENCE of B482, not a new number (DEDUPE-FIRST).** The symptom is byte-identical to the one B482 exists to end — "the project switcher shows 'No projects yet' though the projects exist" — and B475/B482's own fixes (warm the cache; warm again when the switcher OPENS, because auth has not settled at mount) both still hold and are both still load-bearing. What neither of them could see is one layer below: the warm they call is a **no-op by construction** on these routes. Searched Open + ⏳ Verify + Done across `listProjects`, `warmProjectsIfEmpty`, `loadSitesList`, `setActiveUser`, `activeUid`, `isCloudActive`, `cold tab`, `B191`, `B439`, `B475`, `B482`, `B1415`.)*
`[x]` **Shipped 2026-08-04. Parked in ⏳ Verify — `V701` (the whole failure is signed-in-only: the warm never runs logged out, so the sandbox cannot reach it).**
- Verify: **live** — `V701` · `Blocker: auth` + `real-data`
- Origin: filed 2026-08-04 from the owner chat block (NEW-1)
- Recurrence: 2026-08-04 — "the project picker says *No projects yet — start one below* while notebooks in the same rail are bound to projects; on the office machine a couple of badges resolve and the rest do not; on the home machine none of them do." Same account, two machines, two answers.
- **ROOT CAUSE, instrumented rather than guessed — and the two-machine split is what proves it.** `setActiveUser(uid)` is what switches the shared project store from the logged-OUT legacy cache (`planarfit:sites:v1`) to the signed-in user's own (`planarfit:sites:cloud:<uid>`). It was called from **exactly one place in the app**: `SitePlannerApp`'s auth effect. `SitePlannerApp` is a lazily-mounted workspace, and the Shell only mounts a workspace you have actually visited. **"Open where I left off" (`seedBootRoute`) now routinely boots straight into `#/notes`** — so on those boots the Site Planner never mounts, `setActiveUser` never runs, and the store stays bound to nobody for the entire session. Everything downstream then behaves *correctly* on the wrong data: `isCloudActive()` is false → `warmProjectsIfEmpty()` returns instantly having done nothing (B475/B482's fix, correctly declining to pull for a signed-out user) → `loadSitesList()` reads the **legacy logged-out store**. That is the whole two-machine mystery: the office machine has a few pre-cloud legacy sites on disk (so a couple of names resolve, including the street-address one), the home machine has none (so nothing resolves). Same account, same code, different leftover on disk.
- **THE FIX — the binding moved UP to the one component that always mounts.** `Shell.jsx` owns auth already; it now calls `setActiveUser` in its `onAuthChange` subscription, so the store is bound to the account on **every** route, whether or not the Site Planner is ever opened. `SitePlannerApp` still makes the same call and still runs its own pull — the call is idempotent (it early-outs when the value is unchanged) and the planner's same-user re-emit guard is keyed on its own ref, so nothing there changes behaviour.
- **AND THE WARM STOPPED LYING ABOUT WHAT IT DID (LOUD-FAILURE).** `warmProjectsIfEmpty` returned a bare boolean, and `false` meant four different things — logged out · already warm · no uid · **the pull actually failed**. A caller could not tell "nothing to do" from "the cloud refused", so every caller treated a real failure as a no-op. The new `warmProjects()` returns `{ ok, warmed, reason, error }`; `warmProjectsIfEmpty()` is kept as a thin wrapper so the two existing callers' contract is unchanged.
- **A warm that lands now REACHES the other surfaces.** A same-tab `localStorage` write fires no native `storage` event, so a pull that completed inside the header switcher was invisible to every other reader. `notifyProjectsChanged()` / `onProjectsChanged()` broadcast it — deliberately reusing the SAME synthetic `storage` event the breadcrumb already dispatches after a rename, so the existing listeners pick it up with no second mechanism beside them.
- Sandbox: `test/notesModule.test.js` +5 (mutation-checked: reverting the Shell call, the header prop or the badge each turns one red) · full suite **7,957 passed** · lint 0 errors · `MAP.md` regenerated · doc-pointer audit + panel-copy budget green · build green.
- **What `V701` covers:** signed in on planyr.io, on a machine that has NOT opened the Site Planner this session — boot straight to `#/notes` and confirm the picker lists the real projects and every badge resolves. Both machines, because the two-machine divergence is the signature.

**THE ORIGINAL ITEM, moved here from `BACKLOG-DONE.md` with the recurrence (the block is MOVED, never copied — a live↔archive duplicate is what `test/idUniqueness.test.js` fails the build on):**

*B482 — Cold Review tab: project switcher shows "No projects yet" though the projects exist `[Doc Review / shared header]` (bug) — Cowork signed-in verification 2026-06-26, "NEW-2"; the B475/V140 cold-cache fix resurfacing on the direct-to-Review path.*
- **DONE + verified 2026-06-26** (branch `claude/exciting-wright-yb6ruz`). lint 0 · 1597 tests · build green; signed-in cold-tab re-confirm → V146 (the warm only fires signed in).
- **Repro (Cowork, signed-in):** open a fresh tab straight into Review (`/project/<id>/markup`) without opening the Site Planner first → the project "▾" switcher shows "No projects yet — start one below" though localStorage holds all projects (26 known). A *warm* load (Site opened first) lists them — so it's cold-vs-warm, not the lock.
- **ROOT CAUSE (2026-06-26):** `ProjectBreadcrumb` (uncontrolled) called B475's `warmProjectsIfEmpty()` **only once on mount** — but on a cold tab `isCloudActive()` is usually still false at mount (auth hasn't resolved), so the warm no-opped, and it **never retried**. Opening the switcher only re-read the still-empty cache.
- **FIX (2026-06-26, and it still holds):** warm the cache when the switcher **opens** too (auth is settled by then), not just on mount, via a shared `warmThenRefresh()`; a `warming` flag shows "Loading projects…" instead of the misleading "No projects yet" while the one-time cloud pull is in flight. ⚠ **This is exactly the fix the 2026-08-04 recurrence proves was necessary but not sufficient:** it makes the warm run at the right MOMENT, and the recurrence is that on a route which never mounts the Site Planner the warm has nothing to run AS — `isCloudActive()` is false all session, so warming at open, at mount, or a hundred times over would all no-op identically.

### B1419 — The Notes rail captioned a FAILED LOOKUP as if it were the owner's data `[Notes / UI]` (bug) #notes #ui  *(owner chat block 2026-08-04, provisional NEW-1, second half: *"'OTHER PROJECT' is the degraded label meaning 'bound to a project whose name I cannot resolve' — so the badge is not describing his data, it is describing a failed lookup."* Minted **B1419 / V701** via `git fetch origin main && npm run next-id -- --against-main`, LATE, as the last step before push; code and tests keep the provisional `NEW-1` label. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open + ⏳ Verify + Done across `Other project`, `badge`, `projectNameOf`, `notebooksInScope`, `B1374`, `B475`, `B482`, `B1343`: **B1374** shipped the badge and is the item this corrects — but it is deliberately NOT filed as a B1374 recurrence, because B1374's guarantee (a notebook belongs to a project, the row says where, nothing is unreachable) still holds completely and its tests pass unchanged. The defect is that its FALLBACK caption did not distinguish a missing project from an unloaded list. Net-new.)*
`[x]` **Shipped 2026-08-04. Parked in ⏳ Verify — `V701` (the failure banner can only be raised by a pull that FAILS, which needs a signed-in session).**
- Verify: **live** — `V701` · `Blocker: auth`
- Origin: filed 2026-08-04 from the owner chat block (NEW-1)
- **THE DEFECT.** `projectNameOf(id) || "Other project"` printed the same three words whether the project genuinely belongs to another scope, has been deleted, or the project list simply never arrived (B482 ×2 above, which made the last case the common one). Every row wore it at once, and the owner read it as a statement about his notebooks. It was a statement about our own ignorance.
- **THE FIX — the words now differ by REASON, and a real failure is loud.** The rail is handed the project list's STATE, not just its contents: `Loading…` while a warm is in flight · `Not loaded` when the pull failed · `Missing project` when the list is fine and this id genuinely is not in it · the project's own name otherwise · and still nothing at all when the answer is simply the project you are already standing in (repeating the header on every row is noise — PANEL-BREVITY). The `failed` case additionally raises a one-line `role="alert"` strip above the tree with a **Retry**, which re-runs the warm. The in-flight case gets no strip: the rows already say it, and saying it twice is the accumulation PANEL-BREVITY forbids.
- **PANEL-BREVITY:** the default view is UNCHANGED — every new line renders only in a failure state. Healthy rail, before and after: **1 row per notebook / section / page, badge text 5 chars ("Loose") or the project name**; the alert strip is 0 lines when the list is fine and 1 line when it is not. `node ui-audit/panel-copy-budget.mjs --check` green.
- **A duplicate row found by the headless check and fixed in the same commit:** the "Belongs to…" panel's two fallbacks (*this project is not in the list* and *this binding is unresolved*) both fired on an unresolved CURRENT project, emitting two buttons with the same id — a duplicate React key, and one of them naming a raw project id at the user.
- Sandbox: `ui-audit/verify-notes.mjs` §24 (new, 8 checks) — **218/218 PASSED** headless on the real build, driving the owner's own move; the pre-existing §22 assertion that ACCEPTED "other project" was rewritten rather than left passing against dead words.
- **What `V701` covers:** signed in, with the cloud unreachable, confirm the rail says the projects did not load and that **Retry** recovers it.
- **Recurrence: 2026-08-05 (×2) — the SAME class of quiet lie, one layer up.** A rail group header read **"PROJECT NOT LOADED"** on the live build, on the group holding Entitlements and DEV COORDINATION — pages whose old notebook pointed at a project that no longer exists. That phrasing describes an INTERNAL LOADING STATE, not his data, which is exactly what "OTHER PROJECT" did and exactly what this item exists to end. Handled on this id rather than a new number (DEDUPE-FIRST). **Three genuinely different situations were being told with one sentence, and each now gets its own:** a page never filed anywhere → **"Not in a project"** · a project that was DELETED (the list is fine; this id is not in it) → **"From a project you deleted"** · the project LIST itself failing → **"Project names didn't load"**. The middle one is the owner's actual case and the only one he can act on — those pages are re-filed from the row's own menu — so it says so in his language. The decision is a named pure function (`groupHeading`) rather than inline guesswork, and the unit guard now forbids the old wording outright.

### B1414 — The right rail's Parcel flyout carried three of the eleven parcel actions, and "Parcel" named two different things on opposite sides of the screen `[Site Planner / parcel · UI]` (feature) #site-planner #ui #selection  *(owner chat block 2026-08-04, provisional NEW-1, verbatim: "also all the parcel tool should also be on the right hand menu", with the rail inspected and the gap enumerated in the dispatch. Minted **B1414 / V697** via `git fetch origin main && npm run next-id -- --against-main`, LATE, as the last step before push — **renumbered once from a provisional B1406/V691 that `npm run check-mint` caught as claimed by a concurrent branch while this session was working**; code, tests and commits keep the provisional `NEW-1` label. Branch `claude/parcel-tool-right-menu-d6pacs`. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open + ⏳ Verify + Done across `parcel tool`, `rail`, `flyout`, `menu`, `discoverab`, `B416`, `B570`, `B598`, `B720`, `B721`, `B1093`: **B570** folded the Deed / Title tool INTO this group and renamed it "Boundary" → "Parcel" (and is the item whose rename created the collision); **B598** gave the Parcel TOOL its Draw/Remove banner and its Done exit; **B416** surfaced Split in the LEFT panel; **B720** built the left panel's Add ▾ · Split · Merge ops row and click-to-pick merge. Every one of them made ONE surface better and each is still load-bearing — none of them ever asked whether the rail was COMPLETE, and none touched the two-sided naming. Net-new, and deliberately not a recurrence of any of them: their fixes all still hold and are all still reachable.)*
`[x]` **Shipped 2026-08-04. Parked in ⏳ Verify — `V697` (the two GIS-backed create rows need a live county endpoint; everything else was driven headless here and PASSED).**
- Verify: **live** — `V697`
- Origin: filed 2026-08-04 from the owner chat block (NEW-1)
- **THE COUNT WAS THREE OF ELEVEN-PLUS.** The flyout offered Draw / Deed / Split. **Remove** (`parcelMode === "remove"`, B598) had no entry point in the rail at all. **Combine** — a whole tool (`startMergePick` / `mergeParcels`, its own banner, its own Enter binding) — had none either. **Setbacks** lived in the LEFT rail, so the same noun was split across two opposite sides of the screen. And **boundary editing** — drag a corner, add one on an edge, Shift-click one off — existed ONLY as prose inside the Select tool's hint string, so a user who never hovered that tooltip never learned the app could reshape a boundary.
- **`lib/parcelActions.js` IS THE INVENTORY, AND THAT IS THE POINT.** The menu is now built from a pure model — every action, the group the work happens in, what gates it, and what it says when it is disabled — so *"does every parcel action have a menu path?"* is a PROPERTY a test asserts rather than something a reviewer notices. `SitePlanner.jsx` maps a row id to the existing handler and renders; it decides nothing. `test/parcelActions.test.js` fails if an inventory entry has no row, or a row has no handler at the render site — which is exactly the drift that produced a three-of-eleven menu in the first place.
- **THE FLYOUT NOW READS create → modify → remove**, matching the `SITE ELEMENTS` caret pattern beside it: **Add land** (Draw · Deed / Title · Click a lot on the map · Add by address) · **Change a parcel** (Split · Combine · Edit boundary corners · Setbacks & parcel settings → · Lock · Count-in/Exclude-from yield · Hide/Show acreage label · Reset label position) · **Remove** (Remove parcels — click to delete · Delete this parcel). Every one of them arms an EXISTING path — nothing here is a second implementation of an action that already lives elsewhere, which is why a complete menu grew no new behaviour to test.
- **A ROW THE PLAN CANNOT USE IS VISIBLE AND DISABLED WITH ITS REASON, NEVER HIDDEN.** Hiding an unusable action makes it undiscoverable, which is the bug. The ONE exception is *Reset label position*, which is meaningless until a label has actually been dragged.
- **EDIT BOUNDARY CORNERS IS A MODE OVER THE EXISTING SELECT GESTURES, NOT A NEW TOOL** — no new hit-testing, no new drafting, no new Esc handling. It arms Select with a parcel in hand and puts the three gestures on screen. **The trap it uncovered: a freshly drawn parcel arrives LOCKED, and `editablePath()` refuses a locked parcel** — so the mode would have taught three gestures and then silently swallowed all of them. The banner says the parcel is locked and carries the Unlock button (LOUD-FAILURE; never unlock behind the user's back).
- **THE NAMING COLLISION IS RESOLVED ON THE OWNER'S OWN SPLIT, and the split is now recorded in code (`PARCEL_SURFACES`) rather than in a convention.** The **right rail owns ACTIONS** — things you DO — and is **"Parcel tools"**. The **left panel owns ATTRIBUTES & SETTINGS** — what a parcel HAS: its acreage, county record, taxes, setbacks, active/locked state — and is **"Land"**. "Land" rather than "Parcels" (still one word apart) and rather than "Property" (which would have collided with the existing **Properties** element-inspector tab — one collision traded for another). Setbacks stay on the left because they are an attribute, and **each side carries a one-click path to the other**: the flyout's `Setbacks & parcel settings → in Land` row opens the panel with the lot selected, and the panel's `Draw, split, combine, reshape… → Parcel tools` row opens the flyout (sliding the rail in first on a phone). The **panel id stays `parcel`** — it keys persisted panel state and every `setLeftPanel("parcel")` call site, and renaming it would orphan them for no user gain.
- **THE INVENTORY WAS BUILT BY GREPPING EVERY `setParcels` / parcel handler, not by trusting the report's list** — which is how the four label/state rows (lock · active · hide chip · reset chip offset), previously right-click-only, and the two county-backed create rows, previously left-panel-only, got menu paths too.
- **Selector debt paid in the same commit:** ten e2e specs and seven ui-audit harnesses reached the left tab by its LABEL (`button[title="Parcel"]` / `getByRole("button", {name: "Parcel"})`). They now use the stable `[data-rail-tab="parcel"]` hook, so the next rename costs nothing. Two stale assertions in `e2e/standards-footer-setback.spec.js` that hardcoded the pre-**B1192** indigo setback hex (`#534AB7`) were repointed at the palette token they should always have read — they were red on `main` before this branch and are green now.
- **PANEL-BREVITY:** not applicable — no yield/pond panel copy touched; `node ui-audit/panel-copy-budget.mjs --check` re-run and clean.
- **Bundle — this BREACHED `bundle.totalJsBytes` in CI and the breach was worked, not waved through.** The first build measured 4600.6 KB against a 4599.4 KB derived ceiling: **1.2 KB over**. Two things were done, in this order. **(a) A real payback first:** `PARCEL_ACTIONS` shipped an `elsewhere` array per row — provenance naming every OTHER surface each action is reachable from — plus a `byId` Map and a `parcelMenuIds` flattener, all three with **no runtime consumer**. The provenance is now PROSE in the module header (where it reads better anyway), the two helpers moved into the test that was their only caller, and the three toggling rows became `label` + `altLabel` + `altWhen` data instead of closures. **−0.8 KB of pure shipped-string waste**, taking the feature from +7.7 KB to **+6.3 KB** on the Site route. **(b) The remaining ~1 KB was RATCHETED, with the attribution stated in the log entry rather than buried:** `npm run perf:ratchet -- --metric bundle.totalJsBytes --item B1414 --allow-raise`. The reason recorded in `bundle.ratchetLog` opens by saying the raise **re-records accumulated drift, not this feature's cost** — the same CI run measured `notesRouteJsBytes` **+22.9 KB**, `siteRouteJsBytes` **+18.1 KB** and `largestChunkBytes` **+17.8 KB** over their baselines, none of it this menu, i.e. the band was ~90% consumed before this branch existed and *any* honest 7 KB feature breached it. That is precisely the failure mode `docs/PERF-BUDGETS.md` changed the budget's shape to prevent on 2026-07-30, and this follows that precedent. **Deliberately NOT a blanket amnesty:** `siteRouteJsBytes` and `largestChunkBytes` are left UNratcheted and still name **B1064** as the owner of paying them back. The alternative considered and rejected was shaving user-facing copy to buy 0.4 KB — brevity is never bought with accuracy (PANEL-BREVITY 6).

### B1415 — A project's name had no single home: it was copied onto every plan, and nothing kept the copies in agreement `[Site Planner / persistence]` (bug) #site-planner #persistence #sync  *(owner chat block 2026-08-04, provisional NEW-1 — "I just tried renaming a project from the map viewer via the drop down, and it didn't remember it." Minted **B1415–B1418 / V698–V700** via `git fetch origin main && npm run next-id -- --against-main`, LATE, as the last step before push; code, tests and commits keep the provisional `NEW-#` labels. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open + ⏳ Verify + Done across `rename`, `renameSiteGroup`, `rename-revert`, `site group`, `B439`, `B475`, `B191`: **B439** built the breadcrumb's per-row Rename/Delete and the `rename-revert` fix made `renameSiteGroup` resolve a NON-anchor plan id to its group — a real fix to a different half of the same call, and its guarantee still holds (its tests pass unchanged). Neither B439 nor anything else ever claimed the name had ONE authoritative value. Net-new, not a B439 recurrence.)*
`[x]` **Shipped 2026-08-04. Parked in ⏳ Verify — `V698` (concurrency / multi-writer is a mandatory LIVE-VERIFY class).**
- Verify: **live** — `V698`
- Origin: filed 2026-08-04 from the owner chat block (NEW-1)
- **PROVEN IN THE PRODUCTION DB, WITH A SURVIVING VICTIM.** Group `smrp1wrgg6u5` — one project, five plans, TWO names, split for four days. The `.256/.307/.358` writes are ONE `loadPlansOfGroup` loop (the rename); `sms4zs8unbkg` was saved **seventeen minutes later**, after the rename, and still said "Sylvestri" — it was not in the local set when the rename ran, so it kept the old spelling and wrote it back to the cloud.
- **THE STRUCTURAL FIX, ARGUED.** The alternatives were (a) a real `projects` table, (b) a group-keyed name record, (c) an authoritative value per group reconciled on read. **(c) shipped**, because (a) and (b) both mean a new table, a new RLS surface, a migration of every existing group, and a second write path to keep in step with `sites` — a large blast radius to fix a rule that can be stated in one line. The invariant is what matters, not where the bytes live: **a project's name has ONE authoritative value per group, and every `site` field is a DERIVED MIRROR of it.** The per-plan `site` column stays (every read path uses it, and the cloud's slim-header row is keyed off it) — it is simply no longer a source of truth.
- **WHAT MAKES IT AN AUTHORITY RATHER THAN A GUESS: `siteRenamedAt` (schema v13, additive, null on every existing record).** A rename stamps the group; the name on the plan with the NEWEST stamp wins, unconditionally. **This field is the whole point, and the trap it closes is specific:** without it the only available tiebreak is "most recently updated", and on the owner's own data that answer is a coin flip — `sms9c5oc7jnt` (correct name) happens to be later than the straggler, but nothing made that true, and had Concept D been touched last the wrong name would have won. Do not "simplify" the authority back onto `updatedAt`.
- **`lib/projectName.js` is the pure decision** (`nameAuthority` / `reconcileGroupNames` / `resolveNameFor` / `maxStampOf`) — no storage, no network, no DOM. Three bases, and the third is the honest one: `stamp` (a real rename) → `majority` (LEGACY only, no stamp anywhere; this is the shape the bug produces — the loop writes N−1 copies and the straggler keeps the old one, which is how the owner's 4-vs-1 group recovers) → `ambiguous` (legacy, no majority, e.g. a 1-vs-1 split): **there is no honest winner, so nothing is changed and the group is REPORTED** (`project-name-ambiguous`, LOUD-FAILURE) rather than half-renamed. Once a group is stamped it always resolves — a same-instant two-name tie breaks deterministically on count, never back into `ambiguous`.
- **THE READ AND WRITE SEAMS, because a rule that lives in one of them is not an invariant.** `loadSitesList` resolves the authority on the way OUT (so a split group can never reach the map list, the switcher or an export under two names, even before anything is written back); `loadSite` does the same for the single-record read that `pushSiteToCloud` goes through; and **`saveSite` is the write choke point** — every local write passes through `resolveNameFor`, so a stale in-memory model can no longer be *written* with the old name and therefore can never be *pushed* with it. That last one is the exact move that undid the owner's rename.
- **The stamp is STRICTLY MONOTONIC — `max(now, groupMax + 1)`, not a bare `Date.now()`.** Two renames inside one millisecond would otherwise share a stamp and the SECOND could lose; and a device whose clock runs slow would stamp a genuinely later rename with an earlier number. The first case was caught by a test, not by inspection.
- Sandbox: `test/projectName.test.js` (23 new, written against the real production rows) · `test/storage.test.js` (+10, incl. the re-publish move) · full suite **7,902 passed** · lint 0 errors · build green · `MAP.md` regenerated.

### B1416 — A rename only reached the plans this browser happened to have cached, and said nothing when it didn't `[Site Planner / persistence]` (bug) #site-planner #persistence #sync  *(owner chat block 2026-08-04, provisional NEW-2. DEDUPE-FIRST — same search as B1415; filed as its own item because the WRITE path and the AUTHORITY are independently wrong: fixing either alone still leaves the project splittable.)*
`[x]` **Shipped 2026-08-04. Parked in ⏳ Verify — `V699` (multi-writer + a cross-device repro).**
- Verify: **live** — `V699`
- Origin: filed 2026-08-04 from the owner chat block (NEW-2)
- **THE RENAME NO LONGER ENUMERATES PLANS ON THE CLIENT AT ALL.** It used to iterate `loadPlansOfGroup(groupId)` — the LOCAL store — and push each hydrated plan; a plan on a second device, in a fresh browser, or evicted from this one was never written. It now names the GROUP and lets the server touch every row in it: **`rename_site_group`** (`db/rename_site_group.sql`), ONE `update … where coalesce(data->>'groupId', id) = $group` statement, which Postgres applies atomically — so it reaches plans this browser has never loaded and **cannot half-land**.
- **THE GROUP KEY IS `coalesce(data->>'groupId', id)`, NOT the `group_id` COLUMN — and that is load-bearing, not fussiness.** The column is a denormalized mirror that is *known* to drift: the `e2e-fixture-testfit` row's column says `e2e-fixture` while its jsonb says `e2e-fixture-testfit`. Keyed on the column, a fleet-wide split scan reports that fixture pair as a split project and a rename would touch the wrong set; keyed on the jsonb — which is what the client's `groupOf()` reads — it correctly resolves to two different groups. Do not "optimise" this onto the column.
- **SECURITY INVOKER**, so the existing RLS on `public.sites` decides what a caller may rename — no new surface. It touches only `site`, `data`, `version`, `updated_at`: never `team_id` (which would trip the `guard_team_rehome` BEFORE UPDATE trigger and could silently unshare a project), never `user_id`, never `deleted_at`. It returns each row's fresh `version` so the calling tab's CAS tokens stay valid and its next ordinary content push isn't a false stale-version conflict.
- **A DB WITHOUT THE MIGRATION DEGRADES, IT DOES NOT BREAK.** PostgREST answers an unknown function with `PGRST202`; `cloudRenameGroup` then falls back to reading the group's rows **from the server** (never from local storage — that is the whole defect) and rewriting each. Not atomic, but it still reaches every plan, so renaming is never blocked on the migration. **Applied to production 2026-08-04 and used to perform B1417's repair, so the atomic path is the live one.**
- **THE CONFIRMATION IS NOW HONEST.** The old code fired the per-plan pushes with `Promise.all` and did NOT await them, then called `refreshSites()` synchronously — a pull landing in that window rebuilt the list from cloud rows that hadn't been updated yet. `renameSite` now refreshes twice: optimistically (the local half is already written, so the new name paints in the same tick) and again **after the cloud write settles**. A rename that didn't reach the cloud raises a named banner instead of failing silently — which is why the owner only found out by noticing the name had reverted.
- **THE CLOUD WRITE IS LAZILY LOADED** — `lib/cloudRename.js` is reached ONLY by a dynamic `import()` from `renameSiteGroup`, the same pattern as `exportSheet.js` / `rasterIdentifyLazy.js`: a rename is rare and user-initiated, so an RPC call plus a whole un-migrated-DB degrade has no business on the chunk every page load pays for. **⛔ Never static-import it from the boot path.**
- **PERF BUDGET — paid back, and in the end NOT ratcheted.** CI first breached `bundle.totalJsBytes` by 1.6 KB. Measured against `origin/main` 4c76ab5: main alone **4592.9 KB**, this branch **4594.2 KB** → the feature costs **+1.3 KB total**. Three real optimizations shipped WITH the feature rather than a bare baseline raise: the rename's cloud write moved to the lazily-imported `lib/cloudRename.js` (**−1.7 KB off the Site route** — reached only by a dynamic `import()` from `renameSiteGroup`, the `exportSheet.js` pattern), the fallback's three-tier column-degrade ladder collapsed to one `select("id, data")` (the only columns every schema version has), and the inline rename editor de-duplicated into ONE shared module-scope `RenameInput` used by both the row menu and the crumb (**−1.8 KB off the Notes route**, which also renders the breadcrumb). **A ratchet was then made unnecessary by the merge:** B1414 landed on main having hit the SAME ceiling for the same reason and re-recorded the baseline, so this branch's merged build (4606.5 KB) sits inside the band with no raise of its own — this branch's ratchet entry was dropped on the merge rather than stacked on top of it. **⚠ Worth stating because two branches independently tripped it within the hour: the overage is ACCUMULATED DRIFT, owned by B1064, not this feature** — main had already eaten essentially the whole headroom band, so any honest change was going to breach it.
- Sandbox: `test/storage.test.js` (the await + the empty/whitespace refusal + the trim, so a stray trailing space can't fork a project into two) · `e2e/project-rename.spec.js` · full suite green · lint 0 errors · build green · `MAP.md` regenerated.

### B1402 — One URL carried two health policies, and the same endpoint was added to the map twice `[Site Planner / MapFinder · GIS]` (bug) #site-planner #gis #perf  *(owner chat block 2026-08-03, provisional NEW-2 — the mechanism behind B1401's banner, filed as its own item because it is structural and outlives the Larimer wiring. Minted **B1402 / V687** via `--against-main`, LATE. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open + ⏳ Verify + Done across `addDisplay`, `STATEWIDE_KEYS`, `breaker`, `sourceHealth`, `DISPLAY_LOAD_TIMEOUT`, `B244`, `B787`, `B130`, `B629`: **B244** built the circuit breaker and the hang-guard, **B787** decoupled the statewide key from Chambers, **B130** made the statewide layer clickable everywhere, **B629** added the snapshot display preference. Every one of them made the KEY-based model more correct; none of them noticed that the model itself asks the wrong question. Net-new.)*
`[x]` **Shipped 2026-08-03. Parked in ⏳ Verify — `V687` (GIS endpoint behavior).**
- Verify: **live** — `V687`
- Origin: filed 2026-08-03 from the owner chat block (NEW-2)
- **THE BANNER WAS A SELF-INFLICTED FALSE ALARM.** Because `co_larimer.layerUrl` was byte-identical to `co_statewide.layerUrl`, `MapFinder.addDisplay` — which keys its display map by COUNTY — added **two identical Leaflet layers over the same ground**, doubling every request to the slowest host in the app. And `STATEWIDE_KEYS` is derived from the `statewide: true` flag on the KEY, so `co_statewide` was exempt from the 8 s hang-guard while `co_larimer` — the same URL — was not. The guard fired on the county-keyed copy, `markDown` pulled the layer, `recordSourceResult` opened the breaker, and the banner told the owner his county server was slow **while pointing him at the exact host it had just declared dead**. Two health policies on one endpoint.
- **FIXED STRUCTURALLY, TWICE, AND NEITHER FIX MENTIONS LARIMER:**
  - **(a) Displays dedupe by RESOLVED URL, not by county key.** A key that resolves to an endpoint already on the map becomes an ALIAS of the layer that is there. `displaySrcRef` records `{url, owner}` per key; an alias drops only its own reference on removal, removing the OWNER drops every alias pointing at it, `clearDisplays` removes each shared layer once, and `optimisticHitAt` walks each layer's features once instead of twice.
  - **(b) The hang-guard exemption keys off the URL.** `isStatewideLayerUrl(url)` replaces `STATEWIDE_KEYS.includes(key)`: if the endpoint IS the universal fallback it gets the universal fallback's policy, whichever key asked for it. `optimisticHitAt`'s "is this a REAL county CAD hit" answer moved to the same test — a county drawing COMPOSITE features scores as a statewide-backup hit however its key is spelled, so a genuine neighbouring CAD hit correctly wins over it.
- **THIS WAS NEVER LARIMER-ONLY, WHICH IS WHY IT SHIPS ANYWAY.** **Waller** has carried the identical shape in Texas since B629 (its primary IS the TxGIO composite), and the four Colorado counties above still do. Waller was masked only while its Drive snapshot happened to be loaded; with no snapshot it fell straight through to a second TxGIO image layer WITH a hang-guard on it.
- **AND THE NEXT ONE IS BLOCKED.** `sharedLayerUrlConflicts()` is a pure assertion that no two `COUNTIES_MAP` entries share a **non-statewide** layer URL — sharing a COMPOSITE is the sanctioned parking pattern and stays legal, because after (a) and (b) it is genuinely harmless. It runs as a named `console.error` in dev (LOUD-FAILURE) and as a CI test, so a county parked on a composite in future cannot reintroduce this.
- Sandbox: `test/parcelSourcePolicy.test.js` (the URL policy + the assertion, both directions incl. a hand-built colliding config) · full suite green · lint 0 errors · build green.

### B1403 — A truncated parcel draw looked exactly like a complete one `[Site Planner / MapFinder · GIS]` (bug) #site-planner #gis  *(owner chat block 2026-08-03, provisional NEW-3, MEASURED: one view-sized bbox against the Colorado composite returned exactly 2000 features with `exceededTransferLimit = true`. Minted **B1403 / V688** via `--against-main`, LATE. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open + ⏳ Verify + Done for `exceededTransferLimit`, `pageProvider`, `truncat`, `maxRecordCount`, `B629`: the flag IS handled correctly in the two paths that PAGE — `vectorLayers.js` and `scripts/build-parcel-snapshot.mjs`, whose **Waller 26k-vs-48.7k undercount (B629, 2026-07-04) is this exact bug caught once before, one layer over**. No item has ever covered the DISPLAY path, which cannot page because esri-leaflet owns its request loop. Net-new, and the prior instance is why this is filed as a class rather than a one-off.)*
`[x]` **Shipped 2026-08-03. Parked in ⏳ Verify — `V688` (data-density-dependent rendering).**
- Verify: **live** — `V688`
- Origin: filed 2026-08-03 from the owner chat block (NEW-3)
- **WHY THIS IS WORSE THAN SLOW.** ArcGIS answers any query with at most the layer's `maxRecordCount` and sets `exceededTransferLimit` when it had more to give. esri-leaflet's `featureLayer` does not page, so the map drew an authoritative-looking parcel layer with an unknown number of lots simply **not there to click** — and said nothing. A lot the owner needs can be missing from a map that looks complete.
- **THE AUDIT, over every parcel fetch path rather than the one the report came through:** the vector GIS engine (`vectorLayers.js`) and the nightly snapshot builder both already page on the server's own flag and are **untouched**; the point paths (`queryAtPoint` / `identifyAtPoint`) are single-point intersects and cannot reach a record cap; the `/export` image path is rendered server-side and returns no flag to read. The DISPLAY path was the one unchecked consumer, and it is the one that cannot page.
- **SO IT SAYS SO.** `parcelTruncation.js` (a new pure module — split out of `parcelDisplay.js`, which imports Leaflet and therefore cannot be unit-tested) answers "did this come back cut short?" in **every shape a real service returns the flag** (top-level `exceededTransferLimit`, GeoJSON `properties.exceededTransferLimit`, and `transferLimitExceeded`), and produces one honest, non-blocking notice naming the cap and what to do: *"That parcel service capped this view at 2,000 lots — some outlines here are missing. Zoom in to see them all; clicking a lot still adds it."* Wired to the display layer's `requestsuccess`.
- **B1401 also removes most of the OCCASIONS for it** — a county on its own endpoint answers a view-sized bbox well inside `maxRecordCount` — but the notice stays, because the composite is still every county's outage fallback and Waller's primary.

### B1405 — Right-click a road end, get a real roundabout `[Site Planner / roadGeometry]` (feature) #site-planner #road #ui  *(owner chat block 2026-08-03, provisional NEW-5, verbatim: "add a feature to right click the end of a road and it become a round about", with the condition "do not ship a decorative circle that the pavement math and the curb engine do not know about". Minted **B1405 / V690** via `--against-main`, LATE. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open + ⏳ Verify + Done across `roundabout`, `cul-de-sac`, `circle`, `turnaround`, `roadGeometry`, `roadNetwork`, `nodeJunction`, `teeGeometry`: nothing in the repo has ever drawn a circular travelway; **B945–B1011** are the tee/junction family this REUSES (the dissolve, the additive-wedge convention, the class return radius) rather than duplicates. Net-new.)*
`[x]` **Shipped 2026-08-03 — the FULL geometry, not a placeholder. Parked in ⏳ Verify — `V690` (PDF / export parity is a mandatory LIVE-VERIFY class).**
- Verify: **live** — `V690`
- Origin: filed 2026-08-03 from the owner chat block (NEW-5)
- **THE OWNER'S CONDITION, ANSWERED IN THREE PARTS, each unit-tested rather than asserted in prose:**
  1. **THE PAVEMENT MATH KNOWS.** `roundaboutArea` is the **ANNULUS**, never the disc — the central island is landscaped, and counting it would overstate impervious cover, which is exactly what a detention volume is priced off. The annulus is added to the owning road's paved figure (ONE road owns it, so two legs can never double-count), and `legTrimFor` shortens each approach so its strip stops at the circle instead of paving the island. **That trim is the HALF-CHORD √(R²−half²), not the radius** — trimming by the radius stops the CENTERLINE on the circle and leaves the strip's square end face poking past the arc at its outer corners, and the lens-shaped void between face and arc closes as a genuine phantom HOLE in the dissolved pavement (measured: two of them, one per side, before the fix).
  2. **THE CURB ENGINE KNOWS.** The circulatory roadway is contributed into the SAME `dissolveRings` union the rest of the road network goes through, as arc **SECTORS whose union IS the annulus** — union-only, which is the one operation the dissolve is proven on, so no boolean difference and no new failure mode. The result is ONE region with ONE continuous curb outline and the central island as a real PolyTree hole, and every leg clusters with its circle. Curb returns are arcs **tangent to both the leg edge and the circle** (fillet centre at R+Rr from the centre and half+Rr from the leg axis — two conditions, one exact placement), omitted rather than faked when a leg is too wide to solve.
  3. **THE DESIGN VEHICLE DECIDES THE SIZE.** `roundaboutDiameterFor` = 2 × the class's design-vehicle turning radius + one circulatory width, clamped into that class's published FHWA / NCHRP-672 band (mini 45–90 for an auto aisle; single-lane 90–180 for a fire lane; 130–180 for a WB-67 truck route). An auto drive aisle, a fire lane and a WB-67 truck route get **three different circles**, and that is a test, not a claim. **`public` deliberately takes a FIXED band value:** its `minRadius` is a horizontal CURVE radius derived from design speed (~185 ft at 25 mph), not a turning radius, and feeding it to the formula would put a 390 ft circle on a site road.
- **BONDED BY CONSTRUCTION.** The roundabout is stored on the ROAD at a terminus (`el.roundabout = {end, d}`) and **records no position at all** — the centre, the leg bearings and the curb returns are re-derived from the road's current `pts` every frame. So moving or re-aligning the road carries it with nothing to keep in sync, which is this repo's own ROWS-CANONICAL / assembly-integrity lesson applied to geometry rather than to rows. A **second road** whose terminus lands on the same node joins as another LEG rather than creating a second circle, and the **larger** declared diameter wins (a truck leg and an aisle leg at one node must get the truck's circle — the smaller cannot turn the bigger vehicle).
- **THE MENU ITEM IS WHERE HE ALREADY RIGHT-CLICKS** — the road-terminus branch of the same vertex menu that hosts "Add / Delete control point" (`onCanvasVtxContextCapture`). The diameter is then editable in place through the **shared inline numeric editor** every other dimension on this canvas uses — never a dialog (owner rule 2026-06-17) — and an out-of-range value is clamped with a named warning rather than silently accepted.
- **PDF-PARITY holds by construction, and is stated rather than assumed:** the island is drawn INSIDE the road-network region group with `data-export="road-network"`, and `buildExportSvg` clones the live `<svg>` stripping only `data-export="skip"` — so the sheet carries the same node the screen does. There is no second render path to drift. (The live PDF/PNG check is still owed — see `V690`.)
- **A TRAP WORTH THE COMMENT IT CARRIES:** a curb return's closing polygon must run through the CORNER, never straight between the two tangent points. A direct chord passes inside the fillet circle, so the ring self-intersects and the union **silently drops it** — the return then floats as its own island instead of joining the pavement. Found by measurement (5 regions where there should be 1), not by reading.
- Sandbox: `test/roundabout.test.js` — **30 unit cases** over the derivation, the areas, the trim, the sector union (asserted THROUGH the real `dissolveRings`), the tangency (the fillet centre is recovered from the emitted arc and checked against both conditions), the node grouping and the degenerate refusals. `e2e/road-roundabout.spec.js` — **5 specs**, all green: the menu item is on the control-point menu; it lands as one region with the island as a real hole and the landscaped surface drawn through it; the diameter comes from the class and persists on the road; **moving the road carries the circle and re-derives the tie-in**; removing it restores the road's area to within 1%. Full suite **7,819 passed** · lint 0 errors · build green · `MAP.md` + the site-planner folder pointer updated in the same commit.
- **BUNDLE, stated because a budget check went red and the honest number matters.** These five items add **10.4 KB** to the Site route's largest chunk. The `bundle.largestChunkBytes` ceiling was breached by **1.0 KB** — because that ceiling is already **22.7 KB** inflated by the pre-existing, filed baseline defect **B1178** (measured this session: `main` at `ccbfcf2`, with no changes, builds 22.7 KB over its own recorded number). My contribution alone sits well inside the 32 KB headroom band. Recorded via `npm run perf:ratchet` against this item rather than absorbed silently; the payback is owned by **B1064**.
### B1400 — Sketch mode (×2): REBUILT the authoring surface — double-click anywhere, type in the box, drag an arrow `[Notes / sketch]` (feature) #notes #ui #export  *(owner chat 2026-08-03, provisional NEW-1, verbatim: "there should maybe be a separate mode where I can almost start drawing, like a chart. Like I can click something, type in three words, and then put a box around it, and then draw an arrow to another box, and then put text in that box, and then maybe some more detailed information in that text box. I don't know. It doesn't even necessarily need to be a text box, but maybe it's just like an outline." Offered the design fork — free placement vs structure-generated-from-an-outline vs both — and CHOSE **"type first, then rearrange."** DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open / ⏳ Verify / Done across `sketch`, `chart`, `diagram`, `flowchart`, `mindmap`, `outline`, `notes`: **B973** is the pond cross-section diagram (a generated engineering schematic in the Site Planner, no shared surface); **B1290 / B1310–B1318 / B1291 / B1365–B1374 / B1391–B1393** are the Notes module and its four prior rounds, none of which touches a canvas. Net-new.)*

**Recurrence (×2) — 2026-08-04, owner used what shipped and REJECTED it.** Verbatim: *"The sketch feature kinda sucks. Like, if I could just double click anywhere, even if I'm already writing text, that'd be better. And then, like, maybe there's a button where I can just put a box around it. Like, that would be just as good."* DEDUPE-FIRST: this re-opens **B1400** rather than taking a new number — same feature, same surface, the first shipping of it was wrong. **What went wrong is worth recording, because the code was fine and the DESIGN was not:** his original request was already the spec — *"I can click something, type three words, and then put a box around it, and then draw an arrow to another box"* — which is DIRECT MANIPULATION. He was then offered a design fork whose framing pushed him to *"type first, then rearrange"*, and what he got was a two-pane block in which he had to learn an **indent-and-caret syntax in a textarea** before a single box appeared. **The syntax was the defect.** Nobody sketches by writing a structured list first.

**⛔ THE RULE IS REPLACED, and the old one is marked superseded rather than deleted.**
- **DEAD:** *"the OUTLINE owns content, the CANVAS owns only position"* (project doc `claude/decision-2026-08-03-notes-sketch-mode-outline-owns-content-canvas-owns-position.md`). It is dead because the outline is no longer an authoring surface at all.
- **LIVE: THE CANVAS OWNS EVERYTHING.** Each box owns its own **text** AND its own **position**; the arrows are an explicit list of `{from,to}` box references. **There is no second representation, so there is nothing to keep in sync and nothing to arbitrate.** Written down in all four file headers, in the folder pointer (`src/workspaces/notes/CLAUDE.md`) and here — each of them naming the superseded rule.

**WHAT IT DOES NOW — his two sentences, and they were the whole spec.**
1. **DOUBLE-CLICK ANY EMPTY SPOT** on the canvas → a box appears **right there** with the caret already in it; you type immediately. No pane, no syntax, no button first. *"even if I'm already writing text"* is honoured literally: the press takes focus from wherever the caret was (the node view stops every event reaching the document), and the sentence you were mid-way through is untouched — **asserted headless, both halves**.
2. **THE BOX BUTTON** (toolbar, replacing the old "insert a sketch" button — a REPLACEMENT, not an addition, per PANEL-BREVITY). With words selected, or the caret in a paragraph, one click turns them into a box. **DECISION, stated because it was a real fork: boxing CONVERTS the text into a real sketch box; it does NOT draw a border in place.** A border in place would be a dead end — you could not drag it and you could not draw an arrow from it, and *"then draw an arrow to another box"* was his very next clause. A box you cannot connect is a decoration; he asked for a chart. (Boxing your only paragraph leaves a fresh line to keep writing on — an atom last in the document would otherwise swallow the next keystroke.)
3. **DRAG FROM ONE BOX ONTO ANOTHER** → an arrow. Direct, off a dot on the box's own edge, with **no mode to turn on first**. An explicit **↗ Arrow** button is the keyboard route (select a box, press it, click the target), so nothing here is mouse-only — every box is a real focus stop with an accessible name.
4. **BOXES STAY DRAGGABLE.** A drag previews locally and commits once, so it is one undo step; it leaves every word **byte-identical** (asserted headless).
5. **A BOX IS A SHORT LABEL PLUS AN OPTIONAL LONGER BODY** — *"some more detailed information"* — authored **in the box** (two plain fields laid over it; no dialog, house rule), never via a `>` prefix in a textarea.
6. **DELETE** removes the selected box **and every arrow that named it, at either end** (**TOMBSTONE-DELETES**) and says how many it took. `removeBox` is the ONE place a box is destroyed and it returns the arrows it removed, so no caller can skip the cascade; `normalizeSketch` drops a dangler on read as a second line of defence.

**⛔ THE OUTLINE TEXTAREA IS REMOVED, not kept "just in case."** Two authoring paths is exactly the accumulation **PANEL-BREVITY** forbids, and the outline half is the one he disliked. A read-only outline VIEW was considered and dropped: it costs a disclosure and a line of chrome for something nobody asked for. An ordering is still **derived** from the arrows (`outlineFromSketch`) for the Markdown export and the accessible name — derived, on demand, owned by nobody, with no way back into the model. Net chrome change: three buttons before (Outline · ＋ Arrow · Tidy up) and three now (＋ Box · ↗ Arrow · Delete), minus the textarea and its permanent hint line — the one hint that remains **hides itself after the first box**.

**⛔ NOBODY'S EXISTING SKETCH BREAKS.** A sketch saved under the old shape (`outline` + `positions`, no `boxes`) is **migrated on READ**: its lines become boxes carrying their own text at exactly the coordinates the old automatic layout put them at, the indentation's implied parent→child arrows become **real explicit arrows**, and a box he had dragged stays where he dragged it. Opening one does **not** rewrite it (asserted headless — the stored document still has its `outline` after being opened); the new shape is written the first time it is genuinely edited. The two superseded attributes stay declared, defaulting to `null`, and the schema guard asserts exactly that.

**WHAT WAS KEPT, deliberately and unchanged — the spine that was already verified live.** `noteSketch` is still a **NODE IN THE PROSEMIRROR SCHEMA** (`lib/notesExtensions.js`), so it still persists through the one storage seam (**no sketch key anywhere in `localStorage` — re-asserted headless**), still round-trips through cloud sync (B1291) with **no schema change, no new table, no migration — nothing database-related lands on the owner**, and still prints. The **single render builder** still feeds both the screen and the print sheet, and the interactive half is still a **cached dynamic import**.

**PDF-PARITY GOT STRICTLY BETTER.** The old design had a real screen/paper divergence to manage (a chevron on screen, a detail list on paper). Now the canvas owns the text, so a box simply draws its own body — **the same content on both surfaces, with no flag to keep in step**. The only remaining difference carries no content at all: the grip you drag an arrow out of is not drawn on paper, because nothing on a sheet can be dragged. Print sheet asserted headless: same boxes, same arrows, every label and body present, **zero grips**, box drawn on `rgb(255,255,255)`.

**MARKDOWN STAYS HONEST.** Boxes export as a **readable nested list** (nesting derived from the arrows), bodies attached to their own box as `>` continuation lines. An arrow the nesting cannot express — a second arrow into the same box, a link back — is **written out** under `Also connected:`. Where the boxes SIT is the one thing a list cannot say, and it joins `docToMarkdown`'s named lossy list ("where a sketch's boxes sit on the canvas") — reported only when there is more than one box, since a single box has no arrangement to lose. A sketch's words still feed `docToText`, so a note whose whole content is a sketch is still findable — for the new shape **and** the superseded one.

**BUNDLE.** The interactive chunk `notesSketchEditor-*.js` grows **6.2 KB → 9.4 KB** (direct manipulation is more code than a textarea); it is still fetched only when a sketch is genuinely on screen — asserted live, twenty-two harness sections run with nothing sketch-shaped requested. The static Notes path is unchanged (the exporter still imports nothing).

**Files:** `lib/notesSketchModel.js` (rewritten — the five edits, the layout, the derived ordering, the legacy migration) · `lib/notesSketchRender.js` (one builder; surface rect + grips) · `lib/notesSketchNode.js` (attrs `boxes`/`links` + the two superseded ones; the `boxSelection` command) · `lib/notesSketchEditor.js` (rewritten — double-click to create, in-box fields, drag, arrow drag, keyboard route) · the `noteSketch` case in `lib/notesMarkdown.js` (both shapes) · `components/NoteToolbar.jsx` (the **Box** button replaces the sketch-insert button) · the two mirrored CSS blocks · `test/notesSketch.test.js` (**43 pure tests**, rewritten — including the migration) · **13 structural guards** in `test/notesModule.test.js` (rewritten; the outline-syntax guards are REPLACED, not left passing against dead code) · **§23 of `ui-audit/verify-notes.mjs`** (rewritten IN PLACE, no second harness).

**Sandbox:** full suite **7,879 passed** · lint 0 errors · build green · `ui-audit/verify-notes.mjs` **210/210, no uncaught page error** — it double-clicks empty canvas and types straight into the box, does it again while the caret is in the note body, boxes written words with the button, drags an arrow between two boxes (and draws the same arrow from the keyboard), drags a box, reloads the whole browser, exports Markdown off disk, builds the print sheet, deletes a box and demands its arrows go with it, and opens a genuine old-shape document. `MAP.md`, `BACKLOG_OPEN.md` and the notes folder pointer regenerated in the same commit.

### B1391 — A FALSE CONFLICT: one person, one account, two windows — and the app said someone else was editing his note `[Notes / sync]` (bug) #notes #sync #persistence  *(owner chat 2026-08-03, round four, provisional NEW-1, verbatim: "it also thought that someone else was editing this file, but no one else is editing the file. It's literally just me on the file, and it asked if I wanted to keep the other person's copy or mine, but it's the same person. So it shouldn't be doing that." Minted **B1391 / V680** via `git fetch origin main && npm run next-id -- --against-main`, deliberately JUMPING CLEAR of the next free number (9 in-flight branches on the remote; gaps are free, a second renumber pass is not). DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open / ⏳ Verify / Done across `conflict`, `rev`, `guard`, `multi-writer`, `notes`, `sync`: **B1291** built this sync tier and its conflict surface and is NOT re-opened — its guard is correct and stays; this is a defect in what it does with a REFUSAL. **B673** is the Site Planner's own loud-conflict surface, a different module and a different model. **B1113 / ROWS-CANONICAL-ON-SEED** is the rule this restores rather than a duplicate of it. Net-new.)*
`[x]` **Shipped 2026-08-03. Parked in ⏳ Verify — `V680` (concurrency / multi-writer is a mandatory LIVE-VERIFY class).**
- Verify: **live** — `V680`
- Origin: filed 2026-08-03 from chat (round four, NEW-1)
- **THE TRIGGER, stated honestly because it changes what the bug IS:** the same account was open in more than one window. The owner's own tab was open while this cohort opened `planyr.io/#/notes` in extra tabs on his machines and hard-reloaded them. Two clients of ONE account raced. Nobody else has access — notes are own-row and private by default — so the app was not merely rude, it was **wrong about who**.
- **AUDIT-FIRST — three distinct defects, all three fixed, and the third is the real bug:**
  1. **A NO-OP RAISED A PROMPT.** The revision guard answers "did the row move?", and that was being reported as "the two copies disagree" **without anyone comparing the documents**. A sibling window's push, or a hard reload landing between a push and the ledger write, leaves a stale base rev — so the next push is refused over content the server ALREADY HAS. The user was asked to choose between two identical documents.
  2. **THE WORDING NAMED A PERSON.** "Keep the other computer's copy" / "also changed on another device" implied a second human on a private, own-row note.
  3. **⛔ THE ACTUAL BUG: A SINGLE ACCOUNT COULD SILENTLY OVERWRITE ITSELF.** The editor reads its document ONCE at mount (deliberately — B1290's crash fix). When a page's body is replaced underneath it — by a sibling window, or by the cloud seed adopting the account's row — it kept the STALE copy, and the next keystroke wrote that whole stale document back. Guarded on a revision this window legitimately held, so it committed **cleanly**: no conflict, no banner, the other window's paragraph simply gone. That is the B1113 / ROWS-CANONICAL-ON-SEED trap, in Notes. **Reproduced and then killed in a real browser** — see the mutation result below.
- **What shipped:**
  - **`judgeConflict` + `sameDoc` + `isEmptyDoc` (pure, `notesCloud.js`)** — every path that loses the guard now compares the two documents first. **Identical** → adopt the server's revision in silence. **Nothing here to lose** (no body, or an empty one, against real text) → take the row. **Diverged** → and only then, name it. `sameDoc` compares CANONICALLY, so key order, a `null` attribute written where one was omitted, an empty `marks` array or a re-ordered mark set — all the noise a round trip through jsonb adds — cannot masquerade as an edit. The asymmetry is deliberate: **the silent path may only ever ADD text back, never remove it**, so text-here against blank-there is still a real conflict.
  - **`mergeSyncState` (pure)** — the sync ledger now MERGES with what is on disk instead of overwriting it. Two windows share this browser's storage but not its memory, so a blind write flattened whatever the sibling had learned and manufactured the stale bases that caused the refusals. **A dirty page keeps its OWN base rev** even when the disk holds a fresher one — adopting it would let a stale body commit cleanly past a guard doing its job.
  - **A `storage` listener, for EVERY scope** — signed in or out, a window now learns immediately what its sibling did: merge the ledger, re-read the tree, and announce a changed page body.
  - **`onNotesPagesChanged` → a body EPOCH in the editor key** — an open editor re-reads a page whose body changed underneath it. It is a **REMOUNT, not an effect**: NoteEditor must never grow a "sync content" effect (its header says why, and the guard in `test/notesModule.test.js` now asserts both halves of the key). The store only announces a page this window has no unflushed edit on, and the outgoing instance flushes on unmount — so a remount can never discard work in progress.
  - **The copy, in ONE pure function (`notesConflictLine`)** — “…also changed in another of your windows. Nothing was overwritten — pick which to keep.” with **Keep this one** / **Use the other**. It may say WINDOW or COMPUTER; it may never say a someone. A unit test holds it to that, and a source scan fails the build if any user-facing string in the module implies a second person. The footer line moved with it.
- **Guards, and the two-window one was PROVEN RED FIRST.** `ui-audit/verify-notes.mjs` §23 opens a SECOND browser window on the same storage with the same note open in both, types in window two, and asserts window one re-reads it and that window one's next keystroke does not wipe it. With `attachSiblingListener()` commented out the run goes **167/169 — both checks fail, and the failure text shows window two's sentence gone**. With the fix: **169/169**. `test/notesSync.test.js` adds 30 unit cases over `sameDoc` / `isEmptyDoc` / `judgeConflict` / `mergeSyncState` / the conflict copy.
- **What `V680` still has to confirm (needs a real sign-in, which the sandbox proxy CORS-blocks):** that two SIGNED-IN windows on the same account never raise the bar for identical text, that a genuine divergence still does and still names nobody, and that the parked "(this window's copy)" page appears when "Use the other" is chosen.


### B1384 — The landing page rendered with NO VISIBLE TEXT: every word was gated on a vendor animation library `[Landing / marketing]` (bug) #ui  *(owner report 2026-08-03, provisional NEW-1, MEASURED on his own Chrome at planyr.io/landing/ — 34 `.reveal` elements, zero above 0.398 opacity, `<h1>` at 0, two screenshots showing a dark grid, the nav, the CTA and a scale bar and NOT ONE WORD. Minted **B1384 / V676** via `git fetch origin main && npm run next-id -- --against-main`, LATE, as the last step before push. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open / ⏳ Verify / Done across `landing`, `reveal`, `opacity`, `B658`, `V180`, `V212`: **B658** shipped the current landing build and is the regression's origin, but is Done and archived; this is the defect it introduced, filed on its own number per the owner's framing. Net-new.)*
- **AUDIT-FIRST — THE OWNER'S HYPOTHESIS IS REFUTED, and this is the more important finding.** It is **not** viewport-height dependent. Measured at 1600×521 against the exact live bytes (`curl`'d from planyr.io and diffed byte-identical to the repo file): once the scripts load and the page is scrolled, **0 of 39 elements sit below full opacity**. The short window is fine. Nor was the `h1` "frozen mid-transition": 0.0297 opacity with `translateY(21.3px)` is precisely 1% into the hero's `power3.out` stagger, i.e. the animation had barely *started*, and the page's own `transition: all` reading matches no rule in the file (there is no `transition: all` anywhere in it).
- **THE ACTUAL MECHANISM — a chain of three, and the first link is not the one anyone would have guessed.**
  1. **`.reveal { opacity: 0 }` was the page's RESTING state**, and the only thing that ever set it to 1 was GSAP. So every word on the page was gated on a third-party animation library — permanently, if that library never ran. Measured with the vendor requests blocked: **46 of 53 copy elements at exactly 0.000, `h1` 0.000**, at every viewport size. Same with JS off.
  2. **`build()` ran on `DOMContentLoaded`, which also waits for the DEFERRED 603 KB `three.min.js`** to download *and execute* — deferred scripts run before DCL. The reveals therefore waited on ~718 KB of JavaScript rather than the ~115 KB they actually need. The inline script is the last thing in `<body>`, so there was never a reason to wait at all; it now calls `build()` directly.
  3. **THE TRIGGER, and the real answer: the render-blocking Google Fonts stylesheet.** `<link rel="stylesheet" href="fonts.googleapis.com/…">` is render-blocking, and — the part that actually bit — **a synchronous `<script>` cannot EXECUTE until every preceding stylesheet has resolved.** So a slow, blocked, filtered or ad-blocked fonts CDN froze GSAP at the bottom of `<body>` *even though its bytes had already arrived*. **Measured, unambiguous:** all three vendor scripts fully downloaded at **84 ms**; `DOMContentLoaded` at **12,964 ms**. Thirteen seconds of a wordless page with `window.gsap === null` the whole way. The owner's `max 0.398 / h1 0` reading is that state one instant after the stall released, mid-hero-stagger — which is also why his `h1` read `0.0297` with `translateY(21.3px)` a moment earlier, and why `__landingReady` was already true. **Fixed:** the font stylesheet now loads non-blocking (`media="print"` + an `onload` promotion, with a `<noscript>` fallback), which is safe because the stylesheet has always carried a system-font fallback stack. **After: `DOMContentLoaded` 12,964 ms → 149 ms**, and the reveal animation now actually runs instead of timing out.
- **THE VERIFICATION GAP IS THE OTHER HALF OF THE BUG, and the owner is right that it matters as much.** `__landingReady === true` says the init function *ran*; `ui-audit/verify-landing.mjs` screenshots after a fixed wait at Playwright's default 720 px height. **Neither ever asked the browser what opacity the headline was.** A readiness flag is not a rendering assertion — so both reported success over a blank page.
`[x]` **Shipped 2026-08-03. Parked in ⏳ Verify — `V676`.**
- **THE FIX — the resting state is now legible, and the animation is an enhancement it cannot take away.** `.reveal` and every other start state that hid copy (`.crumb`, `.crumb-sep`, `.spine-vert li`, the calibrate/filed badges, the Gantt bars) rest **fully opaque** in CSS. The hidden pre-animation state is scoped to `html.anim`, a class only the new `<head>` gate adds — and which it **releases** on the first of: `build()` arming it (GSAP is here, the animation starts now), a **1200 ms watchdog**, or the `load` event. Reduced motion never arms it at all, so the copy is simply there. Requirement (b) is now structural: **with the vendor scripts blocked, or JS off entirely, the page reads normally.**
- **The converse hole is closed too:** if the gate already released and GSAP then turns up late, `__landingArmAnim()` returns **false** and `build()` takes the static no-motion path — animating then would snatch words back out from under someone already reading them. Legibility outranks the fade.
- Two `<link rel="preload" as="script">` hints were added for the two vendor files so they start downloading with the document instead of after ~700 lines of markup and CSS, which is what keeps the gate from timing out on an ordinary connection and losing the animation.
- **SHORT WINDOWS ARE NOW FIRST-CLASS, which the rendered check exposed and no static reading would have.** With the words finally on screen at 1600×521 they were *present but obstructed*: a headline sized purely off viewport WIDTH grew to four lines, ran under the 3D mark, and pushed the lede beneath the fixed scale bar. A `max-height: 700px` block caps the headline against viewport height as well, narrows the copy column to clear the mark, and stands down the two decorative furniture pieces (the self-measuring scale bar and the scroll chevron) that are pinned to exactly where the body copy lands on a short window.
- **THE GUARD, PROVEN RED THEN GREEN.** `ui-audit/verify-landing-legibility.mjs` reads **computed opacity** off the real elements at **three viewport heights — 521 (the owner's window), 900, and a 390×844 phone — in three modes: normal (scrolled end-to-end and back to top), starved (the GSAP/ScrollTrigger requests aborted), and JS-disabled.** Against the bytes **currently live on planyr.io**: **✗ 6 of 9 combinations fail, `h1` 0.000.** Against this build: **✓ 9 of 9, every line of copy fully opaque**, with the gate ARMED rather than timed out on desktop and phone — i.e. the animation runs and the legibility floor holds underneath it. It also earned its keep during the fix: it caught the `html.anim` gate stranding the phone-only vertical spine, one edit after the gate was written. The static half runs on every CI build (`test/landingLegibility.test.js`): no un-gated rule may set `opacity: 0` on copy, the gate must be in `<head>`, and `build()` must consult it.
- **Verify: live** — `V676`. The sandbox check ran against the exact deployable bytes at all three viewports in all three modes; what it cannot do is confirm the **deployed edge** serves them (MERGED ≠ LIVE, B877), because the proxy resets the headless browser's connection to planyr.io. `V676` is that post-deploy confirmation.

Had that diagnosis been taken at face value, the fix would have been to re-add machinery that already existed.

So walking into any third project showed a correctly-filtered, entirely empty rail that said "No notebooks yet" — which is why he concluded his notes were gone. And **`setNotebookProject` had NO CALLER ANYWHERE** (the B1316 class): a notebook could be bound only by being born inside a project, and once bound could never be re-bound or set loose. There was also nothing on screen naming the scope, so an empty rail was indistinguishable from an empty account.
- **THE RULE IS NOW WRITTEN DOWN, in the store header, because the owner asked for it to be decided rather than inferred.** A LOOSE notebook is visible **everywhere**, from the Dashboard and from inside every project — a scratch notebook you cannot reach from where you are working is one you stop using. A BOUND notebook is visible from its own project and from the ALL scope. Creating inside a project binds by default; creating from the Dashboard is loose. **Every pre-existing notebook keeps exactly the binding it had** — nothing is re-bound, nothing is orphaned, and an absent `projectId` reads as loose.
