- **The binding is now VISIBLE and CHANGEABLE.** A notebook row shows where it lives — "Loose", or the project's name when that is news rather than a repeat of the header (PANEL-BREVITY) — and the row's context menu (B1367) gains **"Belongs to…"**, an inline panel in the row's own style listing Loose / this project / every project, with the current one marked. No dialog box (house rule). The project you are standing in is offered even when the project list has not resolved it, so filing a note here never depends on a lookup succeeding. A binding whose project no longer resolves is shown AS ITSELF rather than dropped — you cannot change a state you cannot see.
- **Scope is never sticky:** entering a project resets to that project, which is the literal ask. Search obeys the same scope as the rail (widen it and a mis-filed note is findable; narrow it and it answers the question you asked). Binding a notebook AWAY from the project you are looking at widens the scope automatically, so the move reads as a move and not as a disappearance.
- **NO SCHEMA CHANGE, AND THE ROUND TRIP IS ASSERTED RATHER THAN ASSUMED.** The binding rides in the tree blob, which is already what syncs. `test/notesSync.test.js` (+4) pins `mergeTrees` carrying it: bindings on both sides survive, a loose notebook stays loose, the LOCAL binding wins for a notebook on both sides (rule 3, same as its title), and re-binding here while the other device adds a page keeps **both**. The headless run additionally reloads the app and re-reads the binding out of storage.

No banner, no prompt, no indication anything was out of date.
- **WHY IT IS LOAD-BEARING and not cosmetic:** it makes every ship unverifiable from the owner's side. Told a feature is live, he opens the app on another computer, sees no sign of it, and correctly concludes it is not. It did exactly that, and cost most of a session's confusion.
- **TWO INDEPENDENT SIGNALS, one dismissible strip.**
  1. **The definitive one — a route this build cannot resolve.** `route.js` gains `unknownModuleSlug(hash)`: a well-formed slug with no module behind it. The tolerance stays (nothing throws, the fallback still happens, no deep link breaks), but the miss is now REPORTABLE, so the shell can offer a reload instead of pretending the link resolved. This is precisely what `#/notes` looked like from inside a pre-Notes build.
  2. **The general one — the served build stamp.** `vite.config.js` emits `/version.json` = `{ build }` alongside `index.html` (dev serves it from middleware), `public/_headers` gives it `Cache-Control: no-store`, and `src/app/buildSkew.js` re-reads it — twenty seconds after boot, whenever the tab is looked at again, and on a slow interval — and compares against the `__BUILD_ID__` baked into the running bundle. The focus check is the one that matters in practice: a laptop reopened the next morning.
- **⛔ IT IS SILENT WHENEVER IT CANNOT KNOW, and that is the property most of the tests are about.** A missing file, a 404, an offline network, a non-JSON body, a dev build on either side — every one resolves to "no opinion", never to a false "you are out of date". A skew notice that cries wolf gets dismissed by reflex, and then the one that matters is invisible too.
- **It never reloads on its own.** A thin dismissible strip with a Reload button (`reloadFresh`, the same cache-busting reload the stale-chunk guard uses, so it actually lands on the new build) — never a modal and never a forced navigation, because the user may be mid-sentence. A dismissal is scoped to the build it was dismissed FOR, so one shrug does not silence every future deploy.

### B1352 — Convert `renderElPx` from a module-level function to a `React.memo` component `[Site Planner / UI]` (task) #site-planner #perf #ui  *(filed 2026-07-31 from the speed program's "RECORDED, NOT FOR THIS PR" list — **filed deliberately, NOT implemented**. Minted via `--against-main`. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open + ⏳ Verify + Done across `memo`, `reconcil`, `renderElPx`, `curbEdgesOf`: nothing covers element-level memoisation. Net-new; distinct from B1351, which is the panel.)*
- There is currently **ZERO `React.memo` anywhere in `src/`**, so React sees a flat array of host elements with fresh props and diffs all of them — 100% reconciliation for the ~2 of 194 states that change during a pan. Corroborated by measurement: `ui-audit/diagnose-pan-commits.mjs` records **193,303 DOM mutation records across 60 pointermoves** even after B1345 cut the node count by 63%.
- **Two preconditions, both load-bearing:** (1) `useCallback` on its four handlers — they are fresh arrows per render, so a memo without this is a no-op; (2) replace the whole-`allEls` argument with **resolved neighbours**, because an element's render genuinely depends on its neighbours through `curbEdgesOf` / `bumpsAlongLength` / `dockSidesFor`. A naive memo on `el` alone produces **STALE CURBS** when an adjacent element moves. Model that dependency explicitly.
`[x]` **SHIPPED 2026-07-31 — and it does NOT move the wheel-zoom number. Both halves of that sentence are measured.**
- **BUILT.** `renderElPx` now renders through `ElNode`, a module-scope `React.memo` component (the first `React.memo` in `src/`). Both preconditions are in: the five element handlers are bundled behind an identity-stable latest-ref indirection (`useCallback` was rejected — these close over a large shifting slice of a 25k-line component, and a missed dependency is a STALE HANDLER, which is worse than a slow render), and the whole-`allEls` argument is replaced by `resolveElNeighbors`, a per-element resolved record of the four things an element's drawing genuinely reads from its neighbours (curb edges, dog-ear bumps, the dimension slide range, and a bump-out's host style). `sel` and the suppressed-dimension Set are likewise passed as pre-resolved booleans, so a selection change re-renders two elements instead of all of them. **No element type was excluded** — the neighbour dependency is modelled exactly, so none had to be.
- **PIXEL PARITY: byte-identical.** `ui-audit/verify-stall-lod-parity.mjs` across five zoom rungs plus the exported sheet — IDENTICAL at every rung, same node counts, same stall counts, zero segment drift on the PDF path. B1345's bar, met with nothing spent against it.
- **⛔ IT MOVES THE TARGET GESTURE BY LESS THAN THE NOISE FLOOR, and the reason is structural, not a shortfall.** Interleaved A/B, 5 pairs at 4x throttle: wheel median **166.6 (base) vs 166.6 (new)**, script mean 4,883 vs 4,794 ms — against a within-arm spread of 149.9–200 ms and 4,021–6,055 ms. The floor is roughly ±20%. **Why:** `f2p` changes identity whenever the view changes and every element's pixel geometry genuinely changes with it, so the memo misses on 100% of elements during a pan or a zoom **by construction**. That is now written at the top of `ElNode` so nobody re-derives it. **B1360** owns what would actually move it.
- **THE WORK IS GENUINELY GONE, even though the frame cannot see it.** CPU profile, same gesture, before vs after: `edgeAbutsPaving` + `curbEdgesOf` **4.8% → 2.1%** of script self-time. The same resolved record now feeds the yield/impervious math (`curbAreaFrom`), which was re-running the O(n²) adjacency scan per element per render whenever the Yield panel was docked.
- **KEPT, on that evidence and not on the theory:** the picture is provably identical, provably less work is done for it, and the boundary is the mechanism B1360 needs. Dropping it would mean deliberately re-adding an O(n²) scan per element per frame.
- Verify: live
- Origin: filed 2026-07-31 from chat (speed program, recorded item (b))

- **THE OWNER'S REPORT, verbatim:** *"fix the fact that when I shrink the trailer parking, it shrinks from both sides."*
- **ROOT CAUSE, confirmed against the code before a line was written (AUDIT-FIRST).** `dockZones.layoutZoneByKind` built the zone centre as `b.c + u·center + tan·alongShift`, and the ONLY along-wall term was `alongShift` — which exists to carry the B492 corner-bump-out trim and is non-zero only when a court is pulled in between bump-outs. The LENGTH came from the user (`alongLen` → `zoneAlongSpan`); the CENTRE did not. So the length changed and the centre did not, and both ends travelled inward by half the reduction. It is not an arithmetic error: the model stored a SPAN WITH NO ANCHOR, and there was no field in which "which end did you grab" could be written down.
- **REPRODUCED LIVE FIRST, on the owner's own geometry, before the fix** — his real "Concept D — Sylvestri Retail" rows (site `sms4zs8unbkg`), building `e1454698mwpaoj` (867.94 × 300, a 55 ft bump-out at each end, clear face 757.94) with court `e1454699mwpaoj` and trailer `e1454796yyuqqs`, seeded logged-out and driven in headless Chromium. Grabbing the row's east end and pulling it in: **the west end moved 59.95 px and the east end moved 59.95 px** — both ends, half the reduction each, exactly as reported. Note what this proves about the class: **not one element on that plan carries an `alongLen`.** This defect needs no poisoned data and no history — it is what a clean plan does the first time a zone is shrunk.
- **THE FIX — the override is an ANCHORED span.** Three fields, of which only the first already existed, so nothing migrates and an unstamped plan renders byte-identically: `alongLen` (the length, unchanged) · `alongAnchor` (`-1` the −along end held, `+1` the +along end, `0` centred — absent ⇒ 0 ⇒ the old behaviour) · `alongOff` (feet from the chain default's corresponding reference to the held one). `anchoredAlongSpan` resolves the three into a length and a centre shift; `layoutZoneByKind` folds that into the `tan` term it already had, **COMPOSING with the bump-out `alongShift` rather than replacing it**. Because the anchor is a REFERENCE and not a world position, it survives everything the zone is derived through: shrink the host and the held end tracks the wall it is bonded to, grow it back and the span springs out, add a bump-out and the whole chain slides together.
- **The gesture is read off the geometry, not off the handle.** An edge drag pins the opposite edge exactly and a corner drag pins the opposite corner, so `alongAnchorFromDrag` takes whichever end moved less; both ends moving (a re-centre) reads as centred, the conservative answer. **B1123's two intent gates are untouched and still decide WHETHER anything is pinned** — a depth-only drag, a host refit, a rotation, a relayout and the load-time heal all still pin nothing. This adds only WHERE.
- **A TYPED length keeps the current anchor** instead of silently re-centring; clearing the override clears the anchor with it (intent withdrawn is intent gone).
- **THE AUDIT, all four resizable bonded zones, as asked — and it was not only the trailer:**
  - **Trailer parking** — defective. Fixed.
  - **Buffer** (and any menu-appended outward layer) — defective by the identical mechanism, same `opts.alongs[i]` path. Fixed by the same rule.
  - **Truck court** — defective, and doubly so: its typed length re-centred on the clear face, AND its along-edge drag was discarded outright (`resized.truckCourt ? null : …`), so it could not be anchored at all. It now pins and anchors like every other zone, still capped to the clear bump-out face, so **B492 is unchanged** — an anchored court can never slide onto a bump-out, and its whole outward stack still tracks it.
  - **Side parking** — **already anchored correctly**, and needed no change: `dogEar.sideParkAlongRun` records `{ run, alongShift }`, so the along-CENTRE the drag produced is carried through beside the run instead of being re-derived to the middle of the wall. That is exactly the shape this item gives the dock zones. Asserted in the new suite so a future edit cannot quietly lose it.
  - **Wall strips** (sidewalk / landscape) — fully derived from the span rule, no user length at all, so there is no anchor to lose. Asserted too.
- **SEQUENCED AGAINST THE IN-FLIGHT ALONG-RUN WORK, deliberately, and it is the reason the shape is what it is.** That work (**B1123** ⏳ Verify — the Goose Creek trailers frozen at 708/707 against 712 ft courts; **B1124** + `normalizeHostRuns` — the Colorado court and parking carrying a different building's 708.58; **B1340 ×2** — the Sylvestri end parking stuck at 205/80 against 260/259 ft sidewalks) **has already landed on `main` and is the base this branch is cut from.** It made a bonded child's span DERIVED-unless-explicitly-stamped, and the anchor is therefore built INTO that override's shape from the start rather than bolted beside it: `alongAnchor` / `alongOff` live on the same element, are written by the same gesture gate, are dropped by the same heals that drop `alongLen`, and are re-clamped on every host change by the same rule. Nothing here re-opens or weakens any of the three.
- **The heals had to move in the same commit or they would have fought the canvas.** All three `layoutZoneByKind` call sites in `siteModel.js` (`normalizeStrandedZones` · `normalizeZoneAlongLen` · `normalizeHostRuns`) now carry `anchors`/`offs`, and `normalizeHostRuns` resolves the court head through the same `anchoredAlongSpan`. Because **B1340's tear detector IS the healer's own diff**, a heal that ignored the anchor would have reported a permanent tear against a canvas laying the zone correctly. A dropped length now drops its anchor with it.
- **Guards.** `test/zoneAlongAnchor.test.js` (47) drives the real `layoutZoneByKind` through a helper that mirrors `relayoutSide`/`courtBumpOpts` line for line, on the owner's flat building AND his rotated one (540 × 1041 at 33.959°): shrink from each end · grow from each end · a second drag from the OTHER end (the case a bare offset cannot express) · a typed length preserving the anchor · composition with a bump-out trim · a host resize · rotations at 0/17.5/90/178.543/269/359° · re-clamping instead of sliding off the wall · a pre-fix baseline proving the centred model moves both ends · the four-zone audit · the three heals leaving an anchored zone identical. **Mutation-checked: 15 of them go red with the anchor removed.** `e2e/dock-zone-anchor.spec.js` (4) drives the REAL render and the REAL drag on the owner's seeded rows; **3 of 4 go red on the pre-fix model, reproducing the 59.95 px double-shrink.** New fixture `ui-audit/fixtures/sylvestri-concept-d.json` (his 22 real elements, verbatim).
- Verify: live
- Origin: filed 2026-07-31 from chat

### B1355 — Measurements print as giant dots with no number, because the export inherits the screen's zoom level-of-detail `[Site Planner / export]` (bug) #site-planner #export #ui #markup  *(owner chat 2026-07-31, provisional NEW-1, verbatim: "fix the fact that my measurements on the Sylvestri site looked like this when I print — they should not look like that big, obviously." Minted **B1355 / V666** via `git fetch origin main && npm run next-id -- --against-main`, LATE — as the last step before push; code, tests and the e2e spec keep the provisional `NEW-1` label. **AMENDS the measurement-annotation strand that shipped in PR #866 — filed there as B1151 / B1152 / B1153 (V534); that PR's TITLE announces B1144–B1146, which is stale and is the exact defect B1177 exists to stop, so read it by its filed ids.** DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open + ⏳ Verify + Done across the export/LOD/measurement families: **B1085** is the closest by far and is deliberately NOT re-opened as a recurrence (see below); **B939 / B942** put measurement labels on the shared zoom-out declutter and are correct for the CANVAS and untouched; **B1152** made that threshold user-settable and this item scopes it to the canvas rather than reversing it; **B1153** composed the summary chip this now guarantees reaches paper; **B1047** made the export GEOMETRY view-independent; **B1174** is a chrome-hit-test item on the same chips, not a print item. None of them owns the export INHERITING a declutter decision as policy. Net-new.)*
`[x]` *(implemented 2026-07-31; parked for the signed-in pass on the owner's own Sylvestri plan — see **V666**.)* The owner's exported sheet showed each length measurement as TWO large filled orange discs joined by a short stub, twice on the plan, and NO value label anywhere. A measurement printed without its number is worthless on an exhibit — the number is the one thing the measurement exists to communicate.
- Verify: live — **V666**
- Origin: filed 2026-07-31 from chat (NEW-1)

**AUDIT-FIRST — the reported root cause was traced against the code before anything was patched, and it holds on every point.** `exportSheet.js`'s `buildExportSvgRaw` CLONES the live `<svg>` and strips only `clone.querySelectorAll('[data-export="skip"]')`, so an export is **by construction exactly what was on screen at that instant**. Two independent things then collided on a sheet printed from a whole-site zoom:
1. **The VALUE was zoom-gated.** The summary chip renders only if `measureLabelVisible` passes, and B1152 had just made that threshold settable per measurement. The owner was zoomed out to see his whole multi-parcel site — the normal thing to do before printing — so the labels were below the gate and simply **were not in the DOM to clone**.
2. **The ENDPOINT MARKERS had no gate at all** and were sized in constant screen px (`<circle r={3}>`), so they kept their size against a drawing that had shrunk to fit several hundred acres. Geometry survived, the number did not, and the marker did not scale.

**⚠ ONE CORRECTION TO THE DIAGNOSIS, because it changes what the fix had to be — and it is why this is NOT a B1085 recurrence.** B1085 already gave the label tier its own frame: on an export pass every gate reads the SHEET's own px-per-foot (`exportLabelScale.js`), not the live zoom. That fix works exactly as specified and still holds — two exports of one plan at different zooms make identical label decisions, which this item's second e2e case now asserts directly. But re-framing a gate is not the same as lifting it: on a several-hundred-acre site the **sheet's own** scale is *also* below the floor, so the label was correctly-but-fatally decluttered off the paper. B1085 closed "the sheet inherits the SCREEN's scale"; this closes "the sheet applies a DECLUTTER POLICY at all". Different decision, same line of code, so it takes its own number.

**THE PRINCIPLE, now written into the code and the folder pointer: AN EXPORT IS A DOCUMENT, NOT A SCREENSHOT.** Level-of-detail gating exists so the canvas stays readable while you work; none of that reasoning survives onto a sheet that will be read at full size on paper.

**(1) THE VALUE ALWAYS PRINTS.** `measureLabelVisible(m, ppf, { …, sheet })` returns true on an export pass regardless of the shared floor, the Standards default, or B1152's per-measurement pin — that pin governs the **canvas only**, and says so in its own docstring. The renderer passes `sheet: labelFrame.sheet`, the flag B1085's own frame already computes, so there is no second notion of "are we exporting".

**THE AUDIT OF EVERY OTHER ZOOM-GATED ANNOTATION THAT CAN REACH THE SHEET, with the line drawn and the reason stated.** The useful distinction is what the gate is ASKING:
- **A PURE ZOOM FLOOR** — a bare px-per-foot threshold with no geometry term — asks *"is the user zoomed in enough?"* That is screen decluttering and has no meaning on paper. **Lifted.**
- **A PHYSICAL-ROOM TEST** — `detailLabelVisible(featureFt, ppf)`, `pondParamLabelVisible(bandFt, ppf)`, the chip's minimum-edge guard — asks *"is there room for this number on the thing it labels?"* Since B1085 that question is already re-asked at the **sheet's** own scale, which is the right question for a document. **Kept.**

| Annotation | Gate | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| **Measurement value chip** | pure floor + B1152's per-measurement pin | **CHANGED — lifted on the sheet.** The number IS the object: strip it and nothing meaningful is left, which is the whole bug. |
| Measurement per-edge segment lengths | `detailLabelVisible(segFt, ppf)` | **Kept.** Physical-room, re-asked at sheet scale. An edge with no room for type cannot carry a number without overprinting, and the headline value is separately guaranteed. |
| Element dimension callouts (buildings) | `dimCalloutVisible(ppf)` — a pure floor | **Kept, deliberately.** Unlike a measurement, a building still prints its own centred name/area label, so geometry-without-a-dimension is a labelled footprint, not an anonymous mark. They also ride the collision pool (`suppressedDimIds`), so forcing them on a whole-site sheet buys illegible overprint, not information. |
| Road / paving width callouts | `detailLabelVisible(dimW, ppf)` | **Kept.** Physical-room, as above; the road still prints as pavement. |
| Pond parameter labels (berm tag, floor/WS elevations) | `pondParamLabelVisible(bandFt, ppf)` | **Kept.** The label is drawn INSIDE a band — a band thinner than the type cannot hold it. The pond's own name/area label is `mustLabel` and always prints (B1147). |
| Setback chips | `setbackChipsVisible(ppf)` | **No change possible — they already never print.** They live in the `data-export="skip"` handle layer, because a chip is an editing affordance. The setback still prints as its dashed inset ring. |
| Parcel acreage chips | **no gate at all** | **No change needed.** They always draw and always print (restyled to haloed exhibit text by `restyleExportClone`). Checked because the brief asked; nothing to do. |
| Easement centroid labels | `dimCalloutVisible(ppf)` — a pure floor | **Kept, flagged.** Same reasoning as the building dimension: the hatched fill and the centerline geometry always print, so the easement is never anonymous. If the owner wants these on paper too, that is a one-line follow-on and the seam is now in place. |

**(2) THE ENDPOINT MARKERS ARE AN EDITING AFFORDANCE, AND ON PAPER THEY BECOME DRAFTING TERMINATORS.** The vertex discs now carry `data-export="skip"` — belt-and-braces, so they are gone from the sheet even in the fallback where no export pass runs — and on the export pass a **length or polylength** is terminated by the architectural 45° tick at each end of the run (`terminatorTicks`, sized through `labelK` so it holds one physical size on paper), which is what a length annotation looks like on a real exhibit. An **area** is a closed outline and gets neither discs nor ticks; a **COUNT's numbered markers ARE content** — they say which items were counted and in what order — so they print untouched, exactly as the brief requires. Nothing is blanket-skipped.

**(3) THE INVARIANT, ASSERTED IN CODE.** *A measurement must never print its geometry without its value.* `enforceMeasureValueOnSheet` runs on the clone immediately after the chrome strip: any measurement group carrying no value text is **removed from the sheet entirely** rather than printed as anonymous marks, and **LOUD-FAILURE** — the drop returns its ids and raises an owner-facing warning, never a silent trim. It is a removal, not a repair, on purpose: by the time the clone exists a number could only be fabricated, and a wrong figure on an exhibit is worse than a missing annotation. This is the backstop for the case (1) is meant to make impossible — a layout hiccup, or a `flushSync` that cannot run mid-lifecycle, which is precisely how the label re-frame can fall through.

**(4) THE WIDER CONSTANT-SCREEN-PIXEL AUDIT — everything found, and what was done with it.** The markers were one instance; there were five more that reach the sheet.
- **Measurement vertex discs** (`r={3}`) — the reported bug. **Fixed** (skip + terminators).
- **Measurement grab layers** — the fat transparent hit polygon/polyline (`strokeWidth 14`) and the count's transparent hit circles (`r 12`). Invisible, so not a visual defect, but constant screen px and pure editing affordance. **Now `data-export="skip"`.**
- **Semantic markup labels** — `utilRoute`'s fitting glyph and route label, `traced`/`infwater`'s label, `encumbrance`'s per-call bearing/distance and its centroid label. All authored as literal `fontSize="8"…"11"` with no `labelK`, so on a wide-zoom sheet they printed several times their intended size — the same defect as the discs, one layer out. **Fixed:** every one now rides `labelK`, which is exactly 1 on screen, so nothing on the canvas moves.
- **`traced` / `infwater` vertex marks** (`r={3}`, `4×4` rect) — same class. **Fixed** (scaled by `labelK`; they are authored marks, so they scale rather than disappear).
- **In-progress tool drafts** — the measure draft (both branches), the draft polygon and the draft rect all render constant-px dots and type and were NOT export-skipped. A half-drawn shape is never document content and the Export menu is reachable mid-draw. **Now `data-export="skip"`.**
- **NOT changed, recorded for the next reader:** the building poché hatch is a `<pattern>` in user space and therefore scales with the drawing, so it is not in this class — it merely LOOKS wrong on a synthetic 8,000-ft test building. The sheet furniture group is deliberately exempt from the stroke-thinning pass and carries its own hairlines (pre-existing, correct).

**PROOF, and it is mutation-checked both ways.** `test/measureSheet.test.js` (23 cases) covers the pure halves — the sheet override against the floor, the Standards default and a per-measurement pin; terminator geometry at four orientations plus every degenerate input; the invariant's verdict and its DOM enforcement; and source guards on the wiring. `e2e/measure-export-lod.spec.js` is the guard the brief asked for and it drives the **real built sheet**: the defect exists only in the clone, so a new `window.__plannerExportSvg` hook (behind the same `window.__PLANYR_E2E` gate the road-network and geo-map hooks use, never present in production) hands the spec the actual export markup. It draws a genuinely large site — zoomed out BEFORE drawing, because a toy plan exports above the floor and hides the defect entirely — puts a Length, a Polylength and a Count on it, zooms past the gate, exports, and asserts every measurement carries its value, that **zero** endpoint discs survive, that each open run carries exactly two terminators, and that the count's numbered markers ARE present. A second case exports the same plan from a wide and a close zoom and asserts the sheet says the same thing (B1085's property, now guarded). **Proven RED on the pre-fix code both ways:** restoring the discs fails on *"editing discs reached the sheet"*; restoring the inherited label gate fails on *"a measurement was withheld from the sheet"* — which is the invariant firing, i.e. the owner's exact sheet minus the anonymous dots.

**THE BUNDLE BUDGET, measured the way B1178 requires rather than read off the report.** The raw audit shows the site route +19.1 KB over baseline, but a stash-and-rebuild of this branch's own base measures +17.1 KB with none of this work applied — that is B1178's unreproducible baseline, not this item. **This change's honest attribution is +2.0 KB on the site route, +2.2 KB total, +2.1 KB on the largest chunk, +0.0 KB on Notes** — all inside the headroom band with 26.6 KB left before the ceiling. **Why the residual stays:** `measureSheet.js` is ~1 KB of pure decision code that BOTH the boot path (the renderer) and the lazy export chunk import, so by the mixed-tier rule in the folder pointer it is hoisted into their common ancestor and no `import()` can move it; the rest is render-path JSX inside the one `SitePlanner.jsx` component that `largestChunkBytes`'s own note already names as the indivisible floor. B1064 owns closing that gap.

**WHAT WAS VERIFIED HERE, AND WHAT IS LEFT.** Lint (0 errors) · the full unit suite (7 544) · build · the bundle audit · the doc gates are all green, and the e2e guard ran headless in this sandbox with a screenshot of the built sheet checked by eye: the two runs read as dimensioned annotations with tick terminators and their numbers (`6,591′` and `6,650′ · 2 segments`), at a sane size against the building. What the sandbox cannot do is the owner's own plan — `V666` carries the signed-in pass on "Concept D — Sylvestri Retail" (`sms4zs8unbkg`), to both PDF and PNG.

Minted via `git fetch origin main && npm run next-id -- --against-main`. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open + ⏳ Verify + Done across `perf-harness`, `perf-scenario`, `frameMedian`, `frame sampling`, `budget`: **B1040** built the budget system, **B1086** is the hidden-tab frame-sampling trap (a different defect of the same instrument, already fixed and still load-bearing here), **B1144** replaced the hand-pinned ceilings, **B1163** is the allowlist defect, **B1178** is the unreproducible bundle baseline. None of them is about the SCENE or the GESTURE the harness measures. Net-new.)*
`[x]` **Shipped 2026-07-31. Parked in ⏳ Verify — `V663`.** The benchmark now measures the owner's real plan, with a drag that actually pans, on a machine slow enough to tell two builds apart.
- **THREE independent defects, all live at once, any one of which made the green 16.7 ms frame budget meaningless:**
  1. **The scene had the expensive work taken out.** The hand-authored reference scenario's road was a `{type:'road', cx, cy, w, h}` RECTANGLE — no `pts`, no `vtx` — and it carried **no ponds** and no polygon elements. `roadNet` / `teeJunctionsOf` / `driveJunctionsOf` / `weldJunctionsOf` / `dissolveRings` and all 1,390 lines of `roadGeometry.js`, plus `detentionRules.js` (2,122 lines), `floodplainMitigation.js` (1,233 lines) and the pond ledger, **executed zero times in the benchmark that certifies them.**
  2. **The gesture did nothing.** The scripted drag pressed at the exact canvas CENTRE, which on any real plan lands on an ELEMENT, so the view never panned. Measured head to head on the real plan: **604 DOM mutations** for the centre press versus **641,730** for the identical drag started on bare canvas. The sampler saw a clean 60 fps for both and reported the first as a 16.7 ms median.
  3. **One measurement point, with no dynamic range.** A fast headless CPU at dpr 1 renders the heavier scene at 60 fps too, so an optimisation that halves the work still reads 16.7 → 16.7.
- **Fixed.** The scenario is **derived** from `ui-audit/fixtures/goose-creek-plan1copy.json` (62 elements, 6 centerline roads with 14 arc vertices, 2 ponds, 6 parcels, the plan's own settings) — derived rather than copied, so it cannot drift from the fixture. The press point is chosen to be bare canvas, and `idleGestureFault` REFUSES a sample whose view transform never moved. `--cpu-throttle N` / `--dpr N` emulate a slower machine; under either, every metric is MEASURED BUT NOT JUDGED, and the plausibility floor drops from 30 fps to 2 fps because under deliberate throttling slowness is the measurand. At 1× the floor is exactly the committed 30, unchanged.
- **A DOM NODE COUNT per zoom level** was added — the harness counted leaflet tile requests and nothing else, so the size of the thing React reconciles every frame was invisible to every budget.
- **`npm run perf:ratchet -- --metric runtime.* --from-harness <a real --json run>`** is now the only way a runtime `measured` / `seededFrom` moves. It refuses an emulated run, a faulted sample, a drag that never panned, and any metric without `seededFrom` (`peakHeapMB` / `aerialTileRequests` hold PRODUCTION figures a sandbox floor must never overwrite).
- **THE NUMBERS GOT WORSE, AS EXPECTED, AND ARE REPORTED RATHER THAN SMOOTHED:** canvas DOM nodes **1197 → 2822** at the innermost rung (+136%); peak JS heap **41.7 → 68.8–98.0 MB**; drag median/p90 **16.7 / 16.7 → 16.7 / 16.7** (3 reps) — unchanged at 1×, because this container renders the heavier scene at 60 fps too. At 4× throttle: pan **14.8 fps (49.9 ms median)**, wheel zoom **6.4 fps — 199.9 ms median, 250 ms p90**, the first reproduction in this repo of the owner's *"I scroll out and it takes probably a whole second."*
- **NO CEILING WAS RAISED and no baseline was re-recorded** to accommodate any of it; **B1178 remains open and unexplained.** The two frame metrics were re-seeded through the named ratchet step at their unchanged value, so the provenance moves on the record.

`[x]` **Closed 2026-07-31 as REFUTED, with the instrument that refuted it. Parked in ⏳ Verify — `V665`.** The diagnosis was reasoned from the code and explicitly not observed; measured, the second render is not there.
- **The claim:** `setView` runs synchronously in the pointermove handler (React 18 batches it → render 1); `setCursor` is scheduled onto the NEXT animation frame by `scheduleFrameJob("cursor")`, a separate task React cannot batch with the pan → render 2. A straight 2× on the hottest path.
- **Measured: 1.02–1.10 DOM-commit batches per pointermove event** (60 events: 1.10 · 120: 1.05 · 240: 1.02). The apparent "2×" in a first pass was **the measuring driver's own artefact** — Playwright's `mouse.move(..., {steps: 2})` dispatches two pointermove events per call.
- **The mechanism is wrong, specifically.** Of 62 batches that touched the coordinate readout, **61 were batched WITH the pan commit** and exactly **1** was a commit of its own. Chrome dispatches `pointermove` before that frame's rAF callbacks, and React 18's scheduler flushes both pending updates in one render pass, so the rAF-scheduled `setCursor` lands in the same commit as the `setView`. The registration effect accounted for **1** batch across the whole gesture.
- **No fix shipped, deliberately** — there is no phantom to fix, and folding the cursor into a ref would have been a real change made for a measured non-reason.
- **What DID come out of it:** `ui-audit/diagnose-pan-commits.mjs`, the repo's first commit-counting instrument, which needs no instrumented build (a MutationObserver's callback fires once per delivery batch; batches are then classified by what they touched). It records the number that IS real: **193,303 DOM mutation records across 60 pointermoves** even after B1345 — i.e. full reconciliation of every element per frame, which is **B1352**'s territory, not this one's.
- Verify: live
- Origin: owner speed-program dispatch, 2026-07-31 chat

### B1340 (×2) — The bonded-assembly tear, at the root: a bonded child's FULL GEOMETRY — position AND span — is DERIVED `[Site Planner / Persistence]` (bug) #site-planner #persistence #sync  *(root-cause dive, 2026-07-31, ordered after EIGHT merged PRs failed to stop this. `[x]` **Shipped 2026-07-31. Parked in ⏳ Verify — `V660`.**

  - **WHAT THE FIRST FIX DID CLOSE, confirmed by the owner on the live rows — keep it.** The write is genuinely atomic now: every row of an assembly shares ONE `updated_at` to the microsecond (`e1454731yyuqqs` all at `18:31:51.768853`; `e1454713mwpaoj` all at `18:31:11.854153`). The host-forty-seconds-ahead-of-its-children shape is gone. The derived POSITION is holding too — see the perpendicular offsets below.
  - **WHAT WAS STILL BROKEN.** "Concept D — Sylvestri Retail", site `sms4zs8unbkg`. Building `e1454731yyuqqs` (`w 566.8, h 200, rot 0`) had just had its DEPTH taken 220 → 200.
