Its two end PARKING fields `e1454734`/`e1454736` read `w 205` against that same 260 ft wall — while their perpendicular offsets (`cx −212.81` / `−849.61` = host ± 318.4 = 283.4 + 5 + 30) were **exact**. Building `e1454713mwpaoj` (`h 199`): sidewalks `h 259`, end parkings `w 80`. Eighty feet of parking on a 259 ft wall is what the owner was looking at.
  - **THE READ, and it is the owner's.** The first fix made a child's POSITION derived and the write atomic. It did **not** make the child's SIZE derived, so the along-wall RUN of a side-parking row stayed a stored value that outlived a host resize. That is the same *preserve-once-touched* rule behind the Goose Creek `alongLen` pinning and the Colorado court/parking carrying another building's 708.58, and it was the single biggest remaining source of these reports.
  - **⚠ ONE CORRECTION TO THE DIAGNOSTIC, so nobody chases it later.** The report reads the children's lower `rev` (5 vs the host's 8; 7 vs 9) as "three revisions behind the host they were written with". `rev` is a PER-ROW counter — it counts how many times that row has been written, not a shared clock — so an assembly's rows can never be expected to share one, and rev-lag is not by itself evidence of staleness. It does not change the conclusion: the geometry is unambiguous on its own (a 205 ft field beside a 260 ft sidewalk on the same wall of the same host), and that is what the detector now keys on.
  - **THE FIX.** The invariant now covers a child's FULL geometry. `sideParkAlongRun` (`lib/dogEar.js`) drops "preserve once touched" entirely: **no stamp ⇒ the run and the along-wall centre ARE the span default, in either direction**; a `sideParkFit` stamp is the ONLY intent that counts, it is written only by a gesture aimed at that field, it is **re-clamped to the host's current wall on every host change**, and dragging the field back onto the default CLEARS it. So a deliberate length still survives every refit — it is RECORDED rather than inferred from geometry, which is exactly the difference between intent and staleness. `assemblyIntegrity` reports `dw`/`dh`/`span` alongside `dx`/`dy`/`dist`, and a **tear is now a disagreement past tolerance on EITHER axis**, so a wrong-LENGTH child pages us like a wrong-PLACE one. `storage.js`'s load-seam watcher reads a `run` delta as well as a centre delta, so a span-only repair can no longer be a repair nobody can see.
  - **MIGRATION, deliberate and one-way.** A legacy plan carrying an unstamped short run is re-derived to its wall on the next open — nobody can distinguish an old accident from an old intent, and the owner has ruled that a field matching its wall is the right default. It is LOUD (`assembly-tear-detected`, span half) and undoable.
  - **CONTRACTS AMENDED IN THE SAME COMMIT, none deleted quietly:** `test/wallKidDrift.test.js`'s "the east field does not move ALONG the wall, ever", `test/hostRunHeal.test.js`'s "a run that FITS is never touched", and `e2e/wall-kid-drift.spec.js`'s two owner-plan cases were all written from the earlier B1039 amendment. Each is rewritten to assert the new rule in BOTH directions (recorded survives · unrecorded follows · recorded is re-clamped when the host shrinks under it) rather than removed.
  - **PROOF.** `test/assemblyIntegrity.test.js` gains the depth-resize reproduction the owner asked for plus a span-only detector case; `e2e/assembly-tear-detector.spec.js` gains a third case that drives the REAL depth grip on the canvas and asserts every bonded child's run follows **in-session, before any reload**. Both were proven RED with the old rule restored — the e2e one fails with exactly the reported symptom, *"spans a different wall from its own sidewalk"*. Note for anyone extending it: a SHRINK proves nothing (an over-length run was already clamped); the case has to GROW the wall back, and it has to put parking on the wall whose length is the depth, or it measures nothing and passes either way.
 A building's bonded children can no longer sit anywhere other than where the building puts them: the position is re-derived from the host at every boundary where a child can arrive without it, so a transaction that applies to half an assembly is invisible instead of destructive — and it now reports itself instead of healing in silence.
- Verify: live
- Origin: owner root-cause request, 2026-07-31 chat ("I feel like I just had this issue yesterday and I thought we fixed it… maybe we just put a band aid on it instead of figuring out the root cause")

**THE EVIDENCE (owner-supplied, from the live rows — not re-derived).** Site `sms7v3ua7ksy`, building `e7373vqgilf` at `cx -411.03, cy -709.35, w 260, h 708.58, rot 354.818`, rev 20, `updated_at 15:58:45.475`. Its seven bonded children (`e7374` truck court · `e7375`/`e7376` north sidewalk + parking · `e7377`/`e7378` west sidewalk + parking · `e7379`/`e7380` south sidewalk + parking) were every one of them displaced from the host-implied position by the SAME vector, ≈ +267 ft east / +4 ft north — and every one is rev 21 or 22 at `15:59:25–26`, **forty seconds after the host**. An earlier snapshot of the same site had `e7377` at `cx -540.29`, correct for the host's current position. So the children were re-written LATER, to the pre-undo coordinates, and won.

**THE ROOT CAUSE.** A bonded child's world position is **REDUNDANT**: it is fully determined by the host's frame (across the wall) and bounded by wall overlap (along it). That one fact is stored **twice** — once in the host row, once in each child row — and the N+1 rows are written, revved, accepted-or-refused, echoed, journaled, folded and healed **independently**. Redundant state that is updated by independent transactions is guaranteed to disagree under some interleaving. Every one of the eight PRs closed a specific interleaving; none removed the redundancy, so the bad state stayed **representable**, and something always found the next interleaving. Two named amplifiers made it invisible: (a) the load-time heal has repaired this since B1097 **in total silence**, so a check that reloaded before it measured saw a clean plan and reported "fixed" (the owner's "looks like it just fixed itself somehow again"); (b) that heal was **never persisted** — measured here in a headless repro, a planted tear rendered correctly and was still on disk, byte for byte, four seconds later.

**THE ENUMERATION — every path that can write, revert, re-apply or echo a child independently of its host** (the deliverable the dive was asked for; `A` = goes through the atomic group path, `—` = bypasses it):

*Write (`lib/elementSync.js`)*
| # | Path | Atomic? | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `reconcile()` diff → `enqueue` → `flush()` | **A** | `closeAssemblies` + `freshen` + `batchSpansAssembly` → `p_atomic` |
| 2 | `closeAssemblies` sibling fold | **A** | folds only members whose LIVE data disagrees with the shadow — correct, but it means a legitimate batch can hold ONE member |
| 3 | `processResults` conflict → LWW re-commit | **—** when ≤1 member is refused | re-closes at the next flush; **this is the ~40 s backoff retry in the evidence** |
| 4 | `processResults` assembly-split re-enqueue (B1116) | **—** same | per refused member |
| 5 | `onAtomicRollback` (B1117) | **A** | whole batch re-queued |
| 6 | `onTransportFailure` re-queue | **A** | whole batch |
| 7 | `restore(kind,id,el)` — the B673 "Restore" toast | **—** | enqueues ONE element, immediate flush |
| 8 | `pendingOps()` + `keepaliveCommit` (unload / `beforeunload` / `visibilitychange`) | **—** | **hard bypass: no closure, no `freshen`, no atomic flag** |
| 9 | delete cascade | **—** by design | `closeAssemblies` skips `cls === "delete"`; TOMBSTONE-DELETES owns it, and a delete cannot leave a DISPLACED child |
| 10 | whole-doc mirror / cloud blob save | n/a | assembly-whole by construction; still a PROPAGATION vector for an already-torn canvas |

*Read / echo*
| # | Path | Atomic? | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| 11 | `applyRemoteRow` → `upsert` → `applyRemoteInstr` | **—** | one row at a time; the largest class |
| 12 | `applyRemoteRow` derived-yield branch | **—** | **had no `foreignAuthor` gate** — the correction B1116 made to its commit-result twin was never applied to this half, so a tab could stand down against its OWN earlier write. **Fixed here.** |
| 13 | `pendingRemoteRef` / `drainRemote` | **—** | buffered mid-gesture instructions, applied one by one |
| 14 | `onRowsCanonical` (B1113) | **—** | assembly-blind: can adopt 4 of 8 children |
| 15 | `refetchReplace` | covered | heals after the folds (B1113) — now reports too |
| 16 | `reconcileSeedRows` | **—** | per-key rev arbitration; the following heal covers it |
| 17 | `foldJournal` | **—** | per journal entry; post-fold heal covers it |
| 18 | `foldNeverSyncedLocal` | **—** | per element; same |
| 19 | `mergeSiteContent` (cross-tab / cloud-vs-local) | **—** | `unionById` per id → can mix a NEW host with an OLD child; ends in `createSiteModel` → heals |
| 20 | `loadSite` / `loadSitesList` / `migrate` / `bootResume` / version restore | covered | heals — **was silent AND unpersisted.** Both fixed. |

*Revert*
| # | Path | Atomic? | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| 21 | `applySnapshot` (undo / redo / `cancelActiveMove`) | canvas-whole | but the snapshot can have been RECORDED torn, and the resulting commit is a per-element diff |
| 22 | `history.js` stack | n/a | whole-canvas snapshots |

*Refit (host-driven, not tear vectors)* — `refitChildren` / `relayoutWallKids` / `relayoutSide` / `layoutZoneByKind` all derive children inside ONE `setEls`; multi-select move expands to the `attachedTo` assembly; `planClipboard` copies whole and remaps bonds.

**Eleven of those bypass the atomic path.** That is the point of the enumeration: no realistic amount of additional atomicity closes eleven, and the twelfth would have been found next.

**THE FIX — the invariant, at every seam.** New pure module `lib/assemblyIntegrity.js`: `assemblyIntegrity(els)` runs the EXISTING derivation (`siteModel.normalizeBondedChildren`) and returns the healed list plus `repairs` (everything rewritten) and `tears` (anything displaced past `ASSEMBLY_TEAR_TOL_FT`, 1 ft). **The detector is the healer's own diff**, so a state called torn is by construction exactly a state the healer repairs — a second "where should this child be" derivation would be the next bug in this family. Identity-preserving on a coherent plan (same array reference), so it is free to run everywhere. Seams wired in `SitePlanner.jsx`:
- **canvas** — one `useEffect` over `els`, covering EVERY mutation (remote upsert, rows-canonical adoption, buffered drain, journal fold, local edit) so a new write path cannot be added that skips it;
- **undo/redo** — `applySnapshot` re-derives the snapshot before restoring it, so a frame recorded torn cannot reinstate the tear;
- **commit** — `reconcileElems` re-derives before the diff, and **flush-override** re-derives what `freshen` re-reads. This is the half that matters: a torn assembly is now **unpersistable**, whatever race produced it locally;
- **load** — `refetchReplace` (rows) and `storage.loadSite`/`loadSitesList` (on device);
- **post-commit** — a new `afterCommit` hook on the engine runs the assertion once per settled batch (accepted, refused, rolled back or transport-failed alike) and cannot throw into the write path.

**THE DETECTOR + THE LOUD HEAL** (the addendum: a silent repair is why this kept shipping as fixed). `assembly-tear-detected` on the `client_errors` channel from every seam, carrying the ids, the host, the bond kind and the delta in feet; `assembly-tear-healed` beside it; `assembly-tear-persisted` when the repair is written back. `normalizeBondedRotations` was the one pass that repaired geometry with **no `onHeal` at all** — it reports now, so every pass in the heal is auditable.

**TWO REAL DEFECTS FOUND AND FIXED ON THE WAY** (both named above, neither treated as *the* fix): the missing `foreignAuthor` gate on the realtime derived-yield (#12), and the load-time heal never reaching disk (#20) — the second is why the owner's plan kept "fixing itself" on screen while the stored copy stayed broken. A third, smaller one: `normalizeWallKids` kept a torn row's ALONG-wall value as user intent when the displacement was mostly ACROSS the wall, leaving ~20 ft of arbitrary slide after a heal; the across-axis error now decides whether the along value is intent or wreckage.

**PROOF.** `test/assemblyIntegrity.test.js` — 28 cases on the owner's real geometry, built by canonicalising through the invariant so no coordinate is hand-encoded. The derivation independently reproduces the owner's hand-computed anchors: `e7377` → `(−542.99, −697.38)`, `e7378` → `(−575.36, −694.45)`. The six required races (move→undo · move→redo · move with a second tab echoing mid-gesture · rejected child + accepted host · accepted child + rejected host · undo of a multi-select move spanning two assemblies) each drive the REAL engine with the shipped guard composition, and **all six were proven RED with the write seam disabled**. `e2e/assembly-tear-detector.spec.js` — headless Chromium through the real render path: move → Ctrl+Z → assert **in the same session, before any reload** (a reload heals it and proves nothing — this is the addendum made mechanical), THEN reload and assert it stays; plus the owner's tear planted on disk, proven to self-heal AND to say so with ids and deltas.
- Bundle: Site route +9.5 KB, total +3.9 KB (the new module + the guard wiring) — inside the headroom band, `perf-bundle-audit` green. Kept: this is a correctness guard on the write path, not a panel.
- Follow-up filed, NOT built: **B1341** (one row, one revision — the DB-level change, deliberately not attempted in one session).
### B1327 — Double-clicking a building does not open Properties: the parcel acreage badge eats the press `[Site Planner]` (bug) #site-planner #selection #ui  *(filed + shipped 2026-07-31 from an owner chat block as NEW-1; minted against a freshly-fetched main. DEDUPE-FIRST: searched Open / ⏳ Verify / Done for `double-click`, `isDoubleTap`, `acreage`, `polylabel`, `pointerEvents`, `swallow` — **B1174** applied this exact rule to measurement chips and **B1189/V562** explains a different inspector-close symptom; neither covers the badge, so this is net-new. It is a REGRESSION FROM **B1186** and says so, rather than re-opening it: B1186's anchor change was correct and stays.)*
`[x]` *(implemented 2026-07-31; parked for a signed-in pass on the owner's own "site phase two" — see **V648**.)* Double-click a building on Goose Creek site phase two and Properties never opens. Nothing happens at all.
- Verify: live — **V648**
- Origin: filed 2026-07-31 from chat (NEW-1)

**THE PANEL WAS NEVER THE PROBLEM — THE PRESS NEVER ARRIVED.** Audited before patching (AUDIT-FIRST) and the reported diagnosis held on every point: `openInspector` → `shouldInspectorTakeDock` → `setLeftPanel("properties")` is sound, the panel's render condition has no element-type gate, and `startMoveEl`'s double-tap branch is intact and unchanged. The parcel acreage badge renders `pointerEvents: auto` whenever the Select tool is up and paints AFTER `drawElsZ.above`. In SVG **paint order IS hit-test order**, so that solid pill won every press inside it. `startAcChip` stops propagation, sets no selection and never calls `isDoubleTap` — so the press produced no visible change, could not pair as a double-tap, and burnt an undo frame through a stray `pushHistory()`.

**WHY NOW.** B1186 moved the badge's anchor from `centroid()` — a vertex average that often floated clean off the lot — to `polylabel()`, the pole of inaccessibility, which is *guaranteed* inside the ring: the developed middle of the lot, where the buildings are. On the owner's own saved plan (`ui-audit/fixtures/goose-creek-plan1copy.json`) three badges moved several hundred feet and landed on two buildings and a road. Not only buildings.

**THE FIX IS THE RULE THE PARCEL'S OTHER CHROME ALREADY FOLLOWS.** The badge's hit target is gated on ITS OWN lot being selected — exactly what `setbackGrabNode` / `setbackChipNodes` do (`if (!selParcel) return null`). It still DRAWS at all times; only its press is gated, and a click on it now falls through to whatever is underneath (over the lot's own fill, that selects the lot and arms the drag). The stray undo frame goes with it.

**THE SAME BUG IN THREE MORE HATS, all fixed, because a fix that names one component protects one component — which is what B1174 already taught.**
- **The dimension grab band.** The fat transparent grab line renders only `if (dimSel)`, i.e. only once the element is selected — so press 2 of a real double-click lands on a layer press 1 just created, and `startDimMove` swallowed it. Double-click was dead in that band **by construction**, on buildings and on centerline roads alike. It now forwards to `isDoubleTap` keyed on the element's own id, the same key `startMoveEl` uses.
- **The `lastTapRef` poison.** `isDoubleTap` keeps ONE tap record, so chrome using a PRIVATE key over its own object destroys the pair AND clobbers the record. The dimension number (`eldim:${id}`) sits ON the footprint, so a body-press → number-press pair was the common case, not a corner; the pond map label (`${id}:label`) overhangs its basin the same way. Both are re-keyed onto the feature's own id. The ACTION still branches on which surface took the press — number → the inline length editor, body → Properties — so no affordance was lost; what is gone is a double-click that does nothing.
- **A reference promoted by "Draw above the plan" (B1198) — REFUTED, deliberately, and here is the reasoning.** It does take the press, but it is not the same defect and must not get the same treatment. The badge is chrome the user never asked to put there, cannot move off the building, cannot lock and cannot demote. A promoted reference is an **explicit per-reference opt-in** whose stated purpose is to sit over the plan, and it has TWO discoverable one-click ways out in the menu it was turned on from — **Lock** (pointer-transparent) and **Draw below the plan**. A markup with `behindEls: false` has behaved identically since it shipped. Making it click-through would make it unselectable on canvas, which is the regression B1198's handle-layer work exists to prevent. It is declared as a deliberate exception in the guard rather than silently unhandled.

**THE GUARD IS STRUCTURAL AND IT IS MUTATION-CHECKED, because the general rule is the deliverable.** `e2e/chrome-swallows-press.spec.js` drives the owner's real plan and asks two independent questions. **(1) STRUCTURAL:** with nothing selected, every element's own centre must answer to that element — asked of every element on the plan through `document.elementFromPoint`, the browser's real hit test, so ANY future late-painted pointer-enabled node that covers content fails here by construction, whatever it is called. **(2) BEHAVIOURAL:** a double-click opens something — driven at the element centre, and once more straight onto the dimension grab band (which the structural half cannot see, because the band lives inside the element's own group and only exists after press 1). The band was given a `data-testid="el-dim-grab"` so the repro addresses it exactly rather than guessing at an offset. **Proven red on the pre-fix code, three ways:** reverting the badge gate turns both structural tests red; reverting the grab-band forward turns the behavioural one red with the owner's exact symptom — `{"dock":"none","inline":false}`, a double-click that opened nothing.

**B1179 STAYS OPEN, and this item does not touch it.** Its inspector-close half is already explained and fixed (V562 / B1189, 3-of-3), and its module-keepalive half is stale. Its THIRD strand — "double-click a centerline road always opens Properties" — is **not** explained by this diagnosis: that spec runs on a blank site with no parcels, so no badge exists, and no handle or grab layer sits at its hit point. Do not close it on the strength of this work.

- **AMENDED 2026-08-06 by B50008–B50011 (this item is NOT re-opened; its fix stands and the CHROME-NEVER-EATS-A-PRESS rule is unchanged).** B1327's diagnosis was right about ITS cause — the acreage badge painted above the footprint and swallowed the press — but a double-click also dies when nothing eats it at all: the pair was measured on a WALL CLOCK read inside the handler (**B50008**), and the native `dblclick` never reaches the feature's node because press 1 re-renders it (**B50009**). Neither is a swallow, so neither was reachable from this item's framing. **B50011** is the audit that would have seen all three: it drives every element type and markup kind, and its `--labels` mode is what finds chrome that only EXISTS once selected — the case this item's corollary 2 names as invisible to a static reading.

### B1328 — A measurement can be layered: send it behind the plan, order it against its peers `[Site Planner]` (feature) #site-planner #ui #markup #export  *(filed + shipped 2026-07-31 from an owner chat block as NEW-2. DEDUPE-FIRST: searched Open / ⏳ Verify / Done for `measure`, `z-order`, `arrange`, `behindEls`, `send to back` — **B820** built Arrange for elements and markups and **B910/B940/B1174** own measurement gestures; none of them reaches the `measures` collection's draw order, which never entered the system at all. Net-new.)*
`[x]` *(implemented 2026-07-31; parked for the export-parity half, which is a mandatory LIVE-VERIFY class — see **V649**.)* The owner has an area measurement he cannot send to back and put buildings over, and right-clicking it offers no layering option at all.
- Verify: live — **V649**
- Origin: filed 2026-07-31 from chat (NEW-2)

**CONFIRMED, AND IT WAS STRUCTURAL RATHER THAN A MISSING MENU ITEM.** Measurements live in their own `measures` collection, so they never entered the `zOrder` / `byZ` system (which reasons over `els`), and they painted in ONE unconditional pass after `drawElsZ.above` — a hard top layer. The context menu offered Properties / Lock / Copy / Delete and nothing else, while overlays and markups have had front/back for ages.

**BUILT ON THE MARKUP MODEL, REUSED RATHER THAN REINVENTED**, exactly as the item asked: an explicit `z` from `lib/zOrder.js` (`nextZ` / `Z_GAP` / `byZAsc` — the same helpers elements and markups use, no second scheme) orders measurements against each other, and a `behindEls` flag picks the band. The render was extracted from the inline `measures.map(...)` into `renderMeasureNode(m, i)` and is now called from TWO passes — one beside the behind-the-plan markups, one where it always drew.

**THE DEFAULT DOES NOT MOVE, BY CONSTRUCTION.** `behindEls` is undefined on every measurement ever saved and on every newly drawn one, and only `=== true` sends one down — so no stored plan changes on load, and a freshly drawn measurement still lands on top. `siteModel.js` has been running `ensureZ` over `measures` since B671, so legacy z order already equals array order and the sort is a no-op on an existing plan. Asserted in `test/measureWiring.test.js`.

**THE INDEX IS THE IDENTITY, AND THAT IS WHY THE SORT TOUCHES THE DOM ONLY.** A measurement's selection is `{ kind: "measure", i }` — an INDEX into `measures`, not an id. So the bands carry `{ m, i }` pairs holding each measurement's ORIGINAL index; the z-sort reorders what is painted and never the model array. Getting this wrong would have re-pointed every selection, every drag and every delete at the wrong measurement.

**CONTROLS, IN THE WORDING THAT ALREADY EXISTS.** Right-click gains *Bring to front* / *Send to back* (within the band, shown only when there is a stack to reorder) and *Send behind the plan* / *Bring above the plan*; the Properties panel gains the same three under a **Layer** sub-label; and ⌘/Ctrl+`[`/`]` now answer for a measurement the way they do for an element or a markup. Crossing the plan re-stacks the measurement on top of the band it arrives in, so it is never dropped underneath whatever was already there. Undo rides `pushHistory` + the setter like every other edit, `histKey` already stringifies `measures` so a layer change is its own frame, and `z`/`behindEls` are plain additive fields that persist through save, copy/paste and the element-sync path with no schema work.

**EXPORT PARITY HOLDS BY CONSTRUCTION, AND IS ASSERTED, BUT IS STILL THE LIVE HALF.** `buildExportSvg` CLONES the live `<svg>`, so both passes ride into the sheet in the DOM order the screen has; the source guard pins that order (below pass before `drawElsZ.above`, above pass after). PDF-PARITY is a mandatory live class and the sheet/PDF confirmation is **V649** — the half that silently breaks is exactly the half a source guard cannot see.

### B1329 — Zoom is slow: the wheel was the one uncoalesced gesture, and every view change rendered twice `[Site Planner]` (bug) #site-planner #perf #ui  *(filed + shipped 2026-07-31 from an owner chat block as NEW-3. DEDUPE-FIRST: searched Open / ⏳ Verify / Done for `zoom`, `wheel`, `coalesce`, `regShift`, `jank` — **B1157** coalesced the POINTER path and **B555** the pinch path; the wheel was left out of both, which is the defect. **B1122** owns the basemap weld and is deliberately untouched here. Net-new.)*
`[x]` *(implemented 2026-07-31; parked for a live zoom on a heavy signed-in plan — see **V650**.)* Owner: *"I scroll out, and it takes probably a whole second to scroll out, and it does it in like two scrolls or two zooms."*
- Verify: live — **V650**
- Origin: filed 2026-07-31 from chat (NEW-3)

**(a) THE HARNESS LANDED FIRST, AND IT HAD TO BE CORRECTED TWICE BEFORE IT MEANT ANYTHING.** There was no zoom frame-time instrument anywhere: `perf-harness.mjs` measured a scripted DRAG only, and `zoomout-frames.mjs` measures dark-pixel fraction on a one-element scene. `perf-harness.mjs --gesture wheel` now reports `zoomFrameMedianMs` / `zoomFrameP90Ms` **and a canvas-commit count per wheel event**, reusing `lib/frameSampling.mjs`'s guards unchanged so a hidden tab or a starved sample is refused rather than reported. Commits are counted off the planner's own published `data-view-*` / `data-reg-*` attributes through a `MutationObserver` — no React internals, no instrumented build.
**Both corrections are recorded in the source, because each one produced a confident, wrong number first.** (1) `page.mouse.wheel()` awaits a CDP round-trip per notch and so delivers roughly one event per frame: against that input a coalescing handler and an uncoalesced one are indistinguishable, and the harness duly reported an identical `1.00 commits/wheel` on both builds. (2) Dispatching the burst inside ONE task is equally useless — React 18 auto-batches every `setView` in a single task into a single commit, and four runs per build came back at an identical 16.7 ms median. Real wheel input arrives one event per TASK, and auto-batching does not span tasks. The driver is now a MessageChannel pump: one event per task, five per burst.
**MEASURED, same machine, same build otherwise, three runs each:** canvas commits per wheel event **1.00 / 1.00 / 1.00 → 0.45 / 0.60 / 0.75** (mean 1.00 → 0.60). Frame median is 16.7 ms on both, because the committed stand-in scenario is not render-bound — which is precisely why V650 exists and why no ceiling was recorded off these numbers.

**(b) THE WHEEL IS rAF-COALESCED.** `SitePlanner.jsx`'s wheel handler called `setView` directly, once per raw event, with no rAF and no throttle — while the pointer path (`scheduleFrameJob`/`flushFrameJobs`) and the pinch path (`flushPinch`) both coalesce. The pinch path's own comment calls itself "the other half of the jank"; the wheel WAS that other half. Zoom factors now accumulate in a ref and commit once per animation frame. **The math is unchanged, not approximated:** an anchored zoom about a fixed screen point composes, so f₁ then f₂ about the same anchor is one zoom by f₁·f₂ about it; the latest cursor position is the anchor (which is where the user is pointing by the time the frame paints) and the clamp is applied once at the end. A capture-phase `pointerdown` on the wrapper flushes synchronously, so no gesture starts against a view with a zoom queued behind it.

**(c) THE SECOND RENDER PER VIEW CHANGE IS GONE.** `setRegShift`'s guard used a `1e-4` px epsilon against a continuously-varying sub-pixel residual, so it essentially never held; `regShift` is component state consumed as the SVG's transform, so every zoom AND pan step committed a second full render of the ~4,600-node tree. The epsilon is now `REG_EPS_PX = 0.02` — an order of magnitude below the quarter-pixel placement accuracy `ui-audit/diagnose-pointer-accuracy.mjs` asserts, so the B1141/B1142 weld is untouched. **The bigger win was deliberately NOT taken:** moving `regShift` out of React state and writing both transforms through refs would also move `window.__plannerView.registration()` and the `data-reg-dx/dy` attributes the harnesses read. Ship the epsilon, measure, then decide — do not do both blind.

**B1122'S WELD IS UNTOUCHED.** The basemap transform is still written in the LAYOUT effect, same frame as the SVG, from the same view value. Nothing here moves that write, and `test/panLockInvariant.js` still passes.

### B1330 — Four render-cost wins with provably complete inputs, plus the last unbounded cache `[Site Planner]` (task) #site-planner #perf  *(filed + shipped 2026-07-31 from an owner chat block as NEW-4. DEDUPE-FIRST: searched Open / ⏳ Verify / Done for `cull`, `memo`, `LRU`, `unbounded`, `keyOf` — **B1159** cached pond contours, **B1162** bounded the previous set of caches, **the culling work** culled the geometry pass; none of them reaches the label pass, the building grid, the two zoom-keyed dispatches or the undo loop. Net-new.)*
`[x]` *(implemented 2026-07-31; parked with **B1329** for the same live zoom — see **V651**.)* Five cost reductions, none of which touches what is drawn.
- Verify: live — **V651**
- Origin: filed 2026-07-31 from chat (NEW-4)

**(a) THE LABEL PASS NOW SEES THE SAME SET THE GEOMETRY PASS DRAWS.** `labelCands` and the `dimItems` collision loop both iterated the FULL `els` while the geometry pass had been culled for releases, and `layoutLabels` then ran twice over that pool. Both now iterate `drawEls`. **This is not a cap and not decimation** — it aligns two passes that were always meant to see the same elements. `cullToView` force-keeps the selection and anything mid-drag, and `CULL_MARGIN` already covers a label hanging outside its element's bounds. **PDF-PARITY is asserted, not assumed:** on an export pass `cullRect` is null, so `drawEls` is IDENTITY with `els` (the same array reference, not a copy) — `test/viewCull.test.js` now pins that identity AND source-guards that both loops read `drawEls`, next to the element-count assertion that was already there. The `cullKeep`/`drawEls` memos moved earlier in the component body so the label pass can read them; nothing else about them changed.
**Deliberately NOT done, per the item:** memoising the label/collision block. `labelCands` carries screen coordinates by design, so its identity changes on every zoom step and there is no key that is both correct and stable. The lever is (a) plus B1329.

**(b) `computeBuildingGrid` IS MEMOISED, WITH A PROVABLY COMPLETE KEY.** It ran once per building per render — twice, in fact, for the column-grid and dock-door passes — with `clipSegmentToRing` then running per grid line, and its inputs contain **no view term at all**, so a pan or zoom recomputed an identical answer for every building on the plan every frame. The function is pure, closes over nothing, and reads exactly `length`, `depth`, `dock` and five numbers off `grid`; the key folds in the other two `grid` fields as well, so an over-broad key can only cost a miss and never return a wrong answer. **This is categorically different from the flood/detention memos we refused** — those had dep sets nobody could enumerate. Bounded at 256 entries with insertion-order eviction (B1162's rule), and the cached value is documented as read-only since it is now shared between callers.

**(c) TWO ZOOM-KEYED DISPATCHES THAT USUALLY WROTE null OVER null.** `setGisHit(null)` and `setGisHover(null)` fire on every `view.ppf` change. Per this file's own B1189 note, a same-value dispatch is still a DISPATCH and React only skips scheduling it when the fiber has no other pending work — which during a zoom it always has. Both now read a plain ref mirror first and skip.

**(d) THE UNDO LOOP STRINGIFIED THE WHOLE MODEL ONCE PER ITERATION.** `lib/history.js`'s `undo` recomputed `keyOf(current)` inside the while loop; `keyOf` is `histKey`, a `JSON.stringify` of every parcel, element, measurement, callout and markup. An undo that skipped ten deduped no-op frames stringified the model eleven times instead of once, on a path the owner hits constantly. Hoisted — behaviour-identical, `current` cannot change inside the loop.

**(e) THE LAST UNBOUNDED CACHE IS BOUNDED — and the answer to "do it or say why not" is DONE.** `lib/layers.js`'s `_probeCache` was one entry per distinct service URL probed, never evicted, for the whole session. The payoff is genuinely small (the entries are tiny), but an unbounded Map keyed on strings arriving from a registry and from user-toggled layers is a leak by SHAPE, and "small" is not an invariant anyone maintains. Capped at 400 through a single write helper, so the cap cannot be bypassed by a second `set` — an evicted probe simply re-probes, which the 40-second TTL already does anyway.

### B1331 — The 278 MB tab: instrument the two retention suspects, cap only what the number justifies `[perf / memory]` (task) #perf #site-planner  *(filed + shipped 2026-07-31 from an owner chat block as NEW-5. DEDUPE-FIRST: searched Open / ⏳ Verify / Done for `memory`, `heap`, `retention`, `undo limit`, `PDFDocumentProxy` — the tile-memory tier (`tileBudget`/`tileLifecycle`) and `releaseCanvas` are different retention classes on different objects; nothing covers the undo stack or the overlay PDF proxies. Net-new.)*
`[x]` *(implemented 2026-07-31; the DevTools heap snapshot with retainer paths is a signed-in live reading and is the only honest instrument for the TAB figure — see **V652**.)* Michael sees ~278 MB on the Chrome tab.
- Verify: live — **V652**
- Origin: filed 2026-07-31 from chat (NEW-5)

**WHAT WAS SHIPPED, PLAINLY: one instrument with a definitive reading, one cap that the reading justified, and one cap deliberately NOT taken.**

**SUSPECT (i) — THE UNDO STACK. INSTRUMENTED, MEASURED, AND EXONERATED. NO CAP.** `ui-audit/retention-probe.mjs` (`node --expose-gc`) builds a plan-shaped model carrying the two payload classes the item names — markup image `src` and deed rasters, 6 × 512 KB — runs `LIMIT + 40` ordinary edits through the REAL `createHistoryStack` doing exactly what the planner does (`setEls(a => a.map(...))`), and compares the retained stack against 80 INDEPENDENT models under forced GC. **Reading: the full 80-deep stack retains 0.4 MB — 5.1 KB per generation — against 6.21 MB for 80 independent copies, a ratio of 0.065.** So the payloads are **structurally shared**: an edit replaces the array and the one changed element, and every untouched element, every other collection and every image/raster STRING keeps its identity across generations. The undo stack is kilobytes per generation, it is not the 278 MB, and **there is no memory case for lowering the limit** — which is what the item required before touching a number it correctly calls a product decision. Left alone.

**SUSPECT (ii) — THE PDF PROXIES. CAPPED, WITH RE-OPEN MADE TRANSPARENT FIRST.** `overlayDocs` held a live `PDFDocumentProxy` per sheet overlay for the WHOLE session — set on load, destroyed only on removal or unmount — pinning JS-side page objects AND a worker-side document for a reference placed once and never touched again. That is squarely "shorter lifetimes", which is authorised. The trap the item names is real and was closed **first**: the References panel gated the page picker's enabled state on `overlayDocs.current.has(o.id)`, so a naive teardown would silently degrade a working control to *"re-add to change page"*. So the gate now asks a different question — `overlayPageReady(o)`: **live OR re-openable** — and `setOverlayPage` routes through the existing `ensureOverlayPdf`, which already downloads the stored bytes and reloads. A proxy is released only when it can be brought back: an overlay with no stored PDF key is never touched, because there the loss would be real. Idle window 5 minutes on an LRU clock stamped by every genuine use; the knockout control reads the same one helper. LOUD-FAILURE: `setOverlayPage` used to `return` silently on a miss and now says so.

**WHAT COULD NOT BE MEASURED HERE, SAID PLAINLY.** `performance.measureUserAgentSpecificMemory()` needs cross-origin isolation, which planyr.io does not set, and most of a map-heavy tab is decoded tile bitmaps plus GPU copies no JS-heap number can see. **The per-proxy byte figure and the tab attribution are a DevTools heap snapshot WITH RETAINER PATHS on a real signed-in session after a long editing run — logged as V652 and not guessed at here.** No cap was sized off an estimate.

**CONSTRAINTS HELD.** Everything above is eviction / teardown / shorter lifetimes. No retina downgrade, no cap on how much can be drawn, no spinner gating overlays, no geometry decimation, and the B65 anti-flash ghost buffer is untouched. No guard was weakened and no ceiling was raised — the bundle audit reports three metrics above baseline inside their headroom band and **no baseline was re-recorded**, because B1178 is still open and unexplained.

### B1291 — Notes belong in the cloud: the tree, the bodies AND the pictures sync to Supabase `[Notes / sync]` (task) #notes #sync #persistence #auth  *(filed 2026-07-30 alongside **B1290**, which shipped the module itself. Minted **B1291** via `git fetch origin main && npm run next-id -- --against-main`. **RE-OPENED AND SHIPPED 2026-07-31** — DEDUPE-FIRST honoured: this is the ORIGINAL item built out, not a new number. Searched Open / ⏳ Verify / Done again for `notes`, `notebook`, `sync`, `cloud save`, `notes_pages`: the Site Planner's element-level sync (**B124** / **B671**–**B674**) and the Doc Review `doc_reviews` table are different data in different tables; **B1311** owns the pictures' local tier, which this extends rather than duplicates. Still net-new, still one item.)*
`[x]` *(implemented 2026-07-31; parked for the cross-device strand the sandbox cannot sign in to reach — see **V640**.)* Notes lived in **one browser on one computer**, and clearing browsing data lost them. They now follow the account: the notebook tree, every page body, and every pasted picture.
- Verify: live — **V640**
- Origin: filed 2026-07-30 from chat; built 2026-07-31 on owner instruction
- Depends on: **B1290** (shipped), **B1311** (the local image tier this lifts to the cloud).

**THE SCHEMA WAS ALREADY APPLIED, AND THE CLIENT WAS CODED AGAINST THE LIVE ONE, NOT A GUESS.** `public.notes_trees` / `notes_pages` / `notes_images` + a private `notes-images` Storage bucket went into production (`lyeqzkuiwngunutlkkmi`) as migration `notes_cloud_sync_b1291`; the client was written after reading the live columns back through the Supabase MCP, and the applied DDL is committed verbatim at `src/workspaces/notes/db/notes_cloud_sync.sql` so the repo is not the one place it does not exist. Own-row RLS only, private by default, anon key only — **no team predicate and no cross-user path**, per KEY DECISIONS; a guard test fails the build if one appears. **Nothing on the owner's plate: he ran no SQL.**

**THE SEAM HELD, AND THE WIDENING IS NAMED (the item asked for exactly this).** The store's public surface — `readTreeRaw` / `writeTree` / `readPage` / `writePage` / `putNoteImage` / `purgePages` — did **not change**, so no component, model function or exporter learned that storage moved. What grew is what lives *behind* it: `lib/notesCloud.js`, a private tier with exactly ONE importer (`notesStore.js`) and reached only by a cached dynamic `import()` — the same shape, for the same bundle reason, as `notesImageDb.js`. A sync engine inlined into `notesStore.js` would have doubled that file and buried the local path, which is the path that must keep working unchanged for a signed-out user. Both properties are guard-tested.

**ROWS-CANONICAL-ON-SEED, WRITTEN INTO THE STORE HEADER the way the site-element rule is written into `/CLAUDE.md`.** For a page the server has already seen, the **row wins** on seed unless a *pending local edit* explains the difference; for a page the server has **never** seen, **local wins** and is uploaded. The tree follows the same rule one level up, and when both moved it is **merged, never clobbered**. This closes the same trap B1113 closed: after a seed the device holds the FRESH rev, so a stale cached body would commit *cleanly* — the revision guard cannot help, because the client legitimately holds the current revision. Adopting the row at seed time is what makes it impossible.

**CONCURRENCY IS A REVISION COUNTER AND A NAMED STATE, NEVER A QUIET OVERWRITE.** A server trigger owns `rev`, so every push sends the **guard** `and rev = <the rev it read>` and no rev of its own; zero rows back means another device wrote first. That is a **CONFLICT**: the page enters a named state, a bar says *"also changed on another device"*, and the user picks. **"Keep the other computer's" parks this device's text as a sibling page FIRST**, so *never a lost edit* is a property rather than a slogan. There is no last-writer-wins path anywhere in the module.

**TOMBSTONE-DELETES, ON THREE SEPARATE PATHS — and the third one was a real bug found while building.** (1) The client **never hard-deletes a row**: `deleted_at` = binned (body intact, which is what a restore on the other machine needs to find), `purged_at` = gone for real, with the page's picture rows purged in the same cascade. A vanished row would read as "not uploaded yet" and be pushed straight back up. (2) A **binned or purged row can never raise a false conflict** — binning bumps the rev through the trigger, so a delete would otherwise report itself as a competing edit; `planPageSeed` rebases instead. (3) **ADOPTION IS ALSO A DELETE PATH.** Adopt a signed-out notebook, delete it from the account, sign in again, and "missing from the account tree" would have resurrected it. A notebook is now skipped when the account has it live, has it **in the bin**, or this device has **adopted it before** (recorded in the sync ledger). Three unit tests pin it.

**PICTURES TOO — eager UP, lazy DOWN, and that asymmetry is the decision.** Bytes go to the private bucket with IndexedDB kept as the local cache. Uploads happen on the seed and on every paste, because an un-uploaded picture is a note that opens **broken** on the second machine. Downloads are lazy: `readNoteImage` falls through to the cloud on a cache miss and writes the bytes back on the way past, so pictures arrive with the page that needs them instead of in a sign-in-time avalanche of photos the user may never open. Adoption re-keys a signed-out note's pictures into the account scope in the same pass — without that half, an adopted note would open with every figure missing.

**LOUD-FAILURE on the footer, and PANEL-BREVITY applied to it.** One line, and it is whatever is TRUE: *Saved on this device* · *syncing* · *Synced to your account 5m ago* · *offline, it will sync when you are back* · *sync failed: <reason>* · *one note also changed on another device*. It is derived in ONE place (`notesStorageLine`), so no surface can claim a sync the store did not make, and a failure always names a cause a person can act on. **The sentence it REPLACED, named as the rule requires: `· not synced to the cloud yet`.** Measured: signed out **1 line / 49 → 20 chars**; signed in **1 line / 65 → 31 chars** — a net reduction in both states, no accumulation. `test/notesModule.test.js`'s honesty guard was **inverted in this same commit** (it used to assert the store never said "Synced"), which is the point: the rule did not change, the truth did.

**SIGNING OUT COSTS NOTHING, PROVEN AT RUNTIME NOT JUST AT BUILD.** Every cloud path sits behind an explicit gate. The headless harness asserts a signed-out visit writes **no sync ledger**, never **downloads** `notesCloud` at all, and issues **zero** requests to a notes table or the picture bucket.

- **Verified here (ATTEMPT-BEFORE-YOU-PARK — everything drivable WAS driven, nothing drivable was filed):** `ui-audit/verify-notes.mjs` extended **in place** to **105/105** against the real built app in headless Chromium, §20 being the nine new signed-out checks above. `test/notesSync.test.js` (**47 new tests**) proves every merge decision — delete-wins in both directions, nothing-ever-dropped, local-title-wins, the four disjoint seed sets, binned-is-not-a-conflict, purged-is-never-resurrected, idempotent adoption and the three resurrection cases — plus the **wire itself**, driven through the shipped transport against a fake client, asserting the guard is on the update and that no rev is ever sent (the **B1120** lesson: test the request, never a mock more forgiving than the server). `test/notesModule.test.js` gains 11 structural guards. Full suite **7461 green**, lint clean, build clean.
- **Perf:** `bundle.notesRouteJsBytes` and `bundle.totalJsBytes` ratcheted under **B1291** with head-to-head measurements in one container — main alone 576.9 / 4488.9 KB vs this branch 588.0 / 4509.2 KB, so this branch's own delta is **+11.1 KB on the route and +20.3 KB total**, of which 9.3 KB is the lazily-loaded `notesCloud` chunk that a signed-out user never fetches. `siteRouteJsBytes` and `largestChunkBytes` are **byte-identical to main**. Both bands had already been mostly consumed by B1310–B1318; the reasons on the ratchet log say so rather than attributing main's drift to this feature.
- **NOT in scope, deliberately, and untouched:** linking a note to a site / element / Library file (**B1318**), file attachments, templates, tags.

### B1314 — A note could not be printed or turned into a PDF `[Notes]` (feature) #notes #export  *(filed 2026-07-31 from an owner review of B1290; minted with B1310. DEDUPE-FIRST: the Site Planner's `exportSheet.js` is a different sheet for a different object; nothing covered Notes.)*
`[x]` *(implemented 2026-07-31; parked for the one strand a headless run cannot reach — see **V631**.)* Markdown is the right archival export, but it is not what the owner sends anyone — he lives in PDFs. Print / Save as PDF now exists on the page and on the notebook.
- Verify: live — **V631**
- Origin: filed 2026-07-31 from chat (NEW-5)
- **PDF-PARITY, BOUGHT BY CONSTRUCTION.** The sheet's body HTML is not hand-written: `lib/notesDocHtml.js` asks ProseMirror's own `DOMSerializer` to render the document through the very `renderHTML` each extension uses to paint the screen. Same schema, same rules — a construct added tomorrow prints with no edit there. Only the image `src` is substituted in (the node deliberately carries an id, not bytes), which is what makes a printed sheet self-contained like an exported one.
- **A separate sheet rather than an `@media print` block on the app**, and that is the reliability decision: printing the live app means fighting the flex column, the scroll container, the sticky toolbar, the rail and the theme tokens (a dark surface prints a black page), and one new wrapper anywhere above the editor silently breaks it. A whole notebook also prints as one continuous document with section headings and a page break per page, which the on-screen layout cannot express at all.
- `lib/notesPrint.js`'s paper CSS is a deliberate **mirror** of the screen's `EDITOR_CSS`, construct for construct; a unit test asserts both style the same construct list, and the live check asserts the sheet carries the picture, drops the app chrome, and is light-on-white whatever the app theme is.

- **WHY THIS ONE PARKS AND THE OTHER SEVEN DID NOT — stated plainly, because it stretches a rule.** Everything our code is responsible for WAS driven here (`verify-notes.mjs` §13: the sheet exists, carries the page's picture resolved to real bytes, drops the rail and toolbar, and is light-on-white whatever the app theme is). What cannot be driven here is the step AFTER our code: headless Chromium's `window.print()` is a no-op, so nothing in this sandbox can produce a paginated document. `VERIFICATION.md` rule 4 names exactly three blockers and none of them fit, so **V631** proposes a fourth (`print-engine`) rather than mislabelling this as an auth or data wall. ATTEMPT-BEFORE-YOU-PARK is honoured in substance: nothing drivable was filed.


### B1254 — Per-layer "Show above plan": opacity was never the escape hatch, and could not have been `[Site Planner / layers panel]` (feature) #site-planner #gis #ui  *(owner chat block 2026-07-30, provisional NEW-1. AMENDS **B1205/B1206/B1207** (PR #880, merged the same night). The owner's instinct — "just have a button that shows it above or shows it below" — was better than what shipped, and this implements it. Minted **B1254** via `git fetch origin main && npm run next-id -- --against-main`, LATE, as the last step before push, against `origin/main` a748911 + 57 in-flight peer branches; code, tests and commit keep the provisional `NEW-1` label. **B779 working as designed, twice over:** the first late mint returned B1228/V573 and `npm run check-mint` REFUSED it because a peer branch had claimed both in the intervening minutes; B1229/V574 was refused too; B1242/V577 passed the gate locally and was then refused by the PRE-PUSH hook, which had a newer view of the peer branches. B1254/V593 is the fifth — B1252/V591 passed the gate cleanly and was then overtaken while a merge-conflict resolution against a fast-moving `main` was in flight. Each renumber was a two-line `sed` — no code, test or commit touched, which is exactly the property late binding buys. Gaps left at B1228–B1253 deliberately (B1140: a gap is cheaper than another renumber pass). DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open + ⏳ Verify + Done across the stacking and ordering families: **B1205** (the fixed model, whose DEFAULT this deliberately leaves alone), **B1206** (the opacity unification, kept), **B1208** (the handle-layer/line-band deviation — related, and explicitly NOT widened here, see below), **B1197/B1198** (the handle layer + the reference front/back band), **B671** (per-element `z`), **B820** (element/markup Arrange), **B461/B654** (the reference overlay's own z-ops), **B898/B760/B761** (the panel row shapes). None of them owns where a GIS layer sits relative to the plan as a USER decision — B1205 owns it as a fixed system default, and this is the named exception to it. Net-new, and it is an AMENDMENT rather than a B1205 recurrence: B1205 is not defective, its escape-hatch CLAIM was.)*
`[ ]` **⏳ IMPLEMENTED — V593 PENDING (the real-flood-data / real-plan half only).**
- Verify: live
- Origin: filed 2026-07-30 from chat (owner block, provisional NEW-1)
- **THE CORRECTION, which is the whole item.** B1205/B1206 shipped saying per-layer OPACITY was "the one escape hatch" in the fixed stacking model. That is false for the case it was offered for: **opacity cannot fix OCCLUSION for a layer that draws UNDER the site elements.** Turning a buried floodplain fill down changes nothing on screen — the building still covers it, and all the slider does is fade the parts that were already visible. Opacity only helps a layer that is already ON TOP and too loud. **Occlusion order can only be fixed by order.**
- **⛔ THE DEFAULT IS UNTOUCHED, deliberately, and that is asserted rather than assumed.** Area fills still draw under the elements and line/point layers still draw over them, so the owner's ORIGINAL complaint — contours vanishing behind his buildings — still needs **zero interaction**. A toggle you never have to touch beats a toggle you always have to touch, so the lift is opt-in and defaults OFF on every layer. `test/layerAbovePlan.test.js` fails the build if any registered layer ever defaults to lifted.
- **Shipped: a two-state, semantically-named control on every toggleable row — "Show above plan".** One `abovePlanControl` implementation and ONE `aboveRow` call site driving all three row shapes (solo · the pairwise City-limits & ETJ composite · the N-ary merge groups), which is the B1206 discipline applied to the new control. It is **not** a free-form z-order picker: no front/back, no up/down, no per-layer number. Planner surface only — the map finder has no plan for a layer to be above.
- **The already-on state is SHOWN, not hidden — and this was the one open question on the item.** A line or symbol layer is over the plan already, so the control has nothing to do on that row. It renders **checked and inert**, with a hover saying why. Chosen over hiding it because **an absent control cannot be told apart from a control that was not offered**: the user would have to interpret the row's silence ("already above?" vs "this layer can't?"), and being able to READ where a layer sits is the point of adding the control at all. It also teaches the fixed model, which is what makes the default comprehensible. One place, one meaning, on every row.
- **WHERE THE LIFT STOPS, and the architectural decision that cost the most.** A lifted layer clears the site elements and stops **below the labels/chips and below B1197's always-on-top handle layer**. The cheap implementation — drop the lifted pane into the map-top host beside B1205's line band — is one line, and it was **refused**: that host sits above the whole plan SVG, so it would have inherited **B1208**'s deviation. That deviation is tolerable for a HAIRLINE (a contour may cross a handle but can never make one unreachable) and **intolerable for a FILL** (a floodplain wash over the handle layer hides the grip you are dragging — strictly worse than the occlusion the lift exists to fix). So the lifted band is hosted **inside the plan SVG**, in a screen-space `<foreignObject>` at a new `data-gis-front-band` anchor rendered after the elements and before the labels. **B1208 is neither closed nor widened by this.**
- **The model: `lib/mapStack.js` gains ONE tier, `gisAreaFront` (z 660).** Only an AREA role is liftable, because it is the only role the default puts underneath. A role-SPLIT source (FEMA zone polygons + hazard boundaries) lifts its **fill half only** and leaves its stroke half where it already was — one row, one toggle, still two export requests.
- **The mechanism, and the trap.** Leaflet fixes a layer's pane at CONSTRUCTION — there is no `setPane` — so flipping the toggle is a tear-down-and-re-add, executed in the SAME sync pass so the layer never blinks out. `bandKey` compares the **resolved pane names**, not the flag, which is what lets the map finder collapse both bands onto one pane and rebuild **nothing**. The teardown goes through the ONE `release` helper the toggle-off path already used, so the role-split resurrection trap (releasing only `refs[k]` and leaving the other half's tiles + in-flight request alive) cannot reappear on the new path.
- **VIEWPORT-STABLE.** The in-SVG host is a THIRD mirror of the wrap's gesture transform, written in the same statement as the original (`setWrapTransform`) and in a LAYOUT effect, plus Leaflet's map-pane translate — and it additionally counter-translates the SVG's own registration shift, because a map pane inside the SVG must not be nudged onto the imagery twice. `pointer-events: none` throughout, so it can neither take a click nor steal a handle.
- **PDF-PARITY.** The sheet now composites **three** bands: `under` at the backdrop anchor, `front` **into the plan SVG's own `data-gis-front-band` group**, and `over` after the plan. So a lifted fill prints above the buildings and still under the printed labels — the same place it reads on screen. LOUD-FAILURE if a sheet has no front anchor: the layer prints over the plan **with a named warning**, never silently underneath.
- **Persisted per plan.** A new sparse `layerAbove` map on the site model — the `layerOverrides` twin, its own field so no existing record, merge or undo frame changes meaning — restored on open, saved on toggle, with its own undo signature so a lift is its own undoable frame. Only layers the lift can actually MOVE are stored; a stale or nonsensical key self-prunes.
- **The copy that claimed otherwise is fixed**, in `mapStack.js`, `LayerPanel.jsx` and this folder's `CLAUDE.md`. Opacity keeps its "See through this layer" hover — still true — and no longer claims to answer "I can't see through my plan". A guard test fails the build if the word "escape hatch" reappears in the opacity control.
- **PERF — paid back IN-DIFF, not raised away.** Three real optimisations were taken first: `MAP_STACK`'s per-tier `label` strings and `ROLE_SPLIT_NOTE` moved into comments (pure documentation that was shipping to every visitor's browser and that no runtime code ever read), the three panel call sites deduped behind one `aboveRow`, and `layerPrefs`' four functions + `layers.js`' two teardown blocks folded into one path each. That reclaimed roughly 1.1 KB of the diff's ~3.5 KB. `bundle.siteRouteJsBytes` was then raised via `npm run perf:ratchet -- --item B1254 --allow-raise` with its reason on the record: **2289.4 → 2293.1 KB, +3.7 KB**, all app-route, no new dependency and no new chunk (`siteRouteChunks` still 7). **That figure is this diff's OWN share and nothing else's** — an earlier pass on this branch recorded a +47.0 KB raise, which was honest arithmetic but misleading provenance: the metric absorbs in-band growth silently and re-baselines to the MEASURED value, so raising it banks everything that accumulated on `main` since the last raise (41.9 KB of it, in that case). Re-measured against B1253's freshly recorded baseline after merging it, the attribution is clean. Raised rather than optimised further because the lifted band **cannot be lazy-loaded — it is a render tier of the planner canvas itself.** `bundle.totalJsBytes` was raised alongside it for the SAME bytes counted a second time (everything here lands on the Site route) — **3886.1 → 3964.4 KB**, of which **74.6 KB is `main`'s own accumulated in-band growth**: `origin/main` 4e40f13 was built and measured at **3960.7 KB against a 3963.8 KB ceiling — 3.1 KB of band left**, so again any feature would have breached it. Payback for both stays tracked by **B1064**. `largestChunkBytes` stayed inside its band. Payback stays tracked by **B1064**.
- **Guards.** `test/layerAbovePlan.test.js` (42 assertions: the tier's position including the below-labels/below-handles bound, the untouched default, liftability over the LIVE registry, the panes + rebuild key, the three export bands, the in-SVG hosting and its DOM position relative to the elements/labels/handle layer, the LOUD-FAILURE paths, the per-site persistence and its undo frame, the panel's one-implementation/one-call-site rule, and the corrected copy). `test/mapStack.test.js` updated — the ban is now on FREE-FORM ordering, with the one named control asserted present. `e2e/map-layer-stacking.spec.js` grew a second case driving the real planner logged out with the AREA service stubbed: default band → one click → the lifted band inside the SVG, painting, after the building and before the handle layer, inert, and welded to the drawing through a pan; plus a **pixel** check over the measured layer∩building rectangle, because every other assertion is DOM-shaped and would be satisfied by a `<foreignObject>` the browser silently declined to render.
- **MUTATION-CHECKED THREE WAYS** (each turns the e2e case red, then restored): hosting the band in the map-top host instead of the SVG · rendering the anchor after the handle layer · dropping the front host from `setWrapTransform`'s mirror list (the layer slid 71.8 px away from the building it covers).

### B1253 — The map's landing view was hardcoded to Houston for EVERY account — it is now derived from the user's own sites `[Site Planner / MapFinder]` (bug + feature) #site-planner #ui #gis  *(owner chat 2026-07-30, provisional NEW-1. Minted **B1253 / V592** via `git fetch origin main && npm run next-id -- --against-main`, LATE — as the last step before push; code, tests and the harness keep the provisional `NEW-1` label. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open + ⏳ Verify + Done for `landing`, `COUNTIES_MAP.harris`, `default landing view`, `initial view`, `setView`, `fit`, `MapFinder`, `viewCounty`, `B11`, `B13`, `B96b`, `B1102`: **B11** removed the county PRE-PICK gate (click routing), **B13** made the Layers-panel jurisdiction FOLLOW the map, **B96b** added the scale bar, and **B1102** raised the zoom-out FLOOR and says on the record *"the landing view is still `COUNTIES_MAP.harris` — deliberately unchanged; where the app opens is a product decision, not a bug fix."* That is the decision this item makes. Nothing has ever owned where the map OPENS. Net-new, not a recurrence.)*
`[ ]` **⏳ IMPLEMENTED — V592 PENDING (`Blocker: auth`).** Every logged-out path — all three account shapes and the do-not-yank rule — is verified HERE, headless, in this session (16/16); what the sandbox cannot reach is a signed-in account whose site list arrives from the cloud AFTER the map is created.
- Verify: live — V592 (`Blocker: auth`)
- Origin: filed 2026-07-30 from chat (owner block, provisional NEW-1)
- Amends: B1102 (which deliberately left this alone), B13 (the jurisdiction follower, now reading a purpose-built resolver)

**The defect.** `MapFinder.jsx` created its Leaflet map with `const cfg = COUNTIES_MAP.harris; // default landing view (no pre-picked county)` and `setView(cfg.center, cfg.zoom)`. Harris County was therefore the opening view for **every account on earth** — a brand-new user in Denver, Phoenix or Atlanta opened over Houston, Texas, which reads as broken software.

**OWNER DECISION — derived, never a preference.** He was explicit: **no setting, no toggle.** The rule has three cases:
1. **No sites yet → the whole continental US.** The honest empty state: the user has no work to show, so show them the country and let them search or click in.
2. **Exactly one site → that site's AREA at metro scale**, never its parcel.
3. **More than one → the DENSEST CLUSTER**, so a single distant outlier cannot drag the camera.

**Why case 3 matters concretely, today.** The owner has 26 sites around Houston (Harris, Fort Bend, Waller, Chambers) and exactly ONE in Weld County, Colorado. The correct answer for him is **Houston, unchanged from what he has now**, with the Colorado site simply not pulling the camera — and if Colorado ever becomes his denser market, the landing view follows on its own, with no action from him.

**What shipped.**
- **`src/workspaces/site-planner/lib/landingView.js` — pure, no Leaflet, no DOM, no React.** Single-linkage clustering at a 50-mile threshold (a metro's working radius), the group with the most sites wins, ties broken by the most recently updated site, then by first-seen order so the answer is deterministic for a given input. **Single-linkage is the point, not an implementation accident:** Waller to Chambers is ~75 miles — further apart than the threshold — and the Harris sites between them chain the two ends into ONE market, exactly as a person reads it. Colorado has nothing within a chain's reach of Texas.
- **ZOOM — "make sure it's appropriately zoomed out."** The cluster's bounds are fitted with generous padding, the fit is FLOORED to Leaflet's integer steps (so it errs wide, never tight), and the result is clamped so the landing view can never land closer than a metro / county-scale reading. Degenerate bounds — one site, or every site within a mile of the next — fit to infinity by construction and fall straight onto that clamp, which is exactly what the clamp is for: one project never opens zoomed to its own lot.
- **It is where the map OPENS, not a leash.** Two latches: `landedRef` (we have landed on real sites) and `userMovedRef` (the user has taken the wheel). Either one ends the landing behaviour for the session, so a late-arriving cloud site list can never yank a camera the user is already driving. `userMovedRef` is deliberately keyed on real INPUT — a press, a wheel, a drag — never on Leaflet's `movestart`/`zoomstart`, which our own programmatic `setView` also fires.
- **A landing view outside Texas now resolves its jurisdiction sensibly.** The Layers-panel follower read `candidateCountiesForPoint(...)[0]`, whose out-of-bbox answer is **harris-first BY CONTRACT** (click routing depends on that order, and `test/counties.test.js` asserts it). Reading it as a jurisdiction is the same hardcoded-Houston bug one layer down — it would have claimed Harris County over Denver. New pure `countyForView(lat, lng)` in `counties.js` answers the jurisdiction question on its own terms: a bbox hit wins (nearest county CENTER among overlapping padded boxes, so downtown Denver reads Denver and not whichever neighbour was declared first), otherwise the nearest configured county **within the point's own state**. Statewide parcel pseudo-keys are never returned — they are SOURCES, not jurisdictions. Click routing is untouched, and a test asserts it stayed untouched.
- **PERF BUDGET — a RECORDED raise, not a silent one.** `bundle.siteRouteJsBytes` 2242.2 → 2289.4 KB, logged via `npm run perf:ratchet -- --metric bundle.siteRouteJsBytes --item B1253 --allow-raise` with its reason on the record. **This diff costs +3.5 KB** (`lib/landingView.js` + `counties.countyForView` + the `MapFinder` wiring); it cannot be lazy-loaded, because it decides the map's FIRST frame. The other **+43.7 KB of that move is accumulated drift that rode inside the 44.8 KB headroom band unrecorded** — `origin/main` a748911 already measured **2285.9 KB against a 2287.1 KB derived ceiling, 1.2 KB of band left**, so any feature at all would have breached it. Recording it here resets the band rather than leaving the next session to trip on 1.2 KB. `largestChunkBytes` moves 1418.9 → 1422.6 KB, inside its own band. Payback stays tracked by **B1064**.

> **Tests / verification (sandbox + headless — ATTEMPT-BEFORE-YOU-PARK honoured; the full V592 script was RUN here, not parked).** `test/landingView.test.js` — 28 pure cases over the owner's REAL distribution as the fixture (Harris / Fort Bend / Waller / Chambers + Weld County CO): zero sites yields the US and the US actually FITS the opening viewport; one site yields that site's area clamped to metro scale and a viewport tens of miles across; 26 clustered + 1 far outlier yields the CLUSTER and **not** a bounding box of both (asserted three ways — the count is 26, the fitted bounds stop short of Colorado, and the Weld point is outside the computed visible rect); two equal-sized clusters tie-break to the most recent, and flip when the other one is touched; a missing timestamp reads as oldest, never newest; sites all within one mile still clamp OUT to the metro floor; two sites at the same coordinate don't divide by zero; the clamp holds at phone, laptop and 4K viewport sizes; the fit never falls below the map's own floor; clustering is order-independent; and a SOURCE GUARD fails if `MapFinder` ever assigns a fixed county as a view again or goes back to reading `candidate[0]`. `test/counties.test.js` +7 for `countyForView`. `ui-audit/verify-landing-view.mjs` drives the built app in headless Chromium across **three seeded accounts**, reading the map's real position from the app's own cursor readout (so it needs no tile host) and asserting off-screen-ness against the real site PINS in the DOM — **16/16**: no sites → the continental US at a country zoom; one Denver site → centered on it, held at the metro clamp, its pin on screen; the owner's 26+1 → **Houston, zoom 9, all 26 Houston pins on screen and the single Colorado pin off-screen**; and after a pan, the derived view does not yank the user back. (It writes screenshots to the gitignored `ui-audit/screens/`, so re-run it to see them.) Full suite **7021/7021** · lint 0 errors · build green · `MAP.md` regenerated · bundle / doc-pointer / panel-copy audits green.
