### B1214 — The user can now OVERRIDE which boundary is Front, Side, Street side and Rear `[Site Planner / parcel]` (feature) #site-planner #ui  *(owner chat block 2026-07-30, provisional NEW-6. Minted **B1214 / V566** via `git fetch origin main && npm run next-id -- --against-main`, LATE, as the last step before push. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open + ⏳ Verify + Done across the role/override family: **B1191** (⏳ Verify) built the role tier and shipped a per-side picker writing a DENSE `pc.roles`; **B1123/B1039** are the derive-by-default / preserve-once-touched precedents (dog-ears, side parking, trailer length); **B214/B1184** the two grouping tiers. This does not re-open B1191 — its inference, its four rows and its NON-NEGOTIABLE all stand. It replaces the storage MODEL underneath its picker, which froze fourteen untouched sides the first time you corrected one.)*
`[ ]` **⏳ IMPLEMENTED — V566 PENDING (`Blocker: auth`).** The role is a per-run override: no override tracks the inference, an override is kept through every re-derive, and "Automatic" hands it back.
- Verify: live — V566 (`Blocker: auth` — the signed-in cloud round-trip of the new `roleOverrides` field; every logged-out path is verified here, see below)
- Origin: filed 2026-07-31 from chat (owner block, provisional NEW-6)
- Amends: B1191 (the role tier — not re-opened)

**The report.** *"You've got setbacks by role, but what if their interpretation of the setbacks is different from your interpretation of the setbacks? We should be able to edit which one is the rear setback and which one is the side setback, just in case."* The inference is a good default and it is frequently wrong in the real world — a corner lot, a flag lot, a double-frontage lot, or simply a reviewer who reads the plat differently — and being wrong changes the required dimension.

**AUDIT-FIRST — what was actually there, and what was actually wrong.** B1191 already stored a user role in `pc.roles` and already let the *By side* picker set one, so "the user can correct it" was half-true. But `setRunRole` wrote a **DENSE** vector: correcting ONE run stamped **every** edge with whatever the app happened to infer at that moment. On the owner's fifteen-side parcel, one correction froze fourteen untouched sides against every later re-derivation — the exact opposite of derive-by-default. Nothing marked a role as the user's rather than the app's, and there was no way back to automatic.

**What shipped.**
- **A SPARSE override vector, `pc.roleOverrides`** — `null` at an edge means "still tracking the inference". This is the repo's established derive-by-default / preserve-once-touched pattern, now applied to roles. `resolveRoles` composes inference + overrides; `setRunOverride(…, role|null)` sets or clears a whole run.
- **Legacy plans migrate in place, without changing a pixel.** A dense `pc.roles` is narrowed on read to the entries that genuinely DIFFER from the inference — an entry equal to auto is a no-op either way, so nothing on screen moves, and everything the user never actually corrected goes back to tracking the boundary.
- **An override is never silently reset.** Alignment is enforced like `pc.setbacks`, and the two in-place reshapes that change the ring length now REMAP it: inserting a control point carries the role across the split (both halves are still the same side); deleting one merges two edges and the merged edge keeps the first half's role. Dragging a corner — the common reshape — never changed the length and always survived.
- **An overridden run is legible as overridden.** Its row reads **· yours** in the accent colour and carries `data-role-source="yours"`; an untouched row reads `"auto"`. The picker's top option is **"Automatic (Rear)"** — it both NAMES the role the app infers and is the way back to it. A **Roles: back to automatic** button appears next to Reset-to-default once anything is overridden, and disappears again when nothing is.
- **The role re-drives what the role feeds.** Changing it moves the run's edges into the other ordinance row, so the **By role** input for that role now writes them (and no longer writes the old one). *Stated plainly: this app has no external jurisdiction setback TABLE yet — the "required value for that role" is the number typed on the By-role row, and that is what follows the override.* One `pushHistory()` + one `setParcels` = one Ctrl-Z.
- **The NON-NEGOTIABLE still holds by construction:** a role is a LABEL, nothing here writes a setback VALUE, and the harness re-proves the drawn ring is identical across assignment and reassignment.

> **Tests / verification (sandbox + headless — ATTEMPT-BEFORE-YOU-PARK honoured).** `test/setbackRoleOverride.test.js` — 15 cases: sparse by default; only real roles honoured; a misaligned vector ignored rather than shifted; the legacy narrowing renders identically; setting a run touches only that run; clearing restores the inference for that run only and then for the parcel; purity; **an override survives repeated re-derivation, a corner drag, a control-point insert, a control-point delete and a JSON round-trip**; and the required-value lookup follows the override (the run's edges move rows, and typing the role's number writes exactly those edges). `ui-audit/verify-setback-roles.mjs` extended and **22/22** on the owner's real production geometry: every side starts on Automatic with no way-back control shown, one correction reads as *yours* and only that one does, the way-back appears, the override **survives a full page reload**, "Automatic" hands it back, and the control disappears again. Full suite green · lint 0 errors · build green · bundle budgets within ceiling.
- **⏳ Live step pending (V566, `Blocker: auth`).** `roleOverrides` is a new key on the parcel's `site_elements.data` blob. The logged-out reload path is verified above; what the sandbox cannot reach is the **signed-in** round-trip — that the override commits, survives a refetch, and does not read as a conflict against another writer. The sign-in proxy blocks Supabase auth here.

### B1205 — GIS layers draw UNDER the site elements, so contours placed under a building disappear — one fixed semantic stacking order for the whole map `[Site Planner / layers]` (feature) #site-planner #gis #ui  *(owner chat block 2026-07-30, provisional NEW-1. His case: he places buildings, then wants to see the site contours, and the contours are now behind the buildings. He explicitly rejected a hold-to-peek key — "i dont want anything on a key, but whatever an apple or a google would do, lets do" — so the answer had to be a system default with NO new mode, NO shortcut and NO per-layer z-order picker. Minted **B1205** via `git fetch origin main && npm run next-id -- --against-main`, LATE, as the last step before push; code and tests keep the provisional `NEW-1` label. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open + ⏳ Verify + Done across the layer family (**B898** the panel group taxonomy, **B1070/B1071/B1075–B1080/B1091** the flood group + its scoping, **B445** the raster cache proxy, **B694/B695/B751/B752** the vector tiers, **B704–B706** terrain) and the ordering family (**B671** per-element `z`, **B820** element/markup Arrange, **B461/B654** the reference overlay's own z-ops, **B1197/B1198** the concurrent handle layer + reference bands): the per-element and per-reference orderings are about the PLAN's own content, and nothing has ever owned where a GIS LAYER sits relative to the plan. Net-new.)*
`[ ]` **⏳ IMPLEMENTED — V564 PENDING.**
- Verify: live
- Origin: filed 2026-07-30 from chat (owner block, provisional NEW-1)
- **THE LOAD-BEARING RULE: filled AREA layers draw UNDER the site elements; LINE/stroke layers draw OVER them.** A contour crossing a building is a hairline and reads fine; a floodplain fill over a building buries it. That one distinction answers the complaint with no control at all — he sees his contours through his buildings, and his buildings never vanish under a blue wash. Neither Google Maps nor Apple Maps lets a user reorder layers; both use a fixed semantic hierarchy and expose opacity, which is exactly what shipped.
- **The model, in one place: `src/workspaces/site-planner/lib/mapStack.js`.** Bottom → top: basemap/aerial → GIS AREA layers → references → parcel → setback band → site elements → references explicitly promoted above the plan (B1198) → GIS LINE layers → labels and chips → manipulation handles. Every renderer names a tier from this file; nothing anywhere picks a z-index of its own.
- **Roles are DECLARED, never inferred at render time.** Every one of the 36 registered GIS sources carries an explicit `role: "area" | "line" | "point"` (points ride the over-the-plan band with the lines — burying a well or a hydrant under a pad defeats the point of turning it on). A source that publishes BOTH splits into its two roles via `roleLayers`: **FEMA** now paints its zone POLYGONS (sublayer 28) under the plan and its hazard BOUNDARIES (27) over it; **BKDD Drainage Information** splits sub-watersheds (116) from streams / BFE lines / outfalls (108, 121, 112, 2); **BKDD Master Plan** splits the study floodplains + proposed detention from the conveyance + proposed channel improvements. One panel row, one opacity, one status dot, two export requests.
- **The mechanism, and why it was not just a z-index.** Leaflet keeps every pane inside its own `_mapPane`, which carries the pan transform and therefore its own stacking context — so NO z-index on a pane can lift it above the planner SVG. The line-role pane is hosted OUTSIDE the map, in a sibling box above the SVG, with the two transforms that position it mirrored in the SAME statement as the original (VIEWPORT-STABLE): the wrap's live gesture transform and Leaflet's own map-pane translate. The host is `pointer-events: none`, so it can neither block a click nor steal a handle.
- **PDF-PARITY.** The sheet composites the same two bands: `under` at the backdrop anchor as before, `over` appended after the drawn plan and before the sheet furniture. Both raster and vector emitters take the band as an argument, so screen order and sheet order cannot drift.
- **NO new mode, NO keyboard shortcut, NO per-layer z-order UI** — asserted by a guard that fails if the Layers panel ever renders one.
- **RECONCILED, not competing, with the concurrent B1197/B1198 work** (merged to `main` mid-session; this branch was rebased onto it). B1198's References front/back stays exactly as shipped and now slots into this model: `lib/overlayOrder.js` owns the ordering WITHIN the reference bands, and its opt-in "Draw above the plan" band is a declared tier (`referenceFront`) rather than a second scheme. B1197's handle layer is the model's top tier.
- **⚠ ONE KNOWN DEVIATION, stated on the item as well as in the code.** `handle` is the top of the model, and B1197 made that true inside the plan (one `data-handle-layer` group, the SVG's last child, so a handle paints over and hit-tests ahead of every drawn element and every AREA layer). It does NOT paint over the LINE band, because that band is a separate DOM host above the whole SVG. Promoting the handle group into its own top host would move it out of the plan SVG, and **every planner drag relies on pointer moves BUBBLING to that SVG** — a handle in a sibling SVG would swallow the moves passing over it mid-drag. The deviation is bounded: the line band is thin and non-interactive, so a hairline may CROSS a handle but can never make one unreachable. Closing it means lifting the handle layer and its pointer plumbing together, with B1197's own guards — filed as **B1208**.
- **PERF BUDGET — a recorded RAISE, not a silent one.** `bundle.largestChunkBytes` 1378.9 → 1418.9 KB, logged via `npm run perf:ratchet -- --item B1205 --allow-raise` with its reason on the record. The diff costs **+8.4 KB minified** on the Site chunk (all app-route; no new dependency, no new chunk — `siteRouteChunks` still 7). Raised rather than optimised because **`origin/main` b2cfd08 already measured 1410.5 KB against a 1410.9 KB derived ceiling — 0.4 KB of band left**, so any feature at all would have breached it; the two lazy-load candidates within this diff's reach were checked and refused (`screeningBfeSite.js` has three render-path exports, `pondOptimizer.js` is called during render by the options card). Payback stays tracked by **B1064**.
- **Guards.** `test/mapStack.test.js` (15 assertions: the order, the load-bearing rule, the role audit over the LIVE registry — an unclassified source fails the build — the split partitioning its own sublayer list, no z-order UI, the export bands). `e2e/map-layer-stacking.spec.js` drives the real planner logged out with both services stubbed: the three hosts in the model's order, the AREA pane inside the backdrop map, the LINE pane outside it and above the plan, both actually painting, the top band taking no pointer event, and the line stroke genuinely overlapping the building's own box.

Net-new.)*
`[ ]` **✅ Sandbox-verified — the audit ran and its result is now machine-enforced.**
- Verify: sandbox
- Origin: filed 2026-07-30 from chat (owner block, provisional NEW-2)

### B1189 — The planner CRASHES to the error boundary when Escape follows the Properties rail click within ~200 ms (runaway render loop) `[Site Planner / UI]` (bug) #site-planner #ui #perf  *(found by the B1188 click-contract audit, 2026-07-30, while chasing why `e2e/inspector-close.spec.js` was red. **Pre-existing on `main` — reproduced on the unmodified baseline build, so it is NOT introduced by B1188.** Minted via `git fetch origin main && npm run next-id -- --against-main`. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open / ⏳ Verify / Done for crash · render loop · maximum update depth · panel resize: relatives are **B962** (the SVG-viewBox squish on panel toggle, which introduced the second `setSize` writer) and **B837** (the pan compensation) — neither covers a runaway loop, so net-new.)*
`[ ]` **⏳ IMPLEMENTED — root cause FOUND and closed, both layers. V562 PENDING (signed-in / real-plan pass only).**
- Verify: live
- Origin: found 2026-07-30 by the B1188 audit (not owner-reported). Fixed 2026-07-30.
- **REPRODUCED first, exactly as filed** (headless Chromium, production `vite preview`, logged out): draw a building → click the Properties rail tab → dispatch Escape in the SAME evaluated tick. The whole planner is replaced by the boundary's `Minified React error #185`. Screenshot captured.
- **⛔ THE PRIOR SESSION'S LEAD IS REFUTED — record it so nobody re-runs it.** Its trace showed `size` getting a new object every render and concluded the loop was a `setSize` feedback cycle, with "quantise `setSize`" as the next step. Instrumented both writers at full precision across the crash: **RO and the B962 layout effect never disagreed** — both reported 1058 exactly — and there were **FIVE `setSize` dispatches in the entire trace** while `size` was replaced ~50 times. The width was never oscillating. Quantising would have changed nothing, and would have put a whole pixel of slop into view maths that `diagnose-pointer-accuracy` asserts to a quarter of a pixel.
- **The actual root cause, from a sourcemapped crash frame** (`SitePlannerApp:7:334513` → `SitePlanner.jsx:2581 setRegShift`): the runaway writer is the **drawing↔basemap registration layout effect**, not `setSize`. Two individually-innocent pieces closed a cycle:
  1. **The effect depended on the `size` OBJECT** (`[view, size, origin, geoOverscan]`) while reading only numbers out of it. `setSize`'s updater ALLOCATES whenever the measured width differs from the state it is applied to, and React re-applies a retained updater against its base state on every subsequent render — so once the panel close left one retained, every render minted a fresh `{w:1058,h:640,…}` holding the SAME numbers, and the effect re-ran on identity alone.
  2. **The effect dispatched `setRegShift` unconditionally**, including on the `!origin` early return (a blank plan) where there is nothing to register against. A `setState` whose updater returns the same value is still a DISPATCH — React only skips scheduling via the eager-bailout path, which needs the fiber to have no other pending work, and during a panel close there always is some. So that dispatch scheduled another render, which minted another `size`, which re-ran the effect…
  Instrumented proof: ~50 consecutive runs with every dep VALUE identical (view `{0.35,60,60}`, 1058×640, overscan 213), one component instance (no remount), zero `setSize` dispatches in the loop. Fifty round trips is React's nested-update limit, and it aborts the subtree.
- **LAYER 1 — the loop.** The effect now depends on `size`'s NUMBERS (`[view, size.w, size.h, origin, geoOverscan]`), so an allocation-only change is invisible to it — correct, because nothing in the body can tell two `{w:1058,h:640}` objects apart. The `!origin` path now guards its dispatch instead of relying on a no-op updater. The B837 pan compensation already depended on `size.w` this way; the registration effect was the outlier. **Scoped to `size` deliberately:** the trace showed `view` and `origin` hold their identity across the loop and their writers replace them only on a real change, so they stay whole-object deps — listing their fields too was belt-and-braces against a churn nothing has exhibited, and it was not free (it cost enough bytes to push `largestChunkBytes` past its CI ceiling, which is how the over-reach was caught).
- **LAYER 2 — a measurement loop must never be able to take the planner down (the non-optional half).** React's "Maximum update depth exceeded" is a CIRCUIT BREAKER, not a diagnosis of corrupt state: the loop is already broken by the time a boundary sees it, and the plan lives in storage, not in the aborted render. Yet the boundary answered it with a terminal card that replaced the entire planner — the drawing, the rails, the session. New pure `src/app/recoverableError.js` classifies that error (dev text **and** minified `#185`, because production is where it fired and where a message-only match would be dead code), and `ErrorBoundary` now spends up to **two automatic remounts** before showing any card, holding a quiet "Redrawing…" placeholder for the frame it takes. The retries are **bounded** so a genuinely repeating crash still surfaces, and the budget resets after 30 s so an unrelated later blip is not held against an hours-old count. **LOUD-FAILURE is preserved on both paths** — every catch still logs and still reports to telemetry, tagged with whether it auto-recovered, so a silently-retried loop is data, not a swallowed error. If a recoverable error does exhaust its retries, the card now says the plan is saved rather than reading as lost work. Deliberately NARROW: an ordinary `TypeError` recurs identically on remount, so it is not recoverable and still goes straight to the card.
- **Verified here (the regression test was PROVEN RED on pre-fix code before it was accepted, as the item required).** New `e2e/panel-escape-race.spec.js` drives the exact race — the rail click and the Escape in ONE evaluated tick, strictly faster than two driver round trips and immune to machine speed — six times per run. **On the unmodified baseline build it fails with the planner replaced by the error boundary (screenshot attached to the run); on the fix it passes 6/6 with no update-depth error raised at all.** Layer 2 is asserted independently of the race in `test/errorBoundaryRecovery.test.js` (8 tests: the minified-code match, neighbouring-code false positives, non-recoverable classes, the bounded retry, the window reset).
- **No regression in what this effect exists to do**, which was the real risk of the dep change: `ui-audit/diagnose-map-lock.mjs` **PASS** (pure-pan round trip returns exactly; zoom re-snap 0.650 px lock / 0.493 px return, both inside the 1 px bound) and `ui-audit/diagnose-pointer-accuracy.mjs` **PASS** (120/120 readings within 0.25 px, compensation still applied) — both on a LOCATED site with a real basemap, so the `origin`-set path is exercised, not just the blank one. Plus e2e `panel-toggle-viewport` (B837), `panel-open-squish` (B962), `panel-toggle-flash` (B933) and `canvas-click-pan-jump` all green.
- **Bonus, measured:** `e2e/inspector-close.spec.js` — one of the three specs **B1179** records as RED on `main` — was red *because of this bug* and is now **3/3 green**. B1179's other two are untouched and stay open.
- **Gate:** lint 0 errors · full unit suite green · build green · bundle budgets within ceiling. **The first CI run FAILED on `largestChunkBytes` by 0.1 KB** — B1178's unreproducible baseline had already consumed the whole headroom band on `main`, so this change's +89 bytes tipped it. Paid back rather than ratcheted (raising the baseline would have baked in B1178's drift): the over-broad dep lists were narrowed to the measured churner, and the registration effect's two reference builders — which each spelled out the same three-call Leaflet "map frame" read, and which built the projection reference TWICE for one measurement — were de-duplicated. Net **−27 bytes vs `main`** on the largest chunk, so this PR now REDUCES it. `diagnose-map-lock` and `diagnose-pointer-accuracy` were re-run after that refactor and both still PASS.
- **What the sandbox cannot prove (→ V562):** the race on a SIGNED-IN, real saved plan (Tsakiris / Bain) on production, where cloud sync adds concurrent state writers the logged-out run has none of. `Blocker: real-data` `Blocker: auth`

### B1190 — Document Review's markup inspector still derives its visibility from the selection (the B1188 defect, other workspace) `[Doc Review / Markup]` (bug) #doc-review #markup #selection #ui  *(spun out of the B1188 audit 2026-07-30 at the owner's explicit ask — "say so and flag it… do not scope-creep into fixing those in this session unless they are the same code path." It is a DIFFERENT code path (`DocReview.jsx`, a rail SECTION rather than a docked panel), so it is filed rather than fixed. DEDUPE-FIRST: not a B750 recurrence — B750 BUILT this marker in both workspaces and its live check passed; this is the follow-on rule change B1188 introduced, which Review has not had applied.)*
`[ ]` **⏳ IMPLEMENTED — V563 recorded PASSED this session (see the live check below). Reclassified `Verify: live` → sandbox-verifiable, with the reason stated.**
- Verify: live *(→ driven in a real headless browser here; see "Verified here")*
- Origin: filed 2026-07-30 from the B1188 audit. Fixed 2026-07-30.
- **The audit AGREED with the filing: Review had the same defect, not a different one.** `DocReview.jsx` kept `propsForId` (an id that had to keep matching `sel`) plus `useEffect(() => setPropsForId((cur) => (cur && cur === sel ? cur : null)), [sel])`. So the section's open/closed state was DERIVED from selection and a deselect — a click on empty sheet, a marquee, a page change — closed Properties the user had deliberately opened. Same shape as B1188, different file.
- **The fix mirrors B1188 rather than paralleling it.** `propsOpen` is a plain boolean only an explicit affordance writes: `openMarkupProps` / `closeMarkupProps`, reached from the double-click, a freshly-drawn markup, a new ✕, and Escape. The selection-clearing effect is **DELETED, not rewritten** — there is deliberately no replacement, because any effect keyed on `sel` that writes the open state is the bug. Selection now chooses the BODY only, and with nothing selected the section HOLDS ITS GROUND on a "Nothing selected" state instead of vanishing.
- **Two things the planner's version did not have to answer, decided explicitly here.** (a) The armed-tool **"Tool style"** block shares the same surface; it keeps its own unchanged trigger, because it is about the tool in your hand, not about the inspector — so arming a tool after a deselect still shows its style rather than an empty state. (b) An owner-owned open flag needs an owner-owned CLOSE or it is a one-way door, so Review gains an explicit ✕ (`aria-label="Close properties"`, matching the planner) and Escape closes the section **before** it touches the selection — the same order `SitePlanner` uses, with the markup left selected so a double-click reopens on it.
- **The declaration check was extended to this surface, as the item asked.** The check's shape did allow it: `e2e/clickContract.table.js` gains `REVIEW_CLICK_CONTRACT` (18 markup tools, each declaring that a double-click opens the inspector and which ones split to in-place text editing) plus `REVIEW_NON_MARKUP_TOOLS` (the five modes that draw nothing selectable, declared so "deliberately no contract" is distinguishable from "somebody forgot a row"). `test/clickContract.test.js` reads Review's own shipped `TOOLS` registry and **fails the build** if a tool is in neither list — so a new markup type cannot ship with an undeclared click behaviour, exactly as for the planner's registries.
- **One guard-quality fix made in passing:** the new source assertions strip comments before matching. These files document the shapes they removed — quoting `setPropsForId(...)` in a comment is how a reader learns what not to reintroduce — and a naive string check trips on its own documentation. Verified the guard still goes RED by reintroducing a selection-derived close and watching it fail, then restoring.
- **Verified here — a real browser, logged out, no blocker left.** New `e2e/review-click-contract.spec.js` drives the actual Review workspace with a locally dropped PDF (client-side pdf.js, no auth, no network) and asserts the whole contract: a freshly drawn markup opens its properties · a deselect leaves the section open on "Nothing selected" · selecting a markup swaps the CONTENTS of the still-open section · a drag on empty sheet (which pans) does not close it · ✕ closes · a double-click reopens · Escape closes · it reopens after that too. **Proven RED on the pre-fix `DocReview.jsx` (both cases fail) and green on the fix.** Because `property-panel` is shared with the tool-style block, the spec asserts against a new `data-props-mode` seam that names the three states apart (markup / tool / empty) rather than inferring state from header text.
- **Why this is recorded as verified rather than parked:** ATTEMPT-BEFORE-YOU-PARK — this is a logged-out, no-external-GIS, locally-dropped-file UI check, which is Claude-doable here, and none of the LIVE-VERIFY classes apply (it is not timing/race, concurrency, GIS, zoom-density, export parity, or real-project data). It was filed `Verify: live` by the audit; the live check has now been run and recorded.
- **PANEL-BREVITY:** the only copy added is the empty state's one line ("Nothing selected. Click a markup to see its properties.") — which replaces a **vanish**, so it is a new state being given words, not an existing group accumulating them. `node ui-audit/panel-copy-budget.mjs --check` **all regions within budget, unchanged** (the audit's regions are the yield/pond panels; Review's rail is not one of them, and nothing there moved).
- **Gate:** lint 0 errors · full unit suite green (including the extended `clickContract` at 23 tests) · build green · `MAP.md` regenerated · e2e green across `review-click-contract`, `click-contract`, `click-behavior`, `inspector-close`, `doc-review-panel-toggle`.

Both halves were **mutation-checked** — restoring the old `sbStroke || PAL.chipInk` turns them red.

### B1197 — A resize handle that falls under the parcel line is drawn behind it AND cannot be grabbed, so the object can't be resized from that corner `[Site Planner / references · UI]` (bug) #site-planner #ui #selection  *(owner chat block 2026-07-30, provisional NEW-1, with a screenshot of the Weld County site `sms7v3ua7ksy` — breadcrumb `2221 E LAMAR BLVD STE 790 / Concept A` — carrying a coloured land-plan exhibit PNG at 85%. Minted **B1197** via `git fetch origin main && npm run next-id -- --against-main`, LATE, as the last step before push; code and tests keep the provisional `NEW-1` label. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open + ⏳ Verify + Done across the overlay/reference family (**B72/B73** the overlay + its calibration, **B461** the overlay right-click menu incl. its z-order ops, **B654** the merged References panel, **B480/B481/B784/B786** overlay persistence + storage, **B576/B578** panel polish) and the handle family (**B230** control points, **B619** the selection outline, **B913** callout width handles, **B1184/B1185** the screen-space handle thinning): nothing has ever owned WHICH LAYER a handle is drawn in. Net-new.)*
`[ ]` **⏳ IMPLEMENTED — V554 PENDING.**
- Verify: live
- Origin: filed 2026-07-30 from chat (owner block, provisional NEW-1)
- **Report, verbatim.** *"one of the edge points that I was gonna use to expand the overlay … it's hidden behind the parcel. So let's layer the overlay above the parcel, but I guess a bigger issue is that I don't even have the option to bring it to the front."* On his screenshot the reference's top-right grip sits directly under the green parcel line at the E County Rd 14 corner.
- **The defect is generic, and fixing only the overlay's z-order would have left the trap in place.** A manipulation handle is **chrome, not content**: it must render above every map layer and win the hit test whenever the pointer is over it, whatever is drawn underneath. A handle you cannot grab is a broken handle regardless of layer order — and the next thing that happens to sit on top would have re-created it.
- **AUDIT-FIRST — the sweep the item asked for, with the answer.** The parcel vertex handles, the element resize/rotate grips, the road vertex grips, the add-nodes and the markup handles were **already correct**: they are built as consts and rendered from one `data-export="skip"` chrome group at the very end of the feet-space transform. **Three sets were NOT**, because they were authored inline inside the content pass that draws their object — the **reference overlay's** scale + rotate grips and its B73 calibration marks (below parcels, setbacks, elements and markups: the reported case), the **callout's** B913 width grips and per-leader grips (below measurements and labels), and the **measurement's** B230 control points (below labels). All three are hoisted.
- **The fix.** One `data-handle-layer="1"` group, the LAST child of the feet-space transform, renders every handle set in the planner. In SVG a later sibling both paints over and hit-tests ahead of everything before it, so that single position buys visibility and grabbability **together** — there is no second hit-test rule that could drift out of step with the paint order. The overlay grips ride the overlay's own rotation transform so they stay on its corners; locked/calibrating states, the export skip, and every drag-starter are unchanged (all five already `stopPropagation`, so hoisting them changes no event path).
- **B1184/B1185 are untouched, as the item required** — the screen-space thinning and the smaller mark with the unchanged grab area are decisions about handle SIZE and COUNT, not about which layer they live in. Asserted in the guard.
- **Verified here, on the real render path, logged out.** New e2e spec `e2e/references-handle-layer.spec.js` seeds a plan whose reference's top edge lies exactly ON the parcel boundary, selects it, and for each of the four corner grips reads `document.elementsFromPoint` at the grip's centre: **all four answer as themselves, and the spec first proves the parcel geometry really is stacked underneath them** (otherwise a plan with no parcel would pass vacuously). A real mouse drag of the boundary-covered top-left grip resizes the reference, so the grip genuinely takes the press. The rotate knob is checked the same way. Plus `test/handleLayerOrder.test.js` (21 source guards: every handle set renders from the layer, none of the five ex-inline drag-starters is wired from a content pass again, nothing paints after the layer in feet space, the export skip and the locked/calibrating states survive the move). lint 0 errors · 6,820 tests · build green.
- **What the sandbox could NOT prove (→ V554):** the owner's own bar — his actual signed-in Weld County plan, his actual PNG exhibit, over the real aerial. The seeded repro reproduces the geometry, not his data.
- **Bundle — a budget BREACH, paid back with a matching optimization rather than a raised ceiling.** The feature costs +2.5 KB on the site route. Three peer PRs merged the same afternoon had already spent 30.6 KB of the metric's 32 KB headroom band, leaving `main` at 1409.6 KB against a derived 1410.9 KB ceiling — so +2.5 KB put `largestChunkBytes` **1.1 KB over**, and CI went red. **`npm run perf:ratchet --allow-raise` was deliberately not used:** the repo's rule is that a feature breaching a budget ships with an optimization or does not ship, and there was a real one to find. **`lib/sheetFurniture.js` was split by TIER.** It held both the drawing PRIMITIVES the live canvas needs (scale bar, north arrow, metrics, `screenFurniturePlates`) and the corner-placement + SVG-string tier only the exported SHEET uses. Because `SitePlanner.jsx` (boot path) and `exportSheet.js` (a lazy chunk) each imported from it, Rollup hoisted the WHOLE module into their common ancestor — the site chunk — and tree-shaking cannot help there, since it drops unused exports, not exports used by a sibling chunk. The export-only half moved to `lib/sheetFurnitureLayout.js` and now rides the lazy export chunk: **5.2 KB off the boot path, 1.6 KB off the minified site chunk.** Behaviour is byte-identical (the same functions, moved; every existing assertion in `test/sheetFurniture.test.js` unchanged and green), and the rule is now written into the folder pointer so the next mixed-tier module gets split instead of hoped over. Net: **1410.5 KB, inside the ceiling.**

Ordering is stable and predictable with several stacked — the panel order is derived from the same array the canvas paints.

### B1191 — The PARCELS panel still spoke in fifteen geometric SIDES, not the four setbacks a zoning ordinance writes `[Site Planner / parcel · UI]` (bug) #site-planner #ui  *(owner chat block 2026-07-30, provisional NEW-1. **AMENDS the B1184–B1187 strand (PR #874 / V547) — that work is live-verified PASS and is NOT re-opened**: chips down to three, sparse handles, the acreage badge inside the parcel and the black chip ink all stand. Net-new tier, filed rather than folded into the archived B1187.)*
`[ ]` **⏳ IMPLEMENTED — V548 PENDING.**
- Verify: live
- Origin: filed 2026-07-30 from chat (owner block, provisional NEW-1)
- Amends: B1184 (the run-grouped panel list) · strand B1184–B1187 / V547 — none of which is re-opened

**The report.** After B1184 the panel offered *By side* / *Per segment* and listed "Side 1 · 2 seg, Side 2 · 6 seg, Side 3 · 10 seg … Side 15". Fifteen rows where there had been sixty is real progress, and the segment counts are a good touch — but it is not what was asked for. The owner does not think in fifteen geometric sides; he thinks in the four setbacks an ordinance writes: **FRONT, SIDE, STREET SIDE (corner), REAR**. Exactly one row had resolved to "Front", so role detection existed and fired once — it was never carried through to the other fourteen.

**What shipped.**
- **A THIRD tier, `By role`, and it is now the DEFAULT** (`sbEditMode` starts at `"role"`). Four rows — Front / Side / Street side / Rear — each one input writing to every side in that role through the same canonical per-edge `pc.setbacks` array. *By side* stays the middle tier and *Per segment* the exception tier, both behaving exactly as before. A role no side currently carries still gets its row (so the four are always the four) but shows an em-dash instead of an input — there is nothing to write to yet. The mode toggle is no longer gated on the boundary being multi-segment: `By role` changes what the list means on a four-sided lot too.
- **EVERY side is auto-assigned on load, not one.** New pure module `lib/setbackRoles.js`. The order is deliberate, each step narrowing what the next can claim: (1) **street abutment** — a run most of whose length lies within 150 ft of a road centerline *and whose outward normal faces it* (distance alone marks a lot's deep side street-abutting merely because its far end reaches the corner); (2) **Front** — the longest abutting run, or simply the longest run when the plan carries no roads, plus any run facing the same way at the same depth, so a frontage broken by a jog is one Front; (3) **Street side** — any OTHER abutting run, the corner-lot case, and only ever from real road geometry — never guessed; (4) **Rear** — runs facing roughly opposite the front; (5) **Side** — the rest. Roles reason over runs built from a FLAT value vector, so typing a setback cannot reshuffle the labels.
- **The assignment is visible and correctable.** Each *By side* row carries a role picker showing the resolved role; changing it writes the role to every edge in that side (stored per edge in `pc.roles`, aligned to the ring exactly like `pc.setbacks`, and re-derived rather than shifted by one if the boundary is reshaped). The user's assignment always wins over the auto one.
- **Map chips read their role** — "Front · 25′", not a bare 25′. The plate now sizes itself to its text, so two consequences had to be handled: `spaceOut` gained a **box** metric beside its radial one (same helper, not a fork — a role chip is three times as wide as a number plate and exactly as tall, so one circular threshold either lets two wide chips overlap side-by-side or throws away vertically-stacked ones with plenty of air between them), and the inboard step now clears the plate's own half-extent instead of a fixed offset, so a wide chip can no longer straddle the boundary and land on the OUTBOARD side-length dimension B215 deliberately put on the other side of the edge.

**NON-NEGOTIABLE — no site's computed buildable area may change. Proven against a real production snapshot.** A role is a LABEL over edges and is never an input to a measurement; nothing in the role layer writes a setback VALUE, so the invariant holds by construction. To make that *provable* rather than merely argued, `offsetPolygon` (and `lineIntersect`) were lifted verbatim out of `SitePlanner.jsx` into `lib/parcelOffset.js` — the one geometric statement this app cannot get wrong had lived as a private function in a 20,000-line component and was only ever checkable by rendering. `test/fixtures/weldParcelProduction.json` is the owner's Weld County parcel read straight out of `planyr_production` (`sites.id sms7v3ua7ksy`, 60 vertices, geometry only — no owner name or address rides into the repo), and the tests assert on it that the per-edge setbacks stay byte-identical and that the ring `offsetPolygon` produces is `toEqual`-identical across role assignment AND reassignment. The browser harness asserts the same thing on the live DOM, and separately that the ring DOES move once a number is typed.

> **Tests / verification.** New `test/setbackRoles.test.js` — **22** tests (auto-assignment incl. winding-agnosticism and degenerate rings, correction, the four-row partition, and the NON-NEGOTIABLE on the production snapshot). New headless harness `ui-audit/verify-setback-roles.mjs` driving that same production geometry in Chromium — **15/15**: By role is the default, four rows in the ordinance's vocabulary, all 15 sides carry a resolved role, a role is reassignable and the By-role rows follow, one Front input reaches every Front side and no other, every chip names its role, and the drawn ring is identical throughout. `ui-audit/verify-parcel-declutter.mjs` updated and **20/20** (chip non-overlap is now a box test, which is the real property). Full suite **6797** green · lint **0 errors** · build green. Bundle: attributable growth **+5.9 KB** on the site route (measured against a stashed baseline build — the other ~24 KB above the recorded baseline is pre-existing drift on `main`), inside the headroom band; tracked by B1064.
- **⏳ Live steps pending (V548).** Everything above ran logged-out on real production geometry. What a browser here cannot settle is how the role chips read at working zooms on the signed-in Weld plan with imagery under them, and whether the auto-assignment reads sensibly on a plan that HAS roads drawn (the sandbox harness has none, so the Street-side branch is exercised only by unit tests and by a manual reassignment).

### B216 (×2) — Harden edge-run setbacks for IRREGULAR parcels: concave inward placement + gentle-curve grouping — and now TIGHT-curve chip grouping `[Site Planner]` (bug/task) #site-planner #ui — follow-up to B214/B215  *(owner-requested edge-case pass 2026-06-19; minted **B216** — highest B# across both files was B215, so this is the real next free ID)*
`[ ]` **⏳ RE-OPENED 2026-07-30 — see the recurrence block below. Originally done 2026-06-19 (branch `claude/sharp-edison-7gdn3y`).** Edge-case testing on irregular parcels (L-shapes, flag lots, curved frontage, dense survey boundaries, triangles) surfaced two issues, both fixed. **(1) Concave inward placement (refines B215):** the setback pill / boundary-dim fan chose the inboard side by stepping *toward the parcel centroid* — but on a concave / L-shaped / flag-lot parcel the centroid can sit in a notch (or outside the polygon), so a pill was thrown to the WRONG side (outside the lot). Replaced with a **point-in-ring test** (a small step that must land INSIDE the boundary) via a new `inwardScreenNormal` helper (computed in feet, mapped to screen), used by the per-side pill, the per-segment pill, AND the run-length dimension — correct on any shape. **(2) Gentle-curve grouping (refines B214):** `edgeRuns` now chains each edge to the **PREVIOUS** edge's bearing (was the run's FIRST edge), so a gently curved frontage (a few degrees per segment) or survey noise on a nominally-straight line groups into **ONE** side (one setback, one pill, one dimension) instead of many; a genuine corner still breaks the run, and a TIGHT curve (each segment turning beyond tolerance) correctly stays per-segment.
> **Tests:** +2 `edgeRuns` unit tests (gentle-curve groups; tight-curve splits — **14** in `test/edgeRuns.test.js`). New headless harness `ui-audit/verify-edge-runs-irregular.mjs` (L-shape, flag lot, tight + gentle curved frontage, dense 12-vertex survey boundary, triangle) — **19/19**: every setback pill lands inside the lot (the concave fix), every run-length dim outside, no NaN, and the shallow arc groups to 4 sides (not 17). lint **0 errors** · **411 tests** · build green; the original **B213–B215 acceptance still 7/7** (the chain change keeps the 3-segment-east-side case at 4 sides). Verified **V48**. **Dedup:** not a new feature — hardens the B214 run-grouping + B215 fan placement for irregular geometry; same canonical `pc.setbacks` model.
`[ ]` **⏳ IMPLEMENTED (recurrence ×2) — V547 PENDING.**
- Verify: live
- Origin: filed 2026-07-30 from chat (owner block, provisional NEW-1)
- **Recurrence: 2026-07-30 (×2) — owner, Weld County CO (breadcrumb `2221 E LAMAR BLVD STE 790 / Concept A`, Unincorporated, 40.348437 / -104.981121, ~62.7 ac, every edge 25 ft), with two screenshots.** The boundary follows a subdivision edge with a long curved run, so it carries dozens of short segments. One curved corner rendered **about twelve overlapping "25′" chips stacked into an unreadable pile**, and the whole parcel carried thirty-plus. Owner: *"the setbacks, that's way too many… this is completely ridiculous"*, and — the line that makes this a recurrence rather than a new number — *"I thought we had already fixed it."*
- **Why the ×1 fix could not hold, stated plainly.** B216 chained each edge to the PREVIOUS edge's bearing so a GENTLE curve groups into one side, and then **explicitly ruled that a TIGHT curve "correctly stays per-segment"** because each of those segments really is its own straight side. That is geometrically true and cartographically wrong: a filleted corner digitized as ~12 segments turns ~7.5° each — *just* past the ±7° tolerance — so every fillet segment became its own side, its own chip, and its own row in the panel. The ×1 verdict was the bug.
- **The fix — a separate, coarser grouping for the LABEL layer; `edgeRuns` is untouched.** New pure `lib/setbackChips.js` (`setbackChipRuns`) collapses **contiguous edges that share a setback VALUE** into one labelled run, breaking only where the run's **direction spread** — the spread of the running SIGNED heading since the run began — passes ~50°. Signed-and-spread (not a per-edge tolerance) is what makes all four real cases right at once: survey noise never accumulates, a filleted right-angle breaks exactly ONCE mid-fillet (a rounded rectangle reads as four sides), a hard corner breaks instantly as it always did, and a long arc breaks about every 50° of sweep, which is honest. The chip anchors at the **midpoint of the longest edge in its run** (the owner's rule) and that edge's length is its declutter priority.
- **Two screen-space guards on top, both re-decided every frame off the live zoom** (new shared `lib/screenDeclutter.js`): a chip whose anchor edge is shorter than ~26 px on screen is not drawn at all, and no two drawn chips may sit within ~40 px of each other — the lower-priority one drops, so the chip on the longest edge always survives a pile. Both are display-only: nothing is deleted, the dropped chip's edges keep their setback, and zooming in progressively reveals detail instead of painting everything at every scale. The SAME helper thins the parcel side-length dimension numbers (which piled up identically) and the vertex handles (B1185) — one declutter helper, reused, never a second one.
- **`edgeRuns.js` is deliberately NOT changed.** It still owns the ±7° geometric-SIDE model that drives run-length dimensions and B912 side resizing; every B214/B215/B216 test passes untouched. A filleted corner is a dozen geometric sides but ONE thing to label — the two models are different questions and now have different code.
- **Verified here.** +29 unit tests (`test/parcelDeclutter.test.js`) including the fillet repro, the noisy-survey case, the value-change break, the seam merge, the long-arc case and the anchor-edge rule. New headless harness `ui-audit/verify-parcel-declutter.mjs` (a 32-vertex Weld-County-shaped parcel, all edges 25 ft) — **16/16**: the chips collapse to **4** for 32 edges, no two drawn chips are closer than the separation at ANY zoom, zooming in reveals more detail, zero JS errors. Screenshots saved. lint 0 errors · 6,717 tests · build green.
- **What the sandbox cannot prove (→ V547):** how it reads on the owner's ACTUAL Weld County parcel with the aerial under it — the bar he set is a screenshot of that curved corner reading cleanly, not a count.

`[ ]` **⏳ IMPLEMENTED — V547 PENDING.**

- Origin: filed 2026-07-30 from chat
- **Report.** The "Parcel 62.7 ac" badge rendered *"well to the right of the parcel, floating over neighbouring land rather than over the parcel it labels."*
- **Root cause, confirmed in the code rather than guessed.** The anchor was the ring's plain **vertex average** — not a centre of anything. It is pulled toward whichever side was digitized with the most points, and on this parcel the subdivision edge carries dozens of short segments while the opposite side is two long ones, so the average slid hard toward the dense edge and off the lot. (The owner's own diagnosis named the area centroid; on a long bent strip that one can land outside the polygon too, so neither was safe.)
- **The fix.** New pure `lib/polylabel.js` — the **pole of inaccessibility**, the centre of the largest circle that fits inside the ring, found by the classic best-first quadtree search. It is always inside, it sits in the visually fattest part of the shape, and it leaves the most clear room around the plate. Written out (~40 lines of arithmetic) rather than added as a runtime dependency, and memoised per points array so a hundreds-of-vertex parcel pays for the search once, not once per frame. The user's dragged `labelOffset` still applies on top; `centroid` remains the fallback for a degenerate ring.
- **Verified here.** Unit tests: the dense-on-one-side strip (the exact report — vertex average lands on the dense edge, the pole lands in the body of the strip), a deep U whose AREA centroid is provably outside while the pole is inside, an L, a flag lot and a triangle, memoisation, and degenerate input answered rather than thrown on. Harness: the badge's centre is inside the parcel ring on the 32-vertex Weld shape. lint 0 · full suite green · build green.

### B1156 — `f` now goes to REAL fullscreen, not just a hidden header `[Shell / UI]` (feature) #ui #site-planner  *(owner chat 2026-07-30, provisional NEW-1. Minted **B1156** via `git fetch origin main && npm run next-id -- --against-main`, LATE — as the last step before push. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open + ⏳ Verify + Done for `fullscreen`, `chrome-hide`, `AppHeader`, `F key`: the shortcut has existed since the header was built and no item has ever owned it. Net-new.)*
`[ ]` **⏳ IMPLEMENTED — V536 PENDING.** F asks the browser for real fullscreen and hides the header on top of it; 17/17 headless checks pass.
- Verify: live
- Origin: filed 2026-07-30 from chat
- **Report.** Michael: pressing `f` should go to true fullscreen. What it did was **chrome-hide, not fullscreen** — `setFullscreen(v => !v)` collapsed the header to nothing and rendered a floating exit button, while the browser tab strip, the address bar and the OS taskbar all stayed exactly where they were.
- **The fix.** The keypress is a user activation, so `requestFullscreen()` is called straight out of the key handler — on **`document.documentElement`**, deliberately never a sub-element: fullscreening a subtree hides every `position: fixed` overlay that lives outside it, the exit button included. The existing chrome-hide is KEPT on top, so the result is edge to edge.
- **The four things that make it hold:**
  - **A refused request still hides the chrome.** `requestFullscreen` returns a promise that can reject (no activation, a permissions policy, an iframe without `allow="fullscreen"`), and iOS Safari has no fullscreen for a non-video element at all. Both paths fall back to today's behaviour rather than leaving a keypress that appears to do nothing.
  - **The header is DERIVED from the document, never guessed.** A `fullscreenchange` listener (plus the webkit-prefixed spelling) drives the React state off `document.fullscreenElement`, so Esc, the browser's own exit affordance, or anything else that ends fullscreen brings the chrome back with it. Entering never sets the state directly — one owner, so it cannot race the event that reports it.
  - **Esc is not fought.** In real fullscreen the browser consumes it and exits; `fullscreenchange` then restores the header. The existing Escape handler now runs only in the fallback mode, where nothing else would.
  - **The exit button calls `document.exitFullscreen()`** in native mode, and only falls back to plain state in the refused/unsupported mode.
- **A regression this session's own harness caught, before it could ship.** `fullscreenchange` is a DOCUMENT event, so **every** mounted workspace header hears it — and with workspaces kept mounted-but-hidden, all of them collapsed and each rendered its own floating exit button (two, stacked). The listener now takes the SAME keep-alive gate the keyboard shortcut has (`headerRef.current.offsetParent === null` → ignore). The gate at the shortcut is untouched.
- **The viewport really does change size, so both surfaces were CHECKED rather than assumed.** Entering: the planner canvas grows into the reclaimed height (800 → 880 px tall) and the Leaflet basemap container re-fits with it (1334 → 1466); leaving, both return exactly. The drawing stays welded to the imagery through both transitions — the B1141 registration shift reads 0.103 / 0.528 px, inside the sub-pixel band, in and out — and the view transform is bit-identical across the round trip, so B1122's VIEWPORT-STABLE fix is not regressed. **Note for anyone re-checking:** the map container does NOT track the canvas by a fixed offset (it is the canvas plus twice the overscan, and the overscan follows the drawable element count), so asserting a constant difference is asserting a false invariant — assert the registration shift.
- **Verified here (`ui-audit/verify-new1-fullscreen.mjs`, 17/17):** F puts the document ROOT into fullscreen · the header collapses · exactly ONE exit button exists · canvas and basemap both re-fit and stay welded · exiting via the browser restores the header unprompted · the ✕ leaves real fullscreen · a refused request falls back to chrome-hide · Esc and the ✕ both still work in that fallback · typing “f” in a text field toggles nothing. Plus 6 source-shape guards in `test/renderBudgetMemos.test.js`.
- **What a headless browser cannot show, and is the whole reason V536 exists:** that the tab strip, the address bar and the OS taskbar are genuinely gone. It has none of them to hide.

### B1157 — Dragging a polygon vertex lagged: every pointer move re-ran a 13,700-line render body `[Site Planner]` (bug) #site-planner #perf  *(owner chat 2026-07-30, provisional NEW-2. Minted **B1157** via `--against-main`, late. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open + ⏳ Verify + Done for `vertex`, `drag`, `lag`, `frame`, `rAF`, `coalesce`, and the perf family B1040/B1042/B1063/B1064/B1086/B1121: **B1086** is the frame-MEASUREMENT trap (a starved sample from a hidden tab), not this; nothing owns the per-move commit rate. Net-new.)*
`[ ]` **⏳ IMPLEMENTED — V537 PENDING.** A 40-move burst delivered faster than the display refreshes went from **40 render commits / 1,642 DOM writes** to **1 / 25**, measured before and after.
- Verify: live
- Origin: filed 2026-07-30 from chat
- **Repro.** Select a polygon (a parcel, an element footprint, or a measurement) and drag one of its points. Expected: it tracks the cursor. Actual: it trails behind.
- **Cause, two layers, both in `SitePlanner.jsx`:** (1) `onMove` called `setCursor(fp)` **unconditionally on every pointermove**, with no frame coalescing anywhere on that path — and the two lines directly above it write refs with comments that say *ref-only, no setState in this hot path*. At 60–240 Hz that re-ran the entire render body and rebuilt the whole JSX tree for a coordinate readout. (2) The vertex branches then setState per move on top of that, each invalidating geometry the render body derives — the O(n²) parcel overlap + dissolve (ear-clip triangulation and Sutherland–Hodgman per pair, no memo in `lib/polyClip.js`) and the `els.forEach` metrics loop whose `curbAreaOf` scans the whole array per element.
- **The fix — one keyed frame job per surface.** A later job with the same key REPLACES the earlier one, so a frame commits at most one cursor update and one geometry update. This is safe because every one of these writes is **absolute and idempotent** (put vertex *i* at this point / the cursor is here), never an increment: a dropped intermediate is a frame that was never going to be painted, not a lost update. The readout additionally carries no correctness risk at all — it is a display value and nothing derives geometry from it.
- **Gesture end is where a coalescer usually goes wrong, so it is handled explicitly.** `onUp` and `abortGesture` **flush synchronously via `flushSync`** before any release logic runs. That matters twice: the one release path that judges the FINAL ring (the reshaped-building self-crossing / zero-area check, which rebuilds the dock frame off it) now reads `stateRef.current.els` rather than its own render closure — a closure captured at the previous render cannot see a commit made microseconds ago — and `flushElems()`, which hands the settled canvas to the element-sync engine, sees the real final geometry rather than one move short of where the finger let go. On an abort the flush happens BEFORE `cancelActiveMove`, so the ordering is exactly the old one and a pending job can never land back on the canvas after the revert. The frame is cancelled on unmount.
- **Third fix, unrelated to coalescing:** while idle in select mode with no selection, every pointermove spread, sorted and reversed the whole element array to find the hovered building. Now one linear scan, no allocation — and provably the same answer, because `byZ` is a total order (it ends in an id comparison), so "the max under `byZ`" is the same single element the sort-reverse-find returned.
- **MEASURED, before and after, with the tab visible — `ui-audit/verify-new2-vertex-drag.mjs` (new).** It reuses the standing harness's reference scenario, its frame sampler, and critically its **refusal to report a median it cannot stand behind** (`lib/frameSampling.mjs` — the B1086 trap: rAF is suspended in a backgrounded tab and says nothing about it, and a PARTLY throttled run still yields a plausible-looking number).
  - **Frame time is UNCHANGED and that is reported honestly, not spun:** 16.7 ms median / 16.7 p90 on both builds, at 60–63 fps with the tab visible. The reference scenario is deliberately LIGHTER than the owner's real plan (its own header says so) so both sit on the vsync floor. Frame time cannot separate these builds here, and claiming otherwise would be dishonest.
  - **What CAN be measured is the mechanism, and it is decisive.** A React commit applies its DOM writes in one synchronous batch, so one MutationObserver callback ≈ one commit — which needs no app instrumentation, and is therefore the only kind of probe that can produce a BEFORE number from the base build. Delivering 40 pointermoves **one per macrotask** (a MessageChannel, so no 4 ms clamp — the 120–240 Hz case real hardware produces): **base 40 commits / 1,642 DOM writes → after 1 commit / 25 DOM writes.**
  - **A note for whoever runs this next:** a Playwright scripted drag awaits between events, so it delivers at most one move per painted frame — precisely the case where coalescing has nothing to do. Both builds read 121 commits over 120 moves on that phase. The burst phase exists because of that.
- **Not touched, deliberately:** the pan path (B1122's layout-effect transform), the B65 anti-flash ghost, and every non-vertex drag mode.

### B1158 — The yield/drainage derivation ran on every render even with no panel open `[Site Planner / Yield]` (task) #yield #perf #site-planner  *(owner chat 2026-07-30, provisional NEW-3. Minted **B1158** via `--against-main`, late. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open + ⏳ Verify + Done for `leftPanel`, `drainage`, `gate`, `lazy panel`, and the B1064/B1042/B1126/B1146 family: **B1064** is the CODE-SPLITTING half (ship less JS), **B1126** is computed-but-never-RENDERED as a class; this is the third, distinct thing — code that ships and runs but feeds nothing on screen. Net-new.)*
`[ ]` **⏳ IMPLEMENTED — V538 PENDING.** ~400 lines of stormwater derivation, including the entire `drainage` object, now run only when something actually reads them.
- Verify: live
- Origin: filed 2026-07-30 from chat
- **Finding.** `leftPanel` starts at `null` — no panel is docked on first paint. The panels' JSX is correctly gated, but the derivation feeding them was not: the pond stage models, the storage reconciliation, the drawdown, the mitigation band ledger, the administrator, the apron, the cut/fill balance and the `drainage` object literal itself all ran on **every** render, including every frame of a drag, for surfaces nobody had open.
- **The fix is GATING, not memoising — and it is demand-driven rather than a hand-written list of open panels.** `drainFacts()` builds the bundle fresh, **once per render**, the first time a consumer reads it, and caches nothing across renders (a plain `let` in the render body). So a gated value is either computed from this render's inputs or not rendered at all: it is structurally incapable of holding a stale engineering number, which is the only failure mode that would matter here.
- **Why demand-driven and not `leftPanel === "yield" || …`:** a hand-written gate can forget a consumer, and the two non-obvious ones are exactly the kind that get forgotten. `exportCtx()` closes over `drainage` and is called at Download time, BEFORE `exportPass` is set — so a panel-open gate would have silently stripped the stormwater content out of an exported sheet (a PDF-PARITY break with no error anywhere). The pond inspector's `drainage?.floodFailed` is on a selection-driven surface, not a panel at all. Reading the value is what triggers the work, so neither can be missed.
- **All five consumers audited and converted:** `exportCtx()` · `printMetricPairs` · `printStormwaterBars` (PDF-PARITY, both) · the Yield panel prop · the pond inspector. A source guard in `test/renderBudgetMemos.test.js` fails if any bare `drainage` binding reappears at a call site.
- **The 400-line body is byte-identical and keeps its original indentation**, on purpose, so the diff that introduced this shows the gate and nothing else.

### B1160 — No canvas backing store was ever released, anywhere in the tree `[Platform / perf]` (task) #perf #infra #doc-review #site-planner  *(owner chat 2026-07-30, provisional NEW-5. Minted **B1160** via `--against-main`, late. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open + ⏳ Verify + Done for `canvas`, `memory`, `backing store`, `toDataURL`, and the B1121/B1063/B1064 memory family: **B1121** is TILE memory (Leaflet grid layers), this is CANVAS memory (offscreen 2D buffers) — a different allocator and a different set of files. Net-new.)*
`[ ]` **⏳ IMPLEMENTED — V539 PENDING.** Nine offscreen-canvas sites now hand their pixels back at the point of last read.
- Verify: live
- Origin: filed 2026-07-30 from chat
- **Finding.** `canvas.width = canvas.height = 0` appeared **zero times** in the entire tree. Every offscreen canvas was left to the garbage collector — and a canvas's pixel buffer is not ordinary JS memory: it lives in the renderer/GPU allocator, outside the JS heap, and the GC tracks it poorly. A few hundred bytes of JS object can hold tens of megabytes of external pixels alive with no pressure to collect them. That is exactly the owner's signature: **~555 MB of tab memory against a JS heap that peaked at ~134 MB.** A heap snapshot cannot see this half, which is why "not a leak, steady-state high" was an honest reading of an instrument that was looking in the wrong place.
- **Behaviourally inert by construction.** The release goes AFTER the last read — after the `toDataURL` / `toBlob` / `getImageData` / copying `drawImage` that has already taken the pixels. Nothing downstream reads the canvas again.
- **Sites, worst first:** `doc-review/lib/pdf.js` `renderInto` (called from `renderDetail` on a 140 ms leading-edge throttle **during a continuous pan**, so a minute of panning was allocating hundreds of full-density buffers — released on the blit AND on the superseded-frame bail) · `site-planner/lib/overlayPdf.js` `renderPageCanvas`, both callers (up to `MAX_RERASTER_DIM` square — an 8192×5500 RGBA buffer is roughly 180 MB, and it re-renders on every zoom-band change per PDF overlay) · `exportSheet.js` ×3 (the stitched aerial, the PNG sheet, the print-DPI PDF sheet) · `dxf/dxfOverlay.js` · `doc-review/lib/pdf.js` page-to-image and page-to-ImageData · `mitigationHeatmap.js` · `image.js`.
- **The one that is released somewhere else, on purpose:** `renderPageToOcrCanvas` HANDS its canvas to the caller, so it must not release it. The OCR runner does, in a `finally`, so a recogniser failure cannot leak it either. Releasing a canvas you have handed out is the way to get this wrong.
- **Deliberately DUPLICATED rather than shared.** `releaseCanvas` exists once per workspace (`site-planner/lib/` and `doc-review/lib/`, byte-identical, each pointing at the other). A single module under `src/shared/` is reachable from both routes, which makes Rollup hoist it into a chunk of its own — measured: `siteRouteChunks` 7 → 8, a real budget breach for four lines of code. The budget was right and the module moved; the ceiling was not raised.
- **The number this is aimed at needs Chrome's own instruments on a real session** — per-tab memory in the Task Manager across a 60 s continuous pan in Review, and `performance.measureUserAgentSpecificMemory()`, which breaks Canvas out as its own type. That is V539, and it is the point of the item.

### B1161 — MapFinder keeps a second Leaflet map that never got the B1121 tile cap `[Site Planner / map]` (task) #perf #gis #site-planner  *(owner chat 2026-07-30, provisional NEW-6. Minted **B1161** via `--against-main`, late. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open + ⏳ Verify + Done for `tile cache`, `keepBuffer`, `MapFinder`, `overlayRefs`, `B1121`: **B1121 / PR #855** capped the PLANNER's two layers and is Done. The Map view has its own map and got none of it — this is the missed half, filed under its own number because B1121's fix is not recurring, it simply never reached here.)*
`[ ]` **⏳ IMPLEMENTED — V540 PENDING.** Both Map-view tile layers are capped, the hidden map sheds tiles and releases its raster overlays, and the 45 s re-probe no longer runs for a map nobody is looking at.
- Verify: live
- Origin: filed 2026-07-30 from chat
- **Finding.** `SitePlannerApp` hides map mode with `display: none` and deliberately does **not** unmount it (its comment says so). So for the whole session: the imagery layer and the labels layer had no cache ceiling at all; `overlayRefs` held a **duplicate** set of every enabled GIS raster overlay, separate from the planner's, each keeping a painted full-viewport `<img>` alive; and a `setInterval(sync, 45000)` kept re-syncing — and re-fetching — those overlays. Only `invalidateSize` and clearing the selection were gated on `visible`.
- **The fix, all eviction:** `boundTileCache` + `tileCacheLimit` on both layers, exactly as the planner does · on `visible === false` the tile caches are squeezed to a token ceiling and every esri raster overlay is torn down through the same `releaseLayer` the planner uses at toggle-off (`syncOverlayLayers` rebuilds whatever is still enabled on the way back in) · the interval is gated on `visible`, and the effect re-runs on it, so returning to the map syncs immediately and then resumes the heartbeat.
- **Nothing here changes what is DRAWN.** `detectRetina` is untouched — the owner has ruled out any retina downgrade — no cap on how much can be drawn, no spinner, no decimation. `capTileCache` never evicts a CURRENT tile, so it cannot punch a hole in the view; everything shed re-fetches on demand.
- **The cap is sized from the keepBuffer these layers ACTUALLY use** (Leaflet's default of 2 — neither layer passes one), rather than borrowing the planner's tuned value. Adding a keepBuffer here would have made them retain MORE, which is the wrong direction for a memory item.

### B1162 — Two GIS caches grew without bound, and one could never evict its biggest entries `[Site Planner / GIS]` (task) #perf #gis #site-planner  *(owner chat 2026-07-30, provisional NEW-7. Minted **B1162** via `--against-main`, late. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open + ⏳ Verify + Done for `gisCache`, `gisFetch`, `coalesce`, `LRU`, `parcelSnapshot`: B445 owns the cache PROXY, B629 owns the parcel snapshot FEATURE; neither owns the retention of either map. Net-new.)*
`[ ]` **⏳ IMPLEMENTED — V541 PENDING.** Both caches are bounded; the third candidate is INSTRUMENTED rather than capped blind, on purpose.
- Verify: live
- Origin: filed 2026-07-30 from chat
- **(a) `gisFetch.js` `_recent` — the request-coalescing map.** Entries were only ever overwritten by the same key or wiped by `clearCoalesced()`, which is called by the tests and by **nothing in app code**. The key embeds the bbox, so a panning session minted unique keys indefinitely, each pinning a whole parsed ArcGIS response whose usefulness expired after five seconds. Now swept on write (the entries were already timestamped) plus a hard entry cap as a backstop. Behaviourally invisible: an entry past its TTL was already never returned, and the coalescing window itself is unchanged and unit-tested both sides of the boundary.
- **(b) `gisCache.js` L1 — the in-memory tier.** The localStorage tier is bounded twice over (512 KB per entry, 3 MB total, `evictOldest` enforcing both). L1 had no bound at all — and the two interact badly: a payload over `maxEntryBytes` **returns early without ever entering the store**, so it never appears in `ourKeys()`, so `evictOldest` can never reach it. The >512 KB GeoJSON responses — the biggest objects in the app — were precisely the ones that lived forever. L1 now has an entry cap with the same recency-touch idiom `pondGeom`'s `_detMemo` uses (a read re-inserts, so insertion order IS the LRU order). A miss is only ever a re-fetch through the existing stale-while-revalidate path, or a rehydrate from the durable tier — it can never change an answer.
- **(c) `parcelSnapshot.js` `loaded` — MEASURED, NOT CAPPED, and that is the finding.** It holds county → the full GeoJSON feature array and is cleared only by the test helper. It could plausibly be tens of megabytes per county, but **the size could not be established from source**, and capping a fallback the map depends on, blind, trades a memory number for a blank map over a county whose live server is down. So `snapshotFootprint()` reports what is actually retained, per county and in total, on demand and never on a render path; it is reachable from a real session's console as `__planyrSnapshotFootprint()`, because a signed-in browser with real county data is the only place the number exists. It is deliberately read-only — a guard asserts it evicts nothing. **If the number justifies a cap, the eviction is nearly free:** the durable copy is already in IndexedDB, so an evicted county rehydrates locally. That work is not done here.
### B1155 — Where a road SPLITS on a curve the branch never resolved into one surface: the outline stepped and one armpit got NO curb return at all `[Site Planner / roadGeometry]` (bug) #site-planner #road #ui  *(owner chat block 2026-07-30, provisional NEW-2, off the same screenshot: "you can see where the road splits on the bottom of it, that it's not splitting correctly." DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open + ⏳ Verify + Done across the whole junction family (**B945/B946/B949/B953/B964/B971/B989/B1005/B1006/B1008/B1009/B1010/B1011/B1012/B1013/B1015/B1017**, plus `dissolveRings` / `driveJunction` / `outlineCut` / `teeGeometry` / `nodeJunction`): every one of them builds the junction AT a stored control point with tangents read off the CHORDS. Not one addresses the case where the drawn centerline does not pass through that point at all — which is what a fillet at a junction vertex does. NET-NEW; it cross-references the family rather than re-opening any of them, and it is the assumption they all shared.)* *(RENUMBERED on merge: minted B1149/B1150/V533 against a fresh `origin/main`, but the B779 mint gate found B1153/V534 already claimed on other in-flight branches — the documented late-bind race, caught RED before merge exactly as designed. Code, tests and the harness carry the provisional NEW-1/NEW-2 labels throughout, so only heading lines moved.)*
`[ ]` **⏳ IMPLEMENTED — V535 PENDING.** Verified headless through the REAL render path on the owner's REAL plan; what is owed is the signed-in cloud read path, the PDF export, and the deployed build.
- Verify: live
- Origin: filed 2026-07-30 from chat
- **READ THE HISTORY FIRST, and this is what it says.** This family has been "fixed" nine times and come back nine times, and every attempt shared one testing mistake — a MOCK of two STRAIGHT roads meeting at a tee. On a straight road the chord between two control points IS the road, so a chord-built junction looks perfect and a chord-based hit test reaches everything. Both defects in this pair are invisible to that mock by construction. So nothing here was declared fixed against one.
- **The failing case, found in the owner's real data rather than guessed.** Goose Creek **"Plan 1 (copy)"** (production site `sms69x8rb2qk`) is the plan in the screenshot — identified from the geometry, not by elimination: its 36' aisle `e1454749rlpiva` runs ~900 ft east off the 100' aisle, turns **~88°** through a vertex whose stored treatment is *unset* (so it defaults to a 25 ft **arc**), and the branch `e1454750rlpiva` is welded to that same vertex heading south. The branch's other end also drive-tees into a truck court, and so does the through road's — the third topology the brief names, present in the same cluster.
- **Root cause: the junction node is not on the road.** A junction is detected at a stored control POINT, and every arm's tangent, half-width offset and curb-return corner is measured from there. But a fillet at that vertex carries the DRAWN centerline clear of it — **9.9 ft** here, on a road whose pavement is 18.5 ft from centerline to back of curb. Two consequences, both visible in the owner's screenshot: the branch's edges sit ~10 ft inboard of the through road's, so the outline STEPS through the split; and the two through arms, read off the chords, come out **179.1°** apart — over the 178° "flat" threshold — so that whole armpit is skipped as a straight run-through and gets **no curb return at all**, leaving a hard square corner beside a clean one.
- **Fix — a junction is where two centerlines MEET, so make them meet.** `roadJunctionVerticesOf` collects every vertex another road tees onto; `roadCenterline` gains `sharpAt`, which renders those corners as hard corners, so the through road passes through the node its branch is welded to. The rounding that the fillet used to provide is then supplied where it belongs — by the curb returns — which is what `nodeJunction`'s new `roundOwnCorner` is for: with the vertex flattened, the road's own buffer miters that corner, so the junction must round it too or a three-way intersection ends up with one square corner and two curb returns. Standard civil practice, and it dissolves cleanly at any angle because nothing is measured against a line the pavement doesn't follow.
- **It is a NO-OP on every straight tee.** `arcCorner` already degenerates to a pass-through on a collinear vertex, and two nearly-opposite through arms are skipped as flat either way — so an ordinary tee renders byte-identically (asserted directly, and by the untouched B1011 suite). Every road-geometry read takes the same set — pavement, curb stripes, paved-area figure and length — so they describe one road.
- **Guards that FAIL on current main, which is the whole point.** `e2e/road-split-curved.spec.js` seeds the owner's real plan and asserts through the live render path: the branch and its through road are ONE region; the outline turns no more than 30° anywhere within a lane of the node (a curb return turns a few degrees per step — a right angle is a step or a notch); BOTH armpits carry a real tessellated return; no sliver holes; the square tee and the drive junctions are unaffected; building z-order preserved. **Proven red on main**: the same spec, run against a build of `main`, fails exactly those two tests (`wedges` 1 instead of 2, worst outline turn well past a right angle) and passes the other five. `test/roadCurvedJunction.test.js` carries the same in pure form, including two tests that DOCUMENT main's numbers so the guard can never go vacuous.
- **Verified here, through the real render path, on the real plan.** `ui-audit/verify-road-split-curved.mjs` parks the viewport on the curved oblique split, a square tee, the branch-plus-drive-junction cluster, the second tee, and the whole network, and shoots each **twice — once at working zoom and once with the pavement fill knocked down to a third**. The faded pass is deliberate: a residual stacked edge is invisible at full opacity, and that is exactly how earlier attempts in this family passed while still broken. Result: one uniform tone, one continuous curb line carried around the junction, a real radius return into the branch on both sides, no step, no notch, no scoop, no balloon, and no darker patch anywhere at reduced opacity. Before/after screenshots of the same junction are in `ui-audit/screens/road-split-curved/` (gitignored — regenerate with the harness).
- **PDF-PARITY.** The export clones the live DOM, so the dissolved network rides along unchanged; PNG export was driven headless from the seeded plan and the roads compose as one continuous surface on the sheet. The PDF path on a real signed-in plan is part of V535.
- **Sandbox evidence.** `npm test` 6520 green · lint 0 errors · build green · doc-pointer / MAP / backlog-index / panel-copy gates green · `e2e/road-split-curved.spec.js` 7/7 · the pre-existing `e2e/road-tee-oblique.spec.js` 8/8 unchanged.
- **Bundle budget — +1.6 KB total JS, and it STAYS (the `perf-bundle-audit` rule wants a reason, not a shrug).** `perf-bundle-audit` passes with 76.1 KB of band left; the growth is the segment-ownership tagging in `roadCenterline` plus the junction-vertex map, both of which are the fix itself rather than incidental weight. There is no cheap deferral to pay it back with — this code is on the canvas render path by definition, and the standing deferral candidates are already taken by B1064.
- **What is owed (V535).** The deployed build, signed in, on the owner's actual Goose Creek and Tsakiris records via the cloud read path (not a seeded local fixture), plus the PDF export at the split and a zoom sweep. See `VERIFICATION.md` → V535. `Blocker: auth`, `Blocker: real-data`.

`[x]` **Shipped — parked in ⏳ Verify for the export half (V534).**
