- **What was wrong, concretely.** The area label was ONE run-on line — `250,000 sf · 5.74 ac · 2,100′ perim` — three unrelated quantities at identical weight separated by middots, painted as raw haloed text at the polygon centroid. Nothing was dominant; both area units competed when only one matters at any scale; an abbreviation carried the headline's emphasis; and haloed text on photography is the least legible option available.
- **(a) One dominant value, the detail subordinate.** Line 1 is the headline in large tabular figures, line 2 the supporting detail in smaller muted text, with the user's own label riding ABOVE as a name line — never concatenated into the number.
- **(b) The headline UNIT is chosen by magnitude.** Below one acre it leads in square feet with acres demoted; at or above, it leads in acres with square feet demoted. Never both at equal weight. One acre exactly is the flip point — a fuzzed threshold would only make it unpredictable.
- **(c) A real chip, not haloed text.** A rounded plate with a hairline keyline in the measurement's own colour, carrying `data-print-chip="measure"` — the parcel acreage chip's contract. `exportSheet`'s restyle now selects on the ATTRIBUTE rather than one of its values, so both chip kinds go through ONE print treatment and cannot drift: the plate is dropped on paper, the text becomes dark haloed exhibit annotation, and the detail line stays subordinate (`data-chip-sub`).
- **(d) Per-edge segment lengths, ON the edges** of a polygon or polyline, upright at any bearing, gated separately from the summary chip on the shared `detailLabelVisible` detail tier — the same gate every other width/length callout on the drawing already uses, so this is one convention rather than a new hand-tuned number. Skipped for a two-point distance, whose one segment IS the headline.
- **(e) Collision-aware and draggable.** The chip is laid out by `labelLayout.layoutLabels` — placed FIRST (a measurement is deliberate), then its boxes seeded as obstacles so element labels yield around it exactly as they do around a parcel badge. It shortens under collision (the detail line drops) but is **never hidden**: a number the user asked for is shortened, not silently dropped. Dragging it stores a `labelOffset` in feet on the measurement and draws a leader back to the anchor — the parcel chip's mechanic.
- **(f) One number convention everywhere.** Tabular figures, thousands separators, acres to two decimals, feet and square feet to zero, and the prime mark as the single feet notation — the app's convention on the rest of the drawing. `perim` is gone; "perimeter" is spelled out and subordinate. The properties panel reads the same formatters as the canvas, so panel, screen and paper cannot disagree.
- **(g) Length and count get the same treatment** — headline the distance or the count, breakdown underneath (`2 segments` · `items`).
- **A REAL BUG THE LIVE HARNESS CAUGHT, worth recording.** An area's grab layer is a transparent FILLED polygon over the whole shape. The chip was painted BEFORE it, so every press over the chip landed on the grab layer and moved the measurement instead of the label — the drag was completely dead. Found by the headless drag check, not by any unit test; fixed by painting the chip last, and guarded by an ordering assertion in `test/measureWiring.test.js`.
- **Code.** `lib/measureLabel.js` (new, pure: the label model, the magnitude-based unit choice, the formatters, `measureSegments`); the chip layout + render in `SitePlanner.jsx`; the one-selector restyle in `lib/exportSheet.js`.
- **Sandbox evidence.** 20 unit assertions in `test/measureLabel.test.js` (incl. a very long label + a 1,000-acre area proving no overflow) + 22 wiring guards + the headless harness at three zooms × light and dark: headline/detail/name split correct per mode, the keyline carrying each measurement's own colour, per-edge dimensions appearing close in, the chip dragging with a leader, and the export restyle proven over the live canvas clone (plate dropped, text dark + haloed, detail dimmed). `npm test` 6547 green · lint 0 errors · build green.
- **What is owed (V534).** A real PDF and PNG export of a signed-in plan over aerial imagery, checked for chip legibility and print parity against the parcel acreage chips — see `VERIFICATION.md` → V534.
- **THE BUNDLE BUDGET, paid the way the standing rule requires — and NO ceiling was touched.** The three items land at **+10.7 KB** across the bundle metrics, all of it synchronous render code inside `SitePlanner.jsx`. Two REAL deferrals shipped as the matching optimization: the metes-and-bounds **parser** was split out of `metesAndBounds.js` into `deedParse.js`, and the deed→parcel **alignment solver** (`deedAlign.js`) folded in with it, both now behind a cached dynamic import (`lib/deedLazy.js`, the `terrainLazy` `loadTerrain()`/`terrainNow()` shape). Neither is needed until the user is already in the deed workflow, which **already** loads its file reader on demand (`shared/files/docxText.js`, deferred by B1141 for this same reason). ### B1141 — Screen→ground transform sat ~1 CSS px off the imagery; hover and click now ride ONE welded transform `[Site Planner / GIS]` (bug) #site-planner #gis #coordinates  *(owner chat 2026-07-29, provisional NEW-2. Minted **B1141** via `--against-main`. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open + ⏳ Verify + Done across the map-lock family (`B65`, `B170`, `B182`, `B1043`, `B1062`, `B1088`, `B1095`, `B1096`, `B1122`, plus `lockOffsetPx`, `exactContainerPoint`, "residual", "quantisation"). **NOT a B170-class detectRetina defect** — the audit below rules that out by name. **It DOES overturn B1062's adjudication**, which measured this same one-pixel residual correctly and decided not to compensate; see "what B1062 got right and what it missed".)* *(RENUMBERED TWICE before merge, and the second time into a DELIBERATELY GAPPED block (B1140–B1143 / V530, skipping B1136–B1139): main merged three PRs while this branch was in flight — #860 took B1130/B1131/V523 and #862 took B1132/V524, each the number `next-id` had just reported. The B779/B780 uniqueness guard caught both collisions RED before merge, exactly as designed. Leaving a gap costs nothing (`next-id` reads the max) and breaks a loop that had already cost two renumber passes. Code and tests carried the provisional NEW-1/NEW-2 labels throughout, so only heading lines and three comment references ever moved.)*
`[ ]` **⏳ IMPLEMENTED — V530 PENDING.** Residual now **0.000 px** against an independent tile-grid ground truth at every zoom × device pixel ratio measured, including 2.15 and a fractional canvas width.
- Verify: live
- Origin: filed 2026-07-30 from chat
- **Report.** *"Sometimes when I place points — for a measurement or drawing something — it seems like my pointer is off … five, ten, fifteen feet off from where I'm actually clicking."* Measured live the same night against the Esri tile grid (each tile's z/x/y is in its URL and its screen rect is readable, so the true lat/lng of any screen pixel is computable without trusting Leaflet or us): **+3.67 ft N / −0.57 ft E at z18 (sd 0.09), +1.54 ft N / −4.36 ft E at z17** — about one CSS pixel, extremely repeatable, direction changing between zooms. A clean OFFSET, not noise and not a scale error. The reporting machine runs `devicePixelRatio` 2.15.
- **AUDIT-FIRST, all four lines the owner asked for, answered against the code:**
  - **(a) fractional devicePixelRatio — RULED OUT as the cause.** Nothing in the screen↔feet↔lat/lng chain rounds: `shared/viewport/viewportTransform.js` (`worldToScreen`/`screenToWorld`) has no `Math.round`/`floor`/`|0` at all, and `mapLock`'s projection has none either. `retinaForZoom` / `detectRetina` only choose tile size and zoom offset — they never touch the pointer chain, so this is **not** a B170-class defect. A fractional ratio still MATTERS, but indirectly: it makes fractional layout widths the norm, which is what (b) trips over.
  - **(b) container origin — one real contributor, and it is OURS.** `p2f` re-reads `getBoundingClientRect()` on every call, so there is no stale origin and no border/padding error. But the planner asks Leaflet to centre on the feet point under the DRAWING's centre (`size.w / 2`, a float off `getBoundingClientRect`) while `commit` lands that centre at the MAP's own half-size, which comes from the integer `clientWidth`. On a fractional CSS width those halves differ by up to a quarter pixel per axis. Leaflet's own whole-pixel snap (`_getNewPixelOrigin` ends in `._round()`, `panBy` rounds its offset) adds up to half a pixel more, twice over. Together: about one pixel per axis — exactly what was measured.
  - **(c) hover vs click — they ALREADY share one path, now proven rather than assumed.** Both funnel through `p2f`: the readout via `cursor` → `cursorLL`, every placement via `p2f(e.clientX, e.clientY)`. There was no second conversion to delete. The harness now measures BOTH ends independently anyway, because "the readout is right" was never proof that a placed point is.
  - **(d) snap/grid quantisation — a real, separate finding, filed as B1143.** Grid snap is OFF by default (`gridSize: 10, snap: false`) and is a deliberate opt-in. The boundary magnet is not: it fired unbounded in feet. See B1143.
- **THE FIX — weld the DRAWING to wherever the basemap actually landed, in the render only.** `mapLock.js` gains `tileNwFeet` / `basemapWrapPoint` / `registrationShift` / `sanitizeShift`; `SitePlanner` measures the residual after each of the three paths that can move the basemap (a resize/container commit, a gesture transform, a settle commit) and applies it as a CSS translate on the SVG canvas. Because `p2f` derives the cursor from that element's own bounding box, **the one transform corrects the render, the readout and every placed point together** — no second conversion to keep in step. `view.offX/offY` are NOT touched: the exactly-reversible pan V478 proved is preserved (`diagnose-map-lock` still returns **0.0000 px** on a pure-pan round trip), nothing accumulates, and the aerial is never resampled.
- **The reference point is the TILE LATTICE, not `map.project`** — and that distinction is worth a paragraph, because it is the difference between 0.29 px and 0.000. Leaflet places the raster lattice from a per-level origin it rounds SEPARATELY from the map's pixel origin, so at a fractional zoom (every wheel gesture leaves one) the tiles and the projection disagree by a sub-pixel amount multiplied by the level's scale factor. The user's reference is what they are LOOKING AT, so registration is measured against a real tile's rendered rect versus its own z/x/y — no Leaflet internals, and the rect already includes the live gesture transform, so one formula serves the gesture and settled branches alike. When no tile is on screen (aerial off, or none arrived yet) it falls back to the map's projection, which is the frame every Leaflet VECTOR overlay is placed in.
- **What B1062 got right, and the one thing it missed.** B1062 measured this residual correctly and adjudicated it as Leaflet's floor, deliberately uncompensated, on the grounds that the only two remedies were (i) a fractional transform on the tile wrap — which resamples, i.e. softens, the aerial (forbidden by B1049/V483) — or (ii) nudging the drawing's view offsets, which would destroy the reversible pan. **Both objections stand; there is a third option it did not consider:** a render-only translate on the SVG, which softens nothing (vector, re-rendered not resampled), leaves `view` pristine, and self-corrects the pointer path for free. It also did not identify contributor (b) as ours. B1062's committed bound stays exactly as it is — it is now a ceiling nothing reaches.
- **LOUD-FAILURE.** A shift past the quantisation range is a MODEL disagreement (a scale mismatch, a stale container size, a half-applied gesture transform), not something to paper over by shoving the drawing sideways: `sanitizeShift` refuses it, applies nothing, and reports `map-registration-out-of-range` with the measured delta. That guard earned its keep during this very session — it is what surfaced B1142.
- **PDF-PARITY, stated rather than skipped.** The shift is deliberately NOT mirrored into the export. It compensates a LIVE-DOM artefact of Leaflet's integer map pane; the sheet composes its own tile mosaic from `view` with no such quantisation, so copying it there would ADD the error it removes on screen. Confirmed by code: `exportSheet.js` / `printSheet.js` never serialise the live SVG, and the shift lives only in that element's inline style.
- **THE COMMITTED HARNESS — `ui-audit/diagnose-pointer-accuracy.mjs`** (the owner asked for it re-runnable, so it is). Ground truth from the tile grid; measures the READOUT path (pointer moved to a pixel, raw lat/lng read back through the `__PLANYR_E2E` probe) **and** the PLACEMENT path (a real two-click Length measurement, checking where its first vertex LANDED) at zoom 16/17/18 × device pixel ratio 1 / 2 / **2.15** plus a deliberately fractional canvas width, on a 60-element plan so culling actually varies the container. Residual reported in CSS px **and in feet at each zoom**, so the overview-zoom case is explicit. **Result: ✓ 120 of 120 readings within 0.25 px — every readout exactly 0.000 ft.** Two design details that keep it honest: the placement round is RETRIED when the frame re-registers mid-gesture (that reading measures nothing), and its click point is chosen in FEET on bare canvas clear of the boundary magnet, because the magnet is a feature and would otherwise be misreported as a transform error.
- **TEETH, measured both ways.** Every case prints the compensation actually applied — 0.07 to 0.77 px, i.e. up to **5.3 ft** at an overview zoom. With the compensation disabled and rebuilt, the harness reports a CONSTANT offset identical at all four spread probes (0.49 px / −2.11 ft E / +3.34 ft N at zoom 16), reproducing the owner's live finding — including its repeatability and its change of direction between zooms — and failing 20 of 60 readings.
- **Sandbox evidence.** `npm test` 6364 green · lint 0 errors · build green · `diagnose-pointer-accuracy` 120/120 · `diagnose-map-lock` PASS (pure-pan round trip 0.0000 px, unchanged) · `contour-hover-elevation`, `measure-select`, `click-behavior`, `panel-toggle-viewport`, `panel-open-squish`, `canvas-gis-identify` e2e all green.
- **Bundle budget — it ships WITH a matching optimization, not with a raised ceiling (the `perf-bundle-audit` rule).** The registration machinery pushed `bundle.siteRouteJsBytes` 2.5 KB over its ceiling, and `main` had only ~1 KB of headroom left (2264.5 KB against 2265.6), so any feature at all would have breached. Paid for by **deferring the deed reader**: `shared/files/docxText.js` — a self-contained .docx/ZIP reader that only runs when someone drops a deed or survey file — was a static import on the boot path and is now a dynamic `import()` at its one call site, the same treatment B1123 gave the title reader and B1042 gave the export path. That single deferral is worth **8.1 KB** on the site route — more than the feature costs — with the chunk count unchanged at 4 and no ceiling touched by this branch.
- **What is owed (V530).** The owner's own environment: 215% real browser zoom (not an emulated device pixel ratio), live Esri tiles, signed in, on real Tsakiris — plus the export-parity read. See `VERIFICATION.md` → V530. `Blocker: real-data`, `Blocker: live-GIS`.



### B1142 — The basemap re-centre never watched its own container, so the aerial could sit TENS of pixels off the drawing `[Site Planner / Map]` (bug) #site-planner #gis #coordinates  *(found 2026-07-30 by B1141's audit + `sanitizeShift`'s LOUD refusal, not by a report. Minted **B1142** via `--against-main`. DEDUPE-FIRST: **not** B1122 (that is the mid-gesture one-frame lag, fixed by the layout effect and untouched here), **not** B1043/B1062 (cumulative scale drift and the one-pixel quantisation — both stay closed). This is a THIRD, larger, independent term nobody had measured.)* *(RENUMBERED TWICE before merge, and the second time into a DELIBERATELY GAPPED block (B1140–B1143 / V530, skipping B1136–B1139): main merged three PRs while this branch was in flight — #860 took B1130/B1131/V523 and #862 took B1132/V524, each the number `next-id` had just reported. The B779/B780 uniqueness guard caught both collisions RED before merge, exactly as designed. Leaving a gap costs nothing (`next-id` reads the max) and breaks a loop that had already cost two renumber passes. Code and tests carried the provisional NEW-1/NEW-2 labels throughout, so only heading lines and three comment references ever moved.)*
`[ ]` **⏳ IMPLEMENTED — V530 PENDING. It also turned `ui-audit/diagnose-map-lock.mjs` from RED back to PASS on current `main`.**
- Verify: live
- Origin: found 2026-07-30 during B1141
- **What was wrong.** The commit path's re-centre trigger watched the CANVAS (`size.w/h`). The map container is a different box — the canvas PLUS twice the overscan (`inset: -geoOverscan`) — and the overscan is derived from the DRAWABLE ELEMENT COUNT, which changes as culling reveals and hides elements while you zoom. So the container can resize with the canvas unchanged: its top-left moves relative to the clip while `invalidateSize({pan:false})` deliberately doesn't move the map pane, and nothing re-centred it. Separately, the re-sync was skipped entirely on the FIRST commit ("nothing on screen yet" — true of the flash, not of the size), so a container that resized between the map's creation and that first commit baked a stale cached size in permanently, with nothing left to compare against.
- **How big.** Measured in the sandbox on a 60-element plan: Leaflet's cached size read 1592×1194 against a real 1438×1366 container, and `diagnose-map-lock` reported the drawing sitting **121.6 px** off the imagery — on current `main`, and on the pre-merge base too, so this is **pre-existing, not a B1122 regression** (verified by building both in throwaway worktrees). The first-commit variant alone measured 86 px at rest, before any gesture. Two orders of magnitude past the one-pixel quantisation B1141 started on, and invisible to any harness whose test plan has no elements to cull — which is exactly why it survived this long.
- **Fix.** Measure the container's own `clientWidth/clientHeight` and fold it into `sizeChanged`, alongside a cached-size-vs-DOM check (**both** are needed: the first catches a resize between commits, the second catches one before the first commit ever ran). Then let the existing branch do its job — re-sync Leaflet's cached size and re-centre through `commit`, which PANS rather than wiping, so this costs no flash and no tile churn, and the B933 no-flash property is preserved. Deliberately the DOM's own number rather than `geoOverscan` arithmetic: the box that matters is the one the browser laid out.
- **Why it matters for the report.** With the container un-watched, B1141's compensation would have had to swallow tens of pixels — and `sanitizeShift` correctly REFUSES that, reporting `map-registration-out-of-range` and applying nothing. Fixing the source is what keeps the registration shift a genuinely sub-pixel correction instead of a mask over a real defect. This is the LOUD-FAILURE rule paying for itself inside one session.
- **Sandbox evidence.** `diagnose-map-lock` PASS (was FAIL at 121.622 px; pure-pan round trip still exactly 0.0000 px, zoom-trip lock 0.650 px inside its committed 1 px epsilon) · `diagnose-pointer-accuracy` 120/120 with the wheel-driven rounds included · `npm test` 6364 green · lint 0 errors · build green.
- **What is owed (V530).** Same live pass as B1141 — with imagery, on a real plan with real element counts, at more than one zoom.



### B1131 — Hovering an electric line, substation or pipeline must say what it is `[Site Planner / layers]` (feature) #site-planner #gis #ui  *(owner-reported 2026-07-29 from chat, verbatim: "I should be able to hover over it and see what it is." Arrived as provisional "ITEM 2"; minted **B1131 / V523** via `git fetch origin main && npm run next-id -- --against-main`. Origin: filed 2026-07-29 from chat. DEDUPE-FIRST: **B695** added hover/click identify to the cached BOUNDARY layers and is the copy model's sibling, but it deliberately left `featureLayerOptions` at `interactive:false` — that gap is this item. **B1095** is contour hover, unrelated. Net-new.)*
`[x]` **Shipped — parked in ⏳ Verify for the live half (V523).**
- Verify: live — GIS endpoint behavior + zoom/data-density-dependent rendering (two mandatory LIVE-VERIFY classes). Sandbox proof: 51 unit assertions + 8 headless browser assertions against stubbed services; what cannot be proven here is that the REAL agency field names resolve.
- **⚠ THE REPORT'S SPLIT WAS WRONG, and correcting it made the fix smaller and better.** The brief asserted that the PUCT and HIFLD electric layers "do NOT paint as vectors at all" and paint through an `f=image` raster export, so they would need an ArcGIS identify. **They are vectors.** `hifld_tx` and `hifld_substations` are both `kind: "esriFeature"` — esri-leaflet `featureLayer`s with their attributes already in the DOM. Their real defect was `interactive: false` and no tooltip: real features that simply never answered. So the owner's red lines and substations are fixed with **wording + interactivity**, not a network round-trip — cheaper, instant, and more accurate. (There is also no PUCT *electric* layer in the registry at all; PUCT appears only as the water/sewer CCN row.)
- **(a) Vector layers — `featureHover.js` (new, pure).** Registry-driven wording in the SAME shape as the OSM tooltips it sits beside in the merged Electric row: `<Title> (<Source>) · <detail> · <detail>` → `Transmission line (HIFLD) · 138 kV · CenterPoint Energy`, `Substation (HIFLD) · Addicks · 138 kV · Houston`. Enabled via `hoverIdentify` / `hoverTitle` / `hoverSource` / `hoverFields` on `hifld_tx`, `hifld_substations`, `env_cleanups`, `faults`, `txdot_aadt`, `bts_rail`, `faa_airports`, `jur_road_authority`. Opt-in per layer, deliberately NOT blanket: county/city/ETJ/ISD polygons cover the whole view and would tooltip under every idle cursor — the same judgement `canvasIdentify` already makes.
- **Redaction is ABSENCE, never a fact.** HIFLD withholds attributes as `"NOT AVAILABLE"`, `0`, or an anonymised `"UNKNOWN30271"`. Those are omitted, reusing `powerScreen.js`'s existing `voltLabel` / `ownerLabel` cleaners so a tooltip and the Site Analysis card can never disagree about a voltage. A fully-redacted record still answers the owner's actual question — it reports `Substation (HIFLD)` rather than nothing.
- **Field names are matched case-insensitively from a candidate LIST**, because the sandbox blocks these hosts so the exact attribute casing cannot be probed from here. This is the specific reason V523 exists.
- **(b) The genuinely raster layers — `rasterIdentify.js` (new, pure) + `rasterIdentifyMap.js` (leaflet glue).** ~Half the registry really does paint as a server-rendered picture through a CORS-exempt `<img>`: FEMA, wetlands, the COH mains, HCFCD, BKDD, the RRC wells, the CCN/MUD territories, and the pipeline layer's zoomed-out tier. No features in the DOM → no tooltip can ever bind → the only way to answer is the service's `/identify`. Debounced ~320 ms on cursor rest, in-flight request aborted on move, a late answer for ground the cursor has left is dropped, click pins a popup. `identifyCapable` DECLINES what it cannot honestly answer: a FeatureServer (identify is a MapServer op), an ImageServer (returns a pixel, and elevation already has its own readout), and any registry opt-out.
- **Failure behaviour (LOUD-FAILURE).** Every outcome is a stated one: `Nothing here` · `This layer can't be identified` · `Source is rate-limiting — try again` · `Source didn't answer in time` · `Couldn't reach the source` · `Source returned HTTP n` · `Source sent an unreadable answer`. Non-hits self-dismiss; there is no branch that leaves a spinner up or falls silent. A sibling layer's FAILURE wins over another's empty result, so an unreachable service can never read as empty ground (the B233 distinction). **The e2e failure test caught a real leak here:** a 200 that wasn't JSON surfaced the raw parser message `Unexpected token '<'…` in the readout; now typed and worded honestly.
- **Reuses the existing mechanisms rather than adding parallel ones.** Liveness is the existing `probeService` verdict (`layerHealthy` gate — a failed dot is not re-asked on every hover), never a second prober. The click gate is the existing `identifyOk()` (the B98 rule). Transport is the existing direct-first-then-B445-cache-proxy pattern from `probeService`, including the `noCors` branch — necessary because these hosts are pictures precisely *because* they send no CORS headers.
- **BOTH surfaces, which the report did not distinguish.** The map finder gets real Leaflet hover. The planner **cannot** — its backdrop map is inside a `pointer-events:none` box, the SVG canvas owns every pointer event (the wall B1092 hit). So the planner drives the identify from its own already-throttled cursor position (the pipeline `contourHover` uses) and renders into the same card shape as the tap identify, gated to the select tool with no drag/draft in progress and suppressed while a pinned card is open. The esri feature layers also gained an `identifyAt` accessor over the SAME pure `hitFeature`, so the planner's tap reaches them too.
- Not fired while panning, dragging, drawing, or on a layer that is toggled off.
- **⚠ THE BUNDLE BUDGET WAS THE REAL FIGHT, and CI caught it — not the sandbox.** `ui-audit/perf-bundle-audit.mjs` runs in the `build` workflow but is **not** in the local pre-push habit, so PR #860 went red on it. The feature landed at **+20.2 KB** on `bundle.siteRouteJsBytes` and **+20.1 KB** on `bundle.largestChunkBytes`, breaching both. The gate's own rule — *a feature that breaches a budget ships with a matching optimization, or does not ship* — was followed, in this order: **(1)** the raster identify glue + state machine moved behind a dynamic import (`rasterIdentifyLazy.js`, the `terrainLazy`/B1095 shape); **(2)** the vector hover/identify attach layer AND its wording engine likewise (`featureHoverAttach.js`, imported at layer-toggle time — hundreds of ms before a cursor can rest on a feature, and `identifyOverlaysAt` already guards on a missing `identifyAt`); **(3)** `identifyCapable` moved into `layerRequest.js` so `layers.js` can gate on it without dragging the identify module onto the boot path (**trap:** a bare `export { x } from "y"` re-export creates NO local binding, so the function was `undefined` inside its own module — 11 controller tests caught it); **(4)** the `L.Icon.Default` fallback rendered from a ~400-byte inline SVG pin instead of leaflet's ~6 KB of inlined PNGs (see B1130). Result: **+20.2 KB → +7.4 KB**, and **`largestChunkBytes` came back UNDER its existing ceiling** (1719.5 → 1706.8 KB) with no number touched — the B1092 standard.
- **The one ceiling that WAS raised, and why (a product decision, stated as such).** `bundle.siteRouteJsBytes` 2320000 → 2332000. **`main` was already at 2262.9 KB against a 2265.6 KB ceiling — 2.7 KB of headroom — so this metric now trips on essentially ANY feature.** That is a headroom problem, not a regression in this PR, and the residual ~7 KB is `SitePlanner.jsx`'s hover card + effect, the geometry-aware point styling and the per-layer `hoverIdentify` flags: all synchronous, all on this route, none deferrable by `import()`. The full justification is written into the metric's own `note` in `perf-budgets.json`, per that file's convention. **B1064** remains the owner of closing the real gap.
- **A SECOND ceiling moved after merging main, and the reason is structural.** `bundle.totalJsBytes` 3960000 → 3985000. That metric counts **every emitted chunk, lazy ones included — by design**, which is what makes it the honest catch-all; so the four deferrals above move bytes off the critical path without reducing it *at all*, and no further code-splitting can. The residual is ~19 KB of genuine minified code for these two defects. New `main` (#859) was itself at 3861.4 KB against a 3867.2 KB ceiling — **5.8 KB of headroom** — so this metric, like the other two, now trips on essentially any feature. Ceiling and target are kept EQUAL, as they were, so it keeps asserting no known gap rather than quietly acquiring one. **Net for this PR: one budget paid down under its ceiling with no raise (`largestChunkBytes`), two raised with the justification written into their own notes.**
- **ID COLLISION, and the LATE-BIND rule doing its job.** Filed as B1126/B1127/V522; main's #859 merged first and took **B1126, B1127 AND V522**. Because the house rule was followed — code, tests and commits carry the provisional `NEW-1`/`NEW-2` labels, never a real number — the renumber to **B1130 / B1131 / V523** touched only heading lines and one `perf-budgets.json` note. Zero code changed. `next-id`'s `⚠ DUPLICATE ACTIVE ids` warning caught it before the push.
- **Worth adopting:** add `node ui-audit/perf-bundle-audit.mjs` to the local pre-push gate. Lint + tests + build were all green here and this still failed in CI, because the audit needs a fresh `dist/` and nothing local runs it.

`[ ]` **⏳ MHFD ENGINE MERGED — V522 PENDING. ⚠ AND ONE PART IS BLOCKED, LOUDLY: THE VOLUME COEFFICIENTS COULD NOT BE READ FROM ANY SOURCE REACHABLE FROM THIS ENVIRONMENT, SO NO MHFD VOLUME IS COMPUTED YET. `Blocker: source-egress`.**
- Verify: live
- Origin: filed 2026-07-29 from chat; built (MHFD only) 2026-07-29
- **⛔ THE BLOCKER, stated first because it is the one thing a reader must not miss.** The dispatch required the WQCV and EURV equations to be read **from the source manuals with section numbers cited**, and explicitly forbade reconstructing them from memory. **They could not be read.** Every primary host — `mhfd.org`, `mhfd.specialdistrict.org`, `old.mhfd.org`, `fcgov.com`, `denvergov.org` — answers **403 to CONNECT at the egress gateway**, and the fetch tooling 403s on *every* host including unrelated ones (Wikipedia), so this is an environment limit, not a bad URL. Web search reaches the open web but returns a **model summary** of a page rather than its text, and **two independent search reads of the SAME UDFCD EURV memorandum returned two DIFFERENT coefficient sets** (`0.140 / 0.113 / 0.100` vs `1.68 / 1.36 / 1.20`). That disagreement is the proof the numbers cannot be transcribed at second hand. Per the dispatch's own instruction — *"if a needed equation cannot be read from an accessible source, say so loudly and ship that part as unavailable rather than approximating"* — **no coefficient was invented.** The `OWNER-TODO.md` entry is the unblock: four PDFs, downloadable from any ordinary browser.
- **WHAT DID SHIP, and why it is an engine rather than a stub.** New `ruleType: "volume-curve"` + `lib/mhfdDetention.js` (lazy, joins the Colorado `coTier` chunk — a Texas user downloads none of it):
  - **WQCV and EURV are DISTINCT components**, never collapsed: each carries its own `role` (`water-quality` vs `flood-volume`), its own `depends` list, its own evidence state and **its own citation** (they come from different documents), plus the routed 100-yr as a third component with `method:"routing"` — because a routed volume is not a coefficient anyone could look up, and saying so is the honest answer rather than a gap.
  - **The MATH IS REAL and tested.** `wqcvDepthIn` / `eurvDepthIn` / `depthInToAcFt` / the combiner are exercised against **synthetic** curves with hand-computed expectations (the full cubic, the soil-group area weighting, C/D folding, clamping, monotonic drain time). So the code is verified independently of MHFD's real numbers, and **transcribing them later is a DATA edit** — one object literal per component, no code change, no new dispatch.
  - **Per-component evidence states, with different cures.** `unavailable` (`source-unreachable` for WQCV; **`source-conflict` for EURV**, because it is worse off than merely unreachable; `requires-routing` for the 100-yr) vs `needs-input` (curve present, imperviousness / soil group / drain-time election missing). Conflating a missing CRITERION with a missing USER INPUT is how a data gap gets mistaken for something the reader can fix.
  - **`rateAcFtPerAc` is ALWAYS null.** A full-spectrum volume has no per-acre rate; back-computing one to fill the Texas badge would invent a criterion MHFD does not publish. `ruleBadge` names the METHOD in that slot instead ("full spectrum (WQCV + EURV)").
  - **Release rates and outlet configuration** are declared present-but-NOT-transcribed, so Planyr's Texas outlet model is never quietly applied to a full-spectrum basin.
- **THE C.R.S. 37-92-602(8) RECONCILIATION — the two features AGREE rather than contradict.** MHFD asks you to hold water; Colorado water law asks you to let it go, so a site can satisfy its drainage criteria and still be an out-of-priority diversion. `reconcileMhfdDrawdown` reads the 72-hour limit **out of the statute record** (never a hardcoded 72) and **borrows the statute module's vocabulary** — `fail` / `not-ruled-out` / `unknown`, never "pass" or "complies", asserted in the suite, because `drawdownStatute.js` deliberately refuses to say "pass" and a second module claiming compliance about the same statute would contradict it on screen. With no drain time elected it answers for **all three options at once** ("all 3 options (12, 24, 40 hours) sit inside the 72-hour limit") rather than assuming one — a silently defaulted drain time would drive a statutory verdict off a number nobody chose. And it names the honest half: **the EURV release above the water-quality zone is the term that could actually collide with the statute, and it is the one Planyr cannot size.**
- **SCOPE HELD — MHFD only, and the boundary is enforced TWICE on independent facts.** (1) `computeRequiredDetention`'s Colorado guard is **fail-CLOSED**: it prices only on a positive `coRegime === "mhfd"` **and** an injected evaluator; a missing chunk, an unresolved regime, Larimer / Weld / El Paso, or an unknown regime all fall through to the **original hard guard byte-for-byte**. (2) `computeMhfdDetention` **re-checks county membership itself** and refuses a non-member, so a mis-wired caller cannot price either. `test/coloradoGuard.test.js` gains the scope-boundary test that goes red if a future session generalises MHFD to the three non-members — the outcome the owner named as the worst possible one.
- **RULES-AS-DATA is enforced, not assumed.** The guard rejects an evaluator carrier that returns a number with **no rule record** (`co-evaluator-malformed`) rather than rendering a naked volume. Every component and the record itself carry authority, `ruleType`, `effectiveDate`, `verifiedOn` and `source{name,section,url}` — and `structureVerified: true` is kept **separate** from `coefficientsTranscribed: false`, because "we know the method" and "we know the numbers" are different claims and this repo has been burned by conflating them.
- **AUDIT ANSWER — district ≠ final authority.** Being inside MHFD does **not** settle the operative rule: the member city or county is the permitting authority and may layer stricter criteria, and **Denver publishes its own combined manual**. `mhfdJurisdictionNote` carries `districtIsFinal: false` / `cityOverlayMayApply: true` always, flags Denver specifically with its own source, and the suite asserts an MHFD answer can never claim finality. A full municipal-overlay registry is too large for this session, so it ships as the explicit "city overlay may apply — confirm" note the dispatch asked for.
- **AUDIT ANSWER — Broomfield: the dispatch's premise was WRONG, nothing to fix.** It was **not** a silent default. `src/shared/coordinates/statePlane.js` carries a dedicated `CO:broomfield` override assigning **EPSG:2231 Colorado North** with its full reasoning (Broomfield is not named in C.R.S. 38-52-101 — the statute predates the county; three of its four parent counties are North, and Broomfield's own parcel service publishes in EPSG:2876 / Colorado North ftUS), plus a `countiesProvenance.js` entry and a test asserting it is "a DECIDED assignment, carrying its reasoning". Only the owner-facing summary omitted it.

Ceiling untouched (`docs/PERF-BUDGETS.md`: *"a feature that breaches a budget ships with a matching optimization, or does not ship"*, and raising one needs the same justification as a product decision). **FOUR cuts, all the SAME principle and all of them the architecturally better home anyway — a string that can only render once the lazy Colorado chunk has landed does not belong on the boot path:** (1) the "Assumptions & method" note lines moved out of `SitePlanner.jsx` into `mhfdMethodNotes`; (2) three separate `coTier.mhfd.*` call sites — each repeating the county-resolution expression — collapsed into ONE `mhfdPanelBag`; (3) the verdict row's subject ("MHFD WQCV + EURV") moved onto the carrier as `verdictSubject`, so `yieldVerdicts.js` (which IS on the boot path, because the row must render instantly) no longer derives it; (4) `ruleBadge`'s volume-curve branch replaced by a `badgeMethod` field on the record, and the guard's duplicated unavailable-carrier factored to one closure. ### B1123 — A spurious `alongLen` pins the trailer parking so it stops following its truck court `[Site Planner / dockZones]` (bug) #site-planner #ui  *(owner chat 2026-07-29, provisional NEW-1, live rows quoted in the brief. Minted **B1123 / V520** with `git fetch origin main && npm run next-id -- --against-main`. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched `alongLen` / `resizedAlongLen` / `zoneAlongSpan` across Open, ⏳ Verify and Done: **B492** introduced the court's typed length and **the 2026-06-30 owner fix** made the chain share one span; the per-zone escape hatch that writes `alongLen` has never been reported before. Not a recurrence.)*
`[ ]` **⏳ MERGED — V520 PENDING (`Blocker: real-data` — the repro cites one signed-in saved plan).**
- Verify: live
- Origin: filed 2026-07-29 from chat
- **Report.** Resizing a building leaves its trailer parking behind — wrong length and detached. On Goose Creek "Plan 1 (copy)" (site `sms69x8rb2qk`) the two trailers on building `e1454729ykduhm` are the ONLY elements in the whole plan carrying an `alongLen`, and the owner never typed a trailer length.
- **Live rows, re-queried against `site_elements` while fixing (verbatim).** building `e1454729ykduhm` w 822 · h 500 · rot 178.543241069641 → courts `e1454739ykduhm` (top) and `e1454741ykduhm` (bottom) both w 712 · h 135 · zd 135 → trailers `e1454740ykduhm` (w 708, `alongLen` 708) and `e1454742ykduhm` (w 707, `alongLen` 707), both rot 178.543241069641.
- **AUDIT-FIRST — the brief's stated root cause does not survive reading the code, and the correction matters.** The brief attributes a phantom length term to the HOST rotation (sin 178.543° ≈ 0.0254 → ~1.3 ft on a 50 ft trailer). `boxExtentAlong(zone, alongUnit(host, side))` is **already host-relative**: it dots the zone's own rotated half-axes with the host's along direction, so it returns w·|cos δ| + h·|sin δ| where δ is the zone's angle MINUS the host's — exact whenever the zone sits at its host's angle, which on this plan **both trailers do** (all three rows read 178.543241069641). Un-rotating by the host would have been the identical number. Two real defects sit underneath the report instead:
  - **(1) the measure is a bounding-box PROJECTION**, so as soon as δ drifts off a right angle the DEPTH leaks into the along measurement as h·|sin δ|. That drift is real in this owner's data, not hypothetical — `e1454737ykduhm` sits at 268.543241069641 under a host at 178.543241069641, and `e1454692dshobp` at 359 under a host at 269.
  - **(2) there was no notion of gesture INTENT at all** — and this is the one that bites. Whether the owner had set a length was inferred from geometry alone, so anything reaching that branch of `refitChildren` could pin `alongLen`, and a pin is by design never reset. **On this plan the pins are collateral from B1124:** the cross-linked `forCourt` had already detached both trailers, the owner dragged them to try to make them fit, that drag legitimately stamped a length — and the stamp then guaranteed they could never track again even once the bond is repaired.
- **Fix, three parts.** (a) `dockZones.zoneAlongExtent` / `zoneDepthExtent` read the along/across **dimension** in the host's frame whenever the zone is within a snap of it (every zone `layoutZoneByKind` produces is), falling back to the projection for a genuinely off-axis box — so a depth change moves the along span by exactly zero. (b) `resizedZoneAlongLen` gates the stamp on INTENT: `refitChildren` now takes the gesture (`userResize` + an edge drag's `dragAxis`), so a host refit, a relayout, a rotation, a court depth change and the load-time heal are all structurally incapable of stamping; a depth-only edge drag is refused outright. (c) `siteModel.normalizeZoneAlongLen` — a load-time heal in the ONE shared `normalizeBondedChildren` (so BOTH read paths run it, the B1097 trap) that DROPS an `alongLen` indistinguishable from the chain span the zone would derive anyway and re-lays the chain in the same pass, so plans already poisoned go back to tracking without the owner clearing anything by hand. Healed elements ride the existing `exempt` set, so the repair diffs and COMMITS (B1118).
- **Order is load-bearing:** the B1124 bond repair runs FIRST, or the length pass has no walkable chain to judge the pin against. Encoded in `normalizeBondedChildren` and asserted end-to-end.
- **Tests.** `test/zoneAlongLen.test.js` (16): a pure host resize NEVER stamps at rot 0 / 90 / 178.543 / 269 / 359 · a real along-axis drag DOES · a depth-only drag does not · the load-time heal clears a stamped-but-equal value while PRESERVING a genuinely user-set one · the court head's own `alongLen` is never touched · idempotent (untouched records returned by identity).
- **BUNDLE BUDGET — the fix shipped WITH a matching optimization, not a raised ceiling.** `bundle.siteRouteJsBytes` went red in CI: the three fixes cost 3,937 bytes of site-route JS and `origin/main` was already within 3,870 bytes of its 2,320,000-byte ceiling (measured 2,316,130 — the ceiling has been eaten by ordinary churn since B1042 set it against a 2,242,725 baseline). Rather than re-baseline, the offset is real deferral: `SitePlanner.jsx` statically imported `lib/titleReader.js` for three lines (`getKey`/`setKey`, which seed a `useState` and an onChange), dragging that module's Claude structured-output SCHEMA and prompt — KB of string literals that minify to themselves — onto the critical path, when nothing needs them until someone uploads a title commitment. ### B1120 — The client never sent `p_atomic` in production, so B1116/B1117 did nothing `[Site Planner / sync]` (bug) #site-planner #sync #persistence #testing  *(owner live V509b run 2026-07-29 on the deployed atomic build, provisional B1400 — the FIFTH recurrence of the assembly tear. Minted **B1120 / V517**. DEDUPE-FIRST — NOT a duplicate of B1117: that item shipped the gate and the transport correctly, and both are right in isolation (their tests still pass unchanged). This is the WIRING BETWEEN them, plus the test-design gap that let a dead feature ship green. Net-new, and the more valuable of the two to have caught.)*
`[ ]` **⏳ merged — V517 PENDING (Verify: live — `Blocker: auth`).**
- Verify: live
- Origin: filed 2026-07-29 from chat
- **Repro (owner, measured on planyr.io, signed in).** `window.fetch` hooked, `Object.keys(requestBody)` recorded for every `commit_elements` call across two full drag + Ctrl+Z runs. **Eight commits, every one with body keys exactly `p_site` + `p_ops`, all HTTP 200.** No 404, no error, no fallback — the `atomicUnavailable` latch was never involved (`NOTIFY pgrst, 'reload schema'` before the second run changed nothing, consistent with that). Consequence: the round-4 failure verbatim — run 1 split the undo's 12-op batch across THREE transactions (22:05:34.922 host restored · :40.557 six children restored · :41.547 five children at the MOVED coordinates, 7 correct / 5 stranded); run 2 produced six commits sized 12, 3, 12, 4, 5, 5, and its FIRST batch already carried non-uniform coordinates.
- **ROOT CAUSE — one line, and it is mine.** `SitePlanner.jsx`: `commit: (ops) => commitElements(supabase, siteId, ops)`. **A fixed-arity adapter.** The engine calls `commit(ops, { atomic })`; this closure accepts ONE parameter, so the second argument was **silently discarded** and `commitElements` never saw `opts.atomic`. Every batch therefore went out as the plain 2-arg RPC — 200, no error, nothing to notice. Not the gate (`batchSpansAssembly` returns true for a 12-member batch, as its test says), not the transport (it sends `p_atomic` when told), not the deployed bytes (`p_atomic` is present in the served chunk, confirmed both by the owner and by `verify-deploy.mjs`). **The wire between two correct halves.**
- **WHY IT SHIPPED GREEN, stated plainly because this is the transferable lesson.** Every B1117 test drove the engine through a harness whose own `commit` was `async (ops, opts) => …` — it accepted the option the real adapter dropped. **A mock more capable than the shipped adapter proves nothing about the shipped adapter.** The suite asserted the gate's return value and the transport's request body separately, and never once asserted the request body produced by the two of them wired together.
- **Fix.** `commit: (ops, opts) => commitElements(supabase, siteId, ops, opts)`.
- **LOUD guard, so this class cannot recur silently.** `commitElements` now reports `sentAtomic` — what actually went ON THE WIRE, not what was asked — and `fellBack` for the one legitimate un-atomic send (a project with no 3-arg overload). The engine compares intent against reality and emits `element-atomic-request-lost` + an `atomic-request-lost` event when a batch asked for atomic and did not get it. The condition is **`sentAtomic !== true`**, deliberately not `=== false`: a fixed-arity adapter never forwards the option, so the transport never learns we asked and reports `undefined` — exactly the shape of this bug, so silence must not read as success. A plain (non-atomic) call's return shape is byte-identical to the pre-B1120 contract, so no existing caller or test sees a new field.
- **Tests at the REAL boundary (the gap that mattered).** `test/assemblyTear.test.js` now drives the engine through the **real `commitElements`** with only the network faked, and asserts the **REQUEST BODY**: a 12-member assembly batch puts `p_atomic` on the wire (keys exactly `p_atomic`+`p_ops`+`p_site`); a single-element batch carries the production 2-key shape; **the fixed-arity adapter reproduces the exact production body AND is caught loudly** (this case fails against the pre-fix guard); the correct adapter warns about nothing; a project without the migration falls back quietly and is NOT flagged as a wiring bug; plus a source guard requiring the two-parameter adapter and forbidding the fixed-arity form.
- **Sandbox evidence.** `npm test` 6258 green (371 files) · lint 0 errors · build green · `element-atomic-request-lost` present in the built bundle · e2e green.
- **One strand the owner flagged that this fix does NOT explain, recorded rather than glossed.** Run 2's FIRST batch already carried non-uniform coordinates (`e29` 581,−14 and `e30` 1052,−429 against 887/1301/444 for the rest), i.e. the CANVAS was torn *during* the gesture, not only after it. Atomicity cannot help there — an atomic write of a torn canvas persists the tear faithfully. If that recurs on the next live run it is a separate defect in the gesture/refit path and needs its own item; V517 asks for it explicitly.
- **What is still owed (V517).** The owner's `fetch`-hook method re-run: a multi-member assembly batch must show `p_atomic: true` in its body, a single-element edit must not, nothing may 404, and `site_elements` must land whole.

### B1113 — A stale local cache still wins on load, for a SUBSET of an assembly, dribbled across transactions `[Site Planner / sync]` (bug) #site-planner #sync #persistence  *(owner live re-verification of V509b 2026-07-29 on the a5d1631 build, provisional B1400 — the THIRD recurrence of the assembly-tear family, hit before the V509b test itself could be run. Cross-referenced, not merged.)*
`[ ]` **⏳ merged — V514 PENDING (Verify: live — `Blocker: auth` + a browser profile carrying a stale cache).**
- Verify: live
- Origin: filed 2026-07-29 from chat
- **Repro (measured on production, signed in).** Open a plan in a browser profile whose local cache holds an older copy of the same elements. The load itself issues ZERO commits — then, seconds later, `site_elements` takes **FOUR separate transactions over six seconds** (16:38:14.693 · :18.637 · :20.627 · :20.630) writing the CACHED geometry for a SUBSET of one twelve-member assembly: `e26duuwgj` (899.44, −559.55), `e27duuwgj` (899.44, −652.05), `e63sascnh` (1312.94, 47.95), `e64cglxqv` (485.94, −522.05) against canonical 1117.20/−336.35, 1117.20/−428.85, 1530.70/271.15, 703.70/−298.85. **The stale delta is exactly (−218, −223)** — a drag made in the previous verification round and then undone. The live canvas afterwards held `e26`/`e27` stale and everything else correct: the tear was **ON THE CANVAS**, not only in the rows.
- **Root cause (AUDIT-FIRST) — the rev guard structurally cannot catch this.** After `seed(rows)` the shadow holds the server's **current rev**. A stale canvas copy therefore commits **CLEANLY**: the CAS sees the rev it expects, because the client legitimately holds it. Nothing in the write path is wrong — `closeAssemblies` folded in nothing because the other eight members genuinely agreed with the server, which is the correct behaviour for a diff committer. The bug is that the divergence was ever read as an edit. And the copy survived the rows-canonical replace because of the **pending-edit journal**: a stale tab hot-looping rejected commits (B1115) keeps adopting the freshest rev, so its journal's `baseRev` tracks the current row and its entries sail through `foldJournal`'s `row.rev <= baseRev` test carrying geometry undone long ago.
- **Fix — the rule is now WRITTEN DOWN (`CLAUDE.md` → **ROWS-CANONICAL-ON-SEED**), because the ambiguity is what cost the plan.** For an element the server ALREADY HAS, rows win at seed time unless a pending local op explains the difference; for an element the server has NEVER seen, local wins (that is the whole of the B124/B756 guarantee). Mechanically: `reconcile(collections, { afterSeed: true })` — **opt-in on purpose**, since only the seeder knows which diff is its own, and an ordinary later diff carries genuine edits that must never be silently reverted — adopts the rows through a new `onRowsCanonical` callback instead of enqueueing. Result: **zero commits**, not a four-op one.
- **Second half — heal AFTER the folds.** `rowsToModel` healed the ROWS, but the journal / never-synced folds run afterwards and can substitute a local copy back over a healed row. `refetchReplace` now re-runs `normalizeBondedChildren` on the FINAL merged canvas, so no fold can put a geometrically impossible assembly on screen (and then commit it). Identity-preserving on a coherent plan, so a healthy load still churns nothing.
- **Tests.** `test/assemblyTear.test.js` — the case the brief specified: seed from rows, inject a divergent cached copy of **4 of 12** assembly members, assert **zero commits** and that all four rows are adopted onto the canvas; plus "never a 4-op commit" stated as an invariant, a pending local edit still committing (not silently reverted), and a never-synced element still winning locally.
- **Sandbox evidence.** `npm test` 6234 green (371 files) · lint 0 errors · build green · bundle budgets within ceiling · `npx playwright test e2e/assembly-move-integrity.spec.js e2e/ctrlz-undo.spec.js` 6/6 green.
- **What is still owed (V514).** A signed-in load in a profile that genuinely holds a stale cache — which is exactly what the owner could not clear from his sandbox, and what this sandbox cannot produce at all.

### B1114 — `strandedFromHost` missed a large-but-not-absurd displacement `[Site Planner / Site Model]` (bug) #site-planner #persistence  *(owner live re-verification 2026-07-29, provisional NEW-2. **AMENDS B1097** — which PASSED its own live check (V508) on a 2,086 ft displacement and stays Done; this is the gap that pass could not see. Minted **B1114**; shares **V514** with B1113 — one signed-in load proves both.)*
`[ ]` **⏳ merged — V514 PENDING (Verify: live).**
- Verify: live
- Origin: filed 2026-07-29 from chat
- **Repro.** A truck-court apron 218 ft off its host's centreline, and its trailer strip 218 ft west / 223 ft north, both **loaded and rendered without being healed**. The V508 case that passed used 2,086 ft, so the threshold sat somewhere in between — which is the tell that **magnitude was the wrong question.**
- **Root cause.** `strandedFromHost` compared an ABSOLUTE distance against `host half-diagonal + chain depth + child half-diagonal + slack`. On a 600×300 building with a full dock stack that reach is comfortably past 300 ft, so a 311 ft tear sat inside it and looked legal.
- **Fix — compare against the COMPUTED ANCHOR per kind, so magnitude stops mattering.** A bond's legal position is derivable: **ACROSS** the wall a stack member's offset is fully determined (`host_depth/2` + everything inboard of it + its own depth/2 — there is no user freedom on that axis at all), and **ALONG** the wall there IS freedom (the owner slides a field to line up a curb return — the B1039 rule) but it is bounded: the member must still OVERLAP the wall it is bonded to. New pure `offAnchor({acrossHave, acrossWant, alongHave, alongLimit, tol})`; tolerance 10 ft, generous enough for stored rounding and legacy sub-foot drift, far tighter than any real displacement. The wall-kid along-axis reset uses the same computed overlap bound instead of a distance.
- **Tests.** Cases at **50 / 200 / 2000 ft** all heal; the **exact reported 218/223** heals; a correct stack returns byte-identical; a **resized court depth is respected, not reset** (the depth is read off the member's own box, so a re-anchor is never a re-design); a legitimately slid side-parking row keeps its slide while one slid clean off the wall re-centres; `offAnchor` never claims a tear it cannot measure. **The 50 / 200 / 218 cases FAIL against the old absolute-distance test** (verified by reverting it), so these are guards, not decorations.

### B1115 — A rejected commit hot-loops at ~1 RPC/second with no backoff and no give-up `[Site Planner / sync]` (task — hardening) #site-planner #sync #perf  *(owner live observation 2026-07-29, provisional NEW-3, spotted while re-verifying V509b. Minted **B1115 / V515**. DEDUPE-FIRST — `onTransportFailure` has had exponential backoff since B671, but ONLY for a transport failure; a batch that returns `ok:true` with every op REJECTED re-queues on the plain debounce, which is a different path and had no backoff at all. Net-new.)*
`[ ]` **⏳ merged — V515 PENDING (Verify: live — `Blocker: auth`, needs a genuinely out-of-date tab).**
- Verify: live
- Origin: filed 2026-07-29 from chat
- **Repro (measured).** A tab running an older bundle with a stale copy issued an 8-op `commit_elements` **every ~1 s for at least 7 s**; **every op was rejected** and `site_elements` revs never moved. The DATA outcome was correct — the CAS did its job — but nothing stopped the client, so one stale tab can hammer the RPC indefinitely.
- **Fix.** `processResults` now reports whether **any** op was accepted. A batch with none increments a reject streak: the retry moves off the 750 ms debounce onto the existing exponential backoff ladder, and after `maxRejectStreak` (default 4) consecutive all-rejected batches the engine **STOPS re-committing**, sets state `stale`, and emits a typed `client-stale` event. One accepted op resets the streak, so a healthy client can never trip it; `retryNow()` clears the hold.
- **LOUD-FAILURE, in plain English.** `conflictToasts` turns `client-stale` into the one message the user must act on — *"This tab is out of date — your recent changes here can't be saved. Reload the page to catch up."* — with no `authoredRecently` gate and no zoom action, because it is not about a single element.
- **Tests.** The retry interval GROWS (each recorded delay strictly greater than the last, the first already past the old debounce) rather than sitting at 750 ms; after N all-rejected batches the state is `stale`, the event fires, and **no further commits are issued**; one accepted op breaks the streak; and the toast reads as a reload prompt.
- **What is still owed (V515).** A genuinely out-of-date tab against a moved-on plan: that the RPC rate visibly decays instead of sitting at ~1/s, that the reload prompt appears, and that reloading clears it.


### B1111 — Colorado county GIS registry: nine counties, a statewide fallback tier, and state-scoped click routing `[Platform / gis]` (feature) #gis #coordinates  *(minted via `git fetch origin main && npm run next-id -- --against-main`. `[x]` **Implemented 2026-07-29 — parked for a live endpoint probe (`V513`).**

- **The brief's premise was half wrong, and the important half.** It assumed Colorado has "no equivalent middle or bottom tier" to Texas's chain. There **IS** a statewide bottom tier: the Colorado OIT **Colorado Public Parcels** composite, county-scopable by `countyName` — the exact TxGIO analogue. So a Colorado county outage degrades to the same honest statewide backup a Texas one does, not to nothing. (No clean *middle* tier exists — DRCOG is metro-only, PPACG El Paso-only — so none is modelled.) Also corrected: the real fallback chain is **two** tiers (county CAD → statewide), not the three the brief described; there is no city tier and no regional tier in the parcel path.
- **Endpoints VERIFIED LIVE 2026-07-29** (queried, metadata read, feature count returned): **Adams** 188,723 · **Denver** 240,360 (layer id **245**, not 0) · **Weld** 163,685 · **Broomfield** 27,531 — all ArcGIS-Online hosted, CORS-open, no key. Plus `GIS_SOURCES.countyCo` (Colorado statewide county boundaries, 64 polygons) and, as a Texas control re-probe, Harris 1,548,457 and Fort Bend 385,648.
- **Endpoints NOT shipped because they could not be probed:** Arapahoe, Larimer, Boulder, El Paso ride the statewide composite with their county-own endpoint parked in `candidateUrl` **with provenance** (a registered ArcGIS Online item — owner, item id — and the reason it was not probed). **Jefferson** has no locatable county parcel endpoint at all and rides the composite outright, exactly as Waller does in Texas. → `V513`.
- **Key collision handled:** Texas and Colorado both have an **El Paso** and a **Jefferson** county. Texas keys are persisted in saved plans and could not be renamed (Constraint 1), so Colorado keys are `co_`-prefixed and `countyKeyForName(name)` stays **Texas-only** unless a state is passed — an unqualified `"El Paso"` returns null rather than guessing.
- **The Texas regression the harness caught, and it was the dangerous one:** `candidateCountiesForPoint`'s out-of-bbox branch returned every configured county, `harris` first — and the Layers-panel jurisdiction resolver reads `candidate[0]`. A Colorado click would have inherited **Harris County**, which is exactly the wrong-but-plausible answer this work exists to prevent. The fallback is now state-scoped; a Texas point's candidate list is byte-identical. B1107's golden master caught this AND a second regression (Colorado's composite leaking into Texas candidates) before either shipped.
- **County identify is now region-routed like ETJ already was** (`countySourcesForPoint`): a Colorado point resolves against Colorado's boundary layer; every Texas point and every point outside Colorado gets the **identical** `JURISDICTION_SOURCES.county` object — asserted by identity, not equality.
- **`ui-audit/gis-source-audit.mjs` extended (check #3, county parcel provenance).** `counties.js` is exempt from the no-inline-URL rule, and that exemption is what would have let a guessed URL ship. Every county row must now declare its `state` and be live-verified, on its state's composite, or carry a `verifiedNote` saying why not; a `candidateUrl` requires `candidateProvenance` and may never be the primary. Wired to CI via `test/gisSources.test.js`.
