### B1103 — Colorado floodplain: the CWCB statewide floor, and the 72-hour drawdown statute as a real pass/fail `[Standards / flood]` (feature) #floodplain #pond  *(minted via `--against-main`. DEDUPE-FIRST: no prior item covers a Colorado flood authority; B707/B758/B760 are the Texas mitigation records this extends the registry beside. Origin: filed 2026-07-29 from chat (NEW-7).)*
`[x]` **Implemented 2026-07-29 — parked for a live check on a real Colorado site (`V512`).**
- Verify: live — `Blocker: real-data` (needs a saved Colorado plan with a drawn pond and a release rate)
- Origin: filed 2026-07-29 from chat
- **FEMA travels; everything around it did not.** The `flood` source is the national NFHL and zone classification is zone-letter logic, so Colorado sites get real flood zones today. But `floodAdministrator.js`'s `RULE_KEY_ALIAS` is entirely Texas, and `DEFAULT_FLOODPLAIN_RULES` has six Texas jurisdictions and no Colorado record — so compensating storage is **unwired in Colorado** and now reports itself as such through B1104's capability matrix rather than going quiet.
- **CWCB checked rather than assumed, and it cuts the OTHER way.** Colorado has a **statewide floor stricter than FEMA** in three specific ways (2 CCR 408-1, recorded in `lib/coloradoRegions.js` `CO_STATE_FLOOD_STANDARD`): **1 ft freeboard** above the 100-yr for new/substantially-improved structures (NFIP requires only at-or-above BFE); **2 ft for Critical Facilities** (NFIP has no separate standard); **0.5 ft floodway designation rise** for newly studied/revised reaches (FEMA's default is 1.0 ft). Unlike Texas, where freeboard is purely a local-ordinance matter, a Colorado site therefore has a known minimum before any local ordinance is read. It is a **floor** — locals commonly adopt more, and a hazardous-materials building can be a Critical Facility even on an industrial site. Marked `verified: true, secondarySource: true`: the CWCB's own adopted-rules PDF returned HTTP 403 to this environment, so the values are triangulated from the rule text as published through the Colorado SoS CCR and Cornell LII — confirm subsection lettering against the primary PDF.
- **C.R.S. 37-92-602(8) wired as a rule record** (`lib/drawdownStatute.js`) — ≥97% of a 5-year storm released within **72 hr**, ≥99% of larger events within **120 hr**, plus the post-5-Aug-2015 **State Engineer notification** (location, surface area at design volume, drain-rate data) and the rebuttable presumption of no material injury. Cheap because the engine already existed: `drawdownTime.js`'s time-to-empty feeds it directly.
- **Two design points worth carrying forward.** (1) **It never reports "pass."** The screening drawdown is a constant-rate *lower* bound — real outflow decays as head drops — so a result inside the limit means non-compliance is **not ruled out**, never that the facility complies; a failure, by the same logic, is real. Verdicts are `fail` / `not-ruled-out` / `unknown`. (2) **It fails the facility, not the average**: the statute applies per facility, so one slow pond fails the site even when the site-wide figure is inside the limit.
- **Texas presentation is unchanged** — `assessStatutoryDrawdown` returns `applies:false` for any state but CO, and the existing informational readout renders exactly as before. Proven by B1107's golden master.
- Verified in sandbox: `test/coloradoGuard.test.js` (26 cases, incl. the never-says-pass rule, the per-facility rule, and the notification defaults) · full suite **6,120 green** · lint 0 · build green.

### B1104 — The Colorado capability guard: no Texas-derived number, no silent fallback, no blank that reads as zero `[Standards / detention]` (feature) #yield #floodplain #ui  *(minted via `--against-main`. DEDUPE-FIRST: no prior item guards a cross-region capability gap. Origin: filed 2026-07-29 from chat (NEW-8, the MUST-BUILD half).)*
`[x]` **Implemented 2026-07-29 — parked for a live check on a real Colorado site (`V512`).**
- Verify: live — `Blocker: real-data` (needs a saved Colorado plan to see the panel render its state)
- Origin: filed 2026-07-29 from chat
- **The constraint this exists to satisfy:** Colorado ships LIVE rather than behind a flag, so any capability not yet wired must render a hard, unmistakable "not available in Colorado yet" state — never a number, never a silent fallback to a Texas rule, never a blank that reads as zero. A wrong-but-plausible number on a Colorado plan is the single worst outcome of this work.
- **Three deliberate placement decisions in `computeRequiredDetention`.** (1) The guard is the **first statement in the function** — above the `acres > 0` check, because "no site area" is a Texas-shaped answer too. (2) It sits **above the authority lookup**, so even a user who overrides the reviewing agency to a Texas authority on a Colorado site gets no Texas rate — tested against **every** rule in `DETENTION_RULES`. (3) It fires only on a **positive** Colorado answer: `siteState: null` (every legacy plan without coordinates) behaves byte-identically to before.
- **The state is resolved geometrically and WITHOUT a network call** (`coloradoRegions.siteState`), because the guard has to hold when every GIS endpoint is down — which is exactly when a site is most likely to fall through to a default. A guard that depends on a fetch is not a guard.
- **Render (corrected after checking the SHIPPED bundle, not the source — see B1110):** what reaches the screen is the **`N/A · CO` chip** in warn tone plus the explicit line *"…Planyr does not yet carry Colorado detention criteria."*. The neighbouring `detVerdict` / `detTone` / `detSub` locals are computed by every branch in that block and read by NONE — a pre-existing dead store, filed as **B1110** — so the chip and the line ARE the guard's visible output. `N/A · CO` is deliberately not "UNKNOWN", which would read as *we could not look it up* and invite the reader to wait for a number that is never coming. In Colorado `detReq` is computed **regardless of whether an authority resolved**, because the normal precondition would otherwise leave the group rendering nothing at all.
- **The four Colorado regimes are NAMED even though detention is not priced** (`CO_DRAINAGE_REGIMES`): **MHFD** (Adams, Arapahoe, Boulder, Broomfield, Denver, Jefferson — 6 of 9), **Larimer**, **Weld**, **El Paso**. Each carries its criteria manual and a `detentionMethod` saying what would have to be built, so the gap reads as legible rather than mysterious. Larimer/Weld/El Paso each state outright that they are **not** MHFD members.
- **Capabilities ending this session NOT wired for Colorado**, each with its own copy in the `CAPABILITIES` matrix: detention volume · compensating storage / floodplain mitigation · tax units and rates · utility easement widths · thoroughfare plan / ROW · **partial**: required FFE (CWCB floor only, no local ordinance) and drainage authority (named, not priced) · **not applicable** (distinct from not-built, so it never implies work that will never happen): subsidence districts.
- **PANEL-BREVITY measured before/after** (`node ui-audit/panel-copy-budget.mjs`): `yield-detention-detail` 11→**12** lines / 500→**557** chars; `yield-stormwater-notes` 146→**150** / 12576→**12779**. Justified in full in `ui-audit/panel-copy-budget.json`: the added literals are **mutually exclusive** with the Texas copy beside them — a Colorado site shows the Colorado line and never the rate badge, band note or outfall note — so **no single site's default view grows by a line**; the static audit counts every literal in the file. All the substance (both statutory tests, the presumption, the notification, the optimism caveat, the regime's manual, the WQCV+EURV explanation) rides the exempt info argument.
- Verified in sandbox: `test/coloradoGuard.test.js` 26 cases · full suite **6,120 green** · lint 0 · build green · PANEL-BREVITY green.
### B1101 — The Standards footer's `Project | All` toggle looked like one axis with Apply and was two — three explicitly named actions, a pending draft, and a footer that stops slicing the settings list `[Site Planner / standards]` (task) #site-planner #ui #persistence  *(owner chat block 2026-07-29, provisional ITEM 2 / NEW-2 — **AMENDS the footer just shipped in B1070 / PR #832** (and the engine under it, B1060). Minted **B1101 / V511** via `git fetch origin main && npm run next-id -- --against-main`; code and tests keep the provisional `NEW-2` label per the house rule. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open + ⏳ Verify + Done across the Standards family (**B1070** the one-Apply-one-scope footer this amends, **B1060** the apply + account-scope engine it is built on, **B653** the Standards panel, **B929** parcel style defaults, **B740** the multi-select workaround): **NOT a recurrence of B1070** — B1070's consolidation was correct and is KEPT in full; what is wrong is the SEMANTICS of the two controls it put side by side, which no prior item questions. Origin: filed 2026-07-29 from chat as ITEM 2.)*
`[ ]` **⏳ merged — V511 PENDING (Verify: live — `Blocker: auth`).** Everything reachable logged-out was driven HEADLESS this session and PASSED; only the signed-in account-level write behind **Save for all projects** is owed. Proof is on the V511 entry.
- Verify: live
- Origin: filed 2026-07-29 from chat as ITEM 2
- **Why the old one was wrong (the owner's diagnosis, and the reason this is a redesign rather than a relabel).** `Project | All` and `Apply` look like one axis and are two: the segmented control chose **where the value is STORED**; Apply **pushed it onto objects already DRAWN**. Read left to right it parsed as "apply to this project or apply to all" — which it can never be, since nothing can retroactively restyle a plan you have not opened. Hierarchy was inverted on top of that: `All` was a loud filled accent chip while `Apply` was faint grey, so the least consequential control shouted the loudest.
- **What it is now — THREE buttons, each named outright, no scope toggle.** **Apply to this plan (N)** · **Save for this plan** · **Save for all projects**. Apply carries the live count of objects it would change and is the primary (filled); the two Saves are quiet outlined secondaries. Apply keeps its existing toast **with Undo** (it is the only action that touches drawn geometry); the two Saves get a brief non-blocking confirmation with **no Undo**, because there is nothing to take back.
- **THE CONSEQUENCE, HANDLED: Standards edits are now a PENDING DRAFT.** Once "Save for this plan" is an explicit button, a field edit can no longer silently commit as the plan default, or that button means nothing. So every Standards style edit lands in `stdDraft` and NOTHING is stored until a button commits it. The pure model is `lib/standardsApply.js` (`EMPTY_STD_DRAFT` / `withParcelDraft` / `withTypeDraft` / `draftParcelValue` / `draftTypeValue` / `draftDirty` / `mergeDraftIntoSettings`); `derivedPanelScope` and the whole per-key scope machinery (`parcelStdScope` / `typeStdScope` / `stdScopeKeys` / `settings.stdScope` / `promoteParcelStd` / `promoteTypeStd`) are DELETED, not left dead.
- **An unsaved-edit trap would be worse than the problem, so the draft is visible, reversible and durable.** The footer shows a quiet **● Unsaved changes** marker (in `--warn-text`, the AA amber this app uses for every saving / unsaved / offline label) with **Discard** beside it; Discard drops the draft, which restores the pre-edit values by construction since nothing was ever written. `draftDirty` compares against what is COMMITTED, so editing a value back to where it started clears the marker instead of leaving a permanent nag. The draft is persisted per PLAN in `sessionStorage` (`planyr:stdDraft:<siteId>`), so closing the panel, switching workspace or reloading cannot silently throw the edits away — **and a draft can never leak onto a different plan**, which plain component state would have allowed on a plan switch.
- **"Apply to this plan" commits AND pushes in ONE undo frame**, exactly as specified — applying implies keeping, so it does not take two clicks. Its toast's Undo takes back the WHOLE action: the drawn objects, the stored plan defaults, and the pending draft all come back.
- **"Save for all projects" writes the account-level defaults** through the existing `cloudReady` path (`public.profiles.prefs`, own-row RLS), then drops this plan's own copies so the plan keeps following the account default when it later changes — the old promote rule, generalised from one key to the panel. It touches nothing already drawn, and signed out it stays disabled with its existing explanatory tooltip rather than passing a per-computer value off as an account default.
- **A draft changes what you SEE, never what gets STORED.** Element type styles resolve at RENDER, so the canvas previews the draft live (`planStyle.setPreviewStyleDefaults`, a layer above the project setting and below a per-object override, where a `null` CLEARS back to the built-in rather than painting nothing). `parcelDefaultStyle` deliberately does NOT read it — it STAMPS a value into a new parcel, and an uncommitted value must never reach stored geometry. "Reset all to built-in" became a draft edit (a null per key) like everything else.
- **PLACEMENT — it is a real footer now, not a sticky bar inside the list.** The old bar was `position: sticky` INSIDE the scrolling settings container with a negative bottom margin, so it hovered over the content and cut whatever row sat at the bottom of the scrollport in half (the reported "Bay band (min / max)" slice) and did not span the panel. It is now rendered as a **sibling BELOW the scroll container** in both hosts — the docked panel and `FloatingPanel`, which gained a `footer` slot — with a hairline rule above and a subtle upward shadow so it reads as chrome. That is strictly stronger than the bottom-padding remedy the brief proposed: a sibling reserves its own space, so **no row can be occluded at ANY scroll position**, not just at the bottom, which is what the e2e asserts (`footer.top >= scroller.bottom`) at both a middle and a bottom scroll. The actions share a row when they fit and wrap into full-width rows when the panel is narrow — never overflowing or clipping.
- **GUARDS.** `test/standardsApply.test.js` gains 20 draft cases (dirty/not-dirty incl. editing back to the committed value, null-as-clear, immutability, the settings fold incl. deleting a key and dropping an emptied type bag, and the preview layer's three rules — previews, clears to built-in, and never reaches `parcelDefaultStyle`). `test/bugHuntGuards.test.js`'s colour-control pins now FORBID `setParcelStd` / `liveTypeStyle` (the direct-to-settings writers) and require the draft writers with no promote hook. `e2e/standards-footer-setback.spec.js` drives it logged out: no scope toggle, the three names, the disabled + explained Save-for-all, the filled-primary hierarchy, dirty → Discard → restored, Save-for-this-plan storing with a no-Undo confirmation, Apply committing AND restyling with a full Undo, the draft surviving a panel close AND a reload, and the footer geometry at desktop + narrow in BOTH themes at two scroll positions (with screenshots).
- **THE PERF BUDGET WAS PAID, NOT WAIVED.** These two items added ~4.4 KB to `SitePlannerApp`, taking `bundle.largestChunkBytes` to 1712.0 KB against a 1709.0 KB ceiling. Per `docs/PERF-BUDGETS.md` a breach ships with a matching optimization or does not ship, so the ceiling was **not** raised. The optimization is in the same neighbourhood as the breach — the panels these items touch — and follows **B1093**'s precedent exactly: five pure inline-style object literals repeated across the panel bodies (a centred flex row ×22, a tighter one ×8, a baseline row ×6, the space-between settings row ×9, the white text halo ×4) are now ONE module-scope const each, the two chip/input variants (×13, ×5) and the uppercase sub-heading (×5) are one component-scope const each, and the three-option line-style list — now at **six** selects, since this PR adds two — is ONE shared `DASH_OPTIONS` array. Byte-identical output by construction (every literal was lifted verbatim), with stable object identity as a free side effect. **1712.0 → 1708.3 KB**, back inside the ceiling.
- **PANEL-BREVITY** — not a yield/pond panel, but measured anyway: `node ui-audit/panel-copy-budget.mjs --check` reports all regions within budget, unchanged. The footer replaced two controls with three and added one conditional marker line; no explanatory prose was added on screen (every explanation is a tooltip).
### B1093 — "Select parcels: off" strands the user: clicking a parcel does nothing, with no feedback `[Site Planner / parcelSelect]` (bug) #site-planner #selection #ui  *(owner-reported 2026-07-29 as "it's not letting me click on Tsakiris parcels"; diagnosed live on `smrjdgmlinea` and handed over as a chat block with the repro already confirmed. Minted **B1093 / V505** via `git fetch origin main && npm run next-id -- --against-main`; code, tests and commits carry the provisional label `NEW-1` per the late-bind house rule. DEDUPE-FIRST: searched Open, ⏳ Verify and Done for `parcelSelect` / "Select parcels" — **B310** (click-vs-drag intent) and **B311** (the mode toggle itself) are the shipped features this bug is ABOUT, not recurrences of; **B441** / **B4** are map-side parcel-selection items with a different mechanism. No prior item covers the silent-failure trap, so this is a new number. Origin: filed 2026-07-29 from chat.)*
`[ ]` **⏳ merged — V505 PENDING (Verify: live). Fully self-verified headless on the branch build this session (5/5 spec cases, desktop + narrow, light + dark, teeth proven against the pre-fix build); what is owed is the same spec against the DEPLOYED planyr.io origin, per MERGED ≠ LIVE.**
- Verify: live
- Origin: filed 2026-07-29 from chat
- **Repro (owner, confirmed live before filing).** `sites.data.settings.parcelSelect` was `false` on the owner's plan `smrjdgmlinea` — it had been `true` earlier the same day, so it was flipped at some point without being noticed. Every press on a lot then fell through to a background pan: no selection, no movement, no message.
- **Root cause (AUDIT-FIRST) — the code is behaving exactly as designed; the DESIGN is the trap.** `startMoveParcel` (`SitePlanner.jsx`) carries B311's `if (!settings.parcelSelect) return;` — a deliberate click-through so a lot's edge doesn't swallow clicks during building work. Three properties turn that into a dead end: the flag is **persisted per plan**, so one flip follows the owner across sessions and devices; the only indication was a header pill that, styled as a borderless ghost with muted text in its OFF state, **read as a passive status label**; and the failure itself was **silent at the point of interaction** — nothing where the click happened said why nothing happened.
- **The click-through behaviour is UNCHANGED.** B311 is the point of the mode; this item adds feedback, a discoverable control, and an announcement — it does not make parcels grab clicks again.
- **(1) The readout IS the control.** The pill was already a `<button>`; it now looks and behaves like one — a real pill border and full-contrast chrome text in BOTH states (no muted-text OFF state, per the theming rule), the state spelled out either way (`Select parcels: on` / `Select parcels: off`), `aria-pressed` + an explicit `aria-label`, a "click to turn it on or off" tooltip, and the native `:focus-visible` ring, so Tab-then-Enter operates it. `data-testid="parcel-select-toggle"`.
- **(2) Feedback at the point of failure.** A press that provably lands on a parcel's boundary or setback hit-stroke while selection is off raises a short non-blocking hint on the SAME bottom-center toast surface the canvas already uses — *"Parcel selection is off — that click panned the map."* — with an inline **Turn it on** action and a Dismiss. It rides one notch higher when the existing pill is occupied, so neither message can swallow the other. The decision is a pure, unit-tested module (`lib/parcelSelectHint.js`): never when selection is on, **never on empty canvas**, at most one per press gesture (keyed on the event's `timeStamp`, deliberately NOT `pointerId` — Chromium reuses id 1 for every mouse press, which would suppress the hint forever after the first), and rate-limited so a pan across a subdivision can never become a stream.
- **(3) The keyboard-shortcut question — ANSWERED: there is none, and this is the reported finding.** A full sweep of the planner's keydown handler and the whole repo for `parcelSelect` shows **no shortcut of any kind, modified or bare, that flips it**; the toggle button is the only writer in the codebase. So the owner's flip came from clicking the pill, not from a stray keypress. The mitigation is therefore the other half of the brief: **the toggle now announces itself when flipped** — turning it off flashes *"Select parcels is OFF — clicks pan the map instead of selecting a lot."* — so an accidental flip is visible at the moment it happens instead of surfacing days later as "the app stopped letting me click my parcels". Both the header pill and the hint's inline action route through one `setParcelSelect` helper, so the two can never drift.
- **Guards.** `test/parcelSelectHint.test.js` (17): the decision matrix; a replayed gesture stream proving exactly one hint per press, one hint for a pan across ten lots, one per cooldown window under impatient repeat-clicking, and zero for 25 empty-canvas presses; plus `settings.parcelSelect` round-tripping per plan through the REAL `saveSite`/`loadSite` path (the cross-session trap itself). `e2e/parcel-select-toggle.spec.js` drives the real render path logged out on a drawn parcel at **desktop and narrow width in both light and dark theme**: with selection off a boundary press raises the hint, does NOT select and does NOT move the lot; an empty-canvas press stays silent; repeat presses don't stack; **Turn it on** restores selection and the SAME boundary point then selects; and the pill is keyboard-operable. Press targets are projected through the live SVG screen matrix and then confirmed via `elementsFromPoint`, so the spec can't pass by pressing thin air.
- **Sandbox evidence.** `npm run lint` 0 errors · `npm test` 6056 green (365 files) · `npm run build` green · `node ui-audit/perf-bundle-audit.mjs` green · `MAP.md` + `BACKLOG_OPEN.md` regenerated · `npx playwright test e2e/parcel-select-toggle.spec.js` **5/5** against the branch's own build, plus `clipboard-standards-swatches` / `click-behavior` / `smoke` (17) green over the surfaces the perf fix touched. **Teeth proven:** with the one-line `noteParcelSelectBlocked(e.timeStamp)` call removed and rebuilt, the spec goes RED on the hint assertion — it is a guard, not a decoration.
- **The perf gate caught this feature's cost, and it was PAID, not waived.** CI went red on `bundle.largestChunkBytes` — 1710.2 KB against a 1709.0 KB ceiling (+1.2 KB). Per `docs/PERF-BUDGETS.md` a breach ships with a matching optimization or does not ship, so the ceiling was NOT raised. - Verify: live
- Origin: filed 2026-07-29 from chat
- **The ask.** "I'd like to be able to hover over any contour and it show me the elevation … probably just similar to how it shows the five foot ones." At Tsakiris ~30 index contours carry a permanent label; the other four-in-five 1-ft lines carried none and could not be interrogated at all.
- **Why they were unhoverable (AUDIT-FIRST).** The polylines render into an `L.canvas` with `interactive:false` — B704's deliberate perf decision, since thousands of 1-ft lines with Leaflet hit areas is the perf cliff. Making them interactive to answer this would undo that decision.
- **Fix — hit-test in JS, never make a line interactive.** `contours.js` gains the pure pair `buildContourIndex` / `hitContour`: a flat spatial bucket over the SAME composed geometry `composeContourPaint` paints (one composition, one index — no second geometry model), probed in longitude-scaled degrees so the tolerance is a constant number of SCREEN pixels at every zoom. Ties resolve by LEVEL, so the answer under a resting cursor cannot depend on which tile resolved first (the B1087 determinism rule).
- **One transient label, in its own sublayer.** `terrainLayers.js` paints exactly ONE marker into a dedicated `hoverGroup`, using the same white-halo divIcon, size and colour as the permanent index labels. It is cleared on every move, re-parented empty on every repaint (a label can never outlive the lines it named), and dropped on `onRemove`. It carries `.planyr-contour-hover` so a harness can tell the transient one from the permanent set. NO DOUBLE-STAMP: a hit whose level already has a permanent label within ~40 px paints nothing. Same z16 gate as the contours.
- **No second listener.** `setContourHover(map, ll)` is fed from the cursor position each surface ALREADY computes for the ground readout (the map finder's rAF-throttled `onCoordMove`; the planner's `cursorLL` memo). The `map` argument means the inactive-but-mounted surface's layer clears instead of painting for a cursor that isn't over it.
- **Sandbox + headless evidence.** `test/contourHoverReadout.test.js` (37 green) pins the hit-test: an unlabelled 1-ft line answers, intermediate values read 152/153/154/155, the returned point lies ON the line, a cursor between lines answers NOTHING (no nearest-line fallback), the result is order-independent, ties resolve by level, a segment longer than a bucket is still found, and the tolerance scales. `e2e/contour-hover-elevation.spec.js` drives the REAL planner logged out at the Tsakiris coordinates against REAL 3DEP LiDAR (the sandbox's browser egress can't reach the USGS host, so the spec relays that ONE request through Node — a transport detail only; the app's own fetch, decode, worker trace and paint all run for real). Measured: **30 permanent index labels · a 110-point sweep landed on a line 71 times, naming 149/150/152/153/154/156/157/158 ft — intermediate 1-ft values, not only multiples of five · never more than ONE transient label · agreement with the bottom-left ground readout median 0.30 ft, p90 1.00 ft · leaving the lines cleared it (0) with the permanent set unchanged (30 → 30) · zero duplicate stamps · zero page errors.**
- **The matching optimization (the perf-budget rule).** The two features added real bytes and tripped `bundle.largestChunkBytes` in CI (1715.5 KB vs a 1709.0 KB ceiling). Per `docs/PERF-BUDGETS.md` a breach ships with an optimization or does not ship, so the terrain pipeline now **loads on demand**: `terrainLazy.js` is the ONE entry point (`loadTerrain()` cached import + a SYNCHRONOUS `terrainNow()` so the per-move cursor sample stays a plain function call once the chunk has landed), `terrainGate.js` carries the zoom gate so the layer registry can read it without dragging the pipeline back in, and `contourTrace.js` splits the worker-only marching-squares tracer (the sole `d3-contour` consumer) out of `contours.js` — the `lercGrid.js` (B1042) precedent, one module over. `layers.js` imports the layer constructors at the first terrain toggle and refuses to resurrect a layer the user switched off while the chunk was in flight. `[ ]` **⏳ merged — V507 PENDING (Verify: live — `Blocker: real-data`, a signed-in project with a real concept + FFE, and a water/void hover). The always-a-state behaviour, the ungated fast path, the LOUD failure and the Prop/cut-fill pair were all DRIVEN AND PASSED headless — see below.**
- Verify: live
- Origin: filed 2026-07-29 from chat
- **Repro (owner).** "Sometimes it shows an elevation, like the existing elevation, but sometimes it doesn't."
- **Root cause (AUDIT-FIRST).** `useGroundElevation` (B706) had two paths: LOCAL bilinear sampling of a cached terrain grid (instant, rock solid) and ONE debounced `getSamples` call after ~300 ms of cursor REST. With the layer off or the map below the z16 gate, path 2 was the only one running — and B706's shipped rule rendered no-data, void, in-flight and failure ALL AS ABSENCE. So a cursor that never rested (the common case while dragging around) produced nothing at all, which reads as a glitch and is indistinguishable from a real "nothing here". The no-fabrication rule was right; the vanishing was not.
- **(a) Always render the field, with an explicit state.** `useGroundElevation` now returns a STATE, and `lib/groundReadout.js` (pure, new) is the ONE composition both surfaces paint: `Exist 152.6 ft` · `Exist …` · `Exist — (no data here)` · `Exist — (unavailable)`. Reason detail rides the chip's existing `title`. No new chrome, no fabricated numbers, and no state can render as the empty string.
- **(b) The fast path is now the NORMAL case.** `warmCursorGrid` pulls the ONE lattice tile under the cursor REGARDLESS of layer toggles and REGARDLESS of the z16 gate — that gate is a cartography judgement about 1-ft LINES on a coarse cell, never a reason to refuse to sample a POINT; a coarse sample is instead MARKED (`≈`) and explained. It asks for the same `latticeTile` the contour layer asks for at that zoom, so with contours on it is a plain cache hit. It deliberately calls `computeTile` directly rather than through `gisCache.swr`: **swr serves the cached contour artifact without ever running the fetch, so a view painted from cache left the grid registry EMPTY — which is why the fast path went missing after a reload even with contours on.** A failed tile is not retried for 30 s, so a dead endpoint can't be hammered per cursor move.
- **(c) PROPOSED, from the ledger's own surface.** `proposedSurface.surfaceGrid` now publishes `owners` — the very ownership array it priced its lattice from — and the new pure `sampleProposedAt` walks it through the SAME precedence (pad → dock stack → the rest), the same pond exclusion and the same B833 transition taper. So the readout and the B826 earthwork rows read ONE surface by construction, not by care. It NEVER extrapolates a plane past its own element: outside every footprint and its daylight wedge the answer is `Prop —` with an honest reason (no FFE set / no graded element here / pond interior = borrow / no ground data).
- **(d) The delta is the point.** Signed and labelled `Fill 2.4` / `Cut 1.8` on the B809/B826 cut/fill ramp (clamped to the readable end of each ramp for the dark chip — same warm-fill / cool-cut families as the exhibit), `On grade` inside the zero band, and SUPPRESSED whenever either side is unknown.
- **(f) One line, at its existing size.** `components/CursorChip.jsx` is the ONE chip both surfaces render. The old chip truncated from the right, which ate the ELEVATION first; the elevation group is now flex-fixed and the COORDINATE pair is what gives way.
- **Bug found by driving it, fixed here (LOUD-FAILURE).** A caller-supplied `AbortSignal` used to REPLACE `samplePoint`'s own controller, silently disabling its timeout with it — so a socket that accepted and never answered NEVER SETTLED, and the readout sat in-flight forever with no way to ever report the failure. `samplePoint` now always owns the controller, chains the caller's signal onto it, and distinguishes the two aborts: a timeout throws as a real failure, a caller abort stays an `AbortError` the hook ignores.
- **Sandbox + headless evidence.** `test/contourHoverReadout.test.js` 37 green — every state renders a field; a void and a failure are DIFFERENT named states; coarse cells are marked and explained; the unit is written exactly once; the delta is suppressed when either side is unknown; **every priced footprint cell AND every transition-wedge cell of a real B826 grid ties out to `sampleProposedAt` exactly**; a pond reads "borrow"; a far-off point returns nothing rather than an extrapolated plane; and the `samplePoint` timeout/abort split is pinned. `e2e/contour-hover-elevation.spec.js`, REAL planner, logged out, real 3DEP: **the field was present on every frame of a 12-point non-pausing sweep · a resting cursor with NO contour layer on resolved to a real Katy elevation and a never-visited neighbour then answered in under the 300 ms debounce (i.e. from the local grid) · a forced endpoint failure produced "Exist — (unavailable)", never silence · on a seeded concept with FFE 156 the pad read `Prop 156.0` and the delta equalled proposed − existing exactly, while bare ground read `Prop —` with "No graded element here" on the title · the chip stayed ONE line and the coordinate pair, not the elevation, is the shrinking part.** `npm test` 6076 green · lint 0 errors · build green.
- **What is still owed (V507).** On planyr.io signed in: three points spot-checked against the Yield → Earthwork cut/fill ROWS on a real project (the engine-level tie-out is proven for every cell, the panel comparison is not), and a hover over water / a DEM void showing "no data here" on real ground.

- **Repro.** Tsakiris (Waller County, inside BKDD), Flood & drainage expanded. LOCAL DRAINAGE AUTHORITY listed "Drainage channels & ROW — HCFCD" and "Storm sewer — City of Houston" beside the two BKDD rows, with nothing said. Neither agency has so much as a pipe in Waller County.
- **Root cause (AUDIT-FIRST).** `scopeFloodEntries` suppressed a district row on ONE signal: `cfg.district !== governing`. `governing` comes from the drainage context (`resolveDrainageContext` → `drainageDistrict`), which is null until a drainage check has run and been remembered — and a snapshot saved before B1080 carries no district at all. Null `governing` → fail open → every district renders. Two further holes underneath it: `COUNTY_DISTRICT` was keyed `"fort bend"` while the panel's own county prop is `"fortbend"`, so the county fallback could never fire in Fort Bend; and `coh_storm` had no district at all, so the district gate could not reach it in any state.
- **Fix — ONE mechanism, four ordered signals** (`floodRowRelevance`, `lib/floodGroup.js`), reusing the coverage-scope machinery the Master Plan gate already uses rather than adding a second: (1) a district row that isn't the governing one; (2) a district row whose district does not REACH this county (`districtReaches`, off `DRAINAGE_DISTRICTS[].counties` — no network, no drainage check, so it works the moment the county is known); (3) a row whose agency's own service area is elsewhere (`cfg.areaCounties`, now declared on `coh_storm`); (4) the coverage engine's published-extent "out". County keys canonicalise (`countyKey`), so `"Fort Bend"` / `"fortbend"` / `"Fort Bend County"` can never miss again.
- **Demoted, never deleted.** A demoted row moves behind ONE collapsed line — "N sources that don't cover this site" — where it keeps its checkbox and carries its own reason ("Harris County Flood Control District doesn't cover Waller County — Brookshire–Katy Drainage District is shown instead."). That satisfies both branches the owner offered (not rendered in the default view / listed with the honest coverage note) and keeps a scoping call one click from being overridden. A layer the user has ALREADY turned on is never yanked away — it stays in its tier with the reason as a caption. The old free-floating swap line is REMOVED (the reason now rides the row it explains): the local tier at Tsakiris goes from four rows + one note to two rows + one collapsed line.
- **Sandbox evidence.** `ui-audit/flood-group-verify.mjs` 34/34 (new: a Waller panel with NO drainage context at all now demotes both, discloses both, and names both reasons); `test/floodGroup.test.js` 54 green; and the B1092 e2e drives the REAL planner at the Tsakiris coordinates logged out — its screenshot shows LOCAL DRAINAGE AUTHORITY carrying only the two BKDD rows.
- **What is still owed (V503).** The signed-in Tsakiris project on planyr.io: that the real record's county resolves the demotion on his page, and that the collapsed line reads right beside the live BKDD rows.

---
- **Recurrence (×2) — 2026-07-29, found on planyr.io minutes after PR #839 merged. CONFIDENT-WRONG, and worse than the silence it replaced.**
- **Repro.** Hard-reload `https://planyr.io/#/project/smrjdgmlinea/site` (Tsakiris, `sites.id smrjdgmlinea`, county waller, origin 29.77938 / -95.89503) → Layers → Flood & drainage. **ACTUAL:** every BKDD row (District streams/watersheds/BFE, District drainage easements, Master Plan floodplains) carried "Brookshire–Katy Drainage District doesn't govern drainage at this site — Harris County Flood Control District does"; the HCFCD and City-of-Houston rows carried none. **EXPECTED:** the exact reverse.
- **Ground truth, re-checked live from this sandbox 2026-07-29 (not a judgement call).** A point-in-polygon query of the site origin against BKDD's own district boundary (`services1.arcgis.com/…/Brookshire_Katy_Drainage_District1/FeatureServer/54`) returns **n=1, Name "BROOKSHIRE-KATY DRAINAGE DISTRICT"**. HCFCD returns n=0 at this point: its jurisdiction ends at the Harris County line and this tract is in Waller.
- **Root cause (AUDIT-FIRST) — THREE distinct defects, all shipped together, each sufficient on its own.**
- **(a) A GUESS was given the authority of a FACT.** `floodRowRelevance` demoted a district row whenever `governing` was non-null and different — including a `governing` the COUNTY heuristic merely inferred. Districts overlap counties: BKDD spans Waller, Harris AND Fort Bend, so "this county's flood-control district is HCFCD" is no evidence whatsoever about BKDD. That single unqualified comparison is the inversion. `governingDistrict` now returns **`exclusive`** — true for a boundary containment, or for a county answer only once every rival district has been boundary-tested and CLEANLY excluded — and only an exclusive answer may say another district doesn't govern. A guess may still demote a district that cannot REACH this county (checkable), and otherwise **fails open**.
- **(b) The panel reasoned over the WRONG COUNTY.** The scoping consumed `LayerPanel`'s `county` prop, which is the parcel-lookup / jurisdiction-layer REGISTRY KEY — a UI selector that `useState`s to `"harris"` on every site and only ever names counties Planyr publishes local layers for. It is not a fact about where the site is. The panel now reasons over the **site identify county** (`floodContext.authority.jurisdiction.county` — the same value the header renders as "Waller County"), falling back to the site record's own county (new `siteCounty` prop); a straddle or an unresolved identify yields null, which fails open. `county` keeps its original job (which county's local layers to offer).
- **(c) A remembered check FORGOT the district the boundary test found — confirmed against the production row.** The Tsakiris snapshot in Supabase has **no `drainageDistrict` key at all** (it predates B1080) while its own `authority.flags` carry **`"bkdd-district-present"`** and its overlays carry the `drainage-district` / `bkdd` record — i.e. the boundary query had answered YES. `hydrateDrainageContext` read only the county-derived `channelAuthority`, so that fact was discarded on every reload and a county guess filled the vacuum. Hydration now reads the flag (and the stored overlay) FIRST and restores the district with `source: "boundary"`.
- **LOUD-FAILURE.** A FAILED district-membership query is no longer indistinguishable from a clean negative: `resolveDrainageContext` publishes `drainageDistrict.tested` — the district ids whose boundary query actually answered — and an outage (`bkdd-unverified`) leaves the id out, so it can never license an exclusion. Unknown stays unknown.
- **The copy itself was kept verbatim** (the owner: "the honest-state copy is good"); only the resolution changed. Zero new visible lines — PANEL-BREVITY not engaged.
- **Regression guards, both directions, so a future inversion fails in CI rather than on the live map.** `test/floodGroup.test.js` adds a `B1091(×2)` block: Tsakiris/Waller → BKDD governs and HCFCD is demoted with the county-reach wording; the mirror (a Harris site whose BKDD boundary test came back cleanly empty) → HCFCD governs and BKDD is demoted with the governs wording; a county guess with no boundary test excludes nothing; a FAILED query is not a negative; and a sweep asserting **no input combination ever prints "BKDD doesn't govern" at a site inside BKDD**. `test/detentionRules.test.js` adds a `B1091(×2)` block built from the REAL production snapshot (verbatim legacy shape) proving it rehydrates BKDD-governed. `ui-audit/flood-group-verify.mjs` **38/38** against the real `LayerPanel`, including a new stale-county panel. `e2e/flood-district-scoping.spec.js` drives the REAL planner logged out with that same production snapshot seeded — and its stale-county case **FAILS on the pre-fix build** (4 sources demoted, every BKDD row gone), which is what makes it a guard rather than a decoration.
- **Sandbox evidence.** `npm test` 6030+ green · `node ui-audit/flood-group-verify.mjs` 38/38 · `npx playwright test e2e/flood-district-scoping.spec.js e2e/canvas-gis-identify.spec.js` green · lint 0 errors · build green.
- **What is still owed (V503).** The signed-in Tsakiris page on planyr.io, which is also where B1092's easement identify finally gets its real width + exhibit (below).

---
- **Recurrence (×3) — 2026-07-29, owner chat block (provisional NEW-1 + NEW-2), on the deployed PR #840 build. Reported as "both notes regressed to SILENCE".** NEW-1: no row anywhere carried a governing/not-governing note, in either direction (`/doesn't govern/` → zero matches over the group). NEW-2: the zone-specific FEMA sentence ("Zone A — a special flood hazard area IS mapped here") was gone, leaving only the standing ZONES-not-channels line (`/Zone A/` → zero matches after a 9 s settle). The suspected cause on the item was that `floodCounty` — rewired in the ×2 fix to the resolved-county signal — was null at panel render.
- **AUDIT-FIRST, and it does NOT land where the report predicted. Recorded here rather than quietly "fixed", because the difference matters.** The tract's ACTUAL production snapshot was read out of Supabase (`sites.id smrjdgmlinea`: `county waller`, `authority.jurisdiction.county ["Waller"]`, `flags [… "bkdd-district-present"]`, `flood.state "loaded"`, `flood.zones [X, A]`) and fed to the REAL planner headless. `floodCounty` resolves to **"Waller"**, `governingDistrict` returns **bkdd / boundary / exclusive**, and the **visible** planner panel renders, correctly and in full: BKDD's three rows listed, HCFCD + City-of-Houston demoted behind "2 sources that don't cover this site" each naming its reason, and **"FEMA effective FIRM: Zone A — a special flood hazard area IS mapped here."** Nothing about the ×2 fix suppressed either line. **The silence is real, but it is a DIFFERENT panel.**
- **(a) ROOT CAUSE — a hidden DECOY copy of the whole group, first in the document.** `SitePlannerApp` keeps BOTH modes mounted and hides the inactive one with `display:none`, so the map finder's Layers panel is never torn down (its Leaflet map would have to be rebuilt). That leaves a COMPLETE second copy of the Flood & drainage group in the DOM whenever the planner is open — one with **no `floodContext` and no `siteCounty`**, hence no verdict line and no row reasons — and, because the map mode is rendered first, it is the copy a page-level text scan reaches first. Verified in the browser: two `Flood & drainage layers` group heads, panel 0 zero-sized under a `display:none` ancestor with no note and no Zone A line, panel 1 visible and complete. A human reading the screen sees the right panel; a regex over the page sees the wrong one. This is also a genuine **accessibility** defect on its own — a screen reader was walking a whole duplicate layers panel — and the same trap the ×2 fix had already caught once, when an e2e `.first()` locator silently resolved into the finder's copy.
- **(b) ROOT CAUSE — and the silent state was reachable for real.** Independent of (a): EVERY honest line in this group is conditional on a resolved drainage context. `femaZoneVerdict` returns null without `flood.state`; `floodRowRelevance` can only demote a row WITH a reason once the county or the governing district is known. So any surface with neither — the finder's copy, and any site whose flood check has never run — renders the group with nothing said at all. **Silence is the one state B1071 exists to abolish, and it was still reachable.** The report was right that the group can go quiet; it was the finder's copy that was quiet, and the fix is to make that state impossible rather than to un-break a fix that was not broken.
- **Fix (b) — the group can no longer render blank.** New pure `floodFactsNote({hasContext, county})` in `lib/floodGroup.js`, rendered by `LayerPanel` as ONE line: no context at all → *"Flood zone and drainage district not checked here yet."*; a check that ran but whose county never resolved → *"County here didn't resolve — every drainage source is listed until it does."*; facts in hand → **null**, so it never accumulates on top of a working readout. `femaZoneVerdict`'s contract is untouched (it still says only what FEMA said, and still claims nothing with no data) — the new function owns the state the old one deliberately declined to speak for. **PANEL-BREVITY:** the Layers panel is not a budgeted region, and this adds a line only in a state that previously rendered ZERO lines — the default view of a site with its facts in hand is byte-for-byte unchanged (`node ui-audit/panel-copy-budget.mjs --check` green).
- **Fix (a) — the hidden mode stops being a decoy.** The inactive mode wrapper in `SitePlannerApp.jsx` now carries `inert` + `aria-hidden="true"` (out of the a11y tree, out of focus order, out of every role-based query) plus `data-mode` / `data-mode-active`; `LayerPanel` stamps `data-testid="layer-panel"` + `data-surface="planner"|"finder"` on its root. Both modes stay MOUNTED — the keep-alive is the point — so the copy is now labelled and inert rather than removed. The FEMA verdict and the state note carry `data-testid`s so a check can assert the live panel's line instead of scraping page text.

### B1092 — The BKDD easement identify never fires on the planner canvas: identify was wired for the map finder only `[Site Planner / GIS]` (task) #site-planner #gis #floodplain  *(owner live-verify 2026-07-29 at the Tsakiris tract, provisional NEW-2: "single-click and double-click on the easement band and on the channel centreline produced only the coordinate/elevation readout, never a feature popup."
