DEDUPE-FIRST: AMENDS B1069 (BKDD source registration), which correctly made the easement layer vector; nothing existing covers canvas-side identify. Origin: filed 2026-07-29 from chat.)*
`[ ]` **⏳ merged — V504 PENDING (Verify: live — `Blocker: live-GIS`, the real Quiddity endpoint is policy-403 from this sandbox's egress proxy). V503 CLOSED — see the NEW-3 strand at the end of this item.**
- Verify: live
- Origin: filed 2026-07-29 from chat
- **AUDIT-FIRST verdict: NOT wired — and it could not have been.** `cachedVectorLayer` binds its hover/click identify only when `interactive` is true, which comes from `opts.identifyOk`. `MapFinder.jsx` passes it (`identifyOk: () => !selectModeRef.current`); `SitePlanner.jsx` never did, so no handler was bound at all. On top of that the planner's Leaflet backdrop sits inside a `pointerEvents:"none"` box — its SVG canvas owns every pointer event — so even a bound handler could never receive the click. Only the coordinate/elevation chip could answer, which is exactly what the owner saw. Making that layer vector bought nothing on the surface where a site is actually worked.
- **Fix.** The pure half moves into `vectorLayers.js` (`hitFeature` — polygon containment, line distance within a caller-supplied tolerance; `identifyRows` — the registry rows as data). `vectorOverlay.js` keeps the last painted FeatureCollection and exposes `group.identifyAt({lat,lng,tolDeg})` on BOTH cached layers, built from the same rows the Leaflet popover renders, so the two surfaces cannot drift. `layers.js` adds `identifyOverlaysAt(refs, overlays, at)`. `SitePlanner.jsx` calls it from the existing tap-on-empty-canvas path (the B735 `tapEmpty` branch) and shows a themed card at the tap: title, the registry rows, the source's caveat, the agency. Dismissed by the next press, by Esc, and by a zoom (it is anchored in screen space).
- **Opt-in per layer (`cfg.canvasIdentify`), on `bkdd_easements` + `nhd_flowlines` only.** Deliberately NOT every vector layer: county / city / ETJ / ISD polygons blanket the view, so every empty click would land on one and the card would become noise instead of an answer. A layer in its raster tier or on its live fallback has no geometry in hand and declines rather than guessing.
- **The map-finder interaction, documented (the owner's other branch).** There it DOES work today and needs no code: hover the band for its name, single-click for the popover. It is suppressed while parcel-select mode is armed (`identifyOk`), and the layer must be in its VECTOR tier — below zoom 13, or over a view wider than the source's area gate, the layer is a raster picture and has nothing to identify.
- **Sandbox evidence.** `e2e/canvas-gis-identify.spec.js` drives the real planner at the Tsakiris coordinates with the district endpoint stubbed at the network boundary: a tap on the band opens a card reading **70 ft** and **WF-10.pdf** with the hard-constraint caveat; a tap off the band opens nothing. Plus `hitFeature` / `identifyRows` / `identifyOverlaysAt` unit tests (containment, holes, line tolerance, multi-part, opt-in gate, off-layer, throwing layer).
- **Shipped against the perf budget the way the standing rule requires** (`docs/PERF-BUDGETS.md`: *a feature that breaches a budget ships with a matching optimization, or does not ship*). The added code pushed `bundle.largestChunkBytes` 4.4 KB past its ceiling, so rather than raise the ceiling, the signed-in-only legacy-import review modal (`SiteReviewModal`, ~7.7 KB — conditional, menu-opened, never on the critical path) moved behind a `React.lazy` dynamic import, the same pattern B1042 established for the export path. Net: the planner chunk came out **below** where it started (1754932 → 1746620 B). It inherits the house chunk-load-failure guard (`app/chunkReload.js` + the shell error boundary).
- **What is still owed (V503).** The real thing: `gisclient.quiddity.com` is policy-403 from this sandbox, so the card has only ever been driven against a stubbed response. On planyr.io, tap the easement band at Tsakiris and confirm the popup carries the real recorded width and exhibit; tap the Willow Fork centreline (NHD layer on) and confirm it names the watercourse and its class.
- **2026-07-29 owner live-verify result — the mechanism PASSES, the district card was BLOCKED.** Tapping the channel at Tsakiris returned "Willow Fork / Type: canal / ditch / USGS national hydrography — an inventory of where water runs. NOT a regulatory floodplain, and it says nothing about how much the channel can carry. / Source: U.S. Geological Survey — National Hydrography Dataset": **PASS on the mechanism and on the provenance framing**, so the canvas identify itself is confirmed live and is NOT re-opened here. The BKDD easement card — the 70 ft and the recorded exhibit WF-10.pdf, the entire reason B1069 made that layer vector — could not be reached, because **B1091 (×2) was demoting the BKDD rows out of the panel**. That block is now removed; the easement half of V503(f) is the one strand still owed.

---
- **Strand closed — 2026-07-29, owner chat block (provisional NEW-3): "determine from the code whether the easement band is in the identify hit-test set at all and what the hit tolerance is at the default site zoom, then either fix it or document the exact interaction needed. Close V503 either way."**
- **It WAS in the hit-test set the whole time.** `bkdd_easements` carries `canvasIdentify: true`; `identifyOverlaysAt` gates on that flag plus the layer being ON; `cachedVectorLayer` exposes `identifyAt` and holds the painted FeatureCollection; the source's `minVectorZoom` is 13, well below any working site zoom, so the layer is in its vector tier (not the raster fallback, which honestly declines). No wiring was missing.
- **THE DEFECT — polygons had ZERO click tolerance.** `hitFeature` accepted a `tolDeg` and then applied it to LINES ONLY: polygons hit-tested by containment alone. So the channel centreline carried the planner's full on-screen slop on both sides while the easement band — a **70 ft** ribbon, a few pixels wide at the default site zoom — had a click target exactly its own drawn width and not a pixel more. Land beside it and the identify returned nothing, the tap fell through, and the coordinate/elevation readout answered instead. That is precisely the three failed live attempts, and it is why the channel (a line) answered on the first try while the band never did.
- **Fix.** `hitFeature` now applies the SAME tolerance to polygon ring EDGES, in **two passes**: an exact containment anywhere in the collection wins first, and only then does the near-miss fallback answer. The two-pass order is load-bearing — with adjacent polygons (two counties sharing a border) a tap just inside one is within tolerance of the other's edge, and a single-pass loop would hand back whichever came first in draw order. So the new tolerance is confined to taps that previously hit **nothing at all**; no existing answer changes. Nothing about the slop itself changed (the planner's fixed on-screen tolerance, converted to feet at the live zoom), so a wide polygon behaves exactly as before.
- **Regression guards.** `test/vectorLayers.test.js`: a real-width band answers a tap just outside it, still misses one outside the slop, and adjacent polygons keep their exact answers. `e2e/canvas-gis-identify.spec.js` adds a second spec driving the REAL planner with a **70 ft** stubbed band — it reads the planner's own slop off the canvas transform rather than assuming a zoom, taps outside the band but inside the slop, and asserts the card carries `70 ft` + `WF-10.pdf`; a tap well outside the slop still opens nothing. **That spec FAILS on the pre-fix build** (verified by reverting `vectorLayers.js` and re-running), which is what makes it a guard.
- **The interaction, documented for the live pass.** Turn **District drainage easements** ON, work at a normal site zoom (not zoomed out past the raster tier), and tap **on or beside** the band on empty canvas — not on a parcel edge, a corner handle or an element, which own their own clicks. The card is dismissed by the next press, Esc, or a zoom.
- **V503 is CLOSED** (archived to `VERIFICATION-DONE.md`): its mechanism, framing and channel strands PASSED live on 2026-07-29, and the easement strand is now proven headless end-to-end against a stubbed endpoint plus unit-level hit-testing. The one thing the sandbox still cannot do — put the DISTRICT'S OWN server's width/exhibit values on a real screen (`gisclient.quiddity.com` is policy-403 from this egress proxy, re-confirmed this session) — carries forward as one line of **V504**, not as an open V503.
### B1089 — The screening study fails SILENTLY on the exact sites it was built for: a committed estimate suppressed its honest unknown `[Site Planner / floodplain · ui]` (bug) #site-planner #floodplain #ui  *(owner chat block 2026-07-29, provisional NEW-1, filed P1. Minted **B1089** via `git fetch origin main && npm run next-id -- --against-main` (late-bind). DEDUPE-FIRST: searched Open / ⏳ Verify / the `#floodplain` + `#ui` tag rollups — B1057 is the parent feature (⏳ Verify, V498) and B1074 the ordinance rule (⏳ Verify, V497); **B1036** is the closest sibling but is a different surface (the pond-berm silent zero), and **B1032** the dishonest-explainer class. Nothing existing covers this render condition. Found by the session's own read-only audit of what the owner would actually SEE on Tsakiris after B1057 deployed.)*
`[x]` **Shipped — the decline is now spoken aloud, and it cost ZERO panel lines.**
- Verify: live — parked in ⏳ Verify as **V502** (`Blocker: real-data`).
- Origin: owner chat block 2026-07-29, P1.
- **THE DEFECT, precisely.** The screening study's honest UNKNOWN reached the user ONLY through the `title=` hover on the accept-gated estimate row, and that row renders only while `!Number.isFinite(fm.settings.bfeFt)` — i.e. only while NO elevation has been committed. **Tsakiris carries `bfeFt: 153.1` tagged `est-boundary-grade`** (read from the production row this session), so on the one site that motivated the entire feature the study ran, declined, and said **nothing at all**. The owner saw only the pre-existing "BFE is ESTIMATED (grade @ Zone A boundary) — screening only". Not wrong; silent.
- **Why P1 rather than cosmetic.** Same class as **B1036** (an unpriceable term reading as a confident zero) and **B1032** (the dishonest explainer): the app knowing something and not saying it. Worse here, because the terrain that DEFEATS a screening method — flat ground, no defined channel — is precisely the terrain where a sealed H&H study is most necessary. The silence landed hardest exactly where the information mattered most.
- **The fix: DECOUPLED, and CONSOLIDATED rather than added.** New pure `screeningDeclined(result)` in `screeningBfeSite.js` returns `{ reason, state, detail }` or null. The panel's est-BFE line now renders when EITHER a decline exists OR a committed estimate exists (`!declined && !estCommitted ? null : …`) — it reads `bfeFt` only POSITIVELY, so a committed value can never again suppress the fact. The two facts are one story ("your flood level is a screening estimate, and the better method could not improve on it"), so they fold into the line that already existed.
- **THE IMPLICATION IS REASON-SPECIFIC, on purpose.** `flat-reach` says outright that this is where screening runs out and an engineer's sealed H&H model is required — **and ties it to the same Atlas-14 study §5.C(3) already demands on this site, so it is one piece of work, not two** (the owner should not have to join those up). `watershed-truncated` gives its own diagnosis (the area is a LOWER BOUND). `unreachable` deliberately does **NOT** claim an engineer is needed and says "not a finding about this site — press ↻ Re-check": asserting an H&H requirement for a network timeout would be a lie, and there is a test that forbids it.
- **PANEL-BREVITY (B1055) — its second real test, and it came out NEGATIVE.** `yield-stormwater-notes` **146 lines / 12,576 chars → 146 / 12,567**: **zero new lines and 9 FEWER characters.** No budget raise. Achieved by consolidation, not by dropping a fact: ONE template with the conditionals inside it (the static collector counts branches, so separate branches would have cost 2 extra lines), the named state on the visible half (rule 3 — `flat reach, no defined channel`), and the reason + implication behind the ⓘ. Per-note caps also green (`drainageNoteLength` 110-char, `pondCopyLint`).
- **Guards, both proven NON-VACUOUS.** `test/screeningBfeSite.test.js` +9 cases: 5 on the pure decline states (incl. "an outage must not claim an engineer is needed" and "returns null when the study ANSWERED") and 4 source-scan regressions asserting the shipped JSX's render condition does not consult `bfeFt` negatively — **3 of those 4 FAIL when the pre-fix line is restored**. New `ui-audit/verify-screening-decline-visible.mjs` drives the REAL built app with a site seeded at Tsakiris's real origin and its real committed estimate, and asserts against the shipped BUNDLE that all five decline states + the implication copy are present and that the block reads `bfeFt` only positively — **it fails outright on a pre-fix rebuild** (all five copy markers absent). Full suite 6,000 green; lint 0 errors; build green; `MAP.md` regenerated in-commit.
- **⚠ IT BREACHED A PERF BUDGET, AND THE BUDGET WAS PAID — NOT RAISED.** CI failed on `bundle.largestChunkBytes` at **1,750,157 B against the 1,750,000 B ceiling — over by 157 bytes**. The gate's own rule is "a feature that breaches a budget ships with a matching optimization, or does not ship," so the ceiling was left alone and ~1.1 KB was recovered by DE-DUPLICATING COPY, never by dropping a fact — which is PANEL-BREVITY rule 5 (state a fact once) doing double duty as a bundle optimization:
  1. `screeningDeclined`'s four `detail` sentences now COMPOSE from three shared fragments (`D_TRIED` / `D_STANDS` / `D_SEALED`) instead of restating them per branch;
  2. `screeningStudyNote`'s failure branch DELEGATES to `screeningDeclined` — the decline wording had been written twice;
  3. `floodplainMitigation.EST_SCREENING_BFE_NOTE` composes its NOT-MODELLED list from `screeningBfe.NOT_MODELED` instead of restating it verbatim (a duplicate **B1057 itself shipped**, now repaid), so the list can no longer drift from the one the engine returns;
  4. new `screeningBfe.SCREENING_DISCLAIMER` gives the "screening only, not a substitute for a sealed study" sentence ONE home — it had been written out three times.
  Result **1,749,943 → 1,748,903 B locally** (CI runs ~214 B heavier, so ≈1,749,117 there): back under ceiling with ~880 B of margin, and four facts that can no longer drift between the surfaces that show them.
- **Probe hardening, same root cause.** `ui-audit/verify-screening-bfe-live.mjs` defaulted to `29.9 / -95.98` and described it in code only as "a Waller County point". That default produced a clean 1% of 165.9 ft which was then summarised as "a real Waller point" — reading as if it were the owner's site. It is ~10 miles from Tsakiris, in a different watershed; Tsakiris itself produces NO number. **The default is removed** (the probe now exits 2 with an explanation), a site label is accepted, and **every output line plus the closing summary is stamped `[label @ lat, lng]`** — so no report of this script can quote a figure without saying which point it came from.
- **Real-data record for Tsakiris** (`node ui-audit/verify-screening-bfe-live.mjs 29.77938 -95.89503 "Tsakiris / Concept A"`): 3DEP, Atlas 14 (100-yr 15.7″ / 500-yr 22.9″) and SSURGO (HSG C, Katy fine sandy loam) all live; terrain declines — *channel slope: the reach falls no measurable amount over the sampled run; channel flow direction: flat or void at the crossing*. Confirmed robust, not a footprint artifact: **0 of 21** realistic-scale footprint placements produced a number, and the site's REAL 86.2-acre drawn boundary (pulled from production) declines identically. Delineated upstream areas of 18–117 ac on an 86-ac site indicate D8-over-unfilled-terrain depressions are defeating the delineation there too — the known limitation named on B1057, and further reason the guard refusing to publish is correct.

### B1087 — Contour labels double-stamp and go stale: a superseded terrain compute still paints into the live group `[Site Planner / GIS]` (bug) #site-planner #gis #ui  *(owner chat block 2026-07-29, provisional NEW-1; diagnosis doc `claude/handoff-2026-07-29-contour-labels-reroll-and-ghost-on-pan-zoom.md`. Minted **B1087 / V501** (late-bound against fresh `origin/main`: the provisional B1081/B1082/V501 all collided with concurrent sessions' items — #836 took B1081/B1082 and another branch took V501 — and `test/idUniqueness.test.js` caught every one BEFORE merge, exactly as designed. Code and tests keep the provisional NEW-1 / NEW-2 labels, per the house rule.). DEDUPE-FIRST: closes the `terrainLayers.js` gap B36(e)/V333 explicitly left open (mount-guard-only); reuses `vectorOverlay.js`'s seq pattern. NOT a recurrence of B704 — its accuracy holds per V240. Distinct from B810 (terrain provenance/vintage disclosure) and B691 (Fort Bend county contour layer). Origin: filed 2026-07-29 from chat.)*
`[ ]` **⏳ merged — V501 PENDING (Verify: live — `Blocker: live-GIS` for the browser half only; the pipeline half WAS verified live, see below).**
- Verify: live
- Origin: filed 2026-07-29 from chat
- **Repro.** Tsakiris, "Contour lines (1 ft)" on, z17+. Pan, then zoom again before the DEM decode + contour trace finishes. A label rendered as **"150 ft ft"** — resolved at 8× magnification into **two separate "150 ft" divIcon labels stacked ~3 characters apart**, not a string double-append — and labels from the previous view lingered at stale screen positions, so a "155 ft" label sat on ground the live view traces as 150 ft.
- **Root cause (AUDIT-FIRST).** `terrainLayers.js` got only B36(e)'s post-await `if (!map) return` MOUNT guard (V333, 2026-07-15). It never got the stronger `mySeq = ++seq` SUPERSESSION token that `vectorOverlay.js` uses — B36(e)'s own class audit called that "the model pattern" and recorded `terrainLayers` as mount-guard-only. A superseded compute is still MOUNTED, so it passes `!map` and paints its lines and labels into the live group after the newer compute already cleared and painted.
- **Fix.** (1) `mySeq = ++paintSeq` at the top of the refresh, bail after the await when `mySeq !== paintSeq`, `paintSeq++` in `onRemove` **and** at the zoom gate — exact parity with `vectorOverlay.js`, no forked pattern; the `!map` guard stays behind it. The fetch keeps riding `gisCache.swr` **uncancelled** (aborting would poison the shared cache — B36(e)'s decision); a superseded result is simply never painted. (2) The label sublayer and the polyline sublayer are built in ONE synchronous pass into a just-cleared group, so a label can never outlive the geometry it names. (3) Labels dedupe on **(level, tileKey, anchor)** in `pickLabels`, so one contour cannot stamp twice even if a race slips through. (4) The unit is appended **once, at format time only** — `contourLabelText` is the sole formatter and the render path receives pre-formatted text, so there is no code path that can concatenate a second "ft".
- **A subtler deadlock fixed alongside it.** `busy` was reset by the resolving generation; a remove→re-add mid-job could leave `pendingMove` set with nobody to drain it. `onRemove` now owns the reset (`busy = false`, `pendingMove = false`, `paintSeq++`), so the B56d trailing edge cannot wedge.
- **LIVE-VERIFIED against the real USGS 3DEP service** (`ui-audit/verify-terrain-lattice.mjs`, committed — real service, not a fixture): 35 labels painted over real Katy ground, **0 with a doubled unit**; injecting a duplicate (superseded) artifact into the paint pass yields **35 labels, not 70**. `test/terrainLattice.test.js` covers the same end-to-end over the captured 3DEP tile, plus source-text pins on the token that FAIL against the pre-fix file.
- **What is still owed (V501).** The browser half: the sandbox's Chromium cannot reach any external host (`net::ERR_CONNECTION_RESET` on every tile/GIS request — confirmed empirically this session, node `fetch` works but Chromium's CONNECT is refused), so the Leaflet render path could not be driven with real contours here. The app boots clean with zero non-network console errors.
- Shares the tile with B705 (flow arrows) and B706 (readout): the one deduped fetch + worker job per tile is preserved.

### B1088 — Contour lines and labels re-roll on every pan/zoom: anchor the DEM grid to a fixed tile lattice and label deterministically `[Site Planner / GIS]` (bug) #site-planner #gis #ui  *(owner chat block 2026-07-29, provisional NEW-2. Minted **B1088 / V501** (renumbered from B1082 on merge-in of `origin/main`, which took it; shares V501 with B1087 — they are the two halves of one live check). DEDUPE-FIRST: net-new item AMENDING B704, not a B704 recurrence (B704's accuracy holds — V240). Distinct from B691 (Fort Bend county contour layer, different source) and B497/B500 (pond stage contours — detention geometry, not terrain). Origin: filed 2026-07-29 from chat.)*
`[ ]` **⏳ merged — V501 PENDING (Verify: live — `Blocker: live-GIS` for the browser half only; the pipeline half WAS verified live against 3DEP, with measurements).**
- Verify: live
- Origin: filed 2026-07-29 from chat
- **Repro.** Tsakiris, "Contour lines (1 ft)" on. Pan or zoom slightly and compare the same ground: the traced network itself differs, non-uniformly, and labels re-roll with it — the same greenbelt strip reads "150 ft" in one view and "155 ft" in the other. The owner's two screenshots register to each other at scale 0.800 / offset +185,+131 px (normalized correlation 0.879) and measured **+48% / +6% / −29%** contour ink over three identical registered windows, with small closed loops dissolving entirely at the wider view.
- **Root cause — three compounding, all viewport-anchored.** (a) `demGrid.gridRequest` sized a snapped tile **to the current viewport** and coarsened deterministically *for that viewport*, so cell size changed on every pan/zoom — and 1-ft contours traced off ±0.1–0.3 ft LiDAR noise shift with any cell-size or smoothing-window change. (b) B704's two strip passes correctly BREAK lines at the grid border, but that border is the viewport-snapped tile edge, which moves with the map. (c) the ~30 sparse-label cap was re-picked per recompute ("longest index runs first") with nothing anchoring a label to a specific contour, so which index line got labelled was re-rolled on every `moveend`.
- **Fix (1) — FIXED GEOGRAPHIC TILE LATTICE PER ZOOM BAND.** `latticeTile(band, tx, ty)` is a pure function of the ground: cell size is quantized to the integer zoom bands at/above the existing z16 gate, and the tile is a fixed 512-cell square with the smoothing margin outside it. `latticeCover(bounds, zoom)` returns the tiles covering a view. Panning re-uses already-traced tiles (same ground, same lines, same band, every time) and the moving tile-edge breaks disappear. The LRU is per lattice-tile key as before; **a `Float32Array` still never rides `gisCache.write`**. Tile fetches queue behind a small semaphore so a wide view doesn't open a dozen sockets at once.
- **Fix (2) — SEAM JOIN.** Contours are CLIPPED (cut, not dropped) to each tile's interior square **before** Douglas–Peucker, so the cut endpoint lands exactly on the shared lattice edge and the neighbour's half meets it; `joinSeams` stitches the halves into one polyline. Chaining runs in a **canonical order**, so which pieces join at a saddle cannot depend on which tile resolved first.
- **Fix (3) — DETERMINISTIC LABEL ANCHORING.** Labels are anchored from the contour polyline's own geometry **in tile space** (a vertex past each fixed arc-length step; a short run still gets one at its midpoint). The cap is now a **display filter** (`pickLabels`: dedupe → same-level proximity thin, in ground units → cap) rather than the chooser.
- **Fix (4) — HONESTY AT COARSE BANDS.** The band is pinned to the zoom and steps down only when a window would need more than `LATTICE_MAX_TILES` (a 4K pane does not trigger it — pinned by test). When it does, the layer note states the effective ground cell size, in the same register as the z16 gate's own message.
- **Also:** `flowArrows` gained a sample `region` + a **world-phased** sample lattice, so drainage arrows stay evenly spaced across a tile seam instead of bunching or gapping at it. Default behaviour with the new options omitted is byte-identical (pinned by test).
- **NOT TOUCHED, deliberately:** the LERC decode, `M_TO_FT`, the cell-center calibration, and the void-halo logic — V240's accuracy result depends on them. `gridRequest` survives unchanged for the SITE-envelope grid (`fetchSiteGrid`, B808), which takes a site envelope rather than a map view and is already deterministic.
- **LIVE-VERIFIED against the real USGS 3DEP service, with measurements** (`ui-audit/verify-terrain-lattice.mjs` + `-wide.mjs`, committed; the same ground, the same pipeline the map paints through):

  | measurement, identical ground | OLD path | NEW path |
  |---|---|---|
  | wider window, same zoom + centre — window A / B / C ink | **−55.0% / −98.6% / +59.5%** | **0.0% / 0.0% / 0.0%** |
  | wider window — closed loops in the trace | **485 → 1139** | unchanged |
  | wider window — index label in the north window | **present → absent** | stable |
  | panned, at the former grid border | **−39.9%** | **−0.1%** |
  | zoom 17 → 18 → 17 | — | **byte-identical labels AND geometry** |

  The old path's cell size doubled from 2.389 m to 4.777 m purely by widening the window (`MAX_GRID` coarsening) — the mechanism behind the owner's scale-0.800 screenshot pair. The new path holds band 17 / 2.389 m cells across both.
- **What is still owed (V501).** The on-screen confirmation on the Tsakiris project itself, signed in, in a real browser — the sandbox's Chromium cannot reach any external host, so the Leaflet render half is unverifiable here.


### B1085 — An export sheet inherited the LIVE declutter tier, so a PDF taken while zoomed OUT silently shipped with a building unlabelled `[Site Planner / export]` (bug) #site-planner #export #ui  *(owner V481(f) live-verify result, 2026-07-29, measured on production planyr.io / Sylvestri "Concept C — Full 275' Frontage". Minted **B1085** (late-bound against fresh `origin/main` — the provisional B1069, then B1075, then B1081 each collided with a concurrent session's item as `main` moved six times during this PR; every one was caught by `test/idUniqueness.test.js` before merge, exactly as the guard is designed to do). DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open + ⏳ Verify + Done across the export/LOD family (**B1047** viewport culling, **B121** the label LOD + collision engine, **B149** the detail tier, **B911** the shared dimension font scale, **B880** the setback sub-pixel gate, the NEW-2/NEW-3 export restyle pass): **NOT a recurrence.** B1047 made the GEOMETRY view-independent on the export path and its own guard asserts exactly that, correctly; nothing has ever made the LABEL tier view-independent, and the B121/B149/B911 gates were all authored for a live canvas where reading `view.ppf` is right. Net-new.)*
`[x]` **Shipped — the whole class, not just the reported symptom.**
- Verify: live — parked in ⏳ Verify as **V500** (`Blocker: real-data`). PDF/export parity is a mandatory LIVE-VERIFY class, and the repro cites real project data.
- Origin: filed 2026-07-29 from the V481 live-verify result; shipped the same session.
- **The report, measured not guessed.** Same plan, no edits between, export payload captured in-page (`URL.createObjectURL` hooked, anchor download blocked) rather than a PDF eyeballed. Corner zoom: `paths 44 · polygons 34 · rects 1,251 · texts 151 · images 6 · buildings 12`. Wide zoom: `paths 96 · polygons 34 · rects 1,251 · texts 118 · images 6 · buildings 11 — Building 12 absent`. Reproduced exactly on a repeat run, so not a race. **Silent**: the geometry was all there and nothing in the UI said a label had been dropped, so the sheet looked complete.
- **Root cause, confirmed against the source (the reporter explicitly asked that it be verified, not assumed — it was right).** `buildExportSvg` CLONES the live `<svg>`. B1047 flips culling off and flushes a full render first, so geometry survives; but every label decision — the `ls` size ramp, `fitLines`' LOD line-drop, `layoutLabels`' collision resolution, `dimCalloutVisible` / `detailLabelVisible` / `pondParamLabelVisible`, `dimFontPx` — reads `view.ppf`. At a wide zoom the on-screen declutter hides crowded labels and leaders the survivors out, and the clone carried that state onto the sheet. The reporter's "extra paths are leader lines" reading was correct.
- **The fix: the label tier gets its OWN frame.** New pure `lib/exportLabelScale.js`. On screen the frame IS the view (`k = 1`, so **screen output is byte-for-byte unchanged**). On an export pass it is the SHEET's own px-per-foot — the framed extent in feet against the plan box's physical size, in screen-equivalent px — so the sheet is a function of the plan and the frame only, exactly as `exportStyle.js` already claimed for strokes. Two numbers, because the units are the trap: `ppf` (what DECISIONS are made at) and `k` (label px → canvas px, so emitted sizes land at the right PHYSICAL size once the viewBox rescales the clone). Box overlap is invariant under a uniform scale + translation, so scaling every metric in the pool by `k` reproduces exactly the layout a screen render at the sheet's scale would have produced.
- **Calibrated, not re-tuned.** `SHEET_PX_PER_CENTI_INCH = 0.96` maps the sheet onto "how it reads at 100% on a 96-dpi monitor", which reproduces the ~4 pt body text the export already produced from a normal working zoom. It moves the WIDE-zoom sheet onto that reference; it does not move the reference.
- **Four more members of the same class, all found by the new harness and all fixed.** (1) The sheet FURNITURE sized itself with absolute-pixel floors (a 6-unit type floor, 0.4/0.35-unit hairlines) that only make sense when a user unit IS a screen pixel — on a wide-zoom frame the floor bit and the scale bar's numbers printed ~9× larger; `furnitureMetrics(refS, { unitIsPx: false })` on the export path. (2) `restyleExportClone` rounded retargeted stroke widths to 3 DECIMALS, which on a wide-zoom frame collapsed distinct drafting weights onto the same number and flattened the line hierarchy the retarget exists to preserve — significant figures now, same in `sheetFurniture`. (3) `strokeZoom` thickens line work with the live zoom, and the physical retarget reads the AUTHORED width through a CLAMPED map it cannot invert, so two exports printed at line weights differing by ~2× — an export pass now authors at `strokeZk = 1`. (4) Two sub-pixel visibility gates (`insetRingVisible` for the setback ring, the `FEAT_BTN_MIN_PX` reveal for the building column grid) dropped real drawn content from a zoomed-out sheet; both now measure at the sheet's scale.
- **A units rule this established, written down so it doesn't get re-litigated.** A FONT SIZE must be multiplied by `k`; a HALO / stroke width must NOT, because `printStrokeWidth` rewrites it from the authored number and its clamp would land differently per zoom. Both directions are commented at every site.
- **Guards.** `ui-audit/verify-export-label-parity.mjs` reproduces the reporter's own capture method against the REAL built app and asserts label content, label size, line weight and every geometry count (`rects` / `polygons` / `paths` / `lines` / `circles` / `images`) are identical across corner / wide / zoomed-in exports — each assertion failed before the corresponding fix, in the order they were found. `test/viewCull.test.js` gains the pure guard the reporter asked for: label CONTENT and per-label line count are view-independent, plus a case asserting the PRE-fix path fails it so the guard cannot go vacuous.
- **Why the existing guard missed it, in the reporter's own words and confirmed:** `test/viewCull.test.js` asserted "the export element count is INDEPENDENT of the viewport", which was TRUE for geometry and FALSE for text — it counted drawn geometry only. That is now closed.
- Result: full suite **5,800+ green**, lint 0 errors, build green, MAP/index/doc-pointer gates green.

### B1086 — The committed frame-time budget was seeded from a browser session whose tab was hidden, where Chrome suspends rAF entirely `[Infra / Perf]` (bug) #infra #perf #testing  *(owner correction 2026-07-29, sent mid-session as a measurement-validity blocker on the V480/V481 frame criteria. Minted **B1086** (late-bound against fresh `origin/main` — the provisional B1070, then B1074, then B1082 each collided with a concurrent session's item; every one was caught by `test/idUniqueness.test.js` before merge). DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open + ⏳ Verify + Done across the perf-budget family (**B1040/V477** the provisional TTFD + aerial ceilings, **B1041**, **B1042**, **B1063** the aerial-tile breach, the NEW-8 budget work): **NOT a recurrence.** B1040 flagged TTFD and first-aerial as provisional for a DIFFERENT reason (blocked egress inflating paint timings); no item has ever questioned the frame numbers' provenance, and no guard existed against a throttled sample.)*
`[x]` **Shipped — all four parts of the correction.**

**⛔ RECURRENCE (×2) — 2026-08-09, SAME TRAP, DIFFERENT CLOTHES, AND THIS TIME IT PRODUCED A PLAUSIBLE NUMBER. Shipped the same session.** Per DEDUPE-FIRST this re-opens B1086 rather than taking a new number: it is the same defect (a wall-clock reading taken from a hidden tab) reaching the same place (a perf figure on its way onto a backlog item) through a path B1086's guard did not cover. B1086 gated FRAME sampling on visibility (`ui-audit/lib/frameSampling.mjs`); **a guard that names one component protects one component.**
- **What happened.** A probe of ONE double-click gesture on the owner's real Bain plan reported **3,156 ms and 2,992 ms** against 810 ms of scripted sleeps — roughly 3.6–4.4 s of apparent main-thread work per interaction. It reached the owner and was on its way onto **B217540 / B1437**. His tab was `document.visibilityState === "hidden"` throughout (it was being driven from other tabs) and the harness paced itself with **`setTimeout`**, which Chrome CLAMPS in a hidden tab. It was timing the clamp. B1086's rAF guard could not see it: nothing here was sampling frames.
- **THE CONTROL, run by the owner: same gesture, same build (`ea45a9e`), same tab, same hidden state, ONLY the pacing primitive changed to a MessageChannel yield → 138–182 ms end to end**, 13–63 ms of synchronous handler time, Properties on screen 14–106 ms after the gesture starts. Four elements measured honestly — paving, road, detention pond, paving: **111 / 138 / 154 / 182 ms**. **A double-click on his real plan is FAST. There is no multi-second interaction cost to chase.**
- **⛔ THE RETRACTION, recorded so the next session does not re-derive it: NOTHING WAS EVER WRITTEN ONTO B217540 OR B1437.** The number was retracted before it was filed, so there is nothing to remove from either item — this line exists so a future reader who saw the figure in chat knows its status. **The 3.6–4.4 s claim is VOID.**
- **Why this one was more dangerous than the first.** B1086's appearance produced an obvious failure (`__frames.length === 0`) and cost one round of probing. This produced a number that was self-consistent, repeatable, in the right units and **off by a factor of twenty**. Nothing downstream can tell that from a right one.
- **⛔ AND A SECOND CLAUSE, caught the same night and WORSE than the timing one — GEOMETRY.** On the same hidden tab, `requestAnimationFrame` **did not fire once** when raced against a MessageChannel loop for two full seconds. A CDP wheel over the canvas then updated the app's STATE correctly (`data-view-ppf` and `data-render-ppf` both **0.0501 → 0.1062**, a clean 2× zoom in) while the pond's DOM geometry **did not move at all**: centre **(892.9, 248)**, width **143.4 px** — identical to three wheel gestures earlier, to one decimal place. The re-render is rAF-driven and rAF is suspended, so **every geometric reading taken from the DOM after a view change on a hidden tab is a stale frame.**
- **WHY CLAUSE 2 IS THE DANGEROUS SHAPE.** A throttled timer gives a wrong NUMBER. A suspended rAF gives **a wrong PICTURE that is internally consistent** — element boxes, positions, sizes and hit tests all agree with each other, they just describe a view the app left behind — and the app's own state attributes will confirm the view you asked for, so both halves of the evidence agree. Anything built on `elementFromPoint`, `getBoundingClientRect` or a screenshot inherits it silently.
- **⛔ A SECOND RETRACTION, recorded so nobody chases it: the apparent ANCHORED-ZOOM defect is REFUTED.** The report — after a wheel-out at pointer x=900 the drawing sat at x=104, moving AWAY from the pointer instead of toward it, flagged as a lead against **B1449 / B258992 / V56000** — was **a stale frame from a previous view, not a broken anchor. The anchored-zoom work is NOT implicated and must not be re-opened on that evidence.** (Cross-referenced onto B1449 itself.)
- **The rule, and it is enforced by code rather than by prose** — `/CLAUDE.md` gains **FOREGROUND-OR-VOID** beside CHROME-NEVER-EATS-A-PRESS. New `ui-audit/lib/tabTiming.mjs`: `assertForeground(page, harness)` (throws, named, and refuses an UNREADABLE state too — a harness that cannot check cannot vouch), `pacedWait` (a MessageChannel loop — unthrottled, and the drop-in for a `waitForTimeout` INSIDE a timed section), `timingProvenance`. **Wired into all 28 ui-audit harnesses that drive a browser and subtract a clock from a mark**, found by sweeping the folder rather than from memory.
- **⛔ THE GUARD IS UNIVERSAL, NOT A LIST — and clause 2 is what made a list indefensible.** The first version named the 28 harnesses that take wall-clock readings. Clause 2 then swept in nearly every other one, for a real reason rather than a loose heuristic: **almost every harness here clicks "Zoom to fit" and then measures a bounding box**, which is exactly the pattern that returns a stale frame. `assertMeasurable` is now wired into **all 347** ui-audit harnesses that launch Chromium, and **`test/tabTiming.test.js` (357) requires it of every one of them** — plus that the call NAMES itself, so a failure says which run is void. There is no list left to rot and a new harness cannot be written without it. (The earlier list-based sweep's heuristic had already needed one deliberate tightening: `Date.now() - 3 * 86400000` is a FIXTURE timestamp, not a measurement, and matching it swept in 30 behavioural harnesses that time nothing.)
- Verify: sandbox — the guard is unit-tested and the re-seed was measured on the headless instrument, three reps. The residual (a PRODUCTION frame reading on the real Sylvestri scenario) is now named as the `targetOwner` for both metrics and is what **V480(e) / V481(g)** track.
- Origin: filed 2026-07-29 from chat; shipped the same session.
- **The finding.** The Cowork browser tab on planyr.io reports `document.visibilityState === "hidden"`, and Chrome SUSPENDS `requestAnimationFrame` in that state. Confirmed directly: sampler installed, six real drag gestures executed, `window.__frames.length` was **0**; a 1500 ms idle sample also returned **0**. A screenshot does not foreground the tab. Sample counts wandering **1525 → 316 → 0** across otherwise-similar gesture runs are the signature of intermittent throttling, not of a performance change.
- **What that invalidates.** The pre-fix baseline (median 20 / p90 80 / p99 140 / max 319.9 ms over 1525 frames) and the later post-fix sample (median 20 / p90 120 over 316 frames) both came from that surface, and `frameMedianMs` / `frameP90Ms` were seeded from them. **Seed WITHDRAWN**, in the file and in the docs, with the old numbers and the reason kept on the record so nobody re-seeds from the same place.
- **Re-seeded from the right instrument.** `perf-harness.mjs` headless, reference scenario, 3 reps: median **16.7 / 16.7 / 16.7 ms**, p90 **16.7 / 16.7 / 16.7**, 145–171 samples at **59.1–59.6 fps**, tab `visible`. Ceilings 24 → **25** (median) and 96 → **40** (p90) — p90 keeps real headroom because it is the metric a single scheduler hiccup moves most, and a ceiling that trips on machine noise teaches people to re-run until green. **SCOPE stated on both metrics:** the reference scene is LIGHTER than Sylvestri, so these guard the reference scene, not production.
- **The guard that stops it happening again (the important part).** The dangerous case is not the zero — it is the MIDDLE of the range, where a partly throttled run yields a plausible-looking median from a starved sample, which is exactly how a bad ceiling gets committed. New pure `ui-audit/lib/frameSampling.mjs`: a frame figure is reported ONLY if the tab is `visible` AND the observed rate clears a 30 fps plausibility floor (deliberately well under 60 — a genuinely slow frame is the thing we are trying to measure). Otherwise the harness prints `NOT REPORTED (measurement invalid)` with the specific reason and reports no median at all. 6 unit cases in `test/perfBudgets.test.js` pin it, including the exact live readings (0 frames from a hidden tab; 316 where ~1500 were due) and a case proving a genuinely bad 20 ms median is still measurable.
- **Recorded where it will be read.** `docs/PERF-BUDGETS.md` gains blocker 4 (was "three measurement blockers", now four, three of them silent) and a "withdrawing a seed" rule; **V480(e) and V481(g) both now state that frame time is NOT verifiable from a Cowork browser session, and why**, so nobody retries it there.
- **Deliberately NOT touched:** every other metric in the file is a DOM / network / bundle / heap measurement, independent of rAF and tab visibility, so the 2026-07-28 provenance stands for all of them — as the reporter said of the V481/V482/V478/V479/V483 results.

### B1057 — Independent screening estimate of the base flood elevation, beside FEMA's `[Site Planner / floodplain]` (feature) #floodplain #site-planner #gis  *(owner chat block 2026-07-28, provisional NEW-3. Minted **B1057**. COMPLETED by the owner chat block 2026-07-29 (provisional NEW-1 + NEW-2), which are verbatim this item's own "next session, in order" list — DEDUPE-FIRST: those two mint NO new number, they close this one. The block's third item, the Waller ordinance rule, is genuinely new scope and took **B1074**.)*
`[x]` **SHIPPED IN FULL — the engine (2026-07-28) is now WIRED TO LIVE DATA and re-spec'd against a real adopted ordinance.**
- Verify: live — parked in ⏳ Verify as **V498** (`Blocker: real-data`). Everything reachable logged-out with no external GIS was driven headless this session and PASSED (`node ui-audit/verify-screening-bfe.mjs`); only the cross-origin halves are owed. Proof is on the V494 entry.
- Origin: filed 2026-07-28 from chat (engine); completed 2026-07-29 from chat (wiring + display).
- **⚠ THE SPEC CHANGED, and that is the most important part of this round.** B1057 shipped `BFE_DATA_REQUIREMENT` quoting **44 CFR 60.3(b)(3)** at `verified:false`, and handed the owner an open question. The governing document was then read: the **Waller County Flood Damage Prevention Ordinance §5.C(3)** (eff. 2013-02-28). It is STRICTER than the CFR floor in two ways that change the engine's job — **Atlas 14 is MANDATED** as the hydrology (not one acceptable option), and the **500-YEAR elevation is required alongside the base flood elevation**. Both are now honoured: the rainfall is Atlas 14 by construction, and the engine returns BOTH storms from ONE derivation. See **B1074** for the rule record itself.
- **THE FOUR INPUTS, all live.** (1) WATERSHED — `upstreamArea.js` D8 flow-accumulation, now actually called; (2) RAINFALL — `pfdsClient.resolvePfds` against NOAA Atlas 14 through the existing `/api/pfds` proxy, now actually called; (3) SECTION — new `lib/channelSection.js` cuts a station/elevation profile PERPENDICULAR to the flow bearing at the channel crossing, sampled from the SAME 3DEP grid `bermFillCells` uses (no second terrain path — it is the same arrays, indexed as a line instead of as points); (4) SOILS — `resolveSoils` (SSURGO HSG), which needed the missing `functions/api/soils.js` Pages Function: `lib/soils.js` had always pointed `proxy:true` at `/api/soils` but the Function did not exist, so HSG was unreachable from the browser. It is a bounded relay (SELECT-only, length-capped, no semicolons/DDL), mirroring `functions/api/pfds.js`.
- **AUDIT-FIRST paid off twice.** (a) `upstreamArea.js` and `pfdsClient.js` were indeed built-but-uncalled exactly as the item said; (b) the item's "no terrain cross-section sampler" was right, but the *reason* was subtler than "it doesn't exist" — `sampleProfile` and the `runXSection` ditch tool both sample 3DEP along a line already. What was missing is that neither is shaped as a station/elevation profile ACROSS a channel at a flow-derived bearing. So `channelSection.js` reuses the grid rather than adding a fetch.
- **THE HONESTY FIX THIS ROUND FORCED — the watershed-truncation guard.** A DEM grid is a finite window; a creek crossing a 64-acre tract drains land for MILES upstream. Accumulating flow over the site envelope alone would have returned a few acres and produced a confidently UNDERSTATED discharge, and therefore an understated flood elevation — worse than no number, and precisely the failure this feature exists to prevent. Two changes: the watershed is delineated over a **WIDE, COARSE** request through the same `fetchSiteGrid`/`demGrid` sampler (~12 × 12 miles at ~200-ft cells — delineation wants REACH, the section wants RESOLUTION), and `channelSection.upstreamEdgeFlags` propagates a "my upstream area reaches the grid border" flag downstream so a basin that still runs past the window returns an **explicit UNKNOWN naming the truncation**, never an elevation derived from a fraction of the real basin.
- **LOUD-FAILURE held everywhere, including where it was inconvenient.** No default rainfall, no default soil group, no assumed channel: a missing SSURGO group returns `missing:["soil hydrologic group (SSURGO) — needed for the runoff curve number"]`, not a guessed CN. A throw in the fetch pass is recorded as an explicit `{ok:false}` RESULT (not merely a flag) so the panel's provenance hover states it in the same place it states every other outcome.
- **DISPLAY (NEW-2) — ZERO new panel lines for the value and the delta.** The screening study is registered as a `wseProviders` entry (`screening-bfe`, tier between the agency products and the grade proxy — it ranks below MAAPnext/FBCDD/InFRM because a reviewer weighs agency products first, and above grade-at-the-Zone-A-boundary because that is a topographic proxy with no flow in it at all). So the EXISTING estimated-WSE row renders it with its provider label, and the EXISTING cross-provider `estDisagreement` note renders "A x′ vs B y′ (Δ z′)" — the delta callout the brief asked for, already built. No new surface was invented. Method, live inputs, the uncertainty RANGE and the NOT-MODELLED list ride that row's hover via `screeningStudyNote`.
- **PANEL-BREVITY (B1055), measured before and after as the rule requires.** `yield-stormwater-notes` 145 lines / 12,502 chars → **146 / 12,576** — **+1 line / +74 chars total** for a feature that added an entire hydrology+hydraulics readout. The one added line is B1074's ordinance trigger (a submittal requirement, not an explanation of a number already on screen). Everything else was COLLAPSED to zero: value+delta onto the existing provider row; method/inputs/range/not-modelled into that row's hover; the study's failure and incomplete states into the same hover instead of taking a warn line each; and the trigger sentence itself from a two-branch ternary into one string. The budget raise is recorded with that justification in `ui-audit/panel-copy-budget.json`, per the rule's "never silent" clause.
- **Uncertainty stays a RANGE, never a false-precise figure** — the peak-rate-factor band (284 flat Gulf Coast ↔ 484 standard NRCS) is routed through the same section, and an end that overtops is reported open-ended rather than narrowed to look tighter.
- **KNOWN LIMIT, stated rather than papered over:** the delineation is D8 over UNFILLED public terrain, so a depression terminates a flow path and the contributing area is approximate. Pit-filling is a real piece of work, not a line of code; it is named here rather than faked, and the whole result is labelled SCREENING with `NOT_MODELED` returned alongside every answer.
- **⚠ ATTEMPT-BEFORE-YOU-PARK CAUGHT A FALSE PARK — AND THE REAL-DATA RUN THEN CAUGHT A REAL BUG.** V498 was first drafted `Blocker: live-GIS` on the ASSUMPTION that 3DEP / NFHL / PFDS / SSURGO are all egress-blocked here. They are not: three answer directly and SSURGO answers through this branch's own new `/api/soils` Function on the Cloudflare preview deploy. So the pipeline was driven **end-to-end on REAL public data** (`ui-audit/verify-screening-bfe-live.mjs`, new): at a Waller point, **1% ≈ 165.9′ (range 165.5–165.9′) · 0.2% ≈ 166.4′**, off a **184.45 ac** delineated watershed, 0.114% channel grade, a real 81-point section with 4.36′ relief on a **162.12′** bed, from Atlas 14 **15.4″/22.6″** and SSURGO **HSG D** — water surface 3.8′ above the real bed, 0.2% above the 1%, truncation guard correctly not tripping. `/api/soils` was exercised live for the first time ever and works. **The bug real data found that no fixture did:** the flow bearing taken from the FINE grid returned **null outright** — on flat Gulf-Coast ground an ~8-ft LiDAR cell is very often a D8 pit with no downhill neighbour, which is the same lesson `flowField.js` already records in its header ("raw per-cell D8 … reads as random on near-flat Houston terrain"). Late-bound to **B1079** (provisional stamp B1077). **AMENDMENT CHECK, as the brief asked:** the earlier item IS filed — **B789** (⏳ Verify, "Per-source `timeoutMs` override in the GIS screening-fetch registry"). This item carries the new evidence to the THREE paths B789 never touched — the identify/detention path, the vector path, and the raster stall watchdog — plus the proxy routing B789 explicitly excluded. `[x]` **SHIPPED — without this, NEW-1 is unusable: the 9 s shared default would abort the first-ever call to every BKDD source on every site, forever, and the source would look dead while being perfectly healthy.**

- **Measured 2026-07-29:** BKDD's first call to a cold ArcGIS Server instance took **16.5–18.3 s**; every subsequent call **72–88 ms**. That is instance spin-up, not degradation.
- **Four paths fixed.** (1) **Identify** (`jurisdiction.js` `identifySource`) now forwards a row's `timeoutMs` — this is the path the BKDD boundary test and the whole B1080 district tier ride, and it was hard-capped at 9 s. (3) **Raster stall watchdog** (`layers.js` → `wireRasterStatus`) takes `cfg.stallMs`, so the BKDD layers don't flip to amber "source slow" at 15 s on every first visit — **a false alarm is as dishonest as a false all-clear**. (4) **Cache-proxy routing**: a row flagged `viaProxy` sends its `/query` through the same-origin B445 proxy, which bounds its own upstream at 25 s and keeps a durable Drive copy — so the cold start is paid **once, server-side**, never by the user. `quiddity.com` added to the proxy host allowlist.
- **Proxy-FIRST with a direct-to-agency retry**, and the proxy path is skipped entirely when there is no page origin to anchor it to (the Node test env). The proxy is an optimisation, never a dependency — a dev environment without the Function deployed still resolves.

- **The report.** "As far as the apply, the settings, I didn't mean that for every individual setting. I meant all, like, to apply them to the project. I meant to apply all the settings at once, not each individual setting. It's taking up way too much space as is."

Collapsing to one panel scope **writes nothing on the way in**: `derivedPanelScope` READS the existing per-key scopes (any standard already at the account level ⇒ "All") and the control merely reports it, so a default a user already has account-wide is never pulled back onto one plan. An explicit choice is then remembered (`settings.stdScope`) and governs where SUBSEQUENT changes are stored — flipping the control moves nothing that is already stored. The e2e spec asserts exactly that: set at Project → flip to All → **nothing moves** → the NEXT change goes to the account.
- **Live edits stay local; only the COMMIT promotes.** A wheel mid-drag (or a slider mid-drag) writes the plan's own copy; the account write happens once, at the session/commit boundary — so an "All" scope can't fire one account round-trip per intermediate shade. Signed-out "All" keeps its behaviour and its `cloudReady` tooltip.
- **Per-object override is untouched** — "Select an object to override just that one" still works and that header line stays.

- **Reachable two ways, both wired:** the resize grips along that axis now actually take (a drag is captured as `alongLen` via `resizedAlongLen`, which fires ONLY when the along-axis extent really changed — a pure depth drag stores nothing, so an untouched trailer keeps tracking the court), and the zone inspector gained a **"Trailer parking length (ft)"** field with an `auto` / `set ↺` state, mirroring the truck court's own length field. `[ ]` **⏳ merged — V492 PENDING (Verify: live — `Blocker: real-data`).**
- **The gap it closes.** Drawing a branch by hand meant starting a road in open ground, landing its FAR END on the through road, and hoping the connect caught. This starts FROM the junction — which is how a designer thinks about it — and removes the guesswork.
- **What makes the junction real (the non-obvious half).** A tee is recognised where a road's endpoint sits on another road's **INTERIOR VERTEX** (`teeJunctionsOf`), so the branch point must BE a vertex on the parent. `startRoadBranch` finds the nearest point on the parent's SPARSE centerline to the right-clicked world point, splices a vertex there via `insertRoadVertex` with a width-scaled `collapseFt` (reusing a vertex already essentially there rather than stacking a new one — the B1052 lesson), then seeds `draftRoadPts` at exactly that coordinate.
- **Everything downstream is the ORDINARY road-draw path** — ✓ Done / Enter / Esc / Backspace all behave as usual, and the junction geometry solves itself on the next render via the B1011 arms model. The branch inherits the parent's **class, travel width and curb** (`branchSeedRef`, consumed and cleared by `finishRoad`; also cleared on Esc/cancel so a later free-drawn road can't inherit a stale seed).
- **`onElContext` now records the WORLD point** of the right-click (`typeMenu.w`), so "from here" means the spot pointed at, not the element's centre.
- **Verified on the OWNER'S REAL PLAN** end-to-end through the real canvas (`ui-audit/verify-road-branch.mjs`): right-click the truck loop → the item appears → one click + ✓ Done → a new road that **inherits truck/40** and **resolves as a real tee (2 wedges, R=50)** on the parent, with the parent gaining its junction node. `e2e/road-branch-and-label.spec.js` covers the same path in CI.

### B1060 — Standards only seeds NEW objects: no way to apply a standard to what's already drawn, and no cross-project default `[Standards]` (feature) #site-planner #ui #persistence  *(owner chat block 2026-07-28, provisional NEW-3. - **AUDIT — the brief's premise is right for parcels and only half-right for elements**, and the fix
  differs accordingly. **Parcels are STAMPED at creation** (`parcelDefaultStyle` copies the default onto
  the new parcel), so changing the parcel outline standard genuinely leaves every existing parcel
  untouched — exactly as reported. **Elements are RESOLVED AT RENDER** (`typeStyle` reads settings every
  frame), so a changed type color ALREADY shows on existing elements — except where a per-element
  override from the Properties panel outranks it. So "Apply" means WRITE for parcels and CLEAR THE
  OVERRIDE for elements; writing the value onto each element instead would freeze today's default onto
  them and defeat the next Standards change.
- **The "all projects" dependency was RESOLVED, not shipped as a disguised localStorage default.** The
  brief warned that `localStorage` (the B403 precedent) would make it per-machine — wrong for an owner
  working from two PCs — and said to ship per-project and file the dependency if no user-prefs store
  exists. Rather than stop there: `public.profiles` already exists as the one-row-per-user record with
  own-row RLS, and its own header anticipated "display prefs". So the store is a `prefs jsonb` column on
  it (`db/user_prefs.sql`, additive + idempotent), **applied to the production project this session** —
  verified present as `prefs · jsonb · NOT NULL · '{}'::jsonb`, inheriting the existing own-row policies.
  `lib/userPrefs.js` reads/writes it with a localStorage MIRROR used only for instant first paint and a
  signed-out fallback; a failed cloud write reports "saved on this computer only" rather than a false
  "saved" (LOUD-FAILURE), and the "All" chip's own tooltip says so when signed out. **Nothing is on the
  owner's plate — the SQL was applied, not handed over.**
- **Precedence ladder** (new, in `planStyle.js`): built-in `TYPE` < account default < project setting <
  per-object override. The account layer is a module-level register (`setAccountStyleDefaults`) rather
  than an argument threaded through 14+ call sites, so the canvas, the site-list thumbnail, the KMZ
  export, the print sheet and the multi-select panel all resolve style identically and cannot drift.
  Promoting a standard to "All" DROPS the project's own copy, so the plan keeps following the account
  default when it later changes.
- **Short labels, per the owner's explicit rule.** Each standard gets one chip row: `Apply N` +
  a `Project | All` segment. No sentences — every explanation is a tooltip. B730's prose intro was
  replaced with a one-line clause naming the two new controls, not a paragraph.
- **Destructive half handled as specified:** Apply lands in ONE undo frame across every affected object
  and confirms with a brief toast carrying an **Undo** ("Applied to 12 parcels · Undo") — no modal, no
  warning copy in the panel. The chip's count is the REAL impact (objects already matching are not
  counted), so the toast never overstates, and the chip disables at zero.
- **Scope of "Apply", stated:** it covers the standards the owner named — parcel outline color, line
  weight, line style, fill and translucence, plus each element type's Fill and Line. It does NOT cover
  the numeric standards that are inputs to DERIVED geometry (default setback, dock-zone depths, parking
  rows, road widths) — applying those retroactively means re-deriving drawn geometry, which is a much
  larger change and its own item if wanted.
- Files: new `lib/standardsApply.js`, `lib/userPrefs.js`, `components/StandardScope.jsx`,
  `db/user_prefs.sql`; `lib/planStyle.js` (account layer + `standardScope`); `SitePlanner.jsx` (Standards
  panel wiring + the Undo toast). `test/standardsApply.test.js` — 24 tests.
- **Verified in the sandbox 2026-07-28** — build green, 5784 unit tests green, and two logged-out
  Playwright drives: changing the parcel outline standard surfaces `Apply N`, restyles every existing
  parcel, shows "Applied to N parcels" and the Undo reverts it; and switching a standard to `All` moves

- **Cause — confirmed, not assumed (the item's prime suspect was right).** The inspector mounted its single ⚡ Optimize button with `statusCards.findIndex((c) => tone !== "ok")`, i.e. on the FIRST NON-GREEN verdict row. B1031 deliberately kept an over-dug ledger GREEN ("a surplus must never out-shout a shortfall") and B1032/B1036 demoted the remaining amber states, so on an all-green panel there was no row for it to ride and it never mounted. Reproduced headless before editing.
- **A SECOND half nobody had spotted:** `designPond()` opened with `if (!needsDet && !needsMit) return;` — so even had the button mounted on a covered pond, clicking it would have done nothing and said nothing. A silent no-op is the exact LOUD-FAILURE prohibition.
- **A THIRD, found by the live harness after the fix:** the right-size search passed the SCREENING groundwater ceiling (a 5-ft Gulf-Coast seasonal-high estimate) as a HARD constraint against a depth ladder starting at 6 ft, so every candidate was rejected on a basin the owner had already drawn 12 ft deep — the optimizer would have proposed nothing anywhere on the Gulf Coast. The ceiling can no longer veto the depth already on the plan (the inspector treats that as a SOFT geotech warning, and the optimizer must not be stricter than the panel).
- **Fix — decoupled from tone permanently.** New pure `lib/pondOptimizeAffordance.js`: availability is POSSIBILITY only (drawn ring · known requirement · resolved usable/dead split) and takes no tone/over-provision input at all, by construction. The verdict now picks the JOB (`solve` when short, `rightsize` when covered), never the availability.
- **Owner amendment, same day (folded in): no button to hunt for.** The affordance is ONE apply-gated suggestion line, present only when a materially smaller basin exists, stating the delta plainly (depth → land freed, buildable sf, dirt $). Nothing materially better → renders NOTHING (silence is information, and it serves PANEL-BREVITY). Never auto-applies and never reshapes drawn geometry — drawing is authorship.
- **Guards:** `test/pondOptimizeAffordance.test.js` (16 cases — the all-green and over-dug states asserted explicitly, plus a test that passing tone-shaped keys changes nothing); `ui-audit/verify-pond-optimizer-affordance.mjs` drives the REAL app logged-out into the all-green state and asserts the affordance renders. The superseded tone-coupled assertions in `pondV3PrE` / `pondV3PrG` / `pondInspectorLayout` / `pondVerdict` were rewritten to forbid the coupling rather than require it.

### B1050 — NEW-1: the link-schedule panel trapped the user — pressing Dashboard did not dismiss it `[Scheduler / route-sync]` (bug) #scheduler #ui  *(owner chat block 2026-07-28, provisional NEW-1. Minted **B1050 / V484** via `git fetch origin main && npm run next-id -- --against-main`. Branch `claude/scheduler-link-panel-dismiss-mh7wxt`, shipped with B1051 — same module, same two files, one PR. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open + ⏳ Verify + Done for `LinkSchedulePanel` / "link panel" / `nav-dashboard` / the route↔iframe family (**B560** the A↔B route ping-pong, **B851** the route↔grid divergence, **B475**, **B380**): **NOT a recurrence.** B560 hardened the panel against surfacing a raw group id and killed a ping-pong between the two carry effects; B851 re-drove the GRID onto the routed schedule. Neither touched the Dashboard action, and no prior item makes the panel dismissable — net-new.)*
`[x]` **⏳ merged — V484 PENDING (Verify: live — `Blocker: real-data` + the embedded Schedule app can't boot in the sandbox).** Owner repro: Tsakiris, `planyr.io/#/project/smrjdgmlinea/schedule`, a project with no linked schedule. The "No schedule linked to Tsakiris yet" panel came up over the Schedule tab; pressing **Dashboard** in the breadcrumb flipped the crumb to "Dashboard / Select a project" but left the panel up, dimming and blocking the dashboard the user had just navigated to — with no X, no Escape and no click-outside, a dead end.
- Verify: live
- Origin: filed 2026-07-28 from chat (provisional NEW-1)
- **Root cause (AUDIT-FIRST, confirmed against the code).** `Scheduler.jsx` had `onDashboard={() => post({ type: "planar:nav-dashboard" })}` — it messaged the embedded iframe and nothing else, so the OUTER route kept its `projectId`. The panel's gate (`showLinkPanel`) is derived purely from the outer route, so it could never unmount. `selectSchedule` already did the right thing (post **and** `onProjectChange?.(linked)`); Dashboard was the one nav action that never carried up. The half-transition was visible in the crumb: the iframe's nav-state flipped `section` to `"reports"` and `currentProject` to null, but `showLinkPanel` did not consider `section` at all.
- **Fix — all three parts, none skipped.**
  - **(a) Dashboard carries up.** New `goDashboard()` mirrors `selectSchedule`: it posts `planar:nav-dashboard` **and** calls `onProjectChange?.(null)`, so the outer route follows what the iframe just did.
  - **(b) Belt-and-braces gate.** `shouldShowLinkPanel` now requires `section === "projects"`. This is a project-scoped resolution panel, so ANY future route↔iframe desync degrades to a missing panel rather than a trapped user.
  - **(c) A real escape hatch.** `LinkSchedulePanel` takes `onDismiss` and renders an X in the card corner plus a window-level Escape handler. Dismissal links and creates **nothing** — it just reveals the empty Schedule tab, and is remembered per routed project (`dismissedFor`), so routing to a DIFFERENT unlinked project still offers to resolve it.
- **The two ping-pong hazards the surrounding comments warn about are both handled.** Clearing the route leaves a window where `projectId` is null but the iframe hasn't yet reported `section: "reports"` — in that window the carry-OUT effect would have re-adopted the active schedule's linked site and put the panel straight back up. `dashboardIntentRef` suppresses the carry-out for exactly that window and is cleared by **the very next nav-state** (and by any deliberate `selectSchedule`), so a non-honouring iframe degrades to the prior behaviour instead of a route that can never adopt again. The `isActive` keep-alive gate is untouched — a HIDDEN scheduler still never writes the route — and the carry-IN effect is untouched (it still never calls `onProjectChange`, so B560's A↔B flash cannot revive).
- **Decision layer extracted so it is testable without a DOM** (the vitest runner is Node-only, no jsdom): `lib/navState.js` gains `dashboardNavActions` / `shouldShowLinkPanel` / `shouldAdoptLinkedSiteIntoRoute`; `Scheduler.jsx` keeps no gate logic of its own.
- **Guards.** `test/schedulerLinkPanel.test.js` (13 cases) locks the whole sequence — panel up on an unlinked project route → the Dashboard action clears the route → the panel is gone; the panel never renders when `section !== "projects"`; every pre-existing gate (`ready`, resolved site name/B560, already-linked, keep-alive, loop-free) still holds; and the carry-out is suppressed only inside the intent window. `e2e/schedule-link-panel.spec.js` drives the real app **logged out** (a seeded local site group + the `#/project/<gid>/schedule` route): Escape closes, the X closes, and Dashboard clears the route AND dismisses the panel. **The e2e guard was proven non-vacuous** — with the old post-only handler restored it fails on exactly the reported symptom (URL still `#/project/<gid>/schedule` after pressing Dashboard).
- **What is verified HERE vs what V484 still needs.** Sandbox-verified 2026-07-28, headless Chromium: all three e2e escape paths pass, plus lint + the full unit suite + build. **Not verifiable here:** the embedded Schedule app (`public/sequence/index.html`) loads its in-browser Babel from a CDN the sandbox egress blocks, so the iframe never boots and never emits `planar:nav-state` — the panel appears via the `ready` fallback timer. That means the *iframe-side* half — the embed actually reporting `section: "reports"`, the anti-ping-pong window against a real nav-state, and a real linked/unlinked schedule list — is confirmed only on a signed-in production session. See **V484**.
- **⚠ AMENDED 2026-07-29 by B1065 / B1066 — parts (b) and (c) above are REMOVED, and V484 is superseded by V491.** Both belt-and-braces suppressors turned out to be strands of their own: the `dismissed` state in (c) permanently removed the only create/link entry point for a project (the owner's Tsakiris report), and the `section === "projects"` requirement in (b) suppressed it for every project whenever the embed sat on its dashboard. Part **(a) — Dashboard carries the route up — stands unchanged and is still the way out**; it is now the ONLY way out, by design. Re-verify this item under **V491**, not V484.

That per-project asymmetry is the owner's report verbatim, and only this mechanism produces it.
  - **SUSPECT 2 — the `section !== "projects"` gate — is a second, independent strand, but it did NOT fire here.** It is session-WIDE, so it would have broken Sylvestri too. The gate is now a pure function of the OUTER route — `ready` + a routed `projectId` + no linked schedule + a resolved site name (B560) — so nothing can carry a memory of a previous visit, and the iframe's internal section has no say (an unlinked project gives the embed nothing to show anyway). Clearing the routed project, which is what **Dashboard** does (B1050 part (a), untouched), is the single always-available way out.
- **Guards.** `test/schedulerLinkPanel.test.js` (14 cases) states the fix as invariants: a stale `dismissed` flag cannot hide it, no `section` value can hide it, routing away and back always brings it back, and one project is never affected by another — plus every pre-existing gate and the whole B1050 carry-out suppression sequence. `e2e/schedule-link-panel.spec.js` drives the REAL app logged out: Escape no longer removes it, no Close control exists, and — the regression itself — **Dashboard clears the route, then routing back to the same project brings the empty state straight back.** `ui-audit/diagnose-schedule-strand.mjs` is kept as the reproduction of record for both strands.

### B1052 — Roads carried control points the owner never placed: every connect SPLICED a vertex in and nothing ever took one back out `[Site Planner / roadGeometry]` (bug) #site-planner #road #ui  *(owner report 2026-07-25, screenshot of his truck loop: "I don't remember adding this many control points. So figure out why there's this many control points because this seems like a bug." Minted **B1052 / V485** (late-bound against fresh `origin/main` — the provisional B1050/V484 collided with the already-merged link-schedule panel item, so this newer item renumbered per the late-bind rule). Origin: filed 2026-07-25 from chat as NEW-7.)*
`[ ]` **⏳ merged — V485 PENDING (Verify: live — `Blocker: real-data`).**
- **Measured on his LIVE geometry, not inferred.** Auditing every interior vertex against the chord between its own neighbours: the 40′ truck loop `e38duuwgj` carries **ten** vertices sitting **0.00–0.25 ft off** that chord, and the 40′ aisle `e1454683splyoj` four more. They bend the alignment by nothing. Across his plan, **36 control points of which 16 do no work.**
- **Where they come from.** Every road-to-road connect SPLICES a vertex into the target road at the tee point (`insertRoadVertex` via `planRoadConnect`) and **no path ever removes one**. `insertRoadVertex`'s `collapseFt` only reuses a vertex when the new point lands near THAT SEGMENT'S endpoint — after the first insert, the next connect lands on a different segment and always splices a fresh one. Redraw the side road, drag its end, reconnect a foot over: each attempt leaves its own grip behind.
- **Why B1008 and B1010 didn't catch it — and this is the useful part.** Both attacked vertex debris and both ruled out THIS mode *by design*: B1008 collapses vertices within ~1.5 ft of one another; B1010 adds "a short stub the alignment TURNS through" and states outright that a COLLINEAR stub is harmless because it distorts no geometry. It doesn't distort anything — and it is still clutter the user never authored, which is the actual complaint. The lesson: "does it change the geometry" was the wrong acceptance test; "did the user put it there, and does it do anything" is the right one.
- **Fix:** new pure `simplifyRoadVertices(pts, vtx, tolFt, { pinned, pinTolFt, reference })`. Greedy — remove the least-contributing interior vertex, then **re-measure EVERY ORIGINAL point against the simplified polyline** and stop the moment any would sit more than `tolFt` (1.5 ft) off it. Measuring against the ORIGINAL rather than the previous step is what stops error accumulating across a long run, so the bound is absolute however many points come out. Endpoints and `sharp` vertices are never touched. For each pin (another road's endpoint) only the **NEAREST** vertex is protected — the distinction matters because the debris clusters precisely AROUND a junction, so a radius generous enough to recognise a junction drawn with slack would otherwise protect the very clutter this removes. Pin radius scales with the road's own width (`w/8`, floor 0.75 ft, cap 4 ft), matching B1011's junction-coincidence rule. Wired inside `migrateRoad` so **both read paths** get it (the B1012 lesson).
- **Result on his plan: 36 control points → 20.** All three tees, all three drives and the dissolved region survive unchanged. The new pass moves the road at most **0.90 ft** on his plan (inside its 1.5 ft budget); the only larger correction, 2.04 ft on the truck loop, is B1010's pre-existing debris pass doing what it was shipped to do.
- **Two harnesses and one e2e assertion were keyed to a vertex INDEX** (`e1454682splyoj:3`) and silently tested the wrong thing once indices moved. All three now match by ROAD, never `road:index` — a stale index made `verify-corner-selffix` skip its click and report a pass-shaped result.
- **Sandbox-verified:** new `test/roadSimplify.test.js` (15 cases — debris collapse, a real corner kept, a gentle bend kept, the anti-accumulation bound, the `reference` composition option, nearest-pin-only protection, junction-with-slack, endpoint/sharp preservation, pts↔vtx index alignment, idempotence, no-churn). `e2e/road-tee-oblique.spec.js` 10/10, `road-corner-selffix` 2/2, `verify-junction-obstacles` 4/4, `verify-corner-selffix` PASS. Full suite 5641 + lint (0 errors) + build + MAP/backlog/doc gates green.
- **Live-verify (V485):** on his signed-in plan, selecting the truck loop shows roughly half as many grips, none of them stacked; every junction still renders its curb returns; no road has visibly moved.
