### B1043 — NEW-1: drawn elements drift off the aerial on N–S pan, cumulatively — the feet frame and the basemap used inconsistent latitude models `[Site Planner / Map]` (bug) #site-planner #gis #coordinates #perf  *(owner chat block 2026-07-28, provisional NEW-1. Minted **B1043 / V478**. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open + ⏳ Verify + Done across the map-lock family (`B65` tile ghost, `B183` stale-centre offset, `B821`, `B837` panel-shift compensation, `B933` panBy commit, `feetToLatLng`, `ppfToZoom`, "drift"): **NOT a recurrence.** Those items all fixed FLASH and one-frame SHIFT on a panel toggle; none touched the projection itself. The owner's report explicitly refutes both previously-filed hypotheses — see below.)*
`[x]` **⏳ merged — V478 PENDING (Verify: live — `Blocker: real-data`).** Measured live, not assumed: an out-and-back N–S excursion of ~89,000 ft left a **-4.3 ft residual, uniform across all six probes at three screen positions**, and it ACCUMULATES; E–W was exactly lossless (0.0 ft); at the far position the basemap disagreed with the drawing by **+0.18% in both axes** while the SVG element pixel widths were unchanged. **Hypothesis A (a `sec(lat)` correction pinned at origin, worse E–W) is REFUTED** — E–W is perfect. **Hypothesis B (a B183/B837 fixed offset after settle) is REFUTED** — the error scales with N–S travel. **Scope, answered and not re-litigated: ALL elements drift together** (`distinctTransformChains: 1`), so this never went near the `detentionStorage` evidence path.

**Root cause (confirmed against the code, AUDIT-FIRST):** scale was re-derived at the CURRENT view centre (`SitePlanner.jsx` — `ppfToZoom(view.ppf, center[0])`) while position was converted through `feetToLatLng(pt, origin.lat, origin.lon)` (`lib/arcgis.js`), an equirectangular frame pinned at the SITE origin using a constant `FT_PER_DEG_LAT` and `cos(origin.lat)`. Mercator's y is nonlinear in latitude and the feet frame's is linear, so the two round-tripped inconsistently and every excursion left a few feet behind.

**Fix — one model for both halves, in one new home.** `lib/mapLock.js` is now THE projection that welds the two together:
- the feet frame is an exact **uniform scaling of spherical Web Mercator** anchored at the site origin (`x = (lon-lon0)·k`, `y = -(mercDeg(lat)-mercDeg(lat0))·k`, `k = FT_PER_DEG·cos(lat0)`), so feet↔screen is a rigid affine map of Mercator↔screen and the round trip is exact at any pan distance in any direction;
- `ppfToZoom` moved beside it and is anchored at the **site origin latitude**, never the panned-to centre;
- both are derived from the SAME `FT_PER_DEG`. They previously came from different constants (a feet-per-degree constant vs the earth's circumference in metres) that disagreed by ~4 parts per million — small, but it left a residual that grew with distance from the view centre. The lock is now exact by construction rather than approximate.
- `arcgis.js` delegates `lngLatRingToFeet` / `feetToLatLng` to it (one seam, not two), and `aerialGeom` places the export aerial through the same Mercator frame so the print path can't drift from the screen (PDF-PARITY).

**No migration needed, and this is checked, not asserted:** at the site origin the new frame is identical to the old to first order. Saved geometry moves by **under an inch across a 2,000 ft site** and a few tenths of a foot a mile out — and that difference is the CORRECTION, since the basemap under the drawing has always been Mercator. `test/mapLock.test.js` pins both bounds.

**The regression guard the report asked for.** `test/mapLock.test.js` (13 cases) asserts the round-trip invariant directly — `lockOffsetPx` computes where a feet point lands on screen TWO independent ways (the planner's SVG transform, and the basemap's own Mercator projection at the derived zoom) and they must agree — out-and-back in five directions, over ten repeated excursions, plus a "the old mixed model would have failed this" case so the invariant can't go vacuous. Headless: `ui-audit/diagnose-map-lock.mjs` drives the real app through a ~25,000 ft excursion and asserts the basemap sits at EXACTLY the drawing's scale at start, far and back. It **fails on pre-fix code and passes on the fix** — verified both ways this session.
- `Verify: live` · `#site-planner #gis #coordinates`
- `Origin: filed 2026-07-28 from chat (provisional NEW-1)`

### B1045 — NEW-3: GIS overlays load off the critical path — the map is interactive before the data arrives `[Site Planner / Map]` (feature) #site-planner #gis #perf  *(owner chat block 2026-07-28, provisional NEW-3. Minted **B1045 / V479**. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched the layer-loading family (`B790` honest raster status, `B694`/`B695` cached vector tier, `B75` SWR ages, `B445` cache proxy): **NOT a recurrence** — those made loading HONEST and CACHED; none of them moved it off the first-paint path.)*
`[x]` **⏳ merged — V479 PENDING (Verify: live — `Blocker: live-GIS`).** Measured: restoring a fully-enabled Layers panel fired **465 requests across 17 hosts** in one burst (planyr.io 180, services.arcgis.com 123, arcgis.netl.doe.gov 30, services1/6.arcgis.com 30 each, gis.rrc.texas.gov 12, the rest single-digit) — all of it racing first paint and starving the coarse basemap backfill that exists to make the map usable instantly.
- `lib/layerSchedule.js` (new, pure) owns the ORDER: what kills a deal first (flood, pipelines), then boundaries, then feature services, then client-computed terrain, then the crowd sources (Overpass, Mapillary) last. Stable — equal-priority layers keep the registry's own order, so the sequence doesn't shuffle between sessions.
- `syncOverlayLayers` gained an `admit` gate that stages only the ADD path. A layer turned OFF is still torn down immediately and a live layer still gets its opacity/width updates, whatever the gate says.
- `SitePlanner` runs pass 0 with nothing admitted (removals + updates only), then widens the admitted set four layers at a time on `requestIdleCallback` — so the map draws and is draggable first and overlays fill in behind it. Staging applies to the RESTORE burst only: once the first pass has admitted everything, a layer the user toggles on by hand is admitted immediately (waiting an idle tick for a chip you just clicked would read as lag).
- Each chip keeps its own honest loading dot (B790), so a not-yet-arrived overlay reads as coming, never broken. No modal, no spinner, no blocked gesture at any point. A layer that lands after a pan requests the view it is ADDED to, not the one it was queued against — every layer derives its bbox from the live map at add time, and the view-driven ones re-request on the next `moveend`.
- `Verify: live` · `#site-planner #gis #perf`
- `Origin: filed 2026-07-28 from chat (provisional NEW-3)`

### B1046 — NEW-4: progressive slowdown is per-gesture allocation CHURN, not retention — the anti-flash ghost cloned the entire overscanned tile container `[Site Planner / Map]` (task) #site-planner #perf  *(owner chat block 2026-07-28, provisional NEW-4. Minted **B1046 / V480**. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched the ghost/flash family (`B65`, `B183`, `B821`, `B837`, `B933`): **NOT a recurrence** — the ghost is doing exactly what B65 built it to do; this is its COST, not its correctness.)*
`[x]` **⏳ merged — V480 PENDING (Verify: live — `Blocker: real-data`).** **Retention is ruled out, definitively.** The owner's full sampled series (usedJSHeapSize MB / heap cap MB / domNodes / svgEls / tile `<img>`): baseline 65.5 / 89.2 / 5708 / 4579 / 387 · idle5 52.0 / 77.9 / 5708 / 4579 / 387 · pan20 68.2 / 137.0 / 5769 / 4579 / 446 · overlays_on 71.3 / 143.5 / 7261 / 5361 / 497 · overlays_off 82.7 / 133.5 / 6012 / 4581 / 497 · pan20b 63.4 / 131.0 / 5879 / 4581 / 365 · **idle5b 64.3 / 83.6 / 5716 / 4581 / 387**. After a FULL cycle — 40 pan/zoom gestures, 23 overlays on and off, and a long-distance drift excursion — the tab returns to **domNodes +8, svgEls +2, and tile `<img>` EXACTLY at baseline**, with heap capacity collapsing 131 → 83.6 MB. Nothing is retained. **Treat "is there a leak" as answered NO.**

What IS real is the churn: heap CAPACITY swinging 89 → 143 MB with USED heap flat is per-frame allocation, and that is what the collector pays for in the p99 140 ms frames. The `geoGhostRef` snapshot was a `cloneNode(true)` of the whole overscanned Leaflet container — **390–500 `<img>` copied on every zoom commit**. `lib/ghostSnapshot.js` (new) replaces it with a FLAT snapshot of only the tiles the user can actually see, each shallow-cloned and positioned absolutely: typically **~12–40 tiles instead of ~400**, with pixel-identical cover (the live coarse backfill underneath covers any reveal, and the ghost stays transparent so its own gaps fall through to it). One batched layout read for the whole set — all reads before any writes — so it costs a single forced layout, not one per tile. Tiles that never painted are skipped: a blank `<img>` in the ghost would be worse than no ghost.

Evidence-layer feature sets replace correctly (780 of 782 svg elements returned on toggle-off) and were **deliberately left alone**. The "across releases" half of this item — accumulated feature weight with no ceiling — stays with the companion NEW-8 budget harness.
- `Verify: live` · `#site-planner #perf`

### B1047 — NEW-5: viewport culling for the feet-frame SVG — a FRAME-TIME fix, with the export deliberately exempt `[Site Planner / Map]` (feature) #site-planner #perf #export  *(owner chat block 2026-07-28, provisional NEW-5, RE-SCOPED by the measurement from a memory fix to a frame-time fix. Minted **B1047 / V481**. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched the render-cost family (`B911` dim font scale, `B1016` pond param LOD, `labelLayout` LOD tiering): **NOT a recurrence** — LOD hides labels by zoom; nothing culled by viewport.)*
`[x]` **⏳ merged — V481 PENDING (Verify: live — `Blocker: real-data`).** Measured: **median frame 20 ms, p90 80 ms, p99 140 ms, max 320 ms over 1,525 frames** of scripted drag — one frame in ten costing five times the 16.7 ms budget. The SVG is NOT a memory driver (4,579 elements, flat across every phase; ~420 MB of the reported 555 MB lives outside the JS heap — see B1049) but it IS the frame-time driver, because cost scaled with the size of the whole model rather than with what is on screen.

`lib/viewCull.js` (new, pure) computes the visible world rectangle from `screenToWorld` on the viewport corners plus a generous margin, bounds each drawable, and filters the element / markup / parcel passes to what the view can reach. Three guards make it safe: the selection and anything mid-drag are force-kept whatever their bounds say; an element whose shape can't be bounded is NEVER culled; and a plan under 40 drawables isn't culled at all (the filter would cost more than it saves).

**The hard constraint is enforced in one place.** `buildExportSvg` clones the LIVE `<svg>`, so `withFullRender` flips culling off, flushes a synchronous full render (`flushSync` — a normal state update would land a frame LATER, i.e. after the clone, and the PDF would quietly print only what was on screen), clones, then restores. `test/viewCull.test.js` asserts the export element count is **independent of the current view** from three very different viewports, that the screen pass at those same views draws strictly fewer, and that every element is visible from SOME view (culling hides nothing permanently). LOD/declutter behaviour is untouched.

Headless, on the real app: `ui-audit/diagnose-map-lock.mjs` reads the drawn set at 125 elements, 64 after panning away, and 125 again on return — culling engages and everything comes back.
- `Verify: live` · `#site-planner #perf #export`
- `Origin: filed 2026-07-28 from chat (provisional NEW-5)`

### B1048 — NEW-6: overlay lifecycle — raster tiles now released on toggle-off, superseded fetches aborted on pan, identical requests deduped `[Site Planner / Map]` (bug) #site-planner #gis #perf  *(owner chat block 2026-07-28, provisional NEW-6, NARROWED by the measurement. Minted **B1048 / V482**. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched the teardown family (`B36e` post-await mount guards, `B55` dead-map guards, `B56d` trailing refresh): **NOT a recurrence** — B36e stopped a stale response RENDERING into a detached group; it never released the raster.)*
`[x]` **⏳ merged — V482 PENDING (Verify: live — `Blocker: live-GIS`).** Measured, and narrower than originally filed: toggling all 23 overlays off correctly released **780 of 782 svg elements** and 1,249 of 1,492 DOM nodes — **the vector/feature teardown is already correct and was deliberately NOT touched.** The defect is the raster half: **0 of 51 overlay tiles released**, lingering until an unrelated later pan happened to prune them (497 → 365).
- `lib/tileLifecycle.js` (new) provides `releaseLayer`, now called on toggle-off instead of a bare `map.removeLayer`: it tombstones the layer FIRST, aborts what the layer can cancel, walks a group's children, drops esri-leaflet's painted `_currentImage` (and its DOM node), empties a grid layer's `_tiles` and level containers, and blocks `onAdd`/`_renderImage` so **a request landing after removal cannot resurrect the layer** — which is what left the images behind.
- **The teardown assertion deliberately does not depend on a later gesture.** Per the owner's caveat, `test/tileLifecycle.test.js` asserts `_tiles` is empty and the image is gone IMMEDIATELY after `releaseLayer`, with no pan involved.
- **Pan supersession now genuinely aborts.** The audit the item asked for found the gap: both evidence layers constructed an `AbortController`, but a `busy`/`pending` queue meant a superseded request ran to COMPLETION before the view the user is actually looking at was even requested. Both now abort on supersession. The old note claiming an abort would "poison the shared SWR cache" is wrong and is corrected in place — `gisCache.swr` writes only on success, so an aborted attempt leaves the last-good copy untouched. Both layers also expose `abortPending` so `releaseLayer` can cancel them.
- **Dedupe:** `gisFetch.coalesceRequest` shares one in-flight request between callers asking for the same thing, and reuses a just-finished result for a few seconds so panning back to a bbox you just left is free. Deliberately seconds, not minutes — the long-lived SWR cache is a separate tier and this must not become a shadow copy of it. Failures are never cached; an injected `fetchImpl`, a request with a body, or one carrying its own signal is never shared.

### B1049 — NEW-7: tile footprint — adaptive overscan, retina gated by zoom band, tiles reused across a same-grid commit, bounded cache `[Site Planner / Map]` (task) #site-planner #gis #perf  *(owner chat block 2026-07-28, provisional NEW-7. Minted **B1049 / V483**. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched the tile-budget family (`B65` overscan + keepBuffer, `B170` detectRetina, `B182`/`B218`/`B220` maxNative clamp, `B839` tile stitch): **NOT a recurrence** — B65 INTRODUCED the overscan deliberately and B182 clamped retina by one level; this bounds both rather than reverting either.)*
`[x]` **⏳ merged — V483 PENDING (Verify: live — `Blocker: live-GIS`).** The 4x claim is CONFIRMED and then some: the Leaflet container measured **2018 x 1025 px = 2.07 Mpx against ~0.53 Mpx visible — 3.9x the pixel area** before retina; at dpr 2.15 the working zoom pulled **105 tiles where a bare viewport needs ~12–15 (7–8x)**; one scenario load fetched **221 tiles ≈ 3.5 MB** (avg 16.6 KB, sampled from the real URLs) across FIVE zoom levels — z11=21, z12=56, z13=24, z15=15, z18=105 — of which **~116 (53%) are transitional levels the user never lingers on**. Since ~420 MB of the reported 555 MB is decoded-bitmap/GPU rather than JS heap, **this is the memory fix**.
- **Retina is NOT switched off** — a soft aerial is a core-credibility regression for a tool people eyeball sites in. `tileBudget.retinaForZoom` keeps full density at the working zooms and clamps only at the wide context zooms, extending the B182/B218 `maxNative-1` clamp rather than replacing it. **Named limitation, stated rather than buried:** Leaflet bakes `detectRetina` into the tile grid at construction, so the band is evaluated when the layer is BUILT (basemap on/off, source switch, origin change) — re-deciding it mid-gesture would mean rebuilding the layer and refetching every tile, a worse trade than the one it saves.
- **Adaptive overscan + keepBuffer.** `tileBudget.overscanPx` / `keepBufferFor` step both down on a heavy plan, a device reporting little memory, or a small window — the measured viewport was only 465 px tall, where a fixed 320 px per side is most of the container. `keepBuffer: 4` is revisited alongside it, since it multiplies on top. A real margin always survives, so the B65 pan-reveal never vanishes.
- **The biggest single lever: tiles are reused across a commit.** Leaflet's `Map._resetView` fires `viewprereset` on EVERY `setView`, and GridLayer's handler wipes every tile and level unconditionally — then immediately asks for most of them back. But tiles are keyed by NATIVE tile zoom, and the planner drives the basemap at fractional zoom, so a commit that moves the fractional zoom without moving the rounded one needs no new tiles at all. `preserveTilesAcrossSetView` skips the wipe exactly then (the caller announces the target zoom, since Leaflet hasn't applied it yet at `viewprereset` time) and falls straight through to stock behaviour when the native zoom genuinely changes. A `setView` from anywhere we did not announce always takes the stock wipe — no stale tiles behind our back.
- **Bounded cache.** `boundTileCache` / `tileCacheLimit` put an explicit ceiling on retained tiles, sized from what the container genuinely needs plus headroom. Only non-current tiles are ever shed, so it can never punch a hole in the visible aerial.
- **Gate:** `ui-audit/diagnose-flash.mjs` re-run — no flash regression detectable, but honestly, **it cannot discriminate in this sandbox**: external tile hosts are egress-blocked so the loaded-tile count is 0 for every frame either way. Tile COUNT held flat across the zoom (45 before, 45 after), which is the half this change affects. The flash check itself is genuinely live-only and is what V483 exists for.
- `Verify: live` · `#site-planner #gis #perf`

### B1040 — NEW-8: standing performance budget + regression harness, gated in CI `[Infra / QA]` (feature) #infra #perf #testing  *(owner chat block 2026-07-28, provisional NEW-8, INFRA half of a nine-item perf run. Minted **B1040 / V477** via `npm run next-id -- --against-main`. Branch `claude/chunk-prefetch-audit-xz54gh`. DEDUPE-FIRST: searched Open + ⏳ Verify + Done for perf/budget/harness/regression items — no existing performance-budget item; `ui-audit/initial-load.mjs` (B65) measures one metric ad-hoc with no committed ceiling and no gate, so this is net-new, not a recurrence.)*
`[x]` **Implemented — parks here for the production re-seed (V477).** The structural reason the app drifted slower is that there was no ceiling: every feature cost a little speed and nothing caught it until the owner noticed. This is the guardrail.
- Verify: live  *(the provisional ceilings must be re-seeded from a run against production + the real Sylvestri scenario — see V477)*
- Origin: filed 2026-07-28 from chat
- **Built — two halves, one committed budgets file.**
  - `ui-audit/perf-budgets.json` — every ceiling, committed and seeded from the owner's measured baseline **plus headroom**, never vibes.
  - `ui-audit/perf-bundle-audit.mjs` — **the CI gate**. Deterministic, no browser: walks `dist/.vite/manifest.json` (new `build.manifest` in `vite.config.js`) to compute what each ROUTE must actually download, which is the number a budget should cap — a per-chunk size table cannot answer that. Breach output names the metric and its delta.
  - `ui-audit/perf-harness.mjs` — the browser half: time-to-first-drag, first-aerial-coverage, drag frame median/p90, peak heap over a scripted pan/zoom + overlay-toggle loop, tile requests, FCP, plus a runtime Site-route chunk assertion.
  - `ui-audit/lib/perf-scenario.mjs` — the fixed, deterministic heavy reference scenario.
  - `test/perfBudgets.test.js` — 8 unit guards (budgets well-formed; no ceiling/target inversion; every above-target metric names its owner; **and the boot-prefetch invariant**, so the B1041 regression class is caught by `npm test` rather than needing a browser).
  - `docs/PERF-BUDGETS.md` — the standing rule + the three measurement blockers.
- **THE RULE, recorded in `docs/PERF-BUDGETS.md`:** *a feature that breaches a budget ships with a matching optimization, or it does not ship.*
- **Ceiling vs target (the honest answer to "commit today's numbers or the aspiration?").** Every metric carries BOTH. `ceiling` = today's measurement + headroom → green on day one, red on a real regression, attributable to the PR. `target` = where it should be → reported as `⚠ ABOVE TARGET` on **every** run, naming the backlog item that owns closing it. A single budget set to today's number is unbreachable and meaningless; set to the aspiration it is red from day one and gets ignored. Currently above target and reported as such: `frameMedianMs` (20 vs 16.7), `frameP90Ms` (80 vs 33), `aerialTileRequests` (221 vs 120), `siteRouteJsBytes`, `largestChunkBytes`.
- **Deliberate scope call — only the DETERMINISTIC half gates CI, and this is stated loudly rather than quietly dropped.** Bundle weight falls out of the build with no browser, network or CPU contention, so a breach is unambiguously the PR's fault. Frame time and heap on a shared `ubuntu-latest` runner are dominated by co-tenant load; gating merges on them yields flaky reds, and flaky reds train people to re-run until green — worse than no budget. The aerial metrics additionally need live tile hosts the sandbox blocks. So `perf-bundle-audit.mjs` is a required build step; the runtime harness runs on demand and before shipping render/load work. `docs/PERF-BUDGETS.md` records that the honest way to gate the runtime half later is a pinned self-hosted runner.
- **All three measurement blockers designed around, and documented so nobody re-learns them:** (1) the 250-entry resource-timing buffer fills during load and then **silently** drops entries — the harness calls `performance.setResourceTimingBufferSize(3000)` in an init script, the only place early enough; (2) cross-origin tiles carry no `Timing-Allow-Origin` so `transferSize` reads 0 — the tile budget counts **requests issued**, never summed bytes, which also keeps it meaningful where tile hosts are blocked; (3) `measureUserAgentSpecificMemory()` is unavailable (no cross-origin isolation) so tab memory is **not measurable** — `peakHeapMB` is JS heap only and says so in the budget note, the docs, and the harness header (the owner's ~555 MB tab vs 134.6 MB JS heap means ~420 MB is invisible here). Chrome also quantises `performance.memory` without `--enable-precise-memory-info`, which the harness passes.
- **TTFD defined here, as instructed — 328 ms was NOT treated as TTFD.** Definition: navigation start → the canvas exists **and** has demonstrably serviced a pointerdown/move/up with a committed frame, i.e. the first instant real work is possible. It is recorded as `measured: null` with a `localFloor`, **not** given a fabricated production number.
- **Reference scenario is a documented STAND-IN.** Sylvestri / Concept C is signed-in real data the sandbox cannot reach. `e2e/fixtures/sites/dense-testfit` was tried first and is the wrong source — it carries the pure-engine `x`/`y` geometry schema and crashes the live render path. The committed stand-in is deterministic and fixed-origin but **lighter** than Sylvestri, so its numbers are a floor — which is exactly why ceilings are seeded from the owner's production figures, not from a local run. (Trap found and documented: element types resolve through `dockZones.js`, so an invented type id crashes the workspace on `ZONE[e.type].label` — there is no `truckCourt` type; a truck court is `paving`.)
- **Load timings are refused, not faked.** `index.html` pulls the Inter webfont via a render-blocking `<link rel=stylesheet>`; where egress is restricted that hangs and drags FCP from ~330 ms to ~13 s. The harness detects failed cross-origin requests and reports load-sensitive metrics as **MEASURED BUT NOT JUDGED** instead of as a breach — a budget that cries wolf is ignored as fast as one that never fires.
- **Verified (sandbox):** bundle audit green (2 above-target, reported); runtime harness green on every measurable metric; `test/perfBudgets.test.js` 8/8 (it caught a real gap during authoring — two provisional metrics lacked a `targetOwner` — which was fixed, evidence the guard bites); `npm run lint` 0 errors; `npm test` 5535/5535; `npm run build` green; `MAP.md` regenerated.
- **Pending live (V477):** re-seed the provisional `timeToFirstDragMs` / `firstAerialCoverageMs` ceilings and confirm frame/heap/tile ceilings against production + the real Sylvestri scenario, where tile hosts and the webfont actually resolve.

Net-new regression with a named cause.)*
`[x]` **⏳ merged — V474 PENDING (Verify: live — `Blocker: real-data`).** Root cause, proven not assumed: `bands.usableCf` (the whole recovered water column) and `bands.mitigationCandidateCf` (the below-flood slice **of that same column**) stopped being disjoint at R1, and both were credited. The owner's LEAD hypothesis (mitigation reading the detention surplus) is REFUTED — 63.4 − 33.8 = 29.6 equals the mitigation figure only because this pond's above-flood band (33.77) lands within a hundredth of its detention requirement (33.8); the ALTERNATE hypothesis (the credit is never clamped out of the detention band) is CONFIRMED. Fixed end to end:
- `pondGeom.bandedStorage` now emits a true PARTITION — `permanentDeadCf` + `mitigationCandidateCf` + `aboveWseCf` == `grossCf` under every policy — and the candidate band starts at the **permanent water level** (pool *and* normal tailwater), so permanently-wet volume can no longer be credited as flood compensation.
- `pondLedger.allocatePondDuty` is the ONE exclusive duty split: the below-flood void serves detention OR compensating storage, never both. A declared MITIGATION-purpose pond dedicates its whole band; every other pond dedicates only what the site's remaining requirement needs and keeps the rest for detention; a gated / absent outfall blocks the dedication; the split declares its boundary elevation (the governing flood WSE) so the reconciler sees a DECLARED split rather than an undeclared dual duty.
- `accumulatePondLedger` is now folded AFTER the mitigation requirement resolves (`pondLedgerGeom` carries the requirement-independent facts before it), and an UNKNOWN requirement dedicates nothing — volume never leaves the detention ledger silently.

### B1019 — NEW-1: Yield reported Detention OK and Mitigation OK while the two together claimed 42.8 ac-ft MORE storage than the ponds physically hold `[Site Planner / yield · pond]` (bug) #site-planner #yield #pond #floodplain  *(owner chat block 2026-07-28, provisional NEW-1, from a Cowork design review of Bain / Concept A. DEDUPE-FIRST: searched Open + ⏳ Verify + Done for reconcile / double-count / overlap / duty-split. **B990** (mitigation credit computed TWO ways) and **B992** (per-pond "holds" chip mismatch) are each a single-number disagreement inside ONE ledger; this is the opposite failure — both ledgers internally consistent, jointly over-committed, which no single-ledger accumulator can see. NET-NEW.)*
`[ ]` **⏳ merged — V465 PENDING (Verify: live — `Blocker: real-data`).** Counted detention + counted mitigation are now summed across all ponds and held against total physical pond storage; an over-claim renders a hard FAIL naming the volume and the ponds.
- Verify: live
- Origin: filed 2026-07-28 from chat
- **Repro (owner's, verbatim):** Bain / Concept A → Yield. Detention 150.9 of 76.7 OK; Mitigation 98.2 of 97.7 OK. Detention detail: Pond 1 61.8 counts / 61.8 holds · Pond 2 60.0 / 115.4 · Pond 3 6.6 / 6.6 · Pond 4 22.5 / 22.5 = 206.3 ac-ft physical. Claimed service 150.9 + 98.2 = 249.1 against 206.3 → a 42.8 ac-ft unreconciled gap, both checks still green.
- **Fix.** New pure `lib/storageReconcile.js` (`reconcileStorage` / `reconcilePond`): per pond it compares claimed detention + claimed mitigation to that pond's own physical storage, and at site level claimed-vs-physical. `state:"fail"` is a HARD fail carrying `overlapCf`, `offenders` (the provable double-counts first, then the dual-duty ponds when the overlap is only visible site-wide) and a plain-English `message`. An UNKNOWN pond (restored check with no split facts) poisons the verdict to `state:"unknown"` — never a silent pass (LOUD-FAILURE).
- **The declared-split invariant.** A pond serving both duties must declare an explicit vertical split — `pondStageModel.dutySplit` puts the MITIGATION band from the floor up to the governing flood elevation and the DETENTION band strictly above it, sharing ONE boundary elevation, so the same acre-foot slice cannot be credited twice **by construction** (`overlapCf` is computed and asserted 0, not assumed). A dual-duty pond with NO declared boundary is itself a finding (`state:"undeclared"`) even when the arithmetic happens to close.
- **Surfaced.** A "Storage reconciles — N claimed / N exists" row in Detention detail (green when it ties, red with the naming sentence when it does not) plus a FAIL override on BOTH storage verdicts in the strip (`applyReconciliation` in `lib/yieldVerdicts.js`).
- Tests: `test/yieldStorageReview.test.js` pins the exact Bain four-pond shape (206.3 physical / 249.1 claimed / 42.8 overlap / offender "Pond 2"), the passing case, the undeclared case, the unknown-poison case and the display-precision tolerance. Headless: `ui-audit/verify-yield-storage-review.mjs` drives the real panel logged-out and reads back "185.1 claimed / 146.0 exists" with the naming sentence on a seeded two-pond over-claim.

### B1020 — NEW-2: the panel printed a between-storms recovery assumption but gave the reader nothing to evaluate it with (no drawdown time) `[Site Planner / yield · pond]` (feature) #site-planner #yield #pond  *(owner chat block 2026-07-28, provisional NEW-2. Minted **B1020 / V466**. DEDUPE-FIRST: `drawdownWarning` in `pondGeom.js` (B708) screens only whether the pond bottom sits below the receiving flowline — a feasibility test, not a TIME; `detentionCriteria.js` has carried a `drawdownMaxHr` criterion since B822 with NO consumer. NET-NEW, and it gives that dormant criterion its first reader.)*

- Origin: filed 2026-07-28 from chat
- **Why.** The strip already stated "the pond recovers to normal tailwater between storms (design storm not coincident with the flood); confirm the coincident-storm rule" (R1/B987) — an unfalsifiable claim without a number next to it. A multi-day drawdown is what invalidates that assumption, and it is also what makes a shared detention/mitigation pond fail FBC §5.02(h)(1)'s "full capacity available for subsequent flood events" test.
- **Fix.** New pure `lib/drawdownTime.js`: `allowableReleaseCfs` (per-acre criterion, or an explicit outlet override), `drawdownHours`, `drawdownTone` (ok / amber / red against a configurable threshold, default 72 hr, overridden by the jurisdiction's `drawdownMaxHr`), `fmtDrawdown`, `assessDrawdown` (per pond + site, prorating one CAPPED site outfall across the ponds by stored volume rather than giving each pond the full site rate). Every result carries `optimistic:true` and says so: outflow decays as head drops, so the constant-rate figure is a FLOOR on the real answer.
- **Worked example pinned as a regression test** (the owner's): 0.125 cfs/ac × 80.34 ac = 10.04 cfs; 150.9 ac-ft = 6,573,204 cf; ÷ 10.04 = 7.6 days. The full 206.3 ac-ft = 10.4 days.

### B1021 — NEW-3: mitigation was compared as a lump sum, so a total that ties could hide every foot of the offset being at the wrong elevation `[Site Planner / stormwater · floodplain]` (feature) #site-planner #yield #pond #floodplain  *(owner chat block 2026-07-28, provisional NEW-3. Minted **B1021 / V467**. DEDUPE-FIRST: **B707/B712** built the compensating-storage engine as a volume TOTAL (the Fort Bend record's own note says "volume-total method (no HCFCD elevation-increment table)"); **B1001** (open) is the BKDD-specific ask to band against the 500-yr as well. This item is the general elevation-matched TEST the engine never had; B1001 remains open as the BKDD criteria transcription.)*
`[ ]` **⏳ merged — V467 PENDING (Verify: live — `Blocker: real-data`).** Compensating storage is now computed and shown by 1-ft elevation band, with per-band pass/fail and an overall result that FAILS if any band is short even when the total nets positive.
- Verify: live
- Origin: filed 2026-07-28 from chat
- **Why.** FBC §5.02(h)(1) requires a HYDRAULICALLY EQUIVALENT (one-to-one) offset. Hydraulic equivalence is elevation-matched — water at one level cannot be stored by a hole dug lower — so Bain's 98.2-vs-97.7 total match is not evidence of compliance and would not survive review.
- **Fix.** New pure `lib/mitigationBands.js`: `bandSpans` buckets each priced grid cell's fill COLUMN (existing grade → top of fill, capped at the governing flood surface) into 1-ft bands in proportion to the height in each; `createdBands` reads the pond side straight off `pondStageModel`'s `volumeBetween` integral (so the two ledgers cannot drift) and EXCLUDES volume below the floodplain bottom from credit while still reporting it (`excludedBelowBottomCf`) — that dirt is borrow, not offset; `bandLedger` produces per-band `{lostCf, requiredCf, createdCf, netCf, pass, shortCf}` with `overallPass` as the AND over bands, plus `totalWouldPass` (what the old lump-sum method would have concluded) so the panel can say "the totals tie, the elevations do not".
- **Engine seam.** `floodplainMitigation.js` gained an opt-in `opts.bandSpans` that collects each cell's elevation span in the SAME pass that sums the volume (`gridIntersect` `opts.spanAt`), so a band can never disagree with the number it came from; `combineMitigation` carries the spans on the same fast path as the retained heat-map cells.
- **Surfaced.** A "Replaced at the right levels" row in Mitigation detail — "every level covered" or "N levels short" with the failing bands listed (elevation range, given back vs taken) and the explicit "the acre-foot totals tie — but the levels do not" line. A failing ledger also demotes a numerically-OK Mitigation verdict to SHORT.
- Tests: 6 cases incl. the proportional split of a 3.4-ft column, the totals-tie-but-bands-fail inversion, the below-bottom exclusion, the unanchored-pond and unknown-flood honesty states, and a tie-out of created bands to the pond's own duty-split integral.

- **The two tests, each citing its source.** (a) FBC Interim Atlas-14 criteria — at least 50% of DETENTION storage must drain by gravity outfall (threshold read from the jurisdiction's `gravityDrainFraction`, defaulting to 0.5). (b) FBC §5.02(h)(1) — MITIGATION storage must FULLY gravity-drain as floodwaters recede so full capacity is available for subsequent flood events; **pumps are not allowed**, so ANY dead mitigation volume above tolerance fails and is excluded from credit entirely (`creditableCf`).
- **Fix.** `pondStageModel.outfallSplit` + `gravityTests`. An unset invert returns `known:false` with a reason — never an assumed pass. The invert is read from the pond's existing modelled outlet stages (`det.outlet.stages[].invertElevFt`, lowest wins), so nothing new is asked of the user.
- **Surfaced.** A named per-pond warn chip in Detention detail — e.g. "Pond 1: 55.4 ac-ft of its flood-mitigation storage sits below the outlet and can never drain back out — that volume earns no credit, and pumping it is not allowed" — with both citations on the ⓘ; a quiet "no outlet elevation set" line when the test cannot run. Deep ponds where most storage sits below any plausible invert surface naturally through this.
- Tests: 6 cases incl. the unknown-invert honesty state, a low invert passing and a high invert failing the 50% test, the full-gravity mitigation rule in both directions, an invert above the whole mitigation band killing all its credit, and the assembled model tying its duty bands back to the stage total.

### B1017 — Junction outline-cut polylines were DOUBLE-ROTATED: stray element-coloured lines projected outside rotated rect elements `[Site Planner / renderElPx]` (bug) #site-planner #road #drive #export  *(owner chat block 2026-07-28 with a root-caused diagnosis, arrived as provisional B1400 — Tsakiris / Concept A (site `smrjdgmlinea`), east end of Building 3: the parking field `e52duuwgj` (150×42, rot 270) that a drive tees into showed two parking-coloured lines 42 ft apart cutting across the field and projecting ~59 ft east into bare aerial, plus a short vertical stub, no fill under them — and the field's own outline missing. Minted **B1017 / V463** via `git fetch origin main && npm run next-id -- --against-main`. Branch `claude/junction-outline-cut-rotation-bcm3p2`. DEDUPE-FIRST: a NET-NEW second-order defect inside the outline-cut render **B1009 introduced**, not a recurrence of it — B1009's own symptom (the target's outline ruled straight across the drive mouth) is genuinely fixed; this is a different failure of the same code at rot 90/270, so it takes its own number and cross-references B1009 / V455 step (b). Nothing else in the ⏳/Open/Done set matches `outlineCut` or a double-rotation symptom.)*
`[ ]` **⏳ merged — V463 PENDING (Verify: live — `Blocker: real-data` + PDF/export parity).** A drive junction can no longer throw geometry outside the footprint of the element it tees into, at any rotation.
- **Root cause (AUDIT-FIRST, confirmed against the code, matching the owner's diagnosis to the foot).** The `if (outlineCut)` block in `SitePlanner.jsx` builds the interrupted-outline corners in **WORLD feet** — `corner(lx,ly)` rotates the local half-extents about the element centre, so `el.rot` is already baked in — and then pushed those polylines straight into `parts`. `renderElPx` returns `parts` inside a `<g transform="rotate(el.rot, c)">`, so **`el.rot` was applied twice**. rot 0 / 180 are unaffected (0° / 360°); rot 90 / 270 land at 540° ≡ 180°, and a rectangle rotated 180° about its own centre is congruent to the unrotated one — so a 42×150 field drew its outline as 150×42 about the same centre, overhanging (150−42)/2 = 54 ft each way (the west half hidden under the building, `Z_LAYER` building 5 > parking 3, which is why only the east overhang was visible). The **second-order symptom** the owner also saw follows from the same line: `outlineCut` sets the plain `<rect>`'s stroke to `none` on the assumption the polylines replace the outline, so at rot 90/270 the field lost its real edge entirely and the only line left on the correct footprint was the derived `curbEdgesOf` band. The adjacent pond baseline ghost and `pondContourEls` already counter-rotate with `rotate(-el.rot)` for exactly this reason — this block skipped it.
- **Fix.** The geometry moved into a pure, documented `rectOutlineCutSegments(el, cutters)` in `lib/roadNetwork.js` (world feet in, world feet out, with the frame contract stated in its header so the next consumer can't repeat the mistake), and the render wraps its polylines in `<g transform="rotate(-(el.rot||0), c)" data-testid="rect-outline-cut" data-el-id={el.id}>` — the same counter-rotate the pond ghost and the stage contours use. With the rotation net-identity the footprint outline is back on the true edge and interrupted only at the drive mouth, so the blanked rect stroke is no longer a hole.
- **Sandbox-verified — and the guard was proven to FAIL on the pre-fix code, not just asserted.** New `test/junctionOutlineCut.test.js` (23 cases): the pure segments' bbox equals the element's true rotated footprint bbox at rot 0/90/180/270 and at oblique rotations; a drive interrupts the outline without pushing anything outside the footprint; the removed length equals exactly the mouth crossings; and the render-frame half asserts the counter-rotate wrapper composes to the identity. Reverting `SitePlanner.jsx` to pre-fix `main` turns that half red. The same file also reproduces the pre-fix composition numerically and proves it was **right at rot 0/180 and transposed at rot 90/270** — the exact reason every earlier rot-0 mock passed while the plan rendered broken.
- **Headless-verified through the REAL render path on the owner's real element set.** New `e2e/junction-outline-cut.spec.js` seeds `ui-audit/fixtures/tsakiris-concept-a.json` and measures the drawn outline against the element's OWN `<rect>` in the live DOM (so the check needs no unit math and is immune to the fit-to-extent zoom): **6/6 green** — the owner's rot-270 field, a rot-90 parking field, rot-0 and rot-180 regressions, a rot-90 paving pad with a truck-court drive, and the export-clone parity case. The rot-90/0/180/paving cases are the SAME real target+drive pair rotated about the target's own centre and moved clear of the plan, so every one goes through the real junction solver. **Confirmed to FAIL on the pre-fix behaviour:** with the counter-rotate removed, rot 270 / rot 90 / the paving pad all report the outline projecting **~35 % of the footprint's diagonal** past its left edge while rot 0/180 still pass — the reported defect, reproduced and then eliminated.
- **PDF-PARITY.** `buildExportSvg` builds the export by cloning the live canvas node, so a transform bug on screen rides straight into the PDF and the PNG. The export case reproduces that clone in-page, re-measures inside it, and asserts the counter-rotate attribute survives verbatim and no outline projects past any footprint edge — it fails on the pre-fix render alongside the on-screen cases.
- **Live-verify (V463):** the look on his signed-in Tsakiris / Concept A over the aerial, plus a real exported PDF/PNG (the sandbox proves the DOM the exporter rasterizes, not the rasterizer's own bytes).

### B1016 — Pond BERM-height and FLOOR-elevation numbers painted at a fixed size at site-overview zoom, out-shouting the building dimensions `[Site Planner / pond]` (bug) #site-planner #pond #ui #yield  *(owner chat block + screenshot 2026-07-26, a 6.58-ac detention pond at working zoom: "it's telling me the berm and floor parameters. I don't need to know that information at that size at least. Like, maybe if I'm zoomed into the pond more, sure. But at that height that stuff is bigger than the building numbers. It definitely does not need to be that big or even visible at that zoom." Minted **B1016 / V462** via `git fetch origin main && npm run next-id -- --against-main`. `[ ]` **⏳ merged — V462 PENDING (Verify: live — zoom-/data-density-dependent rendering).** Pond design numbers are now their own tier below the detail tier.
- **Root cause (AUDIT-FIRST, three separate call sites, none of them sharing a rule):** (a) the berm tag (`SitePlanner.jsx` pond-berm-ring-layer) drew at a **hardcoded `fontSize: 11` bold with a fixed 3px halo** behind a flat `view.ppf > 0.16` gate — i.e. visible at essentially every working zoom regardless of how thin the berm band actually rendered; (b) the contour elevation callouts (`pondContourEls`, `WS …` / `Floor …`) drew at a **fixed `fontSize: 9`** with a fixed 2.6px halo, gated only on `detailLabelVisible(pondMinPlanDimension, ppf)` — keyed to the whole POND, so a big basin passed the gate at overview zoom and painted its floor elevation there; (c) the map label stack's `Holds … · N′ rim to floor` line rode the same whole-pond gate. Net effect at ppf ≈ 0.35 on the owner's pond: an 8.2 ft berm on a 3:1 exterior face is a **~9px band on screen** carrying a full-size 11px bold tag, and a 16.2 ft basin's floor elevation printed over a **~17px** side-slope band — numbers physically larger than the features they annotate, and louder than the building dimension numbers (which correctly shrink and drop out via B911's `dimFontPx` + `dimCalloutVisible`).

The pond's **identity** — its name and footprint acreage — stays on the normal overview label stack, exactly like a building's name + sf, and the depth RINGS keep their own sub-pixel gate and still draw at overview zoom: we hid the numbers, not the grading. The `⚠ Too deep — max ≈ N′` callout is untouched (LOUD-FAILURE: an infeasibility warning is not a parameter).
- **Sandbox-verified:** `test/labelLayout.test.js` +1 case replaying the owner's exact repro (24.6 ft berm band + 48.6 ft slope band at ppf 0.35 → both hidden; both return on zoom-in, deeper feature first; the declutter floor still binds; font never exceeds a dim number). New `e2e/pond-param-zoom.spec.js` drives the REAL SVG canvas headless, logged out, on a seeded-blank site: draws a detention pond, asserts zero `[data-contour-label]` at the default working zoom while the depth rings DO draw, asserts they return on zoom-in at ≤11px, and declutter again on zoom-out — **confirmed to FAIL on the pre-fix behaviour** (thresholded to 0 → 1 label at working zoom, screenshot on file) and pass after. Full suite 5385 + build + `MAP.md` regen green.
- **Live-verify (V462):** the berm-tag half needs a real terrain grade (`fmElev.existGradeFt`, 3DEP) which the sandbox egress blocks, so only the shared helper is proven for it here — plus the owner's own look at the pond that produced the screenshot.

### B1005 — NEW-1: clamp the curb-return fillet to the DRIVE WIDTH (the reach = R) so oblique tees stop scooping `[Site Planner / road]` (bug) #site-planner #road #drive  *(owner chat block 2026-07-24 — the road-connection feature fixed ~6× and STILL scooping on the owner's REAL oblique/curved plan: prior B945/B946/B949/B953/B964/B971 (PRs #757/#760/#764/#767/#771/#774/#781) and the most recent **B989** (#793). DEDUPE-FIRST — **SUPERSEDES B989's width-cap** (see below); filed fresh per the owner's re-diagnosis.)*

### B1010 — Connect debris judged by DISTANCE let a 3.4 ft stub carrying a 37° bend through, starving the corner and mis-aiming the junction `[Site Planner / road]` (bug) #site-planner #road  *(owner live-verify 2026-07-25 on the deployed B1009 build, after he redrew the 36' aisle: a spike hanging off the junction by the pond, with the new radius flag sitting on it. `[ ]` **⏳ merged — V456 PENDING (Verify: live — `Blocker: real-data`).** DISTANCE was the wrong test.
- **Root cause, measured on the live geometry:** the connect that made the new tee dropped a vertex **3.4 ft** from one already on the truck loop — just outside B1008's flat 1.5 ft collapse. The alignment swings **37°** across that stub. A 40 ft road cannot bend 37° in 3.4 ft, so the arc fillet clamped to a **5 ft** radius against the truck class's 50 ft minimum (which is exactly what B1009's new flag was reporting), and — because `roadRunFrom` read the junction tangent at a fixed 1.5 ft — the tee stood ON the stub and built the entrance square to a heading the road abandons three feet later. Hence the spike. The SAME road carries harmless ~2 ft stubs further east: harmless because it runs dead straight through them. **What makes a stub dangerous is a stub carrying a TURN.**
- **Fixed (three places):** (1) `dedupeRoadVertices` gains a geometric test — a segment shorter than a quarter of the road's own width across which the alignment deflects more than ~5° collapses too, and a `pinned` list (every other road's endpoints, supplied by `migrateRoads`) guarantees cleanup can never drop a vertex a tee is welded to; (2) `roadRunFrom` reads the tangent over `roadTangentNoise(el)` = half the travel width instead of a fixed 1.5 ft, so a few feet of debris cannot aim a junction; (3) `planRoadConnect` reuses an existing control point within the same width-scaled tolerance, so the debris stops being created.
- **Sandbox-verified on the owner's CURRENT geometry** (`ui-audit/fixtures/tsakiris-concept-a-live.json`, re-pulled after he redrew the aisle): the loop's debris vertex collapses (19→18 points), the tee node and every welded endpoint survive, and NO corner remains below the truck 50 ft minimum — the 5 ft corner and its flag are gone. `test/roadNetwork.test.js` +6 pure cases (turning stub collapses, straight stub does not, pinned vertex never dropped, B1008 behaviour preserved, idempotent). Full suite 5345 + lint + build + 20 road e2e + the junction harness green.
- **KNOWN REMAINDER — filed as B1011, not fixed here:** the tee lands exactly ON a bend in the through road, and the junction math still assumes ONE straight through-tangent there (it uses the bisector). The two curb returns therefore sit slightly proud on one side and shy on the other, leaving a small notch and a thin dart at that specific junction. Correct fix is a different model (sort the arms by bearing around the node and fillet consecutive pairs) — a real generalisation, deliberately not rushed in behind this one.
- **Live-verify (V456):** the look on his signed-in plan.

### B1011 — A tee that lands ON a bend in the through road was solved as if the through road were straight `[Site Planner / roadGeometry]` (bug) #site-planner #road  *(split out of B1010, 2026-07-25 — the remaining artifact at the owner's pond-west junction after B1010 cleaned the debris. Owner: "alright take care of that". Shipped 2026-07-25 with **V461**.)*
`[ ]` **⏳ merged — V461 PENDING (Verify: live — `Blocker: real-data`).** Root cause and fix as filed, plus a second defect in the same family found while verifying.
- **Root cause.** `teeGeometry` takes a SINGLE `throughDir`. When the tee node is also a bend vertex the through road has TWO tangents there (incoming and outgoing) and the caller could only hand over their bisector — so BOTH curb returns were built against a line the pavement never follows: one sat proud of the real edge (a thin dart), the other fell shy of it (a notch).
- **Fix — model a junction as N ARMS around a NODE.** New pure `nodeJunction({ node, arms, R })` in `roadGeometry.js`: each arm carries its OWN bearing, pavement half-width, available run and owning road id. Sort the arms by bearing; every ADJACENT PAIR is one corner and gets one curb-return fillet built against *that arm's own tangent*. The rule reproduces the straight tee (two armpits plus one ~180° gap that needs nothing) and subsumes the Y, the bend-with-branch and the 4-way without any arm being special. **Two arms of the SAME road are skipped** — that is the road's own bend, already joined by its polyline buffer, not a junction. `teeJunctionsOf` now builds [back, fwd, side] arms and maps the result into the existing `{ wedges, returns, throughTangents, nTee }` contract, so the dissolved-network render is unchanged.
- **Sub-foot tangent step (round 2).** A fillet is tangent to the arm's STRAIGHT edge line, but a real strip edge is the tessellated buffer of a polyline that may bend right there — so a wedge ending exactly at its tangent point left a visible step in the union outline. Each flank now OVERSHOOTS a little past the tangent and a hair INSIDE the edge, so the two boundaries cross instead of one stopping. Free, because everything inside the union is invisible; the inward bias is what guarantees it can never poke out.
- **A junction drawn with sub-foot slack was not recognised AT ALL (same family, found while verifying).** `TEE_COINCIDE_FT` was a flat 0.75 ft; on the owner's plan the 36′ aisle's endpoint sits **0.86 ft** from the 40′ aisle's vertex — a tenth of a foot over the line — so the app saw no tee, added no returns, and the two strips simply butted: a squared-off notch. Sub-foot slack is normal in hand-drawn geometry (grid snap, migration rounding, a nudged vertex) and is not a meaningful separation on a 40 ft road. The tolerance now scales with the narrower road's own width (`w/8`, floor 0.75 ft, cap 4 ft) — the same basis as B1010's debris rule — so two genuinely distinct vertices still can never be welded by accident. That junction now resolves with real returns.
- **Verified on the OWNER'S REAL PLAN** (`ui-audit/fixtures/tsakiris-concept-a-live.json`, harness `ui-audit/diagnose-road-junctions.mjs` + a new hard-zoom view `J6z-fork-crotch`): the pond-west junction renders as a clean Y with a real return on both sides — no dart, no notch — and the previously-unrecognised aisle junction gains its returns. Junction emission before/after confirms 2 tees → 3.
- **Sandbox-verified:** new `test/nodeJunction.test.js` (12 cases — the straight tee's two armpits, the BEND tee's asymmetric pair, a road's own bend skipped, the 4-way, the Y, short-arm clamping, the honest sharp-corner degrade, and the polygon/area invariants the union depends on) + 2 new `e2e/road-tee-oblique.spec.js` specs (a bend tee returns on BOTH sides; a junction with sub-foot slack is still recognised). All prior road guards still green: `road-tee-oblique` 9/9, `road-corner-selffix` 2/2, `verify-junction-obstacles` 4/4, `verify-corner-selffix` PASS. Full suite 5384 + lint (0 errors) + build + MAP/backlog/doc gates green.
- **Live-verify (V461):** on his signed-in plan, the junction by the pond reads as a clean fork with a rounded return on each side, and the 36′/40′ aisle junction no longer shows a squared notch.

### B1015 — The new corner tag sprawled across the plan and its "Fix" printed on top of its own label — and the corner still drew as a blob because the OLD auto-fixer's clamped radius was baked into the vertex `[Site Planner / roadGeometry]` (bug) #site-planner #road #ui  *(owner live-verify 2026-07-25 on the deployed B1013 build, reading his own Tsakiris / Concept A: "Double check, from the ss, it's seems like it's not shaped right, I could be wrong, but the prompts text is so far off." Wired inside `migrateRoad`, not at a call site, so **both read paths** get it (the B1012 lesson).

### B1013 — A corner near a road's END had half its approach taken away by a clamp meant for shared legs, then the app flagged the geometry instead of fixing it `[Site Planner / roadGeometry]` (bug) #site-planner #road  *(owner report 2026-07-25, screenshot of the amber mark on his Tsakiris fire lane: "I don't think you tested it… dont stop until youve tested that this is taken care of", following 2026-07-24: "the exclamation point should never become exclamation points, the software should self fix… if it's on truck route, it should auto go to whatever the minimum radius is." Minted **B1013 / V458**. Origin: filed 2026-07-25 from chat as NEW-2/NEW-3/NEW-4.)*
`[ ]` **⏳ merged — V458 PENDING (Verify: live — `Blocker: real-data`).** Three defects, one root.
- **Root cause — the leg-share clamp was wrong at a road's end.** `arcCorner` limits a corner's run-up to *half* the shorter adjacent leg. That half is correct only for a leg **shared with a neighbouring corner** — it is what stops two fillets overrunning each other. A leg that runs to the road's **own endpoint** has no neighbour to share with, so halving it was pure loss: on the owner's real plan his fire-lane corner drew at **11 ft against a 28 ft class minimum when its geometry could hold 22**, and B1009's flag then reported the app's own clamp as a defect in his layout. **Fixed:** new pure `cornerShares(i, n)` — full leg at a terminus, half on a shared leg — applied identically in `arcCorner`, `roadCornerRadii` and `fixRoadRadii`'s `feasR`, so the render and both measurement paths cannot disagree.
- **The mark never became a fix (owner rule: "the software should self fix").** `fixRoadRadii`'s only geometric move was a vertex **nudge toward the chord**, which on his fire lane skewed a square entry into a **chamfer no one lays out on a site plan** — and still missed the minimum. **Fixed:** new pure `fitRoadCorners` asks for the class radius outright (never writing back a clamped value as if the user had chosen it — the pathology that left a stored 22.89 ft request on a 50 ft truck route) and, where a corner is starved by a leg running to a road END, **runs that approach out along its own bearing**, bounded by `ROAD_FIX_MAX_EXTEND_FT`. Bearings are preserved, so roads still meet square. `solveRoadCorners` runs **extension first, nudge only as the fallback** — order matters, and the chamfer is why.
- **The bare "!" is gone.** The canvas flag is now a chip that names the remedy — *"needs 5′ more approach"* — with an inline **Fix** that applies it in one click and one undo; the toast says what it did in plain language. Still `data-export="skip"`.
- **Verified on the OWNER'S REAL PLAN, not a mock** (`ui-audit/fixtures/tsakiris-concept-a-live.json`): both flagged corners — the fire lane into employee parking and the truck stub into the 40′ aisle — clear on one click each, each road gaining ~5 ft of approach into pavement that already existed, with every bearing unchanged. `ui-audit/verify-corner-selffix.mjs` drives it end-to-end and exits non-zero on any leftover mark or page error.
- **Sandbox-verified:** new `test/roadCornerFit.test.js` (16 cases — shares, the neighbouring-fillet invariant that justifies the half rule, the shortfall readout, extension bounds, sharp-corner and no-op guards) + `e2e/road-corner-selffix.spec.js` asserting the chip names its remedy, clears on click, and does **not** skew the alignment. Two prior tests that encoded the half-leg clamp as truth were updated with the reason. Full suite + build + doc gates green; `e2e/road-tee-oblique.spec.js` 6/6 and `ui-audit/verify-junction-obstacles.mjs` 4/4 still pass.
- **Live-verify (V458):** on his signed-in plan, both amber chips read a remedy and clear on one click; the fire-lane entry stays square.

### B1012 — The road cleanup ran on only ONE of the two read paths, so it did nothing on a signed-in element-synced plan `[Site Planner / sync]` (bug) #site-planner #road #sync  *(owner live-verify 2026-07-25 immediately after B1010 deployed: "i just tried it, doesnt seem like its working" — and he was right. Minted **B1012 / V457**.)*
`[ ]` **⏳ merged — V457 PENDING (Verify: live — `Blocker: real-data`).** B1010 was correct and still invisible.
- **Root cause, measured on the live app + the production rows.** A site reaches the canvas by TWO paths: the site-record blob, normalised by `siteModel.migrate` (where B1008/B1010's `dedupeRoadVertices` cleanup lives), and — for a signed-in, ELEMENT-SYNCED site — the `site_elements` ROWS, folded to a model by `elementRows.rowsToModel`, which imported nothing and applied no migration at all. The owner is element-synced. So: his localStorage site cache showed the cleaned road (18 pts) because that path migrates, while the SERVER ROW still held **24 points with the debris vertex intact** and the canvas rendered from it — the flag still sat on `e38duuwgj:6` at world (231.66, 298.10), the debris vertex, even though the cache's vertex 6 was (301, 450). Proven by reading the flag's rendered position back through the view transform and diffing it against both stores plus the Supabase row.
- **Fix:** `rowsToModel` now runs the SAME exported `migrateRoads` as the blob path, inside the fold rather than at a call site — so a future read path cannot skip it by construction. This is the general lesson from the bug itself: two code paths for the same data will drift unless they share the function.
- **Sandbox-verified:** `test/roadNetwork.test.js` +3 cases — the rows fold collapses debris, a clean road is untouched (no churn), and **both paths produce byte-identical geometry** from the same input, which is the invariant that was broken. Full suite 5347 + lint + build + doc gates green.
- **Live-verify (V457):** on his signed-in plan, the flag at the pond junction clears and the junction renders from cleaned geometry.


### B1009 — Junction pavement ran UNDER buildings, the target's outline was ruled across the drive mouth, and a corner clamped below its civil minimum said nothing `[Site Planner / road]` (bug) #site-planner #road #drive  *(owner live-verify 2026-07-25 on the deployed B1005/B1006/B1008 build, reading his own Tsakiris / Concept A plan: "road obv cant go under the building"; a screenshot of the truck-court entrance with the court's edge line drawn straight across it; and the employee-parking entrance "just doesn't look right... you would never shape it like that". Minted **B1009 / V455** via `git fetch origin main && npm run next-id -- --against-main`.)*
`[ ]` **⏳ merged — V455 PENDING (Verify: live — `Blocker: real-data` + PDF/export parity).** Four fixes; the third is the one that matters.
- **Pavement under a building — measured, not inferred.** Sampling the RENDERED road-network path with `SVGGeometryElement.isPointInFill` over each building footprint found ~100 sf of curb-return pavement under EACH of the two dock dog-ears (`e62sascnh`, `e64cglxqv`). B959's own comment admitted the design — "it never reaches the building — that's also z-order-guarded" — i.e. it relied on the building PAINTING OVER the pavement. That hides an overlap instead of preventing it: the pavement still exists, still counts in the paved-area total, and reads off the plan as a drive running under a dock. **Fixed:** `buildingRunLimit` clamps each junction's along-edge reach to stop short of the first building footprint on the junction's OPEN side (with a small clearance), folded into `throughAvailPos/Neg` for BOTH `driveJunctionsOf` and `teeJunctionsOf`. Pavement can no longer be under a building by construction.
- **The target rect's outline drawn across the drive mouth.** Road↔road junctions dissolve (B1006/NEW-2), but a road teeing into a PARKING FIELD or TRUCK COURT can't — the target is a different element with its own fill. So its outline was still ruled straight across the opening. **Fixed:** `roadNet.outlineCuts` maps each drive target to the dissolved pavement that crosses it; `renderElPx` then paints that rect's FILL with no stroke and draws its outline as four edges trimmed by `clipPolylineOutside`. One continuous curb around the entrance, no line across it.
- **A corner clamped below its civil minimum, silently — the root cause of "that shape is wrong".** `arcCorner` feasibility-clamps a corner's radius to half the shorter adjacent leg. That clamp is geometrically required (without it two corners overrun and the strip self-intersects) but it happened with NOTHING said: on the owner's plan a fire lane whose corner carries the 28 ft inside radius its class requires was DRAWING AT 11 ft, and a truck stub at 23 ft against a 50 ft class minimum. Not cosmetic — a compliance defect, and the visible cause of the shape he flagged. **Fixed:** new pure `roadCornerRadii` / `roadRadiusConflicts` expose requested-vs-drawn per interior vertex, and a `road-radius-flags` layer marks the offending vertex ON THE CANVAS (amber, `<title>` explaining that the leg is too short to hold the turn) instead of hiding the conflict behind selecting the road. `data-export="skip"` — review chrome never rides into a consultant's PDF. The geometry is NOT silently re-cut: resolving it is a layout decision (move the corner / lengthen the leg), which is the owner's call, not the renderer's.
- **Curb return sized by the DESIGN VEHICLE OF THE DRIVE.** `DRIVE_RETURN_SEED[kind]` keyed the return off what the drive was driving INTO; it now derives from the drive's own road class via `classReturnRadius` — the same source road↔road tees already use — with a truck-court floor. A fire lane entering employee parking still has to turn an apparatus; an auto aisle into the same field does not. The old per-junction stored seed also went stale: a value stamped onto `driveTee` at connect time kept driving geometry long after the default changed.
- **Sandbox-verified:** `ui-audit/verify-junction-obstacles.mjs` drives the REAL canvas against the owner's real element set and asserts all three through the rendered SVG (zero building overlap by point-in-fill sampling, the target outline emitted as interrupted segments, both sub-minimum corners flagged) — 4/4 green. `test/roadNetwork.test.js` +5 pure cases for the clamp exposure. Full suite 5339 + lint + build + MAP/index/doc gates green.

### B996 — NEW-26: mitigation credit must be CONNECTED-by-default (the flood backs in through the pond's own outfall), gated only on an explicitly gated / absent outfall — supersedes the B990 berm-seal + role gates `[Site Planner / stormwater · pond]` (bug) #site-planner #yield #pond #floodplain  *(owner directive 2026-07-24, Tsakiris — "the berm-seals-the-pond rule is wrong as a DEFAULT because every detention pond is hydraulically connected to the floodplain through its own outfall (the outlet drawn at 145.1′ the app already routes storms through). During a flood the receiving water backs IN through that outfall unless deliberately gated." Supersedes B990/NEW-21 and outranks NEW-24/25. Minted **B996 / V448** via `npm run next-id -- --against-main`; ships on #799 fresh main. Branch `claude/yield-pond-properties-v3-mfqz2x`.)*
AUDIT-FIRST: B990 correctly unified the credit into ONE shared `mitigationCredit(det, split)` (so the verdict, the ledger, the optimizer, and the ⚡ card can never disagree) — that stays. The bug was the two GATES it chose: (a) a berm whose rim clears the flood WSE was treated as SEALING the pond ("berm-sealed" → 0 credit) and (b) a Detention-role pond's below-flood cut was withheld until designated Mitigation/Hybrid ("role-detention" → 0). Both are wrong physics: the flood reaches the below-flood cut through the pond's OUTFALL (the same outlet the pond drains through, and the app already routes storms through), not over the berm, and the physics doesn't care what role we labeled the pond. Fixed: `mitigationCredit` now credits `bands.mitigationCandidateCf` (the below-WSE storage above the permanent pool/floor, reachable through the outfall invert) BY DEFAULT for any anchored pond with a below-flood cut; credit is withheld only when (a) `split.outletGated` / `det.outletGated` is set — a flap valve / backflow preventer keeps the flood out (reason "outlet-gated"), or (b) `split.hasOutfall === false` — an isolated pit with no outlet (reason "no-outfall"). Neither role nor berm gates any more. A new pond-inspector toggle **"Outfall gated (flap valve, no floodplain backflow)"** stores `det.outletGated` (default off = connected); `pondSplitFor` stamps `outletGated` on both anchored returns; `sizePondForTargets` reads it. The credited cut carries an honest ASSUMED flag (verdict/card + the Mitigation-detail note: "Credited cut assumes an OPEN (ungated) outfall connection; engineer confirms." with a ⓘ citing **BKDD Rules 22-01** as the citation target, unverified until the code text lands; some districts require a dedicated opening or restrict in-pond credit). Expected Tsakiris outcome: the 0.2 ac-ft mitigation SHORT clears via the outfall-connected credit (16.9 ac-ft below flood dwarfs the 0.2 requirement) — the strip flips to OK with the card/verdict still in agreement. The NEW-17/B982 berm-FILL side of the ledger is untouched (the berm ring is still fill that displaces storage; this only fixes the CREDIT side). Verify: live — `Blocker: real-data` (on the signed-in Tsakiris pond the Mitigation strip reads OK, the card/verdict agree, and ticking "Outfall gated" flips it back to a SHORT with the gated explanation). Sandbox-verified: `test/mitigationCredit.test.js` rewritten for the connected-default model (ungated any-role credits, `outletGated`→0 "outlet-gated", `hasOutfall:false`→0 "no-outfall", the berm no longer gates, ledger+optimizer agree, the SitePlanner wiring: toggle + stamp + BKDD assumption copy); `test/pondLedger.test.js` outfall-gate block; full suite (5280) + build + `ui-audit/verify-panel-em-dash.mjs` green. V448 records the on-Tsakiris click-through.

### B982 — NEW-17: pond berm fill in the mapped floodplain reads ~0 in the mitigation requirement (outward-vs-inward geometry) `[Site Planner / stormwater · floodplain]` (bug) #site-planner #yield #pond #floodplain  *(owner-authored NEW-17, 2026-07-24, Tsakiris project smrjdgmlinea — "I'm clearly filling more than the 0.01 ac-ft of floodplain with berm." ### B987 — R1: pond recovers to NORMAL (dry-weather) tailwater between storms, not the 100-yr level — dead storage = below NORMAL tailwater `[Site Planner / stormwater · pond]` (bug) #site-planner #yield #pond #floodplain  *(owner PR-R "R1" chat 2026-07-24, shipped PR-R5 with the coincident-storm policy flagged ASSUMED per the owner's "ship it now with the assumption flagged" order; B987 / V443. Branch `claude/yield-pond-properties-v3-mfqz2x`.)*
Fixed (model change to the usable/dead split): the permanent DEAD-storage floor is now the NORMAL (dry-weather) tailwater the pond recovers to between storms (`deadFloorFt`, the receiving channel flowline / normal-depth from the tailwater ladder), NOT the 100-yr flood WSE. `pondGeom.bandedStorage`/`usablePondVolume` take a `coincidentStorm` flag (default **false**): by default the whole recovered water column above the normal-tailwater floor is usable detention, and the 100-yr flood WSE only feeds routing / outfall checks. The flood WSE floors usable ONLY under a jurisdiction's coincident-storm policy (`coincidentStorm:true`). ### B975 — Outfall TAILWATER source ladder + never-grade root-cause fix + Drainage district surfaced (PR-N / grading DECISION 4 + FOLD IN + PR-O O5) `[Site Planner / yield · pond · floodplain · gis]` (bug) #site-planner #yield #pond #floodplain #gis #ui  *(owner grading-engine brief DECISION 4 + "PR-O O5" chat 2026-07-23 — "it's still not working": the receiving-water/flood value was defaulting to SITE GRADE (153.1 == grade at the Tsakiris pond), a placeholder that DEADLOCKS every pond by construction (outflow can't fall below tailwater, inflow can't rise above grade → usable storage squeezed to zero → "not buildable"), and it hit hardest on this FEMA Zone A site where the fallback kicks in. Minted **B975 / V433** via `npm run next-id -- --against-main`; ships on B974's fresh main. Branch `claude/yield-pond-properties-v3-mfqz2x`. DEDUPE-FIRST — O5 is the acceptance bar for the grading brief's tailwater (DECISION 4); net-new ladder, no prior item sources tailwater from real channel data. O1-O4 (copy/consistency) + the FFE/balance grading engine are SEPARATE follow-up PRs.)*
`[x]` **FIXED + sandbox/real-browser-verified. Parks in ⏳ Verify (Verify: live) → V433 for the live sources + the Tsakiris re-eval against real below-grade tailwater.**
- **O5 root cause (the deadlock):** the outfall tailwater came from `estTailwaterElevFt` = flood WSE, else SITE GRADE. On Zone A the flood WSE is itself a grade-boundary estimate, so tailwater ≈ grade; with the outlet at the pond floor (below grade) the outfall gate ALWAYS fired → false "not buildable" with mostly dead storage. FIX: the outfall discharges into the receiving CHANNEL (cut below grade), never the floodplain sheet and NEVER site grade.
- **The ladder (`lib/tailwaterSource.js`, pure + injectable):** `deriveTailwater` picks by priority — district channel design WSE → FEMA/USGS InFRM est-BFE (webapps.usgs.gov/infrm/estbfe) → USGS gauge → normal-depth (Manning's) → terrain channel-flowline — ALWAYS EST + source-tagged. A `gradeFt` guard REJECTS any candidate equal to site grade (a placeholder leak); with no real below-grade source it returns UNKNOWN (null), an honest blank, never grade. `resolveTailwater` is the async orchestrator (injectable fetchers, graceful degradation like K7); `normalDepthWse` + `channelTerrainWse` are the estimators. Live InFRM/BKDD/USGS/terrain fetch is egress-blocked → V433.
- **Wiring:** `estTailwaterElevFt` reworked to never return grade (channel-only); ONE shared `pondTailwaterResult(el, gradeFt)` helper (override → ladder → UNKNOWN) feeds the buildable envelope, the PR-L section, and the pond panel — so nothing disagrees. With no source the outfall gate can't fire on a grade placeholder → the false deadlock is BROKEN (the seed pond now reads "Buildable", was "not buildable"). The "Receiving water" field shows "needs channel data" honestly instead of a grade placeholder.
- **FOLD IN — Drainage district group:** a new "Drainage district" pond-inspector group surfaces which district governs (the resolved BKDD overlay), its criteria (freeboard, max side slope — SourceTag CODE/UNVERIFIED), the district detail, and the outfall receiving-water SOURCE (value + EST + source label, or "needs channel data"). No more silent server-side-only district logic.
- **Tests:** `test/tailwaterSource.test.js` (22: priority ordering, the never-grade guard, `channelTerrainWse` below-grade-only, `normalDepthWse` monotonicity + non-physical guards, `resolveTailwater` graceful degradation, and the O5 deadlock-broken integration — grade tailwater fires the outfall gate, UNKNOWN does not, a real below-grade value discharges); `test/pondScreeningDefaults.test.js` (estTailwaterElevFt never grade); `test/pondV3PrI.test.js` rewired; `ui-audit/verify-district-tailwater.mjs` drives the live inspector (group renders, tailwater reads "needs channel data", NOT the 153.1 grade placeholder).

- Origin: filed 2026-07-22 from chat ("PR-D") + the D5 amendment ("max berm is only dictated by whether the site can drain to the pond").
- **D1 — inward berm geometry.** New pure `lib/inwardBerm.js`: the drawn polygon is the FIXED OUTER TOE; a rim `h` ft above grade builds the berm INWARD (crest = toe inset by `extSlope·h`), so the water surface + usable storage SHRINK with diminishing returns up to a GEOMETRIC CEILING where the crest pinches closed. `pondGeom.bandedStorage`/`usablePondVolume` take a `gradeFt` and, when bermed, recompute every band on the inset crest ring (the classic drawn-ring model is untouched when `gradeFt` is null or the rim is at/below grade). The `pondSizing` solver is threaded `gradeFt` too, and `solveTobRaise` now SCANS for the target / peak because the inward usable is NON-monotonic (it rises then falls to zero at the pinch) — the old monotonic assumption made Optimize max the rim out at the geometric ceiling (an absurd ~100-ft berm); it now stops at the smallest berm that closes the requirement, else the interior peak.
- **D2 — rows/land-use flip.** Land take = the FIXED drawn footprint (the "incl. berm ring" outward wording is gone; land take never exceeds water). The pond inspector shows "Water area" (shrinking) + a new "Berm ring" (EST) row, water + berm ring summing to the footprint; the LAND USE Pond legend title reads "{water} ac water + {ring} ac berm (inside {total} ac footprint)". - **D3 — inward berm ring on the plan.** The warm-earth hatched ring (`pat-berm`, #b08d57 ~45%) now draws BETWEEN the drawn outline and the inset crest — INSIDE the polygon, over the pond so water shows only in the crest hole — with a "berm {h} ft" tag. Replaces C4's outward apron.
- **D4 — function-based pond label.** New `pondLedger.pondDisplayName`/`pondDisplayNameFor` maps the resolved purpose → noun (Detention / Mitigation / "Detention + Mitigation" Pond), used at every render site that names a pond (element-panel chrome header, map/canvas label, Yield per-pond row, RowInfo, context-menu header). The stored element type/id stays "pond"; only the display string changes. A mitigation pond is no longer mislabeled "Detention Pond".
- **D5 — computed berm cap (no user input).** The C2 "Max berm (ft)" input + its plumbing + the "(your Max berm setting)" toast copy are DELETED. The cap = the smaller of the DRAINAGE cap (runoff must reach the pond by gravity: max WSE = the lowest controlling inflow grade − a 0.5-ft inflow head allowance; max rim + freeboard; needs real per-point terrain, else null) and the GEOMETRIC ceiling (D1). A cap-bound solve names the binding constraint in plain English (`bermCapProposalNote`: drainage-bound vs geometry-bound). Without terrain (no berm-above-grade to cap), the solver falls back to the conservative screening clamp rather than the raw geometric ceiling.

An AUDIT-FIRST trace found there is NO code linkage: Library filing writes ONLY to the doc-review stores (doc_reviews / file_facts / the storage bucket), never to the site model's `sheetOverlays`; the References panel renders only `sheetOverlays`; and the only overlay CREATOR (`addOverlayFile`) has solely Site-Planner-local drop/pick callers. - **Decision:** option (b) — KEEP them independent (a Library holds many NON-spatial docs — title commitments, MEP sets — that must never auto-splat onto the map; auto-creating a map Reference from every Library upload would be wrong), and make the separation CLEAR so a user isn't surprised. - **Verified (sandbox — ATTEMPT-BEFORE-YOU-PARK):** the new guard test (5 assertions) green; **headless real-canvas (logged-out, `vite preview`):** added an overlay to the References panel → the separation note "Map references are managed here, separate from your Library documents…" renders; zero page errors.
