### B914 — Review resume leaks one project's last loose PDF (its "upload didn't finish" banner) onto every OTHER project's Review tab `[Doc Review]` (bug) #doc-review #persistence #ui  *(owner-reported 2026-07-21 during V331/V332/V333 live testing: a "Goose Creek PI APPROVED PLANS…" large-file banner appeared on Mesa AND ZZ-VERIFY-TEST Review tabs — two unrelated projects, not on Goose Creek itself — and blocked opening a new drawing there. Minted **B914 / V386** via `npm run next-id`. Provisional.)*
`[x]` **FIXED + sandbox-verified this session (green build · 17-test unit lib incl. the exact leak matrix · logged-out headless smoke of the clean empty state). Parks in ⏳ Verify (Verify: live — cross-project resume needs the real signed-in projects) → V386.** A large drawing opened loose (via **Open**, never filed to a project) whose cloud upload didn't finish was resuming onto the Review tab of ANY project that had no "last drawing" of its own — showing that file's stuck upload banner and its name in the Reviews field, and (because a stuck review was "active") swallowing the next **Open**. It correctly did NOT show on projects that already remember their own last drawing (Bain, Goose Creek), which is why it only reproduced on Mesa and ZZ-VERIFY-TEST.
- Verify: live
- Origin: filed 2026-07-21 from chat (owner, during V331/V332/V333 verification).
- **Root cause (`DocReview.jsx` boot-resume, the B667 per-project resume machinery):** on mount the resume loop walks candidates from `resolveResume` — the URL's project's own last-doc first, then the LEGACY-GLOBAL "last, anywhere" pointer. Its wrong-project guard was `projectId && rec && rec.projectId && rec.projectId !== projectId`. The leading `rec.projectId &&` short-circuits to *allowed* whenever the loaded review has **no** projectId — i.e. an **unfiled** loose PDF. So on a named-project route with no per-project entry, the loop fell through to the legacy global and resumed that unfiled orphan, leaking it (and its banner) onto that project. A project with its own entry never reached the legacy candidate → no leak there.
- **Fix:** a new pure, unit-tested helper `resumeAllowedForRoute(routeProjectId, recProjectId)` in `lib/lastDoc.js` — **no route → resume anything; a NAMED route → resume ONLY that project's own review (exact match), so a projectId-less orphan (null !== routeProjectId) is rejected.** The boot-resume guard now uses it. A project's own map entry always carries that project's id (`writeLastDoc` keys by the doc's `meta.projectId`), so a legitimate per-project resume is never blocked; an unfiled loose PDF still resumes freely when Review is opened with **no** project in the route (its "" bucket).
- **Secondary stuck-UI (same report, same fix commit):** the "Pick exactly two PDFs to compare…" empty-state hint (`err`) persisted across project switches and after a CANCELLED compare picker. Now: `onPickCompare` only complains when files were actually chosen (a cancel leaves the hint clear); `resetSingle` clears `err` on every switch-to-empty / New; the "⇄ Compare revisions…" button clears any stale hint on open.
- **DEDUPE-FIRST:** searched Open / ⏳ Verify / Done for resume / cross-project / lastDoc / leak / orphan. Net-new defect — a hole in **B667** (⏳ Verify — "Review remembers the last document PER PROJECT + the resume self-clobber fix", the feature this patches; a relative, not a dupe: B667 built the per-project memory + fixed self-clobber but didn't guard the legacy-global fallback against a projectId-less record). Unrelated to B686 (non-PDF resume bar) / B448 (dropped-bytes cache).
- **Verified (sandbox):** `test/lastDoc.test.js` — 3 new `resumeAllowedForRoute` cases (no-route allows anything; named route exact-match only; named route BLOCKS a null/undefined-projectId orphan — the exact leak) on top of the existing 14 (17 total, all green). Logged-out headless smoke of `#/markup`: the Review empty state renders "No drawing open" with the three buttons, NO phantom compare hint, NO stuck banner, 0 page errors. Full suite (4686+3) + lint 0 errors + build green; `MAP.md` regenerated (new `lastDoc.js` export).
- **⏳ V386 (live, planyr.io — SIGNED IN, real projects):** with a loose large PDF last-opened globally, visit the Review tab of a project that has never had a drawing (Mesa / a scratch project) → it shows the clean "No drawing open" empty state (NOT the other project's banner), and **Open** works normally. A project that DOES remember its own last drawing still reopens it.
- **Recurrence — round 2 (2026-07-21, Cowork live re-test found round-1 incomplete; fixed same session):** the leak STILL reproduced on Mesa's Review tab (the "Goose Creek…" banner + Reviews-field name) even though the `doc_reviews` fetch correctly resolved to Mesa's OWN doc (`id=eq.rvmqoihur10mmbv`, clean server title "Mesa - Civil"). Root cause: `resumeAllowedForRoute` is correct, but the boot-resume effect (`DocReview.jsx`, `[]` deps) called it with its **mount-time `projectId` closure**. On a deep link the `projectId` prop arrives a beat after mount, so the effect's captured route is still `null` while a slow legacy-global orphan's `loadReview()` is in flight → `resumeAllowedForRoute(null, …)` waved the projectId-less orphan through, and because its await settled LAST it superseded the correct per-project doc the project-switch effect had already opened, re-painting the orphan's stuck banner/name onto Mesa's route. Round-1 (mount-time-Mesa) worked; the late-route deep-link case did not. **Fix:** the resume loop now (a) guards on a live `routeIdRef.current` — a ref mirroring the `projectId` prop every render — instead of the stale closure, so once the route resolves to Mesa the orphan is rejected (`Mesa !== null`); and (b) `return`s early if `openInFlightRef.current` shows a route-driven open already owns the outcome. Verified: full suite (4748) + lint 0 errors + build green; DocReview stays its own lazy chunk. This is a React effect-timing race (can't boot headless — doc-review needs signed-in real data), so V386 stays ⏳ for the signed-in cross-project click-through.
### B918 — Callout text overflows its box in Document Review `[Doc Review]` (bug) #markup #doc-review  *(owner-reported 2026-07-21 from chat, with a screenshot from the SITE PLANNER map ("0 Mueschke Rd / Concept A"). Minted **B918 / V389** via `npm run next-id -- --against-main`, alongside sibling **B919**. **SCOPE CORRECTION (this session):** the owner's screenshot was the Site Planner map, whose callout overflow was ALREADY fixed on `main` by **B913**'s `calloutLayout` (auto-size + word-wrap) — re-confirmed live-headless this session, the box encloses long-word + multi-line text. The SEPARATE Document Review shared-markup engine (`src/shared/markup/`) still drew ONE unwrapped `<text>` line and DID still overflow; this item is that remaining half. An earlier stale patch bundled both as "B910/B911" against a pre-B913 tree — re-integrated cleanly here.)*
`[x]` **IMPLEMENTED + unit verified this session. Parks in ⏳ Verify (Verify: live — export parity, once a Doc Review export exists) → V389.**
- Verify: live
- Origin: filed 2026-07-21 from chat
- **DEDUPE-FIRST:** searched Open / ⏳ Verify / Done for "callout" / "overflow" / `#markup` — the Site Planner half is **B913** (shipped); this is the Doc Review shared-engine half, not a duplicate. Reuses B913's wrap approach through the shared `textWrap.js`.

### B907 — Civil-engineering roadmap #7: tie detention SIZING to LAND TAKE + EARTHWORK $ `[Site Planner / Pond]` (feature) #site-planner #pond  *(owner-reported 2026-07-19 from chat — seventh of the queued civil-engineering roadmap (#1 B903, #2 B904, #3 B905): the engine now sizes detention well (compound outlet, method-by-area, computed Tc) but a sized pond's real cost — in acreage consumed and excavation dollars — was still disconnected from the Yield land breakdown and the Earthwork cost card. Scope narrowed to the two GENUINE gaps that reading turned up. Parks in ⏳ Verify (Verify: live) → V381.**
- Verify: live
- Origin: owner-reported 2026-07-19 from chat
- **DEDUPE-FIRST:** searched Open/⏳ Verify/Done for `#pond` + "land take"/"earthwork"/"excavation"/"footprint" — net-new; builds on B902–B905 without touching their outlet/routing/Tc math.
- **AUDIT-FIRST finding (the reason this shipped narrower than the brief's framing implied):** the brief described land-take and earthwork-$ as features to build from scratch. Reading the actual code showed otherwise — `YieldPanel`'s land donut already computes `pondArea`/`detPct` from real drawn pond rings (never hardcoded to 0), and the Earthwork cost card already has a "Pond excavation" line priced off the user's own $/CY bid with `{code:"plan"}` provenance. The real, unaddressed gaps: (1) that excavation line always prices the FULL basin cut, even for a pond that reuses an existing depression via the "Expand this pond" flow — explicitly admitted in the card's own caption ("the full basin cut, top of bank → achievable floor"); (2) there was no forward-looking estimate of how much MORE land a detention shortfall would take before a pond is drawn or enlarged to cover it.
- **New `lib/pondGeom.js` functions, both pure:** `incrementalExcavationCf(ring, det)` nets a pond's current-geometry cut against `det.baseline` (the pre-expansion ring snapshot the existing "Expand this pond" flow already captures for its own label rendering, repurposed here) — falls back to the full cut when there's no baseline (a from-scratch pond), never fabricates a negative number, ignores a malformed baseline. `detentionLandTakeEstimate({ requiredAcFt, providedUsableCf, avgDepthFt })` turns the site's existing required-vs-provided detention deficit into a screening footprint (footprint ≈ deficit volume / a typical assumed pond depth) — returns `null` (never a fabricated estimate) when there's no real shortfall.
- **Wired in (`SitePlanner.jsx`):** the pond-ledger build loop now computes `incrementalExcavationCf` per pond and carries a new `excavationIncremental` flag; the Earthwork card's "Pond excavation" row relabels to "Pond excavation (incremental)" and its Basis popover explains the netting whenever ANY basin in the plan reuses an existing pond. `YieldPanel` computes a `detentionLandTakeEstimate` off the same `detReq`/`providedUsableCf` figures the existing "raise TOB" berm-apply screen already reads, rendered as a `WatchOutChip` ("Detention shortfall ≈ +N ac more land — screening estimate") directly under the land donut — deliberately OUTSIDE the pie's real percentage math, so it never double-counts or unbalances the pie (guardrail honored: the pie still nets to 100% exactly as before, since this is an advisory about land NOT YET drawn, not a slice of land already accounted for).
- **New criterion, criteria-configurable, not an inline constant:** `screeningPondDepthFt` (default 8 ft, matching the codebase's existing 8-ft screening-depth convention elsewhere) added to every jurisdiction row in `detentionCriteria.js`, threaded through `criteriaFor()`, overridable like every other criterion — this is the ONLY number the land-take estimate uses to turn a volume shortfall into a footprint.

- **New `lib/timeOfConcentration.js` — the Kirpich Tc calculator.** `kirpichTcMin({ lengthFt, slopeFtPerFt, imperviousPct, urbanAdjustment, floorMin })` implements the published formula (Tc = 0.0078·L^0.77·S^-0.385) with a linear impervious-scaled urban adjustment (no adjustment at 0% impervious, the full adjustment factor — default 0.4, the commonly-cited paved-channel reduction — at 100%) and a configurable floor (default 10 min, "near today's placeholder so results don't jump unreasonably," per the brief). `estimateFlowPathLengthFt({ areaAcres, kFactor })` screening-estimates the flow-path length from the contributing area alone (L≈k·√area, default k=1.5) when a real traced flow path isn't available — which, honestly, is ALWAYS the case in this stage's actual wiring (see below). ### B904 — Civil-engineering upgrade #2 (STAGE 1 of 2): NRCS Type III design-storm hyetograph + Rational-vs-NRCS method-by-area guardrail `[Site Planner / Pond]` (feature) #site-planner #pond  *(owner-reported 2026-07-19 from chat — second of the queued civil-engineering roadmap (#1 was B903): the engine sizes detention with the Modified Rational method regardless of tributary area, which silently stops being valid once a watershed outgrows it, with no signal to the user. Minted **B904 / V379** via `npm run next-id -- --against-main`.)*
`[x]` **IMPLEMENTED + unit + headless-e2e verified this session — STAGE 1 of the owner's own explicit two-stage split (their brief named this exact fallback): the hyetograph generator + the CN excess-rainfall step + the method-by-area selector + honest UI flagging all ship now; the true NRCS unit-hydrograph inflow wired into the #712/#903 level-pool routing pass is STAGE 2, a follow-on. Parks in ⏳ Verify (Verify: live) → V379.**
- Verify: live
- Origin: owner-reported 2026-07-19 from chat
- **DEDUPE-FIRST:** searched Open/⏳ Verify/Done for `#pond` + "hyetograph"/"Type III"/"method-by-area"/"unit hydrograph" — net-new; builds on B900/B901/B902/B903 (all four's e2e specs re-verified passing against this build) without touching the routing/outlet-solver math those shipped.
- **New `lib/hyetograph.js` — the NRCS Type III design-storm shape.** `TYPE_III_MASS_CURVE`, a transcribed dimensionless cumulative-fraction table (the Gulf Coast / SE-Texas distribution — a broader, more gradual peak than Type II's sharp spike, reflecting the region's slower tropical systems), same `secondarySource`/transcription honesty convention as the existing Atlas-14 IDF table (`DESIGN_STORMS`, `detentionRules.js`). `buildTypeIIIHyetograph({ totalDepthIn, durationHr, dtMin })` spreads a total design-storm depth over time at any duration (native 24-hr calibration; a shorter duration rescales the same dimensionless curve and is explicitly caveated as a screening simplification). New `designStorm24hrDepthIn()` (`detentionRules.js`) reads a new 1440-min row added to `DESIGN_STORMS.periods` for every return period (2/10/25/100-yr ≈ 4.3/6.9/8.4/13.0 in, same area-representative transcription as the existing 5–180-min rows) — so the hyetograph's total depth comes from the SAME cited IDF lookup the rest of the engine already uses, never a second, disagreeing source.
- **`lib/curveNumber.js`'s new `excessRainfallSeries()`** turns a rainfall hyetograph into a runoff (rainfall-excess) hyetograph: the standard NRCS step of applying the existing TR-55 cumulative equation (`runoffDepthIn`) at each timestep's CUMULATIVE rainfall, then differencing consecutive values for the incremental excess each timestep contributes. This is the excess-rainfall half of "curve number + hyetograph → hydrograph"; the remaining half (unit-hydrograph convolution, turning an excess-rainfall series in inches into a runoff HYDROGRAPH in cfs) is genuinely the larger, more error-prone piece and is what Stage 2 builds.
- **New `lib/detentionMethod.js` — the method-by-area GUARDRAIL.** `selectDetentionMethod({ areaAcres, criteria })` picks Rational (Q=C·i·A, valid for small quick-responding areas) vs. NRCS (the correct tool once a watershed is too big for a peak-flow-only method) against a **criteria-configurable** ceiling — NOT a hardcoded magic number: new `rationalMethodMaxAcres` criterion (default 200 ac, the industry screening rule of thumb) added to every jurisdiction row in `detentionCriteria.js` (`waller`/`bkdd`/`fortbend`/`harris`/`coh`/`montgomery`/`chambers`/`generic`), threaded through `criteriaFor()`, overridable exactly like every other criterion (a different county manual can set its own ceiling). Returns `routingIsProxy:true` when NRCS is indicated — an honest signal that the routed numbers the pond inspector shows still ride the Rational proxy until Stage 2 lands, never silently glossed over.
- **Surfaced in the pond inspector's RATE CONTROL section** (`SitePlanner.jsx`, the same surface B902/B903 already own): a quiet caption "Method: Modified Rational (tributary area N ac, within the 200-ac screening range)" when comfortably under the ceiling; a loud `WatchOutChip` (reusing the existing B895 amber ⚠ pattern, not a new component) — "Tributary area (N ac) exceeds the Rational method's screening range (≤200 ac) — NRCS unit-hydrograph indicated; the routing above still uses the Rational-method proxy" — when over, with the full method-transition explanation + the "confirm with HEC-HMS" honesty framing in the hover detail. The Yield panel's separate Detention card is NOT yet touched — deferred to Stage 2 alongside the real routing wire-up (a disclosed scope cut, not an oversight).
- **Named rules:** LOUD-FAILURE (hyetograph/excess-rainfall/method-selector all return `null`/`method:null` on bad inputs, never a fabricated storm or pick), DEDUPE-FIRST, MODULE-SCOPE-COMPONENTS (no new components — `WatchOutChip` reused as-is).
- **Verified (sandbox/headless):** full unit suite green (**4613 tests**, incl. 11 new `hyetograph.test.js` tests matching the published Type III cumulative fractions at named time points + monotonicity + the mid-storm-concentration signature; 5 new `excessRainfallSeries` tests in `curveNumber.test.js`; 6 new `detentionMethod.test.js` tests incl. the criteria-configurable-ceiling case; 2 new `detentionRules.test.js` tests for the 24-hr depth row); lint 0 errors; build green; `MAP.md` regenerated (2 new files, 2 changed exports). **Both UI states reproduced live against a real build** with new `e2e/pond-detention-method.spec.js` (2 specs, logged out): (a) a 15-ac tributary area shows the quiet Rational-method caption, no watch-out; (b) a 350-ac area (over the default 200-ac ceiling) shows the loud method-transition watch-out. The sibling `e2e/pond-outlet-render.spec.js` (B900), `pond-outlet-clear.spec.js` (B901), `pond-outlet-autosize.spec.js` (B902), and `pond-outlet-compound.spec.js` (B903) — 13 specs total — all re-verified passing against this build, zero regression to any of the four prior fixes.

### B903 — Civil-engineering upgrade #1: MULTI-STAGE OUTLET + ALL-STORMS-AT-ONCE Post ≤ Pre (a single orifice could silently fail a storm it wasn't sized for) `[Site Planner / Pond]` (feature) #site-planner #pond #ui  *(owner-reported 2026-07-19 from chat — first of a roadmap of civil-engineering upgrades, explicitly "the biggest correctness gain for the detention engine": B902's one-click auto-size sized a SINGLE floor orifice to one governing storm; a real detention pond needs a COMPOUND (stacked) outlet, and Post ≤ Pre must hold at EVERY required return period at once, not just the one the orifice happened to be sized against. Minted **B903 / V378** via `npm run next-id -- --against-main`.)*
`[x]` **IMPLEMENTED + unit + headless-e2e verified this session (all four acceptance checks reproduced against a real build, PLUS a genuine correctness bug found and fixed along the way — see below); parks in ⏳ Verify (Verify: live — real-project-data repro on Waller/Tsakiris) → V378.**
- Verify: live
- Origin: owner-reported 2026-07-19 from chat
- **DEDUPE-FIRST:** searched Open/⏳ Verify/Done for `#pond` + "compound outlet"/"multi-stage"/"overtop" — net-new; builds directly on B900 (crash fix), B901 (clear/persist fix), B902 (one-click auto-size for a single orifice) without regressing any of the three (all three's e2e specs re-verified passing against this build).
- **A REAL CORRECTNESS BUG, confirmed empirically before any fix — exactly the class of bug the brief predicted:** `assessRoutedDetention` (`lib/pondRouting.js`) compared the routed peak to the pre-development allowable, but a routing model that OVERTOPS (the basin fills past top of bank — the routing math has no data above that point, so the reported discharge is CLAMPED there) could still read PASS whenever that clamped, artificially-low discharge number happened to compare ≤ the allowable. Reproduced directly against the real engine: a 300×300 ft, 8-ft pond draining a realistic 45-ac watershed with a single 10-in floor orifice showed the 10-yr storm passing cleanly and the 100-yr storm ALSO reading PASS — while the basin was actively overtopping under the 100-yr inflow. **Fixed:** `pass = routed.routedPeakCfs <= preCfs + PASS_TOL && !routed.overtopped` — an overtopped storm is now ALWAYS a FAIL, with `shortByCfs: null` (never a fabricated cfs number once the comparison itself stops meaning what it looks like it means — LOUD-FAILURE). This is the exact "passes the small storm but fails a larger one, and it doesn't show" defect named in the brief's test (d); pinned by 3 new `assessRoutedDetention` tests using that exact reproduced fixture.
- **1) COMPOUND OUTLET MODEL.** `outletStructure.js`'s stage→discharge summing (`outletDischarge`) already supported an arbitrary-length stage array — the gap was the UI, hard-limited to "one primary orifice/restrictor + one optional weir." Rebuilt as a genuine editable STAGE LIST (`SitePlanner.jsx`): any mix of orifice/weir/restrictor stages, each individually editable (size + invert/crest), with "+ Add orifice"/"+ Add weir" and a per-stage "× Remove." New `sizeWeirForRelease` (`outletStructure.js`, the weir-length inverse of the existing `sizeOrificeForRelease`) plus 4 new tests (`outletStructure.test.js`) confirming a genuine 3-stage compound curve sums correctly and transitions cleanly at each invert/crest (the brief's test (a) — much of this was already covered by an existing 2-stage test; extended to 3 stages + a monotonicity check).
- **2) MULTI-STORM ROUTING + CHECK — already substantially built (worth noting, not re-invented):** `assessRoutedDetention` already looped over EVERY `criteria.requiredStorms` (whatever the active jurisdiction defines — Waller/generic 10/100, BKDD 2/10/100, Harris/FBCDD single 100-yr — nothing hardcoded) and already returned a full `perStorm` array with the allowable, routed peak, peak WSE, and required storage per storm, plus a correctly-OR'd `allPass`. What was missing: the overtopping bug above (a silent false-PASS), and the UI simply never rendered the Peak WSE / Storage columns or a prominent overall verdict — both added now (the table is `STORM | ALLOWABLE | ROUTED | PEAK WSE | STORAGE | PASS/SHORT/OVERTOPS`, with a dedicated "Overall — Post ≤ Pre: PASS — every storm / FAIL" banner that cannot read PASS while any row doesn't).
- **3) AUTO-SIZE SOLVES THE WHOLE STRUCTURE.** New pure `autoSizeCompoundOutlet` (`lib/pondRouting.js`, reuses `rationalPeakCfs`/`assessRoutedDetention`/`sizeOrificeForRelease`/`sizeWeirForRelease` — no new hydrology math): seeds a low-flow orifice at the smallest required storm's pre-development peak (the SAME screening midpoint-head heuristic B902's single-stage sizer used), then iterates — reusing `assessRoutedDetention` itself as the judge, never a parallel routing path — enlarging or SHRINKING whichever stage is responsible for the worst-failing storm (direction matters: overtopping means too little capacity, a rate exceedance without overtopping means too much — getting this backwards was a real bug caught and fixed mid-session, see below) and introducing a control weir the first time a larger storm needs help a bigger orifice alone can't sensibly provide. An emergency spillway (a broad weir at the design water surface / freeboard line) is always present as a safety overflow, sized off the largest storm's unrouted peak — never iterated, since it isn't itself part of the Post ≤ Pre proof. On success: writes the compound outlet, all required storms passing. On infeasibility (bounded at 12 attempts): still writes the best attempt, and reports the WORST still-failing storm honestly — by how much, or that it overtops — pointing at "⚡ Auto-size" (re-solve) or "Expand this pond" (below) as the fix. The "Auto-size detention" / "Propose outlet" button (unchanged label logic from B902 — manual override vs. suggested) now always calls this compound solver; a manual "Allowable release" still meaningfully seeds the solve (an `overrideCfs` param) without overriding what the actual Post ≤ Pre check verifies against.
- **Two solver bugs caught and fixed BEFORE shipping, both found by empirically running the real engine, not assumed correct:** (a) an early growth heuristic grew the RESPONSIBLE stage regardless of failure direction, which for an oversized seed diverged (grew an already-too-permissive orifice even further) instead of converging — fixed by seeding from the full design-column head (matching B902's proven approach) and by making growth direction depend on WHY a storm failed. (b) the solver's own bidirectional growth pushed a orifice's diameter to a physically nonsensical 8 FEET while chasing an extreme drainage-area input — which exposed a real modeling gap in `outletStructure.js`'s simple submerged-orifice equation (head is measured to the CENTROID: invert + half the diameter, so an 8-ft "orifice" reports ZERO flow until the water clears 4 ft of head), producing a nonsensical near-zero routed peak that read as a fabricated PASS. Fixed by capping the orifice's role at a physically sane 48 in (4 ft) — past that the compound structure leans on the control weir instead, which is what a real engineer would do anyway. Pinned by a new regression test (`pondRouting.test.js`) reproducing the exact scenario.
- **4) HONESTY + PROVENANCE — unchanged screening framing, extended.** Every figure still carries the existing screening caveat, per-storm criteria line, and pre-dev-assumption note (runoff coefficient, time of concentration); the suggested-release (i) provenance popover from B902 is untouched. New: the per-storm failure explanation names WHICH storm and WHY (short by N cfs, vs. overtops the basin) rather than a single generic warning banner.
- **Named rules:** LOUD-FAILURE (overtopping forces FAIL, never a fabricated shortfall number once clamped; the solver never fabricates a pass on infeasibility), DEDUPE-FIRST, MODULE-SCOPE-COMPONENTS (no new components — the stage-row renderer is inline JSX inside the existing pond-inspector function, matching the file's established IIFE convention).
- **Verified (sandbox/headless):** full unit suite green (**4589 tests**, incl. 3 new overtopping-fix tests reproducing the exact silent-false-PASS bug + fix, 6 new `autoSizeCompoundOutlet` tests — feasible convergence, genuine 2-stage escalation, single-storm jurisdictions needing no control stage, honest infeasible-failure reporting, refuse-cleanly guards, and the oversized-orifice regression — plus 4 new `outletDischarge`/`sizeWeirForRelease` tests); lint 0 errors; build green; `MAP.md` regenerated (new exports). **All four acceptance checks reproduced live against a real build** with new `e2e/pond-outlet-compound.spec.js` (4 specs, logged out): (a) Auto-size produces a genuine multi-stage outlet (Low-flow orifice + Emergency spillway, at minimum); (b) the per-storm table shows all 5 columns and an overall verdict that can never read PASS while a row doesn't; (c) a real infeasible case (400-ac drainage, 90% impervious, against a small drawn pond) reports an honest FAIL with a specific per-storm shortfall — this is what actually caught both solver bugs above, live, not just in unit tests; (d) stages add/remove by hand. The sibling `e2e/pond-outlet-render.spec.js` (B900, 3 specs — one updated: the removed in-place kind-switch toggle is now exercised via the "+ Restrictor" manual-start button instead, same crash-path coverage), `e2e/pond-outlet-clear.spec.js` (B901, 2 specs), and `e2e/pond-outlet-autosize.spec.js` (B902, 3 specs) all re-verified passing — zero regression to any of the three prior fixes.
- **⏳ V378 (live):** see VERIFICATION.md — the owner will confirm on deployed Tsakiris (Waller jurisdiction, real 52.04-ac drainage area) that Auto-size produces a sensible multi-stage outlet with a per-storm table and an honest overall verdict, then revert their own test edits per their own message. This is stated as #1 of a queued roadmap of civil-engineering upgrades — the next (design-storm hyetograph + method-by-area) is expected in a future session.

### B902 — Make pond detention design genuinely ONE-CLICK: AUTO-SUGGEST the allowable release (pre-development peak) so "Propose outlet" is never a dead greyed button `[Site Planner / Pond]` (feature) #site-planner #pond #ui  *(owner-reported 2026-07-19 from chat, verified live on Tsakiris: for a Post ≤ Pre district that publishes no cfs/ac cap (Waller, Brookshire–Katy DD), "Propose outlet" stayed disabled until the user manually typed an "Allowable release (cfs)" they usually don't know — its own tooltip said "Enter an allowable release (above), or the criteria publish no cfs/ac cap." `[x]` **IMPLEMENTED + unit + headless-e2e verified this session (all three acceptance checks reproduced against a real build — non-empty suggestion, one-click zero-typing outlet+routing, override/clear); parks in ⏳ Verify (Verify: live — real-project-data repro on Waller/Tsakiris) → V377.**
- Verify: live
- Origin: owner-reported 2026-07-19 from chat
- **DEDUPE-FIRST:** searched Open/⏳ Verify/Done for `#pond` + "allowable release"/"propose outlet"/"auto-size" — net-new; distinct from B900 (render crash, fixed) and B901 (clear/persist, fixed) — this is a **usability/dead-end** defect in the same flow, not a correctness bug in either shipped fix.
- **Reuses existing engines only, per the owner's explicit guardrail — no new hydrology math.** `lib/pondRouting.js` already exports `rationalPeakCfs()` (Modified Rational, Q=C·i·A off the transcribed Atlas-14 IDF) — the SAME function `assessRoutedDetention()` calls for the pre-development side of every Post ≤ Pre PASS/SHORT check. New pure export **`suggestedPreDevReleaseCfs({ requiredStorms, areaAcres, runoffC=0.3, tcMin=15 })`** calls it once per the jurisdiction's required design storm (10/100-yr for Waller), returns the smallest (most restrictive) peak as the suggested release, plus the governing storm, the assumptions used, and the full per-storm breakdown — everything the honest "(i)" provenance popover needs. Returns `null` (never a fabricated number) with no required storms or no positive drainage area (LOUD-FAILURE). The pre-dev runoff coefficient (0.3, undeveloped/pasture — the same screening default `assessRoutedDetention` already uses) and 15-min time of concentration are named constants (`DEFAULT_PRE_RUNOFF_C`/`DEFAULT_TC_MIN`, now exported), explicit and overridable via the function's own params — not hidden.
- **One-click, not a second disabled button.** `SitePlanner.jsx`'s RATE CONTROL · POST ≤ PRE section now resolves the outlet-sizing release in priority order: (1) a manual release the user typed, (2) the jurisdiction's published cfs/ac cap × drainage area when one exists, (3) the AUTO-SUGGESTED pre-development peak. The primary button relabels to **"⚡ Auto-size detention"** and enables whenever any tier resolves — for Waller/generic (no cap), that's tier 3, so the button is never dead. ### B901 — Pond outlet flow: "Allowable release (cfs)" could never be CLEARED (typing appended/stuck), and a removed outlet could resurrect on reload `[Site Planner / Pond]` (bug) #site-planner #pond #ui  *(owner-reported 2026-07-18 from chat while cleaning up after the B900 crash hotfix, live on Tsakiris/Concept A: "Allowable release ≈ 15115 cfs (manual)" got stuck after repeated failed clear attempts (Backspace/Delete/Ctrl+A+Delete/triple-click+Delete/End+Backspace all failed), and a proposed outlet removed in the live view came back after a page reload. Minted **B901 / V376** via `npm run next-id -- --against-main`.)*
`[x]` **IMPLEMENTED this session — bug (1) fully headless-verified (reproduced broken, confirmed fixed); bug (2)'s fix parks in ⏳ Verify (Verify: live — the cloud-sync half needs a signed-in session) → V376.**
- Verify: live
- Origin: owner-reported 2026-07-18 from chat
- **DEDUPE-FIRST:** searched Open/⏳ Verify/Done for `#pond` + "clear"/"release"/"outlet persist" — net-new; distinct from **B900** (same flow, different defect — B900 was a hard render crash on `React.Fragment`, this is (1) an input that can't be cleared and (2) a removal that doesn't survive reload for a signed-in session).
- **⚠ OWNER'S TEST DATA NOTE (tracked, not silently dropped):** while reproducing bug (1) live, the owner left a stuck **"Allowable release ≈ 15115 cfs (manual)"** on the real **Tsakiris / Concept A** pond (their own live plan) — this code fix cannot touch that already-saved live data. Per the owner: "once the clear-fix deploys I'll clear it from the app." Nothing further needed from this session on that specific value.
- **Bug (1) root cause — `NumInput` (the shared numeric-field component `SitePlanner.jsx` uses everywhere):** `commit()` treated an EMPTY draft (an intentional clear) identically to unparseable garbage (a typo) — both fell into `clampNum(parseFloat(draft)) == null` → **silently revert to the last committed value, never call `onCommit` at all.** So a field could be typed into but never actually committed to `null` via the keyboard, no matter how it was cleared (Backspace, Delete, Ctrl+A+Delete, triple-click+Delete, End+Backspace — all hit the same silent-revert branch). The reported "1515 → 15115" mangling is this same silent-revert fighting the user's next keystrokes, not a separate bug.
- **Fix (`NumInput`, root cause not a band-aid):** new opt-in `allowClear` prop (default `false` — **every existing call site keeps its EXACT old behavior unless it explicitly opts in**, so a REQUIRED geometry field like building width/depth or a road setback can never silently go `null`). When `allowClear` is set and the draft is emptied, `commit()` now calls `onCommit(null)` instead of reverting. Applied to **all 22** `NumInput` call sites whose `onCommit` already null-coalesces (`Number.isFinite(n) ? n : null` or equivalent) — every one of these was equally broken, not just the reported field: `releaseRateCfs` (the reported field), `daAcres`, `daImpPct`, `pumpRateCfs`, the outlet fields (`diameterIn`, `invertElevFt` ×2, `maxCfs`, weir `lengthFt`), `depth`/`freeboard`/`slope`/`tobElev` ×2/`poolElev`/`receivingFlowlineElev`/`depthToWaterFt`/`padElevFt`/`slopePct`/`shrinkPct`, and the two floodplain-mitigation manual-override fields (`fm.onChange`). Required/geometric fields (width, height, setback, aisle, bay dimensions, …) were deliberately left untouched — their `onCommit` handlers don't null-guard and must never receive `null`.
- **Bug (2) — proposed-outlet removal not surviving a real reload for a signed-in (cloud-synced) session.** Static analysis + a local (logged-out) reproduction attempt **disproved** the owner's own leading hypothesis ("the loader auto-derives an outlet from the persisted release on load") — `defaultOutletForPond`/`propose()` is called from exactly ONE place in the whole codebase (the "Propose outlet" button's own click handler; verified via a repo-wide grep), and a logged-out local reload correctly showed the outlet gone after removal. The real gap, found by reading the element-level cloud-sync engine (`lib/elementSync.js`, B671/B672): the engine's **last-ditch keepalive commit** of still-debounced per-element edits (exists specifically so an edit sitting in the ~750ms debounce window isn't lost on unload) was wired **only** through the app's internal forced-reload registry (`app/flushRegistry.js`'s `flushAll()`), which fires **solely** on chunk-recovery or the ErrorBoundary's own "Reload" button — **never** on a genuine user-initiated browser reload/close, which only fires the native `beforeunload`/`visibilitychange` events. So a real F5/reload-button/tab-close never triggered the keepalive commit; only the (now largely superseded, B672) whole-doc blob save did.
- **Fix (`SitePlanner.jsx`):** the element-sync keepalive-flush effect now ALSO listens to the real `beforeunload` and `visibilitychange`(hidden) events directly — the exact same pattern already used for the whole-doc save a few lines above — in addition to (not instead of) `registerFlush`, which still covers the forced-reload path. Also calls `reconcileElems(false)` first so the very latest edit is diffed into the dirty queue before reading `pendingOps()` (belt-and-suspenders — the debounced autosave effect that normally does this may not have ticked yet).
- **Named rules:** LOUD-FAILURE (the owner's stuck test-data value is called out explicitly, not silently left untracked), DEDUPE-FIRST, MODULE-SCOPE-COMPONENTS (no new components — `NumInput` and the flush effect are both existing module-scope definitions, unchanged in scope).
- **Verified (sandbox/headless):** full unit suite green (**4568 tests**, incl. new `test/elementSyncUnloadGuard.test.js` — 3 source-text anti-drift guards pinning the direct `beforeunload`/`visibilitychange` wiring + the `reconcileElems(false)` re-diff + that `registerFlush` composes rather than is replaced); lint 0 errors; build green. **Bug (1) reproduced AND fixed, both confirmed by building + driving the real app with Playwright** (not assumed): the pre-fix build showed the exact reported symptom (typed "15", triple-click+Delete+Tab reverted to "15", never cleared); the post-fix build clears to empty and accepts fresh input cleanly. New `e2e/pond-outlet-clear.spec.js` (2 specs, logged out): (a) set→clear→retype the Allowable release field — passes; (b) propose→remove→reload→re-select an outlet — shows no outlet (confirms the LOCAL/non-cloud persistence path, which this session found was already correct, as a standing regression guard). Both pass; the sibling `e2e/pond-outlet-render.spec.js` (B900) and `e2e/pond-context-menu.spec.js` re-verified passing (no regression).
- **⏳ V376 (live):** see VERIFICATION.md — bug (2)'s fix needs a SIGNED-IN, cloud-synced session to fully confirm (the exact repro: propose an outlet, wait for it to sync, remove it, reload within the debounce window, confirm it stays gone) — the local/logged-out path this session could drive was already correct, so it can't exercise the actual gap that was fixed. The owner will also confirm the "Allowable release" field now clears normally.
- **DEDUPE-FIRST:** searched Open/⏳ Verify/Done for `#pond` + "NumInput"/"clear"/"beforeunload"/"keepalive" — net-new. Distinct from B900 (same flow, a hard render crash, already shipped separately).

The RATE CONTROL routed per-storm table (rendered only once an outlet exists AND `assessRoutedDetention` (`lib/pondRouting.js`) actually resolves a route — `routed.kind === "routed"`) mapped over `routed.perStorm` using `<React.Fragment key={s.returnPeriodYr}>` — an explicit reference to the bare `React` global, which the automatic JSX runtime never defines. Every other JSX fragment in the file already uses the shorthand `<>…</>`; this one line was the sole holdout (confirmed via `grep -rn "React\." src/` across the WHOLE repo — this was the only bare-`React.` reference anywhere, so the fix is complete, not partial).

- **LIVE crash reproduced AND fixed, both confirmed by building + driving the real app (not assumed):** built the app pre-fix, ran a Playwright script through the exact repro (Start blank → draw a Detention Pond → open its inspector → top-of-bank + drainage area + allowable release → click "Propose outlet") → **error boundary fired with the identical console text "React is not defined."** Restored the fix, rebuilt, re-ran the identical script → **the RATE CONTROL routed table rendered cleanly (STORM/PRE cfs/ROUTED header, PASS chips per storm), zero page errors.** This before/after pair is the proof the fix addresses the actual reported failure, not a lookalike.

(2) Switching the primary outlet to Restrictor (the report's "almost certainly + Restrictor" concern) re-renders the same Fragment block — asserts the same. (3) A page **reload** after proposing an outlet — covers the "crash persists across reload" half of the report — asserts the canvas loads clean, no error boundary. All 3 pass; the sibling `e2e/pond-context-menu.spec.js` (right-click pond menu) re-verified passing, unaffected.

### B880 — Setback offset line "messes up" on zoom-out: scale its dash + stroke with zoom and drop it when the inset goes sub-pixel `[Site Planner]` (bug) #site-planner #ui #selection  *(owner-reported 2026-07-18 from chat — "the lot lines mess up when i zoom out"; clarified as the parcel SETBACK offset ring, `settings.showSetback`. Sandbox-diagnosed handoff (Mueschke Rd / Tomball). Minted **B880** via `npm run next-id`. Branch `claude/planyr-tsakiris-verification-sugso8`.)*
`[x]` **IMPLEMENTED + unit-tested this session; parks in ⏳ Verify (Verify: live — zoom-/data-density-dependent render + PDF/print export-parity classes) → V361.** On a large tract with `showSetback` on, the dashed setback ring read clean at site zoom but on zoom-out crowded/garbled the boundary into a doubled line and (on denser traces) broke into ragged dashes; clean again on zoom-in.
- Verify: live
- Origin: filed 2026-07-18 from chat (owner); sandbox-diagnosed handoff.
- **Root cause (verified):** the setback rendered `strokeWidth={1.25}` + `strokeDasharray="7 6"`, both FIXED screen-px — neither scaled by the B617 zoom factor `zk = view.ppf/0.35` (B617 scaled the boundary's WEIGHT; nothing scaled the setback or any dash PERIOD). Two effects: (1) **sub-pixel inset** — a 25 ft setback on a ~2,900 ft tract collapses to ~2 px off the boundary at the reported zoom (<1 px further out), so the dashed ring sits on top of the solid boundary → the garbled double-line (hits even a CLEAN trace, the dominant driver); (2) **fixed-px dash disintegration** — edges shorter than one 13 px "7 6" cycle can't render (6/42 → 42/42 edges as you zoom out). The GEOMETRY was RULED OUT: `offsetPolygon` returned 0 self-intersections across 7→56-vtx tracts / 25→100 ft setbacks (the handoff's withdrawn NEW-2 clipper rework is unnecessary).
- **Fix:** new pure `lib/lineZoom.js` — `dashZoom(spec, zk)` (mirrors `strokeZoom`: scales the dash period by `zk`, floors it so the period never goes sub-pixel `DASH_ZOOM_FLOOR_PX=3`, caps at 3.5×) + `insetRingVisible(minInsetFt, ppf)` (a dashed inset ring draws only when its smallest inset reads ≥ `INSET_MIN_VISIBLE_PX=3` on-screen px; below that it's SUPPRESSED, reappearing on zoom-in). The setback ring now suppresses when sub-pixel, runs its weight through `strokeZoom` and its dash through `dashZoom`. **PDF-PARITY:** `printSheet` clones the live SVG, so the scaled dash/weight carry to export by construction (B617/B719 precedent — no separate export path).
- **Sibling dashes folded (handoff item 4):** the utility/deed/easement spines + neutral markups (via the shared `da` source) + the overlay-calibration connectors now fold through `dashZoom` too — the same latent B617-sibling class. Transient draft/cursor overlays deliberately stay fixed-px.
- **DEDUPE-FIRST:** dash-scaling sibling of **B617** (weight only) and **B719** (to-scale curb). Net-new; no prior item scales a dash period.
- **Verified (sandbox):** `test/lineZoom.test.js` (10: dashZoom no-op at zk=1 / floored on zoom-out / capped on zoom-in / solid + unparseable passthrough / multi-segment; insetRingVisible visible/suppressed/threshold/non-finite) + `test/bugHuntGuards.test.js` new B880 guard (setback uses insetRingVisible + strokeZoom + dashZoom, not fixed 1.25/"7 6"; the `da` source folds through dashZoom). Full suite green + lint + build green + MAP regenerated.
- **⏳ V361 (live/headless, planyr.io):** see VERIFICATION.md — draw a large parcel, setback on, zoom fully out → a clean continuous dashed inset that cleanly DISAPPEARS once indistinguishable from the boundary, never a garbled double-line; PDF/print export matches.

  - (d) **earthwork** — berm fill CY (`pondBermFillCf`) joins the ledger, netted against basin cut, with "berm can be built from basin spoil — haul math is your engineer's".

### B839 — Export aerial reuses cached basemap tiles instead of a slow on-demand render (fixes the timeout that blanked the PDF) `[Site Planner]` (bug) #site-planner #export #gis #perf #stitching  *(follow-on to B738/V252; owner-dropped 2026-07-15 as the aerial-export "NEW-1" — distinct from the same-day panel-flash NEW-1 → B837, and from the 2026-07-09 NEW-2/NEW-3 folded into B738; minted **B839** via `npm run next-id`. Branch `claude/aerial-export-imagery-cache-vr03je`.)*
`[x]` **IMPLEMENTED + headless-verified this session; parks in ⏳ Verify (Verify: live — PDF/export parity + zoom-/DPI-dependent tile rendering + GIS-endpoint behavior, all mandatory-live classes) → V329.** With the Esri "Aerial" basemap on, a normal/large frame → Download PDF printed on white with "⚠ Couldn't load the satellite imagery…" though the map looked fine on screen. The export now sources the aerial from the SAME fast, pre-rendered tiles the live map shows, so the slow dynamic render is no longer the failure mode.
- Verify: live
- Origin: filed 2026-07-15 from chat (owner live console test, project `smr9olizi5ue` — Katy, 5 parcels ~110 ac).
- **Root cause (live-confirmed from the planyr.io console):** `exportAerialForFrame` requested a **fresh on-demand dynamic image** (`aerialPlacement` → `BASEMAPS[basemapSrc].export`, `maxPx:2400`); Esri's `World_Imagery/MapServer/export` renders that frame in **>8 s**, and `inlineImages`/`fetchAsDataUrl` abort every fetch at the shared `INLINE_TIMEOUT_MS=8000` → the `data-export-aerial` `<image>` is dropped → `aerialDropped` → `flashWarn` (owner console: Esri `export` **AbortError @ 8015 ms**; USGS `export` **200, 1255 KB, 4022 ms** for the same frame).
- **Fix (fast path):** `exportAerialForFrame` is now async and STITCHES the covering XYZ tiles (the browser/CDN-cached tiles the live Leaflet basemap already displays) into a frame-exact data: URL, instead of a dynamic `/export`. New pure Web-Mercator math in `lib/arcgis.js` — `lngLatToGlobalPixel` / `aerialTileGrid` (covering tiles + cropped-canvas size + per-tile draw offset) / `pickAerialTileZoom` (deepest zoom ≤ the source's `maxNative` that keeps the canvas ≤ maxPx — never past the ceiling, or Esri/USGS return the gray "no data" placeholder as HTTP 200, the B182/B220 trap). DOM stitch (`fetchTileImage` + `stitchAerialDataUrl` in `SitePlanner.jsx`) crops to the exact bbox and returns a JPEG data URL, **reusing `aerialPlacement`'s feet geometry unchanged** (Mercator↔linear differs sub-pixel over one site; we anchor to the same bbox corners). The live tile layers now request **`crossOrigin: true`** so those bytes are canvas-readable and the stitch reuses the same cache.
- **Fallback chain (LOUD-FAILURE preserved):** stitch active source → stitch alternate source → dynamic `/export` placement (rescued by B840's longer budget + alt-source retry) → only then dropped + a loud warning. STRICT stitch (any missing tile → fall back) so an exhibit is never gappy. A stitched data: URL is skipped by `inlineImages` (no fetch), so the common case has no timeout at all.
- **DEDUPE-FIRST:** net-new — no item reuses cached basemap tiles for the export backdrop. Builds on **B738** (the export-aerial machinery) and **B202** (the time-boxed `inlineImages` + `dropOnFail`). Cache prior art (reuse, not dupe): **B445** (server-side Drive imagery cache), **B438** (browser SW+IndexedDB, superseded by B445), **B694** (cached vector tier). Distinct from **B171** (gated evaluation of a higher-res imagery *source*).
- **Verified (sandbox/headless):** new pure tile-math tests in `test/aerialExport.test.js` (Web-Mercator pixel origin/scale, bbox crop dims, full tile coverage with in-range indices, zoom clamps to `maxNative` + stays under maxPx) · **B839 source guard** in `test/bugHuntGuards.test.js` (stitch + crossOrigin×2 + async + both callers await) · **new `ui-audit/verify-aerial-tile-stitch.mjs`** drives the REAL stitch DOM path in headless Chromium against a local CORS tile server: all-tiles → a **941×941 JPEG data URL, 100% non-white, canvas NOT tainted**; one 500 tile → stitch returns **null** (strict-fails to the fallback). Existing `ui-audit/verify-aerial-export-cors.mjs` still green. Full suite + lint 0 + build green; MAP.md regenerated (new `arcgis.js` exports). NOTE: the live Esri/USGS tile fetch can't be driven from the *sandbox* browser (the egress proxy resets headless Chromium's TLS to arcgisonline / blocks nationalmap) — same limit as V252; a real browser at planyr.io has no proxy.
- **⏳ V329 (live, planyr.io — no sign-in):** on the owner's Katy site (or any large multi-parcel site) with the **Aerial** backdrop ON, **Download PDF** → the satellite is the background (not white), aligned under the parcels/massing, and it comes back **promptly** (no ~8s stall, no "couldn't load" warning). Repeat with a print frame set, with **USGS** selected, and **Download PNG**. Then confirm parity: basemap **OFF** exports with no aerial as before; a dropped-screenshot underlay still exports.

### B837 — Left-rail panel switch flashes the basemap and jumps the site sideways `[Site Planner / Map + UI]` (bug) #site-planner #ui #perf  *(filed from chat 2026-07-15; minted **B837** via next-id — renumbered from a provisional B835 on merge, which collided with PR #623's Scheduler B835; DEDUPE-FIRST: distinct trigger + new symptom vs B821 — see note)*
> **⚠ FLASH half SUPERSEDED by B933 (2026-07-21).** B837's `spawnGhost()`-on-resize is the ghost that B933 identified as the *actual* toggle flash (the resize `setView` never wipes — Leaflet internal-panBys a same-zoom re-center). B933 removes the ghost from the toggle path (panBy, no wipe). **The JUMP half (the `panelShiftRef` measured-left-edge compensation + `e2e/panel-toggle-viewport.spec.js`) stands and is unchanged** — still ⏳ V328 for the no-jump live check. The toggle-flash live check folds into B933's V392.
`[ ]` Desktop, project open: clicking a left-rail icon to open/switch the left panel (reported on **Parcel**) makes the aerial **flash** (tiles wipe + reload for one frame) AND the drawing/parcels **jump horizontally** a large distance (~a couple hundred feet at working zoom; in the reported case the massing landed on the neighborhood to the west, well off its true parcels). Expected: opening/switching a left panel is seamless — no basemap flash, drawing/parcels stay locked to the aerial in their real-world position (zero sideways shift).
- **IMPLEMENTED 2026-07-15 (parked ⏳ Verify → V328).** **JUMP fixed:** the `panelShiftRef` compensation now measures the ACTUAL canvas left-edge (`wrapRef.offsetLeft`, relative to the position:relative body row) in a `useLayoutEffect` — same-paint, before-paint — instead of an assumed `leftWidth + 6` in a passive (after-paint) effect. Reconciling the measured delta cancels EXACTLY for any panel width, a live rail-resize, AND a panel→panel switch, with no one-frame skip; a phone overlay (position:absolute, B556) and a floating card (portaled out, B717) contribute nothing to `offsetLeft`, so it stays desktop/docked-only with no conditional. **FLASH fixed:** the formerly-separate un-ghosted `map.invalidateSize(false)` (fired ~60ms after the ghosted commit on every `size` change — the residual tile-wipe) is folded INTO the `sizeChanged` branch: `spawnGhost()` → `invalidateSize` → `setView` now run under ONE B65 ghost, and `size` was dropped from the standalone invalidateSize effect (now `active`/show-hide + origin only). Added a viewport-transform seam (`data-view-offx/offy/ppf` on the canvas SVG) + e2e `e2e/panel-toggle-viewport.spec.js`. **AUDIT-FIRST correction:** the assumed `leftWidth + 6` actually equals the real stolen width for the default same-width case, so the SETTLED position was already correct — the user-visible defect is the multi-frame skip on a heavy project (passive effect lands several frames late) + the un-ghosted aerial wipe; the layout-effect + folded ghost close both by construction. Headless-verified LOGGED OUT (seeded 1-parcel site, real origin): a fixed feet point holds its viewport x to **0px** across open / switch→Analysis / switch→Yield / close, zero console errors; build + full suite (`e2e/panel-toggle-viewport.spec.js` green) + lint green.
- Verify: live (timing/state + zoom-/data-density-dependent rendering — LIVE-VERIFY. **Measure before patch (mandatory):** instrument on live planyr.io via Cowork, reproduce rail→Parcel from BOTH panel-closed and panel-already-open-on-another-tab, and confirm the mechanism before writing any fix.)
- Origin: filed 2026-07-15 from chat (owner-reported).
- **Two symptoms, two subsystems (hypothesis — confirm by measuring first):**
  - **Jump** = the SVG-canvas pan-compensation effect (`panelShiftRef` in `SitePlanner.jsx`). It shifts the canvas to cancel the width the docked panel steals, but models only ONE rail width (the persisted resizable-rail width) and reconciles only on `leftPanel` truthiness. If the Parcel panel renders at a different width, or a panel→panel switch changes the canvas width without the compensation trigger changing, it over/under-shoots and the drawing slides by the mismatch.
  - **Flash** = the Leaflet resize path. The seamless zoom/pan system (transform-zoom + ghost-buffer) treats a container resize as "no prior view worth ghosting" and does an immediate hard `setView` → Leaflet `_resetAll` removes and reloads every tile for a frame. The panel toggle hits this un-buffered branch.
- **Measure before patch (mandatory — timing/state class):** capture map-container width before/after, each panel's actual rendered width, `panelShiftRef.current`, `view.offX` before/after, and whether a Leaflet resize/`setView`/tile reload fires. Confirm whether the jump is (a) width-mismatch in the compensation, (b) a one-frame ordering gap between the pan-shift commit and the flex reflow, or (c) panel→panel width change with no compensation — before touching code.
- **Fix direction (once confirmed):** compensate against the *measured* canvas-width delta (drive off a `ResizeObserver` on the map container, not an assumed `leftWidth + 6`) so any panel width and any panel→panel switch cancels exactly · apply the pan-shift in a layout-effect keyed on the observed size so it lands in the same paint as the reflow (no one-frame skip) · ghost-buffer the resize commit (a panel-toggle resize DOES have a valid prior view — spawn the ghost like zoom-out already does, hold current tiles across the `setView`, drop them on the tile-layer `load`). Reuse the existing mechanism; no new dependency. Do NOT hard-code an offset for one panel's width — it masks the stale-size root and drifts on other panels/screens/rail resizes.
- **Files likely touched:** `src/workspaces/site-planner/SitePlanner.jsx` (the `panelShiftRef` effect + the geo commit / ghost resize path). No projection/coordinate files.
- **Gotchas:** keep B556 intact (phone panel overlays are position:absolute, resize nothing → compensation stays desktop/docked-only); B717's floating panels don't resize the canvas either, so exclude floaters from compensation; verify the switch doesn't re-trigger Web-Worker overlay parsing (would re-render overlays and read as a second flash).
- **DEDUPE-FIRST:** minted fresh + cross-linked (NOT a re-open), following B821's own precedent of minting fresh against B65 for "a distinct trigger reaching the same subsystem through the branch a prior fix left un-buffered."
  - **B821** (⏳ Verify → V310, shipped) — same *flash mechanism* (docked-panel resize → un-ghosted `setView` tile-wipe) but a different trigger (single/double-click feature-select) and it does NOT cover the horizontal jump. ⚠ If the flash still reproduces live after B821 deploys, B821's V310 live-verify is implicated — check B821 first when measuring.
  - **B656** (Done) — owns the `panelShiftRef` canvas-shift discipline; NEW-1's jump is a gap against B656's "select/deselect never visually jumps the drawing" guarantee. (The owner's note said "B556" — that's the mobile auto-open-panel bug; the pan-compensation is B656.)
  - **B65** (Done) — the original ghost-buffer (`spawnGhost`) to reuse · **B717** (⏳ Verify) — the floating/dockable left panels + icon rail this rides on · **B329** (Done) — the shared viewport engine (feeds the B838 sweep).

- Verify: live
- Origin: discovered while filing B863 (protocol: a diagnosis reaching the repo mints a B# on sight).
- **What happened (live hs-v1):** two Goose Creek tasks — #86 "Organization Meeting" and #88 "Conduct Confirmation Election" — were `meetingBound:true` pointing at `meetingBodyId: mb_mrmdy43mlhjr`, and #88 carried a correctly-computed election date (2027-05-01) + agenda deadline (2027-02-12) — yet `settings.meetingBodies` was **null**. The calendar definition was never persisted while its BINDINGS were: an orphaned reference. Owner's words fit a stale-tab clobber ("maybe I went over to a tab that didn't update"): the app cloud-saves the WHOLE document last-write-wins, so a second tab lacking the just-created body saved over the tab that had it.
- **Why it bites:** on a fresh load, `cascadeDates` sees `meetingBound:true` but no body in `bodyMap` → `bound=false` → the task falls back to a plain FS date (loses the election date), and **B836's drift guard would then "heal" #88 away from 2027-05-01** to that wrong FS date (a loud rewrite of an intended date).

Re-query confirmed 1 body present, #88 unchanged, post-repair drift = 0.
- **(a) CODE HARDENING — IMPLEMENTED + sandbox-verified 2026-07-16 (own PR, per the meeting-binding/`cascadeDates` own-PR rule):** `cascadeDates` now computes `bodyMissing` (a `meetingBound` leaf whose `meetingBodyId` isn't in the body index) and, when the task HAS a stored date, **soft-pins it** (`t.pinnedStart || (bodyMissing && t.start)`) so preds can't overwrite the intended meeting date + sets `t.meetingBodyMissing`; a bound task with NO stored date still falls through to normal FS scheduling (unchanged). `detectCascadeDrift` now **exempts** `meetingBound` + `deadlineForTaskId` rows (their dates are calendar-/anchor-derived, not simple-cascade drift — like pins), so a legitimate re-snap (or a preserved orphan) never fires the drift banner. The row surfaces the formerly-INVISIBLE broken binding as a danger-toned calendar + alert dot with a plain-English tooltip ("Bound to a meeting calendar that no longer exists… re-create/re-select in Settings → Meeting Calendars, or unbind"). Mirrored in `ui-audit/stress/scheduler-engine.mjs`. **8 new unit tests** (`test/schedulerEngine.test.js`): missing-body preserves the date + flags it; unbinding the same task DOES revert to FS (proves preservation is real); present-body snaps + clears the flag; drift-exemption for meeting + deadline rows; source guards on both files + the badge. Full suite (4176) + lint 0 errors + build green. **→ V346 — CONFIRMED PASS live 2026-07-21** (a scratch calendar+task on Goose Creek: delete the bound calendar → date holds, badge flips to the danger calendar-with-alert-dot, the bind menu shows no checkmark against any remaining calendar (never silently cleared); scratch rows cleaned up after, real schedule data untouched).
- **(b) ROOT CAUSE — IMPLEMENTED + sandbox-verified 2026-07-16 (own PR):** the whole-document cloud-save was last-write-wins with a rev-gate that only BLOCKED a stale tab (snapshotting the loser to history + forcing a reload that dropped its edits) — so a sibling's just-created calendar was lost when the other tab won. **AUDIT-FIRST correction to B850's "Scheduler is two-tab-safe" claim:** the guard blocks the *loser*, but the loser's changes never reach the cloud, and the write itself (`sb.upsert`) is an unconditional whole-doc overwrite — no field-level merge. **Fix:** on a would-be-blocked auto-save the storage layer now **3-way MERGES** our edits onto the newer cloud (`mergeCloudDoc(base, ours, theirs)`, module scope + mirrored/unit-tested in `scheduler-engine.mjs`) instead of blocking: base = the doc this tab last loaded/saved (`baseByKey`), ours = current, theirs = the newer cloud. A side unchanged vs base yields to the changed side; id-keyed arrays (tasks / meetingBodies / contacts) merge per element by id (adds survive, a delete is honored only if the other side left the key alone); a genuine same-leaf conflict prefers ours, the loser kept as a `premerge-ours` Version-History snapshot. The App adopts the merge via a `planar:merged` event, **reconciling against its CURRENT state** (`mergeCloudDoc(ancestor, current, merged)`) so an edit made during the save round-trip is never lost, + a "Merged in changes from another tab" toast. Falls back to the old block-and-snapshot only when no base ancestor exists (seed/offline). **14 merge unit tests** (the exact election-calendar repro: a stale tab's save preserves the sibling's calendar + binding + its own edit; keyed-array add/delete/conflict; nested project add; missing-base fail-safe) + a full node simulation of the two-tab flow incl. an in-flight edit. Full suite (4188) + lint 0 + build green; `index.html` babel blocks esbuild-parse-clean; `MAP.md` regenerated. **→ V347** (the live two-tab race is a mandatory concurrency LIVE-VERIFY class — can't drive two signed-in boards headless). Residual (smaller, noted): a true simultaneous read-check-write TOCTOU (both tabs at the same rev racing the unconditional upsert) is not closed by this — an optimistic conditional write is the follow-up; the merge handles every non-simultaneous ordering.
- **DEDUPE-FIRST:** distinct from **B846** (Site-Planner element-sync false-conflict toasts, its own transport) and **B850** (which asserted Scheduler two-tab safety — this is the counter-example); same multi-writer THEME, different subsystem (Scheduler whole-doc save + meeting bodies). Relatives: **B836** (the guard that would mis-heal the orphaned task — now taught to exempt it), **B815/B816** (the meeting-body engine).
- **⏳ V345 (data repair) — still pending, live, planyr.io, SIGNED IN (needs a real hs-v1 session):** see VERIFICATION.md. **V346 (the (a) orphaned-binding badge) — ✅ CONFIRMED PASS 2026-07-21, moved to VERIFICATION-DONE.md. V347 (the (b) two-tab auto-merge) — ✅ CONFIRMED PASS 2026-07-19, moved to VERIFICATION-DONE.md.**

### B832 — Drainage facts auto-revalidate; the ↻ button becomes an override, not a gate `[Site Planner / yield · GIS]` (feature) #site-planner #yield #gis #persistence #perf  *(owner-dropped 2026-07-14 as "NEW-12"; minted **B832**)*

- **(a) Auto-run on load** when there's no in-session check and the remembered snapshot is stale or geometry-incomplete (the B804/B829-class states).
- **(b) Auto-extend on edit:** debounced (~2–3 s after the last edit), re-fetch ONLY when an element's bbox exits the previously fetched envelope or a new fill/pond appears outside it — pure element moves inside the envelope never refetch.
- **(c) Sampled-point facts** (WSE at the fill centroid, grade tile) revalidate when their anchor moves > ~100 ft.
- **(d) Rate-limit + concurrency-cap** per the B366 discipline — a burst of drags coalesces to one revalidation; degraded sources fall to the honest last-good/unavailable states (B367 SWR), never block editing.
- **(e)** ↻ stays as "force refresh now"; the status line reads "facts as of <time> · auto" vs "· manual".
- **(f) Multi-writer care** (2026-07-14 cascade handoff): revalidation writes `lastCheck` idempotently and must not fight a second open tab (the B793 family).
- Cross-links (DEDUPE-FIRST, not dups): B750 (the remembered check + ↻ it upgrades), B804/B829 (the stale/slim honesty states that define "needs revalidation"), B367/B96 (the SWR cache it rides), B366 (rate-limit discipline).
- **IMPLEMENTED 2026-07-14 (parked ⏳ Verify → V324).** `lib/factRevalidation.js` (new, pure): load-kind triggers (no snapshot / stale sig / geometry-incomplete B804/B829-class records) vs edit-kind (the raw feet envelope exits the persisted fetch envelope; the fill-centroid or ground-line anchor drifts >100 ft), with stable per-target keys so a failed attempt never retry-loops; **pure moves inside the envelope never fetch** (unit-asserted, incl. under a stale sig). `checkDrainage({auto})` persists `lastCheck.fetch = {env, anchorPt, groundPt, mode}`; a DEGRADED auto run (authority unavailable, or flood failed where the snapshot had loaded) shows its honest live state but **never overwrites the good remembered snapshot** (last-good; a manual ↻ keeps replace-always). The auto effect: 1.2 s load / 2.5 s edit debounce via effect re-arm (drag coalescing), a ≥20 s rate floor, one attempt per key, skipped while the tab is hidden (multi-writer care — lastCheck writes stay sig-keyed + JSON-guarded). Status line reads "Facts as of <time> · auto|manual" (same-day time); ↻ is the explicit override; `settings.drainage.autoFacts === false` opts out (headless legacy seeds). 12 unit tests (`test/factRevalidation.test.js`); headless case G (a stale snapshot fires ONE honest failed auto attempt in the sandbox, editing never blocked, the good snapshot survives — asserted via localStorage). ### B821 — Map flashes/blanks on single- & double-click: docked-panel resize → un-ghosted `setView` tile-wipe `[Site Planner / Map]` (bug) #site-planner #ui #perf  *(owner-dropped 2026-07-14 as "NEW-1" — "the map flashes/flickers every time I single- or double-click a feature/parcel/overlay, then repaints"; minted **B821** (late-bound against fresh main). Implemented + shipped same session; parked for the live click-through. → V310.)*
> **⚠ ROOT CAUSE CORRECTED + fix SUPERSEDED by B933 (2026-07-21), after the owner reported the flash still reproduces live.** B821's "un-ghosted `setView` tile-wipe" diagnosis is wrong: instrumented headlessly, a click-driven panel resize fires **zero** `viewprereset` (Leaflet internal-panBys a same-zoom, in-viewport re-center — no wipe). The real flash is the ghost B837 later added to the resize path. B933 fixes it at the source (panBy on a same-zoom re-center, no ghost). B821's V310 toggle-flash live check is subsumed by **B933's V392**.
`[x]` **FIXED this session — root-caused in code, fixed by extending B65's existing anti-flash ghost-buffer to the resize path.** The Site Planner's aerial is a non-interactive Leaflet backdrop under the SVG canvas. Clicking a feature opens a docked side panel that is an **in-flow flex sibling of the canvas** (`SitePlanner.jsx:12119`/`:12141`), so opening it shrinks `wrapRef`; the `ResizeObserver` (`:2486`) calls `setSize`, which re-runs the basemap view-sync effect (`:1682`, deps `[view, size, origin]`) down its `sizeChanged` branch (`:1730`). That branch called `commit(center, z, false)` — **the ghost buffer was skipped** — so a raw `map.setView` fired Leaflet's `viewreset`, whose GridLayer handler **wipes & reloads every aerial tile** = the one-frame flash. It fired on parcel single-click (Parcel panel), element/markup/callout double-click (Properties companion), overlay select (References panel), and click-empty-to-deselect (panel closes) — hence "frequent." (The report's other four hypotheses were each ruled out in code: the map is created once and never re-keyed/remounted on selection; `doubleClickZoom:false` on the backdrop; no per-select layer remove/re-add or `setData` source reload.)
- **The fix (one flag).** `SitePlanner.jsx:1730` now passes `commit(center, z, !!prev)`: first paint (`prev===null`, no tiles on screen to clone) stays un-ghosted exactly as before; a **resize with a prior view on screen** ghost-buffers, so B65's frozen-tile snapshot (`spawnGhost` `:1696`) sits on top until the fresh tiles report `load` and the `setView` wipe never shows. Untouched: the pan/zoom gesture path (`size` doesn't change during a gesture) and initial load.
- Verify: live → **V310** — a single-frame tile-wipe flash is a zoom-/data-density-dependent render the headless sandbox can't capture (the B65 class; the geo aerial also needs a real site + tiles the sandbox egress-blocks), so the live click-through parks for a browser check on planyr.io.
- Origin: filed 2026-07-14 from chat (owner NEW-1).
- **Named rules:** AUDIT-FIRST (traced the real ResizeObserver→`size`→un-ghosted-`setView` chain against B65's ghost machinery, confirming B65 fixed only the gesture path and left the resize branch un-buffered by design); LIVE-VERIFY (one-frame flash → V310); MODULE-SCOPE-COMPONENTS n/a. No `MAP.md` change (inline effect edit — no file add/remove/rename, no primary-export change).
- **DEDUPE-FIRST:** net-new number, NOT a B65 recurrence. **B65** ("White flashing on zoom/pan and general redraw", Done) built this exact ghost-buffer, but its triggers were zoom/pan/load gestures and it never regressed for that scope; this is a distinct trigger (click-select → docked-panel resize) reaching the same subsystem through the branch B65 left un-buffered — so a new B# cross-linked to B65, not a re-open. Relatives (not dups): **B741** (angled-element selection handles, live-gated) and **B750** (single-click select vs double-click open Properties) — adjacent selection-interaction items, different symptom.
- **Verified (sandbox, 2026-07-14):** `npm run build` green (SitePlannerApp/DocReview still separate lazy chunks); full suite **3796** tests green (incl. `backlogIndex`/`mapDrift`/`docPointers`/`contrast` guards); `eslint` 0 errors on the changed file (only pre-existing warnings on other effects); headless smoke (logged-out `vite preview`) — entered the planner via "Start blank", single-clicked + double-clicked the canvas → app stays mounted, zero JS/page errors (only an expected egress-blocked tile fetch). The flash itself is not headless-observable → V310.

### B816 — Meeting-bound tasks: snap to cadence, auto-roll on miss, derived agenda deadline `[Scheduler]` (feature) #scheduler #entitlements #gantt #perf #export  *(owner-dropped 2026-07-13 as "NEW-2"; minted **B816**. → V306. Implemented + shipped same session; the engine is unit-tested in the sandbox (15 tests), the UI is parked for the live click-through.)*
`[x]` **IMPLEMENTED this session — engine + data layer + civic mark + bind picker + roll toast.** Depends on B815. **Own PR, nothing else in it** — this touches `cascadeDates`, the highest-blast-radius function in the codebase (B584/B585/B501/B487/B568 all cluster here). A task bound to a meeting body snaps to the body's cadence, derives its agenda deadline, and **auto-rolls a whole cycle** when the deadline is missed.
- Verify: live — engine end-to-end unit-testable via the verbatim mirror + anti-drift guards; the live click-through (bind a task → slip a predecessor → watch it jump a cycle → pin it → watch it go red) is **V306**, run via Cowork on live planyr.io (the scheduler's CDN React/Babel is egress-blocked in the sandbox).
- Origin: filed 2026-07-13 from chat ("NEW-2").
- **Task fields `_v7 → _v8`** via a new `normalizeToV8` (idempotent), chained after the existing `normalizeToV7` (`:4562`): `meetingBodyId · meetingBound:true · pinnedMeetingDate?`. Existing tasks untouched — a no-op stamp, zero date shift by construction. Run the real before/after diff against the live scheduler dataset (Supabase hs-v1, ~667 tasks) exactly as B621 did. (AUDIT-FIRST: today's version is `_v7`, not `_v8` — B816 adds V8.)
- **★ The agenda deadline is NOT a task row.** It is a **derived field** — a pure function of (body, chosenMeetingDate), recomputed every cascade, never persisted as authoritative, never given an id, never entering `tasks[]` or the dependency graph. Rationale from this repo's history: `renumberTasks`/cut-paste/delete/indent-outdent have each corrupted the task array (B568/B584/B501/B487), so a system-owned row inside a user-owned list reopens all of it; and a real FS link deadline→meeting closes a cycle against the meeting→deadline derivation (`validatePredEdit` rejects it). Precedent: **B583** formula columns (`e:false`, derived, no feedback loop) — except computed *inside* the cascade, because unlike a formula column it participates in date selection.
- **Cascade rule** (in `cascadeDates` `:1861`, after the normal predecessor-derived early start, before `calcEnd`): predecessors produce a packet-ready date; chosen meeting = earliest `m` where **`agendaDeadline(m) >= packetReady`** — NOT `m >= packetReady` (the core of the feature and the obvious wrong implementation; `m >= packetReady` silently puts items on agendas they can't be filed for). `start = end = m`; duration forced to 0d; agenda deadline computed + stored as a derived field for renderers.
- **Tie-break — `sameDayFilingAllowed`, default false:** when the driving predecessor is itself a meeting (first reading → second reading), eligibility is **`agendaDeadline(m) > drivingMeetingDate`, strictly**. Council meets Tuesday evening; the next agenda closed at noon that same Tuesday — a `>=` produces a schedule that cannot physically happen (at a 10-business-day lead on a 2-week cadence the two readings can never be consecutive and the schedule quietly loses a month). `minMeetingsAfter:{taskId,n}` for two-reading ordinances / "must be a subsequent meeting."
- **★ The mark (ships in THIS item — B816 can't land without it).** A bound row breaks three rules other rows follow (date can't be freely typed · duration forced to 0 · slips in cycles not days) — a row that behaves differently with no visible reason is a silent-behavior defect. **Glyph:** a bank/civic mark (`ti-building-bank` from the loaded `ti` webfont, or a hand-rolled SVG to match) in the Start-cell glyph slot beside the padlock (`:8895–8924`), distinct from the amber padlock (`pinnedStart`/`pinnedEnd`, **B621/B622** — in-code labels `B615`/`B616`): padlock = a person fixed this date; civic mark = a meeting calendar fixes it. They co-occur on a pinned bound task (🏛 8/11/26 🔒) — exactly the state that goes infeasible. **Three states, salience tracking severity:** `--text-secondary` (healthy float) · `--text-warning` (≤2 working days float) · `--text-danger` (infeasible — pinned + agenda closed); solid fills; the row tints `--bg-danger` **only** in the infeasible state. **Clicking the glyph explains the row** — body name, cadence, agenda rule, `verifiedOn` stamp, the plain-English reason the date is what it is, and the resolutions (roll to next meeting / unpin / change body). No DevTools, no dialog.
- **Every roll is announced** — reuse **B624**'s toast verbatim: "First reading moved to 8/25/26 — the 8/11 agenda closed 8/4." A bound date that moves without the user seeing why is a defect, not a convenience.
- **Interaction matrix — each case its own test in `test/schedulerEngine.test.js`.** `cascadeDates` already branches on no-predecessors / pinnedStart / pinnedEnd / dep type (FS-SS-FF-SF via the `switch` inside `constrainedStartFrom` `:1740` — AUDIT-FIRST: `DEP_DIRS` was removed with the elbow router, so hook the new case there, not a named map) / lags / unit-aware duration (`resolveDuration`) / blank-unscheduled. "Meeting-bound" is a fifth orthogonal branch, and this matrix is where the bugs will come from:
  - **bound + pinnedStart** → pin wins, do not roll → infeasible flag + red glyph.
  - **bound + pinnedEnd** → nonsense (start==end==meeting date) — reject on entry.
  - **bound + blank/unscheduled predecessor** → stays blank (B386's first-class unscheduled state) — must NOT snap to next Tuesday from today.
  - **bound + SS/FF/SF link** → packet-ready = the normal early start (via `constrainedStartFrom`); snap from there.
  - **bound as a summary/parent** → disallow (parents come from `rollupParentDates`) — guard in `validatePredEdit`.
  - **bound + typed duration** → force 0d with a visible inline error, never a silent zero.
- **Also touches:** `updateTask` (`:5157`) · `previewProject` (`:3728`, must mirror `updateTask` exactly — B585-S1 was a preview that lied about a pinned task) · `mkt` (`:2071`, new-task factory defaults) · `applyUpdate` (`:7875`, typing a date into a bound task snaps to the nearest eligible meeting + toast, mirroring B624's weekend roll-forward) · `validatePredEdit` (`:1705`).
- **Perf (interacts with B256, Open — the live board is already at 667, past its ~500 threshold):** precompute each body's meeting dates once per cascade run (`meetingDatesInRange(body, projectStart, projectEnd+horizon)`) and binary-search — do NOT generate recurrence dates inside the per-task loop. Strongly consider landing B256's id→index + parent→children[] maps first (makes this cheaper, overdue on its own merits).
- **Both Gantt renderers, or neither.** `GanttView.depLines` (screen, `:9296`) and `buildGanttSVG` (PDF/Print, `:10866`) are separate implementations that have drifted (B386/B395/B584 #11) — either put the glyph + markers in both, or have the export render bound milestones as plain milestones — **state which in the PR** (PDF-PARITY).
- **Shipped:** `cascadeDates(tasks, bodies)` + `applyMeetingBinding` (the snap rule `agendaDeadline(m) >= packetReady`, the strict two-reading tie-break, `minMeetingsAfter`), mirrored VERBATIM into `scheduler-engine.mjs` with **15 unit tests + 3 anti-drift guards** covering the whole matrix (bound+pinnedStart→infeasible, bound+blank pred→blank, bound+SS/FF/SF, bound-as-parent disallowed, typed-duration→0, the ★ two-readings-lose-a-month case). Bodies reach the cascade via a global `MEETING_BODY_INDEX` (like `HOLIDAY_SET`; ids are globally unique so no cross-project bleed; `duplicateProject` RE-IDs copied bodies). `normalizeToV8` is a no-op version stamp that refreshes the index on load. UI: the hand-rolled civic-bank glyph in the Start cell (3 severity states + a plain-English hover explainer), a hidden **Meeting** grid column with a native-select bind picker (`updateTask` re-cascades on the meeting fields; `previewProject` mirrors it), and the B624-voice roll toast when a bound task's meeting moves. Full suite green, `npm run build` green, `MAP.md` regenerated, `eslint` 0 errors, scheduler JSX validated via esbuild.
- **Deferred to follow-ups (noted, not silent):** the explainer is a rich **hover** tooltip (a click-open popover is a small NEW-3-era polish); the `--bg-danger` full-row tint is not yet wired (the red glyph carries the infeasible state); direct-typing a date into a bound row currently pins via the normal path (the snap-to-nearest-meeting-on-type is a refinement). **Both Gantts:** bound tasks are duration-0 **milestones**, so they already render as diamonds in BOTH `GanttView` and `buildGanttSVG` (the export shows the plain milestone — the stated PDF-PARITY fallback; the civic glyph lives in the grid). The live before/after diff against the real ~667-task board + the click-through are **V306**.

### B792 — Review delete-safety: same-name re-upload cross-wires two reviews; delete permanently destroys the markup layer; a network blip renders an empty Library `[Doc Review / Library]` (bug) #doc-review #library #persistence #drive #files  *(found by the 2026-07-12 data-deletion-safety audit as "NEW-F1/F3/F5/F7"; lineage: NEW-4/B579/B757 delete honesty, B54 read-failure discipline.
