`[x]` **IMPLEMENTED — four legs, one path:** **(F1)** `buildDriveKey` embeds `srcId` in the key's LAST segment (`project-<pid>/<discipline>/<srcId>__<name>`) so two uploads of the same-named file can never share a key (the old name-only key REBOUND the `drive_files` mapping to the newest Drive file — the older review's backdrop silently swapped, and deleting either review deleted the one mapped file under the other). Legacy keys resolve unchanged (stored on the source record; the server's flat-folder derivation drops the last segment, so folders are byte-identical). Purge-path byte deletes are gated by a **shared-key guard** (jsonb containment over other rows; fail-safe: unconfirmed → keep bytes + notice). **(F3)** `deleteReview` = SOFT delete (`deleted_at`, migration `doc_reviews_soft_delete.sql` — **applied to production via MCP this session**); Library gains **Recently deleted** (Restore / two-click Delete-forever), worded confirms, a ~10s undo toast; `ReviewsBar`'s `window.confirm` removed (owner rule); lazy 30-day purge; pre-migration DBs degrade to the old hard delete. B757 `.select("id")` + B579 ordering preserved; boot-resume can't reopen a deleted review (`loadReview` hides deleted rows; the local draft clears on soft delete — the cloud row keeps full data for restore). **(F5)** `fetchReviews`/`fetchFileFacts`/`fetchProjects` return `{ok, rows}` (the pinStore pattern); FileBrowser keeps the prior list on a failed refresh + a loud Retry notice — never a fake-empty Library (the panic that walks a user into F1's re-upload). **(F7)** purge also removes the `file_facts` row (full TOMBSTONE-DELETES cascade set). **Post-review hardening (same session — 5-lens adversarial review, 25 raw findings triaged, the real ones fixed):** the `fetchReviews` fallback tiers are now GATED on a genuinely-missing `deleted_at` column (a transient error on a migrated DB is an honest `ok:false`, never a filterless re-query that would resurface Recently-deleted rows); `listDeletedReviews` returns null on a failed read (the bin keeps its last list, mirrors NEW-F5); the automated 30-day purge surfaces stranded-bytes cleanup failures; the undo toast fires only on a delete that really landed (0-row no-op → loud notice, B757 honesty); the bin view can't strand you without an exit toggle; ReviewsBar's row keyboard handler no longer hijacks Enter from the inline confirm, and an armed confirm disarms on menu close. **Accepted semantics (documented in the migration file):** on a TEAM-shared review, any member can bin/restore (rides the member-wide UPDATE policy — same editors who can already rewrite content; recoverable by design), while permanent purge keeps the stricter owner/team-admin DELETE policy.
- Verify: live (real-project-data + Drive + signed-in-only surfaces) → **V292**.

### B789 — Per-source `timeoutMs` override in the GIS screening-fetch registry (FEMA flood answered at ~9.5 s, past the 9 s default) `[Site Planner / GIS]` (feature) #site-planner #gis #floodplain  *(coworker live-diagnosis handoff 2026-07-12 as "NEW-2"; late-bound to **B789 / V289** via `npm run next-id -- --against-main`. Origin: filed 2026-07-12 from chat. Same branch as B790. Implemented + sandbox-verified same session.)*
`[x]` **IMPLEMENTED — a GIS source row can now set its own `timeoutMs` to override the shared 9 s screening-fetch default (`GIS_FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS`); `GIS_SOURCES.flood` sets 20 s.** During the 2026-07-11 slowdown FEMA's NFHL answered the flood `/query` in ~9.5 s, so all three retry attempts aborted ~0.5 s too early and the Site Analysis floodplain row went unavailable even though FEMA would have answered. The override lets flood wait ~20 s (flood data changes slowly, so a longer wait is cheap) while every other source keeps the 9 s default.
- **Plumbing:** `reg()` (`siteAnalysis.js`) carries `s.timeoutMs` onto the endpoint; `queryLayer`/`countLayer` forward `{ timeoutMs }` into `fetchArcgisJson`, which already honored `opts.timeoutMs ?? GIS_FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS` — zero change to the fetch core.
- **AUDIT-FIRST correction to the handoff:** the handoff said the *vector* engine rides "the same 9 s substrate." It does not — `vectorLayers.js` `defaultFetchJson` is a **bare `fetch` with NO timeout**, so the 9 s near-miss is the **screening path only**. The vector flood pull isn't aborted at 9 s (it has its own long TTL cache); this override targets the path that actually lost the race.
- **Caveat (live evidence, do not oversell):** FEMA's own gateway still dropped some responses at ~10 s during the worst of it, so 20 s only rescues the *marginal-slow* case — the durable fix is the SWR cache proxy (**B788**), not this alone.
- Verify: live (GIS-endpoint timing class — confirming the flood screening survives a genuinely slow (~9–10 s) FEMA answer needs the live degraded endpoint; the sandbox can't reach `hazards.fema.gov`) → **V289**.
- **DEDUPE-FIRST:** a direct follow-on to **B366** (Done — the shared resilient fetch + the 9 s cap it introduced); B366 added no per-source override. Distinct from **B367**/**B371** (the screening cache tiers).
- **AMENDED 2026-07-29 by B1073** (not re-opened — this item shipped correctly and its scope was the SCREENING path only). New evidence: BKDD's first call to a cold ArcGIS Server instance takes **16.5–18.3 s** (every call after: 72–88 ms), which the 9 s default would abort forever. B1073 carries this mechanism to the three paths B789 never touched — the identify/detention path, the vector pull (which had NO timeout at all, per B789's own AUDIT-FIRST note), and the raster stall watchdog — plus the cache-proxy routing B789 explicitly excluded.
- Sandbox: 2 new `test/siteAnalysis.test.js` cases (flood forwards `timeoutMs: 20000` to the fetch layer; a source without it passes no override → the default applies) + `test/gisSources.test.js` still green (the field is additive, unguarded). Full suite green · lint 0 · build green.

### B409 (×2) — Unlimited-size file uploads: chunked Drive upload through the Worker proxy (replaces the CORS-dead browser-direct path) `[Doc Review / storage]` (bug) #doc-review #drive  *(owner-dropped 2026-06-23 as "NEW-1"; minted **B409**. REWORKED 2026-07-11 per the owner’s unlimited-uploads handoff, branch `claude/unlimited-file-uploads-04zkc9`; → V282 (minted V280, renumbered on merge-in of `origin/main` — the concurrent jurisdiction-badge/ISD session took V280/V281).)*
`[x]` **IMPLEMENTED (rework) — any-size uploads as ~16 MB chunks relayed through new `/api/uploads/*`; the streaming/Range download half fixes "won't open"; parked here for the live 125 MB round-trip → V282.**
- Recurrence: 2026-07-11 (×2) — the owner's 125 MB "GPL - Civil IFP 2026.06.19.pdf" still can't save. The first fix (browser PUTs bytes DIRECTLY to Google) is **CORS-dead by design and could never pass its live gate**: Fetch-over-CORS hides the `Location` header of the session-init response, and Google's upload endpoint answers preflights with no `Access-Control-Allow-Origin`. Re-opens the ORIGINAL B# (DEDUPE-FIRST) — do not re-attempt browser-direct-to-Drive.
- **Rework (all same-origin, so CORS never applies; owner decision: Drive + chunked-through-the-Worker, not R2/Supabase):** the browser slices the file (`File.slice`, never a whole-file read) into 16 MiB chunks (64 × Google's 256 KiB granule) → `PUT /api/uploads/<id>/chunk` → the Worker relays each chunk to the Drive resumable session it minted in `POST /api/uploads/start`. The capability session URI persists in new **`public.upload_sessions`** (`server/storage/db/upload_sessions.sql`, own-rows RLS, **migrated to production this session via MCP**) and is never returned to the browser. `GET …/status` probes Drive (`bytes */total`) for resume-from-offset; `POST …/complete` records the `drive_files` mapping (keeps the NEW-4 rollback: mapping-write failure deletes the Drive file + fails honestly — the V191 guard moved here). No single request is ever large → the Worker's ~100 MB body cap, its 128 MB memory, and Supabase's 50 MB cap all stop mattering, at any total size. Client loop (`src/shared/files/chunkedUpload.js`): sequential chunks, 5× exponential backoff, resume via /status after a drop, `storageQuotaExceeded` → plain-English "Drive is full" without futile retries; Library tray shows an honest per-file **progress bar** (server-confirmed bytes).
- **Download half (this is what "the big file won't open" was): `GET /api/files` now STREAMS** — the Drive body passes through as a ReadableStream (the old handler buffered `arrayBuffer()` in the Worker, blowing the 128 MB memory cap on a 125 MB PDF) — **and forwards the client's `Range` → 206 Partial Content** (`adapter.fetchStream` / `driveBackend.getStream` / `driveClient.mediaStream`). Drive-stored PDFs > 50 MB open BY URL (`driveStreamSource` + URL-source `loadPdf`), so pdf.js range-streams them progressively; the buffered path stays the fallback and for everything else.
- **Removed (per the handoff §9):** the whole-file `POST /api/files` route, `functions/api/files/resumable.js` (browser-direct), `reviewStore.uploadLargeToDrive` + `uploadSource`, and the **Supabase Storage upload fallback** in `storeSource` (the 50 MB fallback IS what produced the silent "oversize" dead end; Supabase Storage reads remain for pre-cutover files). ALL uploads — any size — now take the one chunked path; `sourceState`'s `oversize`/`too-large` states remain only to classify legacy never-stored records.
- **Post-review hardening (same session — a 5-lens adversarial review over the diff; 2 findings double-confirmed, 15 triaged):** the chunk endpoint no longer order-checks against its own best-effort bookkeeping (a missed progress write could 400 a healthy upload; Drive arbitrates offsets authoritatively); `/complete` is **idempotent** (the row is marked `recorded` and kept until expiry, so a retry after a lost response succeeds instead of 404ing a fully-successful upload — status CHECK extended via a second production migration) and a rolled-back session answers a distinct 410 + `sessionLost`; the client **short-circuits `sessionLost`** (no futile retry burn), **re-reads the auth token per request** via a getter (an upload outliving the ~1 h JWT no longer dies mid-flight), resets its retry budget when the /status probe shows progress (bodies landing while responses drop), validates the server's chunkSize granularity, and maps a quota failure at session-mint too; the **real failure cause** (e.g. "Google Drive is out of storage space") now reaches all three surfaces — the Library tray (`fileWarn`), the DocReview banner, and a NEW Stitcher store-failure banner (the Stitcher previously lost a failed store silently); split uploads share one continuous progress bar. **Known residuals (accepted, minor):** pdf.js range reads pin the open-time token, so a page first fetched >1 h after opening can 401 (re-open recovers); a tab closed in the seconds between the final chunk and `/complete` can orphan one Drive file (the 7-day purge removes only the row).
- Verify: live (concurrency/timing + real-project-data + range/parity — mandatory LIVE-VERIFY classes) → **V282**: signed-in ≥100 MB upload completes with a moving progress bar + lands in Drive; opens in the viewer with `206` responses in the network tab; killing the network mid-upload resumes (not restarts).
- Sandbox: full suite green (new `test/chunkedUpload.test.js` · `resumableProxy.test.js` · `uploadEndpoints.test.js` · `filesStream.test.js` — chunk math incl. final-short-chunk / exact-multiple / 256 KiB granularity, **308-as-success**, resume-from-offset, retry cap, quota short-circuit, foreign-uploadId → 404 before Drive is touched (B491), session-URI-never-in-a-response, init→308s→200 integration, Range→206 passthrough + the V150 two-account no-bytes regression) · lint 0 · build green + lazy chunks intact.

### B812 — The single-tab false "another window" toast BURST on a building resize (survived B759×2 + B811) — own-echo-by-rev `[Site Planner / persistence]` (bug) #site-planner #persistence #infra  *(owner-reported 2026-07-13 from chat — "itsstill doing it" with fresh screenshots of a BURST of "you (another window) changed a paving area / sidewalk / parking field you just edited — their version is showing", all one tab, mid building resize; owner confirmed he had already hard-reloaded, ruling out deploy lag. Branch `claude/site-debugging-y82heo`. Minted **B812** via `npm run next-id -- --against-main`. → V304. Third mechanism in the B759/B811 stale-refetch self-echo family; hunted + fixed via a 6-hypothesis reproduction workflow + THREE adversarial red-team rounds.)*
`[x]` **FIXED this session — the burst mechanism reproduced against the real engine, a bulletproof rev-based fix landed, and THREE red-team rounds drove out four residuals (the burst itself + delete-resurrection + serialization-drift + a >15s aged-echo edge); full suite 3728 green, `eslint` 0 errors, build green. The signed-in realtime end-to-end parks in ⏳ Verify → V304.**
- Verify: live — signed-in, **timing/race + concurrency/multi-writer** class (mandatory LIVE-VERIFY); the burst only manifests with a real Supabase realtime reconnect/tab-wake echoing real commits, which the logged-out sandbox can't exercise. Owed on V304.
- Origin: owner-reported 2026-07-13 (false-toast burst still firing after B759×2 + B811).
- **AUDIT-FIRST — root cause: a stale refetch that OMITS a just-committed element evicts it from the shadow, so its own echoes look foreign.** A resize re-commits a building's bonded children (sidewalk/paving/parking) several times fast. On a socket reconnect / tab-wake, `refetchReplace`'s fetch snapshot can OMIT a just-committed child (read-replica lag / the fetch predating the commit burst). `reconcileSeedRows` (B811) can only substitute into rows the fetch still CONTAINS — it cannot re-insert a dropped row — so `eng.seed()` evicts the child from the shadow. The child's own realtime echoes of earlier revs then arrive with no shadow entry (the rev guard can't catch them), no pending entry, and the single-slot `recentSent` held only the latest version → `sentMatches` missed the intermediate revs → a false `remote-upsert(authoredRecently)` per pre-final commit = the burst. B759×2 (data-match suppression) and B811 (present-but-stale reconcile) both left the OMITTED-element path open.
- **The fix (client-only, `lib/elementSync.js` + `lib/elementRows.js`), four layers, each closing a residual a red-team confirmed:**
  1. **`ownRevs` + `maxOwnRev` high-water (own-echo-by-rev).** Record EVERY server rev this tab's commits produce (ok / restore-self-dup / conflict-self-dup), plus a NEVER-time-pruned per-key high-water. `applyRemoteRow` ignores any non-tombstone echo where `isOwnRev(rev)` OR `rev <= maxOwnRev[key]`, before the pending branch — so it kills the `remote-upsert` AND `remote-while-dirty` variants. Server revs are monotonic per element, so anything at/below our high-water is definitively ours (or a foreign write we already superseded); a live foreign edit always lands strictly ABOVE it → still surfaces. The high-water (never pruned) closes the round-2 Angle-4 edge where a >15s-old own echo outlived the 15s `ownRevs`/`recentSent` windows.
  2. **`recentSent` → all-versions** (`Map<key,Map<json,at>>`): covers the pre-RPC / transport-failure window where no rev was learned, for every version put on the wire.
  3. **`stableStringify` → exact JSON wire semantics** (drop undefined-valued keys / functions / symbols, holes+undefined → `null`, Date via toJSON): the old `undefined` token made any element with an undefined property serialize DIFFERENTLY from its post-jsonb echo, permanently defeating every self-echo byte-compare AND producing phantom no-op diffs (red-team Angle 2). Floats were confirmed byte-stable — not a source of drift.
  4. **`reconcileSeedRows` tombstone-aware** (new 3rd arg `tombstonedSnapshot()`): a delete clears the shadow entry, so a stale-alive refetch would adopt the row verbatim and RESURRECT a just-deleted element (a TOMBSTONE-DELETES violation) + later mis-fire "was deleted by you (another window)" (red-team Angle 1). A fetched-alive row whose (kind,id) this tab tombstoned within the window at a rev ≤ our delete is kept deleted; a genuine re-create ABOVE the delete rev passes through alive.
- **Named rules:** LIVE-VERIFY (signed-in realtime → V304); AUDIT-FIRST (6-hypothesis repro workflow located the omitted-element eviction; reconciled against B759×2/B811's "sufficient" claims and found the open path); TOMBSTONE-DELETES (reconcileSeedRows now honours the delete floor — no resurrection); LOUD-FAILURE (own echoes suppressed only by rev identity / delete floor — every genuine foreign write/delete still surfaces, pinned by guard tests). No `MAP.md` change (no export add/remove; `reconcileSeedRows` gained a param but was already exported).
- **Verified (sandbox):** independent node repros of the burst (child dropped → 0 toasts), the resurrection (stays deleted; foreign re-create above delete stays alive), the undefined-prop echo (recognized; no phantom commit), and the >15s aged echo (recognized via high-water). `test/elementSync.test.js` +8 (burst; pending re-create; two genuine-foreign GUARDs; per-element rev keying; high-water aged echo; Angle-4; wire-semantics + no-phantom-diff for stableStringify) and `test/elementRows.test.js` +3 (no-resurrection; foreign-recreate-alive; no-tombstone back-compat). Full suite **3728** green; build green; lint 0. THREE red-team rounds: round 1 found delete-resurrection + serialization-drift; round 2 confirmed those closed + found the >15s aged-echo edge; **round 3 (final) — CLEAN, 0 breaks**: proved the high-water floor cannot over-suppress a foreign edit (server per-element rev monotonicity → any rev ≤ our high-water is superseded by our own write; a live foreign edit is always strictly above it; foreign deletes are exempt via the `!row.deleted_at` gate) + a 48-permutation full-flow integration (mixed edit/delete/create burst × stale-omit/rollback/show-alive × echo orderings × journal × transport-failure) all clean.
- **DEDUPE-FIRST:** same stale-refetch self-echo family as **B759** (the toast) and **B811** (the canvas-revert), but a DISTINCT mechanism (omitted-element shadow eviction, not present-but-stale) and a DISTINCT fix (rev-identity own-echo, not data-match), so filed as its own B# cross-referencing both — mirrors how B811 was filed alongside B759. Two round-2 latent gaps (foldJournal not recognizing the local-tombstone sentinel; boxed-primitive/BigInt in stableStringify) were proven UNREACHABLE in Planyr's element model (no journal survives the delete idle transition; elements never carry wrapper objects or BigInt) — noted, not fixed.
- **Documented KNOWN EDGES:** (1) **>15s stale-alive delete resurrection — the WITHIN-SESSION half is now CLOSED (round-4, owner "close all loose ends").** The floor `reconcileSeedRows` consults is now a NEVER-pruned per-key high-water (`maxDeleteRev`, session-long, mirrors `maxOwnRev`), cleared only when the element is genuinely re-created/restored — so an in-session reconnect ARBITRARILY LATER than a delete keeps it deleted. SAFE by monotonicity: the floor can only ever keep-deleted a fetched row at a rev ≤ the delete (already superseded); a genuine re-create always lands ABOVE it, so no legitimate element can be hidden even if the floor lingered (the same invariant red-teamed clean for `maxOwnRev`). The realtime-echo twin is already covered beyond 15s by `maxOwnRev` (the delete's rev is recorded, so a pre-delete echo is ≤ high-water → suppressed). **Residual (still open):** the cross-**RELOAD** variant — delete, then reload the page, and the post-reload fresh fetch hits a routed read-replica still lagged past the delete. In-memory floors don't survive a reload; fully closing it needs a DURABLE per-element delete tombstone (like B757's plan-level `deltomb`) with clear-on-restore. Config-dependent (Supabase PostgREST reads the primary by default → no lag → no resurrection unless read-replicas are explicitly routed) and SELF-CORRECTING (next edit → `edit-vs-deleted` → drops again). Deferred as higher-risk (persistence in the data-integrity path) than the edge is worth — owner-visible trade-off, revisit on request. (2) **Redundant re-create round-trip.** When a stale fetch OMITS an element this tab already synced, `foldNeverSyncedLocal` folds it back and `reconcile` re-enqueues a create; the server answers `exists` → adopted as an update (one extra rev + a redundant identical write). No toast, no data loss — a benign wasted round-trip, later suppressed by the high-water floor.

### B811 — A resized building's bonded sidewalk / paving "separates" (snaps back) when a stale refetch re-seeds the shadow `[Site Planner / persistence]` (bug) #site-planner #persistence #infra  *(owner-reported 2026-07-13 from chat — "it's separating the sidewalk and paving and building when i change the building size"; a screenshot showed a "you (another window) changed a parking field you just edited — their version is showing" toast during the resize. Owner confirmed it stopped after reloading onto the B759 (×2) build. Branch `claude/site-debugging-y82heo`. Minted **B811** via `npm run next-id -- --against-main`. → V303. The CANVAS-REVERT twin of B759 (same stale-seed root cause, different symptom).)*
`[x]` **FIXED this session — sandbox verified (a node repro against the real engine + 8 new unit tests; full suite 3717 green, `eslint` 0 errors, build green); the signed-in realtime end-to-end parks in ⏳ Verify → V303.** A building's sidewalk/paving/parking are separate elements bonded to it (`attachedTo`) and DO reflow flush on resize (`refitChildren`/`fitKid`), so the "separation" wasn't a geometry bug — it was a stale copy of a just-committed piece getting shoved back onto the canvas.
- Verify: live — signed-in, **timing/race + concurrency/multi-writer** class (mandatory LIVE-VERIFY); the revert only manifests with a real Supabase realtime reconnect/tab-wake landing a stale fetch, which the logged-out sandbox can't exercise. Owed on V303.
- Origin: owner-reported 2026-07-13 (bonded pieces separating on building resize).
- **AUDIT-FIRST — NOT a `refitChildren` bug; it's `refetchReplace` re-seeding from a STALE fetch.** An Explore pass confirmed bonded RECTANGULAR children (sidewalk/paving/parking/dock stack) already track a resize via `refitChildren`→`fitKid`/`relayoutSide`. The real cause is the same stale-seed root as B759: `refetchReplace` (SitePlanner.jsx, fires on every socket (re)join / tab-wake / 4s fallback) `await`s `fetchElements` then `eng.seed(rows)` + `replace(setEls, merged)`. When that fetch's snapshot PREDATES a batch this tab just committed (resize → the building AND its bonded children commit as one batch), the seed rolls the shadow's revs BACKWARD and the rebuild puts the PRE-resize child positions back on the canvas — the building keeps its new size (already on canvas) but a bonded piece snaps back = "separating". `foldNeverSyncedLocal` only covers ZERO-row elements and `foldJournal` is cleared once a commit succeeds, so a committed-then-refetched element was protected by neither. (B759's toast fix suppresses the matching false toast and heals via the echo IF it arrives after the stale replace — but the revert itself needed closing.)
- **The fix (new pure `reconcileSeedRows` in `lib/elementRows.js` + 3-line wiring in `refetchReplace`):** before seeding, replace any fetched row THIS tab's shadow holds a STRICTLY NEWER rev for with our committed data+rev+z (read `eng.shadowSnapshot()` BEFORE `seed` clears it; feed the SAME reconciled rows to `seed` AND `rowsToModel` so shadow and canvas stay in lockstep). Everything else passes through: a foreign-advanced or caught-up row stays canonical (a genuinely stale reconnecting tab has LOWER shadow revs than the server → adopts the server rows → V229 #5 stale-tab clobber guard holds), and a tombstone row is never overridden (TOMBSTONE-DELETES — no resurrection; edit-vs-delete still resolves via the conflict matrix).
- **Named rules:** LIVE-VERIFY (signed-in realtime timing/race → V303); AUDIT-FIRST (Explore-confirmed the geometry reflow is correct, traced the revert to `refetchReplace`'s stale seed); TOMBSTONE-DELETES (tombstone rows are never overridden by a live shadow entry); LOUD-FAILURE (no silent clobber — a foreign-newer row is always adopted, never masked). Docs: `MAP.md` regenerated (new `reconcileSeedRows` export).
- **Verified (sandbox):** a standalone node repro (`seed(fresh) → commit a child move → reconcileSeedRows(staleRows, shadow) → rowsToModel`) reverted to the old position WITHOUT the fix and stayed at the new position WITH it, while a foreign rev-9 row was still adopted (V229). `test/elementRows.test.js` +8 (replace-stale; keep-when-equal; keep-foreign-advanced/V229; never-override-tombstone; leave-unknown-row; malformed-json-safe; empty/non-Map inputs; input-immutability). Full suite 3717 green; build green; lint 0 errors.
- **DEDUPE-FIRST:** same stale-seed root-cause family as **B759** (reopened ×2 for the toast) but a DISTINCT symptom (a canvas REVERT, not a false toast) and a DISTINCT code path (`refetchReplace`/`reconcileSeedRows` vs `applyRemoteRow`), so filed as its own B# cross-referencing B759 rather than a B759 leg. Related folds it complements: `foldNeverSyncedLocal` (B756, zero-row elements) and `foldJournal` (NEW-F4, journaled failed commits) — `reconcileSeedRows` closes the third gap (successfully-committed elements a stale fetch predates).

- Origin: owner-reported 2026-07-11 (spurious concurrent-edit notification, single tab); recurrence owner-reported 2026-07-13 (burst screenshot).
- **AUDIT-FIRST — it's the NEW element-sync toast (B673), NOT the retired whole-doc "changed in another session" banner.** The wording the owner saw ("someone else… or me in another tab") is the B673 conflict toast whose editor name resolves to **"you (another window)"** for the user's own uid (`lib/editorNames.js`). The legacy doc-level banner was retired by architecture (B672 — slim header, no whole-doc payload to fight over), so this is a genuinely new false-positive in the per-element realtime read path.
- **Root cause (`lib/elementSync.js applyRemoteRow`): our OWN write echoing back over realtime is mis-read as a foreign edit.** Supabase realtime echoes a tab's own writes back to it; `applyRemoteRow` is the only guard, and it never checks `row.updated_by`/`deleted_by` against `selfUid` — it relies on (a) rev idempotency (`rev <= shad.rev`) and (b) a data-equality proxy (`sameData`). The realtime READ path (`applyRemoteRow`) had three holes; a red-team of the first fix then found two more on the WRITE-RESULT path (`processResults`) — **five** single-tab self-echo false positives, each reproduced live against the real `createElementSync` engine:
  1. **Edit-in-flight echo vs a newer queued edit (the reported one).** During active manipulation the echo of an in-flight commit (data **D1**, rev N+1) races ahead of its own RPC result, so the shadow rev is still N (< N+1) → the rev guard passes; meanwhile a **newer** edit (**D2**) queued into `dirty`, and the old code compared the echo only against the `dirty || inflight` **winner** (D2). D1 ≠ D2 → fired `remote-while-dirty` → *"you (another window) also just edited Building 3 — your version is being kept."*
  2. **Delete-in-flight tombstone echo.** Our own delete's tombstone echo (before its RPC result) can never satisfy `sameData` (the `!row.deleted_at` guard forces it false) → same false toast on a single-tab delete.
  3. **Stale post-delete echo RESURRECTS the element (worst — a data effect, not just a toast).** After editing then deleting an element, the delete's `shadow.delete()` removes the rev ceiling, so a delayed echo of the pre-delete UPDATE sails past every guard → `remote-upsert` puts the deleted element **back on the canvas** AND (authored within 15s) fires *"you (another window) changed … you just edited."*
  4. **Timed-out-but-committed EDIT (write-result path).** The 8 s `COMMIT_TIMEOUT_MS` aborts a commit that actually landed server-side; the retry re-flushes at the stale expected rev, hits OUR OWN committed row (a `conflict` whose `data` === our data), and `processResults` emitted `edit-vs-edit-lost-race` → *"was also just edited by you (another window) — your version was kept."*
  5. **Timed-out-but-committed RESTORE (write-result path).** Same mechanism on the Restore action → a false `restore-conflict` toast (*"already restored or edited by you (another window)"*).
  Splitting a truck court off a building is a multi-element create/move/delete gesture, so the read-path trio (1–3) can all fire at once; (4)/(5) need the rarer commit-timeout window.
- **The fix (`lib/elementSync.js`, client-only, no schema change):**
  - *(1) `applyRemoteRow` pending branch:* recognize the echo as OURS by matching the row against **either** pending serialization — the in-flight batch entry **and** the dirty entry (not just the winner) → adopt silently, no event.
  - *(2) pending branch:* a pending `delete` + an incoming tombstone is our own delete echo → silent.
  - *(3) new `tombstoned` map (key → {rev, at}):* on a committed delete, remember the delete's rev; a later non-tombstone echo at a rev **no newer** than that delete is a stale pre-delete self-echo → ignored (no resurrect, no toast). A genuine re-create by another session arrives at a **higher** rev, clears the floor, and comes through.
  - *(4)/(5) `processResults` conflict branches:* before emitting `edit-vs-edit-lost-race` / `restore-conflict`, if the conflicting live row's `data` **equals our own op's data**, it's our own timed-out-but-committed write echoing back → adopt the fresh rev silently, no re-commit, no toast. **Gated on data-equality, not `updated_by === selfUid` alone**, so a genuine same-account two-window conflict carrying *different* data still surfaces per the B673 matrix.
  - *(residual) new `recentSent` map (key → {json, at}):* the last serialization this tab put on the wire — it SURVIVES a transport-failure `inflight` clear, so a committed-but-unacked write's realtime echo is still recognized as ours even after `onTransportFailure` requeued a newer edit into `dirty`.
  All new memories are pruned to the 15 s window so they stay tiny. A genuine other-window write matches **neither** pending entry / carries **different** data / arrives **above** the delete floor, so real two-window conflicts still surface loudly; two writes that produce byte-identical data aren't a conflict anyway (the pre-existing `sameData`-adopt-silently semantics). No weakening of genuine multi-writer detection (a dedicated guard test pins this).
- **Why the read-path guards are SUFFICIENT on the success lifecycle:** the (1)/(2) window is exactly "echo passed `rev <= shad.rev`", true only while the commit is in flight (shadow not yet advanced). `inflightKeys` is cleared in the flush `finally` block in the SAME microtask as `processResults` advances the shadow rev — so the moment inflight clears, the rev guard already suppresses late echoes; the tombstone floor (3) covers the post-delete window, and `recentSent` covers the one exception (a `ok:false` transport failure clears inflight WITHOUT advancing the rev). The windows are complementary with no gap.
- **Named rules:** LIVE-VERIFY (signed-in timing/race + concurrency class → V273); AUDIT-FIRST (traced the code, ruled out the retired whole-doc banner, reconciled against the B672/B673 claims); TOMBSTONE-DELETES (the new tombstone floor extends the delete's authority so a stale echo can't resurrect); LOUD-FAILURE (self-echoes are silenced by data-identity, never by blanket-swallowing a class of events — genuine conflicts stay loud). Docs: no `MAP.md` change (no file add/remove/export change — pure logic inside `elementSync.js`).
- **Verified (sandbox):** four standalone node repros confirmed the reported bug + the delete/resurrection/timeout variants pre-fix and their absence post-fix. `test/elementSync.test.js` +9 regression tests — in-flight edit echo w/ newer queued edit → silent; in-flight delete tombstone echo → silent; stale post-delete edit echo → not resurrected; a genuine re-create above the delete rev still upserts; a genuine foreign edit (data ≠ inflight AND ≠ dirty) still fires `remote-while-dirty`; a timed-out-but-committed edit whose retry conflicts with our own row → silent; same for restore; a timed-out edit whose retry conflicts with DIFFERENT data still fires `edit-vs-edit`; a committed-but-unacked realtime echo after a newer edit queued during backoff → silent. All 39 elementSync tests green; full suite **3394** green; `eslint` clean; build green.
- **Note (the idempotency-key alternative):** paths (4)/(5) could alternatively be fixed with a per-op idempotency key on the `commit_elements` RPC (a live-DB change). The data-equality guard is the equivalent client-only fix (the server already returns the conflicting row's `data`), so no schema migration is needed and the whole class is closed in one branch.
- **DEDUPE-FIRST:** NOT a recurrence of B612/B455/B460/B558/B596 (those are the retired whole-doc "changed in another session" banner). First filed false-positive in the B672/B673 per-element realtime toast path. Related-but-distinct from B672's V229 #5 (a lost-UPDATE data-loss on refetch); path #3 above is a spurious RESURRECTION, #1/#2/#4/#5 are spurious notifications.

### B757 — Deliberately-deleted PLAN can resurrect on reload/sign-in when its cloud delete never landed (offline / transient) — no DURABLE record-delete tombstone `[Site Planner / Persistence]` (bug — data-integrity) #site-planner #persistence  *(chat 2026-07-11, from an adversarial-review brief — "NEW-4 (batch 2): deleted plan resurrects after a failed/unlanded cloud delete". Minted **B757** via `npm run next-id`. Branch `claude/backlog-sharing-realtime-site-ioc65x`.)*
`[x]` **IMPLEMENTED this session — sandbox verified (7 new unit tests, full suite 3,391 green, build green, lint 0 errors); the signed-in offline/cross-device round-trip parks in ⏳ Verify → V271.** A deliberate whole-plan delete now sticks across reload / sign-in / device sync instead of coming back.
- Verify: live — offline + cross-device delete durability is a mandatory LIVE-VERIFY class (concurrency / multi-writer timing). The pure suppression/retry logic is unit-proven; the real "delete offline → reload signed-in → still gone" is owed on V271.
- Origin: filed 2026-07-11 from the two-batch review brief; **most of that brief was already handled** (see the DEDUPE note below) — this residual is the one genuinely-open data-integrity gap it surfaced.
- **AUDIT-FIRST — the reported premises were HALF stale; the real gap is narrower and confirmed in code.** `cloudDelete` ALREADY does an affected-row check (`.delete().eq("id",id).select("id")` → typed `interpretDelete`, `cloudSync.js`), `deleteSite` ALREADY awaits it and `deleteSiteGroup` surfaces a LOUD "may reappear" on a failure / 0-row no-op (B372/B468). What was missing: the B372 guard is the **in-memory, per-tab `recentlyDeleted` Set** — cleared on reload and consulted **only in `saveSite`**. It does NOT stop `pullCloud` → `mergePulledSites` from RE-ADDING a cloud row whose delete never landed. So: signed-in, go offline, delete a plan → local removal + the loud warning, but on the next reload/sign-in the surviving cloud row is re-inserted (`map[id] = local ? merge : n`) → the plan is back. B372 fixed the same-session mount-flush half; this is the cross-reload/offline half it explicitly deferred.
- **The fix (`lib/storage.js` + a tiny `onStore` filter):** durable per-user `{id: ts}` tombstones (`planarfit:sites:deltomb:v1:<uid>`, bounded to 300). `deleteSite` records one; `mergePulledSites(existing, cloud, uid, tombstones)` now (a) SUPPRESSES an **owned** cloud row still pending removal (drops it from the merge → no resurrection) and flags it for retry, (b) KEEPS a row whose cloud copy is genuinely NEWER than the delete (`updatedAt > ts` = a real later edit on another device → the delete is stale — cross-device safety, mirrors B18/B511), (c) drops the tombstone for a not-ours (teammate) row or one the cloud already removed; `pullCloud` clears the honored tombstones and **RETRIES `cloudDelete`** for the pending ones, clearing each only on a confirmed removal. Nothing is dropped for a NON-tombstoned id — the change is byte-identical to today whenever no tombstone applies (unit-pinned).
- **Named rules:** TOMBSTONE-DELETES (a deliberate delete records a durable tombstone for the FULL record so a merge/sync can't resurrect it); LOUD-FAILURE (the existing "may reappear" banner stays; the retry now actually makes it land); LIVE-VERIFY (offline/cross-device timing → V271).
- **Also fixed (same delete/sync-hardening theme):** (1) **Doc Review `deleteReview`** now does the SAME `.select("id")` row-count check (`reviewStore.js`) — it previously reported `ok:true` on a 0-row no-op (silent survivor); it returns `removed` now, matching the sites path. (2) **`onStore` cross-tab filter** now excludes the `:history:` and `:deltomb:` sub-namespaces — the `planarfit:sites:` prefix also matched the version-history ring, so every default save ran the signed-out cross-tab fold 2–3× per edit (harmless no-op via the B591 signature check, but wasteful); tightened to the actual store keys.
- **Verified here (sandbox):** `test/storage.test.js` +7 (suppress owned-pending; keep-on-newer-cross-device; clear-on-landed; don't-suppress-teammate; never-drop-non-tombstoned; backward-compat with no tombstones) · full suite 3,391 green · build green · lint 0 errors · `MAP.md` regenerated (new `recordSiteTombstone`/`clearSiteTombstone` exports).
- **⏳ V271 (live, signed-in):** on planyr.io — delete a plan while offline (DevTools Offline), reload signed-in → the plan STAYS gone (and the cloud row is actually removed once back online); a plan legitimately edited on device B after being deleted on device A survives (cross-device exception). See VERIFICATION.md.
- **DEDUPE-FIRST — the rest of the two-batch brief maps to already-shipped work (no new numbers minted for these):** batch-1 NEW-1 (share never sets team_id) + NEW-2 (realtime RLS "leak") = **B714** (⏳ V244; share DOES set team_id — the bug was autosave reverting it, fixed; realtime is RLS-gated by schema, no leak); NEW-3 (cold-start `reading 'length'` crash) = **B690** (Done) + **B692** (⏳ V232 root-cause sanitize); NEW-4 (offline element lost-update, "reproduced twice") = the **B672** V229 #5 recurrence (fixed) + **B673/B674/B756**. Batch-2: NEW-2 (writeSites strips only underlay) = STALE (B473/B474 shed all three raster homes); NEW-3 (cloud push skipped on local-write fail) = **B473** (`pushModelToCloud`); NEW-5 (phantom "reload before saving" from a fold) = STALE (the B672 architecture retired that banner + the signed-in fold); NEW-6 (wire tombstones into all delete handlers) = **B556/B569/B596/B598/B612** (done). NEW-1 (autosave re-serializes the whole account — a real perf enhancement, not a bug) folded into **B479** as a bullet.

### B756 — DATA LOSS: a new signed-in site created from the map ("Plan N parcels →") silently loses ALL its parcels `[Site Planner / persistence]` (bug) #site-planner #persistence #infra  *(owner-reported 2026-07-10 from chat — "I deleted [the Bane site], selected all the same parcels, clicked start plan, it created the plan but then all my parcels went away." Branch `claude/parcels-disappear-plan-bug-iofgka`. → V270 renumbered from V269 on merge-in of `origin/main`, which took V269 for the parcel outline-style editor.)*
`[x]` **FIXED this session — sandbox + integration verified (10 new unit/integration tests, full suite green, build green); the signed-in end-to-end parks in ⏳ Verify → V270.** Confirmed live in Supabase: the reported site `smrfgk3pz3ii` "27211 Hoyt LN, Katy" has 0 parcel rows, 0 tombstones, 0 `site_elements` rows total — the parcels were **never committed**, then wiped. Same 0/0/0 loss on GREEN RIVER, HOLLISTER, WAYSIDE (all created after the 2026-07-06 cutover); every pre-cutover site kept its parcels.
- Verify: live — signed-in, timing/race + concurrency/multi-writer class (mandatory LIVE-VERIFY); the pure fold + engine-commit wiring is proven by unit/integration tests, the real signed-in "Plan parcels → reload → rows exist" end-to-end is owed on V270.
- Origin: owner-reported 2026-07-10 (data loss on new sites planned from the map).
- **AUDIT-FIRST — REGRESSION from the B672 read cutover, not the delete.** The delete-then-replan the owner described is INCIDENTAL; the causal flow is "create a new site from the map while signed in." Since B672 (commit `83411c8`, 2026-07-06, entrenched by `ec7b9fc` 2026-07-07) signed-in reads are canonical from the `site_elements` table and `slimForCloud` strips all 5 element collections out of the cloud `sites.data` header. But `newSiteFromMap` (`SitePlannerApp.jsx`) only writes the parcels to localStorage + that slim header — **nothing commits a brand-new site's initial parcels to `site_elements`** (`explodeModel` has zero runtime callers; no DB trigger explodes the blob). On first planner mount, `refetchReplace` (`SitePlanner.jsx`) fetches 0 rows, rebuilds `next.parcels=[]` (rows-canonical), and `setParcels([])` **wipes the canvas BEFORE** the seed-gated write engine (`reconcile()` is a no-op until `seed()`, which runs only inside `refetchReplace`) could ever diff/commit them; the follow-on autosave then `writeMirror()`s the empty state over localStorage too. Net: 0 rows, empty header, empty mirror → every parcel gone. It's a genuine race (some new sites survived only because the user re-drew shapes after the silent wipe, which then committed).
- **The fix (`SitePlanner.jsx refetchReplace` + a pure helper in `lib/elementRows.js`):** `foldNeverSyncedLocal(next, stateRef.current, rowKeys, isHuskParcel)` folds NEVER-SYNCED local-only elements — those on the pre-replace canvas whose `(kind,id)` has NO row at all (checked against LIVE **and** TOMBSTONE rows) — back into `next` before the replace, so they survive AND the existing `eng.reconcile(merged)` enqueues them as creates → they finally reach `site_elements`. Bounding the fold to zero-row `(kind,id)`s is what keeps it safe: anything that already has a row is left untouched, so rows stay canonical.
- **Named rules:** LOUD-FAILURE (a silent empty-save passed the B473/B592 count/membership check because want==got==0 — this closes that hole for new sites); TOMBSTONE-DELETES (a remotely-deleted element has a tombstone row → excluded from the fold → never resurrected); LIVE-VERIFY (signed-in race class → V270). Docs: `MAP.md` regenerated same commit (new `foldNeverSyncedLocal` export).
- **Verified (sandbox):** `test/elementRows.test.js` +8 (fold keeps a never-synced local parcel; adopts a live row; never resurrects a tombstone; drops husks; no dup; all 5 collections; `(kind,id)` keying vs the legacy e6327 class; input-immutability) and `test/elementSync.test.js` +2 integration (seed([]) + fold + reconcile → exactly one `create` commit; a row-backed stale local copy is NOT re-committed — V229 preserved). Full suite green, build green.
- **Safety vs V229 #5 (the exact clobber the cutover added `refetchReplace` to prevent):** a reconnecting stale tab holds old geometry ONLY for elements that already have rows → those `(kind,id)`s are in `rowKeys` → excluded from the fold → row adopted, never a stale rev-guarded re-commit. The fold can only ever emit *creates* for ids the server has literally never seen.
- **DEDUPE-FIRST:** recurrence-of-CLASS of **B473** (Done — "a NEW site's edits vanish on reload when signed in"), whose regression guard `ui-audit/verify-new-site-save.mjs` runs LOGGED-OUT ONLY, which is exactly why the B672 cutover reopened new-site data loss undetected. Filed as a NEW B# (not a B473 reopen) because the mechanism is entirely new (the row cutover, not the blob path). Overlaps **B692** (husk-parcel funnel — same `refetchReplace` husk-filter code); the fold reuses `isHuskParcel` so a husk is never folded.
- **Owner note (recovery):** the fix stops all FUTURE loss. Already-lost sites (Katy/GREEN RIVER/HOLLISTER/WAYSIDE) have no cloud copy of their parcels; the just-planned Katy site is trivially re-created (re-select parcels → Plan). See V270 / OWNER-TODO for whether older ones held work worth recovering from a device's local version history.
- **Live-verified 2026-07-18 (Cowork session, signed-in on planyr.io) — V270 steps 1-4 PASS:** a new parcel planned from the map on the WAYSIDE site (`smrqq1le5zu3`) stayed on the canvas past the realtime resubscribe, survived a reload, and a direct Supabase check confirmed the row landed in `site_elements` with zero tombstones — the exact create-path this item fixed. Step 5 (the V229 second-tab regression guard) is **blocked, not failed**: this session's synthetic clicks couldn't select the parcel on the map canvas to drive an edit (a browser-automation targeting gap, not a product symptom). V270 not archived (step 5 open, needs a real interactive-mouse retest).

### B625 — Metes-and-bounds deed rotates grossly off-angle on "Align to county parcel" (×2) `[Site Planner]` (bug) #site-planner #coordinates #gis  *(owner-reported 2026-07-02 on Grand Port; original fix shipped that session. RECURRENCE filed 2026-07-10 from chat (Cowork "NEW-1") — the align tool now over-rotates. Reopened per DEDUPE-FIRST / recurrence rule (B636) rather than minting a new B#; branch `claude/metes-bounds-rotation-bug-x58zih`.)*
`[x]` **RE-FIXED this session (recurrence) — sandbox + headless verified; the real-deed/real-parcel end-to-end parks in ⏳ Verify → V197.** The B625 align feature swung a plotted deed to a gross angle (tens of degrees, "~45°") instead of the intended small (~1.5°) basis-of-bearings correction, so it didn't overlay.
- Verify: live — repro cites real county-parcel project data + GIS import (mandatory LIVE-VERIFY class); the pure alignment math is proven by unit tests, the signed-in real-deed end-to-end is owed on V197.
- Recurrence: 2026-07-10 — owner (Cowork, "NEW-1"): a 67.63-ac deed lands over the 67.004-ac county parcel but badly rotated; a 42.32-ac deed floats with no parcel under it and still gets rotated.
- **AUDIT-FIRST — real cause (the reporter's projection / sign-flip / units leads were ruled OUT):** the bearing→vector parser (`metesAndBounds.js` `bearingToAz`/`callsToPath`) is correct (azimuth CW-from-north, dx=sin, dy=−cos, y-down), and deed rings + county rings (`arcgis.js lngLatRingToFeet`) share the SAME y-down feet frame — no sign/mirror bug. The gross rotation came from `deedAlign.js solveDeedAlignment`: it found the rotation by a **full ±180° sweep** minimizing a correspondence-free symmetric nearest-vertex RMS with scale locked to 1, so a near-symmetric / generalized outline snapped to a spurious 45/90/180° alias (the `confident` gate checks residual only, never rotation magnitude). `bestDeedFit` (`SitePlanner.jsx`) compounded it by force-fitting to the lowest-residual parcel even when none corresponded (the floating 42-ac case).
- **The fix (two parts):** (A) `deedAlign.js` — bound the rotation sweep and its clamped refine to a physically-plausible window `MAX_ALIGN_ROT_DEG = 20°` (covers grid convergence ~1.5° + record/magnetic basis slop; excludes the aliases); a deed that only fits past the window is reported not-confident, never force-rotated (reversed winding needs no wide sweep — the point-set metric handles it). (B) `SitePlanner.jsx bestDeedFit` — a spatial-correspondence gate (deed must overlap the parcel by ≥ half the smaller footprint via `polyIntersectArea`, AND their areas within ~4:3) so a non-corresponding parcel can't hijack the fit; with none qualifying it falls back to the small, safe grid-convergence correction / "no parcel" message, and the post-plot banner no longer false-claims an offset.
- **Tests:** `test/deedAlign.test.js` — 3 new (13 total): a near-symmetric deed rotated ~1.5° recovers ~1.5° not a 90° alias (would FAIL under the old ±180° sweep — the exact regression); a 45°-off deed clamps to ≤20° + reports not-confident; the `opts.maxRotDeg` override is honoured. Full suite **3302 green** · lint 0 errors · build green · `MAP.md` regenerated (new `MAX_ALIGN_ROT_DEG` export).
- **DEDUPE-FIRST:** this IS the recurrence of B625 (same feature / module / symbols / user goal). Related, NOT dupes: `alignToParcelEdge` (element-edge snapper, bails on polygons) · `overlayAlign.solveSimilarityLSQ` (scanned-overlay similarity fit, a separate system) · B626 (the stale-sliver *parse*, resolved).

- Verify: live
- Origin: filed 2026-07-10 from chat (owner drop)
- **AUDIT-FIRST — the detection already existed.** `resolveDrainageContext` already queries the real HCFCD channel centerline layer (`HCFCD/Channels/MapServer/0`) → `channel.near`, and resolves COH-vs-HCFCD via `identifyJurisdiction`. The panel fed `drainsToHcfcdChannel: drainCtxData?.channel?.near ?? null` with NO user override, so when the HCFCD host was unreachable (or the visible channel isn't an HCFCD unit) `near` came back `null` and the tool hedged "…is unknown," dead-ending the user.   • **"Remember it"** — a slim, geometry-free summary of the last check + the two override choices persist in `settings.drainage` (rides the existing settings autosave — NO schema/version bump); on reload the readout shows last-known facts with a "Remembered from your last check on <date> — re-check to refresh" line.
- **Pure helpers (new, unit-tested):** `effectiveChannelDischarge`, `effectiveReviewer`, `DETENTION_AUTHORITY_CHOICES`, `slimDrainageContext`/`hydrateDrainageContext` (round-trip: rule + watershed overlays re-derived, geometry dropped) in `lib/detentionRules.js`. The engine's `drainsToHcfcdChannel` true/false/null branches were already tested.
- **Deliberate boundary (not changed):** the owner/primary-source-verified rule that a >20-ac COH tract defers to HCFCD's rate even on "No" (COH IDM Table 9.5, V204) is surfaced + explained, not re-calibrated — a "No drops it to Houston-rate-only" change would be a separate rule decision.
- **Named rules:** LOUD-FAILURE (a failed channel/jurisdiction lookup shows an honest hedge + the override, never a silent all-clear), AUDIT-FIRST (reconciled against the existing detection engine — extend, not fork), MODULE-SCOPE-COMPONENTS (controls are inline JSX, no inner component). Docs: `MAP.md` regenerated same commit.

### B746 — Ctrl+Z doesn't always work; make it Bluebeam-style when drawing an element `[Site Planner / Doc Review]` (bug) #site-planner #doc-review #selection #markup #ui #persistence  *(owner-dropped 2026-07-10 from chat; provisional **B745**, renumbered **B746** — concurrent `main` (PR #566) took B745 for the GIS vector/thin-line export split + V257. Per repo precedent the commit keeps the provisional **B745** label; only the backlog + verification IDs bumped (→ B746 / V258). Branch `claude/ctrl-z-undo-behavior-552b1t`.)*
`[x]` **IMPLEMENTED + unit + headless-e2e verified this session; parks in ⏳ Verify only for the live-only edges below → V258.** Two complaints, one investigation (5-lens adversarial workflow, 15 confirmed root causes RC-1..RC-9): (a) **"Ctrl+Z should work like Bluebeam when drawing"** and (b) **"Ctrl+Z doesn't always work."** The Site Planner's Ctrl+Z always ran a *global* undo — it never stepped back the vertex you were placing — so mid-draw it either did nothing or silently reverted a previously-finished shape while the half-drawn one stayed on screen. Now, in all three canvases (Site Planner, Review, Stitcher), Ctrl+Z **peels the last placed vertex while a multi-point draft is in progress and only falls through to a global undo when no draft is active** (matches Bluebeam + the Review/Stitcher modules, which already did this). Plus a batch of "undo did nothing / undid the wrong thing" reliability fixes.
- Verify: live
- Origin: filed 2026-07-10 from chat
- **DEDUPE-FIRST:** searched Open / ⏳ Verify / Done (BACKLOG*.md + BACKLOG_OPEN.md, `^### B` + `#selection`/`#markup`) — **net-new**. Related, NOT dupes: **B32/B105** (no-op history dedup — the engine this builds on), **B315** (undo read a stale baseline — the `stateRef` fix reused here), **B303** (Review's own mid-draw vertex step-back — the sibling pattern the Site Planner was missing), **B567** (color-pick one-frame session — the coalescing pattern extended to opacity sliders here).
- **AUDIT-FIRST — 9 code-confirmed root causes (each adversarially verified):**
  - **RC-1 (Bluebeam, primary):** `SitePlanner.jsx` Ctrl+Z called `undo()` directly, never `removeLastVertex()`. Fixed to `else if (!removeLastVertex()) undo();` (mirrors `DocReview.jsx` / `Stitcher.jsx`).
  - **RC-2:** `applySnapshot` didn't clear in-progress drafts → a redo/undo could leave phantom draft points floating over reverted geometry. Now nulls every draft (mirrors the siblings).
  - **RC-3:** `removeLastVertex` had no branch for the parcel-edge easement run (`easeEdges`) or the ditch cross-section point (`xsecPts`), and `xsecMode/xsecPts` were missing from the keydown deps → stale closure. Added both branches + deps.
  - **RC-4:** Split tool double-destruction (Ctrl+Z discarded the whole cut path AND reverted a prior action) — falls out for free once RC-1 lands (mid-split Ctrl+Z now peels one cut point). Verified gone.
  - **RC-5:** Edits that recorded NO undo frame — element fill-opacity slider, underlay opacity slider, sheet-overlay opacity slider + %-box, and **Remove aerial underlay**. Now each records exactly one frame.
  - **RC-6:** Standards / type-style edits called `pushHistory()` but `settings` isn't in the snapshot → a **dead frame** that misdirected the next Ctrl+Z into deleting a prior shape. Removed those pushes (Standards are prefs, non-undoable like the 20+ sibling settings fields) — no more misdirection.
  - **RC-7:** Markup fill-opacity slider *flooded* history (one frame per `onChange`) → ~20 Ctrl+Z to undo one drag. All opacity sliders now share one `sliderHistory` coalescing helper (one frame per drag).
  - **RC-8:** Sheet-overlay position was `Math.round`ed in `histKey`, so a sub-foot (zoomed-in) nudge was dedup'd away as a no-op and skipped by undo. Removed the rounding (underlay position never was).
  - **RC-9:** The keydown input-guard diverged — Review/Stitcher skipped only INPUT/TEXTAREA, so a focused `<select>`'s Ctrl+Z hit the canvas. Added SELECT/contentEditable so all three modules gate identically.
  - **RC-10 (found LIVE 2026-07-18 via V258 step 3, ×1 recurrence on this item):** the keydown input-guard (`t.tagName === "INPUT" || …`) treated ANY focused `<input>` — including a `type="range"` slider — as "typing" and unconditionally swallowed Ctrl+Z/Ctrl+Y. A range input has no native browser undo to protect, so select a Building → drag its Fill-opacity slider → press Ctrl+Z WITHOUT deselecting first → silently no-op (confirmed live 3× on project "ZZ-THROWAWAY-TEST", `SitePlanner.jsx` Properties panel). The toolbar Undo button and a click-away-then-Ctrl+Z both worked fine, and the reverted value persisted correctly across reload once undone — isolating the bug to the keyboard-dispatch guard, not persistence. Fixed by narrowing the guard: it now lets ONLY the Ctrl/Cmd+Z / +Y chord through when focus is on a `type="range"` input; every other shortcut (arrows, Delete, letter tools) still respects the guard while a slider has focus, since those DO have real native slider behavior or would nudge/delete the still-selected element out from under the user.
- **Fix (files):** `SitePlanner.jsx` (Ctrl+Z routing, `removeLastVertex`→pure resolver, `applySnapshot` draft-clear, `histKey` overlay precision, 5 opacity sliders + remove-underlay history, RC-6 dead-push removals, deps; RC-10's narrowed keydown guard); new pure **`lib/drafts.js`** (`resolveDraftStepBack`); `DocReview.jsx` + `Stitcher.jsx` (RC-9 guard).
- **Verified (sandbox/headless):** new **`test/drafts.test.js`** (10 cases — every draft type incl. the two new ones + the "no draft → null" fall-through that keeps a real Ctrl+Z from being swallowed) · full unit suite green (3232) · `test/history.test.js` still green · build green · MAP.md regenerated (+`lib/drafts.js`) · **new `e2e/ctrlz-undo.spec.js` (3 tests, LOGGED-OUT via "Start blank", green in headless Chromium): mid-draw Ctrl+Z peels a vertex (finished polygon has 3 pts, not 5); mid-draw Ctrl+Z does NOT revert a previously-committed shape; no-draft Ctrl+Z is a real global undo + redo.**
- **RC-10 fix + verified this session (2026-07-18):** full unit suite green (4522) · lint 0 errors · build green · `e2e/ctrlz-undo.spec.js` gained a new describe block (2 tests, LOGGED-OUT, green in headless Chromium): (a) drag a Building's Fill-opacity slider then Ctrl+Z **WITHOUT deselecting** now correctly reverts it — matching the toolbar Undo button, including its documented side effect of deselecting/closing the Properties panel — and Ctrl+Shift+Z redoes it; (b) a no-regression check confirms Ctrl+Z with focus in a REAL text field (a callout's inline `<textarea>`, placement already on the undo stack) still does **NOT** fire app undo. Sanity-checked the test itself by reverting the guard fix and confirming the new test (a) fails against the old code, then re-applied the fix and reran green — the test genuinely catches the regression, not a false positive.
- **⏳ V258 (live, planyr.io):** the few edges the logged-out sandbox can't confirm — (1) a **sub-foot sheet-overlay nudge at high zoom** undoes cleanly (RC-8, zoom-dependent-rendering class); (2) **Remove aerial underlay → Ctrl+Z restores it**, incl. the reload-after-undo persistence edge where the image was cloud/idb-backed (RC-5, signed-in persistence class) — **still fully pending, untouched by RC-10**; (3) opacity-slider Ctrl+Z **mechanism** is now headless-proven fixed (RC-10) — the ONLY residual is whether the reverted value persists across a reload through Supabase/Drive (signed-in cloud round-trip).


### B742 — Delete on a road silently no-ops for many clicks, then suddenly works `[Site Planner]` (bug) #site-planner #road #selection #persistence #ui  *(owner-dropped 2026-07-09 as "NEW-1"; provisional **B736**, renumbered **B742** — fast-moving concurrent `main` took B734–B741 + V250–V254 across several merges. Per repo precedent the code/tests/commit keep the provisional **B736** label; only the backlog + verification IDs bumped (→ B742 / V255). Branch `claude/road-delete-intermittent-tjrn4s`.)*
`[x]` **IMPLEMENTED + headless-verified this session; parks in ⏳ Verify (Verify: live — the cloud-sync half is signed-in only + a timing/persistence class) → V255.** Selecting a road and pressing/clicking Delete did nothing for ~20 tries, then one finally deleted it. Now a single Delete removes the selected road immediately (button OR keyboard) and never silently no-ops — if a delete can't proceed it visibly falls through to a whole-element delete, and a failed cloud save surfaces loudly.
- Verify: live
- Origin: filed 2026-07-09 from chat
- **DEDUPE-FIRST:** searched Open / ⏳ Verify / Done (BACKLOG*.md + BACKLOG_OPEN.md) — **net-new**, no item covers this. Nearest prior art (NOT dupes): **B673** (element-sync loud-conflict + delete/edit matrix — the conflict *policy*, not this local-no-op/wedge); **B230/B718** (the control-point add/delete feature this bug was mis-firing through); **B372** (a deleted *site* resurrecting — different object, the localStorage unmount-flush).
- **AUDIT-FIRST — three real defects, code-confirmed (not the report's single guess):**
  1. **Road keyboard-Delete trap (primary).** With a road selected and an interior control point *armed* (`selVtx`), `SitePlanner.jsx:2697` routed Delete to `deleteVtx` and `return`ed unconditionally. `deleteVtx`'s road branch (`:3638-3660`) early-returned on a non-removable/**stale** index (endpoint, 2-pt min, or an index gone out-of-range after the road's geometry changed under the armed selection — e.g. a realtime refetch replaced `els`) **without clearing `selVtx`**. So every later Delete re-hit that branch and no-op'd until Escape / a background click reset `selVtx` — "then it finally worked."
  2. **Right-click menu deletes stale selection** (`:12494`): `setSel({kind:"el",id}); deleteSel()` — `deleteSel` reads a ref `setSel` hasn't synchronously updated, so it acted on the previous selection (wrong element, or a no-op).
  3. **Silent cloud-sync wedge** (`elementSync.js:205-230` + `elementApi.js`): the per-element commit had **no timeout**, so a hung `commit_elements` left the single `inflight` slot stuck TRUE forever — all element writes (incl. deletes) piled up unsent, badge stuck "saving", flooding out only when the stall cleared (the persistence-side "then it worked").
- **Fix:**
  - `deleteVtx` now returns a **boolean** (true only when it actually removed a point) and clears `selVtx`+`roadVtxSel` on every no-op/guard path; the keyboard branch (`:2697`) gained `&& deleteVtx(...)` so a no-op **falls through** to the whole-element `deleteSel()` — Delete is never a dead key.
  - `deleteSel(target)` accepts an optional explicit `{kind,id}` (guarded on `.kind` so the five bare `onClick={deleteSel}` buttons that pass an event still fall back to the live ref); the context menu passes the clicked id directly.
  - RoadVtx **drag-end** clears `selVtx`, so reshaping a control point and then pressing Delete deletes the whole road (a deliberate plain click on a dot still arms it for a targeted vertex-delete).
  - `commitElements`/`fetchElements` (`elementApi.js`) bounded by **`COMMIT_TIMEOUT_MS = 8000`** (AbortController + `Promise.race`, mirrors `PARCEL_FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS`) → a hung request resolves `{ok:false}` → `onTransportFailure` retries/backs off → after `maxAttempts` the state goes `failed` → the existing red "error"/Retry badge (LOUD-FAILURE). This also closes the resurrection window (a delete that never lands can no longer be silently rebuilt by a refetch).
- **Verified (sandbox/headless):** new `test/elementApi.test.js` cases (hung commit → `{ok:false, /timeout/}`; abort-signal wired through; hung fetch → ok:false) · full unit suite green (3164) · build green · MAP.md regenerated · **`e2e/element-delete.spec.js` (3 tests, LOGGED-OUT via "Start blank" + a real drawn centerline road, green in headless Chromium): panel "Delete element" removes the road and it stays gone after reload; keyboard Delete after arming an interior control point removes just that vertex (road survives, pts 4→3) then a second Delete removes the whole road — NO WEDGE; and reshape-drag a control point then Delete removes the whole road. 0 page errors.**
- **⏳ V255 (live, on planyr.io, SIGNED IN — the sandbox can't sign in):** the cloud-sync half only. Delete a road with cloud on → it persists and stays deleted across a tab-switch + reload (no resurrection); and on a genuinely slow/failed commit the sync badge flips to "error/Retry" (not stuck on "saving").
- **Live-verified 2026-07-18 (Cowork session, signed-in on planyr.io) — PARTIAL:** deleted a Building and, separately, a Road via the panel's Delete button; confirmed no resurrection two ways (a second-tab full reload, and a same-tab reload) across both element types — the cloud delete persists, no resurrection. The stalled/throttled-commit → "error/Retry" badge check could NOT be run this pass (no DevTools network-throttling capability available in that session); still owed, needs a human with real DevTools access. Not archived.

### B743 — Harden the shared element-delete path so no element type can silently no-op (×2) `[Site Planner]` (bug) #site-planner #selection #persistence #testing #ui  *(owner-dropped 2026-07-09 as "NEW-2", alongside B742; provisional **B737**, renumbered **B743** on the same fast-moving `origin/main` merge-in. `[x]` **RE-OPENED 2026-07-30 (owner: "delete means delete") and RE-FIXED the same session; parks in ⏳ Verify (Verify: live — signed-in cloud persistence) → V567.** The 2026-07-09 pass fixed the routes INTO the shared delete path but left its own silent `if (!sel) return;` in place, so the class stayed open and came back. It is now closed at the source: one pure decision module, delete unconditional at any selection count, and no path that removes nothing without saying why. Original 2026-07-09 record kept below.
- Verify: live
- Origin: filed 2026-07-09 from chat
- **What the shared fix guarantees:** `deleteVtx`'s **non-road** branch (parcel/el/measure/ease/markup) now also decides removability up front, returns `false` + clears the armed point on a min-points no-op (so it, too, falls through to a whole-element delete instead of a swallowed keypress or a bogus history entry). Button-Delete and keyboard-Delete resolve through the ONE `deleteSel` (idempotent — deleting an already-gone id is a safe no-op; no busy flag gates it). The `COMMIT_TIMEOUT_MS` bound applies to **every** element write, so no delete of any type can wedge the sync slot; a failed write goes loud via the shared "error/Retry" badge (LOUD-FAILURE) rather than silently resurrecting.

- **Live-verified 2026-07-18 (Cowork session, signed-in on planyr.io) — PARTIAL, shares B742's result:** Building + Road delete both confirmed persisting with no resurrection (second-tab reload + same-tab reload). The stalled-commit "error/Retry" badge check is still owed (needs real DevTools throttling). Not archived.
- **Recurrence: 2026-07-30 — owner report, and the reason it recurred is recorded below.** *"When I click delete on the building, it's not deleting. And I feel like I have had a LOT of issues with delete not working as a function. Let's dig into the root cause and figure out why it keeps not deleting. It should be very simple. Delete means delete."* Owner evidence on the Colorado site `sms7v3ua7ksy`: 26 live element rows, **ZERO** rows with `deleted_at`, **ZERO** tombstone rows, and the site header's `deletedIds` is EMPTY — so no delete has ever reached the database for that site. Deletes work elsewhere (`smrp1wrgg6u5` 61 soft-deleted, `sms69x8rb2qk` 54, `smr9olizi5ue` 44, `smrjdgmlinea` 33), and the three buildings on the Colorado site are unlocked, un-grouped and not dog-ears — so this is NOT the multiwriter-resurrection family and NOT a rejected write. **The delete was dying CLIENT-SIDE before anything was sent.** Re-fixed this session; see the 2026-07-30 rework below. New live check → **V567**.
- **🔎 Why B742/B743 didn't stick (AUDIT-FIRST, 2026-07-30).** Both prior passes fixed the ROUTE INTO `deleteSel` (the armed-vertex trap, the stale menu ref, the commit timeout) and left `deleteSel`'s own opening line — `if (!sel) return;` — untouched. That bare return is a silent no-op with no message and no telemetry, reachable from FOUR ordinary states, from any of sixteen call sites. So each pass closed one road to the hole instead of filling it, and the next state that reached it read as a brand-new "delete is broken." **Reproduced in headless Chromium on the pre-fix build, not inferred.**
  1. **A MULTI-SELECTION OF EXACTLY ONE.** `deleteSel` branched on `multi.length > 1`, else fell through to `sel` — so a one-item `multi` with no matching `sel` deleted nothing. A marquee that catches one object, or a shift-click that lands on one, reaches this ordinarily.
  2. **A STALE `multi` LEFT BY A SUCCESSFUL DELETE (measured).** The single-selection branch cleared `sel` but not `multi`. Marquee one building → Delete (works) → **every later Delete keypress did nothing at all** (`sel` null + `multi` length 1 → the silent return), until an unrelated click happened to reset `multi`. This is the owner's "a LOT of issues with delete", exactly.
  3. **A STALE `multi` LEFT BY UNDO/REDO (measured).** `applySnapshot` cleared `sel` but not `multi` — same dead key, reached from Ctrl+Z.
  4. **A SELECTION POINTING AT SOMETHING GONE.** Each branch filtered by id, so a dead id removed nothing and `tombstone([])` short-circuited — no rows changed, nothing said. Consistent with the Colorado site's zero-deletes-ever signature.
  5. **THE TYPING GUARD (measured).** The keyboard handler ignores shortcuts while a field has focus. Edit a building's width in Properties, press Delete → nothing happens while the building sits visibly selected, with no explanation.
- **The rework (2026-07-30) — one path, and silence is impossible.** New pure `src/workspaces/site-planner/lib/deletePlan.js` is the ONE decision behind every entry point; `deleteSel` is now a thin shell that applies its result. Three invariants, each tested: **(a) DELETE IS UNCONDITIONAL** — anything visibly selected is deletable, including a PINNED item (pinning guards a drag, never a deliberate Delete); **(b) THE SELECTION IS THE UNION of `multi` and `sel` at ANY count** — the count-dependent branch is gone, so a one-item marquee behaves exactly like a five-item one; **(c) NOTHING IS REMOVED → THE USER IS TOLD WHY** ("Nothing is selected — click the item on the plan first, then press Delete." / "That's already gone…"), and the keyboard Delete is now UNCONDITIONAL so a press with nothing selected reaches the code that can say so. Also: both selection stores are cleared on every delete AND in `applySnapshot`; `deleteMarkupById` / `deleteParcelById` (the two paths that don't route through `deleteSel`) got the same no-silent-return contract; and an unknown ref kind now resolves to NOTHING (the old trailing `else` treated every unrecognised kind as a **parcel**).
- **Also fixed, found in the audit:** the multi branch resolved each element ref to its assembly ROOT first, so shift-clicking a truck court silently deleted the whole building; the single branch went downward. Both now use one downward-only subtree rule — a building takes its whole bonded assembly, a child takes only its own.
- **The entry-point audit (all 16, enumerated in `DELETE_ENTRIES`):** `key:delete` (Delete/Backspace) · `cut` (Ctrl/⌘X) · panel buttons `panel:element` `panel:pond` `panel:parcel` `panel:easement` `panel:markup` `panel:callout` `panel:measure` · context menus `menu:element` `menu:measure` `menu:callout` `menu:markup` `menu:parcel` · plus `deleteVtx` (vertex-only, B742's fall-through, unchanged) and `removeOverlay` (already loud — it re-checks and warns "⚠ Delete didn't take"). Every one now names itself in telemetry (B1215).
- **Data-model question resolved (the owner's part 5): ONE source of truth, not two.** `deleted_at` on a `site_elements` row IS the delete; `kind='tombstone'` rows are a **migration artifact only** — `explodeModel` / `db/site_elements_backfill.sql` turn the legacy blob's `deletedIds` array into one row per dead id with `data=null` (the element's data is gone, only the id survived), which is why `site_elements.sql` says outright that tombstone rows "exist only for migrated legacy `deletedIds`". They cannot disagree: `rowsToModel` reads the single predicate `deleted_at is not null` across rows of EVERY kind into one `deletedIds` set, then subtracts any id that still has a LIVE row of any kind — so a live element always wins over a stray tombstone sharing its id (the legacy `e6327` class). A site carrying both counts (`smqiljx5fngg` 23+12, `smqtu6li9mqy` 20+20) is simply a migrated site that has had real deletes since. **Intentional layering, one predicate, documented tie-break — no action needed.**
- **Verified (sandbox/headless, this session):** new `test/deletePlan.test.js` — **38 tests**: every entry point × every selection shape (single · one-item multi · multi-item multi · locked target · bonded assembly · stale ref · unknown kind · garbage state), the "no no-op without a message" sweep across all 14 entries × 6 hostile shapes, plus a **source guard** holding the wiring (no bare `onClick={deleteSel}` survives, every call site passes a registered `entry`, the keyboard branch stays unconditional, both selection stores are cleared in `deleteSel` AND `applySnapshot`, and every delete path reports). New `e2e/delete-unconditional.spec.js` — **9 tests green in headless Chromium, logged out**: keyboard · panel button · right-click menu · bonded assembly (every member tombstoned) · the stale-multi dead key · delete-after-undo/redo · nothing-selected feedback · a PINNED building still deletes · the typing-guard hint. **Proven RED on the pre-fix build first** — 4 of the 9 fail there (the marquee dead key, the post-undo dead key, the nothing-selected message, the typing-guard hint), which is the recurrence made into a permanent guard. Full unit suite **6,976 green** · lint 0 errors · build green · MAP.md regenerated.
- **⏳ V567 (live, signed-in on planyr.io — the sandbox can't sign in):** on the owner's Colorado site `sms7v3ua7ksy`, delete a building via keyboard, panel button and right-click menu; each must vanish, write a `deleted_at` row to `site_elements`, and stay gone after a reload.
