### B738 — Satellite/aerial basemap missing from PDF/PNG export (plan prints on a blank white background) `[Site Planner]` (bug) #site-planner #export #gis  *(owner-dropped 2026-07-09 as "NEW-1"; provisional **B735**, renumbered **B738** — concurrent `main` (PRs #557/#559/#560) took B734/B735/B736/B737 + V250/V251. Per repo precedent the code/tests/commit keep the provisional **B735** label; only the backlog + verification IDs bumped (→ B738 / V252). Branch `claude/pdf-export-cors-imagery-4l1f8d`.)*
`[x]` **IMPLEMENTED + headless-verified this session; parks in ⏳ Verify (Verify: live — PDF/export parity + GIS endpoint behavior, both mandatory-live classes) → V252.** With the satellite/aerial basemap on, Print/Download PDF (and Download PNG) produced the vectors on a blank white background — the imagery was dropped. The export now composites the on-screen aerial into the sheet, and a fetch that can't be inlined warns loudly instead of silently emitting a background-less file.
- Verify: live
- Origin: filed 2026-07-09 from chat
- **DEDUPE-FIRST:** searched Open / ⏳ Verify / Done (BACKLOG*.md + BACKLOG_OPEN.md) — **net-new**, no existing item covers the aerial missing from the export. Nearest prior art to BUILD ON, NOT dupes: **B50** (Done — made a *tainted-canvas* export failure surface an alert instead of a silent no-op; this is a different, more common failure — a **dropped** image, not a thrown taint); **B202** (Done — time-boxed + parallelized `inlineImages` so a hung tile can't stall print prep; introduced the very `dropOnFail` that this bug turns silent); **B693** (the Off/Aerial/USGS basemap control). The chat's own "NEW-2/NEW-3" bullets were gotchas on this one item, not separate numbers.
- **AUDIT-FIRST — the chat's leading hypothesis (a CORS-tainted canvas swallowing a SecurityError) did NOT match the code.** The export does not rasterize the live Leaflet DOM; `buildExportSvg` clones ONLY `svgRef.current`. The live basemap is a **sibling `<div ref={geoWrapRef}>`** (Leaflet tiles, `data-export="skip"`, zIndex 0) that the SVG clone never captures. So the export's only aerial source was the persisted `underlay` `<image>`. Two ways that goes blank: (1) **basemap on with no `underlay`** (a located site whose from-map capture is absent, or the underlay removed) → the SVG had no aerial at all; (2) `underlay.src` is a remote ArcGIS `export` URL and `inlineImages(dropOnFail=true)` **silently dropped** it on any fetch hiccup → white background, no error (a LOUD-FAILURE violation). CORS itself is fine: `server.arcgisonline.com` `export` **and** `tile` endpoints return `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` (curl-verified), so a plain `fetch` inlines cleanly to a data URL (no taint).
- **Fix (three parts):**
  1. **Capture the live basemap for the export.** New `SitePlanner.exportAerialForFrame(frame)`: when `origin && basemapOn`, synthesize a **frame-exact** aerial by requesting the ACTIVE source's `export` endpoint (`BASEMAPS[basemapSrc].export` — Esri or USGS) sized to the printed area, placed in the SAME feet frame as the parcels so it aligns pixel-for-pixel. This is the same technique the from-map underlay already uses — reused, not reinvented.
  2. **Geometry:** new pure `feetExtentToBbox(ext, lat0, lon0)` in `lib/arcgis.js` (planner feet → lon/lat bbox; +x EAST, +y SOUTH), which `aerialPlacement` reverses exactly (proven by a round-trip unit test). `buildExportSvg` now takes an `exportAerial` and draws `aerial = exportAerial || underlay` (so the dropped-screenshot / basemap-off paths are unchanged), tagging the `<image>` `data-export-aerial`.
  3. **LOUD-FAILURE:** `inlineImages` now returns `{ aerialDropped }`; `exportPDF`/`exportPNG` `flashWarn` the user ("⚠ Couldn't load the satellite imagery, so the PDF was exported without it…") on the **success path** (after the file downloads, so a later encode failure can't leave a contradictory toast), with the **`⚠` prefix that flips the banner to the red warning colour** (without it the notice rendered on the success-green — B341-class).
  4. **Extent unification (review-driven).** Both `buildExportSvg` and `exportAerialForFrame` now crop to ONE shared `exportFeetExtent(frame)` (frame → dev → parcels → underlay bounds), and a reliable data-URL underlay is drawn BENEATH the live synth as a fallback — so a dropped fetch can't regress a previously-good export to white.
- **Adversarial review (4-lens Workflow + per-finding verify) caught a real gap before merge:** the first cut returned `null` from `exportAerialForFrame` for a **parcels-only site** (deed imported, no massing yet) with no print frame, because it keyed on `devExtent()` alone (which ignores `parcels`) while `buildExportSvg` still framed the parcels — so that (very common) state *still* silently exported white. Part 4 above fixes it; a `test/bugHuntGuards.test.js` guard locks the shared-extent wiring so it can't regress.
- **Verified (sandbox/headless):** `test/aerialExport.test.js` (3 tests — `feetExtentToBbox` north/south orientation, exact round-trip through `aerialPlacement` reconstructing the feet extent, and the `maxPx` export-ceiling clamp) · new **B735 guard** in `test/bugHuntGuards.test.js` (shared `exportFeetExtent` + `data-export-aerial` marker + `aerialDropped` signal all present) · **`ui-audit/verify-aerial-export-cors.mjs` (real headless Chromium, runs the ACTUAL `inlineImages` loop): a cross-origin image served with `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` (identical CORS to Esri — asserted live by curl in the same script) inlines to a data URL, does NOT taint the canvas, and rasterizes into the backdrop (100% non-white, high colour variety); an unreachable aerial URL sets `aerialDropped=true` and drops the `<image>` (the LOUD-FAILURE contract)** · existing `ui-audit/verify-pdf-export.mjs` still green (no regression) · full unit suite **3,151 green** · lint 0 errors · build green · MAP.md regenerated (new `arcgis.js` export). NOTE: the live Esri `export` fetch could not be exercised from the *sandbox* browser (the egress proxy resets headless Chromium's TLS tunnel to arcgisonline, and blocks `basemap.nationalmap.gov` outright — 403 CONNECT; curl over HTTP/1.1 reaches Esri). So **Esri CORS `*` is curl-verified; USGS is expected (stock ArcGIS Server defaults AllowedOrigins=*) but pending the live check** — and if USGS turns out non-CORS, the LOUD warning fires (no silent white). A real browser at planyr.io has no proxy.
- **⏳ V252 (live, on planyr.io):** locate a real site → confirm the satellite backdrop is ON → **Download PDF**: the imagery must be the background with parcels/setbacks/markups/massing on top (repeat with the print frame set, and once with the **USGS** source). Then **Download PNG** → same. Toggle the basemap OFF (or a dropped-screenshot underlay) → export still behaves as before. Optional: throttle/kill the network mid-export → the "couldn't load the satellite imagery" warning shows and the file still downloads (no silent white). Also spot-check that a placed site-plan overlay + the "Print overlay" toggle still composite correctly above the aerial.
- **⚠ Amended 2026-07-15 (owner live console test):** USGS's `export` endpoint is confirmed **CORS-clean from the browser** (200, read into JS from the planyr.io origin) — so the V252 step-3 caveat (route USGS through the same-origin proxy) is resolved; no proxy needed. The live gap is the **inverse**: **Esri's slow *dynamic* `/export`** timing out under the 8 s inline cap on a normal large frame (Esri **AbortError @ 8015 ms** vs USGS **200 @ 4022 ms**, same frame) is what dropped the aerial and printed white in the wild. Follow-on fixes filed separately — **B839** (reuse cached tiles for the export backdrop → removes the timeout as the failure mode), **B840** (interim aerial-specific timeout + retry + Esri↔USGS source fallback), **B841** (reword the misleading "check your connection" banner). These are the 2026-07-15 aerial-export "NEW-1/2/3" — NOT the 2026-07-09 NEW-2/NEW-3 that were folded into this item.

### B692 — ROOT-CAUSE fix for the B690 husk-parcel crash: sanitize the model funnel so a null/points-less entry can never be manufactured, persisted, or re-ingested `[Site Planner / model]` (bug — CRITICAL, owner-reported crash; extends B690) #site-planner #persistence  *(owner chat 2026-07-07 — incognito tab on planyr.io: "Site Planyr hit an error and couldn't load… Try again/Reload/Ctrl-Shift-R all send me right back." First minted **B689**; RENUMBERED to **B692** on merge-in of `origin/main` — the concurrent Cowork live run independently hit the SAME crash as its V231 #18, minted **B690** for it and shipped the render-side guard (shoelace/polyArea, PR #540), and also took B689 (inspector de-cream) + B691 (Fort Bend CORS); **B692** = highest B# across both files (B691) + 1. Branch `claude/site-planner-incognito-error-49h3as`. DEDUPE-FIRST — same crash as **B690** (both symbolicated to `ym→Hp→Ij`), so this item is deliberately the ROOT-CAUSE COMPANION, not a duplicate: B690 guarded the reads; B692 stops the husk from ever existing — manufacture (normalizeZ), persistence (createSiteModel funnel), and every ingress (rows, realtime, JSON import) — and makes sanitization LOUD.)*
`[x]` **IMPLEMENTED + fully repro'd/verified headless this session; parks in ⏳ Verify (Verify: live — the repro cites the owner's real signed-in data; the signed-in mirror path + the telemetry signal need a live confirmation) → V232.**
- Verify: live
- Origin: filed 2026-07-07 from chat (crash 2026-07-07 02:23–02:30 UTC, 23 telemetry reports, build dca4f15, all signed-in)
- **Root cause (found via the app's own `client_errors` telemetry — minified stack symbolicated against the deployed chunk):** `MapFinder.siteAcres` reduces `shoelace(p.points)` over `site.parcels`, guarded on the ARRAY but not the ENTRY. A `null` entry in a persisted parcels array (JSON.stringify turns an `undefined` entry or an array hole into `null`) survived `createSiteModel` untouched, and B671's `normalizeZ` then spread it into a `{z:0}` "husk" with no points — `undefined.length` → the workspace error boundary, on EVERY load, because the poison lives in the stored record. Cloud DB swept clean (site_elements + sites blobs, all users) — the husk was client-manufactured into the local mirror during the element-sync churn window (RLS-rejected commit 01:30 + create collisions + a two-tab CAS heal loop 01:33–02:03).
- **Fix (funnel + belt-and-suspenders):** (1) `createSiteModel` now DROPS non-object entries from every collection (parcels/els/markups/measures/callouts/sheetOverlays/parcelDrawings/crossSections) and drops points-less husk parcels — reference-stable when clean, so no state/save churn; runs before `migrateRoads` so a null can't crash the els migration passes either. (2) `normalizeZ`/`needsZ` never spread a non-object into a `{z}` husk (drop instead). (3) `MapFinder.shoelace` returns 0 for a non-array (the list can never crash on residual junk). (4) The rows-read paths (`refetchReplace` + realtime `applyRemoteInstr`) keep husk parcel rows OFF the canvas; the reconcile diff then tombstones the bad row in the cloud — the husk heals into a proper delete (TOMBSTONE-DELETES). (4b) The JSON-import path now normalizes through `createSiteModel` (was raw `setParcels(d.parcels)`) — a hand-edited/stale export can't re-poison the canvas (found by the parallel writer-hunt audit; the audit also confirmed via DB sweep that NO other user has husk data and no one else was affected). (5) LOUD-FAILURE: `loadSitesList` reports a `model-sanitized` telemetry event whenever a stored record needed junk dropped — corruption is a visible signal, never a quiet edit. Bonus: the e2e fixture generator's parcel used `ring:` instead of `points:` (a real husk shipping in the fixture) — fixed + fixtures/goldens regenerated.
- **Self-heal:** no user action — the poisoned record reads clean on the next load (drop-at-read), and the next save persists the cleaned model.
- **Tests/verify (sandbox):** 2,875 green (11 new in `test/modelSanitize.test.js`: husk manufacture, per-collection drops, reference stability, idempotence, junk counting) · build green · **controlled repro BOTH ways headless (`ui-audit/verify-husk-parcel.mjs`): the poisoned seed CRASHES live planyr.io with the owner's exact error, and renders clean (site listed, correct 23.0 ac from the surviving parcel) on the fixed build.**

### B682 — Dragging a parcel's acreage label spawns a "bunch of copies" (id-less parcels + value-based union merge) `[Site Planner]` (bug) #site-planner #persistence #selection  *(owner chat 2026-07-06 — screenshot: "I just tried to move the 69.48 ac label, and it just made a bunch of copies." **B682** = highest real B# across both files (B681) + 1. Branch `claude/acre-label-duplication-ulvjys`. DEDUPE-FIRST — grepped Open/⏳ Verify/Done for `acre`/`label`/`parcel` × `dup`/`copies`: NOT B651 (split double-COUNTS acreage in the yield math — different defect, same area), NOT B22 (rapid-click duplicate SELECTION on the map). Net-new: the parcel-identity/merge defect.)*
`[x]` **IMPLEMENTED + sandbox-verified + headless-verified this session; parks in ⏳ Verify (Verify: live — the accumulation is a concurrency/multi-writer MERGE class per LIVE-VERIFY, only fully exercised signed-in over cloud sync) → V225.**
- Verify: live
- Origin: filed 2026-07-06 from chat
- **AUDIT-FIRST root cause:** map-finder / legacy parcels can be **id-LESS**. `MapFinder.computeAssembly` emits `{points, addr, acct, attrs}` with **no `id`** (the modern `newSiteFromMap` backfills one, but records created before that — or synced from an older client — still hold id-less parcels). Two bugs flow from a missing id: (1) the acreage-chip drag matches `pc.id === draggedId`, and with both `undefined` it moves EVERY id-less parcel at once; (2) the cross-copy union merge (`mergeSiteContent` → `unionById`) can only dedupe id-less items by **`JSON.stringify` value**, so the instant a drag adds a `labelOffset` the edited copy no longer equals its stored twin and the union keeps **BOTH** — a phantom parcel that **multiplies** with each further drag/merge. Proven with a focused `mergeSiteContent` repro (1 id-less parcel + a labelOffset edit → **2** parcels).
- **Fix (one funnel, additive):** `createSiteModel` — which every load/save/merge passes through — now backfills a **deterministic id derived from the parcel GEOMETRY only** (`withStableParcelIds`, djb2-xor over rounded points), so the same parcel hashes identically before/after any mutable-field edit (labelOffset/active/locked/setbacks) and the union dedupes it by id; two genuinely-distinct parcels differ in points → distinct ids. Only fills a MISSING id (in-planner parcels keep their `uid()`), idempotent + reference-stable on already-migrated data. Exact-geometry id-less duplicates collapse to one, which **self-heals the phantom copies the bug already persisted** on the next load. No change needed in `SitePlanner.jsx` — parcels reaching React state now always carry an id, so the chip drag matches exactly one.
- **Verified here (sandbox):** 6 new unit tests in `test/siteModel.test.js` (backfill determinism · geometry-only stability across a labelOffset edit · distinct-geometry distinct ids · existing id never rewritten · the merge repro now yields 1 not 2 · exact-dup self-heal) · full suite **2,788 green** · lint 0 errors · build green.
- **Verified here (headless, logged-out):** seeded a site with 3 id-less parcels (2 exact-geometry dupes, one carrying a dragged `labelOffset`, + 1 distinct), opened it in the real plan canvas → exactly **2** acre chips render (dupe collapsed, distinct survived), zero page errors. (Temp spec, removed after the run — the unit tests are the durable guard.)
- **⏳ V225** = the signed-in / cloud pass: on a real account whose project has (or is seeded with) id-less parcels, drag an acreage label repeatedly across cloud syncs / a second tab and confirm it stays put with NO new copies, and that any pre-existing phantom copies collapse on load.

Boot resolves ordered candidates via `resolveResume` (URL project → that project's own entry first, then legacy, still guarded by `wrongProject` on the actually-loaded record — a project-matched entry now RESUMES where the guard used to drop to empty). Breadcrumb project switch inside Review lands on THAT project's last doc (flushes the outgoing doc first; a pending cross-workspace open intent or an in-flight open wins — no race).

The owner's live ≈31.8 ac most plausibly came from **overlapping county parcels added separately** (a recently-subdivided tract where CAD still lists the parent + both children) or a **stale cached bundle** predating that fix — which is exactly why **B652 (the overlap warning) is the real catch-all** and was built alongside. This item still had a genuine gap vs. the owner's desired UX (the old code DELETED the parent instead of retaining it), so the split was re-architected from "delete parent" to "supersede parent."
- **What shipped (branch `claude/parcel-split-double-count-vk8f0j`; lint 0 · 2,526 tests (+21) · build green · lazy split intact · headless `ui-audit/verify-b651-b652-parcel-split.mjs` 14/14):**
  - **Split is now a REPLACEMENT via supersession** (`performSplit`): one op creates + activates the pieces as CHILDREN (each carries `parentId`) and marks the parent `active:false` (superseded, non-counting) — no longer deleted/tombstoned. Because the superseded parent is inactive, it drops out of every active-parcel area sum automatically (no yield-math change needed; the ~13 inline `active !== false` sums are untouched).
  - **Parent retained + nested** (`parcelOutline` in `siteModel.js`; Parcel panel): the superseded parent stays in the list, greyed + "· split", with its children indented under it. The **on-canvas** superseded outline is hidden (its active children occupy the same ground). Header "Parcels · N" counts CURRENT lots only (excludes superseded), so splitting one lot reads "Parcels · 2".
  - **Lineage naming** (`parcelDisplayInfo`, derived — not stored): Parcel 3 → 3A / 3B → 3A1 / 3A2 (letters odd depth, digits even), tracking the parent's current number; a street address still wins as the name.
  - **Mutual-exclusion guard** (`toggleParcelActive` + `lineageConflicts`): activating a parcel auto-deactivates its ancestors AND descendants (a parent covers its children's ground; siblings are disjoint), so a parent and its split children can never both be active.
  - **Schema:** `SITE_MODEL_VERSION` 10 → 11 (additive `parentId`; existing records migrate losslessly — missing = root, unchanged behavior). Fixtures/MAP regenerated.

(The pure model + logged-out UI are headless-verified; the signed-in cloud path + owner-data repro are the remaining live gate.)

### B672 (×2) — Element-level sync, phase 3/5: realtime read path + rejoin refetch (read cutover; blob frozen) `[Site Planner]` (feature) #site-planner #persistence  *(owner brief 2026-07-06, arrived as "NEW-3"; minted **B672** — see B671's renumber note. `[x]` **IMPLEMENTED this session; parks in ⏳ Verify (Verify: live — cross-tab propagation is a multi-session timing class) → V229.** Each open site now subscribes to its `site_elements` rows and applies changes LIVE; with the edit lock still on, a read-only tab updates in real time. This is also the READ CUTOVER: signed-in loads come from rows + a slim header, and the whole-doc blob is FROZEN (`sites.data_backup` = the ~30-day rollback copy).
- Verify: live
- Origin: filed 2026-07-06 from chat
- **Recurrence (2026-07-07, from the Cowork V229 live run — re-opened, FIXED same session, back to ⏳ Verify):**
  **V229 #5 FAILED with a reproduced LOST UPDATE (data-loss class).** Repro: session B's realtime socket
  dropped (`pfSupabase.realtime.disconnect()`), A edits an element (rev 9→10), B rejoins → the DB ends up
  clobbered back to B's stale geometry at rev 11; reproduced twice. **Root cause — the refetch-replace
  stale-reconcile race:** after `eng.seed(freshRows)` the old `refetchReplace` reconciled against
  `stateRef.current`, which still holds the PRE-replace canvas (setState hadn't rendered) — on a
  socket-dropped tab that canvas is genuinely stale, so the diff committed OLD geometry as valid
  rev-guarded updates on top of the fresh revs. (#4 passed because a hidden tab still receives events;
  only a dropped socket leaves the canvas stale.) Compounding hole: `flush()` clears the dirty map
  up-front, so the batch IN FLIGHT was invisible to both `applyRemoteRow` and the refetch substitution.
  **Fix (this session):** `refetchReplace` now reconciles against EXACTLY the substituted collections it
  just placed (rows ∪ pending local edits), never `stateRef`; it defers wholesale while `busyRef` is live;
  the engine tracks `inflightKeys` during a flush — in-flight commits are protected like dirty everywhere
  (`applyRemoteRow` keeps local + adopts rev; `dirtyEntries()` includes them so the refetch substitution
  keeps a mid-commit edit; `reconcile` skips re-enqueueing data already on the wire; shadow revs stay
  monotonic when an ok result lands after a newer remote rev was adopted; an identical incoming row is
  adopted silently and drops a duplicate queued write). 6 new unit tests pin the exact #5 sequence +
  in-flight invariants (`test/elementSync.test.js`, "refetch-replace safety"). **Re-run V229 #5 live with
  true DevTools offline** (the Cowork run's disconnect() only severed realtime, not the RPC path — DevTools
  offline exercises the queued-commit + rejoin path end-to-end).
  - *Watch note (Observation B, same run):* two transient paint freezes were seen under automation-driven
    load; nothing reproduced organically. No action — watch during the V229 re-run; escalate to its own B#
    only if it shows up under human use.
  - *Related churn fixed same session (Observation A):* the autosave pushed a content-identical slim header
    on every element edit — each push bumped `sites.version` and CAS-ping-ponged every other tab (a heal per
    edit; noise, and it masked #5's mechanism). `cloudUpsert` now skips a push whose header content is
    unchanged (`headerSig` — the slim header minus `updatedAt`; baseline seeded from `cloudList`, advanced on
    every successful push, cleared on delete/user-switch; the unload keepalive shares the skip). Trade-off,
    accepted: `sites.updated_at` advances only on REAL header changes (meta/settings/overlays) — element
    recency lives on the `site_elements` rows. +3 headerSig tests in `test/headerSlim.test.js`.
- **Realtime read path:** one channel per open site (`postgres_changes` filtered to `site_id`); the apply is idempotent per row (`applyRemoteRow`: incoming.rev must BEAT the shadow rev, so our own committed echoes are no-ops); a tombstoned row removes the element; a row for a locally-dirty element keeps LOCAL data and adopts the remote rev (its commit re-targets the fresh row). Remote applies buffer mid-gesture (never yank the canvas mid-drag). **Full refetch + REPLACE on every join/rejoin + tab wake** (visibilitychange) — never trust event gaps; dirty entries substitute back in; value-identical replaces keep state references (an idle wake re-trues nothing, saves nothing). A failed refetch changes nothing and retries (B54 discipline). No-realtime fallback: a plain fetch still seeds + replaces once, so writes work even if WebSockets are blocked.
- **Header slimming (same commit):** `slimForCloud` strips the 5 vector collections + marks `elementsInRows: true`; `mergePulledSites` understands slim rows (local elements kept — empty ≠ deleted; header-only re-push signature — no perma-push; a slim row's stale `deletedIds` are excluded from the union so they can never drop a row-restored element).
- **Kill list executed:** the B459 thin-clobber guard + `siteContent`/`siteTombs` baselines + `noteLocalContent` (a slim header would always read as "thinned"; element safety now lives in per-row rev guards); doc-level `cloudConflict` state + the blocking "changed in another session … Take over editing" banner (a stale header CAS now SELF-HEALS inside `cloudUpsert` — refetch the version, re-push once; the B455/B460/B558/B596 false-conflict class is retired BY ARCHITECTURE); the cloud-active storage-event union fold (signed-out keeps it). `deletedIds` refinement: element ids are reconciled against live rows on every refetch (an id with a live row is purged — rows are deletion-canonical), and it keeps serving header-side collections + signed-out mode.
- **DB executed via Supabase MCP:** backfill re-run captured the phase-1→3 gap (els 496→523 — real owner edits); found + fixed a guard edge (the boot re-push can rewrite blob CONTENT, e.g. the v12 `z` normalization, without advancing `updatedAt` → the update guard is now `<=`, engine rows stay strictly newer and untouched); fidelity after heal: **27/28 sites byte-identical, 1 site's rows strictly AHEAD of its blob** (rev 19, server-stamped 400ms after the last blob snapshot — the healthy dual-write case, rows-canonical). `data_backup` frozen for all 28 sites (`db/site_elements_freeze.sql`).
- **e2e seeds** now explode fixture sites into rows (seed.sql + seed-fixtures.sql), so seeded fixtures open under the rows-canonical read path.
- **Verified here (sandbox):** lint 0 · 2,835 tests (+19: `elementApply` matrix incl. the composite-key twin case, `headerSlim` merge/no-perma-push/stale-tombstone cases; `cloudThinGuard.test.js` retired with its guard) · build green · headless smoke 3/3 (signed-out planner unaffected — engine + channel are cloud-active-only).
- **⏳ V229 (live, two signed-in sessions):** see VERIFICATION.md — cross-tab <2s propagation, rejoin refetch, tab-wake re-true, and the no-conflict-banner regression. Folded into the consolidated Cowork runbook (docs/COWORK-ELEMENT-SYNC-LIVE.md, lands with B674).

### B714 — Sharing a project silently REVERTS: any ordinary save from the owner's open tab overwrote `sites.team_id` back to null, locking the collaborator out `[Site Planner / Review / teams · RLS]` (bug — data-integrity class) #site-planner #persistence #auth  *(owner live repro 2026-07-08 with the Cowork session: right-clicked Goose Creek → Share to michael.butler@hillwood.com → the site APPEARED on the test account, then broke — red cloud, elements gone after reload, no conflict toasts. Cowork's DB forensics found team "HIP Houston" + both members present but 0 sites linked, and filed it as "Share never sets team_id" (their NEW-1). First minted **B692**, then **B714** — BOTH taken by concurrent sessions on successive merge-ins of `origin/main` (B692 = the husk-parcel root-cause fix; B714 = dock-high truck-court pricing); settled as **B714** = highest B# across both files (B714) + 1.)*
`[x]` **IMPLEMENTED + unit-verified this session; parks in ⏳ Verify (Verify: live — the share round-trip is two-account/auth-only) → V244.** Sharing now survives every save: the sharing pointer can only be changed by the explicit Share/unshare action, never by a content autosave.
- Verify: live
- Origin: filed 2026-07-08 from the owner's live session (Cowork brief NEW-1 + NEW-2)
- **AUDIT-FIRST — the reported diagnosis was half right; the code reality is worse and explains everything.** `lib/sharing.js` DOES set `sites.team_id` correctly (UPDATE by `group_id`; the row's `group_id` is populated; the owner passes the rehome-guard trigger) — that's why the site initially appeared on the test account. The real bug: **every ordinary content push re-stamped `team_id` from the client's IN-MEMORY model** (`cloudUpsertCore` + `keepaliveCloudPush` for `sites`; `upsertReviewCore` + `keepaliveFlushReview` for `doc_reviews`; `upsertFileFacts` for `file_facts`, whose filing callers never even carry a teamId → hard `null`). The owner's open Goose Creek tab predated the share, so its next autosave wrote `team_id: null` — silently unsharing (the B486 rehome guard deliberately exempts the OWNER, so it never fired; a signed-in tab never re-reads the store, so it never learned the share happened). Timeline confirmed live: team created 2026-06-24, both members admins; the site row rewritten to v61 the same night with `team_id` back at null.
- **Fix — team_id is write-isolated to the sharing flow, everywhere:** `siteRowFor` / `reviewRowFor` (new pure row builders) OMIT `team_id` on every update — CAS autosaves and unload keepalives physically cannot carry the sharing pointer anymore; a brand-NEW row (first insert) still stamps the model's teamId so a plan/review created inside a shared project is born shared. `upsertFileFacts` sends `team_id` only when a caller explicitly provides one (the plain-upsert update leg then leaves the column untouched). `slimForCloud` additionally strips `teamId`/`ownerId` from the stored jsonb — the columns are the single source of truth, overlaid onto models at read time (`cloudList`/`loadReview`), and this keeps `headerSig` share-neutral so the B672 unchanged-header skip still works on shared sites.
- **Cowork's NEW-2 (realtime RLS "leak") — resolved by the same root cause, no leak.** The test account saw the owner's building move BEFORE its lockout because at that moment the site WAS legitimately shared (team_id set, RLS satisfied); the subsequent autosave-revert then produced the red cloud (writes rejected) and empty reload (reads rejected). Supabase `postgres_changes` enforces RLS per-subscriber, and the un-share also kills the subscription's row visibility. The V244 run includes a sanity check on a genuinely-unshared site.
- **Follow-on (small, filed not lost):** a file FILED into an already-shared project lands with `team_id null` (fact-row callers don't know the project's team) until the next re-share stamps it — pre-existing behavior, now explicit. Fix later by resolving the project's live team at filing time.
- **Verified here (sandbox):** 8-test `test/teamShareGuard.test.js` pins the rule for every writer (update rows carry NO team_id key; insert rows inherit; slim jsonb stripped; headerSig share-neutral) · full suite green · build green.
- **Data heal (prod):** the owner's intended share re-applied after deploy — `sites.team_id = 454aa114…(HIP Houston)` restored on group `smqfy48tlk9j` (Goose Creek) via MCP SQL (rehome-guard trigger safely bypassed for the one maintenance UPDATE; re-verified after).
- **⏳ V244 (live, two accounts — both already exist):** see VERIFICATION.md.
- DEDUPE-FIRST: net-new (no prior B# covers the share flow or team_id write-isolation); DISTINCT from the concurrent **B692** (husk-parcel model sanitize — the other half of the same live run's findings); B486 (Done) is the non-owner rehome guard this bug walked around by BEING the owner. The same owner brief's NEW-3 = **B690**/**B692** (render guard + root cause, both shipped) and NEW-4 = **B672 (×2)** (fixed + merged 2026-07-08) — the live session ran on build 40884e6, which predates those fixes; no new numbers minted for them.
- **⏳ 2026-08-23 — duplicate report investigated, DID NOT REPRODUCE (WRONG-CASE honoured, not closed on a null).** A fresh ticket arrived quoting the exact pre-fix symptom for this exact site/team (evidence dated 2026-07-06, before this item's 2026-07-08 fix), asking to confirm the share flow sets `team_id`. AUDIT-FIRST re-check against LIVE production, not a null result:
  1. **Current DB state:** all 7 live rows in group `smqfy48tlk9j` (Goose Creek) carry `team_id = 454aa114…` correctly; 17 sites total are linked to the team; the 3 `team_members` rows read as expected. A repo-wide scan for the exact bug signature (a group whose OWN rows disagree on `team_id` — some shared, some reverted) returned **zero groups**, so this isn't a live issue anywhere else either.
  2. **Live RLS re-proof against production**, impersonating the real collaborator account (`michael.butler@hillwood.com`) in a self-rolling-back transaction (same technique as `db/test/team_share_scope.test.sql`, pointed at the real report instead of synthetic fixtures): SELECT `sites` ✅, SELECT `site_elements` (95 rows visible) ✅, UPDATE `site_elements` ✅, UPDATE `sites` ✅ — 5/5 passed, nothing persisted. This directly answers the ticket's asks #1–#3 (share sets `team_id`; `site_elements` gates off it; a shared collaborator can select/insert/update) against the real accounts on the real site, live, today.
  3. **Ask #1's second half (accept path should "land" team_id) is BY DESIGN, not a gap:** `claim_team_invites()`/`handle_new_user()` only ever write `team_members` — joining a team and sharing a specific project are two deliberate actions (KEY DECISIONS: "sharing is always a deliberate, explicit act — never automatic"). Auto-linking a joiner's team to every site would be a privacy regression, not a fix.
  4. **Ask #4 (backfill):** no group currently needs one (see #1) — added `db/team_share_backfill_check.sql` anyway, a read-only audit query (repair template commented out, requires a human to name the intended team_id per case) so a future recurrence has a ready tool instead of an ad hoc query.
  5. **Ask #5 (realtime RLS "leak"), flagged not fixed here, per the ticket's own instruction:** already covered by this item's original NEW-2 finding above — `postgres_changes` enforces RLS per-subscriber, so an unshared site delivers nothing to a non-member. No new item minted (DEDUPE-FIRST).

  - **Disposition (STANDING RULE #2): reproduce-and-fix does not apply (nothing to fix — already fixed under this item); instrumented — the new CI test structurally guards the exact regression shape, and the DB trigger already makes the root-cause write path impossible.** Not closing this item to Done yet: the client-autosave-survives-real-edits and realtime-propagation halves of V244 still need an actual two-tab signed-in browser session, which remains `Blocker: auth` here.

### B1166 — The address-search parcel card was a wall of text: a metes-and-bounds Legal blob made it taller than the map `[Site Planner / MapFinder]` (task) #ui #gis #site-planner  *(owner chat 2026-07-30, provisional NEW-1. Minted **B1166** via `git fetch origin main && npm run next-id -- --against-main`, LATE — as the last step before push. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open + ⏳ Verify + Done for `parcel card`, `parcelInfo`, `MapFinder`, `apprRows`, `appraisal`, `Legal`, `B233`, `B244`: **B233** BUILT this card and is Done, **B244/B787** taught its field map the statewide-backup columns, **B630** fixed its backup badge — none of them owns how TALL it is. Net-new, not a recurrence: no prior item ever constrained the card's height.)*
`[ ]` **⏳ IMPLEMENTED — V542 PENDING.** Three rows by default; everything else folded, capped and still reachable. **Measured in Chromium: 455 px tall / 10 rows → 196 px / 3 rows collapsed** (386 px with the fold fully open).
- Verify: live
- Origin: filed 2026-07-30 from chat
- **Report.** Michael: *"fix how big this pop out is when I search by address, I don't think we need the legal description. Owner, parcel #, and acreage is plenty."*
- **Cause.** The card printed `Account / ID` and `Acreage (measured)` explicitly and then spread `apprRows(attrs)` — every remaining curated field. The last of those is **Legal**, and a county Legal is unbounded metes-and-bounds call text (`W2NW4 2-4-68 EXC PT LYING WITHIN COMM N4 SEC COR TH S06D25E 30.118 TPOB…`). In a fixed-width card that wraps to ten-plus lines, so the card outgrew the map controls beside it. The width was never the problem; the row count and one unbounded value were.
- **The fix.** Exactly three rows by default — **Owner · Account / ID · Acreage**, in that order. The situs address is the card's TITLE, so it no longer repeats as a row. Land value, Improvement value, Total value, Land use, Zoning, Year built and **Legal** move behind a **"More details"** disclosure, closed on every search: a real `<button aria-expanded>`, so it is keyboard- and screen-reader-reachable. **Nothing is deleted** — the honesty-stays-reachable rule; the fold is the tool, not the delete key.
- **Bounded even when opened.** The details body is height-capped and scrolls, and the Legal value is capped again inside its own row — so no county's blob can stretch the card, and the two caps are asserted in both the unit test and the browser harness. The card is keyed on the parcel in `MapFinder`, so a new search always re-mounts it CLOSED.
- **Unchanged, deliberately and byte-for-byte:** the statewide-backup and cached-copy warning banners (raw hex included — repointing those at the `--warn-*` tokens is a different change, and doing it here would silently alter how a cached-copy notice reads in dark mode), the **Plan this site** button, the narrow-viewport branch, and the no-parcel / service-unavailable states.
- **Where it lives now.** The card moved out of `MapFinder.jsx` into `components/ParcelInfoCard.jsx` (MODULE-SCOPE-COMPONENTS), and the row split is a pure exported function in `lib/appraisal.js` (`parcelCardRows`). That is what makes the height claim testable at all: the component has no DOM or Leaflet dependency, so it renders in a unit test AND mounts in a harness.
- **Verified here (sandbox — ATTEMPT-BEFORE-YOU-PARK honoured, twice over):** `test/parcelCard.test.js` (14 cases, real component output via `react-dom/server`) — three rows in order, the situs never repeated, a Legal blob 40× longer producing a **byte-identical** collapsed card, the fold absent when there is nothing to fold, and expanding revealing all seven remaining fields with both caps present. Then the real thing: **`ui-audit/verify-parcel-card-height.mjs` (new, 13/13) MEASURES it in Chromium** — collapsed 196 px with a monstrous Legal and 196 px with a one-line Legal (the blob adds no height at all), a real click on the fold reveals the Legal text, expanded stays bounded at 386 px, and the phone branch still renders three rows full-width. lint 0 errors · full suite 6,708 · build green · bundle budgets within ceiling (+1.7 KB total, attributable to the new component).
- **Cost, stated rather than buried:** +1.7 KB total JS / +1.6 KB on the Site route.

### B1167 — Sign-up and password-reset copy never said who the email comes from `[Site Planner / AuthPanel]` (task) #auth #ui #site-planner  *(owner chat 2026-07-30, provisional NEW-2. Minted **B1167** via `--against-main`, late. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open + ⏳ Verify + Done for `AuthPanel`, `signup`, `confirmation`, `sender`, `SMTP`, `email`, `B297/B298/B530`: B297/B298 built the panel, B530 did its modal a11y, B1044 the recovery flow — none of them owns what the copy SAYS about the email. Net-new.)*
`[ ]` **⏳ IMPLEMENTED — V543 PENDING.** Both messages now name the sender and say to check spam. **⚠ Carries a live product RISK the owner must decide on — see the Supabase built-in email note below.**
- Verify: live
- Origin: filed 2026-07-30 from chat
- **Report.** Michael: *"for signups, please let them know when verifying via email who the email will come from, I think it's Supabase."*
- **Cause.** The copy read *"Account created — check your email for a confirmation link, then sign in."* A user watching for something from planyr.io never finds the message that actually arrived, concludes the signup failed, and retries or leaves. The password-reset message (*"Password-reset email sent — check your inbox"*) had exactly the same hole and got the same treatment.
- **The fix.** One constant — `lib/authMail.js` — holds the sender, and BOTH messages are generated from it, so the copy cannot drift from what actually sends. One short line each, naming the display name AND the address (the first is what an inbox shows, the second is what a search box matches) plus the spam prompt.
- **⚠ THE SENDER COULD NOT BE READ FROM THE SANDBOX, and was not guessed.** The egress policy 403s `supabase.com` and `supabase.co` at the proxy, so no dashboard read, no Management API call and no real signup could be triggered from here; the project's auth logs (24 h) hold no mail events. What WAS established from the database through the Supabase MCP: three confirmation emails have ever been sent (2026-07-02 ×2, 2026-07-09), each confirmed 14–77 s later, to `hillwood.com` and `planyr.io` addresses. **The owner confirmed in chat (2026-07-30) that the project is on Supabase's BUILT-IN email service**, and that is what the copy names: `Supabase Auth (noreply@mail.app.supabase.io)`.
- **⚠ AND THAT IS A PRODUCTION RISK, raised loudly rather than silently patched.** Supabase's own documentation says the built-in service *"is not meant for production use"*, is rate-limited to a handful of messages per hour, and — the sharp edge — *"will refuse to deliver messages to addresses that are not part of the project's team"*, failing with **"Email address not authorized."** So today a stranger's sign-up cannot receive a confirmation at all; the three deliveries on record are all team/owner addresses, which is consistent with exactly that. **No mail provider was configured from here — that needs credentials and is the owner's call.** Filed for him in `OWNER-TODO.md` with the concrete options (Resend / Postmark / SES wired as custom SMTP, sending from a planyr.io address, which also fixes deliverability and brand trust).
- **When custom SMTP lands, two lines change** (`AUTH_SENDER_NAME` / `AUTH_SENDER_EMAIL`) and the copy follows automatically — the file says so in a ⛔ note at the top.
- **Verified here (sandbox):** `test/authMailCopy.test.js` (6 cases) — both messages carry the configured address AND display name, the address is a real single address and not a placeholder, both stay one short line and mention spam, AuthPanel imports the constants and hardcodes neither message, and the old sender-less wording appears nowhere. lint 0 errors · full suite 6,708 · build green.
- **What no sandbox test can prove, and is the whole point of V543:** that the From header on a real confirmation email actually matches this copy.

### B1195 — A building's truck court and side parking carried a DIFFERENT building's length, overhanging it by ~195 ft `[Site Planner / dockZones]` (bug) #site-planner #ui #persistence  *(owner chat 2026-07-30, provisional NEW-1, live rows quoted in the brief and re-read from `site_elements` before a line was written. Minted **B1195 / V552** via `git fetch origin main && npm run next-id -- --against-main`, LATE — as the last step before push. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open + ⏳ Verify + Done for `alongLen`, `sideParkFit`, `truckCourt`, `relayoutWallKids`, `relayoutSide`, `forCourt`, `dockZones`, `duplicate`, `B1123`, `B1124`, `B492`, `B1039`: **B1123** fixed a spurious `alongLen` PIN on a trailer and **B1124** fixed a duplicate's `forCourt` CROSS-LINK — both are the same FAMILY and both are ⏳ Verify, but neither owns this defect: these children carry no `alongLen` at all and their bonds are correct; their RUN is baked into `w`/`h`. **B1039**/NEW-3 built the side-parking along-wall intent rule this hardens. Net-new, not a recurrence — the invariant "a child may not claim more wall than its host has" was never stated anywhere.)*
`[ ]` **⏳ IMPLEMENTED — V552 PENDING.** The court and the west parking row are re-laid onto their own 514 ft host, on load and on every resize; the write path can no longer manufacture the intent that froze them.
- Verify: live
- Origin: filed 2026-07-30 from chat
- **Report.** Michael: *"obviously my building is super messed up."* Weld County, CO — site `sms7v3ua7ksy`, "Concept A".
- **What the saved rows say (AUDIT-FIRST — read from `site_elements`, not from the brief).** Three buildings at the identical rotation 354.81766642639934, so they were duplicated from one another: `e7373` 260 × 708.58, `e7381` 260 × 577, `e7389` 260 × 514. The BUILDING is right (its label reads 133,640 sf = 260 × 514). Its truck court `e7390` is 135 × **708.58** and its west parking row `e7394` is **708.58** × 60 — 708.58 being `e7373`'s length. That is **194.58 ft of overhang** past the end of the building, which is exactly what he is looking at.
- **Cause, established from the rows rather than guessed.** Both children sit EXACTLY where the layout would have put them for a 708.58-long host at that host's pre-shorten centre — off by half the shrink along the wall, to the foot. They were never re-laid after the host got shorter. **The brief's reading that "the wall strips track the host properly, so the strip relayout is working" does not survive the timestamps:** the left sidewalk's own row was rewritten **two minutes after** the host's commit, in a separate write (`rev` 8 at 20:34:16 vs the host's `rev` 5 at 20:32:20). That is `normalizeWallKids` — the load-time heal — fixing it on the next open. **The strips being right is not evidence that the resize re-laid anything; it is evidence that a heal exists for strips and for nothing else.**
- **Which of the two candidate mechanisms.** Neither, exactly, and the rows say so. (a) DUPLICATE is already fixed: **B1124** shipped `bondRemap`, and a copy carries the full child set at the copy's own dimensions — asserted now. (b) RESIZE is where the state came from, but the gesture that skipped the refit is **not recoverable from the rows** and is stated as unknown rather than invented: the host and the children landed in two commits 1.2 s apart, and every resize path in `SitePlanner` calls `refitChildren` → `relayoutAllSides` + `relayoutWallKids`, which would have re-laid both. Chasing it further would not change the fix, because **no write path may leave a child claiming more wall than its host has** — so the invariant belongs where it can be enforced regardless of how it was broken.
- **The one write-path defect that IS provable, and it is exactly the regression the brief was suspicious of.** `relayoutWallKids` runs on a host resize with the NEW host box but the OLD child boxes, so a field faithfully TRACKING the old span measures different from the new one and is read as *hand-positioned*. Its run is clamped (so the plan looks right) and the pre-resize run is stamped onto `sideParkFit` as intent to spring back to. **Nobody expressed that intent.** The receipt is on his own plan: Building 2 is 577 ft long and its west field carries `sideParkFit { run: 708.58 }` — the OTHER building's length. Grow that host and the field springs out 131 ft past it. This is B1123's disease (intent inferred from geometry alone) one field over.
- **The fix, at the root rather than as two symptom patches.** ONE pure rule — `lib/dogEar.js` `sideParkAlongRun` — shared by the canvas refit and the load-time heal, so they cannot answer *"is this run user intent?"* differently: **a run LONGER than the wall it hugs is never intent, it is staleness** (every gesture that can set one clamps it to the wall, so an over-length run can only have come from a longer host), and only a gesture aimed AT THAT FIELD (`pinAllowed`, B1123's `userResize` by another name) may pin one. A host refit, a duplicate, a relayout and the heal all pass false and are structurally incapable of stamping.
- **The load-time heal, so his existing plan corrects itself on open.** `siteModel.normalizeHostRuns` (new, in `normalizeBondedChildren`, so BOTH read paths run it — the blob and the `site_elements` rows) re-lays any dock-zone chain member or side-parking row whose along-wall run outruns its host, through the same pure `layoutZoneByKind` / `wallKidBox` the canvas uses, and drops an `alongLen` or a `sideParkFit` that names an impossible length. A run that FITS is left completely alone, so the owner's hand-positioned fields (B1039's fire-lane curb return) still survive every load. The repairs ride the existing B1118 `exempt` set, so they diff and COMMIT rather than being adopted straight back over by the torn rows.
- **Why the three existing passes could not catch it, precisely.** `normalizeStrandedZones` measures the ACROSS axis against its computed anchor and the ALONG axis only for wall OVERLAP — deliberately, because a zone may legitimately slide; the court is 197.5 ft out (exactly right) and overlaps its wall, so it passes. `normalizeZoneAlongLen` drops a spurious `alongLen`; these children have none. `normalizeWallKids` heals a side-parking row's PERPENDICULAR axis only and keeps its run verbatim as intent.
- **Stated trade-off, not buried:** an over-length run set by dragging the field's own end past the wall no longer springs back after a host shrink unless the drag itself stamped it. The render was always clamped, so nothing visible changes; what is lost is a spring-back for a length the product never draws — and keeping it is what re-created a foreign host's length.
- **Verified here (sandbox — ATTEMPT-BEFORE-YOU-PARK honoured, twice over).** `test/hostRunHeal.test.js` (25 cases, driven off the owner's REAL saved elements in `ui-audit/fixtures/weld-concept-a.json`): every child of `e7389` measures 514 and none measures 708.58; the court is re-POSITIONED as well as re-sized; the correct buildings and the untouched sidewalks come back BY IDENTITY (no churn) and the pass is idempotent; the spurious `sideParkFit` is dropped; an `alongLen` past the wall is dropped; a 300 ft field slid 40 ft along a 514 ft wall is untouched; shortening a host re-lays court AND side parking AND strips; a host refit / relayout / heal can never stamp `alongLen` (`resizedZoneAlongLen`) or a run (`sideParkAlongRun`), and only a gesture aimed at the field can; duplicating a building copies all 8 members at the copy's own dimensions with every bond remapped inside the copy and no intent stamped, and a copy of the BROKEN building is repaired exactly like the original. Then the real thing: **`e2e/dock-zone-host-run.spec.js` 3/3 in headless Chromium through the real render path**, seeded with all three of his buildings — every long-wall child of the 514 ft building measures 514 off the LIVE canvas DOM, the court is flush on the dock wall and the parking still flush beyond its sidewalk, no child of ANY building on the plan overhangs its long wall, and the invariant survives a real Properties-panel resize down to 400 ft AND back up to 620 ft with nothing springing out. lint 0 errors · full suite green · build green · bundle budgets within ceiling.
- **Cost, stated rather than buried:** +4.4 KB on the Site route (+1.1 KB largest chunk), inside the band.

### B1196 — Address search showed the OWNER'S MAILING address instead of the situs — and that wrong address became the site NAME `[Site Planner / MapFinder]` (bug) #site-planner #gis #ui  *(found 2026-07-30 while investigating B1195; the owner has not reported it. Minted **B1196 / V553** via `--against-main`, late. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open + ⏳ Verify + Done for `situs`, `ADDR_RE`, `findAttr`, `appraisal`, `parcelInfo`, `MapFinder`, `site name`, `B233`, `B244`, `B787`, `B1166`: **B233** built the card, **B244/B787** taught its field map the statewide-backup columns, **B1166** (⏳ Verify) trimmed its HEIGHT — none of them owns which column the address comes FROM. Coordinated with B1166 rather than colliding: this changes `parcelCardRows`' situs resolution and leaves its three-row split, its caps and its component untouched. Net-new.)*
`[ ]` **⏳ IMPLEMENTED — V553 PENDING.** The card, the "Situs address" row and the seeded plan name all resolve the LAND's address through one ordered ladder; a mailing address can no longer win, and when there is no situs the fallback is what the user searched.
- Verify: live
- Origin: filed 2026-07-30 from chat (found in-session, not reported)
- **Report.** None — found while auditing B1195's site. It is real and it is embarrassing in front of a client.
- **Evidence, from the live row.** Site `sms7v3ua7ksy` is in **Weld County, COLORADO** (`co_weld`, centred near 40.3418 / -104.9765) and is NAMED **"2221 E LAMAR BLVD STE 790"** — FORESTAR (USA) REAL ESTATE GROUP INC's corporate mailing address in **Arlington, TEXAS**. The parcel's own attributes carry both: `SITUS: "4050 CR 50   JOHNSTOWN"` (the land) and `ADDRESS1: "2221 E LAMAR BLVD STE 790"` with `CITY: ARLINGTON` / `STATE: TX` (the owner's head office). He searched "4050 COUNTY ROAD 50"; the card came back titled with the head office; the card title seeds the plan name on **Plan this site**, so the plan was named after it.
- **Cause — and it is NOT what the brief suspected, which matters.** The suspicion was a mail/owner/billing key family leaking through a loose catch-all. **Nothing in `ADDRESS1` says "mail"**, so excluding that family would not have caught this one. The real defect is **missing PRECEDENCE**: the resolver was a single regex with `situs|…|^addr|address` alternatives applied by `findAttr`, i.e. *"the first KEY in object order that matches ANY alternative"*. `ADDRESS1` matched `address`, the service lists it before `SITUS`, and it won. With alternation there is no such thing as a preferred field — only whichever column the service happened to list first.
- **The fix.** An ordered **ladder** (`lib/appraisal.js` `SITUS_LADDER` / `situsKey` / `situsAddress`): every key is tested against rung 1 (*says situs*) before any key is tested against rung 2 (*the land's address under another name*: site/prop/physical/location/street address), and only then rung 3 (the generic `address` / `full_addr` catch-all — kept, because plenty of CADs do name their situs column plainly, but no longer able to outrank rungs 1–2). Mailing columns are excluded at **every** rung by name (`mail`, `owner_addr`, `care_of`, `billing`, `remit`, …) and the generic rung additionally refuses **numbered address LINES** (`ADDRESS1` / `ADDR_LINE_2`) — a line number is the hallmark of a mailing block, and it is what makes the Weld record safe even if its `SITUS` were empty. **No situs → NULL**, which is a real answer: the card falls back to the address the user searched.
- **Applied to the site NAME too.** `siteNameFromParcel` seeds the plan from situs → what was searched → the account id → "Untitled site", and **refuses any candidate that equals a value the record files under a mailing key**, whatever supplied it. The ladder already prevents that on every schema we have; this catches the one we have not.
- **One ladder, four call sites.** The four copies of the loose `ADDR_RE` — `MapFinder` (the card + the plan name), `SitePlanner` (the canvas identify), `counties.detectField` (which column an address SEARCH queries) and `appraisal.APPR_FIELDS` (the "Situs address" row) — now share it, so they cannot drift or disagree about which column is the address.
- **Verified here (sandbox).** `test/situsAddress.test.js` (15 cases) over realistic county attribute sets: the REAL Weld bag (in the service's own key order) resolves `SITUS`, and still does when the mailing column is moved to the front — the exact ordering the old resolver flipped on; the Waller shape (`SITUS_ADDR` + `MAIL_ADDR`) resolves the situs; a record with ONLY a mailing address — named or as an un-named numbered line — yields **no address rather than the mailing one**; a plainly-named `ADDRESS` column still resolves; the seeded name is the land on Weld, falls back to the searched string with no situs, and never equals a mailing value on any shape; `apprRows`' Situs row and `detectField` follow the same ladder. Existing `appraisal` / `parcelCard` / `counties` suites unchanged and green. lint 0 errors · full suite green · build green.
- **⛔ AMENDED 2026-08-14 (B519152 audit) — SEVERITY, STATED FIRST SO IT CANNOT BE SKIM-READ UPWARD: THIS
  IS A NAMING DEFECT. **NO MAP IS WRONG. NO COORDINATE IS WRONG. NO AERIAL SHOWS THE WRONG GROUND.**
  The real worst case, measured rather than reasoned, is **8 plans with a slightly wrong NAME, exactly 1
  of them confirmed wrong** — the rest read as genuine situs addresses.**
- **WHAT THE BUG TOUCHES, precisely: the NAME ONLY.** The coordinates come from the owner picking the
  parcel on the MAP; only the card's TITLE was resolved through the broken ladder. The two are
  independent paths, which is why a wrong title never moved a plan. Verified read-only on both affected
  rows: `sms7v3ua7ksy` ("2221 E LAMAR BLVD STE 790") and `smsdmqosh4sx` ("4050 CR 50 JOHNSTOWN") carry
  the **identical** origin `40.3460 / -104.9779` and the **identical** aerial bbox
  `-104.98235,40.34019,-104.97354,40.35174` — the same point in **Weld County, Colorado**, the correct
  land. Arlington, TX is ≈`32.7 / -97.1`; **no coordinate in the database is near it.**
- **EXPOSURE, established cheaply from those coordinates:** of **71** plans, **8** are named from an
  appraisal address at all — the only ones this resolver can reach — and **1** carries the office-address
  hallmark of a suite token (the known `STE 790` row). 58 plans carry a coordinate-derived aerial; that
  number is listed only to close the question, since the defect cannot reach coordinates.
- **⛔ A HYPOTHESIS THAT WAS TESTED AND IS FALSE — recorded ONLY so it is not re-derived, NOT as a
  residual risk.** Because a `fromMap` aerial's image address is derived from the site's coordinates, it
  is a natural inference that a wrong situs address would silently produce an aerial of the wrong ground.
  **It does not, and could not: the two paths are independent, as measured above.** Both the owner's
  brief and this session's first reply to him asserted the wrong-ground consequence as fact; **both were
  inference, not evidence, and both are struck.** A wrong name is a wrong name; it was never a wrong
  picture. **An item that overstates its own severity is how a small naming defect gets treated as a
  data-integrity incident six months from now** — hence this block leads with the severity and not with
  the hypothesis.
- **Not fixed, deliberately and stated:** the site named `2221 E LAMAR BLVD STE 790` in the database keeps that name until it is renamed — this stops the next plan being misnamed, it does not rewrite a saved record's name behind the owner's back. Renaming that one plan is a one-click owner action (filed in `OWNER-TODO.md`).

- **Extended the existing `ui-audit/verify-schedule-export-health-colours.mjs`, per the brief — did not rebuild it.** Every new claim is mutation-proven, independently: `--mutate-badge` (exact string swap, reinstates the removed component + all three call-sites) flips `badgeAbsenceGridOk`/`badgeAbsenceMasterOk` red while every pre-existing check and both new Automatic-clear checks stay green; `--mutate-automatic-grid` and `--mutate-automatic-master` (each an exact swap of one surface's own commit handler to a no-op) each flip only their own surface's Automatic-clear check (+ its half of the persistence-payload check) while the other surface and the badge checks stay green — proving the two clear-paths are independently tested, not one check standing in for both. ### B662048 — Woods Road "Concept A 1M SF": 57 elements a teammate deleted from the wrong plan, restored + ROOT-CAUSED & FIXED `[Site Planner / persistence]` (bug — data-loss) #site-planner #persistence #sync  *(owner-authorized URGENT production data recovery, 2026-08-22. On 2026-08-21 a teammate, bryndan.nerren@hillwood.com (`74515a27-4157-4696-9c30-3f11c1bc7d16`), soft-deleted 57 of 95 elements from `smsrrlk9u576` ("Concept A 1M SF", project Woods Road, owned by mikeabmab@live.com), believing he was editing his own separate copy (`smt3dobluh5e`, "Concept A 1M SF Bryndan" — untouched, 63 elements, left exactly as-is). DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open/⏳ Verify/Done for `site_elements`, `deleted_by`, `restore`, `Woods Road`, `smsrrlk9u576`: no prior item. Net-new. Minted **B662048 / V337360** from this branch's reserved block B662048–B662063 / V337360–V337375 against `origin/main` d07546e.)*
`[x]` **RESTORED, AND — AMENDED 2026-08-22 (STANDING RULE #2: the "no code changed" line below was a NULL, not a disposition) — ROOT-CAUSED AND FIXED at the storage layer, mutation-proven. Data recovery: AUDIT-FIRST proved the exact row set before any write; restore executed as one atomic transaction with an in-transaction re-count guard; the dual-write mirror reconciled in the same transaction. `Verify: live` → V337360 (data restore, unchanged by this amendment) · code fix is `Verify: sandbox` (deterministic, no live-verify class applies — see below).**
- Verify: live (`Blocker: real-data` — this is one specific signed-in saved plan; only someone with access to it can open it and drive a commit to confirm the assembly-tear resolution live)
- **AUDIT-FIRST — proved the count before writing anything.** `select count(*) from site_elements where site_id='smsrrlk9u576' and deleted_by='74515a27-...' and deleted_at between '2026-08-21 19:32:33+00' and '2026-08-21 20:08:45+00'` → **57**, exact match. Composition cross-checked against `data->>'type'`: parking 18 · paving 12 · building 12 · sidewalk 7 · trailer 3 · road 3 · landscape 2 = 57, matching the reported breakdown exactly. Guardrails confirmed before touching anything: `smt3dobluh5e` (Bryndan's own copy) held 63 live elements and was never targeted by any write; the same site carried 60 OTHER soft-deleted rows, all `deleted_by` the owner himself between 2026-08-13 and 2026-08-17 — confirmed untouched both before and after.
- **Snapshot before writing, for reversibility.** `recovery_20260822_site_elements_snapshot` / `recovery_20260822_sites_snapshot` — full point-in-time copies of every `site_elements` row for this site (155) and the `sites` row itself, taken via `apply_migration` before any UPDATE; row counts verified to match the live table exactly before proceeding. (Safe to drop once the live check below passes — they exist purely as this incident's undo path.)
- **Restore, atomic and self-checking.** A single `DO $$ ... $$` block (migration `recovery_20260822_restore_smsrrlk9u576`) re-derives the 57-row id set *inside* the transaction and **aborts via `RAISE EXCEPTION` if the count is not exactly 57** (guards a race between the audit query and the write), then for those rows: `deleted_at = null`, `deleted_by = null`, `rev = rev + 1`, `updated_at = now()`. `rev` was confirmed (by inspecting real multi-element commits) to be a per-element counter, not a shared per-site value, so each row needed its own `+1`. This makes the restore arrive at connected clients as an ordinary row UPDATE over the existing rows-canonical realtime path, not a silent resurrection.
- **Dual-write reconciled in the SAME transaction.** `sites.data` is a legacy mirror for this site (`elementsInRows: true`, so `data->'els'` is correctly empty — `site_elements` is canonical) but `data->'deletedIds'` is still live and would re-delete a restored row on the next client save. All 57 restored ids were confirmed present in `deletedIds` (122 entries) before the fix; the same transaction removed exactly those 57 (by array exclusion, never a hand-typed id list) and bumped `sites.version` (141→142). Verified after commit by re-querying the live table, not by re-reading the SQL: `deletedIds` length 122→65.
- **Structural damage — traced, not guessed, and resolved by the restore itself.** 59 `event:assembly-tear-unhealable` rows fired for this site between 19:58–20:06 — all logging one identical defect (3 message variants only, for the `commit`/`post-commit(settled)`/`canvas` seams of the same event, not 59 distinct problems): landscape `e1454739vcpvpz` bonded (`forTrailer` + `prevZone`) to host `e1454716vcpvpz`, missing sibling `e1454724vcpvpz` (a trailer). All three elements fall inside the exact 57-row restore set (same actor, same window) — restoring them returns the sibling, so the tear has nothing left to trip on. No separate SQL patch was applied to `assembly_id`/bond metadata; the elements' own `data` payloads were confirmed intact (non-null, non-empty, valid JSON object) both before and after.
- **Final state, verified against the live table, not re-derived from the SQL written:** `site_elements` for `smsrrlk9u576` — 95 live (was 38), 60 still soft-deleted (the owner's own 8/13–8/17 deletions, byte-for-byte untouched), 155 total rows (nothing hard-deleted). `sites.data->deletedIds` — 65 (was 122). `sites.version` — 142 (was 141). `smt3dobluh5e` — unchanged at 63 live.
- **⛔ SUPERSEDED — "No code changed... nothing found here indicates a software defect to fix" was WRONG, and it is exactly the failure STANDING RULE #2 exists to prevent: a null ("the restore didn't need a code change") was written up as a disposition ("there is no defect"), when the CAUSE of the original report was never separately investigated at all — only the DATA damage was. The dual-write reconciliation claim in the sentence this replaces is still true and unrelated to what follows.**
- **⛔ ROOT CAUSE, found by driving the real app (headless Chromium against the real dev build) rather than reasoning from source alone, per AUDIT-FIRST, and proved RED before the fix.** `SitePlanner.jsx`'s `handleDuplicate` (also `handleNewPlan`) calls `flushSite()` — a synchronous `saveSite()` on the SOURCE plan — immediately followed by `SitePlannerApp.jsx`'s `duplicatePlan`, whose OWN `saveSite()` writes the fresh COPY. No `await` sits between them; both land in the same JS tick. `saveSite()` (`storage.js`) stamped `updatedAt: Date.now()`, millisecond resolution — and reproduced **deterministically, with the real `storage.js` functions, replaying this exact call order** (`test/tmp_duplicate_tie.test.js`, scratch, since deleted): the SOURCE and the fresh COPY landed on the **SAME millisecond far more often than not**, with NO artificial timing needed. `loadPlansOfGroup`'s "newest first" sort — `(b.updatedAt||0) - (a.updatedAt||0)` — returns 0 on that tie, and `Array.prototype.sort` has been STABLE since ES2019, so a tied pair keeps its ORIGINAL (insertion) order: the SOURCE, already present in the store, sorts **ahead of** the just-created copy. Two call sites treat `plans[0]` as "the plan to open" whenever they have no more specific pointer to trust: `pickResumeTarget` (`bootResume.js` — the boot resume and the post-sign-in-pull resume in `SitePlannerApp.jsx`'s `applyUser`) and `openProjectGroup` (the route-reconciliation effect and the project-breadcrumb switcher). So: duplicate a plan, then hit ANY path that re-resolves "which plan of this project am I on" with no exact pointer to the copy already in hand — a reload, a fresh tab/device, a sign-in resume shortly after duplicating — and the app silently reopens the SOURCE plan while every other surface (the new plan's own name, "(copy)" suffix, etc.) gives no reason to suspect it. This is the mechanism: canvas, autosave target and header all correctly point at the source plan (self-consistent, so nothing *looks* wrong) — it's the ROUTING decision made once, at that resume moment, that silently picked the wrong plan of the two. The URL is uninformative either way, since it names the PROJECT (group), not the individual plan — duplicating never changes it. **Checked all four the brief asked about, not stopping at the first one that looked correct:** in the ordinary same-tab "duplicate, then keep editing" case (no intervening resume) canvas, autosave target (`activeSiteId`/`currentSiteId`), header plan-name and URL all agree correctly (verified live, headless, against the real dev build using the actual production fixture `ui-audit/fixtures/woods-road-1m-sf.json` seeded as `smsrrlk9u576`) — the divergence is real but requires a resume-with-no-exact-pointer moment to surface, which the 36-minute window of B662048's incident (19:32–20:08, spanning the 20:04:41 duplicate) had ample room for.
- **Dedupe note:** searched Open/⏳ Verify/Done for `pickResumeTarget`, `openProjectGroup`, `updatedAt`, `newest plan`, `loadPlansOfGroup` — **B616673** (a teammate seeing only one plan of a shared project) was checked as instructed and is a DIFFERENT mechanism (a jsonb-id collision in `cloudList`/`mergePulledSites` dropping a plan from the merge entirely, already fixed there) — not a duplicate of this. This item (B662048) IS the exact same incident as the one being investigated, so the finding is filed here as an amendment rather than a parallel B#, per DEDUPE-FIRST.
- **THE FIX — monotonic `updatedAt` per tab, at the one write choke point (`storage.js` `saveSite`), so two saves cannot land in the same millisecond ever again, for ANY caller, not just Duplicate.** `nextUpdatedAt()` tracks the last stamp this tab issued and returns `max(Date.now(), lastStamp + 1)` — the real wall clock is still the basis (it only nudges forward when a genuine collision would occur), so cross-device/cross-tab comparisons elsewhere in this file (the B127 stale-write guard, cloud merge "cloud already same/newer" checks) are unaffected: those compare against OTHER tabs'/devices' independently-clocked stamps, which this per-tab nudge cannot retroactively change. This also closes the identical exposure in `newPlanSameParcel` ("New plan"), which shares the exact same `flushSite()`-then-`saveSite()` shape.
- **Guards, mutation-proven (git-stashed the fix, confirmed RED on the unfixed source, restored, confirmed GREEN).** `test/storage.test.js` — two new tests replaying `duplicatePlan`'s real call order verbatim under a FROZEN clock (`Date.now` mocked to a constant, the exact condition that used to tie): (1) the copy's `updatedAt` is now always strictly greater than the source's, and `loadPlansOfGroup(group)[0].id` is the copy, never the source; (2) general monotonicity — two ordinary back-to-back saves of unrelated sites never tie either, so this isn't a duplicate-only patch.
- Sandbox: `npx vitest run` 12,157 tests, 12,155 passed (the 2 failures are pre-existing and unrelated — `docReviewLayerVisibility.test.js` / `hiddenContentReads.test.js` mutation checks that `git show` a specific historical commit hash not present in this session's shallow clone; confirmed via `git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository` → true and `git cat-file -t <hash>` → not a valid object, on a checkout that had ZERO working-tree changes at the time); `npm run lint` 0 errors (24 pre-existing warnings, untouched); `npm run build` green. `Verify: sandbox` — this is a deterministic pure-function defect (proved and fixed with a frozen clock, no timing dependency), not a `LIVE-VERIFY` class; no `V#` needed.
- Files: `src/workspaces/site-planner/lib/storage.js`, `test/storage.test.js`. (The original data-recovery migrations are unchanged: `recovery_20260822_snapshot_smsrrlk9u576`, `recovery_20260822_restore_smsrrlk9u576` on `planyr_production`.)
